Sheet 20.

Mr Kuh sau Kyi :- I ask that a Cantonese Interpreter be
had in the case of my clients. (request granted).

1st accused :- The book (pro) which is alleged by the
Police to have contained the pistol used in the murder, is not
mine. I have never seen it before. I had a similar book,
but it was in foreign language.

Judge :- You admitted to the Police previously, that
the book is yours. Anyway how do you know that this book
I have here is in Chinese Language ?.

1st accused :- When the book (pro), was shown to me
at the Police Station, it was held some distance away from me,
and I did not see if it had foreign characters. There was
a book similar to the exhibit, brought to my home sometime
in 1933. I forgot the name of the book, or its contents. It
was in foreign language. The book in court is not mine.
The book in my home, was brought to my home by someone, but I
do not know the identity of the person. I received a
Deman pistol from my friend who is a Secretary of the P.S B.,
and I obtained a license from the S.M.Police for this pistol.
Being afraid of my children getting hold of the pistol, I
cut a recess in this book of mine, similar to the recess in
the exhibit, and therein I placed my pistol. I have never
seen this pistol (pro) before. I do not know if it was used
in the crime.

Mr Ru :- I would remind the court, that the firearm
license issued to the accused in respect to the Deman Pistol,
was cancelled.

1st accused :- I do not remember the pistol very well,
but I know that I got a permit for it. I received the
pistol in October 1933. I returned it to its owner named
Lee Mah.

第20页。

顾守基（Kuh sau Kyi）先生：我请求在我的当事人案件中配备一名粤语翻译。（请求获准）。

第一被告：警方声称装有谋杀所用枪支的那本书（物证）不是我的。我以前从未见过它。我有一本类似的书，但是外文的。

法官：你先前已向警方承认那本书是你的。无论如何，你怎么知道我手中的这本书是中文的？

第一被告：在警察局向我展示那本书（物证）时，它离我有一段距离，我没有看清上面是否有外文。1933年的某个时候，有人带到我家一本与呈堂证物相似的书。我忘记了那本书的名字或内容。那是外文的。法庭上的这本书不是我的。我家里的书是由某人带来的，但我不知道此人的身份。我从一位朋友那里得到一把德曼（Deman）手枪，他是公共租界工部局警务处（P.S B.）的秘书，我为这把手枪从上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.Police）获得了执照。因为害怕孩子们拿到这把手枪，我在这本书里挖了一个凹槽，类似于呈堂证物中的凹槽，并将我的手枪放在里面。我以前从未见过这把手枪（物证）。我不知道它是否被用于犯罪。

鲁（Ru）先生：我想提醒法庭，发给被告关于德曼手枪的持枪执照已被注销。

第一被告：我不太记得那把手枪了，但我知道我确实获得了许可证。我在1933年10月收到了那把手枪。我把它还给了它的主人，名叫李马（Lee Mah）。

Sheet 21.

Judg- to 1st accused :- Here is a Demon Pistol .38 calibre identical with the one given to you by Lee Mah, this pistol does not fit into the recess in the book, found at your home.

1st accused :- The book found at my home is not the exhibit, the Police have substituted the exhibit for it. I have never seen this book before. It is true that I have retained the book since 1933, but when I was questioned at the station, I thought it was my book, because it was so much like the exhibit. I can now see however that this book is different and is not mine. The 2nd accused is my assistant, he has been with me for four or five years. He is a member of the Heong Sung Foo Su Wi association. This is a charitable association.

2nd accused :- I am the boy to the 1st accused. I have been employed by him for three years. I know nothing about the book (pre). I do not know anything about the past activities of the 1st accused. I do not know about him obtaining the pistol from Lee Mah.

3rd accused :- My alias is Siao Kwangtung. At the end of November 1934, I went to Tsingtao. I know the two witnesses. Tsung Yuan has given false evidence, he is not a money lender, and is poorer than I am. I have never attended at his premises and asked for a loan. I have never offered any pistol as a security for the loan of $85. from Tsung Yuan. I have never seen the pistol (pre). I do not know if it was used in the crime. I know nothing about the murder. I have fought with the witness Tsung Yuan on two occasions. A man named Leh Foo Dim, reported at the association about something, and the 1st accused asked me to see the witness Tsung Yuan. This witness conducts an opium den in Chapel, and the chief tenant of the premises wanted to eject him. The 1st accused

第21页。

法官对第一被告说：这里有一把.38口径的德蒙（Demon）手枪，与李马给你的那把相同，但这把手枪放不进在你家发现的那本书的凹槽里。

第一被告：在我家发现的那本书不是呈堂证物，警方用证物调换了它。我以前从未见过这本书。的确，我自1933年以来一直保留着那本书，但在警局受审时，我以为那是我的书，因为它与证物非常相似。然而我现在可以看出，这本书不同，不是我的。第二被告是我的助手，他跟随我已四五年了。他是香松福绥维（Heong Sung Foo Su Wi）帮会的成员。这是一个慈善团体。

第二被告：我是第一被告的伙计。我受雇于他已有三年。我对那本书（前文提及）一无所知。我对第一被告过去的活动一无所知。我不知道他从李马那里获得手枪的事。

Murder of Japanese Marine on Darroch Road, 9.5 p.m. 9-11-35.
(Dixwell Road Misc: 112/35).

I beg to report the following facts connected
with pistol used in the murder of the Japanese Marine on
the night of 9-11-35.

The weapon, a Beretta, was manufactured by the
firm of Pietro Beretta, of Brescia, Italy, which was
established in the year 1860. The pistol in question was
made during the years 1915 and 1918, and as this make of
weapon was used extensively during the Great War, it is
quite possible that this particular pistol was issued to
the Italian forces. This data however could only be
obtained direct from the manufacturers, and considering
the time elapsed since the weapon was first issued, it
is quite likely that little or no satisfaction could be
gained by communicating with the manufacturer. Since the
year 1928, thirty nine of this particular make of weapon
have been used in armed crime and seized by the S.M.P.,
whilst a further 140 have been licensed in the Settlement,
which indicates that the Beretta pistol is fairly popular
in Shanghai. The crime pistol, although approximately 20
years old, is still in good condition and working order.
Some person, obviously an amateur, has endeavoured
to improve the appearance of the pistol by covering
it with a coat of paint, but this however does not
interfere with the working of the weapon.

The ammunition used in the above crime is
S.F.M. (Societie Francaise des Munitions) and is
probably the most popular of all continental ammunitions.

达罗克路（Darroch Road）日本海军陆战队员遇害案，晚上9点5分，1935年9月11日。
（狄思威路杂项档案：112/35）。

谨此报告与1935年9月11日晚杀害日本海军陆战队员一案中所用手枪有关之事实。

该武器为贝雷塔（Beretta）手枪，由意大利布雷西亚（Brescia）的彼得罗·贝雷塔（Pietro Beretta）公司制造，该公司成立于1860年。涉案手枪制造于1915年至1918年间，鉴于此种武器在第一次世界大战期间被广泛使用，这把手枪很有可能是配发给意大利军队的。然而，这些数据只能直接从制造商处获得，考虑到自该武器首次配发以来已过去很长时间，与制造商联系很可能收效甚微或毫无结果。自1928年以来，共有三十九支这种特定型号的手枪被用于武装犯罪并被上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）缴获，另有140支在租界内持有执照，这表明贝雷塔手枪在上海相当流行。作案手枪虽然已有约20年历史，但仍处于良好状态且功能正常。显然有一名外行人士试图通过涂上一层油漆来改善手枪的外观，但这并不影响武器的运作。

上述犯罪中使用的弹药是 S.F.M.（法国弹药公司，Societie Francaise des Munitions），这可能是所有欧洲大陆弹药中最受欢迎的一种。

pages.en:
- 2 -

It has been found that in 80% of recent armed crime
in the Settlement, this make of ammunition has been
used.

The Baretta used in the Japanese Marine
Murder, was again tested by the undersigned at Gordon
Road on 19-11-35 and 10 shots were fired to determine
the distance that the empty cases are thrown when
ejected by the pistol. The first case was thrown
in the
high/air and dropped Three Feet right rear of the
firer. The next seven cases were thrown high in the
air and dropped ONE FOOT in front of the firer,
forming a group of about two feet in circumference.
The ninth case was thrown into the air and dropped
EIGHTEEN FEET behind the firer, and the tenth case fell
in the group in front.

The varying distances of the "throw" could be
caused by the power of the charge, jerk and angle of
the firer's arm, firing the pistol whilst firer is in motion
etc., but it can be seen by the aforementioned text that
the pistol is inclined to throw the ejected cases
forward.

The marked round of ammunition found in the
pistol, although it could be a misfire, has in all
probability been struck by the firing-pin, protruding
slightly through the firing-pin hole, as the slide has
gone forward, and without the trigger being pressed.
Tests have been made, in the Arms Identification Section,
with the same kind of ammunition, and it has been found
that a much larger dent on the cap caused by a heavier
strike has failed to fire the charge.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

经查，在租界近期发生的武装犯罪中，有80%使用了该品牌的弹药。

用于日本海军陆战队员谋杀案的贝雷塔手枪，由具名者于1935年11月19日在戈登路（Gordon Road）再次进行测试，发射了10发子弹，以确定手枪抛出空弹壳的距离。第一个弹壳被抛向高/空中，落在射击者右后方三英尺处。接下来的七个弹壳被抛向高空，落在射击者前方一英尺处，形成一个周长约为两英尺的群体。第九个弹壳被抛向空中，落在射击者后方十八英尺处，第十个弹壳落在前方的群体中。

“抛出”距离的变化可能是由装药威力、射击者手臂的急动和角度、射击者在移动中开枪等因素造成的，但从上述文字可以看出，该手枪倾向于将抛出的弹壳向前方抛出。

在手枪中发现的那枚有标记的子弹，虽然可能是哑火，但极有可能已被击针击中，因为套筒已向前运动，且在未扣动扳机的情况下，击针略微从击针孔中突出。军械鉴定科已用同种弹药进行了测试，发现即使因更重的撞击而在底火上造成更大的凹痕，也未能引爆发射药。

Yang Vung Dao, Dixwell Road Station No. 3368 C/No/ 7/36375.
------

I beg to submit the following translation of letters
written by the above mentioned convict as per instruction
of Asst/ Gaoler Chadderton.
Letter (1) "Dear Chief & Asst. Compradores, S.S. "Taiyuen".
I am pleased to know that you are well.
I am in deep gratitude since my employment.
All people know that my present case is a malice
against me, for which I am not mentioning any
more. My wife informed me that you are
continuously paying my salary since my arrest.
I thank you deeply for your generosity by
writing to you this note. Later on I shall
call to express my gratitude.
(Sd) Yang Vung Dao
Dated 22.1.37".
Letters (2) and (3) contain similar expressions but
addressed to persons named Kwan Yuen and Tse Tsai
of s.s. "Tsinan" and the last one to his uncle.

Subject Possible Political Significance of the Murder of Hideo Nakayama.

Made by. D.S.I. Coyne Forwarded by. J.B.Ross D.I.

At about 9 p.m. on November 9, 1935, a First Class Seaman named Hideo Nakayama attached to the Headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, was shot dead on Darroch Road whilst walking alone to the barracks on North Szechuen Road.

The only witness to the shooting was a male Chinese named Woo Ziang Woo, a shoe maker, who was about to enter the home of a Japanese shoe maker at 90 Darroch Road when he heard the report of a firearm being discharged. In his first statement made to the Police within a few minutes of the occurrence, he alleged that on hearing the report he looked along the road and saw a person wearing the uniform of a Japanese sailor running into the Fong Loh Lee, an alleyway leading to North Szechuen Road, and another person lying on the roadway. When questioned more fully by Japanese detectives at Dixwell Road Police Station he modified his statement to the extent of saying that the person running away was wearing a short jacket and trousers of dark material.

Exhaustive enquiries were immediately made but no one could be found who had seen any person loitering the vicinity of the scene, or acting in a manner likely to attract attention.

The pistol with which the crime was committed was found by a Japanese sub-Inspector near a watchman's hut in the alleyway through which the murdered decamped. On examination it was found that this pistol had no record with the Municipal or French Police, and as the Chinese Maritime Customs do not note the number of firearms when they are imported, it was not possible to ascertain by whom the weapon had been imported. 制作人. 特别调查科助理督察长 Coyne 转发人. 特别调查科督察长 J.B.Ross

1935年11月9日晚9时许，隶属于日本海军陆战队总部的头等水兵中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）在独自步行前往北四川路兵营途中，于达罗克路（Darroch Road）被枪杀。

枪击案的唯一目击者是一名名叫吴祥武（Woo Ziang Woo，音译）的中国男子，职业为鞋匠。当时他正欲进入达罗克路90号一名日本鞋匠的住所，听到了一声枪响。他在案发后几分钟内向警方所作的首次陈述中称，听到枪声后他沿路望去，看见一名身穿日本水手制服的人跑进丰乐里（Fong Loh Lee，音译），这是一条通往北四川路的小巷，另有一人躺在马路上。当他在狄思威路（Dixwell Road）警署接受日本侦探更详细的讯问时，他修改了证词，称逃跑者身穿深色面料的短夹克和长裤。

警方立即进行了详尽的调查，但未能找到任何曾在现场附近徘徊或行为举止引人注意的人。

作案手枪由一名日本巡佐在凶手逃逸所经小巷的一处更夫棚附近发现。经查，该手枪在工部局警务处或法租界警务处均无登记记录，且由于中国海关在进口枪支时不记录号码，因此无法查明该武器由何人进口。由于警方缺乏任何可资利用的线索，曾希望

（左侧圆形印章：罪案科）
（左下角手写批注：该手枪为贝雷塔（Beretta）制造，制造商或许能提供帮助。JHS 1936年2月24日）

must be satisfied that the person accused has committed a
serious offence against the Party, such as disclosing secrets
to Police or other authorities which seriously affect the
interests of the party or actually assisting official authorities

properly organized in Shanghai about 1927, it is safe to say
that the only persons assassinated under its orders belonged
to the above category or were close relatives of some member
of the higher organs of the party whose betrayal of its
interests had resulted in the death of one or more important
communists. It is against the principles of the Communist

Authorities, Nakayama had never been affiliated with any
political party or movement or used in any way in detecting
Communist or other activities among his colleagues or others.
Therefore, there is no reason why the Communist Party should
consider or even suspect that he had committed a crime
against their party which should be punished by death.
The fact that the murder of the Japanese sailor was
carried out by one man also tends to discredit the theory
that the Communist Party was responsible for his death. The
personnel of the Group of the Communist Party which carries
out assassinations consists of highly trained men who make
careful plans in advance not only as to the place where an
assassination is to be committed but also as regards the
time it is to take place. There are definite instructions
laid down as to the points to be considered in selecting
both place and time. The scene of the shooting of the
Japanese sailor was a place where the assassin was likely
to be intercepted by either members of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party or Municipal Police, and in view of this and
the fact that the sailor could have with equal convenience
been shot at a point where the risks would not be so great,
it may safely be assumed that the murder was never planned by
the Communist Party.
Communists sent out to commit assassinations usually
operate in parties of three, and special arrangements are
made to ensure that the party will retain custody of the
weapon after the crime. No attempt to observe these methods
is evident in the case of the assassination of the Japanese
sailor.
（批：Somewhat sweeping）

日本水兵被一人单独杀害这一事实，也有力地驳斥了中国共产党对其死亡负责的理论。执行暗杀的中国共产党小组人员由受过高度训练的人员组成，他们不仅就实施暗杀的地点，而且就实施时间，都会事先制定周密的计划。对于选择地点和时间时需考虑的要点，有明确的指示规定。日本水兵被枪杀的地点是一个刺客容易被日本海军陆战队成员或工部局警察拦截的地方，鉴于这一点，以及水兵完全可以在风险较小的地点被同等方便地枪杀的事实，可以稳妥地推断，这次谋杀绝非由中国共产党策划。
被派出执行暗杀任务的共产党员通常以三人小组行动，并做出特别安排以确保小组在作案后仍能控制武器。在日本水兵遇刺案中，显然没有试图遵循这些方法。

The general conditions of the Chinese Communist Party
at the time the assassination took place are also factors
which tend to show the unlikelihood of that party being
responsible for the crime.
    During the Spring and Summer of 1935, the activities
of the anti-communist forces in the cities along the
Yangtze Valley seriously hampered them, bringing about
a curtailment of their activities. The arrest of Walden
led to the complete breakdown of the Military Espionage
Section and the subsequent arrest of the majority of its
personnel. At a later date the discovery of the plot to
effect the release of Walden from the Military Prison at
Wuchang led to the hasty departure from Shanghai of many
important Foreign members of the organization.
    During July the central offices of a number of branches
of the party were raided and in addition to effecting the
arrest of over thirty members of various committees, the
Police seized large quantities of literature. This series
of setbacks, coming in rapid succession in the same year,
completely disorganized the administrative organ, and
attempts to effect its re-establishment have so far failed.
At about the time in question there was in transit, from
South and Central China, several thousand men of the
Communist Forces, moving into positions along the border of
Inner Mongolia.
    The resources of the whole Party were required in
bringing this move to a successful conclusion, and particular
attention had to be paid to the areas into which the forces
were to move. It was for this reason that all experienced

    1935年春夏期间，长江沿岸城市反共力量的活动严重阻碍了共产党，导致其活动缩减。沃尔登（Walden）的被捕导致军事情报科彻底瓦解，随后其大多数人员被捕。后来，企图从武昌军事监狱营救沃尔登的计划败露，导致该组织许多重要的外籍成员匆忙离开上海。
    7月间，该党多个分支机构的中央办公室遭到突袭，除了逮捕各委员会三十多名成员外，警方还缴获了大量宣传刊物。这一系列挫折在同一年内接踵而至，完全打乱了其行政机构，迄今为止重建该机构的尝试均告失败。在事发前后，共有数千名共产党部队人员从中国南部和中部过境，向内蒙古边境沿线阵地移动。
    全党资源都需用于确保此次行动圆满成功，并且必须特别注意部队将要进入的地区。正是出于这个原因，所有经验丰富的

最后必须提到的是，上海还有其他一些中国派系和个人，他们可能认为本案预计会引发的“事件”能带来某些利益。

Subject Murder of Japanese Sailor on Darroch and attempted assassination

Made by D.S. Kamashita Forwarded by [Signature] D.I.
-x File
D. 7075
In view of the fact that the late 1st Class Seaman
Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, who was
murdered on Darroch Road on November 9, was a person of
a gentle disposition and had an excellent record during
his period of service in the Navy, the Japanese Naval
Authorities and the Japanese Consular Police have come to
the conclusion that the motive of the murder could not be
attributed to any love intrigue or to an act of revenge or
robbery. The case must, therefore, be considered to
have a somewhat political background.
Several days prior to the murder of Nakayama, certain
Chinese communists with the object of furthering anti-
Japanese propaganda spread a rumour to the effect that the
outbreak of a second Sino-Japanese incident in Shanghai
was imminent, in view of the fact that a number of Chinese
soldiers in plain-clothes had secretly entered the Chinese
city while the Japanese were concentrating their forces
in the northern part of Shanghai. Their object was to
spread uneasiness amongst local Chinese so that they might
be able to seize upon the opportunity in expanding their
activities. As a result of this rumour considerable
uneasiness prevailed especially amongst Chinese residents
in Chapel. In order to make the people believe that there
was some truth in the rumour the Communists decided to
resort to an act of violence against the Japanese thereby
creating a tumultuous situation. With this object in view
they contemplated assassinating a high Japanese official.
Finding this difficult to carry out as all high officials
are well protected, they changed their original plan and
See D. 7050

help in elucidating
the murder

制作人 下田 D.S. (Kamashita) 转呈人 [签名] D.I.
-x 档案
D. 7075
鉴于11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）被谋杀的日本海军陆战队一等兵中山（Nakayama）性情温和，且在海军服役期间表现优异，日本海军当局和日本领事警察得出结论，认为谋杀动机不能归因于任何情感纠葛、报复或抢劫行为。因此，本案必须被视为具有一定的政治背景。
在中山被杀前几天，一些中国共产党员为了推进反日宣传，散布谣言称，由于日军在上海北部集结兵力，而许多便衣中国士兵已秘密进入华界，上海即将爆发第二次中日事变。他们的目的是在当地中国人中制造不安，以便趁机扩大活动。由于这一谣言，引起了相当大的不安，尤其是在闸北（Chapel，原文如此，应为Chapei）的中国居民中。为了让人们相信谣言有一定真实性，共产党人决定对日本人采取暴力行动，从而制造混乱局面。为此，他们曾策划刺杀一名日本高官。
鉴于所有高官均受到严密保护，难以实施，他们改变了原计划，见 D. 7050
特务科副总监
足够
这无助于阐明
谋杀案真相
（印：刑事处副总监 1935年12月23日）

decided to assassinate a Japanese sailor in uniform because
it would be much easier to undertake and the result obtainable
would be the same in provoking the Japanese Naval Authorities.
The plan was arranged to be carried out in the vicinity of
the Landing Party Headquarters so that the Naval Authorities
would regard the incident as a challenge against the Navy
and adopt emergency measures, thereby causing confusion in
Shanghai.
If this information is correct and if there is any
truth in the statement issued by the Nanking Authorities
that communists were responsible for the attempted assassination
of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, some connection between the two
cases may be regarded as possible.
The Japanese Authorities, however, are of the opinion
that Nanking's statement is incorrect and that the attempt
on the life of Mr. Wang was perpetrated either by
nationalists or by members of the "C.C. Party" (a faction
in the Kuomintang).
According to the Japanese Consular Police, the Chinese
Communist Party have issued a statement declaring that
Sung Fong Ming (孫鳳鳴), Mr. Wang's assailant, is not a
communist but a member of the Fascist Party.

决定刺杀一名身穿制服的日本水兵，因为这样更容易实施，且在激怒日本海军当局方面能达到同样的效果。计划安排在陆战队总部附近实施，以便海军当局将此事件视为对海军的挑战并采取紧急措施，从而在上海造成混乱。
如果此信息属实，且南京当局发布的关于共产党人对汪精卫先生遇刺未遂案负责的声明有任何真实性，那么这两起案件之间可能存在某种联系。
然而，日本当局认为南京的声明不正确，并认为刺杀汪先生的企图是由国民党人或“CC系”（国民党内的一派）成员所为。
据日本领事警察称，中国共产党发表声明称，汪先生的袭击者孙凤鸣（Sung Fong Ming）不是共产党员，而是法西斯党成员。

Section 2, Special Branch XXXX
December 21, 38.

Murder of Japanese Sailor on Darroch and attempted assassination
of Wang Ching-wei.

In view of the fact that the late Warrant Officer
Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, who was
murdered on Darroch Road on November 9, was a person of
a gentle disposition and had an excellent record during
his period of service in the Navy, the Japanese Naval
Authorities and the Japanese Consular Police have come to
the conclusion that the motive of the murder could not be
attributed to any love intrigue or to an act of revenge or
robbery. The case must, therefore, be considered to
have a somewhat political background.

Several days prior to the murder of Nakayama, certain
Chinese communists with the object of furthering anti-
Japanese propaganda spread a rumour to the effect that the
outbreak of a second Sino-Japanese incident in Shanghai
was imminent, in view of the fact that a number of Chinese
soldiers in plain-clothes had secretly entered the Chinese
city while the Japanese were concentrating their forces
in the northern part of Shanghai. Their object was to
spread uneasiness amongst local Chinese so that they might
be able to seize upon the opportunity in expanding their
activities. As a result of this rumour considerable
uneasiness prevailed especially amongst Chinese residents
in Chapei. In order to make the people believe that there
was some truth in the rumour the Communists decided to
resort to an act of violence against the Japanese thereby
creating a tumultuous situation. With this object in view
they contemplated assassinating a high Japanese official.
Finding this difficult to carry out as all high officials
are well protected, they changed their original plan and

第二处，特别分支 XXXX
1938年12月21日。

达罗克路日本水兵被杀案及汪精卫遇刺未遂案。

鉴于11月9日在达罗克路被谋杀的日本海军陆战队准尉中山（Nakayama）性情温和，且在海军服役期间表现优异，日本海军当局和日本领事警察得出结论，认为谋杀动机不能归因于任何情感纠葛、报复或抢劫行为。因此，该案必须被视为具有一定的政治背景。

在中山被杀前几天，一些中国共产主义者为了推进反日宣传，散布谣言称，由于日军在上海北部集结兵力，而许多便衣中国士兵已秘密进入华界，上海即将爆发第二次中日事变。他们的目的是在当地中国人中制造不安，以便趁机扩大活动。受此谣言影响，人们感到相当不安，尤其是在闸北的中国居民中。为了让人们相信谣言有一定真实性，共产党人决定对日本人采取暴力行动，从而制造混乱局面。为此，他们策划刺杀一名日本高官。由于所有高官都受到严密保护，实施起来困难重重，他们改变了原计划，

pages.en:
decided to assassinate a Japanese sailor in uniform because
it would be much easier to undertake and the result obtainable
would be the same in provoking the Japanese Naval Authorities.
The plan was arranged to be carried out in the vicinity of
the Landing Party Headquarters so that the Naval Authorities
would regard the incident as a challenge against the Navy
and adopt emergency measures, thereby causing confusion in
Shanghai.

If this information is correct and if there is any
truth in the statement issued by the Nanking Authorities
that communists were responsible for the attempted assassination
of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, some connection between the two
cases may be regarded as possible.

The Japanese Authorities, however, are of the opinion
that Nanking's statement is incorrect and that the attempt
on the life of Mr. Wang was perpetrated either by
nationalists or by members of the "C.C. Party" (a faction
in the Kuomintang).

According to the Japanese Consular Police, the Chinese
Communist Party have issued a statement declaring that
Sung Fong Ming (孫鳳鳴), Mr. Wang's assailant, is not a
communist but a member of the Fascist Party.

决定刺杀一名身穿制服的日本水兵，因为这样更容易下手，且同样能达到激怒日本海军当局的目的。该计划安排在日本陆战队总部附近实施，以便让海军当局将此事件视为对海军的挑战并采取紧急措施，从而在上海造成混乱。

如果这一情报属实，且南京当局发布的关于共产党人对汪精卫先生遇刺未遂案负责的声明有任何真实性，那么这两起案件之间可能存在某种联系。

然而，日本当局认为南京的声明不正确，并认为刺杀汪先生的企图是由民族主义者或“CC系”（国民党内的一个派系）成员所为。

据日本领事警察称，中国共产党发表声明称，汪先生的袭击者孙凤鸣不是共产党人，而是法西斯党成员。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. .........
Special Branch Station,
REPORT
Date December 18 19 35.

Subject Albert K. de St. Chamas - visit to Police Headquarters regarding
the Nakayama Murder Case.

Made by and Forwarded by C.D.I. Grubb

In the morning of December 18, a Greek subject,
Albert K. de St. Chamas, who claimed to be a correspondent
for the Echo de Grece, called at Police Headquarters and
stated he might be of some assistance to the police in solving
the murder of the Japanese sailor on Darroch Road. When
questioned regarding any information he was in possession of
or assistance he could render to the police he suggested that
all the residents in the vicinity of the scene of the murder
should be placed on bail or security until one of them furnished
information leading to the arrest of the person or persons
responsible.

St. Chamas arrived in Shanghai on December 16
on board the s.s. President Doumer and will leave on the same
vessel for Japan this afternoon (December 18). Upon arrival
at the Central Wharf he saw a Reward Notice issued in connection
with the Nakayama Murder case and decided to call at Police
Headquarters as stated. He found his way to the offices of the
A.D. and was referred by Mr. Rendall of that Department to the
D.C. (Sp.Br.). He appeared to be quite sane and in the
absence of any ulterior motive, other than that of assisting the
police, he was informed that his suggestion would be recorded
and he was allowed to go.

（印：OFFICE OF COMMISSIONER OF POLICE CHANGHAI 19 DEC. 1935）

由 C.D.I. Grubb 制作并提交

12月18日上午，一名自称是《希腊回声报》（Echo de Grece）记者的希腊籍人士阿尔伯特·K·德·圣·查马斯来到警察总局，声称他可能协助警方侦破达罗克路日本水兵被杀案。当被问及他掌握的任何信息或能向警方提供的协助时，他建议将谋杀现场附近的所有居民予以保释或要求提供担保，直到其中一人提供导致逮捕责任人的线索为止。

圣·查马斯于12月16日乘坐“杜美总统号”轮船抵达上海，并将于今天下午（12月18日）乘同一艘船前往日本。他在中央码头到达时看到了与中山谋杀案有关的悬赏通告，遂决定按所述前往警察总局。他找到了助理处长（A.D.）办公室，该部门的伦德尔先生（Mr. Rendall）将其引荐至特别分支副处长（D.C. (Sp.Br.)）。他看起来神志清醒，且除了协助警方外没有其他潜在动机，因此被告知他的建议将被记录在案，随后获准离开。

Subject The shooting of a Japanese sailor on Darroch Road on 9.11.35.
Made by D.S.I. Coyne Forwarded by J.B.Ross D.I.

Acting on your instructions of November 27 to have
inquiries made on the subject of firearms in Shanghai of
the type used in the murder of the Japanese sailor named
Hideo Nukayama on Darroch Road on November 9, I obtained
from D. S. Ewens (Arms Identification Section) a list of
the numbers of eighty-eight Beretta pistols which have at
some time been licensed, and particulars of the licensees
from D.S. Oakley, Arms Licensing Section.
On going through these lists I discovered that one of
these Beretta pistols bore the manufacturer's number 241147
which is one figure above the gun used by the murderer which
bore the number 241146. Further examination of the documents
showed that Beretta Pistol 241147 was licensed by Fu Tse Tung
(傅子東). His address was given as No. 496B Rue Lafayette.
On inquiry, it was found he had left that address, but was
located after considerable difficulty at No. 80 Ming Tsung
(民壮路) Road, Kiangwan. On being interviewed Mr. Fu
confirmed the information given on his license application
form to the effect that he had obtained the pistol from one
Zee Ts Yien (修次行). Zee formerly lived in Shanghai,
and there is good reason to believe that he acted here as
the representative of the 28th Route Army of Szechuen.
Enquiries show that Zee is now Chief of the Financial
Department of the 45th Route Army in Chengtu, Szechuen. This
information has been obtained from his former chauffeur named
Hung Kuo Foong(洪高峯)with whom I got into communication
through the Traffic Office.
On going through my note book, I found that suspicion
was entertained in June 1932 that a motor car which was being

事由 1935年11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）发生的一名日本水兵被枪击案。
呈报人 副督察长 Coyne 转呈人 督察长 J.B.Ross

根据您11月27日的指示，就上海地区与11月9日在达罗克路谋杀名为Hideo Nukayama的日本水兵所用枪支类型相同的枪械进行调查，我从D. S. Ewens（枪械识别股）处获取了一份曾于某段时间获得执照的八十八支贝雷塔（Beretta）手枪的编号清单，并从D.S. Oakley（枪械执照股）处获取了持照人的详细资料。
在查阅这些清单时，我发现其中一支贝雷塔手枪的制造商编号为241147，比凶手所用枪支的编号241146大一位数。进一步查阅文件显示，编号为241147的贝雷塔手枪是由傅子東（Fu Tse Tung）申领执照的。其登记地址为拉斐德路496B号。
经查询，发现他已离开该地址，但经过多方周折，最终在江湾民壮路80号找到了他。在接受问询时，傅先生确认了其执照申请表中所提供的信息，即该手枪是从一名叫修次行（Zee Ts Yien）的人手中获得的。Zee此前居住在上海，且有充分理由相信他曾在此担任四川第28路军的代表。
调查显示，Zee现任四川成都第45路军财务处处长。这一信息是从他以前的司机洪高峯（Hung Kuo Foong）处获得的，我是通过交通股与他取得联系的。
在查阅我的笔记本时，我发现早在1932年6月就曾有人怀疑，一辆当时用于运送在穿越租界途中被盗鸦片的汽车属于Zee。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury. Monday, November 25, 1935

S.M.P. Criticized
In Slaying Case

Proof Said Conclusive
Killer Of Japanese
Was Not Chinese

While the Shanghai Municipal Police today reported there were no clues to even the nationality of the slayer of Hideo Nakayama, Japanese sailor, on Darroch Road on the night of November 9, the China Weekly Review, published by Mr. J. B. Powell, editorially declared that enough evidence has been uncovered for a definite statement that the killer was not a Chinese.

Under the heading of "Conspiracies and Frame-ups in the Nakayama Case," the Review charges that one witness, Kuo Ah-ling, who was taken in custody in the case, originally by the Japanese, told the First Special District Court that he had been "compelled" by his Nipponese inquisitors to say that he seen Nakayama killed by a Chinese. The court the Review says, suppressed this testimony.

No "Conclusive Evidence"

The Review admits there has been "no conclusive evidence" obtained in the case by the new "Special Political Branch" of the S.M.C. which was organized in consequence of the killing under the direction of Assistant Commissioner O. Robertson.

"However," the magazine continues, "all the evidence which was gathered, circumstantial and inconclusive as it might be, pointed away from the view that the slayer of Nakayama was a Chinese, and indicated that most probably it was one of Nakayama's own compatriots or possibly a Korean, who fired the fatal shots.

"Assistant Commissioner Robertson and his aids make no pretense of hoping to definitely clear up the mystery of the murder of Nakayama. And this is quite natural, for the one line of investigation which could prove fruitful is barred. They know perfectly well that efforts to locate the murderer among the Chinese population is a futile undertaking. Japanese officials are determined to fasten the crime upon a Chinese, if there is any possible way in which this can be done, and only lines of inquiry leading in that direction will be permitted by them....

Duty Of Police

Police there appears clearly to rest the elementary duty of blasting the Japanese frame-up by proclaiming publicly what they admit privately. Although with such evidence as they have, it may not be possible to assert that the killer of Nakayama was a Japanese, they are certainly able officially to express the conviction that the killed was not a Chinese."

Mr. Robertson today declined to make any comment on the China Weekly Review article, saying that it was an editorial and and journalists were entitled to draw conclusions but it was not his duty to express agreement or disagreement with them. He added that the police still maintained an "open mind" in the case.

According to Japanese reports, the Association of Japanese Street Unions today were sending a second letter, more strongly worded than the first, to the Shanghai Municipal Council with regard to protection of Japanese subjects here. The reply to the previous letter was not regarded as satisfactory.

The police said the letter had not yet come to their attention, but they pointed out that here was no sound reason for criticism of the protection now afforded, since there had been no anti-Japanese incidents of any consequence whatsoever in recent months excepting the slaying of the sailor and the throwing of bottles into a Japanese store on Nanking Road.

L
55 (Mr. Burke)
Please submit article in China Weekly Review
attach White and pass time.
J.H.G
27 NOV. 1935

《上海晚邮报与水星报》。1935年11月25日，星期一

工部局警务处在
杀人案中受批评

据称证据确凿
杀害日本人的凶手
并非中国人

尽管上海公共租界工部局警务处今日报告称，对于11月9日晚在达罗克路（Darroch Road）被杀的日本水手中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）一案，甚至连凶手的国籍都毫无线索，但由鲍威尔（J. B. Powell）先生出版的《密勒氏评论报》在社论中宣称，已发现足够的证据，可以明确断言凶手并非中国人。

该报以“中山案中的阴谋与栽赃”为标题，指控该案中被拘留的一名证人郭阿林（Kuo Ah-ling，音译）——最初由日本人拘捕——向第一特区法院陈述，他曾被日本审讯者“强迫”供称目睹一名中国人杀害了中山。该报称，法院压制了这一证词。

无“确凿证据”

该报承认，工部局新成立的“特别政治股”在该案中尚未获得“确凿证据”，该股系因应此次杀人案而在副总监O·罗伯逊（O. Robertson）的指导下组建的。

“然而，”该杂志继续写道，“所有收集到的证据，尽管可能是间接且不具结论性的，都指向相反的方向，即中山的凶手并非中国人，并表明极有可能是中山的一名同胞，或者可能是一名朝鲜人，开枪造成了致命伤害。

“副总监罗伯逊及其助手并不假装希望能彻底解开中山被杀之谜。这很自然，因为唯一可能富有成效的调查途径已被阻断。他们非常清楚，在中国人中寻找凶手是一项徒劳的努力。日本官员决心只要有任何可能的方式，就将罪行归咎于中国人，并且只允许朝这个方向进行的调查……

警察的职责

显然，警察的基本职责在于公开宣布他们私下承认的事实，从而粉碎日本的栽赃阴谋。虽然凭借他们目前掌握的证据，或许无法断言中山的凶手是日本人，但他们当然能够在官方层面表达这样一种确信：凶手并非中国人。”

罗伯逊先生今日拒绝对《密勒氏评论报》的文章发表评论，称那是一篇社论，记者有权得出结论，但他没有义务表示同意或不同意。他补充说，警方在此案中仍保持“开放的态度”。

据日本方面报道，日本街道工会联合会今日正致函上海公共租界工部局第二封信，措辞比第一封更为强烈，事关在此地的日本臣民的保护问题。此前信件的回复被认为不能令人满意。

警方表示，该信函尚未引起他们的注意，但他们指出，目前没有任何正当理由批评现在所提供的保护，因为近几个月来，除了这名水手被杀以及有人向南京路上一家日本商店投掷瓶子外，并未发生任何具有重大意义的反日事件。

November 28, 1935 THE CHINA WEEKLY REVIEW 409

Conspiracies and Frame-Ups in the Nakayama Case

CONSPIRACIES and frame-ups have always figured prominently in the arsenals of diplomats and their foreign offices, more especially in the case of countries embarked upon ambitious plans of empire building and territorial aggrandizement. The Japanese Foreign Office, and its representatives in China, have perhaps made more repeated and extensive use of this weapon in modern times, at least insofar as China is concerned, than has been the case with the foreign offices and diplomats of any other country. In the murder of Hideo Nakayama, Japanese marine, who was shot and killed on Darroch Road in the night of November 9, the elements both of conspiracy and frame-up have entered, the latter almost from the moment when the murder was perpetrated.

It became clear at the outset that the local Japanese diplomatic officials, in conjunction with the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party, intended to make the fullest possible use of the murder to bring pressure to bear upon the Nanking authorities in connection with the Fifth National Congress of the Kuomintang. The Japanese aim has been to raise a state of wild alarm, and thus to scare the Congress into sanctioning a policy favorable to Japan.

A brief recital of the events which followed the killing of Nakayama will suffice to indicate quite clearly, assuming that the murder was not instigated by the Japanese themselves, that the latter made the greatest possible use of the happening, just as they did in the case of the strange disappearance of vice-Consul Kurumoto in Nanking some months ago. The only known eye-witness of the killing, a Chinese employed in a shoe-maker's shop in the vicinity, declared that the murderer was dressed in clothing similar to that worn by Nakayama himself. If true, this would mean that Nakayama was killed by a fellow member of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party.

Immediately this assertion had been made, however, it was branded as a lie by the local Japanese authorities, notwithstanding the fact that no other eye-witnesses of the shooting had been discovered. Determined to disprove the wide-spread belief, based upon the first reports of the happening, that the murderer of Nakayama was a Japanese, the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party promptly laid hands on a Chinese alleyway sweep, Kuo Ah-ling, who worked close to the scene of the murder, and conveyed him to their barracks on Kiangwan Road, where he was detained for several days before being handed over to the Shanghai Municipal Police.

What happened to Kuo during the period that he was in the clutches of the Naval Landing Party has not hitherto been made public. The Shanghai Municipal Police, who received Kuo directly from the hands of the Japanese, know perfectly well what happened, but for the customary reasons of "good policy" have refrained from disclosing their information, except in private, confidential, "not for publication" conversations with newspaper reporters.

Kuo came into the hands of the Police Department of the International Settlement with visible marks of severe beatings on his body, beatings administered by the officers of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, who were interested, and who remain interested, in proving that the slayer of Nakayama was a Chinese. Kuo told the S.M.P. (Shanghai Municipal Police) that the beatings had been administered in an effort to get him to confess that he was the slayer of Nakayama. This, however, he refused to do, declaring that he was entirely innocent.

Failing to get a "confession" from Kuo that he was the killer, the officers of the Naval Landing Party decided that three-quarters of a loaf was better than none, and by continued beating finally succeeded in getting Kuo to state that he had witnessed the murder of Nakayama, and that the slayer who ran off into the dark was a Chinese.

Feeling that they had definitely gained something, the Naval Landing Party officers turned Kuo over to the Shanghai Municipal Police as the first "material witness" in the investigation of the slaying, and he was brought before the First Special District Court on November 15, where the S.M.P. asked that his detention be ordered for a period of one week while the investigation continued.

To the great discomfiture of the Japanese, however, Kuo stood up in Court and repudiated the statement made at the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party headquarters to the effect that he had witnessed the shooting of Nakayama, and that the slayer of the latter was a Chinese. Feeling safe now that he was out of the clutches of the notoriously brutal military men of Nippon, Kuo told the Court that he had been intensively questioned by officers of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party, and compelled to state that he had seen Nakayama killed and that the killer was a Chinese.

Notwithstanding this statement, which the Shanghai Municipal Police know to be completely true, Judge Hsiao ordered Kuo detained for one week as a "material witness," and the latter was marched off to the Ward Road Jail. To Chinese newspaper men in the court-room, Judge Hsiao issued a peremptory order, forbidding them to publish anything concerning the court proceedings.

Immediately following this farcical but highly revealing proceeding in the First Special District Court, the Shanghai Municipal Police Commissioner appointed one of his Assistant Commissioners, T. Robertson, to take charge of the investigation of the Nakayama murder. The responsibility, in the hands of this officer, who is well-known in the force for his ability and integrity, should result in a thorough and impartial inquiry which would bring to light the truth.

1935年11月28日 《密勒氏评论报》 第409页

中山案中的阴谋与栽赃

阴谋和栽赃历来在外交官及其外交部的武库中占据显著地位，尤其是在那些致力于雄心勃勃的帝国建设和领土扩张计划的国家中。就中国而言，日本外务省及其在华代表在现代或许比其他任何国家的外交部和外交官更频繁、更广泛地使用这种武器。在11月9日晚于达罗克路（Darroch Road）被枪杀的日本海军陆战队员中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）谋杀案中，阴谋和栽赃的因素均已介入，后者几乎从谋杀实施的那一刻起便开始了。

起初就很明显，当地日本外交官员与日本特别海军陆战队联手，意图充分利用这起谋杀案，就国民党第五次全国代表大会一事向南京当局施加压力。日本方面的目的是制造极度恐慌的状态，从而迫使大会批准一项有利于日本的政策。

简要回顾中山被杀后发生的事件，足以清楚地表明，假设谋杀并非由日本人自己唆使，那么他们最大限度地利用了这一事件，就像几个月前他们在南京副领事栗本（Kurumoto，音译）离奇失踪案中所做的那样。目前已知的唯一目击者是附近一家鞋店的一名中国雇员，他声称凶手穿着与中山本人相似的服装。如果属实，这意味着中山是被日本特别海军陆战队的一名同伴杀害的。

然而，这一说法刚一提出，立即被当地日本当局斥为谎言，尽管当时并未发现其他射击目击者。为了驳斥基于事件初期报告而广泛流传的认为中山凶手是日本人的看法，日本特别海军陆战队迅速抓获了一名在谋杀现场附近工作的中国巷弄清洁工郭阿林（Kuo Ah-ling，音译），并将他带至江湾路的兵营，在移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处之前，将他扣留了数天。

郭阿林在日本海军陆战队控制期间遭遇了什么，迄今尚未公之于众。直接从日本人手中接收郭阿林的上海公共租界工部局警务处完全清楚发生了什么，但出于通常的“政策考量”，除了在与报纸记者进行私下的、保密的、“不予发表”的谈话中外，一直避免披露其掌握的信息。

郭阿林进入国际租界警务处时，身上有明显的遭受严重殴打的痕迹，这些殴打是由日本海军陆战队军官实施的，他们有兴趣且至今仍有意证明中山的凶手是中国人。郭阿林告诉上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.），殴打是为了迫使他承认自己是中山的凶手。然而，他拒绝这样做，声称自己完全无辜。

由于未能从郭阿林那里得到他是凶手的“供认”，海军陆战队军官决定退而求其次，经过持续殴打，最终成功迫使郭阿林陈述他目睹了中山被杀，且逃入黑暗中的凶手是一名中国人。

海军陆战队军官觉得他们确实有所收获，便将郭阿林作为调查这起杀人案的第一位“重要证人”移交给上海公共租界工部局警务处。他于11月15日被提审至第一特区法院，警务处请求在他受审期间将其拘留一周，以便继续调查。

然而，令日本人极为尴尬的是，郭阿林在法庭上站起来，否认了他在日本特别海军陆战队总部所作的关于他目睹中山被枪杀且凶手是中国人的陈述。郭阿林感到自己现已脱离以残暴著称的日本军人的魔爪，便安全地告诉法庭，他受到了日本特别海军陆战队军官的严厉讯问，并被迫陈述他目睹中山被杀且凶手是中国人。

尽管上海公共租界工部局警务处知道这一陈述完全属实，萧法官仍命令将郭阿林作为“重要证人”拘留一周，随后他被押往华德路监狱。萧法官向法庭内的中国新闻记者发布了一项强制命令，禁止他们刊登任何有关法庭诉讼程序的内容。

在第一特区法院这场滑稽但极具揭示性的诉讼程序结束后，上海公共租界工部局警务总监任命其副总监之一T·罗伯逊（T. Robertson）负责中山谋杀案的调查。这项责任落在这位以能力和正直在警队中闻名的官员手中，应当会带来一次彻底且公正的调查，从而揭露真相。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY
File No. D. 70/3
No. S. B.
Special Branch
Date November 11, 1935

Subject Alleged Japanese demands to have been presented to the Chinese
Authorities in connection with murder of Japanese marine.

Made by and Forwarded by Supt. Tan Shao-liang.

Enquiries have been made at the City Government and
the Public Safety Bureau Headquarters as to whether any
demands, either verbal or written, have been presented by
the Japanese Authorities following the murder of a Japanese
sailor on Darroch Road on November 9. Replies in the
negative were received in both cases.

It appears that General Tsai Ching Chun, Commissioner
of P.S.B., who returned to Shanghai from Nanking by aeroplane
on account of the affair, called at the Japanese Marine
Headquarters, Kiangwan Road, on the morning of November 10
and expressed his condolence over the decease of the sailor.
The Japanese Commander is said to have stressed the importance
of the early arrest of the murderer by the Chinese Authorities.

It has been reported unofficially that about a
week ago Japanese Ambassador Mr. Ariyoshi had demanded an
explanation from the Nanking Government for the increase in
the defence force at places along the Shanghai-Nanking and
Shanghai-Hangchow-Ningpo Railways, but this information
could not be confirmed locally.

（印：OFFICE OF COMMISSIONER OF POLICE SHANGHAI 11 NOV. 1935）

Tan Shaoliang
Superintendent.

D. C. (Special Branch).

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES. NOVEMBER 10, 1935

Japanese Sailor Shot
In Darroch Road Last
Night By Unknown Man

Unidentified Chinese Escapes After Shooting
Victim From Behind; Japanese Naval Landing
Party Mobilizes And Patrols Boundary

SERIOUS VIEW OF INCIDENT IS TAKEN
BY JAPANESE AUTHORITIES

A serious incident, which caused a detachment of the Japanese Naval Landing Party to be mobilized last night, took place in Darroch Road, which runs from North Szechuen Road to Kiangwan Road, when a uniformed Japanese sailor was shot through the head and received fatal wounds by an unidentified Chinese who made his escape. The affair took place soon after nine o'clock, and up to an early hour this morning the assailant had not been caught, although Japanese marines, co-operating with the Shanghai Municipal police and the Public Safety Bureau of the Greater Shanghai Municipality, were making a thorough search of the district. A serious view of the matter is being taken by the Japanese authorities.

The following account was obtained from official sources by "The Shanghai Sunday Times" last night:

"A Japanese sailor in uniform was shot through the head on Darroch Road just before 9.30 this evening, by an unidentified Chinese who made his escape.

"The sailor was shot from behind, and as soon as the incident became known, the Japanese landing party immediately sent a detachment and, with the Municipal police and the Chinese police, put a special guard or cordon around the area.

"The Greater Shanghai authorities have been asked to take immediate measures to find the assailant.

"The Japanese authorities are taking a very serious view of the situation from the fact that the Japanese sailor was wearing uniform and must therefore have been the object of a deliberately premeditated attack.

"The Japanese Naval Landing Party and the Consulate have jointly asked for immediate measures from the City Government."

Sailor Succumbs

At 1.10 a.m. this morning the sailor, named Hideo Nakayama, passed away in the hospital of Naval Landing Party.

He was 23 years old and a native of Nara Prefecture. He was conscripted for military service at the Kure Naval Base.

Rumours have been persistent of late that a number of plain-clothes men from Chinese troops in the Shanghai area have been coming into Shanghai, and it is doubtless in view of this fact that the Japanese authorities are viewing the incident with grave concern.

Official Statement

The following official announcement was issued by the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party last right:

"Hideo Nakayama, sailor first class, was shot and fatally injured at about 9.30 o'clock to-
(Continued on Page 3, Col. 3.)

night when returning to the Special Naval Landing Party after liberty.

"Nakayama was shot at from the right side as he was proceeding along the left side sidewalk of Darroch Road. He suffered a bullet wound piercing his skull from the back of his neck.

"While we have no clue regarding the assailant, we consider this attack provocation directed at the Special Naval Landing Party.

"Not only shall we demand a thorough investigation by the Bureau of Public Safety, but we shall demand that a complete inquiry be made by the Shanghai Municipal Police.

"The Special Naval Landing Party was immediately mobilized and still remains on that footing."

（批：Supt. Ian,
Please clear up
points marked with
red pencil and
report.
JW
11 NOV. 1935）

《上海星期泰晤士报》。1935年11月10日

日本水手昨晚
在达罗路被不明身份者枪击

不明身份的中国人从背后开枪后逃逸；日本海军陆战队动员并巡逻边界

日本当局重视此事

昨晚发生了一起严重事件，导致日本海军陆战队分队动员，事发地点位于从北四川路延伸至江湾路的达罗路，一名身穿制服的日本水手头部中弹，受致命伤，行凶者为一名不明身份的中国人，随后逃逸。事件发生在九点后不久，直到今天凌晨早些时候，尽管日本海军陆战队与上海公共租界工部局警务处及大上海市公安局合作，对该地区进行了彻底搜查，但袭击者尚未被捕。日本当局正严肃看待此事。

《上海星期泰晤士报》昨晚从官方渠道获得如下报道：

“今晚9点30分之前，一名身穿制服的日本水手在达罗路被一名不明身份的中国人击中头部，该行凶者随后逃逸。

“水手是从背后被枪击的，事件发生后，日本陆战队立即派出一支分队，并与工部局警察和中国警察一起，在该区域周围设立了特别警卫或封锁线。

“已要求大上海当局采取即时措施寻找袭击者。

“鉴于该日本水手身穿制服，因此必然是蓄意预谋攻击的目标，日本当局正非常严肃地看待这一局势。

“日本海军陆战队和领事馆已联合要求市政府采取即时措施。”

水手身亡

今天凌晨1点10分，名为中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）的水手在日本海军陆战队医院去世。

他年仅23岁，奈良县人。他在吴淞海军基地应征入伍。

最近一直有传言称，上海地区中国军队的一些便衣人员进入上海，毫无疑问，鉴于这一事实，日本当局正严重关切地看待此事件。

官方声明

日本特别海军陆战队昨晚发布了以下官方公告：

“一等水兵中山秀夫在今晚约9点30分外出休假返回特别海军陆战队途中遭枪击，受致命伤。
（续第3栏第3页。）

“中山在沿达罗路左侧人行道行进时，从右侧遭到射击。他颈部后方中弹，子弹穿透头骨。

“虽然我们对袭击者毫无线索，但我们认为此次攻击是针对特别海军陆战队的挑衅。

“我们不仅将要求公安局进行彻底调查，还将要求上海公共租界工部局警务处进行全面调查。

“特别海军陆战队已立即动员，并保持此状态。”

（批注：Ian 警司，
请澄清
用红铅笔标记的
要点并报告。
JW
1935年11月11日）

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL
SPECIAL BRANCH, REGIST.
No. B.D. 2970.

Shooting of a Japanese Sailor on Darroch Road.

Inquiries instituted as a result of a telephone message
received at the Dixwell Road Police Station at 9.05 p.m.
November 9, led to the discovery that a 1st class seaman
sailor named Hideo Yokoyama, age 24, belonging to the Japanese
Naval Landing Party, had been shot in the head, while
walking along Fong Loh Li (豐樂里). The sailor was on
liberty at the time. The victim fell at a point about
eight feet from the curb on the West of the street. A
spent bullet and an empty cartridge were discovered in the
immediate vicinity of the spot, and a .32 calibre automatic
pistol was found hidden behind a watchman's sentry box about
200 yards away. This watchman's sentry box is in Fong Loh Li
(豐樂里), which leads from Darroch Road to North Szechuen Road
Extension and is about eighty yards from the latter street. The
pistol was of Beretta make. It had one round in the breech
and five in the magazine. The victim was removed by the
Japanese Naval Landing Party to their hospital, where
according to the report received from the Japanese Naval
Landing Party's Medical Officer, he died at 1.10 a.m.
November 10.

Shortly after the shooting, a Chinese, named
Woo Ziang Woo (胡祥和), reported at the Dixwell Road
Station that at 9 p.m. on November 9 he was about to enter
No.90 Darroch Road, when he heard the report of a gun.
He immediately looked in the direction of the sound and
saw a man wearing dark coloured long trousers and a short
jacket, who was running, turn East into the Fong Loh Li.
He almost simultaneously saw another man lying on the roadway.
He reported the incident to a Japanese residing at No.90
Darroch Road, and they both proceeded to the scene and found
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局
特别科，登记处。
编号 B.D. 2970。

达罗路日本水手被枪击案。

根据11月9日晚9点05分狄思威路警察局接到的电话消息所开展的调查，发现一名隶属于日本海军陆战队、名为横山秀夫（Hideo Yokoyama，原文如此，应为中山秀夫之误）、24岁的一等水兵，在沿丰乐里行走时头部中弹。该水手当时正在休假。受害者倒在街道西侧距路缘约八英尺处。在现场附近发现了一枚射出的子弹和一个空弹壳，并在约200码外的一个更夫岗亭后面发现了一支隐藏的.32口径自动手枪。该更夫岗亭位于丰乐里，该弄堂从达罗路通往北四川路延伸段，距离后者街道约八十码。该手枪为贝雷塔（Beretta）制造。枪膛内有一发子弹，弹匣内有五发。受害者被日本海军陆战队送往其医院，根据从日本海军陆战队医务官处收到的报告，他于11月10日凌晨1点10分死亡。

枪击发生后不久，一名名为胡祥和（Woo Ziang Woo）的中国人在狄思威路警察局报案称，11月9日晚9点，他正准备进入达罗路90号时，听到了一声枪响。他立即朝声音方向看去，看到一个穿着深色长裤和短夹克的男子在奔跑，向东转入丰乐里。他几乎同时看到另一个人躺在马路上。他将此事报告给居住在达罗路90号的一名日本人，两人随即前往现场，发现

pages.en:
- 2 -

that the man lying on the roadway was a Japanese sailor.
The Japanese Naval Landing Party, on receipt
of the information, mobilised and sent out strong patrols
and posted men in the vicinity.
On the instructions of D.O. "C", special precautions
were taken by the police.
It has been discovered that the spent bullet
found near the dead man was fired from the pistol found
in the Fong Loh Li.
The situation in the vicinity of North Szechuen
Road Extension and Darroch Road this morning is outwardly
quiet. Armed ratings of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party are posted at intervals of about 50 yards, along
Darroch Road and along North Szechuen Road Extension from
Darroch Road to the Japanese Naval Barracks on Kiangwan Road.
The scene of the shooting is guarded by a dozen men.
Between 60 and 70 Chinese residents are reported
to have removed from the vicinity of Darroch Road following
the shooting of the sailor.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

躺在马路上的人是一名日本水手。
日本海军陆战队接到消息后，
动员并派出强力巡逻队，
并在附近部署了人员。
根据“C”区巡官的指示，
警方采取了特别预防措施。
经查实，在死者附近发现的射出子弹
是从丰乐里发现的手枪中发射的。
今天上午，北四川路延伸段和达罗路附近的局势
表面平静。日本海军陆战队的武装水兵
沿达罗路以及从达罗路到江湾路日本海军兵营的
北四川路延伸段，每隔约50码部署一人。
枪击现场由十余人守卫。
据报道，在水手被枪击后，
约有60至70名中国居民
从达罗路附近搬离。

in the magazine. The victim was removed by the Japanese
Naval Landing Party to their hospital, where according to the
report received from the Japanese Naval Landing Party's Medical
Officer, he died at 1.10 a.m. November 10.

Ziang Woo (胡祥和), reported at the Dixwell Road Station that
at 9 p.m. on November 9 he was about to enter No.90 Darroch

looked in the direction of the sound and saw a man wearing
dark coloured long trousers and a short jacket, who was running,
turn East into the Fong Loh Li. He almost simultaneously saw
another man lying on the roadway. He reported the incident
to a Japanese residing at No.90 Darroch Road, and they both
proceeded to the scene and found that the man lying on the

达罗路日本水手被枪击案

根据11月9日晚9点05分狄思威路警察局接到的电话消息所开展的调查，发现一名隶属于日本海军陆战队、名为 Kideo Makoyama（原文如此，应为 Hideo Nakayama 之误）、24岁的日本一等水兵，在沿丰乐里（ 豐樂里 ）行走时头部中弹。该水手当时正在休假。受害者倒在街道西侧距路缘约八英尺处。在现场附近发现了一枚射出的子弹和一个空弹壳，并在约200码外的一个更夫岗亭后面发现了一支隐藏的.32口径自动手枪。该更夫岗亭位于丰乐里（        ），该弄堂从达罗路通往北四川路延伸段，距离后者街道约八十码。该手枪为贝雷塔（Beretta）制造。枪膛内有一发子弹，弹匣内有五发。受害者被日本海军陆战队送往其医院，根据从日本海军陆战队医务官处收到的报告，他于11月10日凌晨1点10分死亡。

枪击发生后不久，一名名为胡祥和（Woo Ziang Woo）的中国人在狄思威路警察局报案称，11月9日晚9点，他正准备进入达罗路90号时，听到了一声枪响。他立即朝声音方向看去，看到一个穿着深色长裤和短夹克的男子在奔跑，向东转入丰乐里。他几乎同时看到另一个人躺在马路上。他将此事报告给居住在达罗路90号的一名日本人，两人随即前往现场，发现躺在马路上的人

2. 受害者是正在接受短期训练的应征入伍者，还是将大日本帝国海军服役作为职业？
他是一名正在服四年兵役的应征入伍者。

3. 受害者在海军服役多久？加入海军前的身份和生活状况如何？
1932年1月加入海军。去世时军衔为一等水兵，死后被追晋为三等兵曹长。

4. 受害者是否从事常规勤务以外的任务？如果是，这些任务的性质是什么？
否。

5. 在试图发现共产党人、朝鲜革命者等的行动中，受害者是否曾被用作诱饵？
否。

6. 受害者在上海待了多久？
1933年9月29日调至日本海军陆战队。

7. 他在以下群体中最好的朋友是谁：(a) 日本海军陆战队；(b) 一般日本侨民社区？
(a) 一等水兵青木正雄 (Masao Aoki)。
(b) 坂井千代小姐 (Miss Chito Sakai)，24岁，住北四川路美眉里27号。她于10月返回日本结婚。

8. 除日本人外，受害者是否有其他朋友？如果有，他们是谁？
无。

他的记录良好。
他性格文静，没有任何弱点。
他没有卷入任何感情纠葛。他不酗酒，但也并非滴酒不沾。

10. 休假时他通常和谁一起外出？去哪里？
休假时他通常独自外出，光顾日本的娱乐场所和剧院。

取消。未来将再次实施此规定。

当天是星期六，休假时间从下午12点15分开始，至晚上11点结束。

他于下午12点15分离开营房，下午4点返回。最后一次在营房见到他是下午5点。

14. 他是独自一人还是有人陪同？

他是独自一人。

15. 他去了哪里？

他去了北四川路美眉里33号的娱乐场所“白月” (Baigetsu)，以及同一条弄堂27号的“kowu”。

16. 医生能否说明开枪时枪手离受害者有多近？
枪口距离受害者头部在50毫米以内。

17. 子弹是从受害者前方还是后方射入的？
一颗子弹是从受害者后方射入的。

18. 两发子弹是否来自同一方向？
其中一发是从后方射出的。

19. 声称目睹枪击事件的那名中国人的背景如何？
吴祥伟 (Woo Ziang We)，通州人，1910年出生，农民之子。1923年来到上海。此后曾在多家日本鞋店工作，起初是学徒，后来成为工人。1934年5月，他在宝兴东路62号开设了自己的作坊。他通过承接日本鞋匠的订单谋生，其中包括达罗克路90号的高冈先生 (Mr. Takaoka)，他在11月9日晚曾拜访过高冈先生。

20. 他被日本人雇佣了多久？他会说日语吗？
他被日本鞋匠雇佣了11年。他的日语讲得很好。

21. 他的日本雇主是谁？
目前他承接达罗克路90号 J. Takaoka 的订单，但并非其雇员。

22. 该雇主在上海从事什么业务？
J. Takaoka 的职业是鞋匠。

获准进入日本海军陆战队营房的日本商人居住在枪击现场附近。

To Detectives,
Sirs,
I beg to secretly report that the instigators of the
assassination of Mr. Ss were one Li Zung Sung and his son
Ts Nyoh. The persons who took actual part in the shooting
of Mr. Ss Liang Tsai (General Manager of the Shanghai Times)
were paid by Li and his son. The motive for the murder was
that Li and his son wished to take hold of the shares of the
Hwa Fung Tobacco Co., belonging to Mr. Ss. They are not
arrested and it is learned that they were also concerned in
the shooting of the Japanese marine (Hideo Nakayama) during
November, 1935.
Hoping that you will put them under arrest.
They are residing at No. 30 Yoong Tsong Li, E. Seward
Road, and the proprietors of the Yoeng Doong Tshang Hardware
shop.
Anonymous.

Translation of Precis of anonymous letter.

December 22, 1935.

To
The Commissioner of Police,
Shanghai Municipal Council.

Sir,

Liu Ts Yuan residing in a rear upstairs room of House No. 66
(one Mr. Chao also resides in an upstairs room of that house), Ta
Yang Miao Road, Chapei, is a bandit chief and responsible for many
armed robberies. Lu Ah Seong residing in a straw hut in the West
of the Ta Hsing Market is wanted by the authorities. On a certain
day in May, if not in June, one Koo Wen T'ung was assaulted at the
corner of Markham and Wuting Roads. The aforesaid Liu was
instigator of the assault. The shooting of Nakayama, a Japanese,
was perpetrated by a follower surnamed Chen of Liu. On that day
3 persons planned to proceed to North Szechwan Road and attempted
to commit an armed robbery there. They passed the Feng Leh Li
Alleyway and urinated. Seeing that they did not speak Japanese,
the Japanese assaulted them badly. The aforesaid Chen became so
angry that he shot the assailant with a pistol. Liu loaned him
(Chen) $10 and told him to leave for Kempo. He is a native of
Kan Ho Pang, Liu Chin Kiu. For this reason it is very difficult
to locate him in Shanghai. They have altogether 4 pistols, two
of them being purchased at $67. Where did they obtain the
remainder, no one has the knowledge. Liu Ts Yuan is a follower
of Wang Kuei Chang and P'an Kin Ch'u. They know the officials at
the Bureau?. The case can never be brought to light if you do not
effect the arrest of the above persons which should be promptly
carried out between 4 a.m. and 5 a.m.

Not signed.

Translator's note : The letter itself is illiterate.
pages.zh:
匿名信摘要译文。

1935 年 12 月 22 日。

致
上海公共租界工部局
警务处处长。

先生：

居住在闸北大阳庙路（Ta Yang Miao Road，音译）66 号楼上后间的刘子元（该楼上也住着一位赵先生）是一名匪首，犯有多起武装抢劫案。居住在大兴市场西侧草棚内的罗阿松正被当局通缉。五月（若非六月）某日，古文通（Koo Wen T'ung，音译）在马克姆路（Markham Road，即斐伦路）与吴同路（Wuting Road，音译）转角处遭到殴打。前述刘某是此次殴打的指使者。日本人中山（Nakayama）遭枪击一事，系刘的一名姓陈的追随者所为。当日有三人计划前往北四川路并试图在那里实施武装抢劫。他们经过丰乐里弄堂时小便。日本人见他们不说日语，便猛烈殴打他们。前述陈某怒不可遏，用手枪射击了袭击者。刘借给陈 10 元钱，并让他前往肯波（Kempo，音译）。他是甘河浜（Kan Ho Pang，音译）人，刘金球（Liu Chin Kiu，音译）。因此很难在上海找到他。他们共有四支手枪，其中两支是以 67 元购买的。其余两支从何而来，无人知晓。刘子元是王桂昌（Wang Kuei Chang，音译）和潘金楚（P'an Kin Ch'u，音译）的追随者。他们认识局里的官员吗？若不逮捕上述人员，此案永远无法揭露，逮捕行动应在凌晨 4 点至 5 点之间迅速执行。

未署名。

译者注：信件本身文理不通。

pages.en:
Chief Inspector, Dixwell Road Police Station.

It is learned that the disguised assassin of Kideo
Nakayama of the J.M.L.Party was one named Ah Nyi, who is a
private ricksha puller employed by Mr. Lai of the Fuk Sing Silk
Store at 436 Bung Teng Loong, Peking Road.

He is hiding in the French Concession during the
night, and working in the day as usual.

He is in possession of one "Man Ling" loaded
pistol, which he carries in his small short jacket pocket.
Precautions are to be taken at the time of arrest.

(Sd) Lee Zeu Ngno.
Confidential Informer.

pages.en:
Translation

Japanese Consular Police,
Shanghai.

Sir,

I beg to bring to your notice all that I know regarding the incident in which Seaman Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party was murdered by shooting.

Since the incident occurred, people have become uneasy as to what will become of Shanghai. Owing to the case being still left in abeyance, uncivilized people have reated unfounded rumours, which resulted in the evacuation of people and removal to safe places to keep off the unforeseen misfortune.

Originally China and Japan are nations of the same race, and all over the countries, the two characters, "Shin Zen" (amity) are longed for. It is indeed a matter of great regret that such an incident took place.

All concerned are taking a serious view of the case, and the police have started investigations in an effort to bring to light the murderer at any cost, offering a reward of $1,000.00.

When this incident happened at about 9 p.m. on the 9-11-35, I happened to be passing along Fong Loh Li, Barroch Road. I heard two shots and had a glimpse of a figure dressed in black foreign clothes. He looked panic-stricken. He crossed the road and hurried away.

I, out of curiosity, shadowed him to Henan and Weechang Roads corner, where he was lost sight of. Subsequently, I, on business, passed Foo Shan Road and, on coming to Tiendong Road, saw the man again. At this time, he was arguing with a hawker and doing violence against him at a small market. I approached and stopped the trouble, whereupon, he walked away. I followed him again, and traced him to a food stall situated in Chapee Lee, Chapee Road. He was sitting at the stall and chatting with the stall-keeper. I then returned to the market and, getting in touch with the hawker, asked him if he knew the man dressed in black foreign clothes. He said that the man was a mastermind rogue with a number of followers, swindling and blackmailing for living, and all innocent neighbours are afraid of him.
pages.zh:
译文

日本驻上海领事馆警察。

先生：

谨将本人所知关于日本海军陆战队水兵中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）遭枪杀一案之情形，呈报钧鉴。

自案发以来，民众对上海之前途深感不安。由于本案至今悬而未决，无知之徒散布毫无根据之谣言，致使民众纷纷撤离，迁往安全之地，以避不测之祸。

中日两国本属同文同种之邦，举国上下皆渴望“亲善”二字。竟发生如此事件，实为极大之憾事。

有关各方均高度重视此案，警方已展开调查，不惜一切代价务求查明凶手，并悬赏一千元。

本案发生于1935年11月9日晚9时许，当时本人正途经百老汇路（Barroch Road）之丰乐里（Fong Loh Li）。忽闻两声枪响，瞥见一身穿黑色西式服装之人影。此人神色惊慌，横穿马路后匆匆离去。

本人出于好奇，尾随其至河南路与武昌路转角处，随后失去其踪迹。此后，本人因公务经过福山路，行至天潼路时，再次见到该人。此时，他正在一个小市场内与一小贩争吵并施以暴力。本人上前制止纠纷，随后该人离去。本人再次尾随，追踪至乍浦路乍浦里（Chapee Lee, Chapee Road）的一处食品摊。他正坐在摊位上与摊主聊天。本人随即返回市场，联系那名小贩，询问其是否认识那名身穿黑色西式服装的男子。小贩称，此人乃是一伙恶棍之首，手下有多名追随者，靠诈骗和勒索为生，周围无辜邻居皆对其畏惧三分。

pages.en:
- 2 -

I continued my enquiries amongst vendors and hawkers living
in Lien Oen Lee, off Chapoo Road, and Yih Woo Lee, off Woochang Road,
and eventually learned that the man had recently obtained a large sum
of money by obtaining a reward participating in a big serious case, and
further that the aforesaid stall-keeper and a sweet potato vendor in
the same alleyway were his accomplices.

I invited one of the neighbours and treated him to wine, who
said that if he had no mother and wife he would go to the Police and
obtain reward of $1,000.00. At first he hesitated but finally he
exposed the identity of the following three men :-

1. Dar Kwei Ding (          ), alias Lao Hsiang (          )
   living in Yih Woo Lee off Woochang Road.

2. Tsu Nyo Ling (          ), alias Sieu Nan King (          ),
   belonging to Tsing Peng (          ) Party, sweet potato vender
   living in Yih Woo Lee, Woochang Road.

3. Lee Lih Kin (          ), alias Kyo Chah (          ),
   food stall keeper, living in Chapoo Lee, Chapoo Road.

I respectfully suggest that you will detail alert officers,
preferably plain clothes men.

Were it not for my old mother and profession, I should like to
go to the Police. I now inform this as an obligation as a citizen
for the benefit of the public, therefore, I do not wish to obtain the
reward.

What I want is only the restoration of the friendly relations
between the two countries.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

本人继续在乍浦路联恩里（Lien Oen Lee）及武昌路益武里（Yih Woo Lee）的商贩和小贩中进行查访，最终获悉该人近期因参与一起重大案件而获得一笔巨额赏金，且上述摊主及同弄堂内的一名红薯小贩均为其同伙。

本人邀请其中一名邻居饮酒，该人称，若非家有老母妻室，定当前往警局领取一千元赏金。起初他尚存犹豫，但最终还是揭发了以下三人的身份：

1. 丁达贵（Dar Kwei Ding）（音译），别名老相（Lao Hsiang）（音译），
   居住于武昌路益武里。

2. 朱友林（Tsu Nyo Ling）（音译），别名小南京（Sieu Nan King）（音译），
   系青帮（Tsing Peng）（音译）成员，红薯小贩，
   居住于武昌路益武里。

3. 李立金（Lee Lih Kin）（音译），别名乔查（Kyo Chah）（音译），
   食品摊主，居住于乍浦路乍浦里。

本人谨建议派遣警觉性高的警员，最好便衣人员前往侦查。

若非顾及家母及职业，本人本欲亲自前往警局。现出于公民义务及公共利益考量特此举报，故无意领取赏金。

本人所求者，唯愿两国友好关系得以恢复。

Special Political Section,
Hongkew
December 5th, 1935.

Sir,

I beg to report that the local Japanese Consular Police
received a telephone message from Mr. Gejo, manager of the
Shanghai Branch of the "Dempo Tsushinsha" (telegraphic news
agency) to the effect that the latter was anonymously informed
by telephone on the 23-11-35 that the murder of the sailor of
the Naval Landing Party was a Cantonese one named Dong (唐)
living at No. 503 Jukong Road, Chapei.

The message was in Chinese, and the informant added that
he would require half of the reward in case the above person
was arrested.

Japanese Consular Police have, acting on this information
conducted brief enquiries and ascertained that the ground floor
of the said premises was a barber's shop known as "Kwong Hua"
(廣華) but failed to obtain any information as to the identity
of the persons living on the upper floors.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
Sd. Nakamura
J.D.S.I.

特别政治科，
虹口
1935年12月5日。

先生：

谨报告，当地日本领事馆警察接到“电通社”（Dempo Tsushinsha，电讯新闻机构）上海分社经理Gejo先生的电话消息，称后者于1935年11月23日匿名接到电话通知，杀害海军陆战队水兵的凶手是一名广东人，姓唐（Dong），居住在闸北菊康路503号。

该消息为中文，举报人并称，若上述人员被捕，他将要求分得一半赏金。

日本领事馆警察据此情报进行了简要查访，查明该址底层为一家名为“广华”（Kwong Hua）的理发店，但未能获取楼上居住者的身份信息。

此致
敬礼
中村（Nakamura）谨上
日本侦探特别调查员（J.D.S.I.）

pages.en:
Hongkew Police Station
Dec.9th.1935

Sir,

With reference to the anonymous telephone message
received by the local Japanese Consular Police to the effect
that the murderer of Seaman Hideo Nakayama was residing at
503 Jukong Road, Chapel, enquiries made of the two Formosans
living at the above address by the undersigned with the assist-
ance of Sergeant Suzukawa of the Japanese Consular Police re-
vealed nothing of an incriminating nature against them who
are registered at the Consulate as local Japanese residents.

Their statements are as follows:-

1    Name Fu So Ten, age 23,
     Permanent address:- 135/1 Baramon, Kokosho,
     Shinchiku-Gun, Shinchiku-Shu, Formosa.
     I had been apprenticed at a certain Japanese Hos-
pital in Yingkow, Manchukuo, until August 1934, when
I came to Shanghai in order to enter the "Tung Nan"
Medical College, and have since been preparing at home.
Whole expenses are furnished by my brother in Formosa.
     On the 9-11-35 at about 5 p.m. I, in company with
a friend of mine named Rin Ki Ko, Formosan student in
the 5th.year class of the above mentioned college,
visited a Chinese shop on Foochow Road and purchased a
gramophone, thence visited the "Sakas Shokai" at Boons
and Chapee Roads corner and purchased several Japanese
gramophone records. We then visited the "Suzukake" Cafe
on Chapee Road and, obtaining drinks there, left for
home at about 10.30 p.m. When I arrived at home, my
inmate, Ryu Gyoku Bai, had already in bed. I was un-
aware of the incident until I read the Chinese newspaper
"Shing Pao" on the following morning with my inmate.
pages.zh:
虹口警察局
1935年12月9日

先生：

关于当地日本领事馆警察收到的匿名电话消息，称杀害水兵中山秀雄的凶手居住在乍浦路（Chapel，原文误植，应为Chapei/闸北或具体路名，此处依上下文指代前文地址）菊康路503号一事，本人在日本领事馆警察铃川（Suzukawa）巡长的协助下，对居住于上述地址的两名台湾人进行了问询，未发现任何针对他们的罪证，此二人在领事馆注册为在沪日本居民。

他们的陈述如下：

1    姓名：傅佐天（Fu So Ten）（音译），年龄23岁，
     永久住址：台湾新竹州新竹郡湖口庄巴拉门135/1 Baramon, Kokosho, Shinchiku-Gun, Shinchiku-Shu, Formosa（音译）。
     我曾在满洲国营口的一家日本医院当学徒，直至1934年8月，
     我来到上海，进入“东南”医学院就读，此后一直在家备考。
     所有费用均由我在台湾的兄长提供。
     1935年11月9日下午5时许，我与我的朋友、上述学院五年级学生、台湾人林基高（Rin Ki Ko）（音译）一同，
     前往福州路的一家中国商店购买了一台留声机，随后前往博恩路（Boons）与乍浦路转角的“坂井商会”（Sakas Shokai）（音译）购买了几张日本留声机唱片。之后我们前往乍浦路的“铃悬”咖啡馆（Suzukake Cafe）（音译）饮用饮料，并于晚上10点30分左右回家。当我到家时，我的室友刘玉梅（Ryu Gyoku Bai）（音译）已经就寝。直到第二天早上我与室友阅读中文报纸《申报》（Shing Pao）时，才得知此事。

pages.en:
2
Name:- Ryu Gyoku Bai, age 27,
Permanent address:- 51 Katokyaku, Hori,
Horigai, Noko-Gun, Taichu-Shu, Formosa.
I came to Shanghai in August 1934 and entered
the "Tung Tuh" Medical College and have since been
studying there with the expenses furnished by my
parents in Formosa.
On the 9-11-35 at 2 p.m.I returned from the
College and, reading books until about 8 p.m.at home,
went to bed. At 7 a.m.on the following day, I went
to Hongkew Park for a morning stroll, and on my way
home I bought a Chinese newspaper, "Shing Pao" and
knew the incident.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
J.D.S.I.
pages.zh:
2
姓名：刘玉梅（Ryu Gyoku Bai）（音译），年龄27岁，
永久住址：台湾台中州能高郡堀街堀51 Katokyaku, Hori, Horigai, Noko-Gun, Taichu-Shu, Formosa（音译）。
我于1934年8月来到上海，进入“同济”医学院（原文为Tung Tuh，疑为Tongji之误或特定译名，此处保留音译对应）就读，此后一直在此学习，费用由我在台湾的父母提供。
1935年11月9日下午2点，我从学院回家，在家读书至晚上8点左右，随后就寝。次日早上7点，我去虹口公园晨练，在回家途中买了一份中文报纸《申报》，从而得知此事。

此致
敬礼
日本侦探特别调查员（J.D.S.I.）

December 2, 19 35
Diary Number: - 12/1 Nature of Offence: - 1
Time at which investigation begun and concluded each day

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
Resume of statements and diaries.
Witness Woo Xiang Woo at about 9 p.m. on the 2-11-35 was about to enter No. 90 Darroch Road, a shoemaker's shop owned by one Takaoka. This witness heard the sound of an explosion to the North of him, he immediately turned his head in the direction and observed a man wearing dark coloured clothing, a short jacket and long trousers and leather boots running from the centre of the Darroch Road East into the Feng Lah Li. Simultaneously he observed a man also wearing dark coloured clothing lying in the roadway.
Woo Xiang Woo immediately informed Takaoka who was inside No. 90 Darroch Road, whom he knows and whom he has worked for. They both went to the scene and found a Japanese sailor lying wounded in the roadway.
Regarding the description of the man who was seen running away from the scene, Woo Xiang Woo, although questioned many times during the enquiry, has adhered to the fact that the man he saw was wearing the apparel described above. Takaoka corroborated Woo Xiang Woo inasmuch as that Woo reported to him and that he accompanied him to the scene, prior to which whilst Takaoka was playing a gramophone in his house he heard the sound of an explosion which he took to be the bursting of a tyre. Woo Xiang Woo stated he only saw rickshas, coolies with their rickshas near the scene after the shooting.

吴祥武立即通知了在高岗店内、他认识并曾为其工作的高岗。两人一同前往现场，发现一名日本水兵受伤躺在马路上。
关于对逃离现场男子的描述，尽管在调查期间多次受询，吴祥武仍坚持称其所见男子穿着上述衣物。高岗证实了吴祥武的说法，因为吴向他报告并陪同他前往现场，在此之前，高岗在家中播放留声机时听到一声爆炸声，他以为是轮胎爆裂。吴祥武称，枪击发生后，他只看到现场附近有黄包车和拉车的苦力。

Furthermore after seeing the sailor lying in the roadway she ran through a hot water shop where there were many Chinese, into Wing On Terrace. She did not speak to any of the Chinese in the hot water shop, this again would appear not to be the truth.

Taking into consideration the statements made by Woo Ziang Woo which has not been shaken and if the statement of Poo Chan Ying is true it seems impossible that Woo Ziang Woo should not have seen the sailor and the civilian who were walking in the same direction as he was when approaching No. 90 Darroch Road. No. 90 Darroch Road is within the distance of 108 feet from the scene.

Comparing the intelligence of the two witnesses, Woo Ziang Woo and Poo Chan Ying, the former is far more intelligent than the latter. The witness Woo Ziang Woo is still available whereas the witness Poo Chan Ying, although permanently employed by a Japanese family before the affair, has since left Shanghai for her native place.

Woo Ziang Woo and Poo Chan Ying are the only two persons that have been obtained who were near the scene in the roadway.

比较两名证人吴祥武和鲍灿英的智力水平，前者远高于后者。证人吴祥武目前仍可找到，而证人鲍灿英虽然在事发前受雇于一个日本家庭，但此后已离开上海返回原籍。

吴祥武和鲍灿英是仅有的两名被找到的、案发时在马路现场附近的人员。

T. Yoshida states that he was walking and pushing his bicycle East in the Fong Leh Li and when a few yards West of the watchman's hut he heard a slight sound which he could not place. He walked on until a few yards past the watchman's hut and then decided to retrace his steps to a sweet shop called Omeri, he turned his bicycle round and after walking a few paces mounted his bicycle and rode at a speed a little faster than a walking pace. Between the watchman's hut and the Omeri sweet shop he states he met two men dressed in Chinese long gowns, walking separately Eastward in the Fong Leh Li on the South pavement. He could not state the colour of the gowns other than that they were not white. Both men were walking leisurely. When Yoshida arrived at the 9th alleyway in the Fong Leh Li near the Darroch Road entrance he gave up the idea of going to the sweet shop and decided to return home via the Darroch Road. On approaching Darroch Road he observed a crowd gathered which included several Japanese and Tibetans on the Darroch Road standing near the sailor lying in the roadway. Yoshida cannot remember seeing any Chinese constables there. Yoshida's statement is of little material value to the crime as his first intimation of the incident was when he saw the crowd gathered on the Darroch Road. Further material statement of Mayuko of the Koma Establishment, 27 Mei Ho Li off the North Szechuen Road, shows definitely that the deceased had been a regular visitor there and left the place some where in the region of 8.40 p.m. on the 9-11-35 and that she can be said to have been the last person to have seen deceased alive as no other witnesses have been obtained to discredit this. She saw him leave the establishment in a normal condition carrying a bundle which it was learned later to contain Japanese rice cakes etc. and stated by the Japanese Naval Landing Party to have been found lying by the side of R. Nakayama in the road. These cakes and a letter found on his person having been given to him by Koyo Sasaki of 23 Mei Ho Li to deliver to seaman Aoki.

Regarding the past life of deceased it has been proved that he had a "steady" in the Koma Establishment in the person of one Chito who it is said completed her contract with the house and left for Japan on the 30th September, 1935. Mayuko in one instance said she had no "regular man" and yet in a revised statement taken in the presence of the S.P.O. and Mr. Uyehara, A.C.P., she admitted having connections with a seaman named Hori. In view of this woman's life why should she want to conceal this fact as she admitted having slept with Nakayama on the night of the 8-11-35, which he had expressed to her to keep quiet.

四川北路旁梅贺里（Mei Ho Li）27号“驹”（Koma，音译）场所的Mayuko提供的进一步实质性陈述明确显示，死者是该处的常客，并于1935年11月9日晚上8点40分左右离开该处，可以说她是最后一个见到死者活着的人，因为没有其他证人能推翻这一说法。她看见他神态正常地离开该场所，携带一个包裹，后得知内装日本年糕等物，日本海军陆战队称这些物品是在路上发现于中山（R. Nakayama，音译）身旁的。这些年糕以及在他身上发现的一封信，是梅贺里23号的佐佐木光洋（Koyo Sasaki，音译）交给他转交给水兵青木（Aoki）的。

关于死者的过往生活，已证实他在“驹”场所有一位“固定相好”，名叫千代（Chito，音译），据说她履行完与妓院的合约，于1935年9月30日前往日本。Mayuko曾一度称她没有“固定男人”，但在特别警务官（S.P.O.）和助理警务处长（A.C.P.）上原先生（Mr. Uyehara）面前所作的修订陈述中，她承认与一名名叫堀（Hori，音译）的水兵有染。鉴于这名女子的生活背景，她为何要隐瞒这一事实？她承认在1935年11月8日晚与中山同寝，而中山曾要求她对此保密。

Some significance must be placed on the fact, in view of the exhaustive enquiries that have already been conducted with the possibility of Nakayama having been shot by some person who may have met him on Darroch Road and resided within that area. That he did leave No. 27 Mei Ho Li and that he was a regular visitor to that locality and became known in person. Furthermore the time for him to return to the barracks was 11 p.m., but he was on his way back to arrive at 9 p.m., therefore it is reasonable to surmise that he was followed from this locality by some person unknown, but acquainted with his movements and intention of returning earlier, and that he intimated to Mayeba that intention, that he would be back in the barracks by 9 p.m.

The finding of the .32 auto pistol by Sub-Inspector Lancyann behind the watchman's hut in the Fong Lah Li 500 feet from the scene, came about in an unorthodox way, he was probing with his walking stick. It cannot be definitely stated which way the pistol was lying as at first it was touched and moved about by the stick and then seen.

The absence of any knowledge of the exact position in which the pistol lay leaves an element of doubt in construing what position the person would be in who placed it there.

Translation of letter addressed to Seaman Aoki
by Miss Koyo Sasaki, alias "Omekiku"

Wai Wai Li,
Shanghai,
Nov. 9, 1930.

My darling Masao,

I am sorry indeed; Libano came this morning.
Your unchangeable devotion for me has touched
me so much and I shall always cherish those sweet mem-
ories of your affection.

O darling, how happy I feel when I am with you !
I may be naughty at times but I really don't mean any-
thing. I love you so.

Did you get back to the barracks in time ? I
do hope you were in time. I am so upset about it that
I can hardly swallow my food.

Masao darling, don't forget and come up and see
me as often as you can. I know you are awfully busy but
please come and see me. I miss you so much. You won't
forget, would you ? I am just crazy about you, darling !
Life is really not worth living without you.

With love and kisses from your sweetheart.

Kiko

1930年11月9日。

我亲爱的正雄（Masao），

实在抱歉；利巴诺（Libano）今天早上来了。
你对我不变的爱恋深深打动了我，我将永远珍视那些关于你深情的甜蜜回忆。

哦，亲爱的，和你在一起时我是多么幸福！
我有时可能有些任性，但我真的没有恶意。我是如此爱你。

你及时回到营房了吗？我真希望你赶上了。我对此非常不安，几乎吃不下饭。

正雄亲爱的，别忘了尽可能多来看我。我知道你非常忙，但请来看我。我非常想念你。你不会忘记的，对吧？亲爱的，我为你痴狂！没有你，生活真的不值得过。

爱你的并献上吻。

你的甜心。

纪子（Kiko）

With reference to the anonymous letter, dated 21-11-36, addressed to the A/C of P, written both in English and Chinese, signed H.F. Ling and Ling See ?, the person referred to therein, one Veng Hai Deng (王茂棠), alias Kuh Lan Wang (格老王), aged 32 years, native of Ningpo, at 10 a.m. on the 27-11-36, was located by D.S. Craig, D.S.I. Chu Chi Huang and C.D.S. 390, at House 28, Lane 72 Yuenfong Road, where he resides.

Interrogation of Veng Hai Deng failed in any way to associate him with this crime.

He is at present employed and has been for the past 3 years in the Ming Hwa Teashop and Theatre, 434 East Seward Road. He has many friends employed in the Jardine & Matheson river boats. It is also known to detectives that he is a money-lender - this he denied.

It is obvious the sender of the letter desired to involve him for an ulterior motive.

Witnesses Keh Ah Liang (郭阿良) and Li Ong Ping (李鴻賓) were again questioned on the 26-11-36, this led to the questioning of two private ricksha coolies, namely Tsang Ah Dee (張阿大) and Sia Kya Kyien (謝家年), and a cook named Ho Sing Zai (何新才), who are employed at No. 27 Peng Lah Li, and sleep together with Li Ong Ping in a loft in No. 19 Peng Lah Li, nothing of interest was unearthed.

The line of reasoning was that, as the pistol, used
in the crime, was found behind the watchman's hut in the
Feng Leh Li, which is the hut of Li Ong Ping, a person
desirous to involve Li Ong Ping in the crime, had placed
the pistol there. The motive for the crime still being
not known, it was reasoned that Li Ong Ping may have had
an affair with either a sweetheart or a wife of some man,
also employed in the Feng Leh Li or its environs.

Movements of seaman H. Kita upon leaving the barracks for a second time on the 9/11/35.

At about 2 p.m. on the 9/11/35, seaman Kita left the barracks for the Naval Club in Miller Road, proceeding by N. Szechuen and Haining Roads, arriving there at about 2.30 p.m. He read books until 4 p.m. and later had dinner. Intending to spend the night in the club he bought a bed ticket, and then read books until about 8 p.m. At this time he found the club was too noisy so decided not to sleep there, and left at about 8.10 p.m. and went to the Midoriya Restaurant on Haining Road and ate some rice cakes. At about 8.25 p.m. he left this restaurant for the barracks, walking along North Szechuen Road and Barrock Road. Arriving near the Yakko Restaurant on Barrock Road, he observed two or three persons standing on the roadway between 20 and 30 metres ahead of him. Dogs were barking, and he thought there was a fight among Chinese. Upon arriving at the scene, to his surprise he found his comrade (H. Nakayama) lying on the road. He raised the upper portion of Nakayama's body and shouted to him saying "Do not worry, you are alright" however, there was no response from Nakayama. Realising that it was serious, seaman H. Kita rushed to the N.L. Party Headquarters and reported to an adjutant on duty, and a N.C.O. in charge of the guard.

1935年11月9日，水兵北田（H. Kita）第二次离开营房后的行动轨迹。

1935年11月9日下午2点左右，水兵北田离开营房前往米勒路（Miller Road）的海军俱乐部，途经北四川路和海宁路，于下午2点30分左右到达。他读书至下午4点，随后用餐。他打算在俱乐部过夜，购买了一张床位票，然后继续读书至晚上8点左右。此时他发现俱乐部太吵，决定不在那里睡觉，于是于晚上8点10分左右离开，前往海宁路的绿屋餐厅（Midoriya Restaurant）吃了一些年糕。晚上8点25分左右，他离开该餐厅返回营房，沿着北四川路和达罗克路（Barrock Road）行走。当走到达罗克路上的雅可餐厅（Yakko Restaurant）附近时，他观察到前方20至30米处的马路上站着两三个人。狗在吠叫，他以为是中国人在打架。当他到达现场时，惊讶地发现他的战友（中山秀夫 H. Nakayama）躺在路上。他抬起中山的上半身并对他喊道：“别担心，你没事”，然而，中山没有任何反应。意识到情况严重，水兵北田迅速冲向海军陆战队（N.L. Party）总部，向值班副官和负责警卫的下士报告。

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

With reference to the anonymous letter, dated 18/11/35, addressed to the Japanese Naval Landing Party, and handed to D.S.I. Nakamura on the 20/11/35, D.S.I.s. Crowther, McPhee and C.D.S. 280, at 6.30 p.m. on the 20/11/35 with the assistance of the North Szechwan Road Police Station (Constable 2404), proceeded to Lane 150, House 34, Chen Chun Road. The house was found to be one of a row of houses, where persons of the middle class Chinese dwell.

Enquiries were made at House 34, and the party were met by Woo Z Ling (吴让霖) subject of the anonymous letter. Woo Z Ling rents two rooms on the ground floor, a front room used as a general living room and a back room used as a bedroom. He lives with his wife and one son.

Constable 2404 S.P.S.Bureau made a search of these two rooms in the presence of Woo Z Ling, D.S.Is. Crowther, McPhee, and C.D.S. 280, but nothing of an incriminating nature was found, or anything that suggested an interest in the murder of Nakayama.

Woo Z Ling willingly attended the North Szechwan Road Police Station, and later with Constable 2404, P.S. Bureau, came to the office at Hongkew Police Station.

Between 8 p.m. and 12 m.n. on the 20/11/35 a statement was taken from him by D.S.I.s. Crowther, McPhee and Chu Chi Kwong.

关于1935年11月18日写给日本海军陆战队分队并于1935年11月20日交给警探长中村的匿名信，警探长克劳瑟（Crowther）、麦克菲（McPhee）和华籍警探280号，在北四川路警察局（巡捕2404号）的协助下，于1935年11月20日下午6点30分前往陈春路150弄34号。经查，该房屋是一排房屋中的一栋，居住者为中国中产阶级人士。

在34号进行了查询，接待调查人员的是匿名信所指的对象吴让霖（Woo Z Ling）。吴让霖租用了底层的两个房间，前间用作一般起居室，后间用作卧室。他与妻子和一个儿子同住。

巡捕2404号（特别分部）在吴让霖、警探长克劳瑟、麦克菲和华籍警探280号在场的情况下，对这两个房间进行了搜查，但未发现任何具有指控性质的物品，或任何表明其对中山谋杀案感兴趣的东西。

吴让霖自愿前往北四川路警察局，随后在特别分部巡捕2404号的陪同下，来到虹口警察局办公室。

1935年11月20日晚上8点至午夜12点之间，警探长克劳瑟、麦克菲和朱志光（Chu Chi Kwong，音译）对他进行了问话并记录了供词。

Zoeng. Passengers, two female Chinese.

M/Car Lic. No. 18103, driver Lic. No. 6358, Leo Ching Foo. Left garage at 9.36 p.m. 9/11/35, for the Shingetsu Kaden Restaurant, Kiangwan Road. Car hired by telephone. Passengers, one female and 3 male Japanese, wearing foreign styled clothing. Passengers entered car at the restaurant and instructed the chauffeur to drive to Kashing Road where one of the males alighted, then to Thorne Road near Dixwell Road where the female alighted. Continued to Kashing Road near Woosung Road where one more male alighted, then to Woosung Road near Yuhang Road where the last male alighted.

All the chauffeurs have been questioned but none of them noticed anything of a suspicious nature attached to any of the passengers.

Further enquiries have been made and are being continued at all Chinese maid servants employment bureaux.

Nightly, detectives have visited the vicinity of the crime but no information has been obtained.

Attached are statements of J.P.C. 178, J.P.S. 61, Woo Z Ling and that of Mr. S. Takeoka taken by the Japanese Consular Police on the 10/11/35. Also attached, translation of anonymous letter.
