Translation of the anonymous letter addressed to
the Japanese Naval Landing Party

With reference to the shooting of the Japanese sailor, named
Hideo Nakayama, attached to the Japanese Naval Landing Party, which
took place at 8.45 p.m. on the 10-11-35, I beg to report that this
crime was instigated by one named Woo Z Ling, a notorious loafer,
formerly employed as a bodyguard by someone residing in the French
Concession. This man is the leader of a gang of loafers and is
known to be in possession of a pistol.

About 6 or 7 months after he lost his job, he felt he was in
great difficulty. He therefore gathered together his followers and
made arrangements to murder Japanese marines.

Woo Z Ling has a bicycle and he rode same out to Darroch Road,
North Szechuen Road, Deng Chi Road, Chapei, to scatter rumours that
there would be a big fight in the near future to the residents.

Only three days after they had definitely planned to murder
Japanese marines, Hideo Nakayama was leaning against a wall sleep-
ing, when a crowd of loafers arrived with their leader, Woo Z Ling.
Woo drew out his pistol and fired at Nakayama. They then made
good their escape. The next day they went around Scott Road,
Hung Feng Li, Sz Dah Li and North Szechuen Road to scatter the
rumour. Nakayama was shot on the 10th and the residents of the
above places evacuated from 11th to 14th. The main hope of the
loafers was to scatter such rumours and cause people to remove, so
that they would have the opportunity to steal money and clothing.

Woo Z Ling is a habitual gambler and his present business is
extortion. I therefore ask that the Japanese Naval Officers will
put this man Woo under arrest at once.

If you want to arrest him, you had better go to his home at
7 p.m. He is residing at No. 34, Lane 189 Chen Chun Road and
the following is his description.

Fat strong build, round face, hair cut short, has a
cataract on his left eye.

If you do not get rid of this man, I believe more cases of
a similar nature will be perpetrated in the near future.

If you are going to arrest him do not send men in uniform, or

致日本海军陆战队的匿名信译文

关于1935年11月10日晚8时45分发生的日本海军陆战队水兵中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）被枪击一案，特此报告，此案由一名名为伍子凌（Woo Z Ling）的 notorious loafer（惯常游手好闲者）唆使。此人曾受雇于法租界某居民担任保镖，是个臭名昭著的流氓头子，据知持有一把手枪。

在他失业约六七个月后，他感到处境十分困难。因此，他召集手下，策划谋杀日本水兵。

伍子凌有一辆自行车，他骑车到达罗克路（Darroch Road）、北四川路、邓志路（Deng Chi Road，音译）及闸北等地，向居民散布谣言，称近期将发生大规模斗殴。

在他们明确策划谋杀日本水兵仅三天后，中山秀雄正靠墙睡觉，一群流氓在其头目伍子凌的带领下赶到。伍拔出手枪向中山射击。随后他们迅速逃离。次日，他们在斯科特路（Scott Road）、鸿丰里（Hung Feng Li）、四达里（Sz Dah Li）及北四川路一带散布谣言。中山于10日中枪，上述地方的居民从11日至14日纷纷撤离。这帮流氓的主要目的是散布此类谣言，迫使人们搬离，以便他们有机会窃取钱财和衣物。

伍子凌是 habitual gambler（惯赌），目前的营生是敲诈勒索。因此，我请求日本海军军官立即逮捕此人。

如需逮捕他，最好于晚上7点前往其住所。他居住在陈春路189弄34号，其体貌特征如下。

体型肥胖强壮，圆脸，短发，左眼患有白内障。

如果不除掉此人，我相信近期还会发生更多类似案件。

如果打算逮捕他，切勿派遣穿制服的人员，否则

Answer to question (2) It is evident that Nakayama did not anticipate any trouble with anyone by sleeping with Miss Hara, who was the only girl available when he visited the establishment. It will be seen from her statement that originally he did not care much about sleeping with her, and therefore he first invited her to go with him to the restaurant to have something to eat. The girl, however, refused by saying that as she had no business that night she preferred to remain, and only consented to leave when Nakayama assured her that he would engage her for the night. According to Japanese custom, it is regarded as a bad etiquette to change a girl each time one visits licensed premises, and a careful psycho-analysis of Japanese temperament is necessary for an Occidental to appreciate this line of reasoning peculiar to Japanese. The fact that Nakayama asked Miss Hara not to mention to other girls about his visit must not be taken so seriously. He merely said that to avoid being teased by other girls. It is true that his paramour was no longer in Shanghai, and he was at liberty to go with any other girls if he so wished, but since he is so well known to people in this establishment he could not help feeling embarrassed when going with another girl.

问题（2）的回答：显然，中山在与原田小姐（Miss Hara，注：前文为Hana，此处原文为Hara，依原文译）同宿时，并未预料到会与任何人发生麻烦，因为当他光顾该场所时，她是唯一可提供服务的女孩。从她的供词可以看出，起初他并不太在意与她同宿，因此他首先邀请她去餐厅吃点东西。然而，女孩拒绝了，她说既然当晚没有生意，她宁愿留下来，直到中山保证会包她过夜，她才同意离开。根据日本习俗，每次光顾特许场所时更换女孩被视为失礼，西方人需要对日本人的性格进行仔细的心理分析，才能理解这种日本人特有的推理方式。事实上，中山要求原田小姐不要向其他女孩提及他的来访，这一点不必过于当真。他说这话只是为了避免被其他女孩取笑。确实，他的情妇已不在上海，如果他愿意，他可以自由地与任何其他女孩交往，但由于他在该场所的人员中非常出名，在与另一个女孩在一起时，他不禁感到尴尬。

J.D.S. 51 Hasse at 11 a.m. on the 18-11-35 interviewed Lieut. Comdr. Odawara, Officer of the Guard, at the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters from whom he learned the following points.
1. The Naval Landing Party Headquarters was first notified about the incident at about 9 p.m. on the 9-11-35 by a 2nd class seaman named Kita, who returned to the barracks via Darroch Road. He also spoke to the sentry standing at the entrance of Darroch Road to whom he stated that someone had been attacked and was lying on Darroch Road.
2. The sentry on North Szechuen Road near Darroch Road first heard a report of an explosion and then saw a Chinese man, aged about 16 years, wearing jacket and pants, running towards two C.P.Cs. on North Szechuen Road from Darroch Road. This man spoke to the constables and then was seen to lead them to Darroch Road. Soon after this the sentry saw seaman Kita who told him that there was someone lying injured on Darroch Road. This sailor immediately rushed to the J.N.L. Party Headquarters to report the affair. Shortly after this another sailor returning from leave was observed by the sentry walking on North Szechuen Road and proceeding towards the barracks. He stopped the sailor and asked him to proceed to Darroch

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.
The witness Koh Ah Liang ( 郭阿良 ) appeared before the S.S.D.Court on the 15/11/35 when a successful application for a Writ of Detention was made.
It was believed from the statements to hand that at the time the murder was committed Koh Ah Liang was actually outside a cigarette and exchange shop situated at No. 93 Darroch Road (corner of Darroch Road and Darroch Terrace) which shop is kept by Zung Dah San ( 陳大生 ) a cousin of Koh Ah Liang.
This belief was substantiated by the counting of coppers - the witness Koh Ah Liang having stated he was counting coppers when he heard the sound of an explosion.
It did not sound feasible that he would be counting coppers whilst walking in the Feng Loh Li near the entrance to the North Szechuen Road. He had stated that between 8 p.m. and 9 p.m. on the 9/11/35 he went to the said cigarette and exchange shop to change 40 cents silver to coppers, receiving 96 coppers for the silver pieces tendered which he divided into two lots and placed in his jacket pockets. It was definitely proved he visited the shop. The few points mentioned tend to substantiate the statements of Woo Ziang Foo lansmuen, as none of the other witnesses neither met nor saw any person running from the scene.
It is possible that the assailant upon entering the Fong Leh Li, took the first alleyway on the North side of Fong Leh Li, leading into the Keeble Gardens, and emerged again into the Fong Leh Li by the alleyway a little east of the watchman's hut. RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Checking of the statements obtained from witnesses in connection with this crime revealed many discrepancies in respect of the statements made by the witness Koh Ah Liang (郭阿良).

His own statements and present demeanour leads to a strong belief that he is with-holding valuable information from the Police officers investigating the murder of Hideo Nakayama, a Japanese sailor attached to the Japanese Naval Landing Party, Shanghai, which was committed at about 9 p.m. on the 9-11-35 on the Darroch Road, by some person at present unknown.

Owing to the circumstances which prevail and have arisen through this crime - it is believed that the witness Koh Ah Liang will abscond, therefore a Writ of Detention will be applied for in the S.S.D. Court on the morning of the 15-11-35 to enable further investigation.

D. D. O. "G"

and searched the house at the South corner of Darroch Road and
Fung Leh Li. This was done with the permission of the inmates
and of Supt. Liang, i/c 5th Division, P.S.B.

The house was inhabited by Dr. Chen and his family,
none of whom were absent at theraid (they were seen to
return at 1.30 a.m. by Supt. Wu ).

Dr. Chen appeared a man of good standing and was eager
to assist the Police. He could not give any information and
nothing incriminating was found in the house.

From the position of the cartridge case and the nature
of the round it was obvious the fatal shot could not have been
fired from this house.

D.O. "C" Division.

C. D. J. Grubb,
Please arrange to have all
copies of reports, etc. on this
case in our possession placed
together carefully and make
sure that the S.I.D is furnished
with a copy of everything we
have.
J.M.S.

由肯尼迪队长制作 转发者

1935年11月10日凌晨约12点15分，吴巡长和我进入并搜查了位于达罗克路与丰乐里（Fung Leh Li）南角的一所房屋。此举得到了屋内住户以及公共租界工部局警务处第五分区主管梁巡长（Supt. Liang）的许可。

该房屋由陈医生及其家人居住，突袭搜查时无人缺席（吴巡长看到他们于凌晨1点30分返回）。

陈医生看似一位地位体面的人士，并急于协助警方。他未能提供任何信息，且在屋内未发现任何罪证。

根据弹壳的位置和子弹的性质，显然致命一枪不可能从这所房屋内射出。

“C”分区总监。

C. D. J. Grubb，
请安排将我们要案中所有的报告副本等文件仔细整理在一起，并确保特别情报科（S.I.D）获得我们所有文件的副本。
J.M.S.
1935年11月18日

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

Enquiries regarding the actions of the victim prior to he being shot on the Darroch Road, it has been ascertained by J.D.S. 131 Iguchi, J.D.S. 81 Inoue, and J.D.C. 68 Oono that he left the Naval Landing Party Barracks at 12.30 p.m. on the 9/11/35, he having special leave this date as he was expected to leave for Japan in the near future. He then proceeded to the Japanese Naval Club situated at No. 408 Miller Road. He left this address at about 4 p.m. and returned to the Naval Landing Party Barracks. At 6.40 p.m. he again left the barracks and not until about 8 p.m. his actions can be learned. At about 8 p.m. he visited an establishment of amusement for Japanese Naval men, known as the "Kingston" situated at No. 33 Mei Ho Lee near Wong Pang Bridge, North Szechuan Road, C.O.L., which place is under the management of one named Mrs. T. Nakamura. At this place he had an idle conversation with a Japanese female named Kayo Sasaki for about 30 minutes, he did not appear to be under the influence of alcohol, and his demeanour was quite normal.

He left this place and at about 8.30 p.m. he visited No. 27 in the same alleyway which amusement place is known as "In U", under the management of Mr. K. Goto. In this place he spoke to a female named Chiyo Hara, and although she asked him to stay overnight, he left about 20 minutes

关于证人 Uee Ziang Uee（原文不清），其书面证词已呈送，该证人首先由警司 CRAIG、华探第119号和书记员 Chi Keong Shen（原文不清）在见习副巡官 Si Hsue（音译）和华捕 SS Oung（音译）在场的情况下进行讯问，随后他陈述，在听到爆炸声后，他看到一名日本士兵向东跑进丰乐里（Fong Lah Li），另一人躺在达罗尔路（Darruell Road）上。

这与其书面证词不符。

已安排由“F”区副总监 Conduit 警监于1935年11月11日向该证人另行录取口供。

1935年11月11日上午9时，本局接到田中中佐的电话留言，称其宪兵队已找到一名女性，据信即为1935年11月9日晚向中央巡捕房第2001号和2004号巡捕报案称有一名男子躺在达罗尔路上的那名女性。田中中佐请求公共租界警务处警官于1935年11月11日上午9时30分赶赴谋杀现场，以便见证该女性陈述其对事件的看法。

助理警务处长 Sykes、代理警监 Kneel、巡官 Butcher、警司 Craig 和见习副巡官 Si Hsue 赶赴现场。

Others present were, Chief Inspt. Fukuyama and Inspt. Okamura of the Japanese Consular Police, Sergt. Matoba, J.M.Police, and Mr. Uyehara, A.C.P. (Japanese).
A photograph was also taken by a photographer of the Japanese Naval Landing Party of the position where she passed the sailor and civilian whilst walking South on Barrock Road, the sailor being substituted by Sergt. Matoba and the civilian by another Japanese civilian dressed in foreign clothes who was present. The position the female witness took up was a little East of the centre of the roadway - quite close to the substituted civilian. This concluded the demonstration of the witness's actions - time being 7.10 p.m.

Shooting of a Japanese sailor on Barresh Road.
At 8.30 p.m. on the 10/11/35, under the supervision of the Officer i/c of this district, witness and officers of the S.M.Police awaited the reconstruction of the incident at the Headquarters of the J.N.L. Party.
At 8.45 p.m. on the 10/11/35, the following officers attended the scene of the shooting:- Mr. Tajima, Deputy Commissioner, Rear Admiral Araki, Commander Chaugi, Lieutenant Commander Yasuda, Naval attache Okino, Sergeant Major, Hatake, Military Police, Chief Inspector Fukuyama, Japanese Consular Police, Inspector Okumura, Japanese Consular Police.
The reconstruction of the incident commenced and Captain Kennedy, D.O."C" and Supt. Conduit, D.D.O."C", arrived later.
The positions of the S.M. Police on duty at about 9 p.m. on the 9/11/35 were explained as follows.
C.P.Cs. 2564 and 2591 (present) walking 5 beat were at North Szechuen Road and Kiangwan Road junction opposite the Headquarters of the J.N.L. Party.
C.P.C. 2769 (absent, as on leave), walking 4 beat which covers the scene of the incident, was at North Szechuen Road and Barresh Road junction.
C.P.C. 213 (present) walking 1 beat, was at North Szechuen Road and Dixwell Road junction.

Shooting of a Japanese sailor on Darroch Road.

At 9.05 p.m. on the 9/11/35, C.P.C. 2064, by street telephone Box 1, informed Maxwell Road Station that a Chinese had been hurt by a Japanese soldier on Kiangwan Road near the Headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party.

P.S. 250 Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61 attended and at 9.10 p.m. on the 9/11/35, P.S. Wilkinson, by the same telephone box, informed this station that something serious had happened and requested that S.I. Butcher and a foreign detective should be sent immediately.

(The above includes message entered in the Telephone books).

S.I. Butcher and D.S. Craig attended to find that a Japanese sailor had been removed from Darroch Road to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Hospital suffering from a bullet wound in the head.

Immediately after P.S. Wilkinson had telephoned the station he and J.P.S. 61 found a Japanese sailor lying on the Darroch Road near the Fung Leh Li (豐樂里) with a wound in the head, standing round him were many pedestrians. P.S. Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61 immediately informed the officer on duty at the Headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party and stretcher bearers with

A witness named Woo Ziang Woo (胡祥和), whose statement is attached, at about 9 p.m. on the 9/11/35 was about to enter No. 90 Darroch Road, which is to the South of the spot where the blood was found, states he heard the report of a firearm being discharged, he immediately looked Northwards and saw a man wearing dark coloured long trousers and short jacket running East into the Feng Leh Li, then he observed a man lying on the roadway. The roadway where the shooting occurred is poorly lighted at night.
The finding of the pistol at the place mentioned definitely proves the assailant was making his way to North Szechuen Road, either having continued along the Feng Leh Li, or taking a branch alleyway which leads to Keeble Gardens where he could also gain the North Szechuen Road. RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

According to the report of the J.N.L. Party's Medical Officer (attached) the sailor died at 1.10 a.m. on the 10/11/35. It is believed he was unable to speak from the time he was shot.

The shooting of the sailor caused the sending of numerous members of the J.N.L. Party to the scene and its vicinity. Special precautions were ordered to be taken by the D.O. "C", who was present throughout.

Reserve Unit also called out.

The spent bullet, empty cartridge case and pistol were immediately sent to the A.I.S. for examination where it was definitely ascertained that the pistol had been recently fired and that the spent bullet and empty cartridge case were fired by the pistol found.

Prior to this examination D.S.I. Dickson examined the pistol for possible finger prints, none were found.

Copy of the statement from witness Woo Ziang Woo given to N.L. Party.

Photographs will be taken and a plan to scale will be made of the scene and its vicinity during the early hours of the 10/11/35.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, MONDAY, NOVEMBER 11, 1935
12375

Responsibility Refused
By Chinese For Murder
Of A Japanese Sailor

Chinese Police Never Had Jurisdiction Over The
Scene Of Murder; Safety Bureau Co-operating
In Investigations Conducted On Killing

NO ULTIMATUM WHATEVER IS PRESENTED
"DEMANDING SATISFACTION"

"Local Chinese authorities are not responsible for the
unhappy incident on Darroch Road on Saturday night when
a Japanese sailor dropped dead with a bullet wound in his
head, because Chinese police have no jurisdiction over the
road, which is guarded by Japanese military and Settlement
police. The rumour that the Greater Shanghai City
Government has received demands from the Japanese in
connection with the incident is absolutely groundless." The
above statement was made last night to a representative of
"The Shanghai Times" by a responsible official of the
Greater Shanghai City Government. The statement that
no ultimatum had been presented
by the Japanese Naval Command
"demanding satisfaction" was
confirmed by Lieutenant-Com-
mander Matao Okima, Assistant
Naval Attache.

The Chinese official went on to
say that the Chinese police had
never been allowed to patrol the
road where the sailor was shot.
He confirmed the news, however,
that the Japanese military had
requested Chinese authorities to
co-operate with them and Settle-
ment police in arresting the
criminal. The request was made
to Mr. O. K. Yui, general secret-
ary of the City Government. He
did not believe that the situation
would assume serious proportions

Officials Returning
From Nanking

NANKING, Nov. 10.—Mr.
Wu Hsin-ya, Director of the
Bureau of Social Affairs and
Mr. Yang Hu, chief of the
Peace Preservation Corps, who
arrived here a few days ago to
attend the Fifth Executive
Congress, are expected to re-
turn to Shanghai today owing
to the fatal shooting Friday
night of a Japanese sailor—
Sailor.

《字林西报》，1935年11月11日，星期一
12375

中方拒绝为日本水兵被杀案负责

中国警方对案发地从未拥有管辖权；公安局正配合调查该起凶杀案

并未提出任何“要求谢罪”的最后通牒

“上周六晚在达罗克路（Darroch Road）发生的不幸事件中，一名日本水兵头部中弹身亡，当地中国当局对此并不承担责任，因为中国警方对该路段没有管辖权，该路由日军和租界警察守卫。有关大上海市政府已收到日方就此事件提出要求之传闻，纯属无稽之谈。”大上海市政府一位负责官员昨晚向《字林西报》记者发表了上述声明。日本海军司令部未提出“要求谢罪”的最后通牒这一说法，得到了海军副武官奥间又雄（Matao Okima，音译）中佐的证实。

这位中国官员接着表示，中国警方从未获准在该水兵遭枪击的路段巡逻。但他证实了如下消息：日军已请求中国当局与日军及租界警察合作，逮捕凶手。此项请求是向市政府秘书长俞鸿钧（O. K. Yui）先生提出的。他不相信局势会发展到严重的地步。

官员自南京返回

南京，11月10日电——社会局局长吴醒亚先生和保安总队总队长杨虎先生，数日前抵此参加第五次全国代表大会，因周五晚一名日本水兵遭致命枪击，预计今日返回上海。

pages.en:
ultimatum to the Chinese authorities "demanding satisfaction" for the murder of the Japanese sailor were emphatically denied last night by Lieutenant-Commander Matao Okino, Assistant Naval Attaché.
The interview took place 10 paces from the spot where Hideo Nakayama, first-class sailor, was fatally shot by an unidentified assassin.

Exodus Deplored
"While it is a matter of no direct concern to us, we feel aggrieved to know that baseless rumours are causing a mass exodus of residents from the Chapei and Hongkew district into the Settlement.
"Aside from asking the fullest co-operation from Chinese authorities on the apprehension of the culprit, we have made no demands whatever," the naval officer declared.

Sympathy Expressed
Chinese expressions of sympathy and promises for full co-operation were received by the Japanese naval authorities in Shanghai yesterday as law enforcement agencies in the International Settlement and outside pushed their search for the unidentified slayer of Hideo Nakayama, Japanese sailor.
Participating in the quest for clues were the Shanghai Municipal Police, the Public Safety Bureau, the Japanese Consular police, the Special Naval Landing Party and gendarmerie.
Pledges to co-operate to their fullest extent in tracking down the criminal were made by the Chinese authorities on four separate occasions yesterday, according to Lieutenant-Commander Matao Okino, Assistant Japanese Naval Attaché.

Promises Co-operation
Mr. O. K. Yui, secretary-general of the Municipal Government of Greater Shanghai, made this attitude clear at 1 o'clock on Sunday morning in an interview with Lieutenant - Commander Yoshitatsu Yasuda, staff officer of the Special Naval Landing Party, Lieutenant - Commander Okino said, to a Rengo representative.
Chief Inspector Wang Ta-tsui and Mr. Liang Fu-tau, chief of the North Station Branch Police Station of the Public Safety Bureau, called on Rear-Admiral Sadaski Araki, commander of the Special Naval Landing Party, at his headquarters on Kiangwan Road at 10.30 o'clock in the morning. They acted as representatives of Mr. Tsai Chin-chun, director of the Bureau of Public Safety.
Following them came Mr. Wang Chang-chun, Japanese secretary of the Greater Shanghai Municipal Government, acting on behalf of Mayor Wu Te-chen.
Lieutenant-Commander Yasuda called on Mr. Yang Fu, director of the Bureau of Peace Preservation at 1 o'clock in the afternoon, and secured similar assurances.

Japanese Suspect Chinese
Meantime, Japanese naval and police authorities apparently were carrying on their investigations under the suspicion that the slayed was a Chinese.
"Judging from the pistol that was used, Lieutenant-Commander Okino said, 'we are convinced that the assailant was not a member of the Japanese Navy. For one thing, we do not use that type of gun. Moreover, the only eye-witness of the attack says that the man was wearing a short jacket and baggy trousers,' a typical Chinese dress. The report that the shooting was the outcome of a quarrel has been proved to be unfounded, the statement added."

Similar views were expressed by the Japanese consular police, who yesterday morning questioned at length Woo Ziang-woo, Chinese employee of the Takaoka Shoe Store, 194 Darroch Road, Eupahiro Takaoka, proprietor of the establishment, was also summoned to the Consular Police headquarters but released after an examination yesterday morning.
Shanghai Municipal Police authorities were reported to be looking for two ricksha coolies who were seen near the scene of the shooting on Saturday night.
Lieutenant - Commander Okino emphatically denied that any arrests had been made. "Reports that the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party had taken Chinese suspects into custody are absolutely unfounded," he said.
"We are trusting the Chinese and Settlement authorities and sincerely hope they will exhaust every possible clue in finding the assailant.

Serious Effect
"We are gratified that the Chinese authorities spontaneously offered to carry on an intensive search for the slayer. Nevertheless we cannot but feel that the incident will have serious effects upon Sino-Japanese relations," he further remarked, according to Rengo.
Lieutenant - Commander Okino made a full report of the affair to Vice-Admiral Teijiro Sugisaka, commander of the Japanese Eleventh Flotilla, when the latter arrived from up-river ports aboard his flagship, the gunboat Ataka, at 2 o'clock yesterday afternoon. The arrival of H.I.J.M.S. Ataka brings the number of Japanese war vessels in port to four, including the cruiser Idzumo, flagship of the Third Fleet. The others are the gunboat Hosu and the destroyer Tsuga.

Funeral To-day
Nakayama, victim of the assault, will be buried with full naval honours at 4.30 this afternoon. Services will be held in the yard of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party Headquarters.
This will cause Japanese war vessels in port that will dress ship in celebration of Armistice Day to take in the decorations before the services begin.
Deceased, who was officially commended as an "exemplary sailor, gentle and laborious," was on his way back to the barracks from a cafe near Wangpangjao Bridge on North Szechuen Road, official investigation has revealed. He was seen leaving the establishment at about 8.45 o'clock. He was fatally shot between 9 and 9.30 p.m.

日本海军副武官奥间又雄（Matao Okino，音译）中佐昨晚断然否认了向日方当局发出就日本水兵被杀案“要求谢罪”的最后通牒的说法。

此次谈话地点距离一等水兵中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）被不明身份刺客枪杀身亡的地点仅十步之遥。

对人口外流表示痛惜

“虽然此事与我们无直接利害关系，但得知毫无根据的谣言正导致闸北和虹口地区居民大规模逃入租界，我们感到愤慨。除了要求中国当局在缉拿凶手方面给予充分合作外，我们未提出任何要求，”这位海军军官宣称。

表示同情

昨日，随着国际租界内外的执法机构加紧搜寻日本水兵中山秀雄的不明身份凶手，中国方面向驻沪日本海军当局表达了同情并承诺全力合作。参与寻找线索的有上海公共租界工部局警务处、公安局、日本领事馆警察、特别海军陆战队以及宪兵队。据日本海军副武官奥间又雄（Matao Okino，音译）中佐称，中国当局昨日四次承诺将竭尽全力配合追踪罪犯。

承诺合作

据奥间中佐向联合通讯社代表称，大上海市政府秘书长俞鸿钧（O. K. Yui）先生于周日凌晨1时在与特别海军陆战队参谋保田义立（Yoshitatsu Yasuda，音译）中佐的会晤中，明确了这一态度。上午10时30分，督察长王达粹（Wang Ta-tsui，音译）和公安局北站分所所长梁福涛（Liang Fu-tau，音译）先生前往江湾路特别海军陆战队司令部，拜访了司令荒木贞夫（Sadaski Araki，音译）少将。他们作为公安局局长蔡劲军（Tsai Chin-chun，音译）先生的代表行事。随后，代表市长吴铁城（Wu Te-chen）的大上海市政府日籍秘书王春生（Wang Chang-chun，音译）先生也前往拜访。下午1时，保田中佐拜访了保安局局长杨虎（Yang Fu，此处原文为Yang Fu，通常指杨虎，但职务表述略有差异，依原文译）先生，并获得了类似的保证。

日方怀疑系中国人所为

与此同时，日本海军和警察当局显然是在怀疑凶手为中国人的前提下进行调查的。“从使用的手枪来看，”奥间中佐说，“我们确信袭击者不是日本海军成员。首先，我们不使用那种类型的手枪。此外，袭击的唯一目击者称，那人穿着短夹克和宽松长裤，”这是典型的中国人装束。声明还补充道，关于枪击是争吵结果的说法已被证明毫无根据。

日本领事馆警察也表达了类似观点，他们昨天上午长时间讯问了达罗克路194号高冈鞋店的中国雇员吴祥伍（Woo Ziang-woo，音译）。该店店主高冈荣平（Eupahiro Takaoka，音译）也被传唤至领事馆警察总部，但在昨天上午接受讯问后被释放。据报道，上海公共租界工部局警务处当局正在寻找周六晚在枪击现场附近被看到的两名人力车夫。奥间中佐坚决否认有任何人被捕。“有关日本特别海军陆战队拘留中国嫌疑人的报道纯属无稽之谈，”他说。“我们信任中国和租界当局，并真诚希望他们能穷尽一切可能的线索来寻找袭击者。

严重影响

“中国当局主动提出对凶手进行密集搜查，令我们感到欣慰。然而，我们不得不认为，此事件将对中日关系产生严重影响，”据联合通讯社报道，他进一步评论道。昨天下午2时，日本第十一舰队司令杉坂悌二郎（Teijiro Sugisaka，音译）少将乘坐旗舰炮舰“安宅”号（Ataka）从上游港口抵达，奥间中佐向他全面汇报了此事。“安宅”号的抵达使港内日本军舰数量达到四艘，包括第三舰队旗舰巡洋舰“出云”号（Idzumo）。其他两艘是炮舰“保寿”号（Hosu，音译）和驱逐舰“樫”号（Tsuga，音译）。

今日举行葬礼

遇袭受害者中山秀雄将于今天下午4时30分以全套海军礼仪下葬。仪式将在日本特别海军陆战队司令部院内举行。这将导致港内为庆祝停战日而挂满旗饰的日本军舰在仪式开始前收起装饰。官方调查显示，死者被正式表彰为“模范水兵，温和且勤勉”，当时他正从四川北路旺盘桥（Wangpangjao Bridge，音译）附近的一家咖啡馆返回营房。有人看到他在约8时45分离开该场所。他在晚上9时至9时30分之间遭枪击身亡。

12376

6. D. J. Grubb
（SI）

涉及同一笔迹的调查。

1938年11月11日

November 10,1935.
SHOOTING OF A JAPANESE SAILOR ON DARROCH ROAD
At 9.05 p.m. on the 9/11/35, C.P.C. 2864, by street
telephone Box 1, informed Dixwell Road Station that a Chinese
had been hurt by a Japanese soldier on Kiangwan Road near
the Headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party.
F.S. 230 Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61 attended and at
9.10 p.m. on the 9/11/35, F.S. Wilkinson, by the same telephone
box, informed this station that something serious had happened
and requested that S.I.Butcher and a foreign detective should
be sent immediately.
(The above includes message entered in the Telephone
books).
S.I. Butcher and D.S.Craig attended to find that a
Japanese sailor had been removed from Darroch Road to the
Japanese Naval Landing Party Hospital suffering from a bullet
wound in the head.
Immediately after F.S. Wilkinson had telephoned the
station he and J.P.S. 61 found a Japanese sailor lying on the
Darroch Road near the Fong Loh Li(豐樂里) with a wound in
the head, standing round him were many pedestrians. F.S.
Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61 immediately informed the officer on
duty at the Headquarters of the Japanese Naval Landing Party
and stretcher bearers with other sailors were despatched to
the scene and removed the wounded sailor to their Hospital.
Enquiries by D.D.O."C" and D.S.I. Crowther.
A Japanese named Hidio Nakoyama (中山秀雄), age
24, 1st class sailor, attached to the Japanese Naval Landing
Party (on liberty) whilst walking on Darroch Road near the
Fong Loh Li received a bullet wound to the head.
A pool of blood was found on the roadway 8 feet
from the West kerb of Darroch Road, practically opposite
pages.zh:
1935年11月10日。
达罗克路日本水兵遭枪击案
1935年11月9日晚9点05分，中国巡捕2864号通过1号街头电话亭通知狄思威路警察局，一名中国人在江湾路日本海军陆战队司令部附近被一名日本士兵打伤。
外国警员230号威尔金森（Wilkinson）和日本警员61号到场，1935年11月9日晚9点10分，威尔金森外国警员通过同一电话亭通知本局发生了严重事件，并要求立即派遣探员巴彻尔（Butcher）和一名外籍侦探。
（以上内容包含录入电话簿的信息）。
探员巴彻尔和侦探克雷格（Craig）到场后发现，一名日本水兵因头部枪伤已从达罗克路被送往日本海军陆战队医院。
威尔金森外国警员给警局打电话后，他和日本警员61号立即发现一名日本水兵躺在达罗克路靠近丰乐里处，头部有伤，周围站着许多行人。威尔金森外国警员和日本警员61号立即通知了日本海军陆战队司令部的值班军官，担架员和其他水兵被派往现场，将受伤水兵抬往他们的医院。
由“C”分区副侦探督察和侦探副督察克劳瑟（Crowther）进行调查。
一名叫中山秀雄（Hidio Nakoyama，音译，原文拼写有误，应为Hideo Nakayama）的日本人，24岁，一等水兵，隶属于日本海军陆战队（休假中），在达罗克路靠近丰乐里行走时头部中弹。
在距达罗克路西路边沿8英尺的路面上发现一滩血迹，几乎正对面

pages.en:
- 2 -

No.236 Darroch Road which house is situated on the East side.

A spent bullet was found by J.P.S. 61 on the road-way about 5 feet South of the pool of blood and about 4 feet from the West kerb.

J.D.S. 51 Hasuo found an empty cartridge case about 3 feet from the wall of 236 Darroch Road.

At about 11.40 p.m. on the 9/1135, S.I. Kaneyasu who was searching with others in the Fong Loh Li found behind a wooden watchman's hut situated on the North side of the Fong Loh Li, approximately 200 yards from the pool of blood and approximately 80 yards from North Szechuen Road entrance, one .32 calibre automatic pistol, No.14114, Beretta make, with one round of ammunition in the breech and five rounds in the magazine which was inserted in the pistol.

A witness named Woo Ziang Woo (胡祥和), whose statement is attached, at about 9 p.m. on the 9/11/35 was about to enter No.90 Darroch Road, which is to the South of the spot where the blood was found, states he heard the report of a firearm being discharged, he immediately looked Northwards and saw a man wearing dark coloured long trousers and short jacket running East into the Fong Loh Li, then he observed a man lying on the roadway. He informed a Japanese named Z.Takaoka, residing No.90 Darroch Road, of the incident and they both went to the scene to find a Japanese sailor lying wounded.

The roadway where the shooting occurred is poorly lighted at night.

The finding of the pistol at the place mentioned definitely proves the assailant was making his way to North Szechuen Road, either having continued along the Fong Loh Li, or taking a branch alleyway which leads to Keeble Gardens where he could also gain the North Szechuan Road.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

达罗克路（Darroch Road）236号，该房屋位于道路东侧。

J.P.S. 61号警员在血泊以南约5英尺、距西侧路缘石约4英尺的路面上发现了一枚已发射的子弹。

J.D.S. 51号警员Hasuo在距达罗克路236号墙壁约3英尺处发现了一个空弹壳。

1935年11月9日晚约11时40分，S.I. Kaneyasu与其他人员在丰乐里（Fong Loh Li）进行搜索时，在丰乐里北侧的一个木制更亭后方，发现了一支.32口径的贝雷塔（Beretta）牌自动手枪，编号14114，枪膛内有一发子弹，插入枪内的弹匣中有五发子弹。该地点距血泊约200码，距北四川路入口约80码。

一名名为胡祥和（Woo Ziang Woo）的证人（其供词附后）称，1935年11月9日晚约9时，他正欲进入位于发现血迹地点南侧的达罗克路90号，此时听到一声枪响。他立即向北张望，看见一名身穿深色长裤和短夹克的男子向东跑入丰乐里，随后他观察到一名男子躺在路面上。他将此事告知居住在达罗克路90号的日本人Z.Takaoka，两人随即前往现场，发现一名受伤的日本水兵躺在地上。

发生枪击的路面夜间照明不佳。

在上述地点发现手枪，确凿地证明袭击者当时正试图前往北四川路，要么是继续沿丰乐里前行，要么是转入一条通往基布尔花园（Keeble Gardens）的支弄，从那里也可以到达北四川路。

pages.en:
-,3 -

C.P.C. 3251, who was on point duty at the corner of
Dixwell and North Szechuen Roads opposite to the entrance
of the Fong Loh Li, has been questioned, but states he
failed to see any person making an hurried exit from the
Fong Loh Li at about 9 p.m. also he did not hear any shot
fired.

According to the report of the J.N.L.Party's
Medical Officer (attached) the sailor died at 1.10 a.m.
on the 10/11/35. It is believed he was unable to speak
from the time he was shot.

The shooting of the sailor caused the sending
of numerous members of the J.N.L.Party to the scene and
its vicinity. Special precautions were ordered to be
taken by the D.O."C", who was present throughout.

Reserve Unit also called out.

The spent bullet, empty cartridge case and pistol
were immediately sent to the A.I.S.for examination where
it was definitely ascertained that the pistol had been
recently fired and that the spent bullet and empty
cartridge case were fired by the pistol found.

Prior to this examination D.S.I. Dickson examined
the pistol for possible finger prints, none were found.

Copy of the statement from witness Woo Ziang Woo
given to N.L.Party.

Photographs will be taken and a plan to scale will
be made of the scene and its vicinity during the early
hours of the 10/11/35.

Major Bourne, A.C.P.
Mr. Young, D.C.(Crime).
Mr. Aiers, D.C.(Divisions).
Mr. Uyehara, A.C.P.(Japanese),
informed and attended.
pages.zh:
-,3 -

已在狄思威路（Dixwell Road）与北四川路交界处、正对丰乐里入口处执行定点执勤任务的C.P.C. 3251号警员接受了问询，但他表示在晚9时左右未看见任何人匆忙从丰乐里退出，也未听到任何枪声。

根据日本海军陆战队（J.N.L.Party）军医的报告（附后），该水兵于1935年11月10日凌晨1时10分死亡。据信他自中枪时起便无法说话。

水兵被枪击一事导致大量日本海军陆战队成员赶赴现场及其周边地区。全程在场的分区警官（D.O."C"）下令采取特别预防措施。

后备队也被召集出动。

已发射的子弹、空弹壳和手枪立即被送往武器鉴定科（A.I.S.）进行检验，经确切认定，该手枪近期曾发射过，且在现场发现的已发射子弹和空弹壳均由该查获的手枪射出。

在此次检验之前，副巡官狄克逊（D.S.I. Dickson）检查了该手枪以寻找可能的指纹，但未发现任何指纹。

附证人胡祥和向日本海军陆战队提供的供词副本。

将于1935年11月10日凌晨对现场及其周边进行拍照并绘制比例平面图。

助理警务处长伯恩少校（Major Bourne, A.C.P.）、刑事处副处长杨先生（Mr. Young, D.C.(Crime)）、分区处副处长艾尔斯先生（Mr. Aiers, D.C.(Divisions)）、日籍助理警务处长上原先生（Mr. Uyehara, A.C.P.(Japanese)）均已获知并到场。

pages.en:
Nov. 10, 1935.

Shooting of a Japanese sailor on Darroch Road.

At 8.30 p.m. on the 10/11/35, under the
supervision of the Officer i/c of this district, witness
and officers of the S.M.Police awaited the reconstruction
of the incident at the Headquarters of the J.N.L.Party.

At 8/45 p.m. on the 10/11/35, the following
officers attended the scene of the shooting:- Mr. Tajima,
Deputy Commissioner, Rear Admiral Araki, Commander Ohsugi,
Lieutenant Commander Yasuda, Naval attache Okino, Sergeant
Major, Matoba, Military Police, Chief Inspector Fukuyama,
Japanese Consular Police, Inspector Okumura, Japanese
Consular Police.

The reconstruction of the incident commenced and

达罗克路日本水兵被枪击案。

事件重现开始，随后分区警官肯尼迪上尉（Captain Kennedy, D.O."C"）和副分区警官康杜特督察（Supt. Conduit, D.D.O."C"）抵达。

A report has been received from Arms Identification

fired. Previous records - none. The above pistol fired

In connection with the pistol the number of same

COPY

Statement of C.P.C. 2864

at Dixwell Road Station on 9.11.35. translated by Clerk Tong

At 9.05 p.m. on the 9.11.35 I was on duty with C.P.C.
2891 on Kiangwan Road near N. Szechuen Road. Suddenly a
female Chinese reported to us that there was one Japanese
lying on the ground. Therefore, we immediately proceeded
to the scene and saw a Japanese marine with a wound in the
head. I at once telephoned to the station and reported
the same while C.P.C. 2891 remained there and watched the
injured person. Afterwards, F.S. 230, Wilkinson came
upon the scene and enquired if any one had seen this
accident. As a result of that we got a Chinese and a
Japanese as a witness and brought them to the station.

C.P.C. 2864.
pages.zh:
副本

C.P.C. 2864号警员供词

1935年11月9日于狄思威路站，由童书记员翻译

1935年11月9日晚9时05分，我与C.P.C. 2891号警员在北四川路附近的江湾路上执勤。突然，一名中国女子向我们报告说有一名日本人躺在地上。因此，我们立即前往现场，看到一名头部受伤的日本海军陆战队员。我立即打电话向分局报告此事，而C.P.C. 2891号警员留在现场看守伤者。随后，F.S. 230号警员威尔金森（Wilkinson）来到现场，询问是否有人目睹了这起事故。结果我们找到了一名中国人和一名日本人作为证人，并将他们带到分局。

C.P.C. 2864号警员。

pages.en:
COPY

Statement of Woo Ziang Woo 胡祥和
native of Zangchow 常州 taken by Clerk Li Yang Kao.
at 11.40 p.m. on the 9.11.35.

My name is Woo Ziang Woo, 26 years of age, native of
Zangchow, M/shoe-maker, residing at No.62 East Paoshing Road.
At about 8.45 p.m. on the 9.11.35, I left my home (East
Paoshing Road) and proceeded to a Japanese shoe-maker's shop,
named "Takaoka," on Darroch Road to get my pay. At about
9 p.m. on the 9th of November, 1935, I had nearly reached
the door of the Japanese shoe-maker's shop, when I heard the
report of a shot being fired. I immediately turned my head
and looked Northwards and saw a male wearing black clothing
running East into Yong Loh Li, off Darroch Road. Simultaneous-
ly I saw a man, also wearing black clothing, lying on the
roadway. I immediately went into the shoe-maker's shop and
informed the master, a Japanese, of the incident. We both
proceeded to where the man was lying and saw that he was
a Japanese marine. The master of the shoe-maker's shop then
instructed me to come to the station where I made the report.
The clothing worn by the man who ran away was similar
in colour as that worn by the man lying on the roadway. It
was long trousers and short jacket and not a long gown.
This is my true statement.

Signed: Woo Ziang Woo.

Taken in the presence of D.S.I. M.L. Crowther, J.D.S. 51
Hasuo, J.D.S. 34 Kobayashi and Clerk Ling Wei Ju (Hongkew).
pages.zh:
副本

胡祥和（Woo Ziang Woo）供词
常州人，由李仰高书记员采集。
1935年11月9日晚11时40分。

我叫胡祥和，26岁，常州人，职业修鞋匠，住宝兴东路62号。1935年11月9日晚约8时45分，我离开家（宝兴东路），前往达罗克路一家名为“高冈”（Takaoka）的日本鞋店去领工资。1935年11月9日晚约9时，我快走到那家日本鞋店门口时，听到一声枪响。我立即转头向北看，看见一名身穿黑衣的男子向东跑入达罗克路旁的永乐里（Yong Loh Li，注：原文此处与前文Fong Loh Li丰乐里拼写不同，依原文译出）。同时，我看见另一名同样身穿黑衣的男子躺在路面上。我立即走进鞋店，将此事告知店主（一名日本人）。我们两人随即前往那人躺卧的地方，发现他是一名日本海军陆战队员。鞋店店主随后吩咐我到分局报案，我便在此作了报告。逃跑男子所穿衣物颜色与躺在路面上的男子所穿衣物颜色相似。是长裤和短夹克，不是长袍。
这是我的真实供词。

签名：胡祥和。

在副巡官M.L. Crowther、J.D.S. 51号警员Hasuo、J.D.S. 34号警员Kobayashi和虹口书记员凌伟菊（Ling Wei Ju）面前采集。

pages.en:
COPY

Statement of Poo Chau Ying 潘巧美
native of Kompo taken by D.S.I. M.L. Crowther.
at Dixwell Rd. Stn. on 11.11.35. interpreted by Clerk Li

My name is Poo Chau Ying, aged 17 years, native of Kompo,
maid servant, employed by a Mr. Koona (河野), Japanese,
residing at No.95 Wing On Terrace.

At about 8 p.m. on the 9.11.35, I was instructed by my
Japanese mistress to take her female child, aged 3 years, to
her friend's house on Kiangwan Road, near the railway - for
amusement.

I proceeded by the North Szechuen Road. I arrived there
about 10 minutes after leaving 95 Wing On Terrace.

I left the address about one hour later. I proceeded
along Darroch Road carrying the child in my arms until I came
to a hot water shop on Darroch Road. Just before I arrived at
the hot water shop, I saw two men- one a Japanese sailor and
the other a civilian wearing dark foreign styled clothing - the
clothing was a short jacket and long trousers and a felt hat,
colour of hat I do not know. I could not distinguish his face.

At this time I saw a private ricsha on the East side of the
road - the coolie was sleeping between the shafts. I was walk-
ing in the middle of the roadway and passed between the sailor
and the civilian. I was nearer to the civilian. I cannot say
what his nationality was. After the Japanese sailor and the
civilian had passed me and I had arrived near the hot water shop,
situated on the East side of Darroch Road, I heard a report of
an explosion. I then turned round and saw the Japanese sailor
lying on the roadway. I could see the white on his collar. I
did not see the civilian when I turned round, but shortly after-
wards I saw a male Chinese wearing blue short jacket and pants
come out from Darroch Terrace, on the West side of the road, this
man I have seen before carrying shoes - so I know he is a shoe-
pages.zh:
副本

潘巧美（Poo Chau Ying）供词
高邮人，由副巡官M.L. Crowther采集。
1935年11月11日于狄思威路站，由李书记员口译。

我叫潘巧美，17岁，高邮人，女佣，受雇于居住在永安台（Wing On Terrace）95号的日本人河野（Koona）先生。

1935年11月9日晚约8时，我的日本女主人吩咐我带她3岁的女儿去铁路附近江湾路上的一位朋友家玩耍。

我经由北四川路前往。离开永安台95号约10分钟后到达那里。

约一小时后我离开该地址。我抱着孩子沿达罗克路前行，直到达罗克路上的一家热水店。就在我快到热水店之前，我看见两个人——一个是日本水兵，另一个是身穿深色西式服装的平民——服装是短夹克、长裤和一顶毡帽，帽子颜色我不知道。我看不清他的脸。

这时我看见路东有一辆私人黄包车——车夫睡在车杠之间。我走在路中间，从水兵和平民之间穿过。我离那个平民更近。我说不出他是哪国人。在日本水兵和平民走过我身边，且我到达位于达罗克路东侧的热水店附近后，我听到一声爆炸响。我随即转身，看见那名日本水兵躺在路面上。我能看到他衣领上的白色部分。我转身时没看见那个平民，但不久后我看见一名身穿蓝色短夹克和裤子的中国男子从路西的达罗克台（Darroch Terrace）走出来，我以前见过这个人挑着鞋子——所以我知道他是个修鞋

pages.en:
Statement of Poc Chau Ying.
- 2 -

maker. I saw some Chinese policemen at Kiangwan Road and North
Szechuen Road corner - but I do not know how many.
After seeing the sailor lying on the road I ran into the
Wing On Terrace through the hot water shop. There were many
Chinese in the hot water shop but I did not speak to them. When
I arrived at my master's house I told my mistress, whilst I
was returning from her friend's house, I saw a Japanese sailor
and a civilian, and I saw the sailor lying on the road shouting.
I do not know what he was shouting. I did not tell my mistress
anything else. I then washed some clothing.
The mistress then asked me if I knew who fired the shot.
I told her I did not know. My mistress then said the shot must
have been fired by a Chinese and there may be a fight.
After I had finished washing the clothing I went to bed.
On the 10.11.35, I went out with the child again and
returned late, so my mistress scolded me. I then ran away to
my aunt's home in Chapel - this is where the Police found me
on the 11.11.35.

Finger-printed: Poo Chau Ying.
Taken in the presence of Supt. Conduit, D.D.O."C", J.D.S.
51 Hasuo and J.D.C. 83 Osano.
(Note by D.S.I. Crowther. Witness is of the country type, only
about 1 year in Shanghai, when being questioned at the scene by
D.D.O."C" in presence of Lieut.Commander Yasuda, Commander
Ohsugi, Mr. Hyehara, A.C.P., Chief Inspt. Fukuyama of the
Japanese Consular Police, she stated she had been to the Ming
Tuh Fong, off North Szechuen Road at the rear of the Headquarters
of the J.N.L. Party.
pages.zh:
卜朝英（Poc Chau Ying）的陈述。
- 2 -

制作者。我在江湾路与北四川路路口看到一些中国警察——但我不知道具体人数。
看到那名水手躺在路上后，我穿过一家热水店跑进了永安里（Wing On Terrace）。热水店里有很多中国人，但我没有和他们说话。当我到达我主人家时，我告诉女主人，在我从她朋友家回来的路上，我看到一名日本水手和一名平民，我还看到那名水手躺在路上喊叫。我不知道他在喊什么。我没有再告诉女主人其他事情。然后我去洗了一些衣服。
随后女主人问我是否知道是谁开的枪。我告诉她我不知道。我的女主人接着说，开枪的一定是中国人，可能发生了斗殴。
洗完衣服后，我就去睡觉了。
1935年11月10日，我再次带着孩子外出，回来得很晚，所以女主人骂了我。于是我逃到了我在 Chapel（音译）的阿姨家——警方就是在1935年11月11日在那里找到我的。

按指印：卜朝英（Poo Chau Ying）。
在“C”区副总监康杜特（Conduit）警司、日籍特别巡捕51号长尾（Hasuo）和日籍华捕83号大园（Osano）面前录取。
（特别调查员克劳瑟（Crowther）注：证人是乡下人类型，来上海仅约1年，当她在现场由“C”区副总监在海军中佐安田（Yasuda）、大杉（Ohsugi）指挥官、上原（Hyehara）助理警务处长、日本领事馆警察福山（Fukuyama）首席督察面前接受询问时，她声称曾去过位于北四川路后方、日本海军陆战队总部附近的明土坊（Ming Tuh Fong）。

pages.en:
Statement of Z. Takaoka living at 90 Darroch Road

native of Japan taken by at Dimwell Road Station.
at 1 a.m. on 10.11.35. interpreted by J.D.S.131 Iguchi.

My name is Z. Takaoka. I am a shoe-maker living at
90 Darroch Road.

At about 9 p.m. 9.11.35 I was playing a gramophone at
my home and heard a sound which I thought was that of a m/car
tyre bursting. Immediately afterwards, my Chinese employee
named Woo Ziang Woo (胡祥祉) opened the front door of my house
from outside and informed me that a man was lying on the roadway.
Realizing that the sound that I heard was a report of a fire-
arm, I left my house and saw a man lying some distance to the
North of my house. I then approached and found that the man
was a sailor of the Japanese Naval Landing Party whom I know
by sight. He was lying on his side, his right arm outstretch-
ed, his body was at a slight angle to the edge of the road. His
position was near to the kerb of the west side of the road. He
was groaning, and although I spoke to him there was no reply.
In the meantime, two or three sailors arrived on the scene and
I told them to report the matter to the J.N.L. P. Headquarters.
Two or three Japanese civilians two of whom were dressed in
"Kimono" also came on the scene. I did not know who they were,
but I told one of them who was with a bicycle to report the
matter to the Headquarters.

At the moment I left my house I did not observe any person
in the vicinity.

This is true.

Z. Takaoka.

Taken in the presence of
Japanese Consular Police official S. Kozakai,
J.D.S.s Kasuo (D.R.) and Uemoto (R.C.)

居住在达罗克路90号的Z. Takaoka的陈述

日本人，于1935年11月10日凌晨1点在狄思威路警局录取。由日籍特别巡捕131号井口（Iguchi）翻译。

我叫Z. Takaoka。我是一名鞋匠，居住在达罗克路90号。

1935年11月9日晚上9点左右，我正在家里听留声机，听到一种声音，我以为是汽车轮胎爆裂的声音。紧接着，我的中国雇员胡祥祉（Woo Ziang Woo）从外面打开我家的大门，告诉我有人躺在马路上。意识到我听到的声音是枪声后，我离开家，看到一个人躺在我家以北一段距离的地方。我走近一看，发现那人是日本海军陆战队的一名水手，我面熟。他侧躺着，右臂伸展，身体与路边成轻微角度。他的位置靠近道路西侧的路缘石。他在呻吟，虽然我和他说话，但他没有回答。与此同时，两三名水手赶到现场，我让他们向日本海军陆战队总部报告此事。还有两三名日本平民来到现场，其中两人穿着“和服”。我不认识他们是谁，但我让其中一名骑自行车的人向总部报告此事。

在我离开家的那一刻，我没有观察到附近有任何人。

属实。

Z. Takaoka。

在日本领事馆警察官员小坂井（S. Kozakai）、日籍特别巡捕加须雄（Kasuo，负责日常巡逻）和植本（Uemoto，负责刑事侦缉）面前录取。

杂项报告第112/35号 D.Rd.，现构成本首次调查报告 176/35 D.Rd.的主题。

关于证人胡祥羽（Woo Ziang Woo），其书面陈述已转送，他首先由刑事侦缉处主任克雷格（Craig）警司、华捕119号和职员池永寿（Chi Yoong Shou）（原文不清），在日籍特别巡捕51号长尾（Hasuo）和日籍华捕83号大园（Osana）面前进行询问，他当时陈述，在听到爆炸声后，他看到一名日本士兵向东跑进丰乐里（Fong Loh Li），另一人躺在达罗克路上。

这与其书面陈述不符。

已安排由“C”区副总监康杜特（Conduit）警司于1935年11月12日再次向该证人录取陈述。

1935年11月11日上午9时，本站收到/发出来自海军中佐安田（Yasuda）的电话留言，称其宪兵队已找到一名女性，据信该女性即为1935年11月9日晚向中国巡捕2891号和2864号报告有人躺在达罗克路上的那名女性。安田中佐请求公共租界工部局警务处警官于1935年11月11日上午9时30分赶赴谋杀案现场，以便见证该女性陈述其对事件的看法。

上原（Uyehara）助理警务处长、霞（Kasumi）代理警司、布彻（Butcher）高级督察、克雷格（Craig）侦探警司和日籍特别巡捕51号长尾（Hasuo）赶赴现场。

On arriving as stated outside the hot water shop she heard

在公共安全局的配合下，该证人被带到本站并录取了陈述。她陈述，1935年11月9日晚，她到达达罗克路上一家热水店外，该处测量位置位于发现血泊地点以南108英尺。就在她到达该地点之前，即距达罗克路191号38英尺处，她遇到了一名水手（日本人）和一名平民，对于后者，除了知道他穿着深色西式服装和一顶毡帽（颜色不详）外，她无法提供更多描述。她陈述那名日本水手正沿着达罗克路西侧向北行走，那名平民则沿着达罗克路东侧朝与水手相同的方向行走。证人沿道路中央向南行走，从平民和水手之间穿过。根据该证人的说法，当她从他们中间穿过时，水手和平民彼此平行。

如所述到达热水店外时，她听到一声爆炸声，立即转身看到那名日本水手躺在马路上，然而，她没有看到那名平民。

1935年11月11日下午6时，在“C”区副总监的监督下，该证人在现场向日本海军陆战队陈述了她的版本。在场人员有：大杉（Chsugi，原文如此，应为Ohsugi）指挥官、安田（Yasuda）中佐。

其他在场人员包括：日本领事馆警察福山（Fukuyama）首席督察和奥村（Okumura）督察、日本警察松叶（Matoba）警长以及上原（Uyehara）先生，助理警务处长（日本人）。

日本海军陆战队的一名摄影师还拍摄了她沿达罗克路向南行走时经过水手和平民的位置照片，水手由松叶警长替代，平民由另一名在场的身穿西式服装的日本平民替代。

Dixwell Road Station,
November 13, 1935.

Re the Statement of Witness Woo Ziang Woo re.F.I.R. 176/35
------------------------------------------------------------

Made by J.D.S. 51 Hasuo

Sir,

I beg to state that on the night of the 9-11-35
I, together with C.D.C. 119, J.D.C. Osano and D.S. Craig,
questioned a witness, Woo Ziang Woo, at the Crime Branch
Office of this Station with the assistance of Clerk Chi
Yoong-shou.

The witness stated that at about 8.45 p.m. 9-11-35
he proceeded to a Japanese shoe-maker's shop at 90 Darroch
Road to collect money. On nearing the shop at about 9 p.m.
even date, he heard a loud report like a pistol shot and,
on looking in the direction, saw a Japanese sailor collapse
on the roadway and another sailor run into Fong Loh Lee.

I, therefore, cross-examined the witness asking
him how he could say that the man who had run away was a
Japanese sailor and further if he could obtain a distinct
view of the man from such a distance away in the darkness,
when he changed his statement stating that he saw that the
man was dressed in black clothes and that he could not say
that he was a Japanese or Chinese.

He then continued his statement relating that
he hurriedly entered the shoe-maker's shop and told
Mr. Takaoka of the incident. Mr. Takaoka and he, then,
went to the scene, and later he accompanied two Chinese
policemen to Dixwell Road Station as a witness.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
Hasuo (signed)
J.D.S. 51

先生，

谨此陈述，1935年11月9日晚，
我与华捕119号、日籍华捕大园（Osano）和侦探警司克雷格（Craig）一起，
在职员池永寿（Chi Yoong-shou）的协助下，
在本站犯罪科办公室询问了一名证人胡祥羽。

证人陈述，1935年11月9日晚上8点45分左右，
他前往达罗克路90号的一家日本鞋匠店收钱。在当天晚上9点左右接近该店时，
他听到一声像手枪射击般的巨响，朝那个方向看去，
看到一名日本水手倒在马路上，另一名水手跑进丰乐里（Fong Loh Lee）。

因此，我对证人进行了盘问，问他如何能说那个逃跑的人是日本水手，
以及在黑暗中从那么远的地方能否看清那个人，
随后他改变了陈述，称他看到那人穿着黑衣服，
不能确定他是日本人还是中国人。

他继续陈述，
他匆忙进入鞋匠店，将此事告诉了高冈（Takaoka）先生。
高冈先生和他随后前往现场，
后来他作为证人陪同两名中国警察前往狄思威路警局。

此致，
敬礼，
长尾（签名）

Report of investigations made by K. Suzukawa, Sergeant of
the Consular Police.    B. D. 7273

On receiving a telephone message from Constable Takimoto
stationed at the Consular Sub-Station, Siu Ching Li (士慶里).
I proceeded to the scene of the incident at 9.30 p.m. The
result of my investigation is as follows :-

Time and date of the incident

About 9.5 p.m. November 9, 1935.

Place

On the road in front of 236, Darroch Road.

Victim

Hideo Nakayama, 1st class seaman of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party.

Description of the wound

A .32 calibre bullet had penetrated from the right side of
the back of the head. The victim was unconscious and was
immediately removed to the Japanese Naval Landing Party Barracks
for treatment, but succumbed to his injuries at 1 a.m. November
10.

Conditions at the scene of the shooting

According to the statement of a Japanese named Takahashi,
residing in the vicinity of the scene of the crime, as he was
playing his gramophone in his home at about 9 p.m., he heard the
sound of a shot, but thought it was a ricksha tyre bursting.
Immediately afterwards, Woo Xiang Woo (胡祥和), a shoemaker
residing at 62 East Paoching Road, called at Takahashi's shop in
connection with business, and informed Takahashi that he had seen
a Japanese lying on the road. Takahashi went out and saw a
Japanese sailor, whom he knew only by sight, lying on the ground
on Darroch Road, in front of a garage owned by a Cantonese named
Ling. This man was lying on his right side, with his head
pointing in a north-easterly direction. His right arm was
outstretched, and his left arm was hanging by his side. He was
groaning. Takahashi called out to him to be brave, as the wound
was not serious. At this moment a sailor who was returning
to barracks, came up from the South. Takahashi told him what had
happened and asked him to report the matter to the Japanese
pages.zh:
领事警察警部 K. Suzukawa 的调查报告。 B. D. 7273

接到驻士庆里领事分署的巡警 Takimoto 的电话报告后，我于晚上9时30分赶赴事发地点。调查结果如下：-

案发时间与日期

1935年11月9日晚上9时05分左右。

地点

达罗路（Darroch Road）236号前的道路上。

受害者

日本海军陆战队一等水兵 Hideo Nakayama。

伤情描述

一颗 .32 口径子弹从后脑右侧射入。受害者昏迷不醒，随即被送往日本海军陆战队营房救治，但于11月10日凌晨1时因伤重不治身亡。

枪击现场情况

Report of telephone message from Terazo
Asahina, residing in Darroch Terrace.

"At 9.5 p.m., November 9, 1935, I heard
the sound of a shot outside my house. I went
out and saw a Sailor of the Naval Landing Party
lying in a pool of blood."

The above message was telephoned to the
Japanese Consulate at approximately 9.5 p.m.,
November 9, by Terazo Asahina, of Darroch Terrace.
The message was relayed to the Szu Ching Road
Sub-Station for investigation, and the Naval
Landing Party and the Chief of Police were informed.

Asahina states that he was asked by
Jenshiro Takaoka to send the message, as Takaoka
had no telephone in his house. Takaoka confirms
this statement, and says he despatched his wife
to ask Asahina to telephone the Consulate.

居住于达罗台（Darroch Terrace）的 Terazo Asahina 的电话报告。

“1935年11月9日晚上9时05分，我听到屋外有一声枪响。我走出去，看到一名海军陆战队水兵躺在血泊中。”

上述信息由达罗台的 Terazo Asahina 于11月9日晚上9时05分左右电话通报给日本领事馆。该信息被转达至四川路分署进行调查，并通知了海军陆战队和警务处处长。

Asahina 称，他是受 Jenshiro Takaoka 之托发送此消息，因为 Takaoka 家中没有电话。Takaoka 证实了这一说法，并称他派遣妻子去请求 Asahina 打电话给领事馆。

Report of investigations made by M. Suzukawa,
Sergeant of the Consular Police.

On receiving a telephone message from Constable
Tanimoto stationed at the Consular Sub-Station, Siu
Ching Li ( 小程里 ), I proceeded to the scene of the
incident at 9.20 p.m. The result of my investigation
is as follows:-

Time and Date of the Incident

About 9.5 p.m., November 9, 1935.

Place

On the road in front of 236, Darroch Road.

Victim

Hideo Nakayama, 1st class Seaman of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party.

Description of the wound

A .32 calibre bullet wound had penetrated from
the right side of the back of the head. The victim
was unconscious and was immediately removed to the
Japanese Naval Landing Party Barracks for treatment,
but succumbed to his injuries at 2 a.m., November 10.

Conditions at the scene of the shooting.

According to the statement of a Japanese named
Takaoka, residing in the vicinity of the scene of the
crime, as he was playing his gramophone in his home
at about 9 p.m., he heard the sound of a shot, but
thought it was a ricsha tyre bursting. Immediately
afterwards, Woo Ziang-woe ( 胡祥和 ), a shoemaker
residing at 62, East Paoshing Road, called at Takaoka's
shop in connection with business, and informed Takaoka
that he had seen a Japanese lying on the road.
Takaoka went out and saw a Japanese Sailor, whom he
knew only by sight, lying on the ground on Darroch
Road, in front of a garage owned by a Cantonese named
Ling. This man was lying on his right side, with
his head pointing in a north-easterly direction.

pages.en:
Report of Sergeant MIYAKAWA

19.50 Hrs.

A detailed account of the incident is still lacking.
It is reported that, according to a Chinese witness, two sailors
of the Landing Party were walking together and when they reached
a point in front of 286 Darroch Road, one of them fell. The other
sailor, it is stated, ran into a nearby alleyway, and the Chinese
witness is reported to have expressed the belief that the shooting
occurred between the two sailors.

Precautionary measures have been adopted by the Landing
Party in the area from Yang Pang Bridge to Headquarters.

The Chief of Police has been informed of the contents
of this message.

November 10, 10th year of Showa.
(1935)

Report on the secret entry of Chinese plain-clothes
soldiers into Shanghai.

Made by Sergeant Shigetaro Hisumi.

I beg to submit the following report on the present
situation:-

1) According to information obtained by Shigetaro Sanai
from Fu Yuet Liu and Chang Shu Ling, leaders of the Green Gang,
residing in the French Concession, on or about November 6 and
7 the Chinese Government secretly sent 6,000 plain-clothes
soldiers to the Chinese controlled territory of Shanghai to
assist the Bureau of Public Safety in suppressing any riots and
making speech that might take place following the introduction
of the currency reform. Yesterday the Bureau of Public Safety
made an investigation into the amount of silver dollars held
by the various shops and afterwards chopped and sealed them.

2) Inquiries were made regarding the source of the report
published in the evening issue of the Shanghai Mainichi on
November 9 to the effect that Chinese plain-clothes soldiers had
secretly entered Shanghai. This information, it has been
ascertained, was collected by Mr. Sanada and two other reporters
of the Shanghai Mainichi about a month ago from various Japanese
banks, companies and exchanges. The mission of the plain-
clothes soldiers as reported by the Shanghai Mainichi is the same
as that given in the first paragraph.

3) Shigetaro Sanai states that the chief of the Investigation
Department of the American Standard Oil Company had informed him
that a large number of Chinese plain-clothes soldiers have
secretly entered Shanghai and that the Company had detailed
many secret agents to secure information regarding the develop-
ments in the currency reform measures as well as in the case
of the murder of the Japanese marines.
pages.zh:
昭和10年（1935年）11月10日。

关于中国便衣士兵秘密进入上海的报告。

由警部 Shigetaro Hisumi 撰写。

谨就当前局势提交如下报告：-

1) 据 Shigetaro Sanai 从居住在法租界的青帮头目 Fu Yuet Liu 和 Chang Shu Ling 处获得的情报，中国政府于11月6日和7日左右，秘密派遣6000名便衣士兵进入上海华界，以协助公安局镇压因推行币制改革可能发生的任何骚乱和演讲活动。昨日，公安局对各商店持有的银元数量进行了调查，随后将其凿孔并封存。

2) 针对11月9日《上海每日新闻》晚刊刊登的关于中国便衣士兵秘密进入上海的报道，对其消息来源进行了查询。经查实，该信息是由《上海每日新闻》记者 Sanada 先生及另外两名记者约一个月前从各家日本银行、公司和交易所收集所得。《上海每日新闻》报道的便衣士兵的任务与第一段所述相同。

3) Shigetaro Sanai 称，美孚石油公司（American Standard Oil Company）调查部主任曾告知他，大量中国便衣士兵已秘密进入上海，该公司已派遣许多密探，以获取有关币制改革措施进展以及日本海军陆战队员被杀案件的情报。

November 9, 1935.

Report of investigations made by
Constable S. Kozakai.

(1) Statement of JINSHIRO TAKAKA.

My name is Jinshiro Takaka, age 53, of the
Takaka Shoemaker's Shop, 90 Darroch Road.

At about 9 p.m. November 9, as I was playing
my gramophone I heard the sound of a shot being
fired, but took no notice as I thought it was the
bursting of a ricksha tyre. Immediately afterwards,
Woo ( ), a shoemaker, came in and said there
was a man lying on the road. I went out to look
and saw a Sailor lying on the ground. I called
out to him to be brave as the wound was not serious,
but he only groaned and made no reply. By this
time two or three more Japanese had gathered there,
and I asked them to report this occurrence to the
Naval Landing Party, but immediately afterwards a
Sailor arrived. When I arrived on the scene I
did not see anybody else there.

(2) The scene of the crime.

There was only a blood stain on the road.

(3) Pistol.

The pistol was discovered at about 11.30 p.m.
and was immediately sent to the Arms Identification
Section of the Shanghai Municipal Police. It was
a small pistol.

1935年11月9日。

警员 S. Kozakai 的调查报告。

(1) JINSHIRO TAKAKA 的陈述。

我叫 Jinshiro Takaka，53岁，住在达罗克路（Darroch Road）90号高卡鞋店（Takaka Shoemaker's Shop）。

11月9日晚9点左右，我正在播放留声机时，听到一声枪响，但我没有在意，以为是人包车轮胎爆裂的声音。紧接着，鞋匠吴（Woo）（ ）进来说路上躺着一个人。我出去查看，看到一名水手躺在地上。我大声鼓励他要勇敢，说伤势并不严重，但他只是呻吟，没有回答。这时又有两三个日本人聚集在那里，我请他们向海军陆战队报告此事，但随即一名水手赶到。当我到达现场时，我没有看到其他人在场。

(2) 犯罪现场。

路上只有一处血迹。

(3) 手枪。

手枪于晚上11点30分左右被发现，并立即送往上海公共租界工部局警务处武器鉴定科。那是一支小型手枪。

(1) Jenshiro Takaoka 的陈述
我叫 Jenshiro Takaoka，53岁，住在达罗克路（Darroch Road）90号高冈鞋店（Takaoka Shoemaker's Shop）。
11月9日晚9点左右，我正在播放留声机时，听到一声枪响，但我没有在意，以为是人包车轮胎爆裂的声音。紧接着，鞋匠吴（胡）进来，说马路上躺着一个人。我出去查看，看到一名水手躺在地上。我大声鼓励他要勇敢，说伤势并不严重，但他只是呻吟，没有回答。这时又有两三个日本人聚集在那里，我请他们向海军陆战队报告此事，但随即一名水手赶到。当我到达现场时，我没有看到其他人在场。

(2) 犯罪现场。
路上只有一处血迹。

(3) 手枪
手枪于晚上11点30分左右被发现，并立即送往上海公共租界工部局警务处武器鉴定科。那是一支小型手枪。

November 9, 1935.
Constable Machiro Tamimoto.
Attached to the Sub-Station
on Sz Ching Road.

Report on the Murder of a Sailor of the Japanese
Special Naval Landing Party.

Enquiries were made into the murder of a sailor of the Japanese
Special Naval Landing Party on Darroch Road at about 9 p.m. this date
(November 9) and the following facts ascertained:-

Hideo Nakayama, aged 24, 1st class seaman of the Japanese
Special Naval Landing Party, visited two naval entertainment houses
in Mei Mei Li (美楣里) on the afternoon of November 9. At about 9 p.m
he left the entertainment house for the barracks of the Naval Landing
Party. On the way, he was shot through the head with a pistol bullet
fired by an unknown person at the corner of Darroch Road and Peong
Leh Li. He collapsed unconscious on the spot. Two Chinese constables
(Nos. 2891 and 2864) of the S.M.P. rushed to the scene and immediately
reported the matter to Dixwell Road Station. Upon receipt of the
information Sergeant Yasukawa and a foreign policeman No. 250 (Wilkinson)
attached to that Station proceeded to the scene. Sergeant Yasukawa
reported the matter to the Naval Landing Party. About 16 members of
the Landing Party arrived at the scene and removed Nakayama to the
Landing Party Barracks on a stretcher. I reached the scene after
Nakayama had been removed to the Landing Party Barracks. Later many
members of the Landing Party and S.M.P. attended and posted guards
and conducted investigations.

Later, a Chinese named Woo Ziang Wu who had seen the sailor
collapse, was interrogated. According to this witness, he is known
to a Japanese named Takaoka, a shoemaker, who resides in a house
about 40 feet from the scene of the shooting. As he reached the
front of Takaoka's house he heard a pistol shot. He looked in the
direction of the report and noticed a sailor lying on the ground and
a man running into the Peong Leh Li. The man who escaped was attired
in a blue coat and long trousers but was hatless.

关于日本特别海军陆战队一名水手被谋杀的报告。

就本日（11月9日）晚9点左右在达罗克路发生的日本特别海军陆战队一名水手被谋杀一事进行了查询，查明以下事实：-

中山秀夫，24岁，日本特别海军陆战队一等水兵，于11月9日下午在美楣里（Mei Mei Li）的两家海军娱乐社逗留。晚9点左右，他离开娱乐社前往海军陆战队营房。途中，在达罗克路与彭乐里（Peong Leh Li）转角处，被一名身份不明者用手枪子弹击中头部。他当场昏迷倒地。两名公共租界工部局警务处华捕（编号2891和2864）赶赴现场，并立即向狄思威路（Dixwell Road）捕房报告此事。接到消息后，隶属于该捕房的安川巡长和一名外籍警员250号（威尔金森）前往现场。安川巡长将此情况报告给海军陆战队。约16名陆战队成员抵达现场，用担架将中山抬往陆战队营房。我在中山被抬往陆战队营房后到达现场。随后，许多陆战队成员和公共租界工部局警务处人员到场，布置警戒并进行调查。

后来，对目睹水手倒地的华人吴祥武（Woo Ziang Wu）进行了讯问。据该证人称，他认识一名叫高冈（Takaoka）的日本鞋匠，此人居住在距枪击现场约40英尺的一所房子里。当他走到高冈家门前时，听到一声枪响。他朝枪声方向看去，注意到一名水手躺在地上，还有一名男子跑进彭乐里（Peong Leh Li）。逃跑的男子身穿蓝色外套和长裤，但未戴帽子。

达罗克路的一名学校教师羽田（Hada）的妻子称，当她听到枪声赶到现场时，

pages.en:

found more than 10 persons already there.
Takaoka, a shoemaker, is said to have rushed to the scene
after being informed of the shooting by the Chinese named Woo
Ziang-wu.
Chinese constables Nos. 2891 and 2864 of the S.M.P. stated
that when they arrived at the scene there was nobody there except
Nakayama, the injured sailor.
A pistol was found between a wall and a watchman's hut in
Jeong Loh Li about 80 yards from Darroch Road. Its muzzle was
pointed toward North Szechnuen Road and one shot appears to have
been fired from it. A Chinese watchman named Lee Hong Ping (李鴻賓)

公共租界工部局警务处华捕编号2891和2864称，当他们到达现场时，除了受伤的水手中山外，没有其他人在场。

November 10, 10th year of Showa (1935)

Report on the murder of a marine of the Landing Party.
Made by Constable Takeo Nagaoka.

As regards the recent movements of the late Hideo
Nakayama, age 24, first class marine of the 7th Company
4th Battalion of the Shanghai Special Landing Party at the
Iansho (Translator's note - This is a brothel especially
established for marines) in Mei Mei Lee, North Szechuen Road,
I have already submitted a report yesterday. I now beg to
submit a further report on the late Nakayama. For the past
two years he was in love with a waitress named Chito Sakai
alias Tayeko, age 24, of the Komu Cafe. He used to visit
the Komu Cafe on an average of two or three times a month
and passed nights with the girl. In September, previous
to the departure of Chito Sakai for Japan, Nakayama visited
her whenever he had leave of absence from the barracks and
passed nights with her on six occasions. The term of Chito
Sakai's service with the Komu Cafe expired at the end of
August, but she remained there during the whole of September
to earn her passage to Japan. At the beginning of October,
she returned to Japan to get married. It is reported that she
has been married to a certain person in Osaka. After the
departure of Chito Sakai for Japan, Nakayama for the first time
visited the Baigetsu Cafe in company with Masao Awoki, 1st
Class Seaman of the same Company, on the night of November 8,
the date previous to the shooting incident. Awoki passed
the night with Umegiku at the Baigetsu Cafe, while Nakayama
went to the Komu Cafe and passed the night with Miyo Hara alias
Miyoke, aged 21.. Nakayama and Awoki returned to the barracks
on the following morning. They were very intimate friends but
as the dates of their leave did not coincide, they were not
pages.zh:
昭和10年（1935年）11月10日

关于陆战队一名海军士兵被谋杀的报告。
由长冈武夫警员撰写。

关于已故中山秀夫（24岁，上海特别陆战队第四大队第七中队一等海军士兵）近期在北四川路美眉里（Mei Mei Lee）艳所（译者注：这是专为海军士兵设立的妓院）的活动情况，我已于昨日提交报告。现谨就已故中山的情况提交进一步报告。过去两年，他一直爱恋着“古木”咖啡馆（Komu Cafe）的一名女招待，名叫酒井千代（Chito Sakai），别名泰子（Tayeko），24岁。他平均每月去“古木”咖啡馆两三次，并与该女子过夜。在酒井千代返回日本之前的9月份，中山每当从营房请假时就去看望她，并与她共度了六个夜晚。酒井千代在“古木”咖啡馆的服务期于8月底结束，但她整个9月都留在那里以赚取回日本的路费。10月初，她返回日本结婚。据报道，她已与大阪的某人结婚。酒井千代前往日本后，中山在枪击事件发生的前一天，即11月8日晚，首次与同中队的上等水兵青木正雄（Masao Awoki）一同前往“白月”咖啡馆（Baigetsu Cafe）。青木在“白月”咖啡馆与梅菊（Umegiku）过夜，而中山则去了“古木”咖啡馆，与21岁的原美代（Miyo Hara），别名美代子（Miyoke），过夜。中山和青木于次日早晨返回营房。他们是亲密的朋友，但由于他们的休假日期不一致，他们并未

pages.en:
-2-

able to go out together. Nakayama was granted special
liberty on November 8 as he was due to return to Japan on
the 13th, so he went out in company with Awoki. November 9,
the day on which the shooting incident occurred, was Nakayama's
regular day of leave. Nakayama was asked by Awoki to deliver
a letter to Umegiku of the Baigetsu Cafe. Nakayama went to the
Baigetsu Cafe to deliver the letter and remained there for about
30 minutes awaiting the girl's reply. After receiving the
letter of reply and a box of cakes from Umegiku, Nakayama proceeded
to the Komu Cafe where he stayed about 10 minutes chatting with
Miyo Hara alias Miyoko. It is reported that Umegiku of the
Baigetsu Cafe saw Nakayama leave the Mei Mei Li alleyway alone
before 9 p.m.

From inquiries made at other cafes the following information
was obtained from a waitress of the "Shanghai Club" Cafe named
Kuniye Miyake alias Kuniko, aged 25:- "I am not sure about the
exact time but I believe it was about 8 p.m. when I saw Nakayama
standing in front of my place with two or three other Sailors.
I went inside without paying any attention to them because I had
a visitor at the time. I do not know where he went. I know his
name because I heard his friends call him "Nakayama" when he came
to my cafe in company with two or three other sailors in January
this year. Since that time Nakayama used to visit my place but
he never spent a night there."

At the Cafe Taishokan it was learned that Nakayama used to
visit the cafe in company with two or three other sailors but never
spent the night there. Nakayama was not known at other places.

As has been already mentioned, Nakayama was not well known
among the cafes in the Mei Mei Li alleyway. For this reason,
inquiries there have had no satisfactory results. The girl with
whom Nakayama was in love was married at Osaka, and there is no
reason to believe that he had been involved in any other love
affair or that any person or persons had any ill-feeling against him.

Further enquiries are proceeding.
pages.zh:
-2-

能够一同外出。中山因定于13日返回日本，故于11月8日获准特别休假，遂与青木一同外出。11月9日，即枪击案发生之日，是中山的常规休假日。中山受青木之托，向百月咖啡馆（Baigetsu Cafe）的梅菊（Umegiku）递交一封信件。中山前往百月咖啡馆送信，并在那里停留约30分钟，等待该女子的回信。收到梅菊的回信及一盒糕点后，中山前往小姆咖啡馆（Komu Cafe），在那里与化名美代子（Miyoko）的原美代（Miyo Hara）聊天约10分钟。据报，百月咖啡馆的梅菊看见中山在晚上9点前独自离开美美里弄堂。

通过对其他咖啡馆的调查，从“上海俱乐部”咖啡馆（"Shanghai Club" Cafe）一名名叫三宅国枝（Kuniye Miyake）、化名国子（Kuniko）、25岁的女招待处获得如下信息：“我不确定确切时间，但我相信大约是晚上8点，我看见中山和另外两三名水手站在我的店门口。当时我有客人，所以我没注意他们就进去了。我不知道他去了哪里。我知道他的名字，因为今年一月他和另外两三名水手来我咖啡馆时，我听见他的朋友叫他‘中山’。从那以后，中山常来我这里，但他从未在此过夜。”

在大正馆咖啡馆（Cafe Taishokan）获悉，中山过去常与另外两三名水手一起来该咖啡馆，但从未在此过夜。中山在其他地方并不为人所知。

如前所述，中山在美美里弄堂的各家咖啡馆中并不广为人知。因此，在那里的调查未取得满意结果。中山所爱恋的女子已在大阪结婚，没有理由相信他卷入其他恋情，或有任何人对他怀有恶意。

进一步调查正在进行中。

关于陆战队海军陆战队员被杀案的报告。由警员长冈武雄（Takeo Nagaoka）撰写。

-------

关于上海特别陆战队第四大队第七中队一等兵、现年24岁的已故中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）近期在北四川路美美里伊那穗（Ianaho）（译者注——这是专为海军陆战队员设立的妓院）的活动情况，我已于昨日提交报告。现谨就已故中山的情况提交补充报告。在过去两年中，他与小姆咖啡馆（Koma Cafe）一名名叫酒井千代（Chito Sakai）、化名照子（Teruko）、24岁的女招待相恋。他平均每月去小姆咖啡馆两三次，并与该女子过夜。在酒井千代返回日本之前的9月份，中山每逢营房休假便去探望她，共有六次与她过夜。酒井千代在小姆咖啡馆的服务期于8月底结束，但她为了赚取回日本的路费，整个9月仍留在那里。10月初，她返回日本结婚。据报，她已与大阪的某人士结婚。酒井千代赴日后，中山首次在同公司一等水兵青木正男（Masao Aoki）的陪同下，于枪击案前一晚即11月8日晚造访大月咖啡馆（Daigetsu Cafe）。青木在大月咖啡馆与梅菊（Umegiku）过夜，而中山则前往小姆咖啡馆，与清原

The following information has been received from
the local Japanese Consular Police regarding the identity
of the murderer of Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party:-

From what is being said amongst Chinese residents in
the vicinity of the scene of the crime and in Fong Loh Li
alleyway, there is not the least doubt that the person who
shot Nakayama was a Chinese youth who wore a "sports jacket",
the colour of which at first sight appeared to be black, and
a pair of trousers tight-fitting in the legs. The jacket
was buttonless and of this design [图] . He was hatless.

He ran at a terrific speed along Fong Loh Li towards North
Szechuen Road. His hair was so long that when he was running
it bobbed up and down. He is slim of build and his height
is about 5 feet 6 or 7 inches. The witness is reported to
have said that, after careful thought, the appearance of
the aforementioned person indicated him to be a Cantonese.

The Chinese who had witnessed this informed his
Chinese friends of what he had seen, but refused to speak
about it to others. If any person having the appearance of
a Japanese were to approach this witness, he would stop
talking as a matter of precaution. This witness is reported
to have further stated that none of the persons taken to
the Police Station had made a statement according to the facts.

Notes
1. A witness who was interrogated at the Police Station soon
after the incident said as follows:- "The culprit was wearing
clothing similar to that of the sailor." Later, the Japanese
Naval Landing Party issued a statement that "this was an
objectionable statement" and that "the inquiries were not
sufficient, etc." Probably it was due to this that the
Municipal Police have stated that "the witness said that the
culprit was wearing a foreign dress."
2. In view of these circumstances, any ignorant Chinese

根据案发地附近及丰乐里（Fong Loh Li）弄堂中国居民的说法，毫无疑问，枪击中山的人是一名中国青年，身穿一件乍看之下似乎是黑色的“运动夹克”，搭配裤腿紧身的长裤。夹克无纽扣，款式如图 [图] 。他未戴帽子。

他沿着丰乐里向北四川路方向飞奔。他的头发很长，奔跑时上下晃动。他身材瘦削，身高约5英尺6或7英寸。据报证人称，经仔细回想，上述人员的相貌表明其为广东人。

目睹此事的中国人将所见告知其中国朋友，但拒绝向其他人谈论此事。如果有看似日本人的人接近这位证人，出于谨慎，他会停止谈话。据报该证人还指出，被带到警察局的人员中，无人作出符合事实的陈述。

附注
1. 案发后不久在警察局接受讯问的一名证人说：“罪犯穿着与水手类似的服装。”后来，日本海军陆战队发表声明称“此言论令人反感”且“调查不充分等”。市警察局称“证人说罪犯穿着西式服装”，可能正是由于上述原因所致。

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE: TEXT OF JUDGMENT DISMISSING APPEAL

The appeal of Yang Wen Dao and Yih Hai Sung against the sentence of death passed on them by the First Special District Court in connection with the Nakayama Murder Case on Darroch Road on November 9 last year, was dismissed by the Second Branch Kiangsu High Court on December 9.
Copies of the decision were sent on December 10 to the appellants and their attorneys.
As great attention was paid to this case by the public, the full text of the decision of the High Court dismissing the appeal is hereby published.

FACTS

Yang Wen Dao was the chairman of the former Hung Zen Mutual Aid Association, while Yih Hai Sung, alias Siao Kwangtung, was a member of the Association. Later, owing to the departure from Shanghai of Yang Wen Dao, the Association was dissolved. In January, in the 23rd year of the Chinese Republic, Yang Wen Dao returned to Shanghai. Together with Yih Hai Sung and others, Yang Wen Dao organized two bodies known as the Dong Jen(同仁) and Dong Nyi(同義), of both of which Yang Wen Dao was the chairman with Yih Hai Sung as member. Owing to lack of members, the influence of these two federations was smaller than that of the former Hung Zen Association. In an attempt to expand their influence, Yang Wen Dao and Yih Hai Sung conspired together to carry out attacks on Japanese officials and marines so as to stir up disturbances. Consequently they made their plans, and carried out an inspection on Darroch Road at 3 p.m. November 3. On the night of November 5, they drew lots in the Dong Nyi Federation at No.71, Yung Chi Lee(永吉里), Range Road, and Yih Hai Sung was chosen by lot to execute the plan. At 8 p.m. November 9, Yang Wen Dao, Yih Hai Sung and Jack (介克) left the Moon Palace Hotel and walked to the Japanese School on North Szechuen Road. Yang Wen Dao produced a pistol from a book and handed it to Yih Hai Sung. They then walked to Darroch Road and saw a Japanese marine named Nakayama walking there. Following the Japanese marine up to the vicinity of Feng Loh Li(豐樂里) on Darroch Road, Yih Hai Sung drew his pistol and shot the marine in the head from behind. Soon after, Nakayama died. Yih Hai Sung ran into Feng Loh Li and threw his pistol under a Police watchman's box in the Terrace. He made good his escape. All this was discovered by the Police. The appellants were arrested. In the house of Yang Wen Dao at No.18, Tung An Li(同安里), Tongshan Road, a book on Physics, which was used to conceal the pistol, was found by the Police and handed to the Court.

REASONS

There is a round wound of entry of about seven milimetre in diameter at about 6 centimetres above the rear of the outer cavity of the ear and about 7 centimetres on the right side of the central joint of the back part of the head of the victim, the Japanese marine Hideo

中山案：驳回上诉之判决书全文

杨文道与易海松就去年11月9日发生在达罗路（Darroch Road）的中山谋杀案中，被第一特区地方法院判处死刑一事提出上诉，江苏省高等法院第二分院于12月9日驳回其上诉。
判决书副本已于12月10日送达上诉人及其律师。
鉴于公众对此案高度关注，现公布高等法院驳回上诉之判决全文。

事实

杨文道系前洪zen互助会（Hung Zen Mutual Aid Association，音译：洪珍互助会）主席，而易海松，别名小广东，为该会会员。后来，由于杨文道离开上海，该会解散。民国二十三年一月，杨文道返回上海。杨文道与易海松等人组织了两个团体，分别名为“同仁”和“同义”，杨文道担任这两个团体的主席，易海松为会员。由于成员不足，这两个联合会的影响力不及前洪zen互助会。为了扩大影响力，杨文道与易海松共谋袭击日本官员及海军陆战队员，以制造骚乱。于是他们制定计划，并于11月3日下午3时对达罗路进行了踩点。11月5日晚，他们在虹口路（Range Road）永吉里71号的同义会内抽签，易海松中签执行该计划。11月9日晚8时，杨文道、易海松和介克（Jack）离开月宫饭店，步行至北四川路的日本学校。杨文道从一本书中取出手枪，交给易海松。随后他们走到达罗路，看见一名名叫中山的日本海军陆战队员正在那里行走。易海松跟随该日本海军陆战队员到达罗路丰乐里附近，从背后拔枪击中其头部。不久，中山死亡。易海松逃入丰乐里，将手枪扔在露台的一名巡捕岗亭下。他成功逃脱。这一切均被警方查明。上诉人被捕。警方在杨文道位于同山路同安里18号的住所内，搜获了用于藏匿手枪的一本物理学书籍，并移交法院。

理由

受害者日本海军陆战队员秀夫

quantity of brain was visible outside the skull and much
blood escaped owing to the rupture of the artery.    This
clearly shows that the deceased had died of hemorrhage and the
effects of a head wound caused by the bullet wound in the
head.    All these facts were established by Mr. Ogawa,
Military Doctor of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, after
he had made an examination and a report to this effect was
drawn up by him.    Furthermore, a spent bullet was later
found by Japanese Constable No.61 at the scene of the incident
about 8 feet to the south of the blood stains.    Simultaneous
with this finding, Japanese detective No.50 found at that
place an empty cartridge, while Japanese Sub-Inspector
"Kayinyasu" found the pistol No.241146 which still contained
six rounds of ammunition under a watchman's wooden box in
Feng Loh Li alleyway.    Both the spent bullet and the empty
cartridge found at the scene of the incident and which had
caused the death of the Japanese marine were fired from
this pistol.    Moreover, this fact has also been established
by the S.M.P. ballistics expert Mr. Caley (vide the report
and photographs which he submitted to the Court).    The
book on Practical Physics which was used for the purpose
of concealing the said pistol was found at the home of Yang
Wen Dao at House No.18 Tung An Li off Tongshan Road on
April 19.    In view of the fact that the hole excavated
inside the book is similar in length, width and size as the
pistol in question, and the rust marks remaining in the hole
of the book corresponded exactly with those of the pistol
in more than 40 points, it is therefore evident that the
book in question was the one that was used for the purpose
of concealing the said pistol but not other pistols of a
similar type as the one seized.    This fact has been
corroborated as a result of examination by the S.M.P. Finger
Print expert Mr. Dickson and the Medico-Legal Laboratory
of the Ministry of Justice.    Furthermore, when the book
in question was taken back to the Police Station and placed
on the desk after its discovery, Yang Wen Dao, upon seeing
it, at once admitted that the book belonged to him before
he was even interrogated.    This admission was made in the
presence of D.S.I. Crowther and Mr. Kawashima and can be
referred to the verbal reports made in the Court of First
Instance (vide the written records of the Court of First
Instance taken down on July 8).    Even on April 20 when
Yang Wen Dao was arraigned before the Court of First Instance
the first time, he admitted that the hole inside the book
was excavated by him for the purpose of concealing a pistol,
although he later retracted this statement and asserted that
the book which he had used for the purpose of concealing
a pistol was one in English, that the licence of his pistol
was secured from the Bureau of Public Safety, that the pistol
belonged to one Li Mou (李 Mou ) and that the book in question
was not his property but was one that had been planted in
his house by Yang Chien Chung (楊健忠) to incriminate him.
However, when the pistol, a "Demon", which was loaned to
Yang Wen Dao by Li Mou, was secured from the Bureau of Public

中山（Hideo Nakayama）耳廓外腔后方约6厘米处及后脑中央接缝右侧约7厘米处，有一个直径约7毫米的圆形射入伤口。子弹触及头部动脉，导致大量出血。此外，在前额部位有一个直径约2厘米的不规则形状射出伤口。周围的颅骨严重受损。受损部位肿胀严重，充血。此外，颅骨外可见大量脑组织溢出，且因动脉破裂流出大量血液。这清楚地表明，死者死于头部枪伤引起的出血及头部创伤后果。上述事实由日本海军陆战队军医小川先生（Mr. Ogawa）经检查后确认，并由他撰写了相关报告。此外，日本第61号警员后来在案发现场血迹以南约8英尺处发现了一枚弹头。与此同时，日本第50号侦探在该处发现了一个空弹壳，而日本副巡官“Kayinyasu”（音译：加藤康保？）在丰乐里弄堂的一个巡捕木箱下发现了仍装有六发子弹的第241146号手枪。在案发现场发现的导致该日本海军陆战队员死亡的弹头和空弹壳，均由这把手枪发射。此外，这一事实也已由工部局警务处弹道专家凯利先生（Mr. Caley）证实（参见其提交给法院的报告和照片）。用于藏匿上述手枪的《实用物理学》一书，于4月19日在同山路同安里18号杨文道家中被发现。鉴于书内挖出的孔洞在长度、宽度和大小上与涉案手枪相似，且书孔内残留的锈迹与手枪上的锈迹在40多处完全吻合，因此显而易见，该书是用于藏匿上述手枪的，而非其他与被扣押手枪类似类型的手枪。这一事实已得到工部局警务处指纹专家迪克森先生（Mr. Dickson）及司法部法医实验室的检查佐证。此外，当该书被发现并被带回警察局放在桌上时，杨文道一见到它，甚至在受审之前就立即承认该书属于他。这一供述是在副巡官克罗瑟（D.S.I. Crowther）和川岛先生（Mr. Kawashima）面前作出的，可参照初审法庭的口头报告（参见7月8日记录的初审法庭笔录）。即使在4月20日杨文道首次被提审至初审法庭时，他也承认书内的孔洞是他为了藏匿手枪而挖的，尽管他后来撤回了这一说法，声称他用来藏匿手枪的书是一本英文书，他的持枪证是从公安局获得的，手枪属于李某（Li Mou），而涉案书籍并非他的财产，而是杨健忠（Yang Chien Chung）栽赃在他家里以陷害他的。然而，当警方从公共安

Safety by the Municipal Police for comparison, it was found that this pistol did not fit the hole in the book; moreover, Yang Chien Chung appeared in the Court of First Instance and denied the allegation that he had planted the book as he had no personal grudge against Yang Wen Dao, nor had he ever visited the home of Yang Wen Dao, nor did he know where Yang Wen Dao lived. He further stated that he had never seen this book before. From this, there can be no doubt that the spent bullet and the empty cartridge produced in Court had caused the death of the Japanese marine Hideo Nakayama and that the book on Practical Physics that was used to conceal the weapon was the property of Yang Wen Dao.

Now as to the question of whether or not the appellants are the murderers: It is to be noted that the accused Yih Hai Sung during his trial in the Court of First Instance at first denied having committed the crime and although later he admitted the crime, yet his statements were very contradictory because at first he stated that it was Yang Wen Dao who fired the shot and later he retracted this statement and admitted that he alone was responsible for the crime and that it had no connection whatever with Yang Wen Dao and others. It was only until after he had been informed of the significance of the case and closely examined by the Court of First Instance that the accused began to state how Yang Wen Dao had planned to assassinate Japanese marines, how the matter was discussed at the Dong Nyi Federation, how they proceeded together to make an inspection of the place where the crime was to be committed, how they later drew lots at the Federation and how he drew the lot which contained the word "go", etc. Yih Hai Sung further said:- "On November 9 last year, I occupied Room No. 9 in the Moon Palace Hotel (月宮飯店) under the name of Hsia Tsung Kee (夏春記). At about 8 p.m. that day, Yang Wen Dao, Jack and I left the Moon Palace Hotel and walked northwards to the Japanese school when Yang Wen Dao took out a pistol from within a book and handed it to me. On arrival at Damoch Road, we saw a Japanese marine. Yang Wen Dao made a sign to me with his mouth. I followed the marine a short distance. As there were no policemen, I shot him, after which I escaped through Dou Lo Li (兜率里), threw the pistol away and returned to the Moon Palace Hotel. All that I have said this time is true and I will not retract." The Judge in the Court of First Instance took Yih Hai Sung to the spot for investigation. In the presence of the Judge, Yih Hai Sung gave full particulars regarding the place where Yang Wen Dao had given him the pistol, where he saw the marine, where he opened fire and how he escaped after the shooting. In the meantime, Yih corrected the point in which witness Hu Ziang Wu (胡祥秋), during a reconstruction, had said that he saw a man running into Feng Loh Li from behind an electric pole; Yih said that he went direct to Feng Loh Li and did not go behind an electric pole. This statement is more logical. Witness Hu Ziang Wu said that when he heard a pistol report that day, he saw a man wearing black clothing, running into Feng Loh Li. Witness Pan Chiao Yin (潘巧英) stated that when she was walking

全局获取李某借给杨文道的“恶魔”牌（Demon）手枪进行比对时，发现这把手枪并不适合书中的孔洞；此外，杨健忠出庭初审，否认栽赃书籍的指控，称他与杨文道并无私人恩怨，也从未去过杨文道家，甚至不知道杨文道住在哪里。他还表示以前从未见过这本书。由此，毫无疑问，庭上出示的弹头和空弹壳导致了日本海军陆战队员中山秀夫的死亡，且用于藏匿武器的《实用物理学》一书归杨文道所有。

至于上诉人是否为凶手的问题：值得注意的是，被告易海松在初审法庭受审时，起初否认犯罪，虽然后来承认了罪行，但其供词前后矛盾极大，因为他起初声称是杨文道开的枪，后来又撤回该说法，承认罪责全在于他一人，与杨文道等人毫无关系。直到被告知案件的重要性并经初审法庭严密讯问后，被告才开始陈述杨文道如何策划刺杀日本海军陆战队员，如何在同义会讨论此事，如何一同前往预定作案地点踩点，以及后来如何在会内抽签，而他抽中了写有“去”字的签等情节。易海松进一步说道：“去年11月9日，我以夏春记（Hsia Tsung Kee）的名字住在月宫饭店9号房间。当天晚上8点左右，杨文道、介克和我离开月宫饭店，向北步行至日本学校，途中杨文道从一本书里取出一把手枪交给我。到达达莫克路（Damoch Road，即达罗路）时，我们看到一名日本海军陆战队员。杨文道用嘴型向我示意。我跟随该陆战队员走了一小段路。由于周围没有警察，我向他开枪，随后通过兜率里（Dou Lo Li）逃跑，扔掉手枪，返回月宫饭店。我这次所说的一切都是真实的，我不会翻供。”初审法官带易海松到现场进行调查。在法官面前，易海松详细说明了杨文道给他手枪的地点、他看到陆战队员的地点、他开枪的地点以及开枪后如何逃跑的情况。在此期间，易海松纠正了证人胡祥秋（Hu Ziang Wu）在重建现场时所说的一个细节，胡祥秋称看到一个人从电线杆后面跑进丰乐里；易海松说他是直接跑进丰乐里的，并没有经过电线杆后面。这一说法更符合逻辑。证人胡祥秋说，那天听到枪声时，他看到一个穿着黑色衣服的人跑进丰乐里。证人潘巧英（Pan Chiao Yin）陈述说，当她正在行走
