SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of Poo Chau Ying (潘周英).
native of Kampo D.S.I. M.L. Ureuther.
D. Rd. Stn. taken by me
at on the 11-11-35 and interpreted by Clerk Li Yang Kao.

My name is Poo Chau Ying, aged 17 years, native of Kampo,
maid servant, employed by a Mr. Koem (河井), Japanese, resid-
ing at No. 95 Wing On Terrace.

At about 8 p.m. on the 9-11-35, I was instructed by my
Japanese mistress to take her female child, aged 3 years, to
her friend's house on Kiangwan Road, near the railway - for
amusement.

I proceeded by the North Szechuen Road. I arrived there
about 10 minutes after leaving 95 Wing On Terrace.

I left the address about one hour later. I proceeded
along Darroch Road carrying the child in my arms until I came
to a hot water shop on Darroch Road. Just before I arrived at
the hot water shop, I saw two men - one a Japanese sailor and
the other a civilian wearing dark foreign styled clothing - the
clothing was a short jacket and long trousers and a felt hat,
colour of hat I do not know. I could not distinguish his face.

At this time I saw a private ricksha on the East side of the
road - the coolie was sleeping between the shafts. I was walk-
ing in the middle of the roadway and passed between the sailor
and the civilian. I was nearer to the civilian. I cannot say
what his nationality was. After the Japanese sailor and the
civilian had passed me and I had arrived near the hot water shop,
situated on the East side of Darroch Road, I heard a report of
an explosion. I then turned round and saw the Japanese sailor
lying on the roadway. I could see the white on his collar. I
did not see the civilian when I turned round, but shortly after-
wards I saw a male Chinese wearing blue short jacket and pants
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。
以下为潘周英（Poo Chau Ying）之供词。
籍贯：江湾（Kampo）。警探长 Ureuther。
狄思威路巡捕房。由本人于1935年11月11日在 [地点缺失] 录取，并由职员李仰高（Li Yang Kao）翻译。

我叫潘周英，现年17岁，籍贯江湾，女佣，受雇于居住在永安里95号的日本人河井（Koem）先生。

1935年11月9日晚8时许，我的日本女主人吩咐我带她3岁的女儿去江湾路铁路附近的一位朋友家玩耍。

我经由北四川路前往。离开永安里95号后约10分钟到达那里。

约一小时后我离开该地址。我抱着孩子沿大通路（Darroch Road）前行，直到来到大通路的一家热水店。就在我到达热水店之前，我看见两个人——一个是日本水手，另一个是身穿深色西式服装的平民——其服装为短夹克和长裤，头戴毡帽，帽子颜色我不清楚。我看不清他的脸。

此时，我看见路东停着一辆私人黄包车——车夫正在车杠间睡觉。我走在马路中间，从水手和平民之间穿过。我离那个平民更近一些。我说不出他是哪国人。在日本水手和平民经过我之后，当我走近位于大通路东侧的热水店时，我听到一声爆炸响。随后我转过身，看见那名日本水手躺在马路上。我能看到他衣领上的白色部分。我转身时没有看见那个平民，但不久之后，我看见一名身穿蓝色短夹克和裤子的中国男子

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of
native of
at
on the
Poo Chun Ying.
taken by me
and interpreted by

come out from Darroch Terrace, on the West side of the road, this
man I have seen before carrying shoes - so I know he is a shoe-
maker. I saw some Chinese policemen at Kiangwan Road and North
Szechuen Road corner - but I do not know how many.

After seeing the sailor lying on the road I ran into the Wing
On Terrace through the hot water shop. There were many Chinese
in the hot water shop but I did not speak to them. When I
arrived at my master's house I told my mistress, whilst I was
returning from her friend's house, I saw a Japanese sailor and a
civilian, and I saw the sailor lying on the road shouting. I
do not know what he was shouting. I did not tell my mistress
anything else. I then washed some clothing.

The mistress then asked me if I knew who fired the shot. I
told her I did not know. My mistress then said the shot must
have been fired by a Chinese and there may be a fight.

After I had finished washing the clothing I went to bed.

On the 10-11-36, I went out with the child again and returned
late, so my mistress scolded me. I then ran away to my aunt's
home in Chapei - this is where the Police found me on the 11-11-
36.

Finger-printed- Poo Chun Ying.

Taken in the presence of Supt. Genduit, D.D.O. "C", J.D.S.
El Mozo and J.D.C. 83 Osano.

(Note by D.S.I. Crowther. Witness is of the country type, only
about 1 year in Shanghai, when being questioned at the scene by
D.D.O. "C" in presence of Lieut. Commander Yasuda, Commander
Ohagi, Mr. Uyehara, A.C.P., Chief Inspt. Fukuyama of the Japanese
Consular Police, she stated she had been to the King Yuh Fong, off
North Szechuen Road at the rear of the Headquarters of the J.M.L.
Party.
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。

以下为
潘春英（Poo Chun Ying）。
籍贯：[原文缺失]
由本人于 [日期缺失] 在 [地点缺失] 录取，并由 [译者姓名缺失] 翻译

从路西的大通坊（Darroch Terrace）走出来，这个人我以前见过他携带鞋子——所以我知道他是个鞋匠。我在江湾路与北四川路路口看见了一些中国警察——但我不知道具体有多少人。

看见水手躺在路上后，我穿过热水店跑进永安里。热水店里有很多中国人，但我没有和他们说话。当我回到主人家时，我告诉女主人，我在从她朋友家回来的路上，看见一个日本水手和一个平民，我还看见那个水手躺在路上喊叫。我不知道他在喊什么。我没有告诉女主人其他事情。然后我去洗了一些衣服。

女主人随后问我是否知道是谁开的枪。我告诉她我不知道。女主人随后说，开枪的一定是中国人，可能会发生打斗。

洗完衣服后，我就去睡觉了。

1936年11月10日（注：原文如此，疑为1935年笔误），我再次带孩子外出，回来得很晚，因此女主人责骂了我。随后我逃往闸北我姨妈家——这就是1936年11月11日（注：原文如此，疑为1935年笔误）警察找到我的地方。

按指印 - 潘春英。

在 superintendent Genduit、“C”区副总监 J.D.S. El Mozo 和 J.D.C. 83 Osano 面前录取。

（警探长 Crowther 注：证人为乡下人类型，在上海仅约1年，当“C”区副总监在现场、安田（Yasuda）中佐、大萩（Ohagi）指挥官、上原（Uyehara）先生、助理警务处长、日本领事馆警察福山（Fukuyama）首席督察在场对其进行盘问时，她声称曾去过北四川路后方、日本青年联盟（J.M.L. Party）总部附近的金玉坊（King Yuh Fong）。

pages.en:
Statement of Wei Wong Sz (魏王氏), taken by D.S.I. McPhee
and interpreted by Clerk Li Yang Kao, on 27-11-35, at Hongkew
Police Station.

My name is Wei Wong Sz (魏王氏), age 42, native of
Zaushing, widow, residing at No. 72 Sawgin Road.

I was married at Tsu-Kyi, Zaushing, when I was 17 years
of age.

About 4 years ago my husband Wei Tsan Yao died.

I first arrived in Shanghai about 20 years ago, and I
am at present unemployed.

Since my arrival in Shanghai I have held several
positions as an amah and wet nurse.

On 3rd or 4th November, 1935, I returned to my native
place, Tsu-Kyi, Zaushing, to collect about $80.00 from a money
club, of which I am a member.

After remaining in Zaushing for about 10 days I arrived
back in Shanghai on or about the 14th or 15th November, 1935.

Whilst in Zaushing I met my sister-in-law, named Wei, who
requested me to bring a black jacket to Shanghai, and give same
to her son, named Wei Ah San (魏阿三), who is employed at
Keeble Gardens off Darroch Road as an alleyway cleaner.

I agreed to bring the jacket to Shanghai, whereupon I
placed same in my suitcase amongst my own clothing.

The morning following my return to Shanghai, I proceeded
from Sawgin Road to Keeble Gardens, where I met Wei Ah San, who
was busy sweeping the alleyway.

Wei Ah San knew that I had been to Zaushing and he
questioned me as to his mother's health, whereupon I told him
that his mother was enjoying good health, and that she had
given me a jacket to bring to Shanghai for him. I then told
pages.zh:
魏王氏（Wei Wong Sz）之供词，由警探长 McPhee 于1935年11月27日在虹口巡捕房录取，并由职员李仰高（Li Yang Kao）翻译。

我叫魏王氏，现年42岁，籍贯赵兴（Zaushing），寡妇，居住在沙泾路72号。

我17岁时在赵兴朱旗（Tsu-Kyi, Zaushing）结婚。

大约4年前，我的丈夫魏赞尧（Wei Tsan Yao）去世。

我大约20年前初次抵达上海，目前失业。

自抵达上海以来，我曾担任过多次保姆和奶妈的工作。

1935年11月3日或4日，我回到家乡赵兴朱旗，从一个我参加的互助会（money club）收取约80元。

在赵兴停留约10天后，我于1935年11月14日或15日左右回到上海。

在赵兴期间，我遇到了我的弟媳，姓魏，她请求我带一件黑夹克到上海，交给她的儿子魏阿三（Wei Ah San），他在大通路附近的基布尔花园（Keeble Gardens）担任弄堂清洁工。

我同意将夹克带到上海，于是将其放在我的手提箱中，夹在我的衣物之间。

回到上海后的第二天早晨，我从沙泾路前往基布尔花园，在那里遇到了正在忙着清扫弄堂的魏阿三。

魏阿三知道我去过赵兴，便询问他母亲的健康状况，于是我告诉他，他母亲身体安康，并且她给了我一件夹克让我带到上海给他。随后我告诉

pages.en:
Wei Wong Sz.    2nd sheet.

Wei Ah San to visit my home and receive the jacket, which he agreed
to do.
    After talking with Wei Ah San for about 2 or 3 minutes, I made
my way back to No. 72 Sawgin Road.
    At about 5 p.m. the following day Wei Ah San visited my home
and received the jacket which I brought to Shanghai for him from
Zaushing.
    After remaining in my room for about one minute, he left the
premises, stating that he was returning to his place of employment.
    At about 7 a.m. the morning following Wei Ah San's visit to
my room, I proceeded to the North Railway Station with my niece Wei
Ah Jing ( 魏少琴 ), who was returning to Zaushing due to the fact
that she had lost her job as a wet nurse, having been employed at
an unknown address in the Kashing Road District.
    When we arrived at the North Railway Station we met Wei Ah San
and his wife, name unknown, whereupon my niece Wei Ah Jing informed
me that Wei Ah San's wife was also returning to Zaushing, and that
they were travelling together.
    My niece also told me that Wei Ah San's wife was returning to
Zaushing, as it was rumoured that there would be fighting in
Shanghai, but she did not state who was going to do the fighting.
    At about 9 a.m. I left the North Railway Station and returned
to my home.

                        Thumb printed and cross marked by
                                Wei Wong Sz.
pages.zh:
魏王氏。 第2页。

魏阿三来我家取夹克，他同意了。
    与魏阿三交谈了约2或3分钟后，我便返回沙泾路72号。
    次日下午5时许，魏阿三来到我家，取走了我从赵兴为他带到上海的夹克。
    他在我的房间里待了约一分钟后离开住所，称要返回工作地点。
    魏阿三来访后的第二天早晨约7时，我和我的侄女魏少琴（Wei Ah Jing）前往北站，她因在嘉兴路地区某未知地址受雇的奶妈工作丢失，正返回赵兴。
    当我们到达北站时，遇到了魏阿三及其妻子（姓名不详），于是我的侄女魏少琴告诉我，魏阿三的妻子也要返回赵兴，他们将同行。
    我的侄女还告诉我，魏阿三的妻子返回赵兴是因为有传言说上海将会发生战斗，但她并未说明是谁将进行战斗。
    上午9时许，我离开北站返回家中。

                        魏王氏按指印并画押。

pages.en:
Statement of Wei Kyi Zung, alias Wei Ah San (魏紀作阿三),
taken by Supt. R. Conduit/and interpreted by D.S.I. Chu on the
27-11-35. (D.S.I.Crowther)

I am 39 years of age. I am married. My wife departed
from Shanghai on the 16-11-35. She now resides at Tsu-Kyi,
Zaushing. I have two children, one son aged 6 years, and a
daughter aged 3 years. She resided in Shanghai with a
Portuguese family at 20 Liuchin Terrace, off North Szechuen
Road Extension. My two children are cared for by my mother
at Zaushing. My wife is 33 years of age and is also a
native of Zaushing. I have been in Shanghai about 12 years.
My wife came to Shanghai one year before me. I married my
wife 15 years ago at Zaushing. I have been working at Keeble
Gardens for 3 years. After the Japanese fighting, in April,
1932, my wife was working at No. 120 Boone Road with a
Cantonese family near Quinsan Gardens.

About the 29 th January, 1932, I went with my wife to
Zaushing. I had been working with a Portuguese family also
residing at 120 Boone Road. I was a coolie.

Since I have been working at Keeble Gardens I met my wife
about twice a week. She slept with me in the watchman's hut
at the entrance to Keeble Gardens off Darroch Road. My wife
left for Zaushing as there were rumours that there would be
fighting between Japanese and Chinese. I do not know the reason
for the rumours of fighting. My wife went to the country
with my nephew's wife, named Lan Ying. Lan Ying's husband
died about four years ago. Lan Ying is over 40 years of age.
She does not have a sweetheart. I know she is not the kind of
woman to have a sweetheart. My wife is not pretty in looks,
and I can vouch for her character regarding having connections
pages.zh:
魏纪作，又名魏阿三（Wei Kyi Zung, alias Wei Ah San）之供词，由警司 R. Conduit 于1935年11月27日录取，并由警探长 Chu 翻译。（警探长 Crowther）

我现年39岁。已婚。我的妻子于1935年11月16日离开上海。她现在居住在赵兴朱旗。我有两个孩子，一个儿子6岁，一个女儿3岁。此前她与一个葡萄牙家庭居住在北四川路延伸段附近的柳青里20号。我的两个孩子由我在赵兴的母亲照顾。我的妻子33岁，也是赵兴人。我在上海大约12年了。我的妻子比我早一年来上海。我15年前在赵兴与妻子结婚。我在基布尔花园工作了3年。1932年4月日本战事之后，我的妻子在昆山路花园附近布恩路120号的一个广东人家庭工作。

1932年1月29日左右，我和妻子去了赵兴。我当时也在布恩路120号为一个葡萄牙家庭工作。我是一名苦力。

自从我在基布尔花园工作以来，我每周见妻子约两次。她和我睡在大通路旁基布尔花园入口处的看守棚里。我的妻子前往赵兴，因为有传言说中日之间将发生战斗。我不知道有关战斗传言的原因。我的妻子和我侄媳兰英（Lan Ying）一起下乡。兰英的丈夫大约四年前去世。兰英现年40多岁。她没有情人。我知道她不是那种会有情人的女人。我的妻子相貌平平，我可以担保她在与其他男人交往方面的品行

pages.en:
-3-

Wei Kyi Zung, alias Wei Ah San.

with other men. This can also be verified by the Portuguese
family at 20 Linchin Terrace off North Szechuen Road Extension.
I get $15 per month as a private watchman and alleyway cleaner
in the Keeble Gardens from Mr. Lieu, who lives at No. 9 Keeble
Gardens. Since holding my present job, I have had no trouble
with any other person or persons who work nearby the Keeble
Gardens. Above my wages I get 40 cents silver from each of the
16 families living in the Keeble Gardens, as I keep their
gardens clean, most of the families are Japanese. I don't
know any other persons who are employed near the Keeble Gardens.
Q. You have been employed in the Keeble Gardens for a period
of 3 years, how is it that you do not know any other persons
in that area?
A. I never speak to others, and I always mind my own business.
Q. Don't you speak to any of the maid servants employed by
different families?
A. No, they are all natives of Kiangsu, so I do not make their
Acquaintances.
Q. How do you then carry out your duties as a private watchman?
A. I have taken complaints from families through their servants
and in turn I told my employer, Mr. Lieu.
Q. Have your ever let off fire-crackers within a recent date?
A. No, I have never let off fire-crackers in Shanghai. But did
so some ten years ago in the country.
Q. Did anyone in your terrace let off fire works?
A. No.
Q. Have you ever fired a pistol?
A. No, never.
pages.zh:
-3-

魏纪作，又名魏阿三。

这一点也可以由北四川路延伸段林钦里20号的葡萄牙家庭证实。我作为基布尔花园的私人看守和弄堂清洁工，每月从居住在基布尔花园9号的刘（Lieu）先生那里获得15元薪水。自从事目前的工作以来，我与在基布尔花园附近工作的任何其他人都没有发生过纠纷。除了工资外，我还从居住在基布尔花园的16户家庭中每户获得40分银币，因为我负责保持他们的花园清洁，这些家庭大多是日本人。我不认识其他在基布尔花园附近受雇的人。
问：你在基布尔花园受雇已有3年，为何你不认识该地区的其他人？
答：我从不与他人交谈，我只管自己的事。
问：你不与各家庭雇佣的女佣交谈吗？
答：不，她们都是江苏人，所以我不与她们结识。
问：那你如何履行私人看守的职责呢？
答：我通过各家的仆人接收投诉，然后转告我的雇主刘先生。
问：你最近放过鞭炮吗？
答：没有，我在上海从未放过鞭炮。但在大约十年前的乡下放过。
问：你所在的里弄有人放烟花吗？
答：没有。
问：你开过手枪吗？
答：没有，从来没有。

pages.en:
Wei Kyi Jung, alias Wei Ah San.

Q. How long have you had the short jacket you are wearing?
A. I bought the material for 90 cents during May 1936, and the
jacket was made by a Chinese tailor at King-kwei Road,
Chapei, for 50 cents.
Q. Where did you buy the material?
A. I bought it from a street hawker in the Keeble Gardens.
I do not know the hawker.
Q. The second jacket you are wearing, when did you buy that?
A. It was brought to me from the country one week ago.
Q. What date?
A. About the 17th or 18th inst.
Q. Who brought it to you?
A. My aunt, named Tong Ah Kwo, residing in Fowgin Road. I do
not know the number.
Q. Why should she bring you a jacket?
A. Because of the cold weather, my mother sent it to me.
Q. How much do you pay for the jacket your aunt brought to you?
A. I did not pay anything, my mother bought it.
Q. When did your aunt come to Shanghai?
A. On the 14th or 15th of this month.
Q. How did your aunt come to Shanghai?
A. By train.
Q. When did your aunt tell you she had a jacket for you?
A. On the 14th or 15th November, 1936.
Q. Where?
A. At my place of employment, Keeble Gardens.
Q. What time?
A. In the morning at about 9 a.m. or 10 a.m.
pages.zh:
魏基荣，别名魏阿三。

问：你身上穿的这件短夹克穿了多久了？
答：我在1936年5月间花了90分买了布料，这件夹克是闸北金桂路的一位中国裁缝以50分的工钱制作的。
问：你在哪里买的布料？
答：我是在基布尔花园（Keeble Gardens）从一个街头小贩那里买的。我不认识那个小贩。
问：你身上穿的第二件夹克是什么时候买的？
答：是一周前从乡下给我带来的。
问：具体哪一天？
答：大约是本月17日或18日。
问：是谁给你带来的？
答：是我的姑妈，名叫童阿国，住在福根路。我不知道门牌号。
问：她为什么要给你带一件夹克来？
答：因为天气冷，是我母亲寄给我的。
问：你姑妈给你带来的那件夹克你付了多少钱？
答：我什么都没付，是我母亲买的。
问：你姑妈是什么时候来上海的？
答：是本月14日或15日。
问：你姑妈是怎么来上海的？
答：坐火车来的。
问：你姑妈是什么时候告诉你她有一件夹克给你的？
答：1936年11月14日或15日。
问：在哪里？
答：在我的工作地点，基布尔花园。
问：什么时间？
答：上午，大约上午9点或10点。

pages.en:
Wei Kyi Zung alias Wei Ah Sam.

Q. Did she come by herself?
A. Yes.
Q. Did she bring anything else for you?
A. No.
Q. Did anyone see your aunt talking to you?
A. I do not know, I was at my master's house and there was
no body there.
Q. Who is your master?
A. Mr. Lieu Ts Ching.
Q. What does your master do?
A. He works for an American firm.
Q. When did your aunt give you the jacket?
A. on the 17th or 18th of this month.
Q. Where did she give you the jacket?
A. At my aunt's house on Songlin Road.

Signed, thumb printed and cross marked by
Wei Kyi Zung, alias Wei Ah Sam.
pages.zh:
魏基荣，别名魏阿三。

问：她是自己一个人来的吗？
答：是的。
问：她还给你带了别的东西吗？
答：没有。
问：有人看到你姑妈和你说话吗？
答：我不知道，我当时在我主人家里，那里没有人。
问：你的主人是谁？
答：刘子清先生（Lieu Ts Ching）。
问：你的主人是做什么的？
答：他在一家美国公司工作。
问：你姑妈是什么时候把夹克给你的？
答：本月17日或18日。
问：她是在哪里把夹克给你的？
答：在松林路我姑妈的家里。

魏基荣，别名魏阿三，签名、按指印并画十字标记。

pages.en:
Woo Z Ling (吳汝霖).
Kan-yen, Yangchow.                                D.S.In. Crowther and McPhee.
9 p.m.                 20/11/35.                  D. S. I. Oon Chi Huang.

My name is Woo Z Ling (吳汝霖), age 80, native of Kan-yen,
Yangchow, Kiangsu, residing at Lane 189, House No. 34 Chan
Chua Road, Chapel.

I came to Shanghai from Kan-yen, Yangchow, when I was 21
years of age, and went to live at Lane 189, House No. 34 Chan
Chua Road, Chapel, my present address.

After residing in Shanghai for 3 or 4 months, I commenced
to teach children in a straw hut, surrounded by straw huts, at
Jukong Jan, near Maxwell Road, which I continued for a period of
2 years, during which time I taught 20 to 30 children daily, and
in one year I obtained approximately $100.00.

At the end of the two years, I obtained a position as a
policeman in the Chapel Police Force, and was attached to the 5th
Division 2nd District. We had no numbers in those days.

I served in the Chapel Police Force for about 7 or 8 years,
and resigned as the Force was taken over by the Northerners,
furthermore the majority of the Force consisted of Northerners,
the food supplied consisted of wheatbread, and I being accustomed
to Southern Food (Rice), this did not agree with my constitution.
I only received $4 or $5 wages per month with board.

After leaving the Police Force I returned to my native
place where I stayed for about 6 months, and then returned to
Shanghai.

At that time the house in which I now reside was a straw
hut which was built by me, and on my return to Shanghai, I went
to live there again.

My straw hut was later demolished and the present stone
pages.zh:
吴汝霖（Woo Z Ling）。
江苏扬州甘泉人。                                副督察长 Crowther 和 McPhee。
晚上9点                 1935年11月20日。                  副督察长 黄恩志（Oon Chi Huang）。

我叫吴汝霖，现年80岁，籍贯江苏扬州甘泉，现住 Chapel 地区陈庄路189弄34号。

我21岁时从江苏扬州甘泉来到上海，居住在陈庄路189弄34号，即我现在的地址。

在上海居住三四个月后，我开始在麦克斯韦尔路（Maxwell Road）附近的朱公詹（Jukong Jan，音译）的一间草棚里教孩子读书，那里周围都是草棚。我持续教了两年，期间每天教20到30个孩子，一年收入约100美元。

两年后，我在 Chapel 巡捕房获得了一份警察的职位，隶属于第五分区第二区。那时我们没有警号。

我在 Chapel 巡捕房服役了大约七八年，后来因为巡捕房被北方人接管而辞职，此外，当时巡捕房大多数成员都是北方人，供应的食物是面食，而我习惯吃南方食物（米饭），这不适合我的体质。我当时月薪仅4或5美元，包伙食。

离开巡捕房后，我回到了家乡，在那里待了大约六个月，然后又回到上海。

当时我现在居住的房子还是一座由我建造的草棚，回到上海后，我又住到了那里。

后来我的草棚被拆除，现在的石

pages.en:
Woo Z Ling.

house built with others, during the demolishing period and the
rebuilding of the present house, I resided at No. 51 Dah Shing
Li, Mei Kyi Road, Chapei.

About 6 months after my return to Shanghai I obtained a
position as an accountant in the Woosung Ricsha Hong, situated
at Urga Road, Chapei. I held this position until the 14th year
of the Chinese Republic (1925).

Owing to the conditions prevailing at that time and busi-
ness being bad, I resigned my position as accountant at the
Ricsha Hong and returned to my native place, Kau-yau, Yangchow,
where I remained for over one year.

I returned to Shanghai to seek employment, and after a
period of about 7 or 8 months, I obtained a position as an
Inspector in the Rolled Tobacco Tax Bureau, situated at the
Small West Gate, Nantao, which position I held for nearly one
year. I lost this position when the Bureau was abolished.

Being without work in Shanghai, I returned to my native
place, where I own land and property, the area of land being
47 mow, valued at $70 per mow. This property was handed down
to me when my father died.

I remained in my native place for about 1 year and again
returned to Shanghai, this being about 1929.

After my return to Shanghai, I was un-employed for a few
months, when I obtained employment as a teaboy on board the
S.S. Lien Ho, plying between Shanghai and Hankow.

I was employed in this way for about 2 years, and lost
my job owing to the change of compradorees.
pages.zh:
吴汝霖。

屋与其他房屋一起建造，在拆除期和重建现有房屋期间，我居住在闸北梅吉路（Mei Kyi Road，音译）大兴里51号。

回到上海大约六个月后，我在闸北乌尔加路（Urga Road，音译）的吴淞人力车行获得了一份会计的职位。我一直担任该职位直到中华民国十四年（1925年）。

由于当时的局势和商业不景气，我辞去了人力车行会计的职位，回到了家乡扬州高邮（Kau-yau，音译），在那里待了一年多。

我回到上海寻找工作，大约七八个月后，我在南市小西门的卷烟统税局获得了一份稽查员的职位，该职位我担任了将近一年。该局撤销后，我失去了这份工作。

由于在上海失业，我回到了家乡，我在家乡拥有土地和房产，土地面积为47亩，每亩价值70美元。这些财产是我父亲去世时传给我的。

我在家乡待了大约一年，再次回到上海，那大约是1929年。

回到上海后，我失业了几个月，随后在往返于上海和汉口之间的“联和”轮（S.S. Lien Ho）上找到了一份茶房的工作。

我以这种方式工作了大约两年，后因买办更换而失业。

pages.en:
- 3 -

Voo Z Ling.

I was unemployed for about 1 year and remained at my present
address.

At the beginning of 1933 I obtained a position as bodyguard
to a Mr. Pen Yeong Foh (潘荣富), a building contractor, residing
at No. 12 Avenue Foch, who now resides at Route Prosper Paris.
I obtained this position through the introduction of one named
Tou Yao Ding, Ex-detective of the French Police, who is the
former master of Vooeung Riecha Kung where I was employed as an
accountant.

I was a bodyguard for Mr. Pen Yeong Foh until October 1934,
when my services were dispensed with (note:- at this juncture,
Voo Z Ling produced a Curfew Pass, No. 11804, dated March, 1933,
issued to him by the S.M. Police).

Since October, 1934, I have been unemployed, but my wife
is employed as a maid servant by a Portuguese family residing
on Vooeung Road.

I am still a follower of Tou Yao Ding.

During July, 1935, I had a quarrel with a fellow country
man, named Voo Yeh Ho (吴亚河), over a money club, which I
conducted, and also the Banker.

Voo Yeh Ho's wife is employed as an ayah by a Russian
Police Officer of the S.M. Police, who was formerly attached to
Maxwell Road Station, and at present resides near the Japanese
Naval Landing Party (probably Ramos Apartments).

Q. Have you had any trouble with any other persons other than
Voo Yeh Ho?

A. No.
pages.zh:
- 3 -

吴汝霖。

我失业了大约一年，一直住在我现在的地址。

1933年初，我通过一位名叫陶耀鼎（Tou Yao Ding，音译）的人的介绍，获得了一份给建筑承包商潘荣富先生做保镖的工作。潘先生当时住在福煦路12号，现住在普罗旺斯路（Route Prosper Paris，音译）。陶耀鼎是前法租界巡捕房的侦探，也是我此前担任会计时的东家——某人力车公司（Vooeung Riecha Kung，音译）的前主人。

我一直担任潘荣富先生的保镖，直到1934年10月被解雇（注：此时，吴汝霖出示了一张由上海公共租界警务处签发的宵禁通行证，编号11804，日期为1933年3月）。

自1934年10月以来，我一直失业，但我妻子在乌尔加路（Vooeung Road，音译）的一户葡萄牙人家里做女佣。

我仍然是陶耀鼎的门生。

1935年7月，我因一个由我主持的标会以及银行事务，与同乡吴亚河（Voo Yeh Ho，音译）发生争执。

吴亚河的妻子受雇于上海公共租界警务处的一名俄国警官当保姆，该警官以前隶属于麦克斯韦尔路捕房，目前住在日本海军陆战队附近（可能是拉莫斯公寓）。

问：除了吴亚河之外，你还与其他任何人有过纠纷吗？

答：没有。

pages.en:
- 4 -

Woo I Ling

Q. Have you guaranteed any person in business or money
transactions?
A. Yes, I guaranteed a friend named Lieu Tuh Su (刘德喜),
carpenter, formerly residing in a straw hut off Chi Mai
Road, Chapel, for the monthly payment of $10.00 to a money
club conducted by one named Kan Tsang Foo (胥志富), resid-
ing at Shang-len Jun.
Q. How did you guarantee Lieu?
A. Lieu drew the sum of $210.00, from the money club, and I
obtained a shop guarantee from one named Wong Sang Yui
(王順裕), master of a candy shop, situated at No. 139
Scott Road, on his behalf, as other members of the club
did not trust me.
Q. Why did you guarantee Lieu in this way?
A. As it was necessary for Lieu.
Q. Where were you on the night of 9-11-35?
A. I was at home.
Q. How can you remember this particular night?
A. Because I never go out at night.
Q. Do you associate with any bad characters?
A. No.
Q. You said in your statement that you are a follower of Tan
Yao Ming?
A. Yes, I call him "teacher".
Q. When did you last see Tan Yao Ming?
A. During the Chinese New Year.
Q. Do you own a bicycle?
pages.zh:
- 4 -

吴汝霖

问：你在商业或金钱交易中为任何人做过担保吗？
答：是的，我为一个叫刘德喜（Lieu Tuh Su，音译）的朋友做过担保，他是个木匠，以前住在 Chapel 地区芝罘路（Chi Mai Road，音译）旁的一间草棚里。担保内容是每月向胥志富（Kan Tsang Foo，音译）主持的一个标会支付10美元，胥志富住在尚仁俊（Shang-len Jun，音译）。
问：你是如何为刘某担保的？
答：刘某从标会中支取了210美元，由于标会的其他成员不信任我，我代他从斯科特路139号一家糖果店的老板王顺裕（Wong Sang Yui，音译）那里取得了一份店铺担保。
问：你为什么这样为刘某担保？
答：因为刘某需要这样做。
问：1935年11月9日晚上你在哪里？
答：我在家。
问：你怎么记得这个特定的夜晚？
答：因为我晚上从不外出。
问：你与任何不良分子有来往吗？
答：没有。
问：你在陈述中说你是谭耀明（Tan Yao Ming，音译）的门生？
答：是的，我称他为“老师”。
问：你最后一次见到谭耀明是什么时候？
答：春节期间。
问：你拥有自行车吗？

pages.en:
- 5 -

Uoo Z Ling.

A. Yes.
Q. Do you regularly ride the bicycle?
A. Yes.
Q. How often?
A. Whenever I go out.
Q. Do you gamble?
A. No.
Q. Never?
A. Yes, when I was a bodyguard I used to gamble, but never since.
Q. Are you acquainted with Maxwell Road District?
A. No, only Scott Road.
Q. Yet you have said in your statement that you have resided at Chin Swee Road for many years, how is it that you do not know the roads surrounding you?
A. Yes, I know the roads.
Q. Which roads do you know?
A. North Bridge Road, Barrow Road, Peng Leh Li and Vengle Road.
Q. Have you any friends residing in the vicinity of Barrow Road?
A. No.
Q. When did you last visit Barrow Road?
A. I have never been to Barrow Road.
Q. Barrow Road is a very short Road, how do you know the road?
A. I have seen a signboard with Barrow Road thereon, whilst
pages.zh:
- 5 -

吴汝霖。

答：有。
问：你经常骑这辆自行车吗？
答：是的。
问：多久骑一次？
答：每次出门都骑。
问：你赌博吗？
答：不。
问：从来不赌？
答：是的，当我做保镖的时候我曾经赌博，但从那以后再也没有赌过。
问：你熟悉麦克斯韦尔路区域吗？
答：不熟悉，只熟悉斯科特路。
问：然而你在陈述中说你在锦西路（Chin Swee Road，音译）居住了很多年，怎么会不认识周围的路呢？
答：是的，我认识那些路。
问：你认识哪些路？
答：北四川路、巴罗路（Barrow Road）、彭乐里（Peng Leh Li，音译）和文勒路（Vengle Road，音译）。
问：你有朋友住在巴罗路附近吗？
答：没有。
问：你最后一次去巴罗路是什么时候？
答：我从未去过巴罗路。
问：巴罗路是一条很短的路，你怎么会知道这条路？
答：我在经过北四川路时，看到过一块写着巴罗路的路牌，当时

pages.en:
- 6 -

Vee Z Ling.

passing along North Szechuan Road.
Q. When did you last visit North Szechuan Road?
A. On the morning of 18-11-35 whilst on my way to Scott Road.
Q. Have you ever been to Fong Leh Li?
A. No, not during the past 5 years.
Q. You have been there?
A. Yes, 5 years ago I walked through.
Q. Where did you enter Fong Leh Li?
A. I have never been to the Fong Leh Li.
Q. You have just stated that you walked through the Fong Leh
Li.
A. I know where the Fong Leh Li is, but I have never been
there.
Q. You seem to be afraid of something?
A. I am not afraid of anything.
Q. Why do you change your statement, if you are not afraid?
A. I have not changed my statement.
Q. When you were in the police force did you carry firearms?
A. No, only a baton.
Q. Are you acquainted with the workings of a firearm?
A. Yes, I became acquainted with the workings of a firearm
when I was a bodyguard.
Q. Who taught you to handle a firearm?
A. Tan Yeo Ding taught me.
Q. When did he teach you?
A. Before I obtained the job as a bodyguard.
Q. Where did he teach you?
pages.zh:
- 6 -

吴汝霖。

问：你最后一次去北四川路是什么时候？
答：1935年11月18日上午，当时我正前往斯科特路。
问：你去过丰乐里（Fong Leh Li，音译）吗？
答：没有，过去五年里没有去过。
问：你去过那里？
答：是的，五年前我曾步行穿过那里。
问：你是从哪里进入丰乐里的？
答：我从未去过丰乐里。
问：你刚才说你步行穿过了丰乐里。
答：我知道丰乐里在哪里，但我从未去过那里。
问：你似乎害怕什么？
答：我什么都不怕。
问：如果你不怕，为什么要改变你的供词？
答：我没有改变我的供词。
问：你在巡捕房服役时携带枪支吗？
答：不，只带警棍。
问：你熟悉枪支的操作吗？
答：是的，我在做保镖时熟悉了枪支的操作。
问：谁教你使用枪支的？
答：谭耀鼎（Tan Yeo Ding，音译）教我的。
问：他什么时候教你的？
答：在我获得保镖工作之前。
问：他在哪里教你的？

pages.en:
- 19 -

Tao Z. Ling

A. In the Carpenters' Guild on Avenue Joffre.
Q. Did you fire the pistol in the Carpenters' Guild?
A. No.
Q. Did you have a pistol?
A. No.
Q. Whose pistol was it?
A. Tan Yao Ding's pistol.
Q. Was the pistol loaded when he was instructing you?
A. No, Tan Yao Ding took out the magazine.
Q. Was Tan Yao Ding a detective at that time?
A. Yes.
Q. How many years ago was this?
A. Just prior to me obtaining the job as a bodyguard.
Q. Were you ever instructed by the Police to use firearms?
A. No, never.
Q. Have you ever fired a pistol?
A. Yes, I fired one round in my friend's house in the French
Concession, the lead part of the bullet was substituted
with a piece of rubber made in the shape of a bullet.
Q. When was this?
A. When I was a bodyguard, and the pistol I fired was my
master's.
Q. Who was present when you fired the pistol?
A. Two police watchmen, and one other bodyguard, also employed
by my master.
Q. Do you own a pistol at present?
A. No.
pages.zh:
- 19 -

陶Z. 林（Tao Z. Ling，音译，应为陶耀鼎或相关人士）

答：在霞飞路的木匠公会。
问：你在木匠公会开枪了吗？
答：没有。
问：你有手枪吗？
答：没有。
问：那是谁的手枪？
答：是谭耀明（Tan Yao Ding，音译）的手枪。
问：他指导你时手枪装有子弹吗？
答：没有，谭耀明取出了弹夹。
问：那时谭耀明是侦探吗？
答：是的。
问：那是多少年前的事？
答：就在我获得保镖工作之前不久。
问：警方曾经指示你使用枪支吗？
答：没有，从来没有。
问：你开过枪吗？
答：是的，我在法租界朋友家里开过一枪，子弹的铅头部分被替换成了做成子弹形状的橡胶块。
问：那是什么时候？
答：是我做保镖的时候，我开的那把手枪是我主人的。
问：你开枪时谁在场？
答：两名巡捕，还有另一名也受雇于我主人的保镖。
问：你现在拥有手枪吗？
答：没有。

pages.en:
- 8 -

Woo Z Ling

Q. When was the last time you handled a pistol?
A. When I was a bodyguard.
Q. Do you want a job?
A. No, my eye sight is very bad, especially at night.
Q. Are you in any way connected with Japanese?
A. No.
Q. Do you know any Japanese?
A. No.
Q. Do you know why you are being questioned?
A. I have no idea.
Q. Are you aware that families have evacuated from the vicinity
of your home?
A. Yes, wealthy Cantonese families have removed.
Q. Why?
A. Because it was rumoured that the fighting would occur.
Q. Who was going to fight?
A. I don't know.
Q. Do you read the newspapers?
A. No, my eye sight is bad.
Q. Can you read?
A. Yes, I can, but my eye sight fails me.
Q. How long have you been married?
A. 21 years ago.
Q. Have you any family?
A. One son, age 16.
Q. Is your wife alive?
A. Yes, she resides with me.
pages.zh:
- 8 -

吴汝霖

问：你最后一次接触手枪是什么时候？
答：是我做保镖的时候。
问：你想要工作吗？
答：不，我的视力很差，尤其是在晚上。
问：你与日本人有任何联系吗？
答：没有。
问：你认识任何日本人吗？
答：没有。
问：你知道为什么审问你吗？
答：我不知道。
问：你是否意识到你家附近的家庭已经撤离？
答：是的，富裕的广东家庭已经搬走了。
问：为什么？
答：因为有谣言说会发生战斗。
问：谁要打仗？
答：我不知道。
问：你看报纸吗？
答：不看，我视力不好。
问：你会识字吗？
答：是的，我会，但我的视力不行了。
问：你结婚多久了？
答：21年前。
问：你有家人吗？
答：有一个儿子，16岁。
问：你妻子还在世吗？
答：是的，她和我住在一起。

pages.en:
- 9 -

Foo Z Ling.

Q. Where does your son live?
A. He lives with me.
Q. Where is your son employed?
A. My son is still at school.
Q. Which school?
A. He attends the Sa Kung Primary School, Tiendong Road, Shanghai.
Q. Does he speak Japanese?
A. No.
Q. Does he speak English?
A. Yes, a little.
Q. Are you interested in Politics?
A. No.
Q. Is your son interested in Politics?
A. No, he is not.
Q. When do you retire for the night?
A. At about 8 p.m. or 9 p.m. every night.
Q. You say you have bad eye sight, how do you come to ride a
bicycle?
A. I only ride in the day light.
Q. You must have money owning so much land in the country?
A. The land is all mortgaged.

Signed : Foo Z Ling.
pages.zh:
- 9 -

吴汝霖。

问：你儿子住在哪里？
答：他和我住在一起。
问：你儿子在哪里工作？
答：我儿子还在上学。
问：哪所学校？
答：他就读于上海天潼路的萨公小学（Sa Kung Primary School，音译）。
问：他会说日语吗？
答：不会。
问：他会说英语吗？
答：会一点。
问：你对政治感兴趣吗？
答：不。
问：你儿子对政治感兴趣吗？
答：不，他不感兴趣。
问：你每晚几点睡觉？
答：每晚大约晚上8点或9点。
问：你说你视力不好，怎么还会骑自行车？
答：我只在白天骑。
问：你在乡下拥有那么多土地，一定很有钱吧？
答：土地全都抵押出去了。

签名：吴汝霖。

报纸剪报及

pages.en:
2.
October 9, 1937. Morning Translation

Social Evening News of October 8 :-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE : REQUEST OF YANG WEN-TAO AND YIH
HAI-SUNG FOR RELEASE

At about 7 o'clock on the night of November 9,
1935, a Japanese sailor was found dead on a quiet street
known as Darroch Road in an area densely populated with
Japanese. Several minutes later the discovery caused a
panic among the residents in North Szechuen Road. The
Japanese Special Naval Landing Party detailed a large number
of fully armed marines to stand duty at various places, while
the entire forces of the Public Safety Bureau (known at
present as the Shanghai City Government Police Bureau) and
the Shanghai Municipal Police were mobilized because of the
murder. The situation at that time presented a scene
similar to the one on the eve of the January 28 Incident.
Every law enforcement officer paid attention
to this dead Japanese. Those who had seen the body well
remembered that the man was of a strong build and fierce
looking. One knew at a glance that he was a drunkard by
the strong smell of liquor. In Shanghai the murder of
a foreigner, particularly a Japanese, was a great affair.
For this reason the Police at once began a house to house
search for the culprit but no one was apprehended. The
body was removed and the spot where the body was found was
marked with white chalk and several armed Japanese marines
were posted on guard.
On the following day the murder was prominently
featured in the local newspapers and the public were thus
acquainted that the murdered sailor was Hideo Nakayama.
The Japanese authorities in Shanghai continually pressed
General Wu Te-chen, former Mayor of Shanghai, to bring the
culprit to justice. They seemed to be sure that the murder
was committed by Chinese. At the same time, Japanese
marines patrolled the district everyday, and this caused
a general exodus from Chapei. Invisibly trade in Shanghai
was adversely affected, while the insurance companies raised
the war risk rates in the districts of Chapei and Hongkew.
In order to bring the case to an early close,
the Shanghai City Government offered a reward of $4,000 for
information leading to the arrest of persons responsible
for the murder. The action was copied by the Shanghai
Municipal Police and the Japanese Special Naval Landing
Party who each offered a reward of $4,000. It happened
that the total reward of $12,000 had its effect and some
time later three "culprits" by the name of Tseu Shou-yong
(周社荣), Yih Hai-sung (葉海生) and Yang Wen-tao (楊文道)
were apprehended.
As a result, the Shanghai First Special District
Court found Tseu Shou-yong not guilty, but sentenced both Yih Hai-
sung and Yang Wen-tao to death. Armed Japanese naval men
attended the handing down of the decision. When Yih and
Yang were sentenced to death, they cried out "grievance".
Enquiries made from various sources show that the truth of
the case has every connection with the reward of $12,000.

10月8日《社会晚报》：

中山案：杨文道与叶海生请求释放

1935年11月9日晚7时许，在一条名为达罗路（Darroch Road）的僻静街道上发现一名日本水兵死亡，该地区日本人聚居密集。几分钟后，这一发现引起了四川北路居民的恐慌。日本特别海军陆战队派遣了大量全副武装的海军陆战队员在各处站岗执勤，而公共安全局（即现在的上海市政府警察局）和上海公共租界工部局警务处的全部警力也因这起谋杀案而被动员起来。当时的局势呈现出与“一·二八”事变前夕相似的场景。
每一位执法人员都关注着这名死去的日本人。那些仔细看过尸体的人都记得，此人身材魁梧，面目凶狠。从强烈的酒气可以一眼看出他是个醉汉。在上海，外国人尤其是日本人的被杀是一件大事。因此，警方立即开始挨家挨户搜捕凶手，但无人被捕。尸体被移走，发现尸体的地点用白粉笔做了标记，并派驻了几名武装日本海军陆战队员守卫。
次日，当地报纸显著报道了这起谋杀案，公众由此得知被杀的水兵是中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）。驻沪日本当局不断向上海市前市长吴铁城将军施压，要求将凶手绳之以法。他们似乎确信谋杀案是中国人所为。同时，日本海军陆战队每天在该地区巡逻，导致闸北居民大规模外逃。上海的贸易在无形中受到不利影响，保险公司提高了闸北和虹口地区的战争险费率。
为了早日结案，上海市政府悬赏4,000美元，征集有助于逮捕谋杀案责任人的线索。上海公共租界工部局警务处和日本特别海军陆战队也效仿此举，各悬赏4,000美元。总计12,000美元的赏金果然产生了效果，不久后，三名“凶手”周社荣、叶海生和杨文道被捕。
结果，上海第一特区地方法院判决周社荣无罪，但判处叶海生和杨文道死刑。武装日本海军人员出席了宣判过程。当叶、杨二人被判处死刑时，他们高呼“冤枉”。经多方查证，本案真相与12,000美元赏金有着千丝万缕的联系。

understand that both Yih and Yang were wrongly involved in

niang (張志讓), lawyer in defence of Yih Hai-sung, and
Mr. Tang Wei-chun (唐豪), lawyer defending Yang Wen-tao,

As a consequence, however, the Supreme Court handed down a

penalty for the two accused.
A nation-wide defensive war has been started in
China and all the fears entertained in the past should be
abolished. The expression "X X" has now been changed
direct into "Japan" and every Japanese soldier has become
our foe. Past grievances should be cleared off now.
Yih Hai-sung and Yang Wen-tao should be released. Both
lawyers Chang Tse-niang and Tang Wei-chun have submitted an
application for the release of the two accused.
On October 7, lawyer Tang Wei-chun made the
following statement to our reporter :- "It is true that
the two accused were wrongly charged. In view of the
difficult position of the authorities, we did not make
excessive demands. However, the protection of personal
rights is the duty of all lawyers. Furthermore, the accused
are truly not the principal offenders in the case and they
should be liberated especially at the present time when

事实上，许多人明白叶海生和杨文道是被错误卷入此案的。原因在于：我们是弱国之民，叶、杨二人成了牺牲品。
为了保护个人权利，叶海生的辩护律师张志让先生和杨文道的辩护律师唐豪先生，就江苏省高等法院第二分院作出的判决向最高法院提出上诉。然而，最高法院作出裁定，维持原判，即对两名被告判处死刑。
中国已发动全国性防御战争，过去所有的恐惧都应消除。“X X”一词现已直接改为“日本”，每个日本士兵都已成为我们的敌人。过去的冤屈现在应当洗雪。叶海生和杨文道应予释放。张志让和唐豪两位律师均已提交申请，要求释放这两名被告。
10月7日，唐豪律师向记者发表如下声明：“两名被告确系被错误指控。鉴于当局处境困难，我们并未提出过分要求。然而，保护个人权利是所有律师的职责。此外，被告确实并非本案主犯，尤其在日本自身不讲理地处理事务的当下，他们应获解放。呼吁公众主持公道”。

Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE: YIH HAI SUNG'S APPEAL

(continued from January 9)

(a) The Court of Second Instance declared that both Hu Ziang Wu and Pan Chiao Ying had said that they saw a man wearing black clothing. It will be recalled that in cold weather people usually wear dark coloured clothing, especially in foreign dress and military uniforms. On July 7, the Court of First Instance wrote a report on the reconstruction of the crime in which it says: "There was an electric lamp on an electric pole, but the light was comparatively weak as the lamp was very high and the street was deserted and wide. The place was very dark, but the length and the bright colour of the clothing could be distinguished. All dark coloured clothing seen under such a street lamp can be said to be black clothing. Hu Ziang Wu's statement, as given in Paragraph (c) above, reads: "It seemed that the clothing of the men who escaped had the style of the clothing worn by marines." Therefore, the so-called dark colour must be intended to mean this.

(b) The Court of Second Instance regarded the statement of Chang Zai Yuen to the effect that on that evening he saw the appellant and others walking on North Szechuen Road towards the northern direction as true. But at the Police Station and in the Court of First Instance, Chang Zai Yuen repeatedly stated that at that time the appellant was dressed in a Sun Yat Sen style of uniform. (Vide the written record of Volume 1 of the Court of First Instance and statement Page No.47). Can his statements then be believed?

(c) The Court of Second Instance accepted the statement of "Hai-Loh-Ya" (海樂亞), a Portuguese, as true. This witness stated: "The door of Room No.9 was pushed half open and I saw Yih Hai Sung in the room." As a matter of fact, the entry of Room No.9 near the door is narrow, so that with the door only half open one would only have seen the wall and not the interior of the room. This can be proved by referring to a plan of the room. (Vide Court File Page No.102, Volume 2, of the Court of First Instance.) The statement of this witness is evidently unfounded.

(d) The appellant clearly stated in the Court of First Instance that Room No.9 in the Moon Palace Hotel was booked by Au Tsung Kyi (夏春記). The Court regarded this statement to mean that the appellant had booked the room in the name of Au Tsung Kyi. This is a gross mistake. Au Tsung Kyi is the name of an actual person and is not a fictitious name used by the appellant.

(e) The appellant did not state in his confessions on May 1 and May 6 that Yang Wen Tao had taken a pistol out of a book and handed it to the appellant. He said this only in his written statement which he copied from one prepared by the Police after he was severely tortured. The book was seized by the Police in April. If the Court of Second Instance holds that the seizure of the book shows that the appellant's statement corresponds with the facts, then the arrest of Yang Wen Tao can prove the same thing.

《辛闻报》及其他本地报纸：

中山谋杀案：叶海生之上诉

（续1月9日）

(a) 二审法院宣称，胡祥武和潘乔英均表示看到一名身穿黑衣的男子。回想起来，在寒冷天气里，人们通常穿着深色衣服，尤其是西式服装和军装。7月7日，初审法院在一份关于犯罪重建的报告中写道：“电线杆上有一盏电灯，但由于灯很高，街道空旷宽阔，光线相对较弱。地方很暗，但可以分辨出衣服的长度和鲜艳颜色。在这种路灯下看到的所有深色衣服都可以说是黑色衣服。上述(c)段中引用的胡祥武的供词写道：‘逃跑者的衣服样式似乎是海军陆战队员穿的样式。’因此，所谓的深色必定是指此意。

(b) 二审法院认为张在元关于当晚看到上诉人等人沿四川北路向北行走的陈述属实。但在警察局和初审法院，张在元反复陈述当时上诉人穿着中山装式样的制服。（见初审法院第一卷笔录及第47页供词）。那么，他的陈述可信吗？

(c) 二审法院采信了葡萄牙人“海乐亚”（Hai-Loh-Ya）的陈述。该证人称：“9号房的门半开着，我看到叶海生在房间里。”事实上，9号房靠近门口的入口处很窄，门只开一半的话，只能看到墙壁，而看不到房间内部。这一点可以通过查看房间平面图来证明。（见初审法院第二卷第102页案卷。）该证人的陈述显然没有根据。

(d) 上诉人在初审法院明确陈述，月宫饭店（Moon Palace Hotel）的9号房是由夏春记（Au Tsung Kyi）预订的。法院将此陈述理解为上诉人以夏春记的名义预订了房间。这是一个严重的错误。夏春记是一个真实人物的名字，并非上诉人使用的化名。

(e) 上诉人在5月1日和5月6日的供词中并未陈述杨文道从书中取出手枪交给上诉人。他只是在遭受严刑拷打后，抄写了一份由警方准备的书面陈述时才说了这话。该书是警方在4月份查获的。如果二审法院认为查获该书表明上诉人的陈述符合事实，那么逮捕杨文道也能证明同样的事情。

There is no ground on which the Courts could have reached
this conclusion. If the Supreme Court will compare the
points for and against the theory that appellant's statement
corresponds with the facts, it will immediately see whether
or not the statement does correspond with the facts.

(7) A general study of all the evidence in this case:
(a) The evidence in this case secured and produced
by the Police would not have been sufficient to justify
the charge against the appellant and Yang Wen Tao for the
murder but for the statements made by the appellant under
torture. Speaking from a logical point of view, even if
the book in question was actually seized at the home of
Yang Wen Tao and was proved to be actually his property
and that it was actually used by him for the purpose of
concealing the pistol that was produced in Court as an
exhibit and that the spent bullet that had caused the death
of the Japanese marine Nakayama and the empty cartridge
shell produced in Court were actually found to have been
fired from the said pistol, can all this be regarded as
evidence proving that the Japanese marine Hideo Nakayama
was murdered by Yang Wen Tao? What was seized in the home of
Yang Wen Tao was only a book and not the pistol that was
produced in Court as an exhibit; in other words, it was
only an article that was used for the purpose of concealing
the crime weapon (if the pistol produced in Court is actually
the weapon that was used in the murder); it was not the
weapon itself. Moreover, it was known that the pistol (the
murder weapon) was not found in the possession of Yang Wen
Tao, but was concealed beneath a wooden box where it was
subsequently found, while the book which was known to have
been used for the purpose of concealing this pistol was
safely deposited at the home of Yang Wen Tao. Now, can it
be definitely alleged that Yang Wen Tao had used this pistol
(the crime weapon) to commit the murder and that he is
a murderer simply because the book which was used for the
purpose of concealing a pistol was seized at his home?
Such a hypothesis is untenable. Can a person be held for
the murder of another person simply because a knife which
was found beside the murdered person is his property?
No; in the same way, much less will he be held guilty if
the knife does not belong to him and still less so if only
an article used for the purpose of concealing this knife
is found at his home.
(b) From the above, it can be seen that even if
all the evidence produced in Court by the Police remains
unchallenged, it cannot be used to prove that Yang Wen Tao
was the person who had murdered the Japanese marine Nakayama.
Supposing that Yang Wen Tao can be held as a suspect for
the murder because the book was seized at his home, this fact
has nothing whatever to do with the appellant, who would not
have been charged with the crime if he had not made any
statements under torture. This is quite clear and deserves
consideration by the Supreme Court, because one who "goes
inside the horn of an ox" (meaning one who is handling a case)
is liable to go astray, but one who remains an on-looker
"above the sky", sees quite clearly. From this, it can be
understood that the appellant would not have become involved
in this case but for his statements made under torture.

法院得出这一结论没有任何依据。如果最高法院将上诉人供述是否符合事实的正反论点加以比较，就能立即看出该供述是否确实符合事实。

(7) 对本案所有证据的总体研究：
(a) 若非上诉人在酷刑下作出的供述，警方在本案中获取并提交的证据不足以证明对上诉人和杨文涛（Yang Wen Tao）提出的谋杀指控成立。从逻辑角度来看，即使那本书确实在杨文涛家中被查获，并被证实确属其所有，且确实被他用来藏匿作为法庭证物出示的手枪，并且导致日本海军陆战队员中山（Nakayama）死亡的已发射子弹以及在法庭上出示的空弹壳确实被证实是从该手枪射出的，这一切能否被视为证明日本海军陆战队员中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）系被杨文涛谋杀的证据？在杨文涛家中查获的仅是一本书，而非作为法庭证物出示的手枪；换言之，它只是用于藏匿作案武器（如果法庭出示的手枪确实是用于谋杀的武器）的物品，而非武器本身。此外，众所周知，该手枪（作案凶器）并非在杨文涛身上搜出，而是藏在一个木箱下面，随后在那里被发现，而据知用于藏匿该手枪的那本书则安然存放在杨文涛家中。现在，能否仅仅因为在其家中查获了用于藏匿手枪的书，就断言杨文涛使用该手枪（作案凶器）实施了谋杀，从而认定他是凶手？这种假设是站不住脚的。一个人能仅仅因为在一具尸体旁发现的一把刀是他的财产而被认定为谋杀犯吗？不能；同样地，如果那把刀不属于他，就更不应认定他有罪；如果在他家中仅发现了用于藏匿这把刀的物品，则更不应认定他有罪。
(b) 综上所述，可以看出，即使警方在法庭上提交的所有证据均未受到质疑，也不能用以证明杨文涛就是谋杀日本海军陆战队员中山的人。假设因为书是在杨文涛家中查获的，就可以将他视为谋杀嫌疑人，但这一事实与上诉人毫无关系；如果上诉人没有在酷刑下作出任何供述，他就不会被指控犯罪。这一点非常清楚，值得最高法院考虑，因为所谓“当局者迷”（意指处理案件的人），容易走入歧途，而“旁观者清”，看得十分清楚。由此可以理解，若非上诉人在酷刑下作出供述，他是不会卷入此案的。

Morning Translation.

(8) The motive of the murder:
The Municipal Police declared that they were unable to find a motive for the murder. It was only after having repeatedly been asked by the Court of First Instance to find the motive that the Police submitted the statement of the appellant and declared that the appellant had admitted at the Police Station that the murder was committed with the object of creating a disturbance and expanding the influence of his clique in Hongkew. However, it has to be noted that the Dong Jen and Dong Nyi Associations are benevolent organizations and that the appellant and Yang Wen Tao are persons of common intelligence only, therefore the influence they would enjoy in Hongkew cannot be gauged. In the event of disturbances taking place in Hongkew, how would they expand their influence? Furthermore, the method of expanding one's influence by assassination is unheard of. It was, therefore, improper of the Courts of First and Second Instance to believe this point without giving careful consideration to the statements made by the appellant.

(9) The Counter-evidence brought by the accused:
During the first few hearings of the case in the Court of First Instance, each time that the Municipal Advocate submitted the statements of the accused that had been taken and written up by the Police after interrogating accused and requested the Court to question the accused according to these statements, the witnesses, after their statements had been taken by the Police, attended the Court and admitted their statements. Although a public charge had been filed against the accused, the Court of Criminal Division of the Court of First Instance based its inquiry on the result of the Police investigations. In the meantime, the Police continued their investigations. Furthermore, the Police had exceeded their authority to investigate entrusted to them by the Criminal Division of the Court, but The Police made the investigations not only in Shanghai as far as Tsingtao. As a result, it has happened that witnesses came but did not dare to tell the truth, while other witnesses went into hiding. Sometimes, statements advantageous to the accused were obtained, but they were put aside. Many statements of such a nature were obtained and brought to Shanghai from Tsingtao, but none of them was produced in Court. On the contrary, the Police regarded the common suit of foreign dress and the letter of introduction as important but the letter was rejected by the Courts of First and Second Instance. This shows how difficult it has been for the appellant to produce counter-evidence.
The following are a few points that are advantageous to the accused:-
(1) With reference to the report that the appellant had a fight with somebody at the Nanyang Dance Hall on the eve of the opening of the hall, both Yao Soong Ding (姚松亭), a private detective of the hall, and Chang Zai Yuan, a Police witness, stated that a fight took place that evening and that a few minutes later, they saw the appellant standing outside the hall. (Vide the 27th report of the Police.) Yao Soong Ding further stated that the

(8) 谋杀动机：
工部局警务处宣称他们无法找到谋杀动机。只是在初审法院多次要求寻找动机后，警方才提交了上诉人的供述，并宣称上诉人在警察局承认，实施谋杀的目的是为了制造骚乱并扩大其派系在虹口（Hongkew）的影响力。然而，必须指出的是，同仁会（Dong Jen Association）和同仁义会（Dong Nyi Association）是慈善组织，且上诉人和杨文涛只是智力平平之人，因此他们在虹口可能拥有的影响力难以估量。万一虹口发生骚乱，他们又如何扩大影响力呢？此外，通过暗杀来扩大影响力的做法闻所未闻。因此，初审和二审法院在未仔细考量上诉人供述的情况下轻信这一点，是不妥当的。

(9) 被告提出的反证：
在初审法院审理本案的头几次听证中，每当工部局检察官提交由警方在讯问被告后记录整理的被告供述，并请求法院根据这些供述讯问被告时，那些经警方录取证词的证人出庭并承认了其证词。虽然已对被告提起公诉，但初审法院刑事庭的调查是基于警方调查结果进行的。与此同时，警方继续进行调查。此外，警方超越了刑事庭委托给他们的调查权限，不仅在上海，甚至远至青岛进行了调查。结果导致有的证人虽出庭却不敢讲真话，而其他证人则躲藏起来。有时获得了有利于被告的供词，但被搁置一旁。许多此类供词从青岛获得并带到上海，但没有一份在法庭上出示。相反，警方认为一套普通的西式服装和一封介绍信很重要，但这封信被初审和二审法院驳回。这表明上诉人提出反证是多么困难。
以下是几点有利于被告的事实：
(1) 关于上诉人在舞厅开业前夕于南洋舞厅（Nanyang Dance Hall）与人打架的报告，该舞厅的私人侦探姚松亭（Yao Soong Ding）和警方证人张在元（Chang Zai Yuan）均陈述当晚发生了斗殴，几分钟后，他们看见上诉人站在舞厅外。（见警方第27号报告。）姚松亭进一步陈述称，

pages.en:
January 11, 1937. Morning Translation.

Nanyang Dance Hall was opened on November 8, 1935. (Vide the written record of the Court of First Instance of June 16.)
(2) On November 10, 193t, the appellant hired some rooms at the Great China Restaurant (大中華) to celebrate the birthday anniversary of his mother. The dinner arrangements was made on behalf of the appellant by Chang Zai Yuan, a Police witness, and this was admitted by Chang. (Vide the written record of the Court of First Instance on June 16;) Therefore, on the day before the murder of Nakayama and on the day after the murder, appellant was engaged. Can it be believed that the appellant would suddenly resort to murder on the day between these two dates?
(3) It will not be difficult to prove that at night the appellant usually visited the restaurant on the upper and the dance hall on the ground floor of the Moon Palace Hotel. In those confessions of the appellant which were made under torture, he confessed to the murder, saying that he left the Moon Palace Hotel before the murder and that he returned to the hotel after the murder. The time was too short for the commission of a murder.
(4) The appellant had received a telephone message from Chang Zai Yuen(張財源) advising him to make good his escape because the Police were about to arrest him. Upon learning of this, the appellant passed the information to Mi Pau Sun(宓保生) who verified this at a hearing of the Court of First Instance (vide record of the hearing held by the Court of First Instance on September 16). If the appellant had been guilty of the crime, he would not have remained in Shanghai.

(10) The facts in the case as revealed by the evidence:
The investigation made by the Court of First Instance into this case shows that the appellant had nothing to do with the murder of the marine Nakayama; it gives an indication of the kind of person who had killed the marine. According to an examination made by the Medico-Legal Laboratory, the powder marks show that the distance of the victim's head from the firing spot is only about five centimeters (vide Item 6 (a)). If the murderer was following the victim at the time of the murder, there is no reason why he should have fired only when he had come into contact with the victim. It clearly shows that the murderer did walk side by side with the victim and then fired. (Pu Chiao Ying's statement proved that the murderer and the victim did walk side by side, see Item 6 (b)). Furthermore, D.S.I. Crowther stated that the movements of the victim on the day in question between 5.40 p.m. and 8 p.m. could not be ascertained, except that from 4 p.m. to 6.40 p.m. he was in the barracks and that the victim had spent nearly all his time in brothel-like places. In all he visited four places. D.S.I. Crowther added:- "At the time in question Kaiji Nishikawa did ask the victim to pass the night at the brothel but he declined," (vide record of the hearing held by the Court of First Instance

南洋舞厅于1935年11月8日开业。（见6月16日初审法院笔录。）
(2) 193t年11月10日（原文年份不清），上诉人在大中华酒家（Great China Restaurant）预订了几个房间以庆祝其母亲寿辰。晚宴安排由警方证人张在元（Chang Zai Yuan）代表上诉人办理，张对此予以承认。（见6月16日初审法院笔录；）因此，在中山遇害的前一天和后一天，上诉人均有事在身。能否相信上诉人会在这两个日期之间的那一天突然实施谋杀？
(3) 不难证明，上诉人夜间通常光顾月宫饭店（Moon Palace Hotel）楼上的餐厅和底层的舞厅。在上诉人在酷刑下作出的那些供认中，他承认了谋杀罪行，称他在谋杀发生前离开了月宫饭店，并在谋杀发生后返回饭店。这段时间太短，不足以实施谋杀。
(4) 上诉人收到张财源（Chang Zai Yuen）的电话留言，劝其赶紧逃跑，因为警方即将逮捕他。得知此事后，上诉人将此信息转告宓保生（Mi Pau Sun），宓保生在初审法院的一次听证会上证实了这一点（见9月16日初审法院听证记录）。如果上诉人有罪，他就不会留在上海。

(10) 证据所揭示的案件事实：
初审法院对本案的调查表明，上诉人与海军陆战队员中山的谋杀案毫无关系；它指出了杀害该海军陆战队员的是何种人。根据法医实验室的检查，火药痕迹显示，受害者头部距离射击点仅约五厘米（见第6(a)项）。如果凶手在谋杀时正尾随受害者，他没有理由只有在接触到受害者时才开枪。这清楚地表明，凶手是与受害者并肩行走，然后开枪的。（浦桥英（Pu Chiao Ying，音译）的证言证明凶手和受害者确实并肩行走，见第6(b)项）。此外，副督察长（D.S.I.）克劳瑟（Crowther）陈述称，除下午4点至6点40分受害者在兵营外，其在当日傍晚5点40分至8点之间的行踪无法查明，且受害者几乎将所有时间都花在类似妓院的地方。他总共去了四个地方。副督察长克劳瑟补充道：“在当时，西川凯二（Kaiji Nishikawa，音译）曾邀请受害者在妓院过夜，但他拒绝了，”（见5月1日初审法院举行的听证记录

on May 1). This proves that the victim was a man of lust.
The murder occurred just after he had refused to pass the
night at the brothel and he was returning to the barracks.
The shooting might have been due to jealousy over some women.
In view of the various reasons mentioned
above, appellant has no connection whatsoever with the
murder of Nakayama. His accusation was brought about
by certain person or persons who desired to secure the
reward and who conspired to bring a false accusation against
him. The Supreme Court is requested to study the appeal
carefully and to quash the decision of the Courts of First
and Second Instance and to return a verdict finding the
appellant not guilty or to order a re-trial.

）。这证明受害者是一个好色之徒。
谋杀发生在他拒绝在妓院过夜并返回兵营之后不久。
枪击可能是出于对某些女性的嫉妒。
鉴于上述各种理由，上诉人与中山的谋杀案没有任何关联。对他的指控是由某些企图获取赏金的人策划的，他们合谋对他进行诬告。恳请最高法院仔细研究本上诉，撤销初审和二审法院的判决，宣判上诉人无罪，或下令重审。

Sin Wen Pao and other local newspapers:

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE: YIH HAI SUNG'S APPEAL

(continued from January 9)

(a) The Court of Second Instance declared that both Hu Ziang Wu and Pan Chiao Ying had said that they saw a man wearing black clothing. It will be recalled that in cold weather people usually wear dark coloured clothing, especially in foreign dress and military uniforms. On July 7, the Court of First Instance wrote a report on the reconstruction of the crime in which it says: "There was an electric lamp on an electric pole, but the light was comparatively weak as the lamp was very high and the street was deserted and wide. The place was very dark, but the length and the bright colour of the clothing could be distinguished. All dark coloured clothing seen under such a street lamp can be said to be black clothing. Hu Ziang Wu's statement, as given in Paragraph (c) above, reads: "It seemed that the clothing of the men who escaped had the style of the clothing worn by marines." Therefore, the so-called dark colour must be intended to mean this.

(b) The Court of Second Instance regarded the statement of Chang Zai Yuen to the effect that on that evening he saw the appellant and others walking on North Szechuen Road towards the northern direction as true. But at the Police Station and in the Court of First Instance, Chang Zai Yuen repeatedly stated that at that time the appellant was dressed in a Sun Yat Sen style of uniform. (Vide the written record of Volume 1 of the Court of First Instance and statement Page No.47). Can his statements then be believed?

(c) The Court of Second Instance accepted the statement of "Hai-Loh-Ya" (海樂亞), a Portuguese, as true. This witness stated: "The door of Room No.9 was pushed half open and I saw Yih Hai Sung in the room." As a matter of fact, the entry of Room No.9 near the door is narrow, so that with the door only half open one would only have seen the wall and not the interior of the room. This can be proved by referring to a plan of the room.(Vide Court File Page No.102, Volume 2, of the Court of First Instance.) The statement of this witness is evidently unfounded.

(d) The appellant clearly stated in the Court of First Instance that Room No.9 in the Moon Palace Hotel was booked by Au Tsung Kyi (夏春記). The Court regarded this statement to mean that the appellant had booked the room in the name of Au Tsung Kyi. This is a gross mistake. Au Tsung Kyi is the name of an actual person and is not a fictitious name used by the appellant.

(e) The appellant did not state in his confessions on May 1 and May 6 that Yang Wen Tao had taken a pistol out of a book and handed it to the appellant. He said this only in his written statement which he copied from one prepared by the Police after he was severely tortured. The book was seized by the Police in April. If the Court of Second Instance holds that the seizure of the book shows that the appellant's statement corresponds with the facts, then the arrest of Yang Wen Tao can prove the same thing.

《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

中山案：叶海松之上诉

（续1月9日）

(a) 二审法院认定，胡祥武与潘巧英均称看见一名身穿黑衣的男子。需知在寒冷天气中，人们通常穿着深色衣物，尤其是西式服装和军装。7月7日，一审法院就犯罪现场重建撰写了一份报告，其中写道：“电线杆上有一盏电灯，但由于灯位很高，且街道空旷宽阔，光线相对微弱。现场非常昏暗，但仍能分辨出衣物的长度和鲜艳颜色。在此类街灯下看到的所有深色衣物，均可称为黑衣。如上文(c)段所述，胡祥武的供词称：‘逃跑者的衣着样式似乎类似于海军陆战队员的制服。’因此，所谓的深色必定是指此意。”

(b) 二审法院采信了张载元的证词，即当晚他看见上诉人等人沿四川北路向北行走。但在警局及一审法院审理期间，张载元反复陈述，当时上诉人身着中山装式样的制服。（参见一审法院卷一笔录及第47页供词。）那么，他的证词是否可信？

(c) 二审法院采信了一名葡萄牙人“海樂亞”（音译）的证词。该证人称：“9号房门半开，我看见叶海松在房内。”事实上，9号房门口附近的入口狭窄，若门仅半开，只能看见墙壁，而无法看见房间内部。这一点可通过查阅房间平面图予以证明。（参见一审法院卷二案卷第102页。）该证人的证词显然毫无根据。

(d) 上诉人在一审法院明确陈述，月宫饭店的9号房间是由夏春記（Au Tsung Kyi）预订的。法院将此陈述理解为上诉人以夏春記的名义预订了房间。这是一个严重的错误。夏春記是一个真实人物的姓名，并非上诉人使用的化名。

(e) 上诉人在5月1日和5月6日的供词中，并未陈述杨文涛从书中取出手枪并交给上诉人。他仅在一份书面陈述中如此说法，而该陈述是他在遭受严刑拷打后，抄录自警方拟好的文本。该书于四月被警方查获。如果二审法院认为查获该书表明上诉人的陈述符合事实，那么逮捕杨文涛同样可以证明这一点。

There is no ground on which the Courts could have reached
this conclusion. If the Supreme Court will compare the
points for and against the theory that appellant's statement
corresponds with the facts, it will immediately see whether
or not the statement does correspond with the facts.

(7) A general study of all the evidence in this case:
(a) The evidence in this case secured and produced
by the Police would not have been sufficient to justify
the charge against the appellant and Yang Wen Tao for the
murder but for the statements made by the appellant under
torture. Speaking from a logical point of view, even if
the book in question was actually seized at the home of
Yang Wen Tao and was proved to be actually his property
and that it was actually used by him for the purpose of
concealing the pistol that was produced in Court as an
exhibit and that the spent bullet that had caused the death
of the Japanese marine Nakayama and the empty cartridge
shell produced in Court were actually found to have been
fired from the said pistol, can all this be regarded as
evidence proving that the Japanese marine Hideo Nakayama
was murdered by Yang Wen Tao? What was seized in the home of
Yang Wen Tao was only a book and not the pistol that was
produced in Court as an exhibit; in other words, it was
only an article that was used for the purpose of concealing
the crime weapon (if the pistol produced in Court is actually
the weapon that was used in the murder); it was not the
weapon itself. Moreover, it was known that the pistol (the
murder weapon) was not found in the possession of Yang Wen
Tao, but was concealed beneath a wooden box where it was
subsequently found, while the book which was known to have
been used for the purpose of concealing this pistol was
safely deposited at the home of Yang Wen Tao. Now, can it
be definitely alleged that Yang Wen Tao had used this pistol
(the crime weapon) to commit the murder and that he is
a murderer simply because the book which was used for the
purpose of concealing a pistol was seized at his home?
Such a hypothesis is untenable. Can a person be held for
the murder of another person simply because a knife which
was found beside the murdered person is his property?
No; in the same way, much less will he be held guilty if
the knife does not belong to him and still less so if only
an article used for the purpose of concealing this knife
is found at his home.
(b) From the above, it can be seen that even if
all the evidence produced in Court by the Police remains
unchallenged, it cannot be used to prove that Yang Wen Tao
was the person who had murdered the Japanese marine Nakayama.
Supposing that Yang Wen Tao can be held as a suspect for
the murder because the book was seized at his home, this fact
has nothing whatever to do with the appellant, who would not
have been charged with the crime if he had not made any
statements under torture. This is quite clear and deserves
consideration by the Supreme Court, because one who "goes
inside the horn of an ox" (meaning one who is handling a case)
is liable to go astray, but one who remains an on-looker
"above the sky", sees quite clearly. From this, it can be
understood that the appellant would not have become involved
in this case but for his statements made under torture.

法院得出这一结论没有任何依据。如果最高法院对比支持或反对“上诉人陈述符合事实”这一理论的要点，就能立即看出该陈述是否符合事实。

(7) 对本案所有证据的综合研究：
(a) 若非上诉人在酷刑下作出的供词，警方获取并提交的本案件证据不足以正当化对上诉人和杨文涛谋杀罪的指控。从逻辑角度而言，即使涉案书籍确实在杨文涛家中被查获，并被证实确为其财产，且确实被他用于藏匿作为法庭证物出示的手枪，并且导致日本海军陆战队员中山死亡的已发射子弹以及在法庭出示的空弹壳经证实确由该手枪射出，所有这些能否被视为证明日本海军陆战队员中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）系被杨文涛谋杀的证据？在杨文涛家中查获的仅是一本书，而非作为法庭证物出示的手枪；换言之，它仅是用于藏匿犯罪凶器（如果法庭出示的手枪确实是作案凶器）的物品，而非凶器本身。此外，众所周知，手枪（作案凶器）并非在杨文涛身上被发现，而是藏在一个木箱下面，随后在那里被找到，而据知用于藏匿该手枪的书则安然存放在杨文涛家中。现在，能否仅仅因为在杨文涛家中查获了用于藏匿手枪的书，就断言杨文涛使用该手枪（作案凶器）实施了谋杀，从而认定他是凶手？这种假设是站不住脚的。能否仅仅因为在一具尸体旁发现的一把刀属于某人，就认定此人犯有谋杀罪？不能；同理，如果那把刀不属于他，就更不能认定他有罪；如果仅在他家中发现了用于藏匿这把刀的物品，则更不能认定他有罪。
(b) 综上所述，即使警方在法庭提交的所有证据均未受到质疑，也不能用以证明杨文涛是谋杀日本海军陆战队员中山的人。假设因为书在杨文涛家中被查获，就可以将他视为谋杀嫌疑犯，但这一事实与上诉人毫无关系；如果上诉人没有在酷刑下作出任何供词，他就不会被指控犯罪。这一点非常清楚，值得最高法院考虑，因为所谓“当局者迷”（意指处理案件的人），容易走入歧途，而“旁观者清”，看得非常清楚。由此可以理解，若非上诉人在酷刑下作出供词，他不会卷入此案。

(8) The motive of the murder:
The Municipal Police declared that they were unable to find a motive for the murder. It was only after having repeatedly been asked by the Court of First Instance to find the motive that the Police submitted the statement of the appellant and declared that the appellant had admitted at the Police Station that the murder was committed with the object of creating a disturbance and expanding the influence of his clique in Hongkew. However, it has to be noted that the Dong Jen and Dong Nyi Associations are benevolent organizations and that the appellant and Yang Wen Tao are persons of common intelligence only, therefore the influence they would enjoy in Hongkew cannot be gauged. In the event of disturbances taking place in Hongkew, how would they expand their influence? Furthermore, the method of expanding one's influence by assassination is unheard of. It was, therefore, improper of the Courts of First and Second Instance to believe this point without giving careful consideration to the statements made by the appellant.

(9) The Counter-evidence brought by the accused:
During the first few hearings of the case in the Court of First Instance, each time that the Municipal Advocate submitted the statements of the accused that had been taken and written up by the Police after interrogating accused and requested the Court to question the accused according to these statements, the witnesses, after their statements had been taken by the Police, attended the Court and admitted their statements. Although a public charge had been filed against the accused, the Court of Criminal Division of the Court of First Instance based its inquiry on the result of the Police investigations. In the meantime, the Police continued their investigations. Furthermore, the Police had exceeded their authority to investigate entrusted to them by the Criminal Division of the Court, but the Police made the investigations not only in Shanghai as far as Tsingtao. As a result, it has happened that witnesses came but did not dare to tell the truth, while other witnesses went into hiding. Sometimes, statements advantageous to the accused were obtained, but they were put aside. Many statements of such a nature were obtained and brought to Shanghai from Tsingtao, but none of them was produced in Court. On the contrary, the Police regarded the common suit of foreign dress and the letter of introduction as important but the letter was rejected by the Courts of First and Second Instance. This shows how difficult it has been for the appellant to produce counter-evidence.
The following are a few points that are advantageous to the accused:-
(1) With reference to the report that the appellant had a fight with somebody at the Nanyang Dance Hall on the eve of the opening of the hall, both Yao Soong Ding (姚松亭), a private detective of the hall, and Chang Zai Yuan, a Police witness, stated that a fight took place that evening and that a few minutes later, they saw the appellant standing outside the hall. (Vide the 27th report of the Police.) Yao Soong Ding further stated that the

(8) 谋杀动机：
工部局警务处宣称无法找到谋杀动机。只是在一审法院多次要求寻找动机后，警方才提交了上诉人的供词，并宣称上诉人在警局承认，实施谋杀的目的是为了制造骚乱，并扩大其派系在虹口地区的影响力。然而，必须注意到，同仁会和同义会均为慈善组织，且上诉人和杨文涛仅为普通智力水平之人，因此他们在虹口地区所能享有的影响力难以估量。倘若虹口发生骚乱，他们又如何扩大影响力？此外，通过暗杀来扩大影响力的方法闻所未闻。因此，一审和二审法院在未仔细考量上诉人供词的情况下轻信这一点，是不妥当的。

(9) 被告提出的反证：
在一审法院审理本案的前几次听证中，每当公诉人提交警方在讯问被告后记录整理的被告供词，并请求法院根据这些供词讯问被告时，那些在警方录取供词后的证人出庭并承认了其供词。尽管已对被告提起公诉，但一审法院刑事庭的调查仍基于警方调查结果。与此同时，警方继续进行调查。此外，警方超越了刑事庭委托给他们的调查权限，不仅在上海，甚至远至青岛进行调查。结果导致证人虽到庭却不敢讲真话，而其他证人则躲藏起来。有时虽获得了有利于被告的供词，但被搁置一旁。许多此类供词从青岛获得并带回上海，但未在法庭上出示。相反，警方将一套普通的西式服装和一封介绍信视为重要证据，但该信件被一审和二审法院驳回。这表明上诉人提出反证是多么困难。

(1) 关于上诉人在舞厅开业前夕于南洋舞厅与人打架的报告，该舞厅的私人侦探姚松亭和警方证人张载元均陈述，当晚发生了打斗，几分钟后，他们看见上诉人站在舞厅外。（参见警方第27号报告。）姚松亭进一步陈述，

At the third session held on May 20, the appellant made a similar statement and gave more detailed answers to questions put to him.
The appellant gave a reconstruction of the crime at the spot on May 22. Here, the evidence produced by the Police, which had been rendered valueless by the appellant's new statement at the second hearing, was still applicable. The only change was that the Police charged the appellant as the chief culprit who fired the fatal shot instead of the charge of being an accessory. However, the record of the hearing of the Court of First Instance of May 20 contained the following note:- "Yih Hai Sung wept. Question: 'As you committed the crime alone and as you alone should bear the consequences, why should you weep?' Yih Hai Sung gave no reply."
The record of the reconstruction of the crime dated May 22 contained the following note:- "Question: 'Did you not previously state that you ran southward upon with-drawing from the scene?' Answer: 'As the facts in the case show that the murderer fled southward, so I stated that I ran southward.' Subsequently Yih murmured that he was being falsely accused." The record also contained the following note:- "Question: 'Did you not previously state that you returned to the Moon Palace?' Answer: 'Eh .... I returned to the Moon Palace.' Question: 'Speak properly. Where did you actually go?' Answer: 'Moon Palace.'" He then cried in a low tone, 'Judge, please save my life.' Question: 'Why did you cry out, "Save life"?' At the hearing on May 27, the appellant wept bitterly and denied any connection with the murder of the marine. A detailed description of the tortures to which the appellant had been subjected is contained in the notes written on 14 sheets of paper by the appellant and submitted to the Supreme Court together with a petition on December 26. The following is an extract from the notes giving an account of events which occurred after the appellant had admitted on May 6 that he had killed the Japanese marine single-handed:- "A wooden box was brought in. （续昨日）

在5月20日举行的第三次庭审中，上诉人作了类似陈述，并对向其提出的问题作了更详细的回答。
上诉人于5月22日在现场重现了犯罪过程。在此过程中，警方提出的、因上诉人在第二次听证会上的新陈述而变得无效的证据，仍然适用。唯一的改变是，警方指控上诉人为发射致命子弹的主犯，而非从犯。然而，5月20日初审法庭的听证记录包含以下注记：- “叶海松哭泣。问：‘既然你是单独作案，后果也应由你独自承担，为何要哭？’叶海松未作回答。”
5月22日的犯罪重现记录包含以下注记：- “问：‘你之前不是说撤离现场时向南跑吗？’答：‘既然案件事实显示凶手向南逃窜，所以我便说我向南跑。’随后叶低声嘟囔称自己遭到诬陷。”记录还包含以下注记：- “问：‘你之前不是说回到了月宫饭店吗？’答：‘呃……我回到了月宫饭店。’问：‘好好说。你到底去了哪里？’答：‘月宫饭店。’”随后他低声哭喊，‘法官，请饶命。’问：‘为何喊“饶命”？’他结结巴巴说了些什么，未能给出回答。”
在5月27日的听证会上，上诉人痛哭流涕，否认与海军陆战队员被杀案有任何关联。他在法庭上脱去衣服，以展示其在警察局遭受的酷刑。关于上诉人所受酷刑的详细描述，载于上诉人用14页纸写成的笔记中，并于12月26日连同请愿书一并提交给最高法院。以下是从笔记中摘录的一段，叙述了上诉人在5月6日承认独自杀害日本海军陆战队员之后发生的事件：- “搬进来一个木箱。里面装有电池；被称为电箱。我的双眼被一块黑布蒙住。我被剥去所有衣物。我被按在长凳上，手脚被绑在长凳上。我听到一阵咔哒声，有什么东西掠过我的肋骨。我昏厥过去，失去知觉，如同死了一般。随后冷水浇在我身上。我感到一阵寒意，逐渐恢复意识。二十分钟后，一个带电的东西套在我的生殖器上。几分钟后，精液如水般流出。当他们把我从长凳上解开时，我已无法说话或行走。我的身体软如棉花……我的双眼

were again blindfolded, but this time they did not use electricity. They poured water into my nostrils and stuffed my mouth with cotton so that I could not breathe through the mouth. My ribs were rubbed with fists to cause the water to flow into my body. This went on for more than one hour. After this they thrust burning cigarette butts into my nostrils ......... I could not stand the torture and was compelled to copy word by word a statement previously prepared by Zung Wei Ming."
This was the most serious part of the torture. When the appellant stated that he had been tortured, the Court of First Instance ordered him to be examined by the Court Doctor who issued the following report :- "He (the appellant) stated that he felt pains in the ribs, especially in the left side, and that the pain was caused not by blows but by the rubbing of some soft article. Upon examination it was found that the pains occurred at the 6th, 7th and 8th ribs."
This is definite proof of the allegation that water was poured into his mouth and that his ribs had been rubbed to cause the water to flow into his body. The Doctor's report went on:- "There is an oval shaped scar on the upper lip beneath the nostrils, 1 centimeter in length and 5 millimeters in width. The scar is soft and regular in shape. The centre part was of pink colour with white lines. Judging by its condition, the skin must have dropped off not longer than three weeks ago."
Evidently this wound was caused by burning with a cigarette end. The certificate issued by Superintendent Johnson of the Municipal Hospital also stated that it was possible that the scar had been caused by burning. The regularity and size of the scar shows that it was not caused by scratching or biting.
The Courts of First and Second Instance evaded the point regarding the rubbing of the ribs by simply saying that there was no external injury. As to the wound on the lip, it is true that the appellant told the lawyer when the letter went to the Police Station to interview him that he had caused it himself by scratching, but he had said this because he did not dare do otherwise in the presence of the Chinese and foreign Detective Sub-Inspectors, but he did clearly say that he knew nothing of the murder. He also wept very hard and said that he wished he could be a spirit so that he might take revenge on the persons who had falsely accused him. Again, the Courts of First and Second Instance failed to pay attention to this point.
The appellant told his lawyer during an interview about the swallowing of a metallic article. The lawyer was also told at the time that the appellant was suffering from diarrhoea. This was heard by the Chinese and foreign police officers present during the interview and was mentioned in a petition submitted by the appellant's lawyer the next day. It was possible that the metallic article swallowed had been discharged from the bowels before the appellant was examined by the Court Doctor and this might be the reason why the Court Doctor had failed to find any metallic article in the bowels of the appellant. This, however, is an altogether different question and does not prove whether or not torture had been applied.

再次被蒙住，但这次他们没有使用电刑。他们往我的鼻孔里灌水，并用棉花塞住我的嘴，使我无法通过嘴巴呼吸。他们用拳头摩擦我的肋骨，迫使水流进体内。这一过程持续了一个多小时。之后，他们将燃烧的烟头塞进我的鼻孔……我无法忍受酷刑，被迫逐字抄写由宗伟明（Zung Wei Ming）事先准备好的供词。”
这是酷刑中最严重的部分。当上诉人陈述其遭受酷刑时，初审法庭命令法庭医生对其进行检查，医生出具了如下报告：- “他（上诉人）称感到肋骨疼痛，尤其是左侧，且疼痛并非由击打造成，而是由某种柔软物品的摩擦所致。经检查，发现疼痛部位位于第6、第7和第8根肋骨。”
这确凿地证明了水被灌入其口中，且其肋骨受到摩擦以迫使水流进体内的指控。医生的报告接着写道：- “鼻孔下方的上唇处有一个椭圆形的疤痕，长1厘米，宽5毫米。疤痕质地柔软，形状规则。中心部分呈粉红色，带有白色纹路。根据其状况判断，皮肤脱落的时间不超过三周。”
显然，此伤口是由烟头烫伤所致。市立医院约翰逊（Johnson）警司出具的证明也指出，该疤痕可能是由烫伤造成。疤痕的规则性和大小表明，它并非由抓挠或咬噬造成。
初审和二审法庭仅以没有外部伤痕为由，回避了关于摩擦肋骨的问题。至于嘴唇上的伤口，确实，上诉人在律师去警察局会见他时曾告诉律师，伤口是他自己抓挠造成的，但他之所以这么说，是因为在中外副督察面前不敢有其他说法，但他确实明确表示自己对谋杀案一无所知。他还痛哭不已，并表示希望自己变成鬼魂，以便向诬告他的人复仇。然而，初审和二审法庭再次忽视了这一点。
上诉人在一次会见中告诉其律师，他曾吞下一件金属物品。当时还告知律师，上诉人正患有腹泻。出席会见的中外警官听到了这一情况，上诉人的律师在次日提交的请愿书中提到了此事。有可能在法庭医生检查上诉人之前，吞下的金属物品已通过肠道排出，这可能是法庭医生未在上诉人肠道中发现任何金属物品的原因。然而，这是一个完全不同的问题，并不能证明是否施加了酷刑。

The Courts of First and Second Instance asked why, if the appellant had been subjected to torture after May 6, he had made a confession before May 6. The Courts have misunderstood this point. The appellant was subjected to torture not only after May 6, but also before May 1, on which date the appellant made the confession, only that the torture applied after May 6 was more vigorous than that applied before that date. This can be seen from the statement made by the appellant in Court and also from the notes written by the appellant (which I request the Supreme Court to regard as a part of the reasons for the appeal). The appellant on May 1 admitted that he had aided and abetted in the murder but on May 6 he changed his statement and said that he committed the murder single-handed. For this reason he was subjected to more severe torture after May 6, until he made up for the inconsistency of his statements on May 20. This was what had actually occurred.

(5) The reconstruction of the crime was not made by appellant of his own free will

On May 22 the appellant gave a reconstruction of the crime at the place where it occurred. The reconstruction was based directly upon his statements made in Court on May 20. At the time he not only still bore in mind the torture to which he had been subjected, but prior to the reconstruction he had, on several occasions, been led by the Police to the scene of the murder to reconstruct the crime. For this reason, whatever mistakes he might have made in the reconstruction had already been corrected, (vide the appellant's statement contained in the record of the Court of Second Instance and his written statement which was attached to the previous appeal). Even D.S.I. Crowther admitted that the appellant was led on two occasions to the scene to reconstruct the crime, (vide the record of the Court of First Instance of May 20). Thus, the appellant had full knowledge of all particulars about the place and of the reconstruction itself. Moreover, from the beginning to the end of the reconstruction, he was held by two Japanese policemen, one on each side, and his hands were handcuffed separately to the two officers. Furthermore, a number of Japanese policemen closely surrounded him. All this can be verified by the photographs of the reconstruction published in local newspapers and which were submitted to both the Courts of First and Second Instance by appellant's lawyer. Therefore, during the reconstruction, the appellant moved only when others moved and stopped when others stopped. It was a reconstruction in name only; to tell the truth, it was a kind of "directed" reconstruction. As the record on the reconstruction does not indicate that it was made under compulsion and force, the Court of Second Instance, therefore, took it for granted that the reconstruction of the crime was made of appellant's free will. This is incorrect. The Court further declared that the appellant's lawyer had initialled the record on the reconstruction at that time and had not said anything about the reconstruction not being made with appellant's free will. However, it is to be noted that the record contained only what took place during the reconstruction; the record does not say whether the appellant had been subjected to torture prior to the reconstruction, nor does it say anything about

初审和二审法院质问，如果上诉人在5月6日之后遭受酷刑，为何他在5月6日之前就作出了供认。法院误解了这一点。上诉人不仅在5月6日之后，而且在5月1日之前也遭受了酷刑，而上诉人正是在5月1日这一天作出的供认，只不过5月6日之后施加的酷刑比该日期之前更为猛烈。这可以从上诉人在法庭上的陈述以及上诉人所写的笔记中看出（我请求最高法院将这些笔记视为上诉理由的一部分）。上诉人在5月1日承认他协助并教唆了谋杀，但在5月6日他改变了口供，称他是单独一人实施了谋杀。因此，在5月6日之后他遭受了更严厉的酷刑，直到他在5月20日弥补了其口供中的不一致之处。这才是实际发生的情况。

(5) 犯罪现场重演并非上诉人自愿进行

5月22日，上诉人在案发地点进行了犯罪现场重演。这次重演直接基于他于5月20日在法庭上所作的陈述。当时，他不仅仍铭记着所遭受的酷刑，而且在重演之前，警方已多次带他到谋杀现场进行犯罪重演。因此，无论他在重演中可能犯下的任何错误都已被纠正（见二审法院笔录中包含的上诉人陈述及其附在前次上诉状中的书面陈述）。甚至副巡长（D.S.I.）克劳瑟（Crowther）也承认，上诉人曾两次被带到现场进行犯罪重演（见5月20日初审法院笔录）。因此，上诉人对该地点的所有细节及重演本身均完全知情。此外，从重演开始到结束，他一直由两名日本警察挟持，每侧一人，他的双手分别铐在这两名警官身上。而且，许多日本警察紧紧包围着他。所有这些均可由当地报纸刊登的重演照片证实，这些照片已由上诉人的律师提交给初审和二审法院。因此，在重演过程中，上诉人仅在他人移动时移动，在他人停止时停止。这仅是名义上的重演；说实话，这是一种“受指挥”的重演。由于重演笔录并未表明这是在强迫和武力下进行的，因此二审法院想当然地认为犯罪重演是出于上诉人的自由意志。这是不正确的。法院进一步宣称，上诉人的律师当时在重演笔录上草签了姓名，且未对重演非出于上诉人自由意志一事提出任何异议。然而，需要注意的是，该笔录仅记录了重演期间发生的情况；笔录并未说明上诉人在重演前是否遭受过酷刑，也未提及

the movements of the hands of the two Japanese policemen who were handcuffed to the appellant at that time. Moreover, lawyer Chang Tse Niang declared at the time when he was asked to initial the record: "I was present during the reconstruction, but owing to the large number of persons present, I did not hear quite clearly the questions put to the accused and his replies. So, I am adding the characters 'Generally Correct' after my initials on the record." Moreover, lawyer Tong likewise stated: "Accused Yih Hai Sung was supported by two Japanese policemen; his hands were handcuffed. This is most improper." However, the Court of First Instance declared: "This is another matter, and this Court is at present unable to state whether or not this can be believed because this Court is at present unaware whether the lawyer for the defence, who was present at the reconstruction, will declare that the record, which was loudly read out at that time, contained parts which do not correspond to the facts." (vide the record of the Court of First Instance of May 27). Is the allegation of the Court of Second Instance to the effect that appellant's lawyer had failed to make any objection at the time he initialled the record, reasonable? A study of the record on the reconstruction shows that it contained the following statement about Yih Hai Sung:- "Yih Hai Sung replied that when he was told to run in a southerly direction, he ran in a southerly direction. (Afterwards he sighed and said in a low voice that he was being wrongfully accused.) Ah! Later (?) he returned to the Moon Palace Hotel. (Afterwards he cried in a low voice asking the Presiding Judge to save his life.) When he was asked why he cried, he gave no reply even after a long pause." The Court of Second Instance alleged that the appellant's lawyer had not made any protest, but it has also to be noted that the Court failed to notice sighs of the appellant during the reconstruction and that he had cried that he was being wrongfully accused.
(6) Appellant's statements and reconstruction do not correspond with facts:
According to Article 270 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the confessions of an accused cannot be regarded as reliable evidence if they had been obtained by means of compulsion or coercion or trickery or seduction or through any other unlawful and improper means; and furthermore, they should should correspond with the facts. But the statements appellant made after he had been subjected to torture by the Police do not correspond with the facts on many points.
The following are a number of these irregularities:
(a) Report No.43, Character Wen(文), of the Medico-Legal Laboratory states that, according to the angle of the bullet's course in the head, the bullet could have been fired from a distance of 50 centimeters, but according to the powder marks at the point of entry, the distance could have been only about 5 centimeters. During the reconstruction of the crime, the appellant demonstrated that he fired from a distance of 5 or 6 paces; this is several tens greater than the distance calculated by the Medico-Legal Laboratory. To get the angle of the bullet's course at such a distance of 5 or 6 paces, one has to shoot from a lying-down position, but then it will not cause powder marks at the point of entry. This is a most important part because it shows

当时与上诉人铐在一起的两名日本警察的手部动作。此外，张子良（Chang Tse Niang，音译）律师在被要求在笔录上草签时声明：“我在重演现场，但由于在场人数众多，我没有听清向被告提出的问题及其回答。因此，我在笔录上我的签名后添加了‘大致正确’字样。”此外，童（Tong，音译）律师同样表示：“被告叶海松（Yih Hai Sung，音译）由两名日本警察搀扶；他的双手被铐住。这是极不恰当的。”然而，初审法院宣称：“这是另一回事，本庭目前无法陈述此说法是否可信，因为本庭目前不知晓出席重演的辩护律师是否会声明，当时大声宣读的笔录中含有与事实不符的部分。”（见5月27日初审法院笔录）。二审法院关于上诉人律师在草签笔录时未提出任何异议的说法，是否合理？研究重演笔录显示，其中包含以下关于叶海松（Yih Hai Sung，音译）的陈述：“叶海松回答说，当被告知向南跑时，他便向南跑。（随后他叹息并低声说他被冤枉。）啊！后来（？）他回到了月宫饭店（Moon Palace Hotel）。（随后他低声哭泣，请求审判长饶命。）当被问及为何哭泣时，即使沉默良久，他也未作回答。”二审法院声称上诉人的律师未提出任何抗议，但也需注意，法院未能注意到上诉人在重演期间的叹息，以及他哭诉自己被冤枉的事实。
(6) 上诉人的陈述和重演与事实不符：
根据《刑事诉讼法》第270条，如果被告的供认是通过强迫、胁迫、欺诈、引诱或任何其他非法和不正当手段获得的，则不能被视为可靠证据；此外，供认应与事实相符。但是，上诉人在遭受警方酷刑后所作的陈述在许多方面与事实不符。
以下是一些不规则之处：
(a) 法医实验室第43号报告，文字编号为“文”，指出，根据子弹在头部轨迹的角度，子弹可能是从50厘米的距离发射的，但根据入口处的火药痕迹，距离可能仅为约5厘米。在犯罪重演期间，上诉人演示他是从5或6步的距离开枪的；这比法医实验室计算的距离大出数十倍。要在5或6步这样的距离上获得子弹的轨迹角度，必须采取卧姿射击，但那样就不会在入口处造成火药痕迹。这是最关键的部分，因为它表明
