The pistol was the weapon which fired the shot. The book on physics in which a hole in the shape of a pistol was excavated was used by Yang Wen Tao to conceal the pistol. Yang Wen Tao and appellant, in an attempt to extend their influence, had plotted attacks on Japanese naval officers so as to give rise to disturbances.
On the night of November 9, 1935, in company with Jack, they left the Moon Palace Hotel. On the way, Yang Wen Tao took the pistol from the book and handed it to appellant, who used this pistol to kill the Japanese marine Nakayama. The judgment which found the appellant and Yang Wen Tao guilty of the murder of the Japanese marine was based (1) upon the death of Nakayama, (2) the bullet which was produced in Court as an exhibit, and (3) the connection between this bullet and the pistol as well as the connection between the pistol and the book and that between the book and Yang Wen Tao, and as between Yang Wen Tao and the appellant.
But all these materials and other evidence which had been used as a basis for the judgment by the Court of First Instance are not reliable and substantial evidence against the appellant unless they have been given in evidence, that is to say, if the relations between any one of the exhibits produced in Court cannot be established, then the appellant cannot be held responsible for the death of the Japanese marine Hideo Nakayama. Moreover, unless there was sufficient evidence to prove that the appellant did use the pistol and had used it to shoot the Japanese marine, thereby causing his death, the appellant could not be found guilty of murder. However, a study of the case reveals that none of the material proofs submitted to the Court were reliable, nor were the connections between all these exhibits proved. Yet, in the face of all this, the Court of First Instance based its judgment entirely on appellant's statements which had been obtained under torture and on his other statements which were contradictory to one another. This clearly shows that the Court of First Instance had not dealt with the case properly and in a just manner.
It is to be noted that this unjust prosecution was due to a conspiracy on the part of Zung Wei Ming (鄭偉民) alias Hirayama, Tseng Yuen (曾元), Chang Zai Yuen (張財元) and Yang Chien Chung (楊健忠) who, with the object of securing the large rewards offered by the S.M.C. and the Japanese authorities for information leading to the apprehension of the murderer or murderers, plotted to create false evidence against the appellant and Yang Wen Tao. However, the Courts of First and Second Instance recklessly sentenced the appellant to death for the murder of the Japanese marine simply on this superficial evidence without first considering whether such evidence was true or otherwise.

(1) The police exhibits produced in Court, viz. one spent bullet and one empty cartridge shell.

手枪是发射该子弹的武器。杨文涛利用一本挖有手枪形状孔洞的物理书来藏匿手枪。杨文涛与上诉人为了扩大其影响力，策划袭击日本海军军官，以制造骚乱。
1935年11月9日晚，他们与杰克（Jack）一同离开月宫饭店（Moon Palace Hotel）。途中，杨文涛从书中取出手枪并交给上诉人，上诉人使用该手枪杀害了日本海军陆战队员中山（Nakayama）。判定上诉人与杨文涛犯有杀害日本海军陆战队员罪行的判决，是基于：(1) 中山的死亡；(2) 在法庭上作为证物出示的子弹；以及 (3) 该子弹与手枪之间的关联、手枪与书籍之间的关联、书籍与杨文涛之间的关联，以及杨文涛与上诉人之间的关联。
但是，除非这些材料及其他被初审法院用作判决依据的证据经过当庭举证，否则它们并非针对上诉人的可靠且确凿的证据；也就是说，如果法庭上出示的任何一件证物之间的关系无法确立，那么就不能认定上诉人对日本海军陆战队员中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）之死负责。此外，除非有充分证据证明上诉人确实使用了该手枪，并用其射击日本海军陆战队员致其死亡，否则不能判定上诉人犯有谋杀罪。然而，对案件的研究显示，提交给法庭的所有物证均不可靠，且所有这些证物之间的联系也未得到证实。尽管如此，初审法院完全基于通过酷刑获得的上诉人供述及其相互矛盾的其他陈述作出了判决。这清楚地表明，初审法院未能公正、恰当地处理此案。
值得注意的是，这一不公正的起诉是由于郑伟民（Zung Wei Ming，别名平山/Hirayama）、曾元（Tseng Yuen）、张财元（Chang Zai Yuen）和杨健忠（Yang Chien Chung）的阴谋所致，他们为了获取工部局（S.M.C.）和日本当局为提供线索抓捕凶手所设下的巨额赏金，密谋伪造针对上诉人和杨文涛的证据。然而，第一审和第二审法院仅凭这些表面证据，在未首先考量此类证据真伪的情况下，便轻率地判处上诉人因杀害日本海军陆战队员而死刑。

(1) 警方在法庭上出示的证物，即一枚已发射的子弹和一个空弹壳。

Police were said to have been picked up separately at
the scene of the incident by Japanese Constable No. 61
and Japanese Detective No. 51 of the Dixwell Road Police
Station. The Court of First Instance regarded these exhibits
as having been actually found at the scene of the incident
and that the bullet was the one that had caused the death

this bullet had in fact no connection whatever with the
death of the Japanese marine Nakayama, because
(a) According to the statement of the
Japanese Constable No. 61, he picked up the spent bullet
at a spot about 8 feet to the south of the blood stain
(vide the record of the Court of First Instance of May 1).
But the deceased Japanese marine at that time was walking
in a northerly direction on Darroch Road on his way to
barracks (vide the record of the same Court of May 1 and
the verbal statements on the movements of the deceased
Japanese marine on that day made by D.S.I. Crowther).
The bullet entered the head of the deceased marine from
the back and emerged from the front. Moreover, there
was only one bullet wound (vide the report of examination
made by the Japanese military doctor Ogawa and his verbal
statements made in the Court of First Instance on May 6).
If this was actually the bullet which had caused the
death of the Japanese marine, then it should have dropped
in front of the marine instead of at a spot about 8 feet
behind him where it was subsequently found. Therefore,
irrespective of the fact as to whether or not it was
actually found at that place after the murder, there is
serious doubt as to the origin of the bullet. This point
deserves careful consideration before it can be definitely
alleged that this bullet was actually the one which had
killed the Japanese marine. It is to be noted that it
was only until after this point was raised in the Court
of First Instance by the appellant's lawyer that the
Municipal Advocate began to say that this bullet was
actually found at a spot in front of the deceased marine.
When the lawyers produced a plan to the Police showing
the various points, D.S.I. Crowther, at first, argued
that the bullet had entered the back part of the head
slantwise. If it is true that the bullet had entered

had entered by the back part of the head and emerged
from the front, replied in the affirmative. The
explanation "there is a hole at both the back part and
the front part of the head" can hardly be established.

height of the deceased was 5 feet, 8 inches. He was

警方在法庭上出示的证物，即一枚已发射的子弹和一个空弹壳，是由狄思威路（Dixwell Road）警察局的第61号日本巡警和第51号日本侦探分别在案发现场拾获的。初审法院认为这些证物确实是在案发现场发现的，且该子弹是导致日本海军陆战队员死亡的子弹，确实是从法庭上作为证物出示的手枪中射出的。然而，所有这些观点不仅缺乏确凿证明，而且引起了诸多疑点；它们还表明，这颗子弹实际上与日本海军陆战队员中山之死毫无关联，因为：
(a) 根据第61号日本巡警的陈述，他在血迹以南约8英尺处拾获了这枚已发射的子弹（参见5月1日的初审庭审记录）。但当时遇害的日本海军陆战队员正沿着达罗克路（Darroch Road）向北行走，前往兵营（参见同一法院5月1日的记录，以及副督察长克罗瑟（Crowther）关于遇害日本海军陆战队员当日行动轨迹的口头陈述）。子弹从遇害海军陆战队员的后脑射入，从前部穿出。此外，只有一个枪伤伤口（参见日本军医小川（Ogawa）的检查报告及其在5月6日初审法庭上的口头陈述）。如果这确实是导致日本海军陆战队员死亡的子弹，那么它应该掉落在该海军陆战队员的前方，而不是随后在其身后约8英尺处被发现的地方。因此，无论该子弹是否确实在谋杀发生后于该地被找到，其来源都存在严重疑点。在断言该子弹确实是杀死日本海军陆战队员的那一颗之前，这一点值得仔细考量。值得注意的是，直到上诉人的律师在初审法庭上提出这一点后，市公诉人才开始声称该子弹实际上是在遇害海军陆战队员前方的某处被发现的。当律师们向警方出示标明各点的平面图时，副督察长克罗瑟起初辩称子弹是斜着射入后脑的。如果子弹确实是斜向射入，那么子弹应该掉落在前侧方。军医小川的报告和死者头部的照片显示，子弹是以略微偏向一侧的角度射入的。因此，这位军医在初审法庭上被问及子弹是否由后脑射入并从前面穿出时，给予了肯定的回答。“后脑和前脑都有孔洞”这一解释很难成立。副督察长克罗瑟继续辩称：“死者身高5英尺8英寸。他是

4
January 3, 1937. Morning Translation.

suddenly shot and it is possible that he fell to the
ground after he had moved forward two steps". This
argument was adopted by the Court of First Instance.
Still dissatisfied, D.S.I. Crowther made a further
explanation, saying that the bullet might have been kicked
away because as many as one to two hundred persons had
visited the scene of the murder. (Vide the written record
of the Court of First Instance made on May 27.) The
Municipal Advocate, in his first argument in the Court
of First Instance, stated that in all some 300 to 400
persons had visited the scene of the murder. (Vide the
written record of the Court of First Instance made on
July 10.) The Court of First Instance adopted this
explanation as one of the foundations of its decision.
If actually so many persons had visited the scene of the
murder and conditions were in such a disorder, then it
is also possible that some person had planted the evidence
and placed the bullet and the empty cartridge shell there.
The Japanese policemen who claimed to have found the
bullet and the empty cartridge shell arrived at the scene
of the murder several minutes after 9 o'clock that evening,
but the bullet and the empty cartridge shell were not
found until about 10 o'clock. (Vide the statements made
by Japanese policeman No. 61 and Japanese detective No. 51
on May 1 in the Court of First Instance and the answers
of the Police to arguments.) This strengthens the
possibility that someone had planted the evidence by
placing the bullet and the empty cartridge shell there.
Furthermore, D.S.I. Crowther explained that it was only
a possibility that the bullet had been kicked away by
someone, but it was also possible that the bullet had
not been kicked away by someone and was in its original
position.
What the Police should prove is that the
bullet found was the one that killed Nakayama and that
it was kicked away in a southern direction by somebody
after the murder; otherwise, it cannot be admitted that
the bullet has any connection whatever with the death
of Nakayama. The appellants gave a detailed explanation
of this point in the Court of First Instance. Although
the Police maintained its former views, the Court of
First Instance dropped this point and explained "that
the spot where Nakayama was shot was only three large
paces from the place where he fell; that the bullet had
dropped at the place between the spot where he was shot
and the place where he fell; that after being shot, Nakayama
still continued to move forward three steps before he
collapsed". The pistol that shot Nakayama was discharged
5 centimetres behind the back part of his head (Vide below
Item A, Section 6) and the bullet penetrated the brain.
The report made by Japanese military doctor
Ogawa clearly states: "There was a bullet wound at the
back part of the head and a large quantity of blood
came out. There was a hole in the front part of
the head, and around the hole the skull was broken
and swollen, and some of the brain had fallen out.

突然遭到枪击，有可能在向前移动两步后倒在地上”。初审法院采纳了这一论点。副督察长克罗瑟仍不满意，进一步解释说，由于有多达一两百人到过谋杀现场，子弹可能被踢走。（参见5月27日的初审书面记录。）市公诉人在初审法庭的首次辩论中称，总共有约300至400人到过谋杀现场。（参见7月10日的初审书面记录。）初审法院将这一解释作为其裁决的基础之一。如果确实有如此多的人到过谋杀现场，且现场状况如此混乱，那么也有可能有人栽赃证据，将子弹和空弹壳放置在那里。声称发现子弹和空弹壳的日本警察是在当晚9点过后几分钟到达谋杀现场的，但直到大约10点左右才找到子弹和空弹壳。（参见5月1日第61号日本警察和第51号日本侦探在初审法庭上的陈述，以及警方对辩词的答复。）这增加了有人通过放置子弹和空弹壳来栽赃证据的可能性。此外，副督察长克罗瑟解释说，子弹被人踢走只是一种可能性，但也存在子弹未被人踢走且处于原始位置的可能性。
警方应当证明的是：所发现的子弹就是杀死中山的那一颗，并且是在谋杀发生后被某人向南方向踢走的；否则，不能承认该子弹与中山之死有任何关联。上诉人在初审法庭上对这一点进行了详细解释。尽管警方坚持其原有观点，但初审法院搁置了这一点，并解释说：“中山中枪地点距离他倒下的地方只有三大步；子弹掉落在中枪地点与倒下地点之间；中山中枪后仍继续向前走了三步才倒地。”射击中山的手枪是在其后脑后方5厘米处开火的（参见下文A项第6节），子弹穿透了大脑。
日本军医小川的报告明确指出：“后脑有一个枪伤伤口，流出大量血液。前脑有一个孔洞，孔洞周围的头骨破碎肿胀，部分脑组织流出。

pages.en:
5
January 6, 1937. Morning Translation

There was profuse bleeding due to a rupture of the arteries."
Again, "Death was due to injury to the brain and haemorrhage
of the brain." Can it be believed that a man, after having
been struck in the head by a bullet which had penetrated the
entire brain, fractured the skull, ruptured the arteries and
caused haemorrhage, could have walked forward 8 feet beyond
the spot where the fatal bullet had dropped? The spot where
Nakayama collapsed is 8 feet in front of the place where the
bullet was said to have dropped, (vide the statement of
Japanese Constable No.61 who claimed to have found the
bullet and the record of the session held on May 1 by the
Court of First Instance). A bullet after passing through
a human head does not drop immediately upon emerging but
continues in its trajectory. This is one of the established
theories of physics. Therefore it follows that there must
be some distance between the spot where the bullet dropped
and the spot where the bullet entered the skull and to this
distance should be added the distance (8 feet) which the
marine had moved before he collapsed. It is almost
incredible that the marine, after having been shot, could
have moved such a distance. If this incredible circumstance
is a fact, then the bullet could not have been the one which
had killed the marine. Nevertheless, the Court of First
Instance regarded it as a fact and used it as a basis for
finding the appellant guilty of murder and sentenced him to
death. Needless to say, such a judgment is improper.
The Court of First Instance further accepted
as fact a statement that the place where the marine was shot
was three paces from the place he collapsed, and that the
bullet fell at a spot between them. It should be remembered
that the bullet was found at a spot about 8 feet away from
the place where the marine collapsed, (vide the statement of
Japanese Constable No.61 who claimed to have found the
bullet). It is quite clear that, in addition to the
trajectory of the bullet, the distance should have been
more than three paces. Yet, the Court of First Instance
accepted as fact that the place where the bullet had dropped
was somewhere midway of these three paces. This is a
further misunderstanding of the facts on the part of the
Court of First Instance. This misunderstanding was due
to a plan based on the first reconstruction of the crime.
It should be borne in mind that in this plan it is clearly
stated: "The place where the marine dropped, as indicated
by the witness Hu Ziang Ho(胡祥和), is about three paces
apart from the place which Yih Hai Sung pointed as the spot
where the marine stood." The location of these two places
was not a result of the reconstruction, but was based on the
evidence of the witness and the appellant. The distance
between these two places did not tally with the statement
of the Japanese Constable who claimed to have found the
bullet. The Court of First Instance should regard this
as one of the points in appellant's statements which did
not tally with the facts.
(b) In the Court of First Instance, Japanese
Constable No.61, who claimed to have found the bullet, after
making his report on the finding of the bullet, added: "When
I found the bullet, I saw there was some reddish colour
resembling blood. There was also some oily substance and
pages.zh:
5
1937年1月6日。晨间译本

“因动脉破裂导致大量出血。”
此外，“死因为脑部损伤及脑出血。” 难道可以相信，一个人在头部被一颗贯穿整个大脑、击碎头骨、 ruptured 动脉并引起出血的子弹击中后，还能从致命子弹掉落的地方向前走出8英尺吗？中山（Nakayama）倒下的地点位于据称子弹掉落处前方8英尺处（参见声称发现子弹的日本巡捕第61号的陈述，以及初审法院于5月1日举行的庭审记录）。子弹在穿过人头后，并不会在射出后立即掉落，而是会继续沿其弹道飞行。这是物理学中既定的理论之一。因此，子弹掉落的地点与子弹进入头骨的地点之间必然存在一段距离，而这段距离还应加上该水兵在倒下前移动的距离（8英尺）。该水兵在中枪后竟能移动如此距离，这几乎令人难以置信。如果这一不可思议的情况属实，那么这颗子弹就不可能是杀死该水兵的子弹。尽管如此，初审法院仍将其视为事实，并以此作为判定上诉人犯有谋杀罪的依据，判处其死刑。毋庸赘言，这样的判决是不当的。
初审法院还接受了一项说法为事实，即水兵中枪的地点与其倒下的地点相距三步，而子弹掉落在两者之间的某处。应当记住，子弹是在距离水兵倒下地点约8英尺处被发现的（参见声称发现子弹的日本巡捕第61号的陈述）。很明显，除了考虑子弹的弹道外，这段距离应该超过三步。然而，初审法院却接受子弹掉落在这三步路程中间的某处为事实。这是初审法院对事实的进一步误解。这种误解是基于第一次犯罪现场重建所制定的计划造成的。应当牢记，在该计划中明确写道：“证人胡祥和（Hu Ziang Ho）所指出的水兵倒下地点，与伊海松（Yih Hai Sung）所指出的水兵站立地点，相距约三步。” 这两个地点的位置并非重建的结果，而是基于证人和上诉人的证词。这两点之间的距离与声称发现子弹的日本巡捕的陈述不符。初审法院本应将此视为上诉人陈述中与事实不符的点之一。
(b) 在初审法院中，声称发现子弹的日本巡捕第61号在报告发现子弹的情况后，补充道：“当我发现子弹时，我看到上面有一些类似血液的红色痕迹。还有一些油性物质和

sqme 'neir sticking to it." Yet, the report No. 101
Character Chien(木修、) of the Medico-Legal Laboratory states:
" No blood stains were found on the bullet nor were any human
cells found in a precipitate made of the fluid in which the
bullet had been soaked." The report also says: "If there
had been blood stains on the bullet and they had been cleaned
away with paper or cloth, some blood stains would generally
remain in the riflings and at the tip of the bullet." It is an
indisputable fact that no blood or human cells were found on
the bullet. The evidence of the Japanese Constable is there-
fore unreliable. The Court is requested to consider this
point and to study the other points mentioned above and to
decide whether or not the bullet had not been planted there.

一些‘内脏’粘在上面。” 然而，法医实验室的第101号木修（Character Chien）报告指出：“在子弹上未发现血迹，在浸泡子弹的液体沉淀物中也未发现人体细胞。” 报告还指出：“如果子弹上有血迹，并且是用纸或布擦拭掉的，通常在膛线和子弹尖端会残留一些血迹。” 子弹上未发现血液或人体细胞，这是一个无可争议的事实。因此，该日本巡捕的证词是不可靠的。恳请法庭考虑这一点，并研究上述其他各点，以判定子弹是否并非被放置在那里。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of D.S. 325 B. Craig
native of taken by me
at D. Rd. Station on the 11-11-38 and interpreted by
Verbal statement of witness Woo Ziang Woo made in the
presence of J.D.S. 51 Hasuo, J.D.C. 83 Osano, C.D.C. 119 and
Clerk Chi Yoong Shou.
I left home at about 8.45 p.m. 9-11-38 and proceeded to
a Japanese shoe-maker's shop at No. 90 Darroch Road owned by
Mr. Takaoka, to collect some money.
At about 9 p.m. as I neared my destination I heard a
loud report like a pistol shot so I immediately looked in the
direction of the sound and saw two Japanese soldiers both
wearing black clothing, one of the Japanese soldiers was running
East into Fong Loh Li and the other one was lying on the roadway.
I then hurriedly entered No. 90 Darroch Road and informed
Mr. Takaoka of the incident.
Mr. Takaoka and I then went to the scene and later he
instructed me to go to the Police Station and report that I had
witnessed the affair.
I then accompanied two Chinese policemen to Dixwell Road
Station.
S. Craig.
D. S. 325

以下为 D.S. 325 B. Craig 的陈述，
籍贯 [原文缺失]，由本人于1938年11月11日在 D. Rd. 警局录取，并由
在 J.D.S. 51 Hasuo、J.D.C. 83 Osano、C.D.C. 119 及

我于1938年11月9日晚上约8点45分离开家，前往达罗克路（Darroch Road）90号由高冈先生（Mr. Takaoka）拥有的日本鞋匠店收取一些款项。
晚上约9点，当我接近目的地时，听到一声像手枪射击般的巨响，于是我立即朝声音方向看去，看到两名身穿黑衣的日本士兵，其中一名日本士兵向东跑进丰乐里（Fong Loh Li），另一名则躺在马路上。
随后我急忙进入达罗克路90号，将此事告知高冈先生。
高冈先生和我随即前往现场，之后他指示我去警察局报告，称我目击了此事。
随后我陪同两名中国警察前往狄思威路（Dixwell Road）警局。
S. Craig.

先生，
谨此报告，1935年11月9日晚，我与 C.D.C.119、J.D.C. Osano 及 D.S. Craig 一起，在书记员 Chi Yoong Shou 的协助下，在本局刑侦科办公室讯问了一名证人 Woo Ziang Woo。
该证人称，1935年11月9日晚上约8点45分，他前往达罗克路90号的一家日本鞋匠店收款。当晚约9点，当他接近该店时，听到一声像手枪射击般的巨响，朝声音方向看去，看到一名日本水兵倒在马路上，另一名水兵跑进丰乐里（Fong Loh Lee）。
因此，我对该证人进行了盘问，问他如何能说逃跑的人是日本水兵，以及在黑暗中从那么远的地方是否能看清那人。随后他改变了说法，称他看到那人穿着黑衣服，但不能确定他是日本人还是中国人。
接着他继续陈述，称他急忙进入鞋匠店，将此事告知高冈先生。高冈先生和他随后前往现场，之后他作为证人陪同两名中国警察前往狄思威路警局。
先生，
您顺从的仆人
J.D.S.51

The witness stated that at about 8.45 p.m.9-11-35 he proceeded to a Japanese shoe-maker's shop at 90 Darroch Road to collect money. When he came near the above shop at about 9 p.m.same date, he heard a loud sound like a pistol shot and, on looking in the direction, saw a Japanese sailor fall on the roadway and another Japanese sailor run into Fong Loh Lee. He hurriedly entered the shoe-maker's shop and informed the shop master, Mr.Takaoka, of the incident. He then in company with Mr.Takaoka went to the scene, and subsequently he accompanied two Chinese policemen to Dixwell Road Station as a witness.

日期：1935年11月13日
主题：关于证人 Woo Ziang Woo 的陈述，F.I.R.176/35 号案件
由 J.D.C. Deano 制作 转呈...
先生，
谨此报告，1935年11月9日晚，我与 C.J. Coll9、J.D.S. Hasuo 及 D.S. Craig 一起，在书记员 Chi Yoong Shou 的协助下，在本局讯问了一名证人 Woo Ziang Woo。
该证人称，1935年11月9日晚上约8点45分，他前往达罗克路90号的一家日本鞋匠店收款。同日晚上约9点，当他接近上述店铺时，听到一声像手枪射击般的巨响，朝声音方向看去，看到一名日本水兵倒在马路上，另一名日本水兵跑进丰乐里（Fong Loh Lee）。他急忙进入鞋匠店，将此事告知店主高冈先生。随后他与高冈先生一同前往现场，之后作为证人陪同两名中国警察前往狄思威路警局。
我与 J.D.S. Hasue 及 D.S. Craig 一起，仔细盘问该证人如何能说跑进丰乐里（Fong Loh Lee）的人是日本水兵，以及在夜间从那么远的地方是否能看清他。该证人改变了说法，称他只能看到那人穿着黑衣服，无法分辨是日本人还是中国人。
先生，
您顺从的仆人，
J.D.C.85

C.D.C. 119 Mo Zeh Nying, attached to Dixwell Road Police
Station, reports,

At 6 p.m. on the 9-11-35, I came to the station on night
duty. At about 6.10 p.m., C.P.C. 2664 reported by telephone
that a Japanese soldier had been murdered on Darroch Road. After
receipt of the telephone message, D.S.I. Crowther, D.S. 325
Craig and I proceeded to Darroch Road to make enquiries. On
arrival we found that the Japanese sailor had been removed away.
D.S. Craig then told me that a witness had been brought to the
station by a C.P.C. and instructed me to come back to the
station to bring the witness to the detective office for
enquiries. Whilst in the detective office I heard that the
witness give the following statement.

"My name is Woo Siang Woo, 36 years of age, native of
Zangchow, married shoe-maker, residing 62 East Paoching
Road. At about 8.45 p.m. today (9-11-35), I left home and
proceeded to a Japanese shoe-maker's shop, named "Takaoka",
Darroch Road, to collect money. At about 9 p.m., when I
was near the shop door, I heard the report of a shot being
fired. I immediately looked forward and saw two Japanese
soldiers, both wearing black short clothing, one was running
away into the Fong Leh Li and the other was lying on the
roadway. I immediately entered the Japanese shoe-maker's
shop and informed the master of the incident. The master and
I then went to the scene and later he instructed me to come
to the Police Station to be a witness. I then accompanied a
Chinese policeman to the Police station."

Signed, Mo Zeh Nying, C.D.C. 119.

隶属狄思威路警局的 C.D.C. 119 Mo Zeh Nying 报告如下，

1935年11月9日下午6点，我来警局值夜班。下午约6点10分，C.P.C. 2664 通过电话报告称，达罗克路上有一名日本士兵被谋杀。接到电话留言后，D.S.I. Crowther、D.S. 325 Craig 和我前往达罗克路进行调查。到达后，我们发现那名日本水兵已被移走。D.S. Craig 随后告诉我，一名证人已被一名 C.P.C. 带到警局，并指示我返回警局，将该证人带到侦探办公室进行问询。在侦探办公室期间，我听到该证人作了如下陈述。

“我叫 Woo Siang Woo，36岁，常州人，已婚，职业鞋匠，住宝庆路东段62号。今天（1935年11月9日）晚上约8点45分，我离开家，前往达罗克路一家名为‘高冈’的日本鞋匠店收款。晚上约9点，当我靠近店门口时，听到一声枪响。我立即向前看，看到两名日本士兵，都穿着黑色短衣，一人跑进丰乐里（Fong Leh Li），另一人躺在马路上。我立即进入这家日本鞋匠店，将此事告知店主。店主和我随后前往现场，之后他指示我来警察局作证。随后我陪同一名中国警察前往警察局。”

签名，Mo Zeh Nying, C.D.C. 119.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No............
Dixwell Road Station,
REPORT
Date.. November 10, 19 35.

Subject Re a telephone and a brief questioning.

Made by... Clark Chi Young Shou Forwarded by...

Sir,
I beg to report that at 9.05 p.m. 9/11/35 I received a
telephone message from C.P.C. 2864 through the No.1 Box (Kiangwen
Road) stating that a Chinese had been hurt by a Japanese soldier
on Kiangwen Road near the Japanese Naval Landing Party.
At 9.20 p.m. I saw C.P.Cs. 2864 and 2891 bringing into
the Charge Room a male Chinese who was said to be the witness of
the shooting, and according to the speech given by these C.P.Cs.
I began to understand that those two involved in this matter
were all Japanese.
Afterwards, this witness told me that at about 9 o' clock
in the afternoon of November 9, 1935, he went from East Pao Shing
Road where he was now living, to Darroch Road near Fong Loh Lee
to get some money back from a Japanese. As soon as he reached
the above mentioned place and before he had entered the Japanese
house, he suddenly heard a bang which he took to be the burst
of a ricsha tyre. Turning back his head he perceived a Japanese
soldier lying on the ground and another one wearing black garment
similar to that of the first one and creeping into Fong Loh Lee.
Being frightened, he hurried into that Japanese house and called
him out to the scene.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Sgd: Chi Young Shou.

先生，
谨此报告，1935年11月9日晚上9点05分，我通过1号信箱（江湾路）收到来自 C.P.C. 2864 的电话留言，称在江湾路日本海军陆战队附近，一名中国人被一名日本士兵打伤。
晚上9点20分，我看到 C.P.C. 2864 和 2891 将一名中国男子带入拘留室，据说他是枪击案的证人，根据这两名 C.P.C. 的说法，我开始了解到卷入此事的两人都是日本人。
随后，这名证人告诉我，1935年11月9日下午约9点，他从目前居住的宝兴东路前往丰乐里附近的达罗克路，向一名日本人讨回一些钱款。当他一到达上述地点，尚未进入那户日本人家时，突然听到一声巨响，他以为是人力车轮胎爆裂。他回过头，看到一名日本士兵躺在地上，另一名穿着与第一人相似的黑色服装的人正爬进丰乐里。由于受到惊吓，他急忙冲进那户日本人家，并将那人叫到现场。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
签名：Chi Young Shou.

1935年11月9日晚9时30分，华捕第2064号及第2081号从靠近丰乐里（Fong Loh Li）的巴罗克路（Barrock Road）将一名证人带至巡捕房。该证人名叫吴祥福（Woo Ziang Voo，音译），30岁，常州人，职业为男鞋匠，住复兴东路68号。据报称，当晚9时05分，他正沿巴罗克路前行，打算向一位居住在丰乐里附近的日本人收取款项。在进入该日本人的住所之前，证人突然听到一声爆炸响，他立即转身，看见一名日本士兵躺在地上，同时他还看见另一名衣着与该日本士兵相似的人跑进丰乐里。随后，证人向那位他欲向其收款的日本人报告了此事。该日本人与证人随即前往现场，发现警方已经到达。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of. Woo Ziang Woo
native of. Zangchow taken by me Clerk Li Yang Kao
at. 11.40 p.m. on the 9-11-35 and interpreted by.

My name is Woo Ziang Woo, 26 years of age, native of
Zangchow, M/shoe-maker, residing at No. 62 East Paoshing Road.
At about 8.45 p.m. on the 9-11-35, I left my home (East
Paoshing Road) and proceeded to a Japanese shoe-maker's shop,
named "Takaoka", on Darroch Road to get my pay. At about
9 p.m. on the 9th of November, 1935, I had nearly reached
the door of the Japanese shoe-maker's shop, when I heard the
report of a shot being fired. I immediately turned my head
and looked Northwards and saw a male wearing black clothing
running East into Fong Loh Li, off Darroch Road. Simultaneous-
ly I saw a man ,also wearing black clothing, lying on the
roadway. I immediately went into the shoe-maker's shop and
informed the master, a Japanese, of the incident. We both
proceeded to where the man was lying and saw that he was
a Japanese marine. The master of the shoe-maker's shop then
instructed me to come to the station where I made the report.
The clothing worn by the man who ran away was similar
in colour as that worn by the man lying on the roadway. It
was long trousers and short jacket and not a long gown.
This is my true statement.
Signed, Woo Ziang Woo.
Taken in the presence of D.S.I. H.L. Crowther, J.D.S. Si
Hsue, J.D.S. 34 Kobayashi and Clerk Ling Wei Ju (Hanghow).

以下为证人吴祥伍（Woo Ziang Woo，音译）之陈述，由其同乡常州人、男鞋匠、住宝兴东路62号提供。本陈述由文书李仰高（Li Yang Kao，音译）于1935年11月9日晚11时40分记录，并由……翻译。

本人名叫吴祥伍（Woo Ziang Woo，音译），26岁，常州人，职业为男鞋匠，住宝兴东路62号。1935年11月9日晚8时45分左右，我离开家（宝兴东路），前往达罗克路（Darroch Road）一家名为“高冈”（Takaoka）的日本鞋匠店领取工资。1935年11月9日晚9时许，当我快要走到那家日本鞋匠店门口时，听到一声枪响。我立即转头向北望去，看见一名身穿黑衣的男子从达罗克路向东跑进丰乐里（Fong Loh Li）。与此同时，我看见另一名同样身穿黑衣的男子躺在马路上。我立即进入鞋匠店，将此事告知店主（一名日本人）。我们两人随即前往那人躺卧之处，发现他是一名日本海军陆战队员。鞋匠店店主随后指示我前来巡捕房报案。逃跑男子所穿衣物的颜色与躺在马路上的男子所穿衣物颜色相似。均为长裤配短上衣，而非长袍。
以上为本人真实陈述。
签署人：吴祥伍（Woo Ziang Woo）。

Woo Ziang Woo (胡祥和), age 26, married,

xx D.S.I. Yung Ts King in the

Tsuang Zung Pau
translated

Zangchow
H.Q.C.B.          10-11-35

I am a shoe-maker by profession and only do business with
the Japanese.

At about 8.45 p.m. on the 9-11-35 I left my home and
proceeded to the Takaoka Shoe-maker, 90 Darroch Road, for the
purpose of collecting a sum of money from the owner of the shop
As I was going to open the door of the house, the sound of a
gun-shot was heard and I saw a person collapse at a place about
20 yards to the west of 90 Darroch Road. At the same time I
saw another person, dressed in a black short jacket (I cannot
remember whether he wore a hat or not), run away from the
scene and proceed to the north, where he entered the Foeng Leh
Li alleyway. The height of this man was about 5 ft. and he was
probably dressed in Japanese military uniform. The above inci-
dent occurred at about 9.05 p.m. I then entered the shop and
reported the matter to the Japanese proprietor. We went to
the place where the person lay, and I found that his dress was
similar to the one who escaped. The Japanese owner of the shop
told me that the wounded man was a Japanese marine. Two
Settlement Chinese Policemen arrived soon afterwards. I remained
at the entrance of the house (No. 90) for about 5 minutes, when
the Japanese shop-owner told me to go with the Policemen to the
Police Station and make a statement.

Signed by Woo Ziang Woo

常州
总部刑事侦缉处          1935年11月10日

本人职业为鞋匠，仅与日本人做生意。

1935年11月9日晚8时45分左右，我离开家，
前往达罗克路90号的高冈鞋匠店，目的是向店主
收取一笔款项。正当我要打开房门时，听到一声
枪响，我看见一个人在达罗克路90号以西约20码
处倒地。与此同时，我看见另一个人，身穿黑色
短上衣（我不记得他是否戴帽），从现场逃离并
向北跑去，进入了丰乐里（Foeng Leh Li）弄堂。此人身高
约5英尺，可能身穿日本军服。上述事件发生在
晚9时05分左右。随后我进入店内，向日本店主
报告了此事。我们前往那人躺卧的地方，我发现他的衣着
与逃跑者相似。日本店主告诉我，伤者是一名
日本海军陆战队员。不久后，两名
租界华捕到达。我在该房屋（90号）门口停留了
约5分钟，此时日本店主让我随警察去
巡捕房做陈述。

吴祥和 签署

The following is the statement of
J.P.S. 61 T. Yasukawa, Dixwell Road
Station, taken by D.S.I. Crowther,
on the 20/11/35.

At about 9.07 p.m. on the 9/11/35, I was in the Japanese
Office of Dixwell Road Police Station when I was informed by
telephone by Sergt. 198 Stocks on Charge Room duty that he had
received a telephone message from a C.P.C. stating that there
was some trouble between Japanese sailors and Chinese on the
Darroch Road. I immediately proceeded to the Charge Room and
obtained a bicycle and left the station for Darroch Road, proceed-
ing along Dixwell Road, North Szechuen Road to Kiangwan Road.

Before I reached the corner of Darroch Road and North
Szechuen Road I saw Sergt. 230 Wilkinson riding a bicycle, who
was making a complete turn in the form of a circle on his bicycle
at the corner of North Szechuen Road and Darroch Road. He then
saw me and pointed with his hand down Darroch Road, and at the
same time shouted "Over there" several times. Sergt. Wilkinson
then proceeded South into Darroch Road - this all occurred within
a few seconds.

I arrived at the corner of Darroch Road and North
Szechuen Road, but I could not see Sergt. Wilkinson, however, in
the distance, I saw a crowd of persons gathered on the West side
of Darroch Road. I immediately cycled forward and I saw a Japanese
sailor lying on his back with his head in a pool of blood being
attended by two or three Japanese sailors.

About 12 feet South of where the sailor lay I saw 14 or
15 persons. In the meantime J.P.C. 173 came from the direction of
the crowd, who told me that he had found a Japanese witness, and
who had told him, that the sailor had been shot. I told J.P.C. 1
to stay at the scene. By this time J.P.C. 86 had arrived on the
pages.zh:
以下为日籍巡捕第61号 T. Yasukawa（安川，音译），
隶属狄思威路巡捕房，
由副督察 Crowther 于1935年11月20日
记录的陈述。

1935年11月9日晚9时07分左右，我正在狄思威路
巡捕房的日籍警官办公室，当时值班室警长
Stocks（第198号）通过电话通知我，他收到一名
华捕的电话留言，称达罗克路上日本水兵与中国人
之间发生了一些纠纷。我立即前往值班室，
取了一辆自行车，离开巡捕房前往达罗克路，
沿狄思威路、四川北路行至江湾路。

在我到达达罗克路与四川北路拐角之前，
我看见警长 Wilkinson（第230号）骑着自行车，
他正在四川北路与达罗克路的拐角处骑车绕圈。
他随后看见了我，用手指着达罗克路方向，
同时大喊了几声“在那边”。随后 Wilkinson 警长
向南进入达罗克路——这一切都发生在
几秒钟之内。

我到达达罗克路与四川北路的拐角处，但未见
Wilkinson 警长，然而，在远处，我看见一群人聚集在
达罗克路西侧。我立即骑车向前，看见一名
日本水兵仰面躺着，头部浸在一滩血泊中，
有两三名日本水兵正在照料他。

在该水兵躺卧处以南约12英尺处，我看见14或
15个人。在此期间，日籍巡捕第173号从人群
方向走来，他告诉我他发现了一名日本证人，
该证人告诉他，水兵是被枪击的。我让日籍巡捕第1
号留在现场。此时，日籍巡捕第86号已到达

pages.en:
-2-

scene, who I told to go and get J.D.S. 51 Hasuo. I then mounted
my bicycle and went to the J.N.L. Party Headquarters where I
made a report of what I had seen. Following which I telephoned
from Box No.1, situated at Kiangwan and North Szechuan Roads
corner, to Sergt. Stocks on Charge Room duty at Dixwell Road
Police Station, informing him that a Japanese sailor had been
injured on Darroch Road.

On returning to the scene, at North Szechuan Road and
Darroch Road corner, I met Japanese sailors conveying the
injured sailor on a stretcher towards the J.N.L. Party Headquar-
ters.

At the same time I met J.D.S. 51 Hasuo, who was seated in
a ricksha, and I told him what had occurred. I then rode to the
scene followed by J.D.S. 51 Hasuo, I then told J.P.C. 173 to
take the Japanese witness (named Takeuchi) to the Station.

I then proceeded to Inspt. Hirai's address, No. 634 Dixwell
Road, and informed him. I then returned to the station and inform-
ed the Japanese Consular Police by telephone.

Immediately I had informed them I was met by Capt. Kennedy,
D.O."C" in the Charge Room, who instructed me to inform
Mr. Uyehara A.C.P. (Japanese), so I proceeded to his address
No. 888 Dixwell Road and carried out his instructions.

After this I returned to the scene of crime and commenced
a search with others, I later found one round of spent ammunition
about 8 feet South of the pool of blood.

Q. When you arrived on the scene, did you see Sergt. Wilkinson
A. Yes.

现场，我让他去叫日籍特别巡捕第51号 Hasuo（波苏，音译）。随后我骑上
自行车前往日本海军陆战队党部 headquarters，
就我所见情况进行了报告。之后，我从位于江湾路与
四川北路拐角的1号电话亭打电话给狄思威路
巡捕房值班室的 Stocks 警长，通知他有一名日本水兵
在达罗克路受伤。

返回四川北路与达罗克路拐角的现场时，我遇见
几名日本水兵正用担架将受伤的水兵抬往
日本海军陆战队党部 headquarters。

与此同时，我遇见坐在人力车上的日籍特别巡捕
第51号 Hasuo，我向他讲述了发生的情况。随后我骑车前往
现场，日籍特别巡捕第51号 Hasuo 紧随其后，我随后让
日籍巡捕第173号将日本证人（名为 Takeuchi，竹内，音译）带往巡捕房。

随后我前往平井（Hirai）督察的住所，地址为狄思威路634号，
并向其报告。之后我返回巡捕房，并通过电话
通知了日本领事馆警察。

我刚通知完他们，便在值班室遇到了“C”区
主管警官 Kennedy 上尉，他指示我通知
日本籍助理巡官 Uyehara（上原，音译），于是我前往
其住所狄思威路888号，执行了他的指示。

此后，我返回犯罪现场，与他人开始
搜查，后来我在血泊以南约8英尺处发现了一枚
已发射的子弹壳。

问：当你到达现场时，你看见 Wilkinson 警长了吗？
答：看见了。

pages.en:
-3-

Q. Where was he ?
A. Standing near the injured sailor.
Q. Did he go with you to the J.N.I. Party Headquarters to make a report ?
A. No.
Q. Did he give you any instructions ?
A. Yes, he told me to go and report the occurrence to the J.N.L. Party.
Q. Did you see any Chinese Constables on the scene ?
A. At the time I saw J.P.C. 173, I also saw one tall C.P.C.
Q. Do you know his number ?
A. No.
Q. Can you say who were in the crowd?
A. They were all civilians.
Q. Were they Japanese or Chinese ?
A. I cannot say, but I think most of them were Japanese.
Q. Did you see Sergt. Wilkinson when you returned from the J.N.L. Party and having informed Dixwell Road Police Station by telephone ?
A. No.
Q. Do you know where he had gone ?
A. No.
Q. When you first arrived on the scene did you see any Japanese civilians standing by the injured sailor, other than the 1 or 2 Japanese sailors ?
A. No.
Q. When you reported to the J.N.L. Party, to whom did you make the report ?

问：他在哪里？
答：站在受伤水兵附近。
问：他是否随你一起去日本海军陆战队党部 headquarters 做报告？
答：没有。
问：他是否给你任何指示？
答：是的，他让我去向日本海军陆战队报告此事。
问：你在现场看见任何华捕了吗？
答：当我看见日籍巡捕第173号时，我也看见了一名高大的华捕。
问：你知道他的编号吗？
答：不知道。
问：你能说出人群中有哪些人吗？
答：都是平民。
问：他们是日本人还是中国人？
答：我说不上来，但我认为大多数是日本人。
问：当你从日本海军陆战队党部回来并通过电话通知狄思威路巡捕房后，你看见 Wilkinson 警长了吗？
答：没有。
问：你知道他去了哪里吗？
答：不知道。
问：当你初次到达现场时，除了那一两名日本水兵外，你看见有任何日本平民站在受伤水兵旁边吗？
答：没有。
问：当你向日本海军陆战队党部报告时，你是向谁做的报告？

pages.en:
A. The person who I informed was wearing a Petty Officer's
uniform.
Q. When you informed this Petty Officer did he appear to be
aware of the incident ?
A. Yes, as I was told by a sailor that they were aware of the
occurrence, further I saw some Japanese sailors armed with
rifles and fixed bayonets, wearing steel helmets, leaving
by the main entrance and proceeding towards Barrock Road.
Q. When you first saw the sailor lying on the road, did you
see a bundle of any kind ?
A. I cannot remember.

Y. Yamakawa
pages.zh:
答：我通知的那个人身穿海军士官制服。
问：当你通知这名士官时，他似乎知晓此事吗？
答：是的，因为一名水兵告诉我他们已知晓
此事，此外，我还看见一些日本水兵手持
装有刺刀的步枪，头戴钢盔，从正门离开并
朝巴罗克路（Barrock Road）方向走去。
问：当你初次看见水兵躺在路上时，你看见
有任何包裹之类的东西吗？
答：我不记得了。

Y. Yamakawa（山川，音译）

pages.en:
Statement of J.P.C. 173 T. Sawano, attached to Dixwell Road
Station, taken by D.S.I. McPhee on 20-11-35 and interpreted
by Mr. T. Kawashima.

My name is T. Sawano, employed by the S.M.C. as
Japanese Police Constable No. 173, attached to Dixwell Road
Police Station.

At about 6.45 p.m. 9-11-35, I reported for 2nd day
duty, i.e. 7 p.m. to 11 p.m., and was instructed to walk 3
Beat which covers Darroch Road, Fong Loh Li, Darroch Terrace,
Keeble Gardens, Tse An Fong alleyway and North Szechuen Road.

At about 9 p.m. 9-11-35, I left the corner of Darroch
and North Szechuen Roads and proceeded West on Darroch Road.

When I arrived at the corner of Darroch Road and East
Wang Pang Road, leading to Chinese Territory, I met three male
Chinese of the labour class. One of the three Chinese was
carrying a parcel and he informed me in Chinese that there was
some trouble with a Japanese soldier. I asked where and he
pointed North on Darroch Road and said, "a little way ahead",
this was about 9.07 p.m. 9-11-35.

Immediately this information was imparted to me, I
proceeded North on Darroch Road, without asking the Chinese
any further questions.

When I arrived at Darroch Road near the Fong Loh Li,
I observed two C.P.Cs., Numbers unknown, 2 or 3 Japanese sailors
7 or 8 male Japanese civilians and 7 or 8 male Chinese civilians
standing around a Japanese sailor who was lying on the West side
of Darroch Road.

The sailor was lying on his back at a slight angle
to the West kerb, his head towards North.

As it was dark where the sailor was lying, I borrowed
pages.zh:
日籍巡捕第173号 T. Sawano（泽野，音译）之陈述，
隶属狄思威路巡捕房，由副督察 McPhee 于1935年11月20日记录，
并由 T. Kawashima（川岛，音译）先生翻译。

本人名叫 T. Sawano，受雇于工部局，任
日籍巡捕第173号，隶属狄思威路
巡捕房。

1935年11月9日晚6时45分左右，我报到准备
第二个班次执勤，即晚7时至11时，并受命巡逻
第3段辖区，涵盖达罗克路、丰乐里、达罗克台、
基布尔花园（Keeble Gardens）、治安坊弄堂及四川北路。

1935年11月9日晚9时许，我离开达罗克路
与四川北路的拐角，沿达罗克路向西行进。

当我到达通往华界的达罗克路与东旺浜路
拐角时，遇见了三名劳工阶层的中国男子。其中一名
中国男子携带一个包裹，他用中文告诉我，有一名
日本士兵出了事。我问在哪里，他指向达罗克路
北方，说“就在前面一点”，当时约为1935年11月9日
晚9时07分。

刚一得知此消息，我便
沿达罗克路向北行进，未再向那些
中国人询问更多问题。

当我到达靠近丰乐里的达罗克路时，
我看见两名华捕（编号不详）、两三名日本水兵、
七八名日本男性平民以及七八名中国男性平民
围站在一名躺在达罗克路西侧的
日本水兵周围。

该水兵仰面躺着，身体与西侧路缘石
成轻微角度，头部朝北。

由于水兵躺卧处光线昏暗，我借用了

pages.en:
-2-

T. Sawano

an electric torch from one of the C.P.Cs. and shone the light of
the torch on the sailor's face, when I observed that his head
was lying in a pool of blood, his eyes closed, and foaming from
the mouth.

The sailor had a small wound on the top of the head and a
white substance was protruding from same.

A blue cloth bundle was lying on the road near the sailor's
right foot, and when I questioned the persons present as to whom
the cloth bundle belonged, one of the Japanese pedestrians
stated that it was the property of a sailor, but did not say
which sailor.

An unknown Japanese amongst the crowd was then heard by me
to say, that the sailor appeared to be suffering from a bullet
wound, whereupon I ordered the crowd to stand back from the
injured sailor.

When I asked if the Maxwell Road Police Station and Naval
Landing Party had been informed one of the C.P.Cs. stated that
he had informed the station by telephone, and an unknown Japanese
in the crowd stated that the Naval Landing Party had also been
informed, but he did not say by whom.

At this point I looked at my wrist watch and the time was
9.10 p.m.

I then instructed the two C.P.Cs. to question the Chinese
who were present if anyone had witnessed how the sailor received
his injuries, whilst I questioned the Japanese present with the
same object, but no witnesses were located.

Whilst I was questioning the Japanese present, a Foreign
pages.zh:
-2-

T. Sawano

从一名华捕（C.P.C.）处取来一支手电筒，将光照在那名水手的脸上，此时我观察到他的头躺在血泊中，双眼紧闭，口吐白沫。

该水手头顶有一处小伤口，并有白色物质从中 protruding（原文如此，意为突出/流出）。

在水手右脚附近的路面上躺着一个蓝色布包，当我询问在场人员该布包归谁所有时，一名日本行人称其属于一名水手，但未说明是哪名水手。

随后，我听到人群中一名身份不明的日本人说，该水手似乎遭受了枪伤，于是我命令人群远离受伤的水手。

当我询问是否已通知麦克斯韦路（Maxwell Road）巡捕房及海军陆战队登陆部队时，一名华捕称他已通过电话通知了巡捕房，而人群中一名身份不明的日本人称海军陆战队登陆部队也已获知，但他未说明是由谁通知的。

此时我看了一下手表，时间是晚上 9:10。

随后，我指示两名华捕询问在场的中国人，看是否有人目击该水手是如何受伤的，同时我也以同样的目的询问在场的日本人，但未找到任何证人。

就在我询问在场的日本人时，一名外籍

pages.en:
-3-

T. Sawano.

Sergeant and J.P.S. 61, arrived at the scene on bicycles, and
after looking at the injured sailor, they immediately left the
scene in a Northerly direction.
    About 9.15 p.m. 9/11/35, 4 armed Japanese Marines led by
an N.C.O. arrived at the scene from the Japanese Naval Landing
Party, and after looking at the injured Sailor they left running
North on Darroch Road, and a few minutes after they left another
party of Japanese Marines consisting of 5 or 6 carrying a
stretcher, and led by an Officer arrived at the scene.
    The Officer spoke to me saying that the Police would be
informed, and then gave instructions to the 5 or 6 Marines to
lift the injured Sailor on to the stretcher which they did, and
immediately left together with the Officer in the direction of
the Naval Landing Party.
    The 2/3 Japanese sailors who were present at the scene when
I arrived, left together with the party who removed the injured
sailor.
    The Foreign Sergeant returned to the scene before the injured
sailor was removed, and left about 1 minute later, and again
returned to the scene after the injured sailor had been removed.
    After the injured sailor had been removed I instructed one
C.P.C. to make enquiries at an exchange shop situated on the
West side of Darroch Road, near the entrance to Darroch Terrace,
with a view to locating witnesses.
    I then instructed the other C.P.C. present, to make enquiries
amongst a crowd of Chinese who had by this time assembled on the
East side of Darroch Road near the Fong Leh Li, with the same
pages.zh:
-3-

T. Sawano.

巡长（Sergeant）和日本警员（J.P.S.）61号骑自行车抵达现场，在查看了受伤的水手后，他们立即向北方向离开现场。
    约在 1935 年 11 月 9 日晚上 9:15，由一名士官率领的 4 名武装日本海军陆战队员从日本海军陆战队登陆部队抵达现场，在查看了受伤的水手后，他们沿达罗克路（Darroch Road）向北奔跑离开；在他们离开几分钟后，另一支由一名军官率领、由 5 或 6 人组成并携带担架的日本海军陆战队分队抵达现场。
    该军官对我说，警方将会得到通知，随后指示那 5 或 6 名陆战队员将受伤的水手抬上担架，他们照办了，并随即与军官一同朝海军陆战队登陆部队的方向离开。
    在我抵达时就在现场的 2 至 3 名日本水手，随同移走受伤水手的那支队伍一同离开。
    那名外籍巡长在受伤水手被移走前返回了现场，并在大约 1 分钟后离开，之后在受伤水手被移走后再次返回现场。
    在受伤水手被移走后，我指示一名华捕前往达罗克路西侧、靠近达罗克里（Darroch Terrace）入口处的一家兑换店进行查询，以期寻找证人。
    随后，我指示在场的另一名华捕，在丰乐里（Fong Leh Li）附近达罗克路东侧聚集的一群中国人中进行查询，目的相同。

-4-

T. Sawano.

object in view.

I then questioned the Japanese who were present, whereupon
a male Japanese residing at No. 90 Darroch Road approached me
from amongst the crowd and told me that a male Chinese who was
known to him had witnessed the incident.

By this time J.P.S. 61 had returned to the scene, whereupon
I imparted this information to him.

The male Japanese then returned to his home at 90 Darroch
Road, and brought a male Chinese dressed in blue jacket and
pants to the scene, stating that he was the witness. I then
instructed the two C.P.Cs. to take the male Chinese witness to
the Station which they did, whilst I accompanied the Japanese
informant to the Station, whom I later ascertained to be one
named Mr. Takaoka.

On arriving at the Station J.P.S. Nakamura and I took a
statement from Mr. Takaoka.

At 10.30 p.m. 9/11/35 I returned to the scene, where I
remained until 1.40 a.m. 10/11/35, when I returned to the
Station, and reported off duty at 2 a.m. 10/11/35.

J.P.C. 173 T. Sawano.
pages.zh:
-4-

T. Sawano.

以期寻找证人。

随后我询问了在场的日本人，此时一名居住在达罗克路 90 号的日本男子从人群中走近我，告诉我一名他认识的中国男子目击了这一事件。

此时，日本警员（J.P.S.）61号已返回现场，我便将此信息告知了他。

随后，该名日本男子返回达罗克路 90 号的家中，带了一名身穿蓝色夹克和裤子的中国男子来到现场，称其为证人。我随即指示两名华捕将该中国男证人带往巡捕房，他们照办了；同时我陪同那名日本报案人前往巡捕房，后经查明其名为高冈先生（Mr. Takaoka）。

抵达巡捕房后，日本警员（J.P.S.）中村（Nakamura）和我记录了高冈先生的供词。

1935 年 11 月 9 日晚上 10:30，我返回现场，并一直停留至 1935 年 11 月 10 日凌晨 1:40，随后返回巡捕房，并于 1935 年 11 月 10 日凌晨 2:00 报告下班。

日本警员（J.P.C.）173号 T. Sawano。

pages.en:
Report of J.P.S. Nakamura of Dixwell Road Station.

Upon being informed that a Sailor of the
Landing Party had been shot at about 9.10 p.m.
by an unknown person in front of the office of
the Darroch Road Street Union, I immediately
proceeded to the scene. The bullet had entered
the forehead and penetrated through the back of
the head.

According to a statement made by a Chinese
eye-witness, persons wearing similar dress had
fired at each other, but this was not verified.
The victim was removed to the Landing Party Barracks,
and the Chinese witness was detained. A bullet was
found in the vicinity of the scene and was taken
by the Landing Party. The seriousness of the
injury and the name of the victim are unknown.
pages.zh:
迪克斯韦尔路（Dixwell Road）巡捕房日本警员（J.P.S.）中村（Nakamura）的报告。

获悉一名登陆部队水手于晚上 9:10 左右在达罗克路街道工会办公室前被不明身份者枪击后，我立即赶赴现场。子弹从前额射入，穿透后脑。

根据一名中国目击者的陈述，穿着相似服装的人互相射击，但此说法未经证实。受害者被送往登陆部队营房，中国证人被拘留。在案发现场附近发现一颗子弹，由登陆部队带走。伤势的严重程度及受害者姓名不详。

REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.

The following is the statement of F.S. 230 Wilkinson.
native of taken by me D.S.I. McPhee.
at Hongkew Stn. on the 19/11/35. and interpreted by

My name is T.E. Wilkinson, employed by the S.M.C, as
Foreign Sergeant 230 attached to Dixwell Road Police Station.
At about 9.05 p.m. 9/11/35 I visited the Dixwell Road
Charge Room with a dog which I had captured on Kiangwan Road a
few minutes previous.
I had only arrived in the charge room about two minutes
when the street Telephone bell rang, which was answered by Clerk
Kyi, who informed F.S. 198 Stocks on charge room duty that
C.P.C. 2864, was reporting that a Chinese had been injured by a
Japanese Soldier on Darroch Road.
Immediately I heard Clerk Kyi inform F.S. 198 Stocks
that a Chinese had been injured on Darroch Road, I left the
charge room and proceeded to North Szechuen Road and Kiangwan
Road on a bicycle, turning South on Darroch Road and when a few
yards South of the Feng Loh Li alleyway I observed about 20
Japanese civilians standing on the West side of Darroch Road.
I immediately dismounted my bicycle and C.P.C. 2864 pointed to
a Japanese Sailor who was lying on the Road.
When I observed the sailor he was lying on his back at a
slight angle to the West kerb, bleeding from the head, and his
head lying in a pool of blood.
As I was viewing the injured sailor, J.P.S. 61 Dixwell
Road Station Interpreter arrived at the scene on a bicycle, where-
upon he looked at the injured sailor.
I then requested J.P.S. 61 to accompany me to the Japanese
Naval Landing Party Headquarters to report the matter, which he
did.
pages.zh:
上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。
续
以下为外籍巡长（F.S.）230号威尔金森（Wilkinson）的供词。
籍贯：（原文不清）
由副督察（D.S.I.）麦克菲（McPhee）于 1935 年 11 月 19 日在虹口巡捕房录取，并由……翻译。

我叫 T.E. Wilkinson，受雇于工部局（S.M.C.），任迪克斯韦尔路巡捕房外籍巡长（Foreign Sergeant）230号。
1935 年 11 月 9 日晚上 9:05 左右，我带着几分钟前在江湾路（Kiangwan Road）捕获的一条狗来到迪克斯韦尔路巡捕房的值班室。
我到达值班室仅约两分钟，街面电话铃响，由职员 Kyi 接听，他告知正在值班室值班的 F.S. 198号 Stocks，华捕（C.P.C.）2864号报告称一名中国人在达罗克路被一名日本士兵致伤。
我一听到职员 Kyi 告知 F.S. 198号 Stocks 有一名中国人在达罗克路受伤，便立即离开值班室，骑自行车前往北四川路和江湾路，然后转入达罗克路向南行驶。当行至丰乐里（Feng Loh Li）弄堂以南几码处时，我看到约 20 名日本平民站在达罗克路西侧。
我立即下车，华捕 2864号指向一名躺在路上的日本水手。
当我观察该水手时，他仰面躺着，身体与西侧路缘石成一定角度，头部流血，头躺在血泊中。
就在我查看受伤水手时，迪克斯韦尔路巡捕房的翻译日本警员（J.P.S.）61号骑自行车抵达现场，随即查看了受伤的水手。
随后，我请求 J.P.S. 61号陪同我前往日本海军陆战队登陆部队总部报告此事，他照办了。

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
=========================
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
================================
                P.S. 230          -2-
The following is the statement of............................................................
native of...................................................taken by me.......................
at.........................on the................................and interpreted by............

    When we arrived at the Naval Landing Party, I instructed
J.P.S. 61 to inform the Officer of the guard, that a Japanese
Sailor had been injured and was lying on Darroch Road, and to
request that an Ambulance be sent to remove the injured man.
    Immediately the Officer of the guard was informed by
J.P.S. 61 he looked surprised and shouted in the Japanese language,
whereupon the guard turned out.
    At this point, I left the Naval Landing Party, leaving
J.P.S. 61, whilst I proceeded to the No. 1 Street Telephone Box
situated on the East side of Kiangwan Road opposite the Naval
Landing Party and telephoned the Station, informing P.S. 198
Stocks on charge room duty that something serious had happened
on Darroch Road, and requesting that the Crime Branch and
Sub-Inspt. Butcher be informed.
    I then returned to the scene, and about 1 minute later
about 8 Japanese Sailors armed with rifles and 4 carrying a
stretcher arrived at the scene.
    The injured sailor was then lifted on to the stretcher by
Japanese Sailors, and removed to the Naval Landing Party by 4
stretcher bearers, whilst the 8 armed Sailors remained at the scene
    I then made enquiries at shops in the vicinity and amongst
the Japanese who had assembled at the scene, with a view to
locating witnesses, but without result.
    The only Chinese pedestrian observed by me at the scene
was a Chinese male dressed in blue jacket and pants, and on being
questioned he stated in Chinese that he had witnessed what
happened.

    当我们抵达海军陆战队登陆部队时，我指示
J.P.S. 61号告知卫兵军官，一名日本水手受伤并躺在达罗克路上，并请求派遣救护车将伤者运走。
    J.P.S. 61号刚告知卫兵军官，后者便露出惊讶的神色并用日语喊叫，随后卫兵出动。
    此时，我留下 J.P.S. 61号，自行离开海军陆战队登陆部队，前往位于江湾路东侧、正对海军陆战队登陆部队的第 1 号街面电话亭，打电话给巡捕房，告知正在值班室值班的 P.S. 198号 Stocks，达罗克路发生了严重事件，并请求通知刑事科（Crime Branch）及副督察（Sub-Inspt.）布彻（Butcher）。
    随后我返回现场，约 1 分钟后，约 8 名持步枪的日本水手和 4 名携带担架的人员抵达现场。
    受伤的水手随后被日本水手抬上担架，由 4 名担架员运往海军陆战队登陆部队，而 8 名武装水手则留在现场。
    随后，我在附近的商店及聚集在现场的日本人中进行查询，以期寻找证人，但无果。
    我在现场看到的唯一一名中国行人是一名身穿蓝色夹克和裤子的中国男子，经询问，他用中文表示他目击了事发经过。

Further statement of C.P.C. 2864, Hsu Sung Woo, attached
to Dixwell Road Police Station, taken by D.S.I. McPhee,
and interpreted by Clerk S.Y. Wong on 18·11-35.

My name is Hsu Sung Woo (        ), employed by the
S.M.C. as C.P.C. 2864, attached to Dixwell Road Police Station.
At 6.45 p.m. 9-11-35, I reported for 2nd day duty, i.e.
7 p.m. to 11 p.m., and was instructed to walk 5 Beat together
with C.P.C. 2891.
At about 9.02 p.m. 9-11-35, C.P.C. 2891 and I were
standing on the East side of Kiangwan Road opposite the Japanese
Naval Landing Party Headquarters, when my attention was attract-
ed by an unknown Chinese girl, age between 12 and 15 years, dress
ed in blue short jacket and pants, who was standing on the South
East corner of Darroch and North Szechuen Roads, shouting in
Kempo dialect that a man was lying on the road, but did not
mention which road.
Immediately after the girl shouted, C.P.C. 2891 and I
proceeded to the South East corner of Darroch and North Szechuen
Roads, where the girl was still standing.
We questioned the girl as to where the man was lying
and she answered that the man was lying on Darroch Road near the
Feng Loh Li.
C.P.C. 2891 and I then left the girl standing at the
corner of Darroch and North Szechuen Roads, without asking any
further questions, and proceeded South on Darroch Road.
When a few yards South of the Feng Loh Li, C.P.C. 2891
drew my attention to a body lying on the West side of Darroch
Road, whereupon we approached and C.P.C. 2891, who was carrying
an electric torch, his own property, shone the light of the
torch on the body, when we discovered same to be a Japanese
pages.zh:
附属于迪克斯韦尔路巡捕房的华捕（C.P.C.）2864号徐松武（Hsu Sung Woo）的补充供词，由副督察（D.S.I.）麦克菲（McPhee）录取，并由职员 S.Y. Wong 于 1935 年 11 月 18 日翻译。

我叫徐松武（        ），受雇于工部局（S.M.C.），任华捕（C.P.C.）2864号，附属于迪克斯韦尔路巡捕房。
1935 年 11 月 9 日下午 6:45，我报到开始第二天勤务，即晚上 7 点至 11 点，并受命与华捕 2891号一同巡逻 5 段（5 Beat）。
1935 年 11 月 9 日晚上 9:02 左右，华捕 2891号和我正站在江湾路东侧，正对日本海军陆战队登陆部队总部，此时我的注意力被一名身份不明的中国女孩吸引，她年龄在 12 至 15 岁之间，身穿蓝色短夹克和裤子，站在达罗克路与北四川路的东南角，用宁波话（Kempo dialect，音译，通常指宁波话或本地土语）喊叫说有人躺在路上，但未说明是哪条路。
女孩喊叫后，华捕 2891号和我立即前往达罗克路与北四川路的东南角，女孩仍站在那里。
我们询问女孩那人躺在哪里，她回答说那人躺在达罗克路靠近丰乐里（Feng Loh Li）的地方。
华捕 2891号和我随后让女孩继续站在达罗克路与北四川路的路口，未再追问，便沿达罗克路向南走去。
当行至丰乐里以南几码处时，华捕 2891号引起我对躺在达罗克路西侧的一具尸体的注意，于是我们走近，华捕 2891号用他自己的手电筒照亮尸体，我们发现那是一名日本

pages.en:
sailor, lying on his side, at a slight angle to the West kerb,
with his right arm outstretched, and bleeding from the forehead,
No person was to be seen in the vicinity when we arrived
at the scene. I then placed my hand near the sailor's mouth
to ascertain if he was breathing, and touched his wrist ( left
or right I cannot remember) to feel his pulse.
I told C.P.C. 2391 to watch the body whilst I telephoned
to the station for assistance.
I then left the scene and proceeded to the street
telephone box situated on the East side of Nangwan Road,
opposite the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters, where
I telephoned the station stating that a Japanese sailor was
lying on Darroch Road near the Fong Loh Li alleyway with blood
oozing from his head.
After an absence of about 5 minutes I returned to Darroch
Road and joined C.P.C. 2391 who was the only person at the scene.
About 5 minutes after I returned to the scene, P.S. 230
Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61 arrived at the scene on bicycles, and
looked at the injured sailor, and then proceeded North on
Darroch Road.
About 2 minutes after P.S. 230 Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61
left the scene, a Japanese sailor who was walking North on
Darroch Road, on observing the body lying on the road to be that
of a Japanese sailor, he approached and shouted two or three
times in the Japanese language and then left running North on
Darroch Road.
About 4 minutes later about 10 Japanese sailors carrying
pages.zh:
一名水兵侧卧，身体与西侧路缘石成微小角度，右臂伸展，前额流血。当我们抵达现场时，附近未见任何人。随后我将手靠近该水兵的嘴边，以确认他是否还有呼吸，并触摸他的手腕（左手或右手我已记不清）以感知脉搏。

我指令华捕巡长 2391 号看守尸体，同时我打电话向警署请求支援。

随后我离开现场，前往位于南湾路东侧、正对日本海军陆战队总部的街边电话亭，致电警署报告称：一名日本水兵躺在达罗克路（Darroch Road）丰乐里弄堂附近，头部渗血。

大约离开 5 分钟后，我返回达罗克路，与当时现场唯一的华捕巡长 2391 号会合。

在我返回现场约 5 分钟后，印捕巡佐 230 号威尔金森（Wilkinson）和日捕巡佐 61 号骑自行车抵达现场，查看了受伤的水兵，随后沿达罗克路向北离去。

在印捕巡佐 230 号威尔金森和日捕巡佐 61 号离开现场约 2 分钟后，一名沿达罗克路向北行走的日本水兵发现躺在地上的尸体是一名日本水兵，便走近并用日语喊叫了两三次，随后沿达罗克路向北奔跑离开。

约 4 分钟后，约 10 名携带

pages.en:
- 3 -

officers arrived at the scene from the direction of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party Headquarters and about 2 minutes after their
arrival, five or six Japanese sailors arrived with a stretcher.
The injured sailor was then placed on the stretcher by Japanese
sailors, and carried away in the direction of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party.

When the injured sailor was being lifted on to the stretcher
I observed a blue cloth bundle lying on the road near where the
injured sailor was lying.

The bundle was picked up by one of the Japanese sailors
who arrived with the stretcher.

I am unable to state when P.S. Wilkinson returned to the
scene, but immediately after the injured sailor was removed I
observed P.S. Wilkinson questioning a male at the entrance to
a cigarette shop situated on the West side of Darroch Road near
the scene.

Two or three minutes after the body was removed, about 10
persons including Japanese and Chinese arrived at the scene.

Whilst P.S. Wilkinson was questioning the persons who had
assembled at the scene if they had witnessed how the sailor
received his injuries, a male Chinese dressed in blue jacket
and pants approached P.S. Wilkinson and stated in Chinese that
he knew how the sailor received his injuries.

P.S. 230 Wilkinson then instructed C.P.C. 2991 and I to
take the witness to the station, which we did. I did not
question the Chinese witness at the scene or on the way to
the station.

Signed, Hsu Sung Woo.
許勝武
pages.zh:
- 3 -

军官的日本水兵从日本海军陆战队总部方向抵达现场；在他们抵达约 2 分钟后，五六名日本水兵带着担架赶到。

受伤的水兵随即被日本水兵抬上担架，并朝日本海军陆战队方向抬走。

当受伤水兵被抬上担架时，我观察到在受伤水兵躺卧处附近的路面上有一个蓝色布包。

该布包被一名随担架前来的日本水兵捡起。

我无法说明印捕巡佐威尔金森何时返回现场，但在受伤水兵被移走后，我立即看到印捕巡佐威尔金森正在达罗克路西侧、靠近现场的一家香烟店门口讯问一名男子。

尸体被移走两三分钟后，包括日本人和中国人在内的约 10 人抵达现场。

当印捕巡佐威尔金森询问聚集在现场的人是否目睹了该水兵如何受伤时，一名身穿蓝色夹克和裤子的中国男子上前，用中文向印捕巡佐威尔金森表示他知道该水兵是如何受伤的。

印捕巡佐 230 号威尔金森随即指令华捕巡长 2991 号和我将该证人带往警署，我们照办了。我在现场或前往警署的途中均未讯问该名中国证人。

签名：许胜武 (Hsu Sung Woo)。
許勝武

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
REPORT OF POLICE INVESTIGATIONS.
The following is the statement of. C.P.C. 7864.
native of ........................................taken by me.........................
at Dismell Rd. Stn. on the 9/11/38. translated and interpreted by Clerk Tong.

At 9.05 p.m. on the 9/11/38 I was on duty with C.P.C. 7891
on Kiangnan Road near E. Szechuen Road. Suddenly a female Chinese
reported to us that there was one Japanese lying on the ground.
Therefore we immediately proceeded to the scene and saw a Japanese
marine with a wound in the head. I at once telephoned to the
station and reported the same while C.P.C. 7891 remained there
and watched the injured person. Afterwards, P.S. 230, Wilkinson
came upon the scene and enquired if any one had seen this
accident. As a result of that we got a Chinese and a Japanese as
a witness and brought them to the station.

C.P.C. 7864.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
警务调查报告。
以下为华捕巡长 7864 号的陈述。
籍贯 ........................................由本人.........................于 1938 年 11 月 9 日在狄思威路警署录取。由通事童先生翻译及传译。

1938 年 11 月 9 日晚上 9 点 05 分，我与华捕巡长 7891 号在靠近四川路东段的江南路执勤。突然，一名中国女子向我们报告说有一名日本人躺在地上。因此我们立即前往现场，看到一名头部受伤的日本海军陆战队员。我立即打电话向警署报告此事，而华捕巡长 7891 号留在原地看守伤者。随后，印捕巡佐 230 号威尔金森来到现场，询问是否有人目睹此事故。结果我们找到了一名中国人和一名日本人作为证人，并将他们带往警署。

华捕巡长 7864 号。

pages.en:
Further statement of C.P.C. 2891, Tsu Ts Ching, attached
to Dixwell Road Police Station, taken by D.S.I. McPhee
and interpreted by Clerk S.T. Wong, at Hongkew Station
on 18-11-35.

My name is Tsu Ts Ching (          ), employed by the
S.M.C. as C.P.C. 2891, attached to Dixwell Road Police Station.
At 6.45 p.m. 9-11-35, I reported for 2nd day duty, i.e.
7 p.m. to 11 p.m., and I was instructed to walk 5 beat together
with C.P.C. 2864.
At about 8.55 p.m. 9-11-35, C.P.C. 2864 and I arrived
at the corner of Kiangwan and North Szechuen Roads, and stood on
the East pavement opposite the Japanese Naval Landing Party
Headquarters.
At about 9.4 p.m. 9-11-35, C.P.C. 2864 and I were still
standing on the East pavement of Kiangwan Road, when I observed
a Chinese girl, age about 13 or 14 years, dressed in short
jacket and pants, running South to North on Darroch Road, and on
arriving at the corner of Darroch and North Szechuen Roads, she
stopped at the South East corner, and started shouting in Kiangsu
dialect, "Policeman, Policeman, there is a man lying on Darroch
Road."
C.P.C. 2864 and I immediately ran across North Szechuen
Road, and continued South on Darroch Road, passing the girl who
had raised the alarm, and who was still standing at the corner of
Darroch and North Szechuen Roads.
After passing the girl who raised the alarm I did not
see her again, but I would be able to identify her should I see
her at any future date.
When C.P.C. 2864 and I arrived a few yards South of the
Feng Loh Li, I observed a body lying on the West side of Darroch
Road, whereupon I lighted my private torch and shone the light
pages.zh:
附属于狄思威路警署的华捕巡长 2891 号朱志清（Tsu Ts Ching）的进一步陈述，由副督察麦克菲（McPhee）于 1935 年 11 月 18 日在虹口警署录取，由通事黄 S.T. 先生传译。

我叫朱志清（          ），受雇于工部局，任华捕巡长 2891 号，附属于狄思威路警署。
1935 年 11 月 9 日下午 6 点 45 分，我报到开始第二天值班，即晚上 7 点至 11 点，奉命与华捕巡长 2864 号一同巡逻第 5 区。
1935 年 11 月 9 日晚上约 8 点 55 分，华捕巡长 2864 号和我到达江湾路与四川北路交叉口，站在正对日本海军陆战队总部的东侧人行道上。
1935 年 11 月 9 日晚上约 9 点 04 分，华捕巡长 2864 号和我仍站在江湾路东侧人行道上，此时我看到一名约 13 或 14 岁的中国女孩，身穿短夹克和裤子，在达罗克路上由南向北奔跑，到达达罗克路与四川北路交叉口时，她在东南角停下，并用江苏方言喊道：“警察，警察，达罗克路上躺着一个人。”

华捕巡长 2864 号和我立即跑过四川北路，继续沿达罗克路向南行进，经过那个发出警报的女孩，她当时仍站在达罗克路与四川北路的交叉口。

经过发出警报的女孩后，我没有再看到她，但如果将来见到她，我应该能认出她。
当华捕巡长 2864 号和我到达丰乐里以南几码处时，我看到一具尸体躺在达罗克路西侧，于是我点亮私人手电筒，将光线照

pages.en:
- 2 -

on the body lying on the road, and discovered same to be that
of a Japanese sailor.
C.P.C. 2864 and I then approached the sailor who was
groaning, and I observed that he was lying on his back at a
slight angle to the west kerb, and bleeding from the forehead,
his head lying in a pool of blood.
I also observed a blue cloth bundle lying by the sailor's
side.
We did not touch the body, and on arriving at the scene
no person was to be seen in the vicinity.
I then told C.P.C. 2864 to telephone the station for
assistance, whilst I remained at the scene.
C.P.C. 2864 then left to telephone the station and returned
about 5 minutes later.
During the absence of C.P.C. 2864 no person arrived at the
scene, or observed by me in the vicinity.
About 4 minutes after C.P.C. 2864 returned to the scene,
P.S. Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61 arrived at the scene on bicycles,
and after looking at the sailor lying on the road, they imme-
diately left the scene in a Northerly direction on Barrowsh
Road, without saying anything.
About 3 minutes after P.S. 230 Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61
left the scene, a Japanese sailor walking South to North on
Barrowsh Road arrived on the scene and when he observed the
sailor lying on the road, he approached the sailor and shouted
two times in the Japanese language, and then immediately left
running North on Barrowsh Road.
pages.zh:
- 2 -

在躺在路上的尸体上，发现那是一名日本水兵。
华捕巡长 2864 号和我随后走近那名正在呻吟的水兵，我观察到他是仰卧着，身体与西侧路缘石成微小角度，前额流血，头部浸在一滩血泊中。
我还观察到在水兵身旁有一个蓝色布包。
我们没有触碰尸体，当我们抵达现场时，附近未见任何人。
随后我告诉华捕巡长 2864 号打电话向警署请求支援，而我留在现场。
华捕巡长 2864 号随即离开去打电话给警署，约 5 分钟后返回。
在华捕巡长 2864 号离开期间，没有其他人抵达现场，我也未在附近观察到任何人。
在华捕巡长 2864 号返回现场约 4 分钟后，印捕巡佐威尔金森和日捕巡佐 61 号骑自行车抵达现场，在查看了躺在路上的水兵后，他们立即沿巴罗斯路（Barrowsh Road）向北离开现场，未发一言。
在印捕巡佐 230 号威尔金森和日捕巡佐 61 号离开现场约 3 分钟后，一名沿巴罗斯路由南向北行走的日本水兵抵达现场，当他看到躺在路上的水兵时，便走近该水兵并用日语喊叫了两次，随后立即沿巴罗斯路向北奔跑离开。

Three minutes later, J.P.C. 173 arrived on the scene, and
at about the same time a Japanese civilian dressed in a kimono
also arrived on the scene.
The Japanese civilian approached the body and touched
the sailor's mouth with his hand, and then started a conversa-
tion with J.P.C. 173.
P.S. Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61 returned to the scene after
an absence of about 7 minutes.
About 1 minute after P.S. 230 Wilkinson and J.P.S. 61
returned to the scene, about 13 or 14 Japanese sailors arrived,
two of whom were carrying a stretcher.
The injured sailor was then placed on the stretcher by
Japanese sailors, and carried away in the direction of the
Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters.
I do not know who picked up the blue cloth bundle which
was lying on the road, near the injured sailor, but after the
injured sailor was removed, I did not see the cloth bundle again.
A few minutes after the injured sailor had been removed,
about 10 or 11 Japanese and Chinese pedestrians arrived at the
scene.
After the injured sailor had been removed, P.S. 230
Wilkinson questioned a male Chinese in a cigarette shop, situat-
ed on the West side of Barrow Road, if he knew how the sailor
received his injuries.
P.S. 230 Wilkinson also made enquiries amongst the
pedestrians who had assembled at the scene, and was successful
in locating a male Chinese dressed in blue jacket and pants, who

三分钟后，日捕巡捕 173 号抵达现场，几乎同时，一名身穿和服的日本平民也抵达现场。
该日本平民走近尸体，用手触摸水兵的嘴，然后开始与日捕巡捕 173 号交谈。
印捕巡佐威尔金森和日捕巡佐 61 号在离开约 7 分钟后返回现场。
在印捕巡佐 230 号威尔金森和日捕巡佐 61 号返回现场约 1 分钟后，约 13 或 14 名日本水兵抵达，其中两人抬着担架。
受伤的水兵随即被日本水兵抬上担架，并朝日本海军陆战队总部方向抬走。
我不知道是谁捡起了躺在受伤水兵附近路面上的蓝色布包，但在受伤水兵被移走后，我没有再看到那个布包。
在受伤水兵被移走几分钟后，约 10 或 11 名日本和中国行人抵达现场。
在受伤水兵被移走后，印捕巡佐 230 号威尔金森在巴罗斯路西侧的一家香烟店里讯问一名中国男子，问他是否知道该水兵是如何受伤的。
印捕巡佐 230 号威尔金森还向聚集在现场的行人进行了查询，并成功找到一名身穿蓝色夹克和裤子的中国男子，该男子

C.P.C. 3964 and I were then instructed by P.S. 220
Wilkinson to take the Chinese witness to the station which we

This is a true statement.

籍贯........................................由本人....................于 1935 年 11 月 9 日在麦克斯韦尔路警署（Maxwell M.Stan）录取......由通事方先生传译。

1935 年 11 月 9 日晚上 9 点 05 分，我与华捕巡长 2864 号在靠近四川北路的江湾路（Kingwen Road）执勤。突然，一名中国女子向我们报告说有一名日本人躺在地上。因此我们立即前往现场，看到一名头部受伤的日本海军陆战队员，华捕巡长 2864 号立即打电话向警署报告此事，而我留在原地看守伤者。不久之后，印捕巡佐 730 号威尔金森来到现场，询问是否有人目睹此事故。结果我们找到了一名中国人和一名日本人作为证人，并将他们带往警署。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JULY 29, 1936

Youthful Amah's Story Of
Nakayama Shooting

Men In Black Foreign Clothes Who Stalked His
Victim In Darroch Road; Girl Fails To
Indentify Any Of Accused As The Man

An 18-year-old amah, Pu Chao-
ying, whose appearance in the
First Special District Court in
connection with the Nakayama
case had been requested by Judge
Tien, who reserved his decision on
account of the absence of her
testimony, finally appeared in
court yesterday. She testified
that on the night of November 9
she heard a shot and saw Naka-
yama lying on the ground but she
could not point out the assailant.
She said he was dressed in black
foreign clothes.

The three accused said they did
not recognize Pu and the amah
could not identify any of them as
being the man who fired the shot.

Summoned to Shanghai from
her home in Klangpeh, Pu's ap-
pearance in court was a surprise
to all except a few police officers,
lawyers and the judges. Her
testimony was given before an
almost empty court room, in the

presence of "Shao Kwangtung,"
Yang Wen-tao and Chou Tao-
yung.

Pu testified that being an amah
in a Japanese family in Yung An
Alley, North Szechuen Road, she
led several children to a woman
friend's home in Min Deh Fang
near the Kiangwan Headquarters
of the Japanese Landing Party
about 8 p.m. on November 9 last
year. When returning she passed
through Darroch Road where she
saw a Japanese officer walking
north, followed by a man in black
foreign clothes, walking on the
eastern side of the street.

Walking Between Men.

Witness was walking in the
middle of the street, between them,
and saw that the Japanese and
the man in foreign clothes were
about 20 or 30 feet apart. At this
juncture, the judge stopped Pu
and asked her if she could recog-
nize any one of the three accused
as the man she saw in Darroch
Road. She shook her head vio-
lently.

Proceeding, she said she sud-
denly heard gunfire while nearing
a boiled-water shop. She dared
not turn her head and slipped in-
to the shop the protect herself.
After hiding for sometime she re-
turned to her mistress's home by
another road. She told her mis-
tress what she had heard in the
street but did not mention the man
in the black suit. Seven or eight
days later, her service was dis-
continued and she went back to
her Klangpeh home.

Questioned as to whether or not
she could remember the roads she
passed through, Pu answered in
the affirmative.

It is understood that as the
result of this testimony, the form-
al re-opening of the Nakayama
case which was arranged for Fri-
day, July 31, may be postponed.

1936年7月29日

《字林西报》，1936年7月29日，星期三

年轻女佣讲述中山（Nakayama）枪击案经过

身穿黑色西装的男子在达罗克路（Darroch Road）尾随受害者；女孩未能指认任何被告为凶手

一名18岁的女佣浦巧英（Pu Chao-ying），因田法官（Judge Tien）此前以其证词缺席为由暂缓判决，要求其在中山案中出庭，她最终于昨日到庭。她作证称，去年11月9日晚，她听到一声枪响，看见中山倒在地上，但她无法指认袭击者。她说袭击者身穿黑色西装。

三名被告表示不认识浦氏，而该女佣也无法指认他们中的任何一人是开枪者。

浦氏从其高邮（Klangpeh）家中被传唤至上海，除了少数警官、律师和法官外，她的出庭令所有人感到意外。她在几乎空无一人的法庭上提供了证词，当时“邵广东”（Shao Kwangtung）、杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao）和周道庸（Chou Tao-yung）在场。

浦氏作证说，作为四川北路永安里一户日本家庭的女佣，去年11月9日晚8点左右，她带着几个孩子去了江湾日本海军陆战队总部附近的明德坊一位女性朋友家。回来时，她经过达罗克路，看见一名日本军官向北行走，后面跟着一个穿黑色西装的人，走在街道东侧。

走在两人之间。

证人走在街道中间，位于那两人之间，她看到那名日本人和穿西装的男子相距约20或30英尺。此时，法官打断浦氏，问她是否能从三名被告中认出她在达罗克路看到的那个人。她剧烈地摇头。

接着，她说当走近一家开水店时，突然听到枪声。她不敢回头，溜进店里保护自己。躲藏了一段时间后，她经另一条路回到女主人家。她告诉女主人在街上听到的情况，但没有提及那个穿黑西装的男人。七八天后，她被解雇，回到了高邮老家。

当被问及是否记得经过的路线时，浦氏给予了肯定的回答。

据悉，由于这一证词，原定于7月31日星期五正式重审的中山案可能会推迟。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, July. 21, 1936

MUNICIPAL POLICE
REGISTRY
D. D.

Nakayama Case
Opening Opposed

Attorneys Disgusted;
Wild Rumors Spread
About Kayau Case

Complete disgust with the re-opening of the pleadings in the Nakayama case was expressed by lawyers defending the three accused, Yang Wen-tao, Yih Hai-sen (Shao Kwangtung) and Chow Hsio-yang, when called by the Evening Post and Mercury this morning.

Mr. G. R. Grove, lawyer for the defence, expressed his opinion that both he and his colleague attorney were convinced of the innocence of their clients, but that nevertheless he could see no reason why judgment had not been given as scheduled last week.

Would Have Appealed

It was pointed out that if judgment has been rendered at that time, all contingencies could have been taken care of by appeal cases. It is known that if a verdict of guilty is turned in the defendants will appeal and it is almost certain that if a verdict of non-guilt is rendered, the police will appeal the case. The next hearing in the trial is scheduled or Friday, July 31, at 2 p.m.

It is not believed, as previously stated, that evidence concerning the manufacture of the death bullet will be given. It is, however, understood that Judge Dzian wished to hear the testimony of a woman who reported seeing a figure fleeing from the scene of the crime.

Feared Consequences?

While it has now been fairly definitely established that the pleadings in the case were reopened because of instructions from Nanking, it was further stated by authoritative sources this morning that certain statements published in Japanese papers and certain statements emanating from Japanese sources brought so much pressure to bear that in fear of possible consequences, the case was re-opened.

Wild rumors concerning the killing of Kosaku Kayau on Chimei Road on the night of July 10 have been circulating freely throughout Shanghai in the past few days. Anonymous tips and unasked-for conjectures have all been carefully tracked down, but Japanese, Chinese and Settlement authorities express themselves as much in the dark as ever concerning the actual murderer or the motive for the slaying.

The theory that Chinese cabaret girls had anything to do with or had any knowledge of the crime is not given credence in responsible quarters.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年7月21日，星期二

工部局警务处
登记科
D. D.

中山案
反对重开审理

律师感到厌恶；
关于加屋案的谣言四起

今天上午，《晚邮报与水星报》致电为三名被告杨文涛、叶海森（又名邵广东，Yih Hai-sen (Shao Kwangtung)）和周孝扬（Chow Hsio-yang）辩护的律师时，他们对中山案诉辩程序的重开表达了完全的厌恶。

辩护律师 G. R. Grove 先生表示，他和他的同事律师都确信他们的当事人是无辜的，但他看不出上周为何没有按计划作出判决的理由。

本拟上诉

有人指出，如果当时作出了判决，所有后续情况都可以通过上诉案件来处理。众所周知，如果判决有罪，被告将上诉；而如果判决无罪，警方几乎肯定会对此案提出上诉。审判的下一次听证会定于7月31日星期五下午2时举行。

人们并不像先前所说的那样相信会提供有关致死子弹制造过程的证据。然而，据了解，詹法官（Judge Dzian）希望听取一名声称看到有人从犯罪现场逃离的女性的证词。

担心后果？

虽然现在已经相当明确地确定，该案诉辩程序的重开是因为南京方面的指示，但权威人士今天上午进一步表示，日本报纸上发表的某些声明以及来自日本方面的某些声明施加了巨大压力，出于对可能后果的恐惧，案件得以重开。

过去几天，关于7月10日晚在集美路（Chimei Road）杀害加屋功作（Kosaku Kayau）的疯狂谣言在上海四处流传。匿名举报和不请自来的猜测都经过了仔细追踪，但日本、中国和租界当局都表示，对于实际凶手或杀人动机，他们仍然一无所知。

负责方面不相信中国舞女与此案有任何牵连或知情。

中山案
判决延期
新证据成为延迟理由

第一特区地方法院钱弘义法官（Judge Tsien Hung-yih）主持了对叶海森（又名“小广东”）、杨文涛和周祖荣（Chow Zeu-yoong，均为广东人）的审判，他们被控于去年11月9日在达罗克路谋杀日本海军陆战队员 H. 中山（H. Nakayama）。他昨天宣布，他没有像上周宣布的那样在昨天上午对中山案作出判决，而是决定在待定日期重开该案的诉辩程序，因为警方提出了新证据，且将有额外证人从外地抵达此处。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, July 18, 1936

All Quiet Along
Hongkew Front

Reopening Nakayama
Case Fails To Cause
Reverberations

The two Japanese murder cases were still occupying the Shang-hai limelight this morning, but expected reverberations of the re-opening of the pleadings in the Nakayama case failed to lead to any untoward incidents, and the Japanese and Chinese communities remained calm.

Chinese dancing girls and North Szechuen Road again leaped into prominence when it was reported that five taxi-dancers living in back of the Moon Palace, which figured so prominently as a "hangout" of Yih Hai-sen (Bao Kwangtung) when he was put on trial for his life for the murder of Hideo Nakayama, were detained by police early this morning and were later handed over to the Bureau of Public Safety for questioning.

While the ostensible reason for the re-opening of the Nakayama case was the introduction of new police evidence, and while it has been expressed that the court is not quite clear over the motive for the slaying, it was again stated by authoritative quarters this morning that the pleadings in the case were re-opened on instructions from Nanking.

Meeting in an emergency session, officials of the Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Union yesterday discussed the latest developments in the Nakayama case.

Reports on their conversations with the authorities of the Japanese Consulate-General and the Special Naval Landing Party were also made by Mr. Yuso Hayashi and Mr. Hikaru Kondo, respectively honorary president and chairman of the standing committee of the Federation.

The deliberations continued for nearly two hours, following which it was decided to call other emergency sessions in case of necessity, local Japanese papers reported.

Five Chinese taxi-dancers, said to be involved in the murder of Mr. Kosaku Kayau, were detained by the officials of the North Szechuen Road Police Station of the Public Safety Bureau yesterday.

Following a brief examination all five were taken to the headquarters of the Bureau in Nantao for further questioning.

The dancers lived behind the Moon Palace Dance Hall, on North Szechuen Road.

Two brothers-in-law and a five-year-old son of Mr. Kayau will leave here on Tuesday for Japan aboard the Shanghai Maru, carrying with them an urn containing the ashes of the murdered man.

On Friday, Mr. Kayau's relatives paid courtesy calls on local Consular and civic officials.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年7月18日，星期六

虹口前线平静无事

中山案重开审理
未引起反响

今天上午，两起日本谋杀案仍占据着上海的焦点，但预计中山案诉辩程序重开引起的反响并未导致任何不幸事件，日本和华人社区保持平静。

据报道，住在月宫舞厅后面的五名伴舞女郎今天上午被警方拘留，随后被移交给公安局审讯，这使得中国舞女和四川北路再次成为焦点。月宫舞厅曾是叶海森（又名包广东，Bao Kwangtung）在因谋杀中山秀雄受审时的主要“出没地”。

虽然重开中山案诉辩程序的表面原因是警方提出了新证据，且有人表示法院对杀人动机尚不清楚，但权威人士今天上午再次表示，该案诉辩程序的重开是奉南京方面的指示。

日本街道联合会官员昨天召开紧急会议，讨论了中山案的最新进展。

据当地日文报纸报道，联合会名誉会长林勇三郎（Yuso Hayashi）先生和常务委员会主席近藤光（Hikaru Kondo）先生分别报告了他们与日本总领事馆和特别海军陆战队当局的会谈情况。

审议持续了近两个小时，随后决定在必要时召开其他紧急会议。

据称涉及加屋功作先生谋杀案的五名中国伴舞女郎，昨天被公安局四川北路警察局的官员拘留。

经过简短讯问，五人全部被带往南市公安局总部接受进一步审讯。

这些舞女住在四川北路月宫舞厅后面。

加屋先生的两名姻兄弟和他的一名五岁儿子将于周二乘坐“上海丸”号离开这里前往日本，随身携带装有死者骨灰的骨灰盒。

周五，加屋先生的亲属拜访了当地领事馆和市政官员。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, JULY 18, 1936

Nakayama Case Hearing
Will Now Be Reopened
As Motive Is Not 'Clear

General Tension Drops As Order Is Pronounced
By Judge; Four Motives Had Been Given
For Killing By "Shao Kwangtung"

JAPANESE HOLD MEETING AND DECIDE TO
WATCH FURTHER DEVELOPMENTS

Coming as a bombshell on the court room crowded with lawyers, Settlement Police, Japanese Consular Police, representatives of the Japanese Naval Landing Party and other interested parties, came the announcement at 8.35 a.m. yesterday that the hearing of the Nakayama case would be reopened. The announcement greatly relieved the tension which was hanging over the court room for about half-an-hour since officials commenced to gather.

Although coming as a great surprise to both the prosecution and the defence, the ruling was cleared up when it was explained that the three judges presiding over the case were not satisfied with the motive given for the killing of Warrant Office Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing force on Darroch Road on the evening of November 9, last.

In the court room the chief judge, Mr. Dzien, pointed out that the court after due deliberation considers it necessary to question an amah named Pu Chiao-ying, who was alleged to have witnessed the killing, but was never questioned in court.. Judge Dzien therefore remanded the case sine die pending the appearance of the witness, who is now in Yangchow, Kompo. It was also indicated by reliable sources that other witnesses would be recalled for further questioning by the court.

Four Motives Given

It was stated on reliable authority yesterday that Judges Dzien, Feng and Shao upon coming to rule on the case, found themselves confronted with four separate motives for the killing put forward by Yin Hai-sen, alias "Shao Kwangtung," who alternatively confessed to the killing, denied any part in same and implicated others afterwards exonerating them.

In reviewing the case among themselves in order to pass judgment on the three accused, the judges found a stumbling block in the four separate motives, neither of which, it was stated, proved plausible to them. At various times "Shao Kwangtung" had told the court that he had killed the Japanese marine because he hated Japanese. His second motive was because Jack the Korean had asked him to commit the crime, thirdly he said he shot the Japanese in order to show that his organization and China was powerful, and his fourth motive given at one of the hearings was that he killed the man in order to create trouble in Chapei and embarrass the Nanking Government.

Police Satisfied

The police, according to Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Y. Bu, who ably conducted the prosecution in the case, were quite satisfied with the way the case was conducted, the evidence which was produced and were expecting judgment to be passed yesterday morning. The defense counsel yesterday morning also proved to be surprised and immediately after the hearing could not get any explanation as to why the case was ordered to be reopened.

Precautions were taken in the actual court room and in the court compound yesterday morning to prevent any outbreak as a result of tense feeling over the expected verdict. A number of officers of the Reserve Unit, S.M.P., were seen patrolling in the court compound and outside. A red riot van stood parked near-by on Tsepo Road. A high ranking officer of the Japanese Naval Landing Party accompanied by some 12 marines was also present as was Assistant Commissioner S. Uehara.

Shortly before 8.30 a.m. the three accused, Yih Hai-sen, Yang Wen-tao and Chow Hsia-yung, were led into the dock. They all stood with their heads dropped, looking at the floor. A few minutes after 8.30 the court was called to order and the three judges walked in. Perfect silence settled over the court room and then standing-up while everyone including the accused held their breath Judge Dzien ordered the case to be reopened. Everyone stood as in a trance while the judges trooped out of the court room. The three accused were led away and then a babble of conversation commenced, until everyone walked out of the court room.

Meeting in an emergency session, officials of the Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions yesterday morning discussed the latest developments in the Nakayama case.

Reports on their conversations with the authorities of the Japanese Consulate-General and the Special Naval Landing Party were also made by Mr. Yuzo Hayashi and Mr. Hikaru Kondo, respectively honorary president and chairman of the standing committee of the Federation.

The deliberations continued for nearly two hours, following which it was decided to call other emergency sessions in case of necessity, local Japanese papers reported.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年7月18日，星期六

中山案听证
现将重新开庭
因动机“不明”

法官宣判后总体紧张局势缓解；
“邵广东”行凶曾提出四种动机

日方举行会议并决定
密切关注事态进一步发展

昨日早晨8时35分，在挤满了律师、租界巡捕、日本领事馆警察、日本海军陆战队代表及其他相关人士的法庭上，突然宣布中山案将重新开庭，这一消息犹如晴天霹雳。自官员们开始聚集以来，法庭内笼罩着约半小时的紧张气氛，此宣布极大地缓解了这种紧张局面。

尽管这一裁决令控辩双方都大为惊讶，但随着解释的展开，疑云得以消散：主持本案的三位法官对去年11月9日晚在达罗克路（Darroch Road）杀害日本海军陆战队准尉官中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）一案所给出的动机并不满意。

在法庭上，主审法官迪恩先生（Mr. Dzien）指出，法院经慎重考虑，认为有必要讯问一名名为卜娇英（Pu Chiao-ying，音译）的女佣，据称她目击了杀人过程，但此前从未在庭上接受过讯问。因此，迪恩法官将该案无限期延期，以待这位目前位于江苏扬州（Yangchow, Kompo）的证人出庭。另有可靠消息来源指出，法院还将传唤其他证人进行进一步讯问。

提出四种动机

据昨日可靠权威人士称，迪恩、冯和邵三位法官在对案件作出裁决时，发现尹海森（Yin Hai-sen），别名“邵广东”，提出了四种不同的行凶动机。尹海森时而承认行凶，时而否认参与，随后又牵连他人，继而又为他们开脱。

法官们在内部审议以对三名被告作出判决时，发现这四种不同的动机构成了障碍，据说其中任何一种对他们来说都显得不合情理。“邵广东”在不同时间曾向法庭表示，他杀害这名日本水兵是因为他憎恨日本人。他的第二个动机是受一名朝鲜人杰克（Jack the Korean）指使作案；第三，他说他枪杀日本人是为了显示其组织和中国的力量；第四，他在某次听证会上提出的动机是，他杀害此人是为了在闸北制造麻烦，并使南京政府陷入困境。

警方感到满意

据在该案中出色地主持公诉的副市政检察官保罗·Y·布（Paul Y. Bu）称，警方对案件的审理方式及提交的证据相当满意，并原预计昨日上午会宣判。辩护律师昨日上午也证明对此感到意外，且在听证会结束后立即无法就为何命令重审此案获得任何解释。

昨日上午，在实际法庭内及法院大院均采取了预防措施，以防因对预期判决的紧张情绪而引发任何骚乱。可以看到多名上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）后备队警员在法院大院内及外围巡逻。一辆红色防暴车停在附近的资福路（Tsepo Road，音译）。日本海军陆战队的一名高级军官在约12名水兵的陪同下到场，副局长上原（S. Uehara）亦在场。

上午8时30分前不久，三名被告尹海森、杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao，音译）和周夏勇（Chow Hsia-yung，音译）被带入被告席。他们全都低着头，看着地板。8时30分过后几分钟，法庭宣布开庭，三位法官入席。法庭内一片死寂，随后，在包括被告在内的所有人屏住呼吸站立时，迪恩法官命令重新审理此案。当法官们成群走出法庭时，所有人都如入定般站立。三名被告被带离，随后交谈声四起，直到众人走出法庭。

日本各街联合会（Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions）的官员昨日上午召开紧急会议，讨论了中山案的最新进展。

该联合会名誉会长林雄三（Yuzo Hayashi，音译）先生和常务委员会主席近藤辉（Hikaru Kondo，音译）先生分别报告了他们与日本总领事馆当局及特别海军陆战队当局的会谈情况。

据当地日文报纸报道，审议持续了近两个小时，随后决定在必要时召开其他紧急会议。
