THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, JULY 18, 1936

No Decision
In Nakayama
Case Given

Trial To Be Reopened
On Basis Of New
Police Evidence

Although judgment was scheduled, Judge Dalen in the First Special District Court yesterday morning ordered the reopening of the Nakayama murder case for the purpose of taking further police evidence. It is reported that a witness has been found who can tell how the bullet that killed Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama on November 9 of last year was manufactured.

The three accused men, Yang Wau-tao, Yih Hai-sen (Hsiao Kwangtung), and Chow Sha-yung, were brought into court early yesterday morning but were there only a few minutes. Immediately after taking his seat, the judge announced the reopening of the case and remanded it sine die.

Few Spectators In Court

There were only a few spectators in the courtroom. No one had expected that the case would be brought up in the morning since it had been remanded from the last hearing until 2 p.m. yesterday for judgment. A few police stood outside the court while the only Japanese present were police officers and a few official observers. They refused to comment on the action of the court when questioned by a CHINA PRESS representative.

Although the action of the court came somewhat as a surprise, there was no disturbance. The three prisoners were hustled out of the dock, downstairs to the distributing office and then back to the black patrol wagon for conveyance to their cells. Municipal Advocate R. T. Bryan and Assistant Advocate Paul Y. Ru were both present at the proceedings and both hurried away immediately after the judge had announced the reopening.

Mr. R. D. Grove, attorney for the defendants, stopped long enough to speak to newspapermen. "It's nonsense. Absolute nonsense," he declared.

No further developments in connection with the slaying of Mr. Kosaku Kayau last week were reported yesterday. Secrecy still surrounds the investigation of the crime.

Two brothers and a five-year-old son of the murdered man arrived in Shanghai yesterday aboard the Nagasaki Maru to take the remains of the dead man back to Japan for burial. Kayau has two other younger sons and his wife living in Japan.

Love Triangle Denied

The idea of a love triangle being involved was definitely denied by the Japanese authorities yesterday. The latter still hold the opinion that it was a political killing.

In the meantime, all is quiet in the Hongkew area, although a very definite high tension feeling was manifest among members of the Japanese community who hold that sufficient evidence has already been presented in the Nakayama Case to warrant a conviction.

Meeting in an emergency session, officials of the Federation of Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions yesterday morning discussed the latest developments in the Nakayama case.

Reports on their conversations with the authorities of the Japanese Consulate-General and the Special Naval Landing Party were also made by Mr. Yuto Hayashi and Mr. Hikaru Kondo, respectively, honorary president and chairman of the standing committee of the Federation.

The deliberations continued for nearly two hours, following which it was decided to call other emergency sessions in case of necessity, local Japanese papers reported.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》，1936年7月18日，星期六

中山案
未作判决

基于新的
警方证据
案件将重审

虽然原定宣判，但第一特区地方法院的达伦法官（Judge Dalen，音译）昨日上午命令重新开庭审理中山谋杀案，目的是采集进一步的警方证据。据报道，已找到一名证人，能够说明去年11月9日杀害准尉官中山秀夫的那颗子弹是如何制造的。

三名被告杨华道（Yang Wau-tao，音译）、尹海森（即邵广东）和周少勇（Chow Sha-yung，音译）于昨日上午早些时候被带上法庭，但仅停留了几分钟。法官入座后立即宣布重审此案，并将其无限期延期。

法庭旁听者寥寥

法庭内只有少数旁听者。由于上次听证会将案件延期至昨日下午2时宣判，无人预料到案件会在上午提审。几名警察站在法庭外，在场的日本人仅有警察和少数官方观察员。当《大美晚报》记者询问时，他们拒绝对法院的行动发表评论。

尽管法院的举动有些令人意外，但并未发生骚乱。三名囚犯被匆忙带出被告席，下楼至分发室，然后回到黑色巡逻车上，以便押回牢房。市政检察官R. T. Bryan先生和副检察官Paul Y. Ru先生均出席了诉讼程序，并在法官宣布重审后立即匆匆离去。

被告代理律师R. D. Grove先生停下脚步与报界人士交谈。“真是胡闹。绝对的胡闹，”他宣称。

昨日没有报道关于上周Kosaku Kayau先生被杀案的任何进一步进展。对该罪行的调查仍然保密。

遇害者的两个兄弟和一个五岁的儿子昨日乘坐长崎丸（Nagasaki Maru）抵达上海，将死者遗体运回日本安葬。Kayau在日本还有另外两个年幼的儿子及其妻子。

否认三角恋情

日本当局昨日明确否认涉及三角恋情的说法。日方仍坚持认为这是一起政治谋杀。

与此同时，虹口地区一切平静，尽管在日本侨民中明显表现出一种高度紧张的情绪，他们认为在中山案中提交的证据已足以定罪。

日本各街联合会的官员昨日上午召开紧急会议，讨论了中山案的最新进展。

该联合会名誉会长林雄三（Yuto Hayashi，音译）先生和常务委员会主席近藤辉（Hikaru Kondo，音译）先生分别报告了他们与日本总领事馆当局及特别海军陆战队当局的会谈情况。

据当地日文报纸报道，审议持续了近两个小时，随后决定在必要时召开其他紧急会议。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, July 18, 1936

The Nakayama Case
MORE THAN the defendants are on trial in the Nakayama murder case, verdict in which was postponed yesterday on orders from Nanking. Certainly no consideration of this delicate matter can exclude the factors of the independence of the Chinese judiciary, and the self-restraint of Japanese having a vital interest.
It seems to us imperative that the Chinese authorities be given the benefit of all possible manifestations of confidence and co-operation, from every quarter. There are indications of new evidence, and if that can be adduced it is obviously desirable that it be brought forward—without complications through malicious reports concerning either intimidation (to prevent an acquittal) or pressure (to force conviction). Rumors are merely rumors and should be treated as such.
Certainly it is to no one's interest that anything but justice be done. An unjust verdict in either direction would inevitably stir up trouble one way or the other. The court has no easy task, but at least it has a clearly-indicated one. And when the court has completed its task, and given a verdict according to evidence and law, it will be the duty of everyone to accept that verdict as final.
Any other attitude will sow seeds which may easily result in international complications of great and grave magnitude.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年7月18日，星期六

中山案

在中山谋杀案中，受审的不仅仅是被告，该案的判决已于昨日奉南京之命推迟。当然，对这一微妙事项的任何考量都不能排除中国司法独立以及具有重大利害关系的日本方面的克制这些因素。

在我们看来，必须让中国当局得到各方尽可能表现出的信任与合作。有新证据的迹象，如果能提出这些证据，显然宜将其呈堂——而不必因有关恐吓（以防止无罪释放）或施压（以强迫定罪）的恶意报道而产生复杂化。谣言仅仅是谣言，应如此对待。

当然，除了实现正义之外，任何其他结果都不符合任何人的利益。无论哪一方的不公正判决都不可避免地会以某种方式激起麻烦。法院的任务并不轻松，但至少其任务是明确指出的。当法院完成任务，并根据证据和法律作出判决时，每个人都有责任接受该判决为最终判决。

任何其它态度都将播下种子，极易导致巨大且严重的国际纠纷。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, July 17, 1936

Nakayama Case
Re-Opened By
District Court

Order Declared Issued
By Nanking Authorities
To Avoid Trouble

JAPANESE REMAIN
UNUSUALLY QUIET

Report Circulated Navy
Landing Party Ready
To Occupy Center

Following fast on the heels of the re-opening of the Nakayama case by Judge Chien in the First District Court this morning came the startling announcement that orders had come down from the Central Government in Nanking not to give any verdict today.

While the Shanghai Evening Post obtained this piece of news from a reliable source, no direct confirmation of the reasons for the postponement of the verdict could be unearthed up until 1 o'clock today.

Take Over Civic Center?

It was rumored that the intelligence bureau of the Central Government had dug up the information that the Japanese in Shanghai were ready to take over the Civic Center if a verdict of "not guilty" were returned against Yih Hai-sen, alias Hsiao Kwang-tung, Yang Wen-tao and Chow Hsia-yung, and that this was the real reason why instructions were given to re-open the case.

No untoward incidents have as yet occurred as the result of today's decision, and the Hongkew district went about its business in a normal way. Japanese officials, who have recently been issuing strong statements regarding the verdict in the Nakayama case and regarding investigations into the killing of Kosaku Kayau last week, this morning were attempting to keep their nationals quiet.

New Witness

It was reported that defense attorneys after the announcement of the re-opening of the case were going to institute an urgent search for a witness who claimed to know who manufactured the bullet that killed Nakayama. This man is alleged to have come forward with this information after pleadings in the case had been closed and when it was too late to submit the evidence.

It was also stated by Chinese sources that the defense attorney formerly had two witnesses whose testimony was of prime importance in the case, but that they had been badly beaten by "Japanese" and with their eyes badly blackened had gone off to Hongkong without being called to give testimony in the case.

Effect Of Pressure

Japanese officials refused to comment on the decision of Judge Chien this morning, but it was pointed out by native sources that if the reopening of the pleadings was due to the effect of outside pressure, action, it might prove to be a serious matter.

Great precautions were taken at the First District Court this morning to forestall any possible outbreak of feeling over the result of the scheduled verdict. Outside the court building a number of Chinese and foreign police were on patrol. In the courtroom itself, Chinese police and Japanese police from reserve units; and from various stations rubbed elbows. A few foreign policemen were there in uniform. Two foreign detectives who have been working on the case all along stood by and watched proceedings. Very few spectators attended.

Japanese Officers Present

About 8:25 o'clock, the chief of the Japanese Naval Landing Party strode in followed by a half a dozen officers in pea-green uniforms. Mr. S. Uehara, assistant commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police, turned to greet them.

Shortly afterward, Yih Hai-sen, Yang Wen-tao and Chow Hsin-yung, the three accused were brought in and placed in the dock. They kept quiet and looked at the ground. Shao Kwangtung (Yih) kept looking at his patent leather dancing pumps which were without shoe laces.

About 8:35 o'clock, Judges Chien, Feng and Shao came in and took their places on the bench. Spectators leaned forward to catch Judge Chien's words. They were delivered in such a low voice that only those right beneath his desk could catch them.

Further Evidence

In substance, the judge declared that the pleadings in the "Nakayama case would be re-opened as the police had further evidence to present."

A startled murmur went up from the spectators in the courtroom. Certain Japanese faces looked around in a bewildered manner. The prisoners were led swiftly away, and the court room emptied quietly and with no outward fuss.

Paul Y. Ru, assistant municipal advocate who has been prosecuting the case, hurried away with Municipal Advocate Bryan before reporters had a chance to speak to them. Mr. R. D. Grove, when approached by a reporter and asked if he was still as surprised over the judge's decision as he had expressed himself yesterday, was extremely voluble.

"It's nonsense. Absolute nonsense," he declared and went on to give reasons.

Feeling Strong

A definite statement of Japanese attitude could not be learned officially from the consulate here this morning, but it is understood that the Japanese officials and community feel very strongly that the guilt of both Yih Hai-sen (Shao Kwangtung) and Yang Wen-tao has been definitely proven, and that anything but a conviction for these two defendants can be only regarded as a definite miscarriage of justice. The recent slaying of Kosaku Kayau has put the Japanese community into a fevered state of unrest, and it is alleged that Japanese officials are having a difficult struggle in their attempt to stem the rising tide of resentment among their countrymen.

in Shanghai, had anything to do with the case. At 10 a.m. this morning, Mr. Wakasugi called on Mr. Cikawa, commander-in-chief of the 3rd Squadron, and at 11 a.m. called on Mr. H. E. Arnold, chairman of the Shanghai Municipal Consul. At 3 o'clock he was to call on General Yang Hu, garrison commander of the Shanghai and Woosung areas. While it is believed that the calls were to be of a purely social nature, it is thought that the Nakayama and the Kayau cases will come up for discussion in the meeting with General Yang Hu.

Kayau Case Quiet

No further developments have arisen in the death of Kosaku Kayau, Japanese sea-food broker who was killed on Chimei Road on the night of July 10. Another set-back has been met with, however, as the ricksha puller who took Mr. Kayau to the Foo Ming Hospital says that he had found no blood on his ricksha. No love-angle is possible involved, Japanese authorities state, but a previous spokesman of the Japanese Police had said that murder might have been caused by political reasons.

Secrecy still surrounds the investigation which has been going on with redoubled intensity. It is believed that a meeting of detectives of the Bureau of Public Safety has taken place for the purpose of discussing the crime and to exchange views on the situation.

Relatives Arrive

Two brothers and a five-year old son of Kayau, arrived here yesterday aboard the Nagasaki Maru to take the remains of Kayau back to his native place in Chiba Prefecture.

Immediately upon arrival here, the three relatives went to the Honkokuji Temple on Chapoo Road, to pay respects to the soul of the murdered man.

Kayau has two other younger sons and his wife in Japan.

Statement Made

The murder of Kayau has occasioned much comment in the Japanese community. A statement was made Wednesday by the Foreign Relations Committee of the Japanese Residents' Corporation to the effect that since the assassin is still free, much uneasiness is being caused.

The Bureau of Public Safety has increased the patrols that have been policing the districts where many Japanese reside.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年7月17日，星期五

中山案
由地方法院
重新审理

据称南京当局
为避免事端
已下达命令

日本人保持
异常安静

谣传海军陆战队
已准备好
占领市中心

继今早第一特区地方法院钱法官重新审理中山案之后，随即传来令人震惊的消息：南京中央政府已下达命令，今日不作任何判决。

虽然《上海晚邮报》从可靠消息来源获悉此新闻，但截至今日下午1时，仍未能直接证实推迟判决的原因。

接管市中心？

有谣言称，中央政府情报部门获悉，如果以“无罪”判决乙海森（又名萧广东）、杨文涛和周夏荣（音译），在上海的日本人准备接管市中心，这才是指示重审此案的真实原因。

截至目前，今天的决定并未引发任何不幸事件，虹口地区照常进行日常活动。日本官员最近就中山案的判决以及上周对加屋功作（Kosaku Kayau）被杀案的调查发表了强硬声明，今早他们正试图让本国侨民保持安静。

新证人

据报道，在宣布重审案件后，辩护律师打算紧急寻找一名证人，该证人声称知道是谁制造了杀死中山的子弹。据说此人在案件辩论结束后才提出这一信息，当时提交证据为时已晚。

中方消息人士还称，辩护律师原本有两名证人，其证词在案件中至关重要，但他们遭到“日本人”的毒打，双眼被打得青肿，在未出庭作证的情况下前往香港。

压力的影响

日本官员拒绝评论钱法官今早的决定，但本地消息人士指出，如果重新开庭辩论是由于外部压力的作用，这可能会证明是一件严重的事情。

今早第一特区地方法院采取了严密的预防措施，以防因预定判决结果而可能引发的情绪爆发。法院大楼外，有多名中外警察在巡逻。法庭内，中国警察与来自后备队及各分局的日本警察摩肩接踵。几名身着制服的外国警察也在场。两名一直负责此案的外国侦探在一旁旁观庭审过程。旁听者寥寥无几。

日本军官在场

大约8点25分，日本海军陆战队队长大步走进法庭，身后跟着半打身穿豌豆绿制服的军官。上海公共租界工部局警务处副总巡捕上原S先生（S. Uehara）转身迎接他们。

不久之后，三名被告乙海森、杨文涛和周信勇（音译）被带入法庭并站在被告席上。他们保持沉默，低头看着地面。萧广东（即乙）一直盯着他那双没有鞋带的漆皮舞鞋。

大约8点35分，钱、冯和邵三位法官入庭并就座。旁听者前倾身体，试图听清钱法官的话。他的声音极低，只有紧靠他桌下的人才能听见。

进一步证据

法官实质上宣布：“鉴于警方有更多证据要提交，‘中山案’的辩论将重新开启。”

法庭内的旁听者发出一阵惊讶的低语声。某些日本人的脸上露出困惑的神情。囚犯被迅速带离，法庭安静地清空，未引起外在的骚动。

助理市检察官鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru）一直负责起诉此案，他在记者有机会与他们交谈之前，便与市检察官布莱恩（Bryan）匆匆离去。当记者接近R. D. Grove先生，询问他是否像昨天表达的那样对法官的决定感到惊讶时，他变得非常健谈。

“这是胡说八道。绝对的胡说八道，”他宣称，并继续阐述理由。

情绪激烈

今早无法从当地领事馆官方获悉日本态度的明确声明，但据了解，日本官员和侨社群情激愤，认为乙海森（萧广东）和杨文涛的罪行已确凿无疑，对这两名被告的任何判决若非定罪，只能被视为明显的司法不公。最近加屋功作（Kosaku Kayau）的被杀使日本侨民处于一种狂热的不安状态，据称日本官员在试图遏制同胞中日益高涨的怨恨情绪方面正面临艰难斗争。

在上海，与此案有任何关联。今天上午10时，若杉先生（Mr. Wakasugi）拜访了第三舰队司令长川崎先生（Mr. Cikawa，音译），上午11时拜访了上海公共租界工部局总董阿诺德先生（H. E. Arnold）。下午3时，他将拜访上海及吴淞地区卫戍司令杨虎将军。虽然人们认为这些拜访纯属社交性质，但据信在与杨虎将军的会晤中，中山案和加屋案将成为讨论议题。

加屋案平静

7月10日晚在集美路被杀的日本海鲜经纪人加屋功作（Kosaku Kayau）死亡案未有进一步进展。然而，调查又遇挫折，因为送加屋先生去福明医院的人力车夫表示，他在车上未发现血迹。日本当局表示，不可能涉及情感纠葛，但日本警方的一位前任发言人曾表示，谋杀可能是出于政治原因。

调查仍在加紧进行，周围仍笼罩着神秘色彩。据信，公共安全局侦探们举行了一次会议，目的是讨论该罪行并交流对局势的看法。

亲属抵达

加屋的两名兄弟和一名五岁的儿子昨天乘坐长崎丸号抵达此处，以便将加屋的遗体运回其家乡千叶县。

三人抵达后，立即前往乍浦路的本国寺，悼念遇害者的亡灵。

加屋在日本还有另外两个年幼的儿子和他的妻子。

发表声明

加屋被杀一事在日本侨民中引起诸多议论。日本居留民团外交委员会周三发表声明称，由于凶手仍然在逃，引起了极大的不安。

公共安全局已增加了对许多日本人居住地区的巡逻力度。

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JULY 17, 1936

Verdict Today
In Nakayama
Case Uncertain

Official Sources Still
Say Judgment To
Be Rendered

Although denied in official quarters, reports that the First Special District Court will withhold its verdict today on the Nakayama case continued to gain currency last night.

From usually reliable sources, THE CHINA PRESS learned that the Court will re-open pleadings of the case, in which three accused, Yih Hai-sen (Hsiao Kwangtung), Tang Wen-tao, and Chou Shan-yung, are facing a charge for allegedly murdering Japanese Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama on the night of November 9, 1935 on Darroch Road.

Despite reports that judgment will be postponed, official sources insisted that when the Court comes to order this afternoon, the judges will deliver its ruling as scheduled. In keeping with ordinary procedure, the bulletin board of the First Special District Court yesterday listed the Nakayama case as one of the cases in which a verdict is pending today.

It was widely reported yesterday that the Japanese have made a demand for the conviction of at least two of the three accused. The demand further stated that in the judge's summary of the case he must point out that the motive for the murder is political, said yesterday's widely-circulated stories.

These reports could not be confirmed.

The two accused named in the alleged demand for conviction are understood to be Yih Hai-sen and Yang Wen-tao.

Japanese Press Warned

Meantime, Japanese official sources continued to make strong statements regarding the case. The local Japanese newspapers, the reporter learned, were yesterday ordered not to print any report on the verdict if it is given today. This order, originating from the office of the Consul-General, stated no reason for the news ban.

Rear-Admiral Eijiro Kondo, Commander of the Special Japanese Naval Landing Party, who conferred yesterday with leading residents of the local Japanese community on projected measures to defend the lives and property of Shanghai Nipponese, in a statement stated:

"The Nakayama case representing as it does an insult to the Imperial Navy, is the subject of deep indignation not only among the officers and men but among the people as well.

"By restraining our emotions and maintaining a calm attitude, we have waited the just action of the Chinese judiciary. However, should an attempt be made to bury the case, I fear that the imperial navy will be unable to watch such move in silence."

His statement was followed by this comment by the Foreign Relations Committee of the Japanese Residents Association, which said:

"All evidence in the Nakayama case convinces one that the defendants should be found guilty. We fear that a serious situation would be created by the failure of the Court to bring in a verdict to this effect."

These declarations were accompanied by the report yesterday that the Japanese Naval Landing Party has established five temporary patrol stations in different parts of the city. One of these was at the corner of Bubbling Well Road and Jessfield Road, where on the night of July 10, Kiyasu, Japanese independent broker was slain on the night of July 10.

Other patrol stations are scattered on Scott Road, Chapoo Road and one each in the Yangtsepoo and the Western district. A Japanese officer who gave this information was unable to say where the patrol quarters in Yangtsepoo and the Western district are located, but he admitted that these special stations have been set up.

Patrols Augmented

A visit to the Dixwell Road and Hongkew districts last night indicated that the Japanese Naval Landing Party patrols have been visibly augmented. But the residents in these areas, both Japanese and Chinese, were quiet.

Also, immediately around the place where Kiyasu was killed, Bureau of Public Safety police had put on several additional guards. In other places under its jurisdiction, the regular beat of one constable is being patrolled now by a party of several officers.

These Chinese policemen were making their rounds in the Chapel and Dixwell Road districts last night.

At the First Special District Court today, a large crowd of Chinese spectators and Japanese official and military men are expected to fill up the court room long before the session starts at 2 o'clock. Like in the previous hearings, tickets of admittance to the court will be issued to members of the general public who want to watch the proceedings.

（右侧手写批注及印章内容）
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE

《字林西报》，1936年7月17日，星期五

中山案
今日判决
尚不确定

官方消息源仍称
将如期作出
判决

尽管官方予以否认，但有关第一特区地方法院将在今日暂缓对中山案作出判决的报道昨晚继续流传。

《字林西报》从通常可靠的消息来源获悉，法院将重新开启该案辩论。该案中，三名被告乙海森（萧广东）、唐文涛（音译）和周山勇（音译）面临指控，涉嫌于1935年11月9日晚在达罗克路谋杀日本军曹中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）。

尽管有报道说判决将推迟，但官方消息人士坚持认为，当法院今天下午开庭时，法官将按计划宣读裁决。按照常规程序，第一特区地方法院的公告栏昨日将中山案列为今日待决判决的案件之一。

昨日广泛报道称，日本人要求至少判处三名被告中的两人有罪。据昨日广泛流传的说法，该要求还指出，法官在案件总结中必须指出谋杀动机是政治性的。

这些报道未能得到证实。

据信，所谓定罪要求中点名的两名被告是乙海森和杨文涛。

警告日本媒体

与此同时，日本官方继续就该案发表强硬声明。记者获悉，当地日本报纸昨日接到命令，如果今日宣判，不得刊登任何关于判决的报道。这项来自总领事馆的命令未说明新闻禁令的原因。

日本特别海军陆战队指挥官近藤英次郎少将（Eijiro Kondo）昨日与当地日本侨民领袖就保护上海日本人生命财产的拟定措施进行了磋商，他在一份声明中表示：

“中山案代表了对帝国海军的侮辱，不仅在官兵中，而且在民众中也引起了深深的愤慨。

“我们克制情绪，保持冷静态度，等待中国司法机关的公正行动。但是，如果有人试图掩盖此案，我担心帝国海军将无法对此类举动保持沉默。”

随后，日本居留民团外交委员会发表评论称：

“中山案的所有证据都使人确信被告应有罪。我们担心，如果法院未能作出此类判决，将会造成严重局势。”

伴随这些声明的是昨日的报道，称日本海军陆战队已在市内不同地点设立了五个临时巡逻站。其中一个位于静安寺路与极司菲尔路路口，7月10日晚，日本独立经纪人清须（Kiyasu，音译）在此被杀。

其他巡逻站分散在斯科特路、乍浦路，以及杨树浦区和西区各有一个。提供此信息的日本军官无法说明杨树浦区和西区巡逻站的具体位置，但他承认已设立这些特别站点。

加强巡逻

昨晚对狄思威路和虹口地区的走访表明，日本海军陆战队的巡逻力量明显增强。但这些地区的居民，无论是日本人还是中国人，都很安静。

此外，在清须被杀地点附近，公共安全局警察增派了几名警卫。在其管辖的其他地方，原本由一名警员负责的常规巡段，现在由几名警官组成的小组进行巡逻。

昨晚，这些中国警察在教堂区（Chapel，音译）和狄思威路地区巡逻。

预计今天在第一特区地方法院，大量中国旁听者以及日本官员和军人将在下午2点开庭前很久就挤满法庭。与之前的听证会一样，法院将向希望观看庭审过程的公众发放入场券。

（右侧手写批注及印章内容）
上海公共租界工部局警务处
特别分部登记处
S. D. 2023
1936年7月17日

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 16, 1936

Nakayama Case
Reopening Seen

Rumor Is Circulated
No Verdict Scheduled
For Tomorrow

While the assassin of Mr. Kosaku Kayau, shot and mortally wounded on Chi Mei Road on the night of July 10, is still at large and while a statement has been issued by the foreign relations committee of the Japanese Residents' Corporation to the effect that the shooting of the clerk would bring about "another Kayau case," the rumor that the "Nakayama Case" was going to reopen tomorrow and that no judgment would be handed down by Judge Chen Hung-nyish against Yih Hai-sen, alias Hsiao Kwang-tung, Yang Wen-tsao and Chow Hsia-yung, who have been standing trial for the murder of the Japanese marine on November 9 on Darroch Road, threw consternation into Japanese circles this morning.

While no direct confirmation of the news that no verdict will be given in the "Nakayama case" and that pleadings will again be resumed has yet been obtained the Shanghai Evening Post learned from authoritative sources this morning that "due to certain reasons" the case is almost certain to be reopened tomorrow morning.

All Surprised

A call to the office of the municipal advocate's revealed the fact that they were completely in the dark concerning the rumor. Mr G. R. Grove, attorney for the defense, expressed complete surprise when told over the phone this morning that the case may reopen once more, to allow further pleadings. The lawyer said that his latest information was to the effect that a verdict will be given. Another source denied the rumor saying that "Japanese pressure" would force a verdict.

Japanese officialdom was taking a keen interest in the verdict to be handed down in the Nakayama case and it is believed that they are awaiting the verdict in this case before bringing full pressure to bear on the Chinese authorities to find the murderer Of Kayau.

"Should Be Found

The Foreign Relations Committee of the Japanese Residents' Corporation, commenting yesterday on the Nakayama case are reported declaring that all evidence convinces one that the defendants should be found guilty.

"We fear that a serious situation would be created by the failure of the court to bring in a verdict to this effect."

Other Japanese circles sources continued to make strong statements concerning both the Nakayama and Kayau cases. One said:

Japanese Indignation

"The Nakayama case, involving as it does an officer of the Imperial Navy, is the cause of deep indignation not only among the officers and men in the service but among our people as well.

"By restraining our emotions and maintaining a calm attitude we have awaited the just action of the Chinese judiciary. However, should an attempt be made to bury this case, I fear that the Imperial Navy will be unable to watch such a move in silence.

"Under these circumstances, the Kayau case assumes an extremely serious aspect. It goes without saying that, if this case is regarded lightly, similar occurrences are bound to happen."

Requests Filed

Concerning the Kayau case, the Japanese Foreign Ministry has already filed formal requests with the Nanking government and the Greater Shanghai Municipality for the apprehension of the culprit as well as for the adoption of measures designed to safeguard Japanese lives and property.

Anticipating the possibility of an acquittal of the Chinese now being tried on charges of having assassinated Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama in Shanghai November 9 last, the Gaimusho has already instructed its representatives in China to take all necessary steps to cope with any possible development.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年7月16日，星期四

中山案
预计将重审

谣言流传
明日不宣判

尽管7月10日晚在集美路枪击并致加屋功作（Kosaku Kayau）先生重伤的刺客仍在逃，且日本居留民团外交委员会已发表声明称，此次枪击职员事件将引发“另一起加屋案”，但今晨日本各界因一则谣言而陷入恐慌。该谣言称，“中山案”将于明日重审，法官陈洪尼什（Chen Hung-nyish，音译）不会对因去年11月9日在达罗克路谋杀日本海军陆战队员而受审的易海森（Yih Hai-sen，别名萧广东 Hsiao Kwang-tung）、杨文藻（Yang Wen-tsao）和周夏荣（Chow Hsia-yung）作出判决。

虽然尚未获得关于“中山案”不予宣判并将恢复辩论这一消息的直接证实，但《上海晚邮报》今晨从权威人士处获悉，“出于某些原因”，该案几乎肯定将于明日上午重审。

各方惊讶

致电市公署检察官办公室后得知，他们对这一谣言完全不知情。辩护律师G. R. Grove先生在接到电话告知该案可能再次重审以允许进一步辩论时，表示完全惊讶。这位律师表示，他收到的最新消息是将会作出判决。另一消息来源否认了这一谣言，称“日本方面的压力”将迫使法院作出判决。

日本官方对即将在中山案中作出的判决极为关注，据信他们正等待此案的判决结果，然后再向中国当局施加全面压力，以缉拿加屋案的凶手。

“应被判有罪

据报道，日本居留民团外交委员会昨日就中山案发表评论时宣称，所有证据都使人确信被告应被判有罪。

“我们担心，如果法院未能作出此类判决，将会造成严峻局势。”

其他日本界人士继续就中山案和加屋案发表强硬言论。其中一人说：

日本人的愤慨

“中山案涉及一名帝国海军军官，这不仅引起服役官兵的深切愤慨，也引起我国民众的愤慨。

“我们克制情绪，保持冷静态度，等待中国司法界的公正行动。然而，如果有人试图掩盖此案，我担心帝国海军将无法对此保持沉默。

“在这种情况下，加屋案呈现出极其严重的局面。不言而喻，如果对此案掉以轻心，类似事件必将发生。”

已提出请求

关于加屋案，日本外务省已向南京政府和上海特别市政府正式提出请求，要求逮捕凶手，并采取旨在保护日本人生命财产的措施。

鉴于目前因被指控于去年11月9日在上海刺杀海军准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）而受审的中国人可能被无罪释放，外务省已指示其在华代表采取一切必要步骤，以应对任何可能的事态发展。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY 16, 1936

Japanese Diplomats Take
Serious View Of Likely
Nakayama Case Decision

“Ambiguous” Verdict Would Affect Diplomatic
Relations, Suma States; Naval Officials
Intimate Taking “Necessary Steps”

CHINESE POLICE TAKE MEASURES TO
PROTECT JAPANESE LIVES

A series of conferences was held by Japanese diplomats and naval officers yesterday in connection with the judgment to be delivered in the First Special District Court to-morrow morning on the three alleged slayers of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party. Mr. Y. Suma, Consul-General at Nanking, drew the attention of the Chinese authorities to the fact that an “ambiguous” verdict would seriously affect diplomatic relations between the two countries. Naval officials intimated that unless a verdict “justified by the defendants’ confessions and evidence” was given the Navy would take “all necessary steps.”

In the meantime the Chinese authorities had greatly increased their police patrols in all areas populated by Japanese and were working hard in an attempt to apprehend the slayer or slayers of Kayau who was murdered off Dirxwell Road on the night of July 10 the day that the Nakayama trial was concluded.

The judgment to be given to-morrow by the First Special District Court on the “Nakayama case,” yesterday monopolised the attention of local Japanese diplomatic and naval officials.

Mr. Shigeru Kawagoe, Ambassador to China, spent the entire morning and most of the afternoon conferring with Mr. Yakichiro Suma, Consul-General in Nanking, who arrived here on Tuesday night on a hurried summons from the envoy.

Mr. Suma, Domei learned, made a detailed report to Mr. Kawagoe regarding his interview with Mr. Hau Mo, Vice-Minister for Foreign Affairs, on July 12, during which he called the attention of the Chinese Government to the fact that an “ambiguous” verdict in the case would seriously affect the Sino-Japanese diplomatic relations.

No Doubt Of Guilty

The Consul-General told Mr. Hsu that the general tenor of the last session of the court, on July 10, was favourable to the two principal defendants, Yih Hai-sen and Yang Ven-tao, although there was “no doubt that they were guilty of the crime of which they were accused,” Domei learned.

Staff officers of the Third Fleet and the Special Naval Landing Party yesterday continued to confer on the possible verdict in the “Nakayama case.”

Naval officials intimated that if the First Special District Court fails to bring in a verdict “justified by the defendants’ confession and the evidence,” the Navy would take “all necessary steps,” foreshadowed in a statement issued on July 11 by Vice-Admiral Eijiro Kondo, Commander-in-chief of the Special Naval Landing Party.

May Take Steps

In his statement, issued in connection with the assassination of Mr. Kosaku Kayau, the officer declared that the Naval Landing Party may be “compelled to take steps it considers necessary at any time that it should find that the Chinese authorities lack the good faith or the ability to maintain order or to protect the lives and property of our residents.”

Recalling that eight months had elapsed since the murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama on Darroch Road, the statement remarked that the Chinese officials were “unable even to arrest the criminal. This had to be done by the Shanghai Municipal Council authorities.”

“In the course of the trial of the criminals, we had to serve several warnings upon the Chinese in view of their apparent failure to appreciate the seriousness of the case and to deal with the issue conscientiously and with the necessary care.”

Insult To Navy

“The Nakayama case, representing as it does an insult to the Imperial Navy, is the subject of deep indignation not only among the officers and men in the Service but among our people as well.

“By restraining our emotions and maintaining a calm attitude, we have awaited the just action of the Chinese judiciary. However, should an attempt be made to bury this case, I fear that the Imperial Navy will be unable to watch such a move in silence.

“Under these circumstances, the Kayau case assumes an extremely serious aspect. It goes without saying that, if this case is regarded lightly, similar occurrences are bound to happen. The Special Naval Landing Party, charged with the important duty of protecting Japanese lives and property finds itself unable to watch the situation with equanimity and sincerely hopes that the Chinese authorities will exhibit their good faith and speedily arrest the criminal,” the statement concluded.

Measures Taken

Measures taken by the Chinese authorities to protect the lives and property of Nipponese residents were described in a letter addressed by Mr. Yu Hung-chun, acting Mayor of Greater Shanghai, to Mr. Arata Sugihara, acting Consul-General here.

The letter, quoted in full in local Japanese papers, was dispatched in connection with the thus far fruitless search for the gunman, who, on the night of July 10, shot and mortally wounded Mr. Kosaku Kayau, seafood broker, on Chi Mei Road.

Since Mr. Kayau’s murder, the letter said, the Public Safety Bureau has assigned 167 specially trained constables to its North Station branch and sub-branches in the district.

These men, the communication added, have been since patrolling, in plain clothes and uniforms, the district most heavily inhabited by Japanese. Arrangements have also been made to increase the number of police officers, should necessity arise.

Eighteen detectives attached to the North Station branch, the letter continued, have been ordered to patrol North Szechuen, Scott, Darroch and Dixwell Roads, where the Japanese population is especially dense.

Four superintendents, the communication went on, have been detailed to the North Station branch to supervise its activities in safeguarding Japanese lives and conducting a search for Mr. Kayau’s murderer.

In accordance with a table submitted by the Japanese Consulate-General showing the distribution of Nipponese population in the city, the North Station branch and its sub-branches have divided their functions between themselves.

Arrangements have also been made, Mr. Yu’s letter concluded, to exchange information with the Shanghai Municipal police and Japanese authorities.

Japanese Dissatisfied

Dissatisfaction with the trial of the alleged assassins of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama now coming to its close at the First Special District Court was expressed in a resolution passed on Tuesday by the Seikokai Society, an organization composed of local Nipponese politicians and businessmen.

The resolution, according to the Shanghai “Nichi-Nichi,” also urged the local Nipponese authorities to keep a strict watch upon the attitude of the Chinese officials in disposing of the case.

The resolution was presented to the Japanese Consulate-General and the Naval Attache’s office yesterday morning. The delegation which submitted the document included Mr. Hachiro Hayashi, a member of the Council of the Japanese Residents’ Corporation, and Mr. Jutaro Aiuchi, Director of the Great Eastern Trading Company.

More than 40 “professional assassins” have arrived in the city recently on an errand from the South-Western authorities, the Shanghai “Mainichi” reported yesterday.

Rumours have been circulated by Japanese papers to the effect that a large party of “professional assassins” have arrived from the South-Western authorities in order to continue the killings but in a more subtle manner.

《字林西报》，1936年7月16日，星期四

日本外交官严肃看待
中山案可能的判决结果

须磨弥吉郎称“模棱两可”的判决将影响外交关系；
海军官员暗示将采取“必要步骤”

中国警方采取措施保护日本人生命安全

昨日，日本外交官和海军军官举行了一系列会议，讨论第一特区地方法院将于明日上午对涉嫌杀害日本海军特别陆战队准尉中山秀雄的三名凶手作出的判决。驻南京总领事须磨弥吉郎（Y. Suma）提请中国当局注意，“模棱两可”的判决将严重影响两国之间的外交关系。海军官员暗示，除非作出“由被告供词和证据证明正当”的判决，否则海军将采取“一切必要步骤”。

与此同时，中国当局在所有日本人居住区大幅增加了警察巡逻力度，并努力追捕于7月10日晚——即中山案审判结束之日——在狄克斯威尔路（Dirxwell Road）附近被谋杀的加屋的凶手。

第一特区地方法院将于明日对“中山案”作出的判决，昨日垄断了当地日本外交和海军官员的注意力。

驻华大使川越茂（Shigeru Kawagoe）整个上午和下午大部分时间都在与驻南京总领事须磨弥吉郎会谈，后者于周二晚奉特使之急召抵达此处。

据同盟社获悉，须磨先生向川越先生详细报告了他于7月12日会见外交部次长徐谟（Hau Mo，音译，注：此处原文为Hau Mo，对应历史人物应为徐谟或类似高官，按音译处理）的情况，期间他提请中国政府注意，此案中“模棱两可”的判决将严重影响中日外交关系。

无疑有罪

据同盟社获悉，总领事告诉徐先生，虽然“毫无疑问他们犯下了被指控的罪行”，但7月10日法庭最后一次庭审的总体倾向有利于两名主要被告易海森和杨文藻。

第三舰队和海军特别陆战队的参谋人员昨日继续就“中山案”可能的判决结果进行磋商。

海军官员暗示，如果第一特区地方法院未能作出“由被告供词和证据证明正当”的判决，海军将采取“一切必要步骤”，这与海军特别陆战队司令近藤英次郎（Eijiro Kondo）海军少将于7月11日发表的声明中所预示的内容一致。

可能采取行动

在该军官就加屋功作先生遇刺案发表的声明中，他宣称，如果海军特别陆战队发现中国当局缺乏维持秩序或保护我国居民生命财产的诚意或能力，“可能被迫随时采取其认为必要的步骤”。

声明回顾自去年11月9日中山秀雄准尉在达罗克路被谋杀以来已过去八个月，指出中国官员“甚至无法逮捕罪犯。这不得不由上海公共租界工部局当局来完成。”

“在审判罪犯的过程中，鉴于他们显然未能认识到案件的严重性，并未认真谨慎地处理此事，我们不得不向中方发出数次警告。”

对海军的侮辱

“中山案代表着对帝国海军的侮辱，这不仅引起服役官兵的深切愤慨，也引起我国民众的愤慨。

“我们克制情绪，保持冷静态度，等待中国司法界的公正行动。然而，如果有人试图掩盖此案，我担心帝国海军将无法对此保持沉默。

“在这种情况下，加屋案呈现出极其严重的局面。不言而喻，如果对此案掉以轻心，类似事件必将发生。负有保护日本人生命财产重要职责的海军特别陆战队发现自己无法平静地注视局势，并真诚希望中国当局表现出诚意，迅速逮捕罪犯，”声明最后说道。

已采取措施

上海特别市代理市长俞鸿钧（Yu Hung-chun）致驻沪代理总领事杉原荒太（Arata Sugihara）的信中，描述了中国当局为保护日本居民生命财产所采取的措施。

这封信被当地日文报纸全文引用，是针对至今未果的搜捕行动而发出的，枪手于7月10日晚在集美路枪击海鲜经纪人加屋功作先生并致其重伤。

信中说，自加屋先生被谋杀以来，公安局已向其北站分局及该地区各分所派遣了167名经过专门训练的警员。

信函补充说，这些人此后一直便衣和着装混合巡逻日本人最密集的地区。还已作出安排，如有必要，增加警力。

信中还提到，隶属于北站分局的18名侦探已受命巡逻北四川路、斯科特路（Scott Road）、达罗克路和狄克斯威尔路，这些地区日本人口尤其密集。

信函接着说，已指派四名督察前往北站分局，监督其保护日本人生命安全和搜寻加屋凶手的活动。

根据日本总领事馆提交的城市日本人口分布表，北站分局及其分所已在彼此之间划分了职能。

俞先生的信最后总结道，还已作出安排，与上海公共租界警务处和日本当局交换情报。

日本人不满

对于涉嫌刺杀海军准尉中山秀雄的审判在第一特区地方法院即将结束之际，由当地日本政治家和商人组成的精国会（Seikokai Society，音译）在周二通过的一项决议中表达了不满。

据上海《日日新闻》报道，该决议还敦促当地日本当局密切关注中国官员处理此案的态度。

该决议于昨日上午提交给日本总领事馆和海军武官处。提交文件的代表团包括日本居留民团评议员林八郎（Hachiro Hayashi）和大东贸易公司董事相内寿太郎（Jutaro Aiuchi）。

据上海《每日新闻》昨日报道，最近有40多名“职业刺客”奉西南当局之命抵达本市。

日本报纸流传着这样的谣言：一大群“职业刺客”已从西南当局抵达，以便以更隐蔽的方式继续实施杀戮。

KAYAU MURDER CASE
INVESTIGATION

While officers of the Bureau of Public Safety, the Settlement Police, and the Japanese Consular Police are sparing no efforts in their investigation of the murder of Mr. Kosaku Kayau, a Japanese sea-food broker, in Chi Mei Road, on July 10, adequate measures have been devised by the Chinese Police for the protection of foreign residents in Chinese territory, especially in Chapel. A meeting of inspectors in charge of various police sub-stations in Chapel was held yesterday afternoon, when details concerning police patrols and guards in areas where foreigners live were reported. Maps showing the houses in which foreigners reside were displayed at the meeting, and it is understood that police posts in these areas already have been doubled.

Neither the weapon used in the crime nor the cartridge case have been found yet. A high police officer, interviewed by a representative of the "North-China Daily News," explained that in the case of certain weapons, the empty cartridge case remains in the pistol after the shooting until it is ejected by the user. This probably explains the absence of the empty cartridge case on the scene of the killing.

Settlement Police, who are assisting the Chinese Police in the investigation, have assigned additional officers to the work, and are co-operating with the Chinese Police in every way.

The statements of two rickshaw pullers are being examined by the Chinese Police, but it is reported that no valuable clue has been obtained from either of them. According to a Japanese report, the two pullers, Chen Lung-chuang and Liu Keu-ken, told the police they reside in Chi Mei Road. Both thought the Japanese was drunk. They saw no blood. One of the pullers conveyed Mr. Kayau's body, another a Japanese woman, to the Fooming Hospital, where some five hours later the victim succumbed to his wounds.

Settlement Police Thanked

Mr. Hidenari Terazaki, Japanese Consul, yesterday called on M.M. Baudez, the French Consul-General, to ask for the protection of Japanese residents in the French Concession and to acquaint him with details of the Kayau case. Mr. Masusaburo Amano, President of the Japanese Residents Corporation, called on Mr. A. Tajima and Mr. S. Uyehara, respectively Deputy Commissioner and Assistant Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police, to thank them for the prompt measures taken by the S.M.P. for the apprehension of the assassin of Mr. Kayau.

Mr. Hikaru Kondo, Chairman of the Federation of the Amalgamated Japanese Street Unions, presented to Mr. Bughara, acting Consul-General, a copy of the resolution adopted by that body on Monday afternoon. The resolution urged the local Japanese Consulate-General to approach the Nanking Government with a request for the safeguarding of peace and order in Shanghai.

《华北日报》，1936年7月15日，星期三

外籍居民获保护

中国警方制定充分措施

加纳庸谋杀案调查

尽管公共租界工部局警务处、租界警察和日本领事馆警察正不遗余力地调查7月10日发生在集美路（Chi Mei Road）的日本海鲜经纪人加纳庸（Kosaku Kayau）谋杀案，但中国警方已为保护在中国领土上的外籍居民制定了充分措施，尤其是在闸北（Chapel，原文误拼，应为Chapei/闸北）。昨日下午召开了负责闸北各警察分署的督察会议，会上通报了关于外籍人士居住区域的巡逻和警卫细节。会议上展示了标有外籍人士居住房屋的地图，据悉这些地区的警察岗哨已经加倍。

作案使用的武器和弹壳尚未找到。一位接受《华北日报》记者采访的高级警官解释说，对于某些武器，空弹壳在射击后会留在手枪内，直到使用者将其退出。这大概解释了凶案现场没有空弹壳的原因。

协助中国警方调查的租界警察已增派人员投入此项工作，并在各方面与中国警方合作。

中国警方正在审查两名黄包车夫的证词，但据报道未从他们那里获得任何有价值的线索。据一份日本方面的报告，这两名车夫陈龙庄（Chen Lung-chuang，音译）和刘狗根（Liu Keu-ken，音译）告诉警方他们居住在集美路。两人都认为那名日本人是喝醉了。他们没有看到血迹。其中一名车夫将加纳先生的尸体送往福民医院（Fooming Hospital），另一名则送了一名日本妇女前往，受害者在约五小时后因伤重不治身亡。

感谢租界警察

日本领事寺崎英成（Hidenari Terazaki）昨日拜访法国总领事鲍德兹（M.M. Baudez），请求保护法租界内的日本居民，并向其通报加纳案的细节。日本居留民团团长天野益三郎（Masusaburo Amano）拜访了上海公共租界工部局警务处副总巡官田岛（A. Tajima，音译）和助理副总巡官上原（S. Uyehara，音译），感谢工部局警务处为缉拿加纳先生凶手所采取的迅速措施。

日本各街道工会联合会主席近藤光（Hikaru Kondo，音译）向代理总领事布加拉（Bughara，音译）递交了该机构周一下午通过的决议副本。该决议敦促当地日本总领事馆向南京政府提出要求，以维护上海的和平与秩序。

July 15, 1936. Morning Translation.

NICHI-NICHI

THE NAKAYAMA CASE

At 6 p.m. yesterday a Japanese organization known as the "Seiko Society" held a meeting at the Japanese Club to consider the Nakayama and the Kayau cases.

The meeting decided to urge the Japanese authorities to keep a close watch on the attitude of the Chinese authorities in connection with the Nakayama and the Kayau cases because Japanese lives are in danger and the Chinese judiciary is unreliable.

At 9.30 p.m. July 15 officers of the Society will call on the Japanese Consular authorities and the Japanese Naval Attache's office to convey to them their decision.

MAINICHI

Yang Ven Tao and the Blue Shirts Society.

It has been ascertained that Yang Ven Tao was at one time connected with the Blue Shirts Society. In 1933 prior to the Fukien incident, Yang Ven Tao had, together with Tsu Tso Ven and Mei Kwang Pei, planned to unify all the Red Fangs throughout China. Mayor Wu of the Shanghai City Government submitted a report to the Nanking Government on their activities and issued a warrant for their arrest. Consequently Mei Kwang Pei was arrested and sent to Nanking, while Yang Ven Tao and Tsu Tso Ven ran away to Canton and Hongkong respectively. Later Yang Ven tao and Tsu Tso Ven took part in an abortive independence movement in Fukien. Tsu Tso Ven was arrested by General Chen Chi Tang and Yang Ven Tao was engaged as a spy for the Nanking Government to secure information regarding the movements of important officials in Fukien and Canton. Chiang Kai Shek instructed the Blue Shirts in Canton to co-operate with Yang Ven Tao. The Tong Jen Association in Shanghai, which is under the control of Yang Ven Tao, co-operated with the Blue Shirts and certain members of the Association received their pay from the Blue Shirts. The Social Bureau of the Shanghai City Government issued an arms license to Yang Ven Tao for some other reason than that because he was connected with the 19th Route army.

The Chi Mei Road murder case.

Yesterday morning Mr. Hayashi, honorary chairman of the Japanese Amalgamated Association of Street Unions, accompanied by other committeemen, called on Mr. Sugihara, acting Japanese Consul-General, and handed him the resolution passed by the Association.

The Acting Consul-General informed Mr. Hayashi that the Chinese authorities will issue another order to the Chinese people to maintain good relations with neighbouring countries. He also reported the conversation he had with Mr. O. K. Yu, Secretary of the Shanghai City Government.

1936年7月15日。晨间译文。

《日日新闻》

中山案

昨晚6时，一个名为“精义会”（Seiko Society，音译）的日本组织在日本俱乐部举行会议，审议中山案和加纳案。

会议决定敦促日本当局密切关注中国当局在中山案和加纳案上的态度，因为日本人的生命处于危险之中，且中国司法不可靠。

7月15日晚9时30分，该会干部将拜访日本领事当局和日本海军武官处，传达他们的决定。

《每日新闻》

杨文藻与蓝衣社。

经查明，杨文藻曾一度与蓝衣社有关联。1933年福建事变之前，杨文藻曾与朱佐文（Tsu Tso Ven，音译）和梅光沛（Mei Kwang Pei，音译）策划统一全中国的红帮（Red Fangs，即洪门/洪帮）。上海市政府吴市长就他们的活动向南京政府提交报告，并签发逮捕令。结果梅光沛被捕并被送往南京，而杨文藻和朱佐文分别逃往广州和香港。后来杨文藻和朱佐文参与了福建未遂的独立运动。朱佐文被陈济棠将军逮捕，杨文藻则受聘为南京政府间谍，以获取关于福建和广东重要官员动向的情报。蒋介石指示在广州的蓝衣社与杨文藻合作。由杨文藻控制的上海同仁协会（Tong Jen Association，音译）与蓝衣社合作，该协会部分成员的薪俸由蓝衣社支付。上海市政府社会局出于与第十九路军无关的其他原因，向杨文藻颁发了枪支许可证。

集美路谋杀案。

昨天上午，日本街道工会联合会名誉主席林先生（Hayashi，音译）在其他委员的陪同下，拜访了日本代理总领事杉原（Sugihara，音译），并向其递交了该联合会通过的决议。

代理总领事告知林先生，中国当局将再次向中国人民发布命令，要求与邻国保持良好关系。他还报告了与上海市政府秘书长余鸿钧（O. K. Yu，音译）的谈话内容。

July 14, 1936.
Morning Translation.

MAINICHI

THE NAKAYAMA CASE AND THE CHI MEI ROAD CASE:
WARNING TO CITY GOVERNMENT.

All parties concerned are paying close attention to the last hearing of the Nakayama case because the Chinese authorities seem to be adopting a most insincere attitude in the case.
The public is being led to believe that the Chi Mei Road murder has some connection with the Nakayama case. Yang Ven Tao and Yih Hai Sung are reported to be also involved in the attempted murder of Wang Ching Wei and in the murder of Tang Yu Jen. For this reason, the judgment to be handed down by the Court in the Nakayama case is being awaited with exceptional interest. Should the accused be found not guilty, in accordance with the views of Procurator Chang, all the parties concerned will regard the matter as serious and a grave situation will arise.
On the morning of July 13 Acting Consul-General Sugihara held a conference with Japanese naval authorities.
At 2 p.m. he called on Mr. O.K. Yu, Acting Mayor of the Shanghai City Government, and informed him that should the accused in the Nakayama case be found not guilty, serious situation would be created. He further warned that the Chinese Judges should act justly. The Acting Consul-General then drew Mr. Yu's attention to the seriousness of the Chi Mei Road incident.

Suspicious Attitude of the Court and Bureau of Public Safety in Nakayama Case.

The attitude of the Chinese authorities in the Nakayama case is being criticized on the following grounds :-
(1) The insincerity of the Bureau of Public Safety in the investigations into the Nakayama case.
(2) The attitude of the Court in disregarding, without reason, the scientific evidence and witnesses submitted by the Municipal authorities.
(3) Procurator Chang's reckless arguments.
With the exception of two or three reports, the Bureau of Public Safety had forwarded no further information to the Japanese Landing Party regarding its investigations into the Nakayama case, whilst, on the other hand, the Municipal authorities kept in close touch with the Landing Party and informed it of all developments in its investigations. The Bureau of Public Safety kept the S.M.P. officers waiting several hours when the latter called at the Bureau to secure assistance in searching the homes of suspects in the Nakayama incident. This action is very suspicious.
In the past, the Court used to accept everything submitted by the Identification Department of the S.M.C., but in the Nakayama case the Court referred the exhibits of the S.M.C. to the Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory for further examination. 晨间译文。

《每日新闻》

中山案与集美路案：
对市政府的警告。

各方正密切关注中山案的最后一次庭审，因为中国当局在此案中似乎采取了极不真诚的态度。
公众被引导相信，集美路谋杀案与中山案存在某种关联。据报道，杨又道（Yang Ven Tao）和易海松（Yih Hai Sung）也参与了刺杀汪精卫未遂案以及唐玉珍（Tang Yu Jen）谋杀案。因此，人们以极大的兴趣等待法院在中山案中作出的判决。如果按照张检察官的观点宣判被告无罪，所有相关方都将视此事为严重问题，并将引发严峻局势。
7月13日上午，代理总领事杉原与日本海军当局举行了会议。
下午2时，他拜访了上海市政府代理市长俞鸿钧先生（Mr. O.K. Yu），并告知他，如果中山案的被告被宣判无罪，将会造成严峻局势。他进一步警告称，中国法官应当公正行事。随后，代理总领事提请俞先生注意集美路事件的严重性。

法院与公安局在中山案中的可疑态度。

中国当局在中山案中的态度因以下原因受到批评：
(1) 公安局在调查中山案过程中缺乏诚意。
(2) 法院毫无理由地无视工部局当局提交的科学证据和证人证言。
(3) 张检察官的鲁莽辩词。
除了两三份报告外，公安局未就其中山案的调查情况向日本登陆部队提供进一步信息，而另一方面，工部局当局则与登陆部队保持密切联系，并向其通报调查的所有进展。当工部局警务处（S.M.P.）警官前往公安局寻求协助搜查中山案嫌疑人的住所时，公安局让警官们等候了数小时。这一举动非常可疑。
过去，法院通常接受工部局巡捕房识别科提交的所有材料，但在中山案中，法院将工部局的证物送交陈居法医实验室进行进一步检验。关于物理学书籍与杨又道之间的联系，法院

rejected the evidence already established without definite
proof to the contrary. This shows that the Court was
adopting an unnecessarily offensive attitude towards the
Municipal Identification Department.
Procurator Chang attempted to
establish the innocence of the accused at the last hearing
by rejecting the connection between the book on physics and
Yang Ven Tao on the ground of lack of evidence.

Biography of Yih Hai Sung.

Yih Hai Sung alias Siao Kwangtung,
aged 27, who is being charged in connection with the Nakayama
case, was born in Canton and brought up in Shanghai. When
17 years old, he became a follower of Yang Ven Tao, the
leader of the San Huh Association. During the Sino-Japanese
hostilities in Shanghai, Yih was very active as a member of
the Dare-to-Die Corps of the 19th Route Army. He also
became a powerful member of the Iron and Blood Corps. When
the People's Revolutionary Government was established in
Fokien in 1933, Yih organized a plain clothes corps and was
appointed Battalion Commander by General Chen Ming Shu. On
the night of January 3 of the following year, he was arrested
together with six others by officers of the Public Safety
Bureau and the Garrison Commissioner's Headquarters as they
were holding a secret meeting at the Moon Palace. In April
he was released through the good offices of Yang Ven Tao.
It has been ascertained that the assassination of Wang Ching
Wei, Nakayama and Tang Yu Jen was the work of the same
clique.

Chinese Throw Stones At Japanese Naval Officer
On Dixwell Road.

Acts of insult towards Japanese by
Chinese are of daily occurrence.
At 9.50 a.m. July 13 several Chinese
loafers approached a motor car carrying Captain Tsukamoto of
the Flagship "Idzumo" and used abusive language towards the
officer and threw a stone at him. The incident occurred
near the Chuwa Apartments on Dixwell Road. The stone dropped
near the foot of the driver of the motor car. The officer
alighted and gave chase after the Chinese who disappeared
in the crowd. The stone was thrown from Chinese controlled
territory. This cannot be regarded as a mischievous
prank on the part of ignorant Chinese because it was done
after the loafers had ascertained the number of the motor
car. It is an insult to the Japanese Imperial Navy.

Chinese Youth Throws Stone at Aged Japanese.

At 9 a.m. July 13 a Chinese of
18 years of age threw a stone at a Japanese of 60 years of
age as he was passing the Jukong Road Market in a ricksha.
The Japanese was unhurt.
S. Akamatsu, proprietor of a shop
at the corner of Woosung Road and Haining Road, who observed
the incident, informed Chapel policeman No. 2485 who was on
duty in the vicinity, but the officer did nothing. Mr.

张检察官试图在最后一次庭审中通过以缺乏证据为由驳回物理学书籍与杨又道之间的联系，来确立被告的清白。

易海松生平简介。

易海松，别名小广东，现年27岁，因涉及中山案而被起诉，出生于广州，在上海长大。17岁时，他成为三合会首领杨又道的追随者。在上海的中日冲突期间，易作为第十九路军敢死队成员表现活跃。他还成为了铁血团的一名有力成员。1933年福建成立人民政府时，易组织了一支便衣队，并被陈铭枢将军任命为营长。次年1月3日晚，他在月宫举行秘密会议时，与另外六人一起被公安局和淞沪警备司令部的官员逮捕。4月，经杨又道斡旋获释。
现已查明，刺杀汪精卫、中山以及唐玉珍系同一帮派所为。

中国人在狄思威路向日本海军军官投掷石块

中国人侮辱日本人的事件每日都在发生。
7月13日上午9时50分，几名中国闲散人员接近一辆载有旗舰“出云”号塚本大尉的汽车，对该军官使用辱骂性语言并向其投掷石块。事件发生在狄思威路中和公寓附近。石块落在汽车司机脚边附近。该军官下车追赶那些消失在人群中的中国人。石块是从华人控制区域投掷出来的。这不能被视为无知中国人的恶作剧，因为这些闲散人员在行动前已查明了汽车号码。这是对日本帝国海军的侮辱。

中国青年向年迈日本人投掷石块

7月13日上午9时，一名18岁的中国人在一名60岁的日本人乘坐人力车经过菊恭路市场时，向其投掷石块。该日本人未受伤。
吴淞路与海宁路拐角处一家店铺的店主S. Akamatsu（音译）目睹了这一事件，通知了在附近执勤的2485号教堂巡捕，但该警官未采取任何行动。先生。

July 14, 1936. Afternoon translation.

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE : KWANGTUNG CLUB ISSUES NOTICE

The Kwangtung Club publishes the following
urgent notice in the "Shun Pao" and other local newspapers:-
According to a report in yesterday's local
newspapers of the trial of the accused charged with the
murder of the Japanese Marine Nakayama, it is stated that
a Portuguese witness gave evidence that he met Yang Yung
Tao (楊又道) at our club several years ago. We are
exceedingly surprised over this statement. The Club has
no member bearing the name of Yan Yung Tao nor has any
Portuguese come to this Club for a talk. To avoid
misunderstanding, we hereby publish this notice for the
information of the public.

中山谋杀案：广东俱乐部发布通告

广东俱乐部在《申报》及其他本地报纸上发布如下紧急通告：
据昨日本地报纸关于被控谋杀日本海军陆战队员中山的被告庭审报道，称有一名葡萄牙证人作证说，几年前曾在我们的俱乐部见过杨又道（楊又道）。我们对这一说法感到极为惊讶。本俱乐部没有名为杨又道的会员，也没有任何葡萄牙人来过本俱乐部交谈。为避免误解，特此发布本通告，以告公众。

pages.en:
July 14, 1936.
Afternoon Translation.

MAINI CHI

YANG VEN TAO, PROFESSIONAL MURDERER, HAS A THOUSAND
FOLLOWERS.

Yang Ven Tao, age 42, who is now being
charged with having instigated the murder of the Japanese
marine Nakayama, was brought up by his grandfather. His
father died when he was an infant. He was engaged in various
trades before he secured employment with Butterfield & Swire
in Shanghai as a tallyman. After the Manchurian incident,
he organized the Hung Shun Association with Cantonese workers.
As President of the Association, he collected strong anti-
Japanese elements and secured about a thousand followers.
Through the good offices of the Kuomintang, he obtained
from the Social Bureau permission for the organization of
the Association. He was appointed Councillor to the
North-East Volunteer Army in the 22nd year of the Republic
(1933). He served in the 19th Route Army as an advisor
during the Sino-Japanese hostilities in Shanghai and it was
then that he secured the pistol used in the murder of Nakayama.
After the hostilities, he ran away to Fokien Province where
he was actively engaged in an anti-Chiang Kai Shek movement.
It is said that the Nanking Government had issued a secret
warrant for the arrest of Yang Ven Tao because of his anti-
Chiang Kai Shek activities in Fokien and Shanghai. He later
participated in the establishment of the People's Government
in Amoy, whence he proceeded to Hongkong in company with
General Chen Ming Chu where he held a conference with the
persons connected with the 19th Route Army to consider an
attack on the Nanking Government. Later, he secured an
understanding with the Nanking Government and came to
Shanghai and organized the Dong Zung Association with a
large sum of money which he had obtained from persons
connected with the 19th Route Army. It was Yang Ven Tao who
planned the assassination of Wang Ching Wei and the creation
of disturbances in Shanghai.

Arrest of Yih Hai Sung.

Yih Hai Sung's arrest was effected
in Tsingtao by Detective Inspector Nakamura and Detective
Sergeant Tanaka of the Special Political Office of the
S.M.P.

When the two officers raided Yih's
home they found a secret passage in the ceiling leading to
a room under the ground. Yih's arrest was made in that room.
Upon being arrested, Yih asked whether he was being taken to
Dixwell Road Station.

The Secret Organization known as "San Huh Association":
Lawyer Kuh a member.

The San Huh Association of which
Yang Ven Tao and Yih Hai Sung are members has great influence.
It consists of various Cantonese secret organizations. Lawyer
Kuh, who is defending Yang Ven Tao, is also a member of the
Association. As regards the San Huh Association, the late

《每日新闻》

职业杀手杨又道拥有千名追随者。

现年42岁的杨又道，目前被指控煽动谋杀日本海军陆战队员中山，由祖父抚养长大。他在婴儿时期父亲去世。在受雇于上海太古洋行担任理货员之前，他曾从事各种行业。九一八事变后，他与广东工人组织了洪顺协会。作为协会主席，他汇集了强烈的反日分子，并获得了约一千名追随者。通过国民党的斡旋，他从社会局获得了组织该协会的许可。民国二十二年（1933年），他被任命为东北义勇军顾问。在上海中日冲突期间，他在第十九路军担任顾问，正是在那时他获得了用于谋杀中山的手枪。冲突结束后，他逃往福建省，在那里积极参与反蒋介石运动。据说，南京政府因杨又道在福建和上海的反蒋活动，已发出秘密逮捕令。后来，他参与了在厦门建立人民政府的活动，随后与陈铭枢将军一同前往香港，与第十九路军相关人员举行会议，商讨进攻南京政府的事宜。后来，他与南京政府达成谅解，来到上海，并利用从第十九路军相关人员那里获得的大笔资金组织了东纵协会。策划刺杀汪精卫并在上海制造骚乱的正是杨又道。

易海松被捕。

易海松是在青岛被工部局警务处特别政治股的中村督察官和田中警佐逮捕的。

当两名警官突袭易的住所时，他们在天花板中发现了一条通往地下房间的密道。易就是在该房间被捕的。被捕时，易询问是否要将他带往狄思威路巡捕房。

被称为“三合会”的秘密组织：
顾律师是成员。

杨又道和易海松所属的三合会影响力巨大。它由各种广东秘密组织组成。为杨又道辩护的顾律师也是该协会的成员。关于三合会，已故

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. M. REGISTRY.
No. D_______
Date ___/___/___

July 14, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

- 2 -

Dr. Sun Yat Sen stated in one part of his book on China's political and diplomatic policy that his life was linked with the fate of the San Huh Association.
This Association has a long history. It has a huge number of persons as members and concerns itself with political activities behind the scenes. In the United States it is known as the Chi Kung Party and is regarded as a most powerful organization. No unauthorized person will be able to join the Association without being detected. The Association is a very powerful anti-Japanese body. Yang Ven Tao is a leader of one of the various parties in the Association. Yih Hai Sung is one of Yang Ven Tao's followers. For this reason, Yih Hai Sung is in a position to execute any order issued by the Association. It is not difficult to tell what part the San Huh Association played in the Nakayama murder.

Threatening Letter to Japanese.

At the beginning the Chinese authorities propagated that the Nakayama murder was an act of private vengeance. As a result of their investigations, the Japanese authorities discovered that the assassination was a political affair. Following the arrest of the accused, the Tung Yih Association and other secret organizations sent threatening letters to the Japanese authorities. A certain Chinese who gave important information has since changed his nationality to Japanese. Much difficulty was experienced in giving protection to important witnesses.

The Canton Fellow Countrymen's Association Actively Engaged in trying to save Yang Ven Tao.

It is reported that following the arrest of Yang Ven Tao and Yih Hai Sung, the Canton Fellow Countrymen's Association, No. 16 Tuh Shing Lee, Boone Road, organized a body known as the "Society to save Yang Ven Tao". The Canton Fellow Countrymen's Association is a very powerful anti-Japanese organization. After the first hearing of the case on May 1, the officers of the Association held several conferences at which a large number of representatives of secret organizations, including Lee Dah Chao and Koh Shun of the Shanghai City Government, were present to consider ways and means to save Yang Ven Tao. The presence of important officials at the conference shows that the accused in the Nakayama case are important figures in politics.
As a result of the conference a movement was started to induce, through the good offices of high Chinese officials, Chiang Kai Shek, Mayor Wu of the Shanghai City Government and the Judges of the Court to save the accused. The reason advanced by the Association for its movement is that Yang Ven Tao is a good man.

Chinese Students Distribute Anti-Japanese Handbills On Nanking Road and Clash with Police Officers.

At 3 p.m. July 12 (?) about one hundred Chinese students assembled on Nanking Road near the New World and distributed anti-Japanese handbills and shouted anti-Japanese slogans. They clashed with the Police as they were proceeding towards Thibet Road, several Police officers were injured. About 15 of them, who appeared to be leaders, were arrested by the Police.

上海公共租界工部局警务处
S. M. 登记处。
编号 D_______
日期 ___/___/___

1936年7月14日。下午译件。

- 2 -

孙中山博士在其关于中国政治与外交政策的著作中某处指出，他的一生与三合会（San Huh Association）的命运紧密相连。
该会历史悠久，成员众多，从事幕后政治活动。在美国，它被称为致公党（Chi Kung Party），被视为一个极具实力的组织。未经认可者无法在不被察觉的情况下加入该会。该会是一个势力强大的反日团体。杨文道（Yang Ven Tao）是该会内各派系之一的领袖。易海松（Yih Hai Sung，音译）是杨文道的追随者之一。因此，易海松有能力执行该会发出的任何命令。不难看出三合会在中山（Nakayama）谋杀案中扮演了什么角色。

给日本人的恐吓信。

起初，中国当局宣称中山谋杀案是一起私人复仇行为。经过调查，日本当局发现这起暗杀是一起政治事件。在被告被捕后，同益会（Tung Yih Association，音译）及其他秘密社团向日本当局发送了恐吓信。一名提供重要情报的中国人此后已归化日本国籍。在保护重要证人方面遇到了极大困难。

广东同乡会积极致力于营救杨文道。

据报道，在杨文道和易海松被捕后，位于博恩路（Boone Road）土山路16号（Tuh Shing Lee, No. 16，音译）的广东同乡会组织了一个名为“救杨委员会”的团体。广东同乡会是一个势力强大的反日组织。在5月1日案件首次聆讯后，该会干事举行了多次会议，包括上海市政府的李达朝（Lee Dah Chao，音译）和葛顺（Koh Shun，音译）在内的大量秘密社团代表出席会议，商讨营救杨文道的方法。重要官员出席会议表明，中山案的被告在政界是重要人物。
会议结果发起了一场运动，试图通过中国高官、上海市政府吴市长以及法院法官的斡旋来营救被告。该会为其运动提出的理由是杨文道是个好人。

中国学生在南京路分发反日传单并与警察发生冲突。

7月12日（？）下午3时左右，约一百名中国学生聚集在新世界附近的南京路上，分发反日传单并高呼反日口号。当他们向西藏路（Thibet Road）行进时与警察发生冲突，数名警员受伤。其中约15名看似为首者被警方逮捕。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 8, 1936

7073
9 7-8

New Evidence
Expected In
Nakayama Trial

Hearing Of Murder
Case To Be Resum-
ed Today

Major developments beneficial to
the defense are anticipated in the
First Special District Court this
afternoon when the hearing of the
Nakayama murder case is scheduled
to be resumed.

It is understood that reports from
the Judicial Laboratory at Chenju,
which was assigned to study some
of the exhibits concerning the case,
will be revealed during the hearing.

The reports, according to Chinese
sources, will contradict the confes-
sions made by Yih Hai-sen, better
known as "Hsiao Kwangtung," and
among other things will attempt to
disclose that Hideo Nakayama, of
the Japanese Naval Landing Party,
who lost his life on Darroch Road,
November 9, 1935, was shot at close
range.

Yih Hai-sen, in one of his earlier
confessions, stated that he shot
Nakayama from about five feet be-
hind the man. This statement was
later retracted, but despite this it is
understood that the Judicial Labora-
tory will venture the opinion that
even if it is to be taken into consi-
deration, there is some mistake,
since the man was shot at close
range.

Another revelation expected to be
made has to do with fingerprints
on the book which was used to hide
the death gun. It is stated that no
fingerprints of Yang Wen-tao, ac-
cused with Yih, have been found
although fingerprints of other per-
sons have been discovered.

While no definite statement has
been made to that effect, it is re-
ported that "Jack, the Korean,"
who was arrested by Japanese au-
thorities on the grounds that he was
involved in the shooting, may ap-
pear in court today. This is far
from certain, however. Reports that
the Korean would be brought into
court have been circulated on nu-
merous occasions and up to the pre-
sent time, he has failed to appear,
usually because of illness.

The fourth accused man in con-
nection with the slaying of Naka-
yama is Chow Sha-yung, manager
of a Ningpo Road cabaret.

《字林西报》，1936年7月8日，星期三

7073
9 7-8

预计中山案审判
将出现新证据

谋杀案聆讯
今日恢复

预计今天下午在第一特区法院恢复中山谋杀案聆讯时，将出现有利于辩方的重大进展。

据悉，受命研究该案部分物证的陈居（Chenju，音译）司法实验室的报告将在聆讯期间公布。

据中方消息人士称，这些报告将与易海森（Yih Hai-sen，即广为人知的“小广东”）所作的供词相矛盾，并将试图披露其他事项，其中包括1935年11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）丧生的日本海军陆战队队员中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）是在近距离被枪杀的。

易海森在早期的一份供词中称，他在距离受害者身后约五英尺处开枪射击中山。这一说法后来被撤回，但尽管如此，据悉司法实验室将提出意见认为，即使考虑到这一点，也存在某些错误，因为死者是在近距离被枪杀的。

另一项预期披露的内容涉及用于藏匿作案手枪的书本上的指纹。据说，虽然发现了其他人的指纹，但未发现与易一同被指控的杨文道（Yang Wen-tao）的指纹。

虽然尚未就此作出明确声明，但有报道称，因涉嫌参与枪击案而被日本当局逮捕的“朝鲜人杰克”（Jack, the Korean）今天可能会出庭。但这远非定论。关于该朝鲜人将被带上法庭的报道已多次流传，但截至目前，他通常因病未能出庭。

与中山被杀案有关的第四名被告是宁波路一家歌舞厅的经理周少庸（Chow Sha-yung，音译）。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 17, 1936

YIH HAI-SEN MEMBER
OF "AXE CORPS"

Tsingtao Visit Made Public at
Nakayama Trial

COURT AWAITS JUDICIAL
LABORATORY REPORT

Yih Hai-sen, alias "Little Canton-
ese," one of the three men now held
by the police on the charge of the
murder of H. Nakayama, a Japanese
marine, on November 9 last, had
connections with a loafer gang known
as the "Axe Corps," according to a
statement made by Mr. T. S. Lea,
Assistant Municipal Advocate, in the
First Special District Court, yester-
day.
Yih admitted that he was arrested
by the Chinese military in 1934, but
said he and all the others were re-
leased after being detained for over a
month, as there was no evidence
against them.
The result of a visit paid to Tsing-
tao by police detectives was un-
folded before the Court by Det.-Sub-
Inspr. Crowther, of Dixwell Road
Station, who produced a suit of dark
blue foreign-style clothing, a photo
of Yih Hai-sen, and a letter, all of
which he obtained in Tsingtao with
the assistance of the Public Safety
Bureau there. Witness said it was
seen that, after the Darroch Road
crime, Yih Hai-sen had money, as he
entered into partnership with Tang
Shek in the Vienna Cabaret in
Tsingtao. According to Tang Shek
and another man called "Darky,"
Yih Hai-sen at first offered $1,000 as
his investment in the business, but
later he produced only $500.

Connections With Jack

Regarding the connection between
Yih Hai-sen and Jack, a Korean,
Inspr. Crowther stated that the letter
found in Tsingtao showed it was
written by men named Costa and Lee,
introducing the Korean to Yih. The
latter had denied knowing the Korean,
but from this letter, which was
obtained from Yih's brother-in-law
in Tsingtao, it was not so.
Mr. T. S. Lea said that, during the
period of remand, investigations were
made on a number of points in ac-
cordance with the Judge's order.
One concerned the movements of
Chow Zeu-yoong, the third accused,
in November last. According to
Chow, he remained at home, but his
tenant said he frequented dancing
halls in that month.
Yih Hai-sen denied that the money
invested in a Tsingtao cabaret was
his, saying his wife, Zung Kwei-
ching, produced the money for him.
Li Hung-ping, a watchman in the
Ting Loh Li Alleyway, Darroch
Road; Yao Tseng-ting, a guard at the
Nanyang Cabaret; Mee Pau-ching, an
inspector at the Moon Palace Cabaret;
and Tseng Yuan also gave evidence.
The second witness said the Nanyang
Cabaret was opened on November 3
last year, contrary to Yih Hai-sen's
previous statement that he was pres-
ent at the opening on November 9.
After questions about two threat-
ening letters sent to a Chapel school
principal, the hearing was again ad-
journed sine die, the Judge mention-
ing that he was waiting for reports
from the Chenju Judicial Research
Laboratory on a book, a pistol, and a
spent bullet which had been sent
there for special examination.

《华北每日新闻》，1936年6月17日，星期三

易海森系
“斧头帮”成员

中山案审判中公开青岛之行

法院等待司法
实验室报告

据助理市检察官T. S. Lea先生昨日在第一特区法院的陈述，易海森（别名“小广东”）是去年11月9日谋杀日本海军陆战队员H. Nakayama一案中被警方拘留的三名男子之一，他与一个被称为“斧头帮”的流氓团伙有联系。
易承认他于1934年被中国军方逮捕，但称他和所有其他人因缺乏针对他们的证据，在被拘留一个多月后获释。
迪克斯韦尔路（Dixwell Road）巡捕房的副督察Crowther向法庭展示了警探青岛之行的结果，他出示了一套深蓝色西式服装、一张易海森的照片和一封信，所有这些都是在当地公安局的协助下在青岛获得的。证人表示，可以看出，在达罗克路罪案发生后，易海森手头有钱，因为他与唐石（Tang Shek，音译）合伙在青岛开设了维也纳歌舞厅。据唐石和另一名被称为“Darky”的人说，易海森起初提出出资1000美元作为生意投资，但后来只拿出了500美元。

与杰克的联系

关于易海森与朝鲜人杰克的联系，Crowther督察指出，在青岛发现的信件显示，该信由名为Costa和Lee的人撰写，将这名朝鲜人介绍给易。后者曾否认认识这名朝鲜人，但从这封从易在青岛的妹夫处获得的信件来看，事实并非如此。
T. S. Lea先生说，在还押候审期间，根据法官的命令对若干要点进行了调查。其中一点涉及第三被告周祖荣（Chow Zeu-yoong，音译）去年11月的行踪。据周称，他待在家里，但他的房客说他那个月经常出入舞厅。
易海森否认投资于青岛歌舞厅的钱是他的，称是他的妻子宗桂清（Zung Kwei-ching，音译）为他提供的资金。丁乐里（Ting Loh Li，音译）弄堂（位于达罗克路）的看门人李鸿平（Li Hung-ping，音译）、南洋歌舞厅的警卫姚增定（Yao Tseng-ting，音译）、月宫歌舞厅（Moon Palace Cabaret）的稽查员梅宝庆（Mee Pau-ching，音译）以及曾元（Tseng Yuan，音译）也提供了证词。第二名证人表示，南洋歌舞厅于去年11月3日开业，这与易海森此前声称他于11月9日出席开业典礼的说法相悖。
在就寄给一所教会学校校长的两封恐吓信进行提问后，聆讯再次无限期休庭，法官提及他正在等待陈居司法研究实验室关于送往那里进行特别检查的一本书、一把手枪和一颗弹壳的报告。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 17, 1936
1497b
7073
17-6 36.1

'Shao Kwangtung' Said Had
Funds After Murder

Heavy Guard In Court As Rumours Spread That A
Threat Had Been Made To Murder The Chief
Suspect; Detective Back From Tsingtao

An allegation that the finances of Yin Hai-sen, alias "Shao Kwang-tung," the alleged slayer of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing force, had increased considerably following the murder of the marine on Darroch Road on November 9, last, were made by the prosecution at the resumption of the long drawn out and complicated trial of three suspects in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon.

To substantiate the allegation the prosecutor told the court that, following the murder, "Shao Kwangtung" proceeded to Tsingtao and there invested money in a cabaret. It was further alleged by the prosecution that, following the murder, the chief suspect and self-confessed slayer, became very friendly with Jack, the Korean suspect, held by the Japanese Consular Police.

The hearing yesterday was mainly occupied with the questioning of several witnesses and a lengthy outline of further evidence by the prosecution and the replies of the defence counsel. The hearing was again postponed sine die pending the report being issued on the expert examination of the pistol and bullet allegedly used in the crime.

Suspect's Life Threatened

A high tension of excitement seemed to be current in court yesterday when an extra heavy guard of police was on hand and always carefully surrounded "Shao Kwangtung." It could not be ascertained definitely, but it was rumoured that the police had received a letter stating that "Shao Kwangtung" would be killed despite the fact that he was kept in police custody.

Notwithstanding the repeated requests made by Judge Dzien to have Jack, the Korean suspect, brought to court, the Japanese Consular Police did not bring him yesterday maintaining that they had not completed their inquiries. Murmurs of dissatisfaction on this point were heard during the proceedings as it is believed that Jack's appearance in the witness stand would greatly facilitate the investigation conducted by the Settlement Police.

Assistant Municipal Advocate T. S. Lea opened the proceedings by outlining the latest developments. In his address he denied the allegation that the case was a frame-up. He stated that Yang Gien-chun, who was implicated by the defence in the alleged frame-up, had played a very small part in helping the informant, Tseng Yuan, to ascertain the address of Yang Wen-tao, a former employee of the China Navigation Company and one of the men facing trial.

Mr. Lea also told the court that Chou Tso-yung, the third accused, had lied deliberately in saying that he was in financial difficulties in October and November of last year, as evidence could be produced that Chou was well supplied with money at the time.

Detective Returns

Detective Sub-Inspector Crowther, who had been conducting investigations in the case since the crime took place, and who recently returned from Tsingtao, where he had been conducting investigations, informed the court that "Shao Kwangtung" was quite well-to-do when he was in Tsingtao.

Argument arose during the proceedings between the defence and the prosecution over the letter of introduction taken by Jack to "Shao Kwangtung" in Tsingtao. The defence contended that if the two knew each other in Shanghai, no introduction would be necessary; the contention of the prosecution was that the letter was sent to inform "Shao Kwangtung" that Jack was "our extraordinarily beloved brethren" as written in the letter.

The prosecutor further contended that evidence would be later brought forward to prove that "Shao Kwangtung" was one of the 18 men arrested following the attempt to murder Mr. T. V. Soong. He was later released. Several witnesses were questioned by the judge before the hearing was adjourned sine die.

《字林西报》，1936年6月17日，星期三
1497b
7073
17-6 36.1

据称“邵广东”在谋杀案后拥有资金

随着有关威胁要谋杀主要嫌疑人的谣言传播，法庭戒备森严；侦探从青岛返回

昨日下午，在第一特区法院恢复审理这起旷日持久且错综复杂的三名嫌疑人案件时，检方提出指控称，被指为日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）凶手的尹海森（Yin Hai-sen），别名“邵广东”（Shao Kwang-tung），在去年11月9日于达罗克路（Darroch Road）发生海军陆战队员被杀案后，其财务状况显著增加。

为了证实这一指控，检察官告诉法庭，“邵广东”在谋杀案发生后前往青岛，并在那里投资了一家歌舞厅。检方还指控称，在谋杀案发生后，这位主要嫌疑人兼自认的凶手，与由日本领事馆警察拘留的朝鲜籍嫌疑人杰克（Jack）变得非常亲密。

昨天的听证会主要用于询问几名证人，以及检方对进一步证据的详细概述和辩护律师的回应。听证会再次无限期推迟，等待关于据称用于犯罪的手枪和子弹的专家检验报告发布。

嫌疑人生命受到威胁

昨天法庭上似乎弥漫着高度紧张的气氛，现场部署了额外的重兵警力，并始终小心翼翼地包围着“邵广东”。虽然无法确切查明，但有谣言称警方收到一封信，声称尽管“邵广东”处于警方拘留中，但仍将被杀害。

尽管迪恩法官（Judge Dzien）多次要求将朝鲜籍嫌疑人杰克带上法庭，但日本领事馆警察昨天并未将其带来，理由是他们的调查尚未完成。庭审期间可以听到对此不满的低语声，因为人们认为杰克出庭作证将极大地便利工部局警察进行的调查。

助理市政检察官T. S. Lea开庭陈述了最新进展。他在发言中否认了该案是栽赃陷害的指控。他指出，辩方指控参与所谓栽赃陷害的杨健春（Yang Gien-chun），在帮助线人曾元（Tseng Yuan）查明中国航业公司前雇员、也是受审人员之一的杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao）的地址方面，只起了很小的作用。

Lea先生还告诉法庭，第三被告周作庸（Chou Tso-yung）故意撒谎，声称自己去年十月和十一月陷入财务困境，因为有证据可以证明周当时资金充裕。

侦探返回

自犯罪发生以来一直负责此案调查、最近刚从青岛调查回来的副督察克罗瑟（Crowther）通知法庭，“邵广东”在青岛时相当富裕。

庭审期间，辩方和检方就杰克在青岛带给“邵广东”的介绍信发生了争论。辩方主张，如果两人在上海就认识，就不需要介绍；检方则主张，发送这封信是为了告知“邵广东”，杰克是信中所述的“我们特别敬爱的兄弟”。

检察官进一步主张，稍后将提出证据证明，“邵广东”是在刺杀宋子文（T. V. Soong）未遂案后被捕的18人之一。他后来被释放。在听证会无限期休庭前，法官询问了几名证人。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 17, 1936
6 Japanese
Guard Yen
During Trial
Threats Said Made On
Life Of Nakayama
Case Defendant
TORTURE CHARGES
ARE AGAIN AIRED
“Hsiao Kwangtung” In
Better Spirits, Is
Nattily Dressed
An unusually heavy guard comprised of Japanese constables of the Shanghai Municipal Police Force surrounded Yen Hsi-san (Hsiao Kwangtung), Yang Wen-tao and Chow Tung-sse, the three accused in the Nakayama murder case, as they faced the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon to undergo further question in connection with the slaying last November of a member of the local Japanese Naval Landing Party.
No explanation for the heavy guard was offered in court although six constables stood directly to the rear of the accused. The officers scarcely moved out of their steps during the three hours that the session lasted.
After considerable inquiry, a CHINA PRESS reporter was informed that this was a precaution taken to prevent any possible attempts on “Hsiao Kwangtung’s” life. It was pointed out that anonymous threats have been made against him and that the police are not taking any chances.
Nothing out of the ordinary occurred during yesterday’s hearing. Judge Dzien was not on the bench but Judge Zee appeared in his place. “Hsiao Kwangtung” continued his allegations of police torture, while the police introduced evidence to the effect that the accused had been involved in a plot to assassinate a high ranking Government official some three years ago.
According to the police, the accused man was arrested but was later released owing to lack of evidence. Most of the afternoon was occupied with presenting this evidence.
The report of the Court Chemical Laboratories on the death bullet and box in which the gun was supposed to have been kept was not placed before the tribunal yesterday as expected. It is understood that the investigations of the laboratory have not been completed and will probably be submitted to the court at the next hearing.
“Hsiao Kwangtung” appeared to be in much better physical condition yesterday than he was during previous sessions. He was attired in a black suit of foreign cut, the trousers of which were of knicker style, and wore a pair of black patent leather shoes. He answered questions in a clear voice and was far from being the agitated nervous person he was a few weeks ago.
The case was remanded once more in order to allow the Japanese authorities further time in which to complete their report.

6名日本
警卫在

中山案被告
发出生命威胁

“萧广东”精神
较好，衣着
整洁

昨日下午，当颜希三（Yen Hsi-san，即萧广东/Hsiao Kwangtung）、杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao）和周通四（Chow Tung-sse，音译）这三名中山谋杀案的被告在第一特区法院出庭，就去年11月杀害当地日本海军陆战队成员一案接受进一步讯问时，一支由上海公共租界工部局警务处日本巡捕组成的异常庞大的警卫队伍包围了他们。

法庭上没有对重兵守卫作出解释，尽管有六名巡捕直接站在被告身后。在持续三个小时的庭审期间，这些警官几乎寸步不离。

经过多方打听，《大美晚报》记者获悉，这是为防止任何可能针对“萧广东”生命的企图而采取的预防措施。有人指出，已有人对他发出匿名威胁，警方不愿冒任何风险。

昨天的听证会上没有发生什么异常事件。迪恩法官（Judge Dzien）未出庭，由齐法官（Judge Zee，音译）代替。“萧广东”继续指控警方施以酷刑，而警方则引入证据，表明被告曾在约三年前卷入一起刺杀政府高官的阴谋。

据警方称，该被告曾被逮捕，但因证据不足后来被释放。下午的大部分时间都用于出示这些证据。

正如预期的那样，法院化学实验室关于致死子弹和据称存放枪支的盒子的报告昨天未提交给法庭。据悉，实验室的调查尚未完成，可能会在下次听证会上提交给法院。

“萧广东”昨天的身体状况似乎比前几次庭审时要好得多。他身穿一套西式剪裁的黑色西装，裤子是灯笼裤样式，脚穿一双黑色漆皮鞋。他回答问题时声音清晰，完全不像几周前那样焦虑不安。

案件再次还押，以便让日本当局有更多时间完成报告。

THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, JUNE 14, 1936

MURDER TRIAL WILL
RESUME TUESDAY

Nakayama Case Again
Before Court After
Bullet Tests

Hearing of the case in which
Yih Hai-sen, alias "Shao Kwang-
tung," Yang Wen-tao and Chou
Tso-yung are charged with mur-
dering the Japanese sailor Naka-
yama, on November of last year,
is scheduled to be resumed in the
First Special District Court on
Tuesday at 2 p.m., the court hav-
ing finished its investigation of
the pistol and bullet allegedly used
in the murder.

Altogether five public hearings
have been heard in connection
with the case, with "Shao Kwang-
tung" making various confessions
which led the court astray. At the
last hearing he repudiated his
former confession. The court then
decided to examine the pistol and
bullet allegedly used in the mur-
der and entrusted the mission to
the Institute of Legal Medicine,
despite the fact that the police
submitted proof that they had been
used in the crime.

What the court wished to know
then was whether or not the bullet
found by the police was the one
which had actually gone into the
sailor's brain as stated by a
Japanese doctor attached to the
Japanese landing force.

The Institute is reported to have
finished its investigations and the
court notified the three lawyers
defending the accused to appear
at the Tuesday hearing.

谋杀案审判将于

中山案在
子弹测试后
再次开庭

涉及尹海森（Yih Hai-sen，别名“邵广东”/Shao Kwang-tung）、杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao）和周作庸（Chou Tso-yung）被控于去年11月谋杀日本水手中山（Nakayama）的案件，定于周二下午2点在第一特区法院恢复审理，法院已完成对据称用于谋杀的手枪和子弹的调查。

与此案有关的公开听证会共进行了五次，“邵广东”作出了各种误导法庭的供认。在最后一次听证会上，他推翻了之前的供词。随后，法院决定检查据称用于谋杀的手枪和子弹，并将此任务委托给法医研究所，尽管警方已提交证据证明这些物品曾被用于犯罪。

当时法庭想知道的是，警方发现的子弹是否如日本海军陆战队附属的一名日本医生所述，确实是射入水手大脑的那一颗。

据报道，研究所已完成调查，法院已通知为被告辩护的三位律师出席周二的听证会。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, JUNE 9, 1936

3RD-DEGREE TACTICS

Editor, THE CHINA PRESS.
Sir:—The conflicting versions of the confession of the murder of Nakayama made successively by Yih Hai-sen leave no doubt that either the accused is mentally unbalanced or else these confessions were wrangled from him through the so-called third-degree tactics of the police—a misnomer for the ugly word "torture."
Medical examination has been made recently on the accused and he was found to be sane. His apparent anxiety to admit the crime, to have the whole thing over with, even though it means certain death, can only be attributed to his inability to withstand the cruel maltreatment at the Headquarters, for men do not go to their death so anxiously unless they are suffering extreme physical or mental anguish.
It makes me shudder to think of the fate that awaited Yih as he was led, with tears streaming down his cheeks, away from the Court to be returned to the Police Station, after the judge had overruled the motion of his counsel that he be remanded in the Court's detention cells.
That the alleged torture should be permitted to be perpetuated in this "Model Settlement" is incredible and yet there is much damaging evidence pointing to its existence. By what means, for instance, have the police been able to locate and raid the hide-outs of accomplices of a criminal a few hours after the arrest of the latter as has so often happened in the Settlement?
The personnel of the Police Department of the Municipality is exclusively white and colored natives have a right to expect them to be scientific methods and not depend on the antiquated practice of extracting confessions through brutality which is the hallmark of backward nations rather than it is high time that the Municipal Council appoint a commission to investigate the matter.
With the notorious case of the torture of Tsai Yang-chi still pending, it is evident that it is through the protection of the Police Department that the operations of the First Division Gang carried on the Chinese section are allowed to continue unmolested, and with the bodies now being cast into fresh in the waterway, the public should demand in the interest of humanity and for the reputation of the Settlement that an immediate investigation be instituted against the recurrence of such outrages.

《大美晚报》，1936年6月9日，星期二

第三度审讯手段

致《大美晚报》编辑：
先生：——尹海森相继作出的关于中山谋杀案的相互矛盾的供词版本，毫无疑问地表明，要么被告精神失衡，要么这些供词是通过警方所谓的“第三度审讯手段”——即“酷刑”这一丑陋词汇的委婉说法——从他那里逼取出来的。
最近对被告进行了医学检查，发现他神志清醒。他明显急于承认罪行，希望尽快结束这一切，即使这意味着必死无疑，这只能归因于他无法忍受总局的残酷虐待，因为除非遭受极度的身体或精神痛苦，否则人们不会如此急切地走向死亡。
想到尹的命运让我不寒而栗，当法官驳回其律师关于将他羁押在法院拘留室的动议后，他泪流满面地被带离法庭，送回警察局。
在这个“模范租界”里，允许所谓的酷刑持续存在是不可思议的，然而有许多确凿的证据指向其存在。例如，警方是如何能够在逮捕罪犯几小时后，就定位并突袭其同伙的藏身之处的？这在租界中屡见不鲜。
市警务处的人员完全是白人，有色人种居民有权期望他们采用科学方法，而不是依赖通过残暴手段提取供词这种过时做法，后者是落后国家的标志而非文明社会的特征。现在是时候让工部局任命一个委员会来调查此事了。
鉴于蔡阳吉（Tsai Yang-chi，音译）遭受酷刑的著名案件仍未解决，显然正是由于警务处的庇护，第一分部帮会在华界的活动才得以继续进行而不受干扰。随着尸体不断被抛入河道，公众出于人道主义考虑并为维护租界的声誉，应要求立即对此类暴行的再次发生进行调查。

Procurator wildly advocates innocence of accused
in the Nakayama case

The 8th hearing of the Nakayama
case was held at 2.07 p.m. July 10 in the Special District
Court.
The Municipal advocate summing
up the case declared that the evidence produced by the
prosecution was sufficient to show that the three accused
were concerned in the Darroch Road crime.
Seven Chinese lawyers appearing
for the defence of the three accused then submitted their
arguements, after which Procurator Chang rose to his feet
and wildly stated that the connection between the book on
practical physics and the pistol was clear but it could
not be said that the book belonged to Yang Ven Tao. As
regards Yih Hai Sung he said that Yih was not a person
who could have created such a serious incident because
he is a habituee of dance halls and had he committed the
crime he would have fled. The Procurator added that Yih
made his confession under torture. As regards Tseu Shou
Yung, he was arrested on Yih Hai Sung's statement, but he
had no connection with the case.
The procurator concluded by
saying that the evidence against the accused was not
sufficient.

The Japanese Military Attache's

"Taking advantage of the visit of Major-General
Watari, Chief of the Second Section of the General Staff

DETERMINATION OF JAPANESE AUTHORITIES IN REGARD

At the 8th public hearing of
the Nakayama case in the First Special District Court,
Procurator Chang stated that there was insufficient
evidence against Yang Ven Tao and Yih Hai Sung for they

As some political influence
being exerted from a certain direction, the Japanese
Consular authorities and the Japanese naval authorities

日本武官处就一次军事会议发表如下声明：——

日本当局对中山案的决定
