pages.en:
July 10, 1936.
Morning Translation.

MAINICHI, NICHI NICHI AND NIPPO

CHENJU MEDICO-LEGAL LABORATORY'S WILD EXAMINATION OF
EXHIBITS IN NAKAYAMA CASE: ATTITUDE OF COURT DOUBTFUL

The Nakayama murder case will come up for hearing
to-day.
The insincerity and the political activities of the
Chinese authorities in the case are being revealed as the
trial goes on. The exhibits have already been given a
strictly scientific examination by the Arms Identification
Department of S.M.C. Headquarters, yet the Court has sent
them to the Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory for further
examination. The result of this examination was published
by local Chinese newspapers before the hearing on July 8.
This reveals how the handling of the case by the judiciary
is being affected by the political activities behind the
scenes.

Violent Arguments and Mistakes Made by the
Unscientific Examination

The greatest surprise is the unscientific
examination made by the Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory.
This gave rise to the suspicions mentioned above. The report
made by the Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory is in four sections
and is as follows:-
(1) Is the rust in the excavated hole of the book belonging
to Yang Vung Tao natural or had it been produced by
human agency?
The Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory reported that
the rust on the book and the pistol came from the same
source and that the rust marks could have been produced
by a pistol of the same model and size.
This statement is absolutely contrary to scientific
principles because it has been scientifically proved that
different marks are made by different pistols though
they may be of the same model and type. The pistol
in question is an old type weapon and had been painted
over; for this reason, it left unusual marks in the book.
In an attempt to give an impression that the marks
had been made by human agency, the report stated
that the oil stains in the book could not have been
produced without some pressure having been applied on
the book from both sides.
Yang Vung Tao used to carry the pistol by placing
it in the book even when he was travelling, therefore
the book must have received outside pressure.
(2) Does the book ("Practical Physics") bear any of Yang
Vung Tao's fingerprints?
The Chenju examination found none. On Page 27
of the book are some marks resembling fingerprints and
it was evident that it was impossible to prove them
clearly. It is meaningless to look for fingerprints
in a book which has been handled by Police officers and
Judges. For this reason, it would be strange had
Yang Vung Tao's fingerprints been found in the book.

1936年7月10日。
晨间译件。

《每日新闻》、《日日新闻》和《日本新闻报》

陈竺法医实验室对中山案证物的荒谬检验：法院态度令人怀疑

中山谋杀案将于今日开庭审理。
随着审判的进行，中国当局在此案中的不诚意和政治活动正逐渐暴露。证物已经过工部局总部枪械鉴定科的严格科学检验，但法院仍将其送往陈竺法医实验室进行进一步检验。该检验结果在7月8日开庭前已由当地中文报纸公布。这揭示了司法部门处理此案如何受到幕后政治活动的影响。

非科学检验引发的激烈争论与错误

最令人惊讶的是陈竺法医实验室进行的非科学检验。这引起了上述怀疑。陈竺法医实验室的报告分为四部分，内容如下：——
(1) 杨文道（Yang Vung Tao）书中挖出的孔洞内的锈迹是自然形成的还是人为造成的？
陈竺法医实验室报告称，书上和手枪上的锈迹来源相同，且锈痕可能是由同型号和尺寸的手枪造成的。
这一说法完全违背科学原理，因为科学已证明，即使是同型号和类型的手枪，也会留下不同的痕迹。涉案手枪是一种旧式武器，且表面曾重新喷漆；因此，它在书中留下了不寻常的痕迹。为了给人留下痕迹是人为造成的印象，报告称，书中的油渍不可能在没有从两侧对书施加压力的情况下形成。
杨文道即使在旅行时也习惯将手枪放在书中携带，因此书本必然受到外部压力。
(2) 《实用物理学》一书上是否有杨文道的指纹？
陈竺实验室的检验未发现任何指纹。该书第27页有一些类似指纹的痕迹，显然无法清晰辨认。在一本经过警察和法官 handling 的书上寻找指纹是没有意义的。因此，如果在书中发现了杨文道的指纹，那才是奇怪的。

(3) The connection between the photographs showing the
wounds, the doctor's certificate and Yih Hai Sung's
confession.
Yih Hai Sung has stated that he shot Nakayama
from 5 to 6 steps behind. In spite of this, the doctor's
certificate states that the attack had probably been
made from about 50 centimetres behind. Therefore,
these two points do not agree. The angle of the wound
of entry and the wound of exit is thirty degrees.
Basing its decision on the degree of this angle, the
Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory surmised that the bullet
must have been fired from a point of 5 centimetres away.
This does not agree with the statement made by Yih Hai
Sung. The report states that, according to the nature
of the powder burns around the wound of entry, the
shot must have been fired at a distance of 5 centimetres.
This is contrary to scientific principles. The report
had failed to take into consideration Nakayama's motion
in walking and the character of the resistance received
by the bullet. It is unscientific to judge the
distance between victim and attacker on the basis of the
enlarged photograph of the wound of entry and the angle
formed by the wound of entry and the wound of exit.
The report had evidently ignored a scientific theory
because it stated that no gun powder would remain around
the wound of entry unless the attack was made from a
spot 5 centimetres away from the victim. The theory
established by science is powder burns will be found even when
a gun is fired 50 centimetres away.
A study of the report of the Chenju Medico-Legal
Laboratory shows that it contains many wrongful and
unscientific surmises. Should the Court accept this
report --- a report which is believed to have been
twisted for political considerations --- and ignore the
definite evidence produced by the S.M.P. the judiciary
of China will lose the confidence of the public.
Therefore, the Court proceedings should be watched with
close attention.

(3) 显示伤口的照片、医生证明书与叶海生供词之间的联系。
叶海生声称，他在距离中山后方5到6步的地方开枪。尽管如此，医生证明书指出，袭击可能发生在后方约50厘米处。因此，这两点不一致。入口伤口和出口伤口的角度为三十度。陈竺法医实验室基于此角度的大小，推测子弹一定是从5厘米远处发射的。这与叶海生的陈述不符。报告称，根据入口伤口周围火药烧伤的性质，射击距离一定为5厘米。这违背了科学原理。报告未能考虑到中山行走时的动作以及子弹受到的阻力特性。仅凭入口伤口的放大照片以及入口伤口与出口伤口形成的角度来判断受害者与袭击者之间的距离，是不科学的。报告显然忽视了一个科学理论，因为它声称，除非袭击发生在距离受害者5厘米的地方，否则入口伤口周围不会残留火药。科学确立的理论是，即使在50厘米远处开枪，也会发现火药烧伤。
对陈竺法医实验室报告的研究表明，其中包含许多错误和非科学的推测。如果法院接受这份被认为出于政治考虑而被歪曲的报告，而无视工部局警务处提供的确凿证据，中国司法界将失去公众的信任。因此，应密切关注法庭诉讼程序。

July 10, 1936. Morning Translation.

"World Morning Post"(世界晨報) published the following comment on July 9 :-

THE DECISION IN THE SASAKI CASE.

On the night of May 26, two Japanese military officers, Sasaki and Ohnishi, were assaulted at No. 27 bar in Peiping. One of them subsequently died, while the other sustained some injuries. At that time, Cook and Hunter, guards of the British Embassy, were identified as the assailants. The Japanese took the matter seriously and demanded that these two men be severely punished. After several Court hearings, Mr. Fitzmaurice, the British Consul, on July 4 found Cook not guilty.
The Japanese are greatly dissatisfied with the decision and are preparing to lodge a protest.
Supposing the Japanese had suspected Chinese soldiers of having been responsible for this affair, the Chinese would have been arrested long ago by Japanese gendarmes and secretly executed without any consideration of their case. In addition, the Japanese would have demanded compensation, the demilitarization of the area, etc., and would develop the case in such a manner as to make it as serious as if a fatal assault had been committed upon the Japanese Ambassador. It is fortunate that the Japanese suspected British soldiers of having committed the act. Although Britain's influence in China is waning, still Japan is afraid of her military strength and she cannot deal with British subjects in the same manner as she deals with Chinese. When Cook was found not guilty of the charge by his own Consul, the Japanese cannot do anything more in the matter and if the Japanese were to die of mortification, it would not have any effect on the case.
Had the Doo Zoong Yuen (杜重遠) affair occurred in Peiping, he would have been barbarously assaulted if not dead long ago. His punishment of two years imprisonment was due to the fortuitous circumstance of his being a resident of the Settlement. Even then, one felt very sad over his case. Is not Yih Hai Sung(葉海生), who is being charged in connection with the Darroch Road murder case, suffering in a similar way?
Japanese newspapers may write intolerable remarks about Chinese political leaders, but the Chinese must show respect to the Japanese Emperor whenever mention has to be made of him.
The Japanese Imperial Army is also held sacred by the Japanese. However, if you have an armed force and if I also have an armed force, what would you do to me should I trespass upon you?

1936年7月10日。晨间译件。

《世界晨报》于7月9日发表如下评论：——

佐佐木案的判决。

5月26日晚，两名日本军官佐佐木和大西在北平27号酒吧遭到袭击。其中一人随后死亡，另一人受伤。当时，英国大使馆的警卫库克（Cook）和亨特（Hunter）被指认为袭击者。日本方面对此事高度重视，要求严惩这两人。经过几次法庭听证，英国领事菲茨莫里斯先生于7月4日裁定库克无罪。
日本方面对该判决极为不满，并准备提出抗议。
假如日本方面怀疑是中国士兵所为，这些中国人早就被日本宪兵逮捕并秘密处决，根本不会考虑他们的案件。此外，日本还会要求赔偿、该地区非军事化等，并将此案发展到如同日本大使遭受致命袭击般严重的程度。幸运的是，日本方面怀疑是英国士兵所为。虽然英国在华影响力正在减弱，但日本仍忌惮其军事实力，无法像对待中国人那样对待英国臣民。当库克被其本国领事裁定无罪后，日本方面在此事上已无能为力，即使日本人气愤致死，也不会对案件产生任何影响。
如果杜重远事件发生在北平，他若不早已身亡，也会遭到野蛮殴打。他被判处两年监禁，纯属因其为租界居民的偶然情况。即便如此，人们对其遭遇仍感到非常悲哀。因达罗克路谋杀案而被指控的叶海生（Yih Hai Sung），难道不是在遭受类似的苦难吗？
日本报纸可能会对中国政治领导人写出难以容忍的言论，但每当提及日本天皇时，中国人必须表示尊重。
日本帝国陆军也被日本人视为神圣。然而，如果你有武装力量，而我也有武装力量，若我侵犯你，你会对我做什么？

中山谋杀案：预计今日庭审将出现激烈辩论

涉嫌谋杀日本水兵中山的三名嫌疑人杨文道（Yang Vung Tao）、叶海生（Yih Hai Sung）和周守庸（Tseu Shou Yung）一案，将于今天下午在上海第一特区地方法院再次开庭审理。

July 10, 1936, Morning Translation.

At the last hearing of the case on July 8,
a very important point was raised by all the lawyers acting
for the defence of the accused. This point was not mentioned
by any of the local newspapers.
The point raised by the lawyers was as
follows:-
After the murder, a certain witness named
Hu Wu Ziang (胡和祥) stated at the Police Station that
the dress of the man who killed Hideo Nakayama was of the
same colour as the uniform worn by the deceased. After
the arrest of the three accused Yang Vung Tao, Yih Hai Sung
and Tseu Shou Yung by the Police this year, Hu Wu Ziang,
the witness, stated in Court that he could not remember
very clearly the colour of the clothing worn by the murderer.
At the hearing on July 8, the Municipal Advocate made the
following statement to the Court:-
'It is a rule for marines of the
Japanese Landing Party to go out in pairs when on
leave. At the time of the murder of the Japanese
marine Nakayama, the Chinese Policeman (C.P.C.) who
was on duty in the vicinity of Feng Loh Li immediately
hurried to the side of the victim within less than
ten minutes from the moment he had heard the shot,
and asked him (Nakayama) in which direction the
assailant had made his escape. However, owing to
language difficulty, the policeman could not get any
information from Nakayama, but he stood there waiting
for the arrival of Police officials. Shortly after-
wards, "Kai-Tu" (開脫), a companion of Nakayama,
arrived on the scene in a ricksha and conveyed Nakayama
to hospital for treatment.'
Now, despite the fact that Yih Hai Sung
had previously admitted in Court that Nakayama was murdered
by him, Jack, the Korean, who appeared at the last hearing,
flatly denied any knowledge about the case and stated that
had he desired to murder some person, he would not have
conspired with one who was his enemy. Upon hearing Jack's
statement, Yih Hai Sung thereupon retracted all his previous
statements.
All this shows that all these accused are
innocent. As to-day is the last day and accused will all
be interrogated, heated arguments are expected.

Lih Pao (立報) :-

ELEVEN CANTON AVIATORS JOIN NANKING

Eleven of the 21 Canton aviators who are
opposed to the unlawful activities of the Liang-Kwang
authorities arrived in Shanghai from Hongkong yesterday by
the s.s. President Jefferson.
When interviewed by a reporter, they stated
that their action had no ulterior motive whatever nor had
it been induced by the Central Government.
The Canton aviators left for Nanking at 11 p.m.
the same day after sending a lengthy telegram of warning to
General Chen Chi Tang.

1936年7月10日，晨间译件。

在7月8日对该案的最后一次审讯中，所有代表被告辩护的律师提出了一个非常重要的问题。本地任何报纸均未提及此点。
律师们提出的问题如下：-
谋杀发生后，一位名叫胡和祥（Hu Wu Ziang）的证人在警察局陈述称，杀害中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）的那名男子的衣服颜色与死者所穿制服的颜色相同。今年警方逮捕了三名被告杨文涛（Yang Vung Tao）、易海松（Yih Hai Sung）和周寿荣（Tseu Shou Yung）后，证人胡和祥在法庭上表示，他已记不清凶手所穿衣物的确切颜色。
在7月8日的审讯中，市公诉人向法庭作了如下陈述：-
‘日本海军陆战队队员休假外出时，两人结伴而行是一条规定。在日本海军陆战队员中山遇害时，当时在丰乐里（Feng Loh Li）附近执勤的中国巡捕（C.P.C.）在听到枪声后不到十分钟内立即赶到受害者身边，并询问他（中山）袭击者向哪个方向逃跑了。然而，由于语言障碍，巡捕未能从中山那里获得任何信息，但他站在那里等待警务官员的到来。不久之后，中山的同伴“开脱”（Kai-Tu）乘人力车到达现场，并将中山送往医院救治。’
现在，尽管易海松此前曾在法庭上承认中山是由他所杀，但在最后一次审讯中出庭的朝鲜人杰克（Jack）断然否认对该案有任何了解，并表示，如果他想要谋杀某人，他不会与他的敌人共谋。听到杰克的陈述后，易海松随即撤回了之前所有的供词。
这一切表明，所有这些被告都是无辜的。由于今天是最后一天，且所有被告都将接受讯问，预计会出现激烈的辩论。

《立报》（Lih Pao）：

十一名广东飞行员赴南京

反对两广当局非法活动的21名广东飞行员中的11人，昨日乘坐“杰斐逊总统号”轮船从香港抵达上海。
在接受记者采访时，他们表示，他们的行动没有任何 ulterior motive（不良动机），也非受中央政府诱导。
这些广东飞行员在向陈济棠将军发出一封长篇警告电报后，于当晚11时启程前往南京。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, July 11, 1936

Nakayama Case
Hearings End

Verdict Expected Next
Friday; Advocate
Asks Death

With a new "Nakayama Case" looming large on Shanghai's horizon today, the conclusion of the original "Nakayama Case" has been overshadowed, yet on the same day that one started, another was being finished. Three Cantonese charged with the murder of Japanese Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama on Darroch Road on November 9 last will know their fate next Friday, July 17. The last hearing was concluded between Judge Dzien in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon.

Yi Hai-sen, alias Shao Kwang-tung, Yang Wen-tao, shipping man, and Chow Sha-yung, former cabaret manager, have been on trial during 10 hearings for the killing that so stirred up Shanghai last November, when another Shanghai Incident seemed imminent and Chinese evacuated Chapei wholesale. At yesterday's session attorneys summed up their case, as did the assistant municipal advocate, Mr. Paul Y. Ru, who asked for the extreme penalty for all three. He said the evidence left no doubt that they were guilty of the murder.

Mr. G. R. Grove, head of the defense lawyers, made an emotional plea for dismissal, declaring that all were innocent of the crime. Only evidence given at the session was that of a Mr. R. Pereiro, Portuguese, who testified that he was in the Moon Palace on the night of the murder and had heard Shao Kwangtung being scolded there by another man for "being late," and Shao Kwangtung answering that he was tardy because he had had "some trouble."

After the summing up the case was adjourned to next Friday for judgment.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年7月11日，星期六

中山案
审讯结束

预计下周五宣判；公诉人
要求判处死刑

随着一个新的“中山案”今天在上海地平线上赫然显现，原“中山案”的结案相形见绌，然而在一个案件开始的那一天，另一个案件正在结束。三名广东人因去年11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）谋杀日本军曹中山秀夫而被控，他们将于下周五，即7月17日知晓自己的命运。昨天下午，第一特区地方法院的丁恩法官（Judge Dzien）结束了最后一次审讯。

易海森（Yi Hai-sen），别名邵广东（Shao Kwang-tung）；杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao），航运从业者；以及周少勇（Chow Sha-yung），前舞厅经理，因去年11月那起如此震动上海的杀人案而受审，历时10次庭审，当时另一次上海事变似乎迫在眉睫，中国人大量撤离闸北。在昨天的庭审中，双方律师进行了总结陈词，助理市公诉人保罗·鲁（Paul Y. Ru）先生也是如此，他要求对三人处以极刑。他说，证据毫无疑问地表明他们犯有谋杀罪。

辩护律师团负责人G. R. Grove先生情绪激动地请求驳回起诉，宣称所有人都无罪。庭审中提供的唯一证据来自一位葡萄牙人R. Pereiro先生，他作证说，案发当晚他在月宫（Moon Palace），并听到邵广东在那里因“迟到”而被另一人斥责，邵广东回答说之所以迟到是因为遇到了一些“麻烦”。

总结陈词结束后，案件休庭，延至下周五宣判。

pages.en:
NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, JULY 11, 1936

JUDGMENT RESERVED
IN NAKAYAMA CASE

Portuguese as Witness at Trial
of Cantonese

Mr. R. Pereira, a Portuguese, testified for the police when the case was heard for the last time by the First Special District Court yesterday against three Cantonese, Yih Hai-sen, alias "Little Cantonese," Yang Ven-tao, and Chow Zeu-young, charged with the murder of H. Nakayama, a Japanese marine, on November 9 last.

Mr. Pereira's testimony briefly was to the effect that, on the night of the Darroch Road crime, he was in a room of the Moon Palace Hotel, North Szechuen Road, which was engaged by a friend of his, a Cantonese named Li Tien. Between 9.30 and 10 p.m., he left his friend's room and so did Ah Choh, also a guest. When they passed Room No. 9 of the Hotel, Ah Choh entered Room No. 9 in which was seen "Little Cantonese," who then looked pale in the face. Ah Choh asked "Little Cantonese": "What is wrong with you?" and "Little Cantonese" replied: "I just had a fight." There were a couple of other persons in the room, but witness said he did not know them.

Questioned by the Judge, the accused said they all knew this witness, the third accused, Chow Zeu-young, saying that, when he was arrested in the Continental Dancing Hall, witness was there too. "Little Cantonese" told the Judge that, on the night of the murder, he might be in the Moon Palace Hotel, but he was not sure.

Lawyers for both S. M. Police and defence then summed up in the case. Representing the Police, Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, asked for the conviction of all of the accused after speaking for nearly an hour.

In the course of his address, Mr. Ru pointed out that evidence produced by the prosecution were sufficient to show that the three accused were concerned in the Darroch Road crime. Insofar as Yang Ven-tao was concerned, a book was found in his house and a pistol found near the scene of the crime fitted perfectly the hollowed part of the seized book. As to "Little Cantonese," he had confessed at least three times in open court, which was sufficient to prove his responsibility for the crime.

Seven Chinese lawyers spoke for the accused, after which, the Judge reserved his decision.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年7月11日，星期六

中山案
判决保留

广东人受审期间
葡萄牙人作为证人出庭

昨天，第一特区地方法院最后一次审理针对三名广东人——易海森（Yih Hai-sen），别名“小广东”（Little Cantonese）、杨文涛（Yang Ven-tao）和周祖荣（Chow Zeu-young）——的案件，他们被控于去年11月9日谋杀日本海军陆战队员H. 中山（H. Nakayama）。一名葡萄牙人R. Pereira先生在警方传唤下出庭作证。

Pereira先生的证词简要大意是，在达罗克路犯罪案发生的当晚，他在北四川路月宫酒店的一个房间里，该房间由他的朋友、一位名叫李天（Li Tien）的广东人预订。晚上9点半到10点之间，他离开了朋友的房间，另一位住客阿卓（Ah Choh）也离开了。当他们经过酒店的9号房间时，阿卓进入了9号房间，里面可以看到“小广东”，当时他脸色苍白。阿卓问“小广东”：“你怎么了？”“小广东”回答说：“我刚才打了一架。”房间里还有另外几个人，但证人说他不认识他们。

经法官讯问，被告表示他们都认识这位证人，第三名被告周祖荣说，当他在大陆舞厅（Continental Dancing Hall）被捕时，证人也在场。“小广东”告诉法官，案发当晚他可能在月宫酒店，但他不确定。

随后，代表上海公共租界警务处和辩方的律师分别对案件进行了总结陈词。代表警方的助理市公诉人保罗·鲁（Paul Y. Ru）先生发言近一个小时，要求判定所有被告有罪。

鲁先生在发言中指出，检方提出的证据足以表明三名被告参与了达罗克路的犯罪。就杨文涛而言，在他家中发现了一本书，而在犯罪现场附近发现的一把手枪与这本被扣押的书中的挖空部分完全吻合。至于“小广东”，他至少在公开法庭上认罪三次，这足以证明他对犯罪的责任。

七名中国律师为被告辩护，随后，法官保留了判决。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, JULY 11, 1936
Judge Indicates Verdict
In Nakayama Trial
Decision Reserved For A Week At Conclusion Of
Hearing; Likely To Be In Favour Of The Three
Accused; Closing Speeches By Counsel

An indication that he would
probably feel compelled, after a
hearing spread over many weeks
and involving 16 full days of
evidence-taking, to find in favour
of the three men accused of the
Nakayama murder, was given by
Judge Chang, Chief Procurator of
the First Special District Court
at the conclusion of the case
yesterday.
While suggesting that he could
see no ground for returning a
verdict of other than "Not
Guilty," the Judge decided to
reserve his decision for a week,
and final judgment will be given
on Friday.
Judge Chang said that after
hearing the many arguments and
the judicial doctors' report, he
was of opinion that Yang Wen-
tao, in whose home the hollowed
book was found might have been
trapped. "Shao Kwangtung"
could not be found guilty because
of the many contradictions in
his confessions and as to Chou
Tso-yung, he could find no evid-
ence against him at all.
As a last witness, Mr. Ru
yesterday called a Portuguese,
who testified to the presence in
the Moon Palace Cabaret on
November 9 of last year of "Shao
Kwangtung." Witness declared he
was in Room No. 4 when "Shao
Kwangtung" was in Room 9.
Between 9.30 and 10 p.m. on
leaving the place, he saw "Shao
Kwangtung" in room No. 9 which
was half shut. He heard Shao
questioned as to why his face was
pale by Tso Cheng-hsiao. "Shao
Kwangtung" said he had had a
fight. Witness said he knew all
three accused but was not their
intimate friend.

Prosecutor's Case
Mr. Ru, in his final speech, said
the police had tried to deal with
accused in a just way. There were
two cold facts: That Naka-
yama was shot on November 9
and died shortly after 1 a.m. next
day. Both the pistol and the
bullet were discovered by Japan-
ese police officers the same night.
Dealing with accused individual-
ly, Mr. Ru said that near the bed
of Yang Wen-tao, police found the
book in which the pistol used in
the crime was hidden. Yang re-
cognised it and said it was the
book in which he put his licensed
pistol. No one could trap Yang
by putting a similar book in
Yang's home because, to do so he
must have the pistol to fit the
hole in the centre of the book.
As to "Shao Kwangtung," Mr.
Ru continued, he made a detailed
confession after knowing that
Yang had been arrested and that
the book had been found. Before
he knew Yang had been arrested
he refused to confess. His state-
ments that the police had beaten
him and that he had swallowed
keys to commit suicide had been
proven untrue. He could have re-
fused to demonstrate the crime in
the street where no police officer
would have dared to beat him.
Chou's only plea was that on
November 9, having pawned all his
clothes, he slept in bed all day.
His landlord denied his statement.
Jack, the accused Korean, could
not help the accused in any way.
Mr. Ru concluded by requesting
the court to pronounce sentence.

Defence Arguments
The seven lawyers for the de-
fence then rose one by one and
presented their arguments, agree-
ing with the doctor's report that
Nakayama was shot at close
range, which no Chinese criminal
under the circumstances would
have done. It was also contended
that the hole in the centre of the
book found in Yang's home was
much smaller than the licenced
pistol which Yang used to possess
but for which the licence was can-
celled long before the crime.
The pistol alleged to have been
used was found under a wooden
box in which a watchman carried
out his duty at night. No crim-
inal could have put the weapon
there while running for cover.
Supporting the doctors' report
stating that the victim was shot
at very close range (about half
an inch), counsel for the defence
said the Japanese must have been
shot by a man who walked with
him. The police traced the mur-
dered man to several houses of
ill-fame during the night of Novem-
ber 9. It was likely that the
victim was a "romantic" man
and that his death was "romantic."
The police could only prove
that a pistol found near the scene
of the crime fitted in with a
bullet also found near the scene
of crime. Besides the bullet was
found several hundred feet be-
hind the dead man which fact
could hardly prove that it was
the bullet which pierced the
victim's head.

《上海泰晤士报》，1936年7月11日，星期六

法官暗示中山案审判 verdict（裁决）
听证结束时判决保留一周；可能有利于三名被告；律师结案陈词

第一特区地方法院首席检察官张法官（Judge Chang）在昨天案件结束时给出了一种暗示，即在经历了持续数周、涉及整整16天取证的听证会后，他可能会感到被迫做出有利于被控谋杀中山的三名男子的裁决。
虽然法官表示看不出除了“无罪”之外还有其他裁决的理由，但他决定将判决保留一周，最终判决将于周五公布。
张法官表示，在听取了许多辩论和法医报告后，他认为杨文涛（在其家中发现了挖空的书）可能是被陷害的。“邵广东”不能被判有罪，因为他的供词存在许多矛盾；至于周佐荣（Chou Tso-yung），他根本找不到任何对他不利的证据。
作为最后一名证人，鲁先生昨天传唤了一名葡萄牙人，他作证说去年11月9日“邵广东”出现在月宫舞厅。证人声明，当“邵广东”在9号房间时，他在4号房间。当晚9点半到10点之间离开时，他看到半掩着的9号房间里的“邵广东”。他听到左承孝（Tso Cheng-hsiao）质问邵为何脸色苍白。“邵广东”说他打了一架。证人表示他认识所有三名被告，但并非他们的密友。

公诉方案件
鲁先生在最后陈述中说，警方一直试图公正地处理被告。有两个冰冷的事实：中山于11月9日遭枪击，并于次日凌晨1点后不久死亡。手枪和子弹均为日本警官当晚发现。
在逐一处理被告时，鲁先生说，警方在杨文涛的床边发现了藏匿作案用手枪的书。杨认出了它，并说这是他用存放持枪许可证手枪的书。没有人能通过将类似的书放入杨的家中来陷害杨，因为要做到这一点，他必须拥有能 fitting（契合）书中心孔洞的手枪。
关于“邵广东”，鲁先生继续说道，他在得知杨被捕且书被发现后做了详细供述。在得知杨被捕之前，他拒绝认罪。他关于警察殴打他以及他吞下钥匙自杀的说法已被证明不实。他本可以拒绝在街上演示犯罪过程，在那里没有警察敢殴打他。
周的唯一辩解是，11月9日，在典当了他所有的衣服后，他整天躺在床上。他的房东否认了他的说法。
被告朝鲜人杰克无法以任何方式帮助被告。
鲁先生最后请求法庭宣判。

辩护方论点
随后，七名辩护律师逐一起身陈述他们的论点，同意医生的报告，即中山是在近距离被射击的，在这种情况下，任何中国罪犯都不会这样做。此外还辩称，在杨家中发现的书中心的孔洞比杨曾经拥有但早在犯罪发生前很久就被吊销执照的手枪要小得多。
据称用于作案的手枪是在一个木箱下发现的，该木箱是一名守夜人夜间执勤时使用的。任何罪犯在逃跑寻找掩护时都不可能将武器放在那里。
支持医生关于受害者在极近距离（约半英寸）被射击的报告，辩护律师表示，日本人一定是被一个与他同行的人射击的。警方追踪被害人在11月9日晚去了几处妓院。受害者很可能是一个“风流”的人，他的死也是“风流”所致。
警方只能证明在犯罪现场附近发现的一把手枪与同样在现场附近发现的子弹相匹配。此外，子弹是在死者身后几百英尺处发现的，这一事实几乎不能证明它就是穿透受害者头部的子弹。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, JULY 11, 1936

Nakayama
Death Trial
Is Concluded

Court To Rule On Guilt
Of Yih, Chow, Yang
On July 17

PORTUGUESE IS
DAY'S WITNESS

Attorneys Argue For
Innocence Of 3 Men In
November Crime

After 10 sessions covering a period of three months, the trial of Yih Hai-sen (Hsiao Kwangtung), Yang Wen-tao, Cantonese shipping man, and Chow Sha-yung, erstwhile cabaret manager, on charges of murdering Hideo Nakayama was brought to a conclusion before the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon. The final session started at 2 p.m. and finished at 6 p.m. Judgment will be given on Friday, July 17.

The session yesterday was featured largely by the arguments of the prosecution and the defense. One witness was examined at the opening of the hearing but remained on the stand only a few minutes. He was Mr. R. Pereira, Portuguese, who testified that he was at the Moon Palace on the night of the killing.

He stated that he knew the accused and that on the night of the murder he had gone to the Moon Palace Hotel to meet a friend. As he left his friend's room some time before midnight, he heard "Hsiao Kwangtung" talking to a man in another room. He stated that "Hsiao" was being scolded for being late and that the latter replied he was tardy because he had had some trouble.

Ask Death Penalty

The witness left the stand and Mr. Pang Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, in charge of the prosecution, outlined the history of the case, summarised the evidence and asked for the extreme penalty for all three of the accused. He declared that the evidence had showed no doubt that the three were guilty of the slaying of Warrant Officer Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party on the night of November 9, 1935.

Mr. G. R. Grove, head of the battery of defense lawyers, addressed the court for almost an hour on behalf of Yang Wen-tao and Chow Sha-yung, his clients. He asked for the dismissal of both for lack of evidence. There was no evidence against Chow, he said, except that he knew Yang, and as far as the latter was concerned, the man had told the truth to the court when he declared that he knew nothing about the case.

Attorney Grove referred to the incident of the finding of the book apparently used to contain the death weapon in Yang's home. He intimated that this book had been prepared by the police and had been placed there as a plant. In other words, he charged the police with having framed Yang. He based his statement on the report of the experts of the Judicial Laboratories.

He pointed out that the report concerning the book stated that no fingerprints of Yang's had been found on the book and that the gun had left its impression on 12 pages. He declared that if the book had been really Yang's and that he had had it over a period of years, his fingerprints would have been found.

Says Yang An Honest Man

He maintained that Yang was an honest man and referred to the fact that he had never changed his story throughout the trial, that he had always reiterated his innocence, and that he had repeatedly insisted that he knew nothing about the affair.

Defense attorneys for Yih Hai-sen spoke for more than two hours. They based most of their defense on allegations that Yih was irresponsible, that he had changed his confessions so many times that he could not be believed and that his confessions were made under duress.

They took his last confession as a case in point and argued that the bullet which killed Nakayama must have been fired at close range, since the bullet went in below the ear and came out on top of his head. There were powder burns where the bullet entered, they argued, hence "Hsiao Kwangtung," who stated that he was 15 feet to the rear of the man when he fired the shot, must have been lying; that his lies proved that he had no knowledge of what really happened and therefore his dismissal was asked.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年7月11日，星期六

中山案
死刑审判
已终结

法院将于7月17日
裁定叶、周、杨三人之罪责

葡萄牙人
为当日证人

律师为十一月犯罪案中
三名男子的清白进行辩护

经过为期三个月的十次庭审，针对叶海森（即“小广东”）、粤籍航运商人杨文涛以及前舞厅经理周少庸被控谋杀中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）一案，于昨日下午在第一特区地方法院审理终结。最后一次庭审于下午2时开始，至6时结束。判决将于7月17日（星期五）宣判。

昨日的庭审主要以控辩双方的辩论为特征。听证会开始时传唤了一名证人，但其仅在证人席上停留了几分钟。该证人为葡萄牙人R. Pereira先生，他作证称案发当晚他在“月宫”（Moon Palace）。

他表示认识被告，并称案发当晚他去月宫饭店是为了会见一位朋友。午夜前不久，当他离开朋友的房间时，听到“小广东”在另一个房间里与一名男子谈话。他表示，“小广东”因迟到而受到斥责，后者回答说因为遇到了一些麻烦所以迟到了。

要求判处死刑

该证人退庭后，负责公诉的助理市检察官庞毓荣（Pang Y. Ru，音译）先生概述了案件经过，总结了证据，并请求对三名被告均处以极刑。他宣称，证据确凿无疑地表明，这三名被告犯有于1935年11月9日晚杀害日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄的罪行。

辩护律师团负责人G. R. Grove先生代表其当事人杨文涛和周少庸向法庭发言近一小时。他请求因证据不足驳回对两人的起诉。他说，除了认识杨文涛之外，没有任何证据针对周少庸；至于杨文涛，当此人声称对此案一无所知时，他向法庭陈述的是实情。

Grove律师提到了在杨文涛家中发现一本显然用于藏匿作案枪支的书这一情节。他暗示这本书是警方预先准备好并放置在那里以栽赃陷害的。换言之，他指控警方构陷杨文涛。他的陈述基于司法实验室专家的报告。

他指出，关于这本书的报告称，书上未发现杨文涛的指纹，且枪支在12页纸上留下了压痕。他宣称，如果这本书确实是杨文涛的，并且他已经持有多年，那么上面应该会发现他的指纹。

称杨为诚实之人

他坚持认为杨文涛是一个诚实的人，并指出他在整个审判过程中从未改变过供词，始终重申自己是无辜的，并反复坚称他对此事一无所知。

叶海森的辩护律师发言超过两小时。他们的辩护主要基于以下指控：叶海森精神不负责任；他的供词多次更改，因此不可信；且其供词是在胁迫下作出的。

他们以其最后的供词为例进行辩论，认为杀害中山的子弹必定是在近距离发射的，因为子弹从耳下射入，从头顶穿出。他们辩称，子弹入口处有火药灼伤痕迹，因此，“小广东”声称开枪时站在死者身后15英尺处，这一定是在撒谎；这些谎言证明他对实际发生的情况一无所知，因此请求驳回对他的起诉。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, July 10, 1936

Nakayama Case
May End Today

Final Hearing Slated;
Japanese Criticize
Chenju Reports

Judgment was expected to be
passed on Yih Hai-sen, alias Shao
Kwangtung, this afternoon in the
First Special District Court when
the Cantonese accused of the
murder of Japanese Warrant
Officer Hideo Nakayama was to
appear once again before Judge
Dzien. Shao Kwangtung faces a
murder charge in company with
two other Cantonese. A Korean,
Jack Hanson, is being held by
Japanese Consular Police in con-
nection with the case. The Can-
tonese have denied the charges
though circumstantial evidence is
against them. The trial has been
a long and involved one, the last
hearing being held day before
yesterday.

Press Assails Report

A point-by-point refutation of
the report on the "Nakayama
case", presented by the Legal In-
stitute of Medicine, Chenju, to the
First Special District Court of
July 8, was carried today by the
local Nipponese papers.

The articles, which also assail-
ed the Court for consulting the
Institute, despite a thorough in-
vestigation already conducted by
the Shanghai Municipal Police,
were nearly identical, apparently
originating from the same source.

The first point of the fourpoint
refutation dealt with the presence
of rust in the hollowed book,
which contained the revolver used
in the crime.

An Old Model

The report of the Chenju In-
stitute asserted that such rust
could have been left by any re-
volver. This view was challenged
by the Nipponese papers, which
emphasized that the "crime" re-
volver was of an old model and
was enamelled, thus leaving
marks specifically its own.

The failure of the Institute to
find Yang Wen-tao's finger prints
on the book was described as "im-
material" by the papers, on the
ground that the book has been
handled by innumerable hands
since the murder of Hideo Nak-
yama on Darroch Road on Nov.
on Nov. 9 last.

Distance Disputed

The conclusion of the institute
that the presence of powder marks
on the body showed that the shot
was fired five centimeters from
the body was also disputed by the
papers, which favored the S.M.P.'s
conclusion that the distance was
half a meter.

All three papers also asserted
that it has been proved that shots
fired at any short distance, "be it
15 or 50 centimeters", might leave
identical marks on the body and
the bullet.

No Blood Stains

Also disputed was the Institute's
view that the absence of blood
stains on the bullet might have
meant that it did not pierce the
body of Nakayama.

A thorough investigation made
by the S.M.P. immediately after
the murder has, according to the
papers, conclusively shown that
the bullet in question was respon-
sible for Nakayama's death.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年7月10日，星期五

中山案
或于今日终结

预定进行最后听证；
日本人批评
震旦大学报告

预计今天下午将在第一特区地方法院对叶海森（又名邵广东，Shao Kwangtung）作出判决，这名被控谋杀日本准尉中山秀雄的广东人将再次出现在Dzien法官面前。邵广东与另外两名广东人共同面临谋杀指控。一名朝鲜人Jack Hanson因与此案有关，正被日本领事馆警察拘留。尽管间接证据对他们不利，但这些广东人否认了指控。此次审判漫长而复杂，上一次听证会是在前天举行的。

媒体抨击报告

当地日文报纸今天刊登了对震旦大学（Chenju）法医研究所于7月8日向第一特区地方法院提交的关于“中山案”报告的逐点反驳。

这些文章还抨击法院在工部局警务处已经进行了彻底调查的情况下，仍咨询该研究所。这些文章内容几乎完全相同，显然出自同一来源。

四点反驳中的第一点涉及那本中空的书（用于藏匿作案左轮手枪）中存在的铁锈。

一种旧型号

震旦研究所的报告断言，这种铁锈可能是任何左轮手枪留下的。这一观点遭到日文报纸的挑战，它们强调“作案”左轮手枪是一种旧型号，且表面有珐琅涂层，因此会留下其特有的痕迹。

对于研究所未能在书上找到杨文涛指纹一事，报纸描述为“无关紧要”，理由是自去年11月9日中山秀雄在达罗克路（Darroch Road）遇害以来，这本书已被无数人经手。

距离之争

研究所得出的结论是，尸体上的火药痕迹表明射击距离为五厘米，这一结论也遭到报纸的反驳，报纸支持工部局警务处（S.M.P.）的结论，即距离为半米。

这三家报纸还断言，事实证明，在任何短距离内（“无论是15厘米还是50厘米”）发射的子弹，都可能在尸体和子弹上留下相同的痕迹。

无血迹

此外，研究所认为子弹上没有血迹可能意味着它并未穿透中山的身体，这一观点也受到质疑。

据报纸称，工部局警务处在谋杀案发生后立即进行的彻底调查已确凿地证明，涉案子弹导致了中山的死亡。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, JULY 9, 1936 15273

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
S. D. RECS
S. B. D. 7073
10 7 36

DARROCH RD. CRIME
CASE NEAR END

Jack, the Korean, as Witness
at Trial of Cantonese

JUDICIAL LABORATORY
REPORT ANNOUNCED

Jack, the Korean, implicated in the
Darroch Road crime of November 9
last by Yih Hai-sen and whose
presence as a witness had been re-
peatedly requested by the Chinese
Judge, yesterday was escorted to
the First Special District Court by
Japanese officials when the hearing,
after being adjourned for over two
weeks, was resumed of the case
against three Cantonese, Yih
Hai-sen, alias "Little Canton-
ese," Yang Ven-tao and Chow
Zeu-yoong, charged with the murder
of H. Nakayama, a Japanese marine.
No light, however, was thrown on
the case by the Korean witness who
denied any knowledge of the plot to
kill certain Japanese alleged by Yih
Hai-sen at various hearings in the
District Court. Jack told the Judge
it was true he had known the "Little
Cantonese" for about three years, but
that, since he was involved in a
cabaret scuffle with Yih Hai-sen in
July or August last year, he had not
seen the latter until he was arrested
in February this year on suspicion
of being involved in Nakayama's
murder.
The Judge told the Korean that
Yih Hai-sen had mentioned that
he was a member of the secret Can-
tonese society known as Dong Nyi
Hui with its office in a Range Road
alleyway and had discussed at a
meeting the proposed murder of
certain Japanese in that society. In
reply, the Korean stated that what
Yih Hai-sen had said was a lie and
he never knew the name of the
Cantonese society.
Jack admitted having brought a
letter of introduction signed by one
Costa to see Yih Hai-sen in Tsingtao
some time in June last year, but ex-
plained that he did not ask Costa to
write this letter, it being Costa's own
idea to give him this letter to help
him to find accommodation during
his first visit to Tsingtao. Jack told
the court that he formerly frequented
the Moon Palace Cabaret in North
Szechuen Road and occasionally
visited a Korean friend in a room
of the Moon Palace Hotel, but never
carried a pistol.

Movements Explained

Questioned about his movements
on the night of November 9 when
the Japanese marine was shot on
Darroch Road, Jack said he remained
in his Hart Road house. Witness said
he first read the news about the
Japanese marine's murder in news-
papers either on November 11 or 12
after being told by a Russian em-
ployee of a cabaret. After being
questioned about his relationship
with Yih Hai-sen, the witness was
dismissed.
A report of findings on a book, a
pistol and a spent bullet, submitted
to the court by the Chinese Govern-
ment Judicial Laboratory at Chenju,
was read by the court clerk at yes-
terday's hearing. The important points
of this report were that the finger-
prints found on the seized book were
incomplete and that the laboratory
staff could not tell whether Yang
Ven-tao, one of the accused, had
similar fingerprints as those in the
book, and that the laboratory staff
were of the opinion that the deceased
marine's gunshot wound could not
have been inflicted by a gun when
it was fired within five steps from
deceased's body as told by Yih Hai-
sen during a reconstruction of the
crime.
Yang Ven-tao was questioned by
the Judge whether the book seized
in his house was that he had used to
conceal his pistol, and the accused
replied in the negative. Det.-Sub-
Inspr. Crowther of Dixwell Road
Police Station told the court that,
after his arrest, Yang Ven-tao ad-
mitted this book belonged to him
when he saw it in the police station
and he made the statement without
being asked by the police. Sub-
Inspr. Crowther's testimony was
substantiated by Mr. Kawashima, an
officer of the Council, who was
present when Yang made the self-
confession.
After questioning another witness,
Tseng Wei-ming, a Formosan physi-
cian who supplied the information
which led to the arrest of the ac-
cused, the Judge adjourned the hear-
ing till to-morrow afternoon, at 2
o'clock, when counsel are expected
to sum up in the case.

《字林西报》，1936年7月9日，星期四 15273

上海公共租界
特别巡捕房记录
S. B. D. 7073
10 7 36

达罗克路犯罪案
接近尾声

朝鲜人Jack作为证人
出席广东人审判

公布司法实验室
报告

去年11月9日达罗克路犯罪案中，叶海森牵连出的朝鲜人Jack，其作为证人的出庭一直由中国法官多次要求，昨日在日本官员的陪同下被护送至第一特区地方法院。此前休庭两周多的针对三名广东人——叶海森（又名“小广东”）、杨文涛（Yang Ven-tao）和周祖荣（Chow Zeu-yoong，音译）——被控谋杀日本海军陆战队员H. Nakayama一案的听证会得以恢复。然而，这位朝鲜证人并未为案件带来任何线索，他否认知晓叶海森在地方法院各次听证会上所称的谋杀某些日本人的阴谋。Jack告诉法官，他确实认识“小广东”约三年，但自从去年七月或八月他与叶海森在一次舞厅斗殴中发生纠葛后，直到今年二月因涉嫌参与中山谋杀案被捕之前，他再未见过叶海森。

法官告诉这名朝鲜人，叶海森曾提到他是名为“东义会”（Dong Nyi Hui，音译）的广东秘密社团的成员，该社团办事处位于兰路（Range Road）的一条弄堂里，并在一次会议上讨论了在该社团内谋杀某些日本人的计划。作为回应，这名朝鲜人表示叶海森所说的是谎言，他从未听说过这个广东社团的名字。

Jack承认去年六月某时曾持有一封由一名叫Costa的人签署的介绍信去青岛见叶海森，但他解释说并非他要求Costa写这封信，而是Costa主动提出给他这封信，以帮助他在首次访问青岛期间寻找住处。Jack告诉法庭，他以前常去北四川路的月宫舞厅（Moon Palace Cabaret），并偶尔去月宫饭店的一个房间拜访一位朝鲜朋友，但他从不携带手枪。

解释行踪

当被问及11月9日晚日本海军陆战队员在达罗克路被枪杀时的行踪时，Jack说他待自己在哈特路（Hart Road）的家中。证人称，他是在一家舞厅的俄国雇员告知后，于11月11日或12日首次在报纸上读到关于日本海军陆战队员被杀的新闻。在被询问与叶海森的关系后，该证人被遣退。

在昨日的听证会上，书记员宣读了中国政府震旦大学司法实验室提交给法庭的一份关于一本书、一把手枪和一颗已发射子弹的鉴定报告。该报告的重点包括：在查获的书上发现的指纹不完整，实验室人员无法判断被告之一杨文涛的指纹是否与书上的指纹相似；以及实验室人员认为，死去的陆战队员身上的枪伤不可能是如叶海森在重建犯罪现场时所述，在距离死者身体五步以内开枪造成的。

法官询问杨文涛，在他家中查获的那本书是否是他用来藏匿手枪的，被告予以否认。狄思威路（Dixwell Road）警署的副督察Crowther先生告诉法庭，杨文涛被捕后，在警署看到这本书时承认该书属于他，且这一陈述是在警方未询问的情况下主动作出的。副督察Crowther的证词得到了公董局官员川岛（Kawashima，音译）先生的证实，川岛先生在杨作出自白时在场。

在讯问了另一名证人、提供导致被告被捕信息的台湾医生曾伟明（Tseng Wei-ming，音译）之后，法官宣布休庭至明天下午2时，届时预计律师将对案件进行总结陈词。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 8, 1936    152-B

“Jack, The
Korean” Up
Before Court

Makes Sudden Appear-
ance To Testify In
Nakayama Case

DENIES GUILT
IN SLAYING

Describes Relations With
“Hsiao Kwangtung”,
Pleads Alibi

Jack Hanson, better known as
“Jack, the Korean,” provided a
mild sensation in the First Special
District Court yesterday afternoon
when he appeared in the witness
stand to testify in connection with
the murder of Warrant Officer
Heideo Nakayama, of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party, on November
9 of last year.

Although he flatly denied every-
thing that has been said of him
by Yih Hai-sen (Hsiao Kwangtung)
in the latter’s various confessions
of guilt, the fact that he was finally
brought into court was something
of a surprise. In many circles, it
was beginning to be felt that “Jack,
the Korean” was a myth, but this
idea was completely dispelled when
the prosecution called him to the
stand.

He was brought into court by a
single representative of the Japan-
ese Consular Police. He wore no
handcuffs and he and his guard
occupied a seat in the rear of the
courtroom until he was called to the
stand. No one, apparently, had
noticed his presence and plenty
of hushed exclamations of amaze-
ment rippled over the crowd of
spectators occupying four benches
when his presence became known.

On Stand Over An Hour

The man was on the stand for
more than an hour, and was closely
questioned by Presiding Judge
Dunn. He spoke flawless Russian,
stating that he could speak neither
Japanese nor Chinese and that he
knew very little English. He was
born and raised in Russia, he de-
clared. His words were translated
from Russian into English and from
English into Chinese.

During his testimony, he stated
that he was a musician and had
played in orchestras in various
cabarets along North Szechuen
Road. He mentioned the Moon
Palace, Happyland and the Golden
Eagle. He never possessed a pistol,
he declared, and was in no way
connected with the murder of Heideo
Nakayama.

He admitted that he knew Yih
Hai-sen and also declared that he
had seen the latter’s friend Chow
Shu-hai. He denied ever having
seen the first accused, Yang Wan-
tzu before. He also declared that
Yih had once intimated that
he had joined the Tung Yih As-
sociation, a secret society
located on Szechuen Road, where the
murder of Nakayama is alleged to
have been planned.

Asked how long he had known
Yih, he said three years. The man
came into the Happyland Cabaret
where he was working one evening,
he declared. The court then want-
ed to know if he had not made a
trip to Tsingtao last year to see
Yih. He said he had gone to
Tsingtao but not to see Yih. A Chin-
ese friend of his in Shanghai had
given him a letter to a friend in
Tsingtao, he declared, but he did
not know Yih was the man to whom
the letter was addressed until he
reached the resort city.

Returned To Shanghai

The Korean continued that he
saw Yih and recognised him as the
man he had seen two years before
in the Happyland. Yih was nice
to him at first, he declared, and
then refused to assist him. He de-
clared that he returned to Shanghai
after that. He went to Tsingtao in
June, he added.

He then stated that he did not
see Yih until several months later
when he met him on the street.
“Yih said ‘hello’ and acted friend-
ly,” declared the Korean, “but I
told him I didn’t want to speak and
to get along. He went along.”

The witness then said that he
proceeded to the Golden Eagle
Cabaret and that about 15 minutes
later, Yih appeared with about 16
men, evidently for the purpose of
beating him up. Nothing much
happened, he added, for eight of
the men suddenly left and the
police came and ran the other eight
away.

He was arrested by the Japanese
Consular Police on February 3 of
this year, he said, but did not
know what he was arrested for.
He continued that he only knew
recently why he had been thrown
into jail and branded Yih’s state-
ments implicating him in the
Nakayama killing as nothing but a
pack of lies. He was at a house
on Hart Road on the night of the
murder, he said, and the first he
knew of the shooting was two days
later when a Russian friend he
met at the Venus Cabaret told him
about it.

Previously, the Korean had
stated that he resided on North
Szechuen Road, and when he said
that he spent the night of Novem-
ber 9 on Hart Road, the court
wanted to know if he resided at
that address. He stated that he did.
The court wanted to know about
the Szechuen Road address and he
declared that his mother lived there
and he used her quarters as his
regular address.

Denies All Guilt

He denied that he had gone to
the Tung Yih Association on the
evening of the killing and was pre-
sent when lots were drawn to see
who would take the gun. He then
repeated that he did not know about
the association and had never been
there. The witness was then dis-
missed from the stand.

The Korean was attired in a dark
blue suit and a neat purple shirt
and black tie. His head had been
shaven and he was just beginning
to get a slight growth of hair. He
was very pale and looked as though
he might have been under medical
care for a long time.

707,3
9. 7 36.

Questioned by the court, Yih re-
peated that the Korean had been
implicated in the murder. He was
just about to go into detail and
recite the whole story over again
when the court ordered him to re-
main quiet.

The session opened yesterday with
the reading of the reports of the
Judicial Laboratory concerned the
bullet, death gun and the book in
which the gun had been kept. These
reports coincided with statements
made by the Shanghai Municipal
Police experts on the same topics
except that the shot that killed
Nakayama had been fired at close
range. The report also stated that
the death gun fitted perfectly into
the book.

Yang the first accused, was again
grilled on the question of the book.
He emphatically denied that he had
ever owned it. Sub-Inspector Crow-
ther, of Dixwell Station, then re-
peated how Yang had admitted
ownership of the book at the police
station and that the later had
denied it. Detective Kagoshima, of
the S.M.P., who was present when
Yang was first shown the book, con-
firmed Inspector Crowther’s
evidence and added that “Yang
smelled the book and said it was
his.” The case was adjourned until
Friday afternoon of this week.

《字林西报》，1936年7月8日，星期三    152-B

“朝鲜人杰克”
出庭受审

突然现身作证
中山案

否认杀人罪名

描述与“小广东”的关系
提出不在场证明

杰克·汉森（Jack Hanson），更广为人知的名字是“朝鲜人杰克”，昨天下午在第一特区法院的证人席上作证，就去年11月9日日本海军陆战队准尉中山英夫（Heideo Nakayama）被杀一案提供证词，此举引起了轻微的轰动。

尽管他断然否认易海生（即“小广东”）在其多次认罪供词中对他所说的一切，但他最终被带上法庭这一事实仍令人有些意外。在许多圈子里，人们开始觉得“朝鲜人杰克”是个虚构人物，但当检方传唤他出庭作证时，这种想法被彻底打消了。

他由一名日本领事警察代表带入法庭。他没有戴手铐，他和看守坐在法庭后部的座位上，直到被传唤至证人席。显然，没有人注意到他的存在，当他的出现为人所知时，坐在四条长凳上的旁听人群中泛起了一阵压低的惊叹声。

在证人席上一个多小时

此人在证人席上待了一个多小时，并受到主审法官邓恩（Dunn）的严密盘问。他能说流利的俄语，声称自己既不会说日语也不会说中文，且英语知之甚少。他宣称自己在俄罗斯出生并长大。他的证词先从俄语译成英语，再从英语译成中文。

在作证期间，他表示自己是一名音乐家，曾在北四川路沿线的各家歌舞厅乐队中演奏。他提到了月宫（Moon Palace）、大世界（Happyland）和金鹰（Golden Eagle）。他宣称自己从未拥有过手枪，与中山英夫的被杀案毫无关联。

他承认认识易海生，并宣称见过易的朋友周树海（Chow Shu-hai，音译）。他否认以前见过第一被告杨万子（Yang Wan-tzu，音译）。他还宣称，易曾暗示自己加入了位于四川路的同义会（Tung Yih Association，音译），这是一个秘密社团，据称中山遇害案就是在那里策划的。

当被问及认识易多久时，他说三年。他宣称，有一天晚上，易来到他工作的大世界歌舞厅。随后法庭想知道他去年是否曾去青岛见易。他说他去了青岛，但不是为了见易。他宣称，他在上海的一位中国朋友给了他一封给青岛朋友的信，但直到抵达那座海滨城市，他才知道收信人就是易。

返回上海

这位朝鲜人继续说，他见到了易，并认出他就是两年前在大世界见过的那个人。他宣称，易起初对他很友好，但后来拒绝帮助他。他宣称此后便回到了上海。他补充说，他是六月去的青岛。

接着他表示，直到几个月后在街上遇到易之前，他都没再见过易。“易说了声‘你好’，表现得很友好，”这位朝鲜人宣称，“但我告诉他我不想说话，让他走开。他就走了。”

证人随后说他前往金鹰歌舞厅，大约15分钟后，易带着大约16个人出现，显然是为了殴打他。他补充说，没发生什么大事，因为其中八人突然离开，警察赶来驱散了另外八人。

他说，今年2月3日他被日本领事警察逮捕，但不知道因何被捕。他继续说，他最近才知道自己为何入狱，并称易将他牵涉进中山杀人案的陈述纯属一派胡言。他说，案发当晚他在哈特路（Hart Road）的一处住宅里，两天后，他在维纳斯歌舞厅（Venus Cabaret）遇到的一位俄国朋友告诉了他枪击之事，他才得知此事。

此前，这位朝鲜人曾声称住在北四川路，当他说11月9日晚他在哈特路度过时，法庭想知道他是否居住在该地址。他表示是的。法庭询问四川路的地址情况，他宣称他母亲住在那里，他使用母亲的住处作为其固定地址。

否认所有罪行

他否认在案发当晚去过同义会，也否认在场参与抽签决定谁持枪。他随后重申，他不了解该协会，也从未去过那里。证人随后退庭。

这位朝鲜人身穿深蓝色西装，搭配整洁的紫色衬衫和黑色领带。他的头曾被剃光，刚开始长出一点头发。他脸色非常苍白，看起来似乎长期接受医疗护理。

707,3
9. 7 36.

经法庭讯问，易重申该朝鲜人牵涉进谋杀案。他正欲详述并再次复述整个故事时，法庭命令他保持安静。

昨天的庭审始于宣读司法实验室关于子弹、致死枪支以及藏枪书籍的报告。这些报告与上海公共租界工部局警务处专家就同一主题所作的陈述相符，只是指出杀死中山的子弹是在近距离发射的。报告还指出，致死枪支可以完美地放入那本书中。

第一被告杨再次就书籍问题受到严厉盘问。他坚决否认曾拥有该书。狄思威路捕房（Dixwell Station）的副督察克劳瑟（Crowther）随后重述了杨如何在警察局承认拥有该书，而后来又予以否认的过程。当时杨首次看到该书的警务处侦探鹿儿岛（Kagoshima，音译）证实了克劳瑟督察的证词，并补充说：“杨闻了闻那本书，说是他的。”案件休庭，直至本周五下午继续审理。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY 9, 1936

Korean Appears As Witness
In Murder Trial

Hearing Adjourned Until To-morrow, Judgment Is
Expected; Korean Denies All Knowledge, Was
Ill On Night Of Murder Of The Marine

Jack, the Korean, held by Japanese Consular Police for alleged complicity in the murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama, on Darroch Road on the night of November 9, last, was finally brought as a witness before the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon. He failed, however, to throw any additional light on the case in which three Chinese are facing a murder charge. Following a lengthy hearing yesterday, Judge Dzien adjourned the trial until to-

morrow afternoon when judgment is expected to be passed.

Placed in the witness stand, Jack, who was very neatly dressed, immediately informed the court that on the night of the murder he was ill and staying at home in Hart Road. Jack spoke in Russian, his statements being first translated into English and then into Chinese.

After Jack had given his evidence, "Shao Kwangtung," the main suspect, who since the opening of the trial several months ago has confessed and again denied taking part in the crime, once again exonerated the Korean.

Another highlight of the hearing was the report of the Legal Institute of Medicine, Chengju, which was read out to the court.

The Korean, after stating that he was sick on the eventful night of November 9, last, also denied knowing Yang Wen-tao, the Cantonese accused and former president of the now defunct Tung Yi Association. The Korean denied being a member of the association and entered a categorical denial when asked whether he had drawn lots to decide who should murder a Japanese officer. "I only know of the murder from the papers," stated the Korean.

He admitted once having a fight with "Shao Kwangtung" and the latter's supporters, but stated that he was not injured, due to the timely arrival of the police. He sought his revenge, but could not find "Shao Kwangtung." He admitted meeting "Shao Kwangtung" in Tsingtao, but denied that he went there for the express purpose of seeing him.

Repudiates Statements

"Shao Kwangtung" repudiated all his former statements, trying to exonerate Jack. He said that Jack had not participated in the drawing of lots before the murder to decide as to who should do the killing. He confessed that he had collected about him 16 men and explained that the fight did not develop to any serious proportions.

The results of the findings of the Legal Institute of Medicine, Chenju in regard to the bullet allegedly used in the murder and the book hollowed at the centre to fit with the pistol, were read in court. It was a long document prepared on a scientific basis. It was revealed that the book hollowed at the centre, which was found in Yang's home, had none of his fingerprints. The judicial doctors admitted that, after careful examinations, they could not find out how long ago the book had been hollowed out at the centre as the hollowed centre itself had not been exposed to the daylight.

As to the bullet shell, the experts did not actually state that it had gone through the body of the Japanese sailor. Although it was not blood stained when examined it might have been used in a close range shooting. The judicial doctors had shot a living dog to prove that after being shot at close range the bullet shell came out without bearing any blood. This finding contradicted the statement made by "Shao Kwangtung" who asserted that the sailor was shot five feet away.

Not His Book

When questioned by the judge at the opening of the hearing, Yang Wen-tao still refused to recognize the book hollowed at the centre and seized by the police at his home as being his property. His book was said to be an English book with no Chinese characters on the cover although its colour and size looked the same as the one found by the police. He alleged that if the book was found in his home it must have been changed by Yang Gien-chun, his enemy who once visited his home and saw the book.

Yang admitted that at the police station he recognized the book as his, but he did not see it clearly. Detective Sub-Inspector Crowther, of the Dixwell Road Police Station, and a Japanese officer attached to the same station testified that Yang saw the book clearly at the police station. The book was placed on a desk near which Yang sat. The Japanese officer even said that Yang smelled the book and said that it was his. Yang was also alleged to have said that he had hollowed out the book at the centre to put his licenced pistol in to avoid the danger of it being found by his children.

Two More Witnesses

The Assistant Municipal Advocate, Mr. Paul Ru, told the court that two witnesses whom the police desired to call had gone to outports. He said that after being examined by experts of the Municipal Police the pistol found near Nakayama's body was turned over to the Japanese marine authorities for an examination on November 10, of last year, one day after the murder. The pistol had been kept by the Japanese for nine days. Besides these nine days the weapon had always been in the custody of the police. Although a Japanese sailor Kita saw Nakayama lying on the ground and reported the matter to his superiors he only did so after the police had already arrived at the scene of crime. Kita did not walk with Nakayama.

Tseng Wei-min, who claimed to be a Formosan and who was the first to report the case to the police, appeared to tell his story. He denied the statement made by Chang Shun that the case was a frame-up. He was not a fairy and so he could not invent a story like this, he said. He admitted, however, that he got all his evidence from other men, including Tseng Yuan.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年7月9日，星期四

韩国人作为证人出庭
在谋杀案审判中

听证会休庭至明日，预计将作出判决；韩国人否认知情，称海军陆战队员遇害当晚他正患病

去年11月9日晚，在达罗克路（Darroch Road）涉嫌共谋杀害海军士官中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）而被日本领事馆警察拘留的韩国人杰克（Jack），于昨日下午终于作为证人被带至第一特区地方法院。然而，他未能就三名中国人面临谋杀指控的案件提供任何新的线索。经过昨日的长时间听证，迪恩法官（Judge Dzien）宣布休庭至明日下午，届时预计将宣判。

杰克衣着十分整洁，站上证人席后立即向法庭陈述，在谋杀案发生的当晚，他因病待在家中，地点位于哈特路（Hart Road）。杰克使用俄语发言，其陈述先被译成英语，随后再译成中文。

在杰克作证之后，主要嫌疑人“邵广东”（Shao Kwangtung）再次为这名韩国人开脱。“邵广东”自数月庭审开始以来，曾承认参与犯罪后又予以否认。

听证的另一个焦点是宣读呈交法庭的法医学院（Legal Institute of Medicine）陈居（Chengju，音译）的报告。

这名韩国人在陈述自己于去年11月9日那个多事之秋的夜晚患病后，还否认认识被控的广东人杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao），即现已解散的同义会前会长。该韩国人否认自己是该会成员，并在被问及是否通过抽签决定由谁去刺杀一名日本军官时，断然予以否认。该韩国人称：“我只是从报纸上得知这起谋杀案。”

他承认曾与“邵广东”及其支持者发生过一次斗殴，但表示由于警察及时赶到，他并未受伤。他曾试图报复，但未能找到“邵广东”。他承认曾在青岛见过“邵广东”，但否认去青岛是专门为了见他。

推翻先前供词

“邵广东”推翻了之前所有的供词，试图为杰克开脱。他说，杰克并未参与谋杀前的抽签以决定由谁行凶。他承认自己召集了约16人，并解释说斗殴并未发展成严重的局面。

法庭宣读了法医学院陈居（Chenju，音译）关于据称用于谋杀的子弹以及中心被挖空以适配手枪的书本的鉴定结果。这是一份基于科学依据撰写的长篇文件。结果显示，在杨家搜出的中心被挖空的书本上，没有发现他的任何指纹。法医承认，经过仔细检查，他们无法确定书本中心是何时被挖空的，因为挖空部分本身未暴露于日光下。

至于弹壳，专家并未明确断定它穿过了那名日本水兵的躯体。虽然检查时弹壳上没有血迹，但它可能是在近距离射击中使用的。法医通过射杀一只活狗来证明，近距离射击后，弹出的弹壳上并不带有血迹。这一发现与“邵广东”的供述相矛盾，后者声称水兵是在五英尺外被枪击的。

并非他的书

在听证会开始时接受法官讯问时，杨文涛仍拒绝承认警方在他家中搜获的中心被挖空的书本归其所有。据说他的书是一本英文书，封面上没有汉字，尽管其颜色和尺寸与警方查获的那本看起来相同。他声称，如果这本书是在他家发现的，那一定是被他的仇人杨健春（Yang Gien-chun，音译）调换了，此人曾去过他家并见过这本书。

杨文涛承认，他在警察局时曾认出该书是他的，但他当时没看清楚。狄思威路（Dixwell Road）巡捕房的侦探副督察克劳瑟（Crowther）以及隶属于同一巡捕房的一名日本警官作证称，杨文涛在警察局清楚地看到了这本书。书本被放在一张桌子上，杨文涛就坐在旁边。那名日本警官甚至说，杨文涛闻了闻那本书，并说是他的。据称杨文涛还表示，他将书本中心挖空是为了存放他的持枪许可证下的手枪，以避免被孩子们发现而产生危险。

另外两名证人

市助理检察官保罗·鲁（Paul Ru）先生告诉法庭，警方希望传唤的两名证人已前往外地港口。他说，在去年谋杀案发生次日，即11月10日，经工部局警务处专家检验后，在中山尸体附近发现的手枪已移交给日本海军当局进行检验。该手枪由日方保管了九天。除这九天外，该武器一直由警方保管。虽然一名名叫北田（Kita）的日本水兵看见中山躺在地上并向其上级报告，但他这样做时警察已经到达了犯罪现场。北田并未与中山同行。

自称是台湾人的曾为民（Tseng Wei-min）是第一个向警方报案的人，他出庭讲述了自己的经历。他否认了张顺（Chang Shun）关于此案是栽赃陷害的说法。他说，他不是神仙，编造不出这样的故事。然而，他承认自己的所有证据都来自其他人，包括曾元（Tseng Yuan）。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, JULY 7, 1936

Nakayama Was Shot At Close
Range, Experts State

Completely contradicting the
confession made by "Shao Kwang-
tung," the alleged slayer of
Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese
Naval Landing force on Darroch
Road on the evening of November
9, last, experts of the Legal
Institute of Medicine, it is under-
stood, will state in court to-
morrow afternoon that the Japan-
ese marine was shot at a very
close range.
This statement, according to
Chinese reports, will be made in
court to-morrow afternoon when
the three suspects will be brought
up for trial before Judge Dz'en
in the First Special District
Court. The officials of the Legal
Institute of Medicine, it is under-
stood, have completed their ex-
amination of the bullet allegedly
used in the murder and the hol-
lowed-out book, in which the pistol
was supposed to have been hidden.
It is also reported that the
Japanese Consular Police will to-
morrow bring Jack, the Korean
suspect, to court to testify. Pre-
viously the Japanese refused to
produce the Korean as a witness
on the plea that they had not
concluded their investigations. It
is believed that the questioning of
Jack will throw some additional
light on the case.
It is understood that investiga-
tion revealed that no finger-
prints of Yang Wen-tao, the
Cantonese accused, have been
found on the hollowed-out book
seized on his premises. Many
fingerprints were found on the
book, but not one of these be-
longed to Yang Wen-tao.
"Shao Kwangtung," Yang Wen-
tao and a cabaret employee named
Chao Sha-yung, are facing trial
on charges of having murdered
the Japanese marine.

《字林西报》，1936年7月7日，星期二

专家称中山系近距离被射杀

据悉，法医学院的专家将于明日下午在法庭上陈述，日本海军陆战队员是在极近距离被射杀的，这与据称于去年11月9日晚在达罗克路杀害日本海军登陆部队成员中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）的凶手“邵广东”（Shao Kwang-tung）的供词完全矛盾。

据中文媒体报道，这一陈述将于明日下午在法庭上作出，届时三名嫌疑人将被提审，由第一特区地方法院的迪恩法官（Judge Dz'en）审理。据悉，法医学院的官员已完成对据称用于谋杀的子弹以及据信藏匿手枪的挖空书本的检查。

另有报道称，日本领事馆警察将于明日将韩国嫌疑人杰克带至法庭作证。此前，日本方面以调查尚未结束为由，拒绝让该韩国人作为证人出庭。人们相信，对杰克的讯问将为该案提供一些新的线索。

据悉，调查显示，在广东籍被告杨文涛住所搜获的挖空书本上，未发现杨文涛的指纹。书上发现了许多指纹，但没有一个属于杨文涛。

“邵广东”、杨文涛以及一名名为赵少勇（Chao Sha-yung，音译）的舞厅雇员，正面临谋杀该名日本海军陆战队员的指控并接受审判。

中山案定于周三审理

与三名中国人被租界警察拘留有关的中山案听证会，定于周三恢复审理，因法医学院已完成对子弹及据信藏匿手枪的书本的研究工作。据报道，日本当局最终已同意允许一名同样被指控犯有此罪的韩国人杰克出庭。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, JULY 4, 1936

Nakayama Slayer Suspects To
Face Court Again Wednesday

After an adjournment of nearly three weeks, the Nakayama Murder Trial will resume in the First Special District Court next Wednesday, THE CHINA PRESS learned last night.

At the hearing the reports of the Judicial Laboratories on the death bullet and the book in which the gun, which was alleged to have killed the Japanese Warrant Officer on Darroch Road Nov. 9, 1935, was supposed to be hidden, will be presented to the court.

In the dock to answer the murder charge will be Yih Hai-seng, better known as "Hsiao Kwangtung," Yang Wen-tao, local Cantonese merchant, and Chow Shan-yung, "bouncer" of the Continental Ballroom.

The trial was adjourned June 18 to enable the Court laboratories to complete their examinations of the bullet and the book.

At Wednesday's hearing the laboratory report will deal with whether the bullet ever was smeared with human blood. The experts were requested to find out if the blood, in case it was erased, could still be visible to the scientific eye.

Also, the judges directed the laboratory technicians to find out whether the rust mark found on the green book found in Yang Wen-tao's home came from the gun which the police alleged as the weapon that killed Hideo Nakayama.

《大美晚报》，1936年7月4日，星期六

中山案嫌疑人将于周三再次出庭

《大美晚报》昨晚获悉，在中断近三周后，中山谋杀案审判将于下周三在第一特区地方法院恢复审理。

在听证会上，司法实验室关于致死子弹以及据信藏匿了1935年11月9日在达罗克路 allegedly 杀害日本海军士官的手枪的书本的报告，将呈交法庭。

站在被告席上回答谋杀指控的将是易海生（Yih Hai-seng，更广为人知的名字是“小广东” Hsiao Kwangtung）、本地广东商人杨文涛，以及大陆舞厅（Continental Ballroom）的保镖周山勇（Chow Shan-yung，音译）。

审判于6月18日休庭，以便法院实验室完成对子弹和书本的检查。

在周三的听证会上，实验室报告将涉及子弹是否曾沾染人血。专家被要求查明，如果血液曾被擦除，是否仍能在科学检测下显现。

此外，法官指示实验室技术人员查明，在杨文涛家中发现的绿色书本上发现的锈迹，是否来自警方指称为杀害中山秀夫凶器的那把手枪。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, JUNE 4, 1936S. B. REGIST
S. B. D.

YIH HAI-SEN TO BE
HELD AT STATION

X-Ray Examination Reveals
No Key in His Stomach

SEIZED BOOK AND PISTOL
SENT TO CHENJU

An X-Ray examination of Yih
Hai-sen, alias "Little Cantonese," one
of three men accused of murdering
H. Nakayama, Japanese marine, con-
ducted jointly by the Municipal and
Court doctors, revealed that there
was no trace of keys or other metals
in the prisoner's body, contrary to
his statement last week that he had
twice attempted to commit suicide
at police station by swallowing keys.
It was officially disclosed in the
First Special District Court yesterday
when the hearing was resumed of
the case against Yih and his alleged
two accomplices, Yang Ven-tao and
Chow Zeu-yoong.

The Court doctor's report was read
by court clerk and, according to this,
there were bruises between Yih's
sixth, seventh and eighth ribs,
caused not by beating, but by what
were believed to be rubbing with
soft things. The prosecution pointed
out that it could not prove torture
as it was not mentioned how these
bruises had come. The prosecution
then submitted to the court reports
in this respect prepared by both
foreign and Chinese detectives work-
ing on this case. The contents of
these reports were not disclosed.

Questioned by the Judge, Yih
insisted that he had swallowed keys
in attempts to end his life and
mentioned that the attempts were
after his first and second confessions
respectively. Regarding the bruises
on his body, the accused alleged
that, during the two weeks' adjourn-
ment of the case, he was once
tortured by pouring water into his
nose and at the same time rub-
bing his ribs. The accused alleged
he was bound to a bench when he
was tortured and he could not tell
who did this because his eyes were
blindfolded.

An application was made by
counsel for defence for Yih's deten-
tion in the Court's detention house
during the period of adjournment,
but the Judge overruled this, point-
ing out that there was no detention
house in court for criminal cases.
Mr. G. R. Grove, lawyer for Yang
Ven-tao, asked for his client's re-
moval to hospital, but his request
was likewise rejected by the Judge
who mentioned that if, as Yang
alleged, there were torture, the de-
tectives concerned would be respon-
sible but it was a separate question.
Mr. Grove protested and cited the
Tsai Yang-gee case.

To show that the prisoners had
not been ill-treated while they were
held by the police, Mr. Paul Y. Ru,
Assistant Municipal Advocate, who
conducted the prosecution, told the
Judge that detectives working on
this case were attached to Dixwell
Road Police Station, but, since he
was arrested in Tsingtao and brought
here, Yih Hai-sen had been detained
at Chengtu Road Station. As to
Yang, he had been detained at the
Central Station. Mr. Ru said that
detectives of both Chengtu and
Central Stations had nothing what-
ever to do with investigations in
this case, and he could not believe
that they would have tortured the
accused in this case. As a matter
of fact, Yih Hai-sen, while he was
held at the station, was given better
treatment than other prisoners
because he was allowed to smoke
cigarettes and take any kind of food
he desired, Mr. Ru said.

After much argument over the
place of detention, the Judge turned
down the request for the prisoners'
detention in the Court's civil deten-
tion house and ordered that they be
returned to police station custody.
The Judge announced that the hear-
ing was to be adjourned sine die
because he had sent the seized spent
bullet, pistol and book to the Chenju
Judicial Laboratory for further ex-
aminations and it would take some
time to receive a report.

Jack, the Korean, did not appear
in court as a witness despite the
Judge's request that he be brought
before him yesterday for questioning,
the Japanese consular officials hav-
ing told the police that they had not
yet completed their inquiries.

《字林西报》，1936年6月4日，星期四。S. B. 登记
S. B. D.

叶海森将被羁押于警局

X光检查显示其胃内无钥匙

查获的书籍和手枪已送交陈菊（音译）

由工部局医生和法院医生联合对叶海森（别名“小广东”）进行的X光检查显示，该囚犯体内没有钥匙或其他金属的痕迹，这与他上周声称曾两次在警局吞食钥匙试图自杀的说法相反。叶海森是被控谋杀日本海军陆战队员H. Nakayama的三名男子之一。

昨日，第一特区地方法院恢复审理叶海森及其两名 alleged 同伙杨文道（音译）和周祖荣（音译）的案件时，官方披露了上述情况。

法庭书记员宣读了法院医生的报告，根据该报告，叶海森的第六、第七和第八肋骨之间有瘀伤，据信并非由殴打造成，而是由软物摩擦所致。检方指出，由于未说明这些瘀伤是如何造成的，因此无法证明存在酷刑。随后，检方向法庭提交了负责此案的外国和中国侦探就此问题准备的报告。这些报告的内容未予公开。

在法官讯问下，叶海森坚持称他吞下钥匙是为了结束生命，并提到这些尝试分别是在他第一次和第二次供认之后进行的。关于身上的瘀伤，被告声称，在案件休庭的两周期间，他曾遭受过一次往鼻子里灌水并同时摩擦肋骨的酷刑。被告称，受刑时他被绑在长凳上，由于眼睛被蒙住，他无法说出是谁干的。

辩护律师申请在休庭期间将叶海森羁押于法院拘留所，但法官驳回了这一申请，指出法院没有用于刑事案件的拘留所。杨文道的律师G. R. Grove先生要求将其当事人移送医院，但该请求同样被法官驳回，法官提到，如果如杨所称存在酷刑，相关侦探将承担责任，但这是一个单独的问题。Grove先生提出抗议，并引用了蔡阳吉（音译）案。

为了表明囚犯在被警方拘留期间未受到虐待，负责公诉的助理市政检察官Paul Y. Ru先生告诉法官，负责此案的侦探隶属于狄思威路（现溧阳路）警察局，但是，叶海森在青岛被捕并被带到这里后，一直羁押在成都路警察局。至于杨，他一直羁押于中央捕房。Ru先生说，成都路和中央捕房的侦探与此案的调查毫无关系，他不相信他们会对此案被告施以酷刑。事实上，Ru先生说，叶海森在警局被拘留期间，待遇比其他囚犯要好，因为他被允许吸烟，并可食用任何他想吃的食物。

经过关于拘留地点的激烈辩论后，法官驳回了将囚犯羁押于法院民事拘留所的请求，并命令将他们交还警方拘留。法官宣布，听证会将无限期休庭，因为他已将查获的弹壳、手枪和书籍送往陈菊（音译）司法实验室进行进一步检查，收到报告需要一些时间。

尽管法官要求昨天将朝鲜人“Jack”带到庭前接受讯问，但他并未作为证人出庭，日本领事官员告知警方，他们的调查尚未完成。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, June 4, 1936

Torture Charges
Not Verified

Physician's Testimony
Fails To Indicate
Yih Maltreated

Yih Hal-sen, alias "Shao Kwangtung", is back in detention cells at Chengtu Road Police Station, and Yang Wen-tao is in Central today following a resumed hearing in the First Distric. Court yesterday afternoon of the case against Yih and two alleged accomplices connected with the murder of H. Nakayama, Japanese marine. The hearing was marked by testimony as to alleged torture methods employed by police to force confession of the crime.

It was brought out by court physicians that an X-ray examination of Yih revealed no trace of keys or other metals in the prisoner's body, contrary to his statement last week that he had attempted to commit suicide at the station to avoid further third-degree methods. The doctor said that he had found bruises on Yih's ribs, apparently made by rubbing with "soft things," but this could not prove torture.

Yih declared that he had been tortured by having water poured into his nose and by rubbing of his ribs. He added that lighted cigarettes had been stuck in his nose and his lip had been burned. He said he was blindfolded at the time and could not see his persecutors.

The session was marked by arguments between prosecution and defense regarding place of future detention, and the judge finally ordered the prisoners to be sent back to police cells. The Korean, "Jack," did not appear at the hearing, as Japanese Consular Police declared that they have not yet completed their inquiries.

叶海森（别名“小广东”）在昨日下午第一特区地方法院恢复审理针对叶某及两名涉嫌与谋杀日本海军陆战队员H. Nakayama有关的同伙的案件后，已回到成都路警察局的拘留牢房，杨文道今日则在中央捕房。听证会的焦点是关于警方为逼供而采用的所谓酷刑手段的证词。

法院医生指出，对叶某的X光检查显示，其体内没有钥匙或其他金属的痕迹，这与他上周声称为避免进一步的“第三度审讯”手段而在警局试图自杀的说法相反。医生说，他发现叶某肋骨上有瘀伤，显然是由“软物”摩擦造成的，但这不能证明存在酷刑。

叶某宣称，他遭受了往鼻子里灌水和摩擦肋骨的酷刑。他还补充说，点燃的香烟被塞进他的鼻子，他的嘴唇被烫伤。他说当时他的眼睛被蒙住，看不见迫害者。

会议期间，控辩双方就未来的拘留地点发生了争论，法官最终命令将囚犯送回警察牢房。朝鲜人“Jack”未出席听证会，因为日本领事警察声明他们尚未完成调查。

pages.en:
14 . 9 .
THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, JUNE 4, 1936

Death Suspect
Testifies To
Police Torture

‘HsiaoKwangtung’ Takes
Stand In Nakayama
Murder Trial

Alleged police torture again took the spotlight at a brief session of the Nakayama murder trial at the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon.

Reiterating that his previous confessions admitting that he killed Japanese Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama on Darroch Road, Nov. 9, 1935, were forced through the application of third-degree methods, Yih Hai-sen, better known as “Hsiao Kwangtung,” told the Court that he was blind-folded and given various punishments by officers.

Yih appeared in the prisoners' dock yesterday with the two other accused, Yang Wen-tao, prominent local Cantonese, and Chow Yao-yoong, a “bouncer” of the Continental Ballroom.

During a two-week remand, Yih said, he was tied to a bench by police officers who forced water through his nostrils.

“Couldn’t Breathe”

“I couldn’t breath when the water was poured into my nose,” Yih told the Court. Glancing toward the side where the police officers were sitting, “Hsiao Kwangtung” said to the judges, “the punishment was more painful when they rubbed my ribs with their knuckles.”

He further stated that lighted cigarettes were inserted into his nose and that the wounds on his lower lip was a burn inflicted by a live butt.

Yih admitted when questioned by Judge Dzien that he could not identify the officers whom he alleged tortured him. He was blind-folded, he said.

The medical report of the doctor attached to the First Special District Court, made public at the hearing yesterday, indicated that the sixth, seventh and eighth ribs of Yih showed signs of being rubbed with some soft articles.

Regarding the wound on “Hsiao Kwangtung’s” lip, the doctor limited his observation by saying that the mark was clean-cut and might have been inflicted about two or three weeks ago.

After an X-ray examination conducted by the physician sent by the S.M.P., the Court doctor reported that he could not locate any keys and hooks in Yih’s intestines.

“Hsiao Kwangtung” in a hearing last Wednesday claimed that he swallowed three metal articles in attempted suicide.

Lawyers Battle

Yesterday’s short session was marked by lively arguments between the Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Y. Ru and the defense lawyers.

On several occasions the opposing lawyers wr it into a verbal tangle on the third-degree allegations and also when the defense attorneys insisted that the prisoners be brought by the police into the custody of the Court.

Answering further statements that Yih was manhandled by police, Mr. Ru revealed that the accused was given special treatment by officers in charge.

Unlike other prisoners, he said, Yih was allowed to pick the food he liked and given cigarettes to smoke.

The charge of torture, he continued, had been thoroughly investigated by police authorities. These investigations, he stated, could not reveal any evidence to substantiate the charge. Reports on the handling of the prisoners have been written by every member of the police staff connected with the case and submitted to the court, the prosecution pointed out.

Heatedly maintaining that torture was applied, the lawyers for the defense replied by asking that the three accused be turned over to the Court detention cells from the police. This motion, strenuously objected to by the prosecution, was overruled by the Court.

Petition Denied

Also, Judge Dzien turned down a petition from Mrs. Yang Wen-tao asking that her husband be sent to the hospital for examination of wounds allegedly inflicted by police.

In ordering a remand yesterday for an indefinite period, Judge Dzien disclosed that the murder gun, the death bullet and the book in which the pistol was alleged to be hidden before the killing were handed over to Court officials for study.

An examination will be made, the Judge stated, to ascertain rust marks in the book and the blue pencil mark outlining the pistol-shaped cut-out in the green volume. The bullet will be examined to see whether any blood-stain, after being wiped out, can still be visible through scientific means.

Chang Sen, a witness who figured prominently in a frame-up allegation, was called back to the stand and questioned regarding a certain Yang Chien-tsung, who Yang Wen-tao alleged was the man who “planted” the green book to “frame” him

14 . 9 .
《大美晚报》，1936年6月4日，星期四

死亡嫌疑犯
作证指控
警方酷刑

“小广东”在中山
谋杀案审判中
出庭作证

昨日下午在第一特区地方法院举行的中山谋杀案审判简短庭审中，所谓的警方酷刑再次成为焦点。

叶海森（更广为人知的名字是“小广东”）重申，他之前承认于1935年11月9日在达罗克路杀害日本准尉Hideo Nakayama的供认是通过“第三度审讯”手段强迫作出的，他告诉法庭，他被蒙住眼睛，并受到警官的各种惩罚。

叶某昨日与另外两名被告出现在被告席上，他们是当地著名的广东人杨文道，以及大陆舞厅的保镖周耀荣（音译）。

叶某说，在为期两周的还押期间，他被警官绑在长凳上，警官强行通过他的鼻孔灌水。

“无法呼吸”

“当水灌进我的鼻子时，我无法呼吸，”叶某告诉法庭。“小广东”瞥了一眼警官坐的一侧，对法官说：“当他们用指关节摩擦我的肋骨时，惩罚更加痛苦。”

他进一步陈述，点燃的香烟被插入他的鼻子，下唇上的伤口是由燃烧的烟头造成的烧伤。

当Dzien法官讯问时，叶某承认他无法指认他指控对其施以酷刑的警官。他说，当时他的眼睛被蒙住了。

第一特区地方法院附属医生的医疗报告在昨日的听证会上公开，报告显示叶某的第六、第七和第八肋骨有被某些软物摩擦的迹象。

关于“小广东”嘴唇上的伤口，医生的观察仅限于说伤口切口整齐，可能是在两到三周前造成的。

在由工部局警务处派遣的医生进行X光检查后，法院医生报告说，他未在叶某的肠道中发现任何钥匙和钩子。

“小广东”在上周三的听证会上声称，他在试图自杀时吞下了三件金属物品。

律师激辩

昨日的短暂庭审以助理市政检察官Paul Y. Ru与辩护律师之间的激烈辩论为标志。

反对派律师几次陷入关于“第三度审讯”指控的口舌之争，此外，当辩护律师坚持要求警方将囚犯移交给法院羁押时，也发生了争执。

针对有关叶某被警方粗暴对待的进一步陈述，Ru先生透露，负责看守的警官给予了被告特殊待遇。

他说，与其他囚犯不同，叶某被允许挑选他喜欢的食物，并获得香烟吸食。

他继续说，警方当局已对酷刑指控进行了彻底调查。他指出，这些调查未能揭示任何证据来证实该指控。检方指出，与该案有关的每一位警务人员都撰写了关于处理囚犯情况的报告，并提交给法庭。

辩护律师激烈地坚持认为使用了酷刑，并要求将三名被告从警方移交给法院拘留牢房。这一动议遭到检方的强烈反对，并被法院驳回。

请愿被拒

此外，Dzien法官驳回了杨文道夫人的请愿，她要求将其丈夫送往医院，以检查据称由警方造成的伤口。

在昨日下令无限期还押时，Dzien法官透露，杀人凶器、致死子弹以及据称在杀人前藏匿手枪的书籍已移交给法院官员进行研究。

法官 stated，将进行检查以确定书中的锈迹，以及绿色卷册中勾勒出手枪形状切口的蓝色铅笔痕迹。将对子弹进行检查，以查看擦拭后是否仍能通过科学手段看到任何血迹。

张森（音译），一名在诬陷指控中扮演重要角色的证人，被重新传唤出庭，并就一名杨建宗（音译）接受讯问，杨文道指控此人就是“种植”绿色书籍以“陷害”他的人。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, JUNE 3, 1936

Nakayama Case
Hearing Will
Resume Today

New Charges Of Police
Torture Are
Levelled

With new charges levelled at the police of forcing confessions through torture, the resumption of the Nakayama murder trial at the First Special District Court this afternoon is watched with interest by the Shanghai public.

At today's hearing, the medical report on the examination of Yih Hai-sen, better known as "Hsiao Kwangtung," who charged in Court last Wednesday that his previous confessions were extracted through third degree methods, is expected to be made public.

Yih, who retracted his statements that he killed Japanese Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama on Darroch Road November 9, 1935, also claimed that he swallowed various metal articles in an attempted suicide.

To add to this charge of police torture, Yang Wen-tao, facing the same murder charge as Yih, is understood to have petitioned the Court through his counsel, Mr. G. R. Grove, to have him removed to the Police Hospital from the detention quarters at the Central Station. Yang also alleged that he suffered maltreatment at the hands of police.

It was learned, however, that a request has been made to the police by the Court to have "Jack" brought before the Tribunal from Japanese Consular Police custody. Previously, the Japanese authorities said that they would assist in the case and that "Jack" would be arrested and brought up.

《大美晚报》，1936年6月3日，星期三

中山案
听证会将
于今日恢复

新的警方
酷刑指控
被提出

随着对警方通过酷刑逼供的新指控被提出，上海公众饶有兴趣地关注着今天下午在第一特区地方法院恢复的中山谋杀案审判。

THE CHINA PRESS, TUESDAY, JUNE 2, 1936

Physicians Give
Yih Examination

Result Of Medical Test
Not Released By
S.M.C., Police

A solid wall of reticence today confronted press representatives of the medical examination given seeking information on the results Yih Hai-sen, alias Shao Kwang-tung, whose retraction of his confession that he killed Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party and whose charges of torture in hands of police caused a stir in the First District Court Wednesday morning.

The authorities are not prepared to issue any information concerning the examination which was known to have been conducted at the Police Hospital of the Shanghai Municipal Council under the joint supervision of Dr. Wei Lin-kung of the Chinese court, a Japanese physician from the Foo Min Hospital and doctors of the S.M.C. on Thursday. A report is expected to be sent to the court when it resumes the hearing of the three Cantonese charged with having murdered the Japanese marine.

From private sources, it was reported that Yih was given an X-Ray examination to ascertain his claim that he had swallowed a key, a buckle and buttons in attempts to end his own life. Nothing was found, however. A mental test given Yih revealed that he is sound and sane. Regarding the torture charge, a few bruises were found in his body, it is said.

No date has yet been set for the resumption of the trial. The last hearing was conducted on Wednesday when Yih, bursting into tears, retracted his confession of having killed Nakayama and charged that he has been tortured. In his previous statement he said that he and the other accused had plotted the murder of a Japanese and that he was the man who fired the shots at Nakayama, killing the Japanese on Darroch Road on November 9 last year.

《字林西报》，1936年6月2日，星期二

医生对叶海森进行检查

工部局警务处未公布体检结果

今日，面对试图获取叶海森（又名邵广东）体检结果信息的新闻界代表，当局保持着一道沉默的坚墙。叶海森撤回了其杀害日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄的供词，并指控在警方手中遭受酷刑，此事于周三上午在第一特区地方法院引起了轰动。

当局目前不愿发布任何关于此次检查的信息。据悉，该检查于周四在公共租界工部局警察医院举行，由中国法院的魏立功医生、福民医院的一名日本医生以及工部局的医生共同监督。预计当法院恢复审理三名被控谋杀日本海军陆战队员的广东人时，会将一份报告提交给法院。

据私人消息来源报道，为核实叶海森声称吞下钥匙、皮带扣和纽扣以图自杀的说法，对其进行了X光检查。然而，并未发现任何异物。对叶海森进行的精神测试显示，他神志清醒且精神正常。至于酷刑指控，据说在其身上发现了几处瘀伤。

复审日期尚未确定。上次听证会于周三进行，当时叶海森泪流满面，撤回了杀害中山的供词，并指控自己遭受了酷刑。在他之前的陈述中，他说自己与其他被告密谋杀害一名日本人，并且是他向中山开枪，于去年11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）将该日本人杀死。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, June 1, 1936

Chinese Held
For Nakayama
Killing X-rayed

Keys, Hooks Alleged
Swallowed Not
Revealed

Doctors who X-rayed Yih Hai-sen, better known as "Hsiao Kwang-tung," could not find the keys and hooks which he claimed to have swallowed in various attempts at suicide, private sources stated yesterday.

Yih, who retracted his previous confessions that he killed Japanese Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama and charged that his statement was forced through police torture at a hearing at the First Special District Court last week, is still being detained at the Police Hospital on the order of the tribunal.

While the officials in charge of the case continued to be silent regarding the finding of the physicians, information from other sources stated that a few bruises were found on Yih's body.

Following the order given by Judge Tsien of the First Special District Court, an X-ray examination was made by Dr. Wei Lin-kaung, a member of the medical staff of the tribunal, together with a doctor of the Police Hospital and a Japanese physician from the Foo Ming Hospital.

The doctors also conducted a mental test and Yih was said to have been found sane.

A complete medical report of the findings is expected to be sent to the Court when it resumes hearing on the Nakayama murder case.

At last Wednesday's hearing, "Hsiao Kwangtung," with tears streaming down his cheeks, denied he had any knowledge of the killing. He charged police torture and bared his chest to show the court the alleged wounds.

Yih's lawyer also entered a plea that the accused, as evidenced by his conflicting statements, was mentally unsound. The defense requested that Yih be sent to a hospital for examination.

Adjourned for a week, the Nakayama murder case in which Yang Wen-tao, prominent Cantonese merchant, and Chow Yao-yung, "bouncer" of the Continental Ballroom, were also charged with the killing, is scheduled to be reopened at the First Special District Court tomorrow.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年6月1日，星期一

涉嫌杀害中山的中国人被拘押并接受X光检查

据称吞下的钥匙和钩子未被发现

据私人消息来源昨日称，对叶海森（更广为人知的名字是“小广东”）进行X光检查的医生未能找到他声称在各种自杀企图吞下的钥匙和钩子。

叶海森在上周第一特区地方法院的听证会上，撤回了此前承认杀害日本准尉中山秀雄的供词，并指控其供述是在警方酷刑下被迫作出的，目前仍根据法庭命令被拘留在警察医院。

虽然负责此案的官员对医生的检查结果继续保持着沉默，但其他来源的消息称，在叶海森身上发现了几处瘀伤。

遵照第一特区地方法院钱法官的命令，由法庭医务人员魏立功医生、警察医院的一名医生以及福民医院的一名日本医生共同进行了X光检查。

医生们还进行了精神测试，据说叶海森被认定神志正常。

完整的医疗检查报告预计将在法院恢复审理中山谋杀案时提交给法院。

叶海森的律师也提出抗辩，称被告前后矛盾的陈述证明其精神不健全。辩护方请求将叶海森送往医院进行检查。

中山谋杀案休庭一周，该案中著名的广东商人杨文涛和大陆舞厅的保镖周耀荣也被控参与杀人，定于明天在第一特区地方法院重新开庭。

June 1, 1936. Morning Translation.

Lih Pao (立報) of May 31 :-
THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE: THE DOCTOR'S EXAMINATION OF YIH HAI SUNG

On May 27, during the hearing of the case against Yih Hai Sung (葉海生) (alias Siao Kwangtung 小廣東) and others charged in the Nakayama murder case, Yih stated that he was wrongfully accused and that in an attempt to commit suicide he had swallowed two keys while under detention at the Police Station and that the keys were still in his body and that he was feeling sick. The Court ordered that he be sent to the Municipal Hospital for treatment and examination by the Municipal Doctor in conjunction with the Court Doctor.
On May 30 a reporter of this paper interviewed Dr. Wei Lih Koong (魏立功) of the 1st Special District Court and asked him about the result of the examination of Yih Hai Sung.
The doctor smiled and said, "The press should not treat such a small thing seriously. It should pay attention to really important events. As regards Yih Hai Sung, I went on Thursday morning (May 28) to the Municipal Hospital and examined him carefully by scientific means in conjunction with the Municipal Doctor. During the examination, a doctor from the Foo Min Hospital was also present. I made a report on the result of the examination to the Court to-day (May 30). The contents of the report cannot be divulged at present, but will probably be made public at the next hearing of the case."

Lih Pao of June 1 :-

As Yih Hai Sung, one of the suspects in the Nakayama murder case, stated that he had swallowed some keys at the Police Station in order to commit suicide, he was ordered to be sent to the S.M.C. Hospital for examination by Judge Chien Hung Nieh (錢鴻業), Chief of the Criminal Division of the Shanghai First Special District Court. A joint medical examination was held on Thursday last by Wei Lih Kung (魏立功), the Court doctor, and the doctors of the S.M.C. Hospital and the Foo Ming Hospital. All the parties concerned refuse to disclose the results of this examination.
According to reliable information secured by a reporter of this newspaper as a result of exhaustive enquiries, the latest medical method was employed in the joint examination by the Chinese, foreign and Japanese doctors and as a result, Yih Hai Sung was found to have sustained some slight injuries to his body, but no keys were discovered in his stomach (X Rays was used), nor was he suffering from nervous breakdown, although he is very weak and low-spirited.
According to medical experts, Yih Hai Sung stated that it was sometime after 2 p.m. on May 27 that he swallowed the keys with the intention of committing suicide. There is no doubt that the swallowing took place before he made this statement. Thus there is every possibility that the keys have already been discharged through the bowels.
