The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, May 21, 1936 14615

'I Killed Nakayama!'
Says Little Kwangtung
Before District Court

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. D. REGISTRY
B. D. 7073
22

(Photo By Isadora taken "on the run")
Under escort of two Japanese policemen, Yih Hai-sen, better known as "Shao Kwang-tung," is shown walking out from the First Special District Court building where he reiterated that he had killed Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama on Darroch Road on November 9 last year.

Hsiao Kwangtung
Changes Motive

Killing Calculated To
Create Hongkew Panic,
Strengthen Society

A new motive for the killing of Hideo Nakayama, warrant officer of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, on Darroch Road on the night of November 9, 1935, was given by Yih Hai-sen alias "Hsiao Kwangtung" at the resumed hearing of the case yesterday afternoon in the First Special District Court. The shooting, he declared, was done deliberately to kill a Japanese in order stir up trouble in Hongkew, and in the ensuing panic to strengthen the political position of the Cantonese secret society known as the Dong Nyi Yat Hui.

In making this statement, Little Kwangtung further revised his confession of the crime. He said that Yang Wen-tao, second accused, was chief of the society, and with other members including Chow Yao-yung, assistant manager of the Continental Ballroom, and the Korean "Jack" now being held by Japanese Consular Police, they had plotted the murder together.

Yang and Chow continued to deny the implication yesterday, declaring that they are being framed, despite Yih's assertion that they helped map out the plot. Yih stuck to his story that he himself had fired the fatal shot.

Tomorrow afternoon at 2 o'clock Judge Chien Hung-yih, who has been hearing the case, will visit the scene of the crime on Darroch Road with police to see another reconstruction of the shooting. The case has been adjourned until next Wednesday afternoon, and the judge has ordered that the Korean, "Jack," be brought to court by the Japanese for an examination.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮与信使报》，1936年5月21日，星期四 14615

‘我杀了中山！’
小广东在特区法院
如是说

上海公共租界警务处
特别分部登记处
B. D. 7073
22

（照片由伊莎多拉在“行动中”拍摄）
在两名日本警察的押解下，叶海森（更广为人知的名字是“小广东”）走出第一特区法院大楼，他再次重申自己于去年11月9日在达罗路杀害了海军曹长中山秀雄。

小广东
改变动机

杀人旨在制造
虹口恐慌，巩固社团地位

昨天下午在第一特区法院恢复审理该案时，叶海森（别名“小广东”）为1935年11月9日晚在达罗路杀害日本海军陆战队曹长中山秀雄一案提供了新的动机。他宣称，这次枪击是蓄意杀害一名日本人，以便在虹口制造事端，并在随后的恐慌中加强被称为“同义益会”的广东帮会的政治地位。

在发表这一声明时，小广东进一步修改了他的犯罪供词。他说，第二被告杨文涛是该帮会的首领，并与包括大陆舞厅副经理周耀荣以及目前被日本领事馆警察拘留的朝鲜人“杰克”在内的其他成员共同策划了这起谋杀案。

杨和周昨天继续否认涉案，声称他们是被陷害的，尽管叶坚称他们帮助策划了阴谋。叶坚持自己的说法，称致命的一枪是他自己开的。

明天下午2点，一直审理此案的钱洪义法官将偕同警察前往达罗路的犯罪现场，观看另一次枪击过程的重建。案件已休庭至下周三下午，法官已命令日方将朝鲜人“杰克”带至法庭接受审讯。

pages.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, MAY 21, 1936

ANOTHER SUSPECT IN
DARROCH RD. CRIME

Yih Hai-sen Tells Motive of
Shooting of Nakayama

JUDGE TO VISIT SCENE OF
MURDER TO-MORROW

A third man was charged with being concerned in the murder of H. Nakayama, Japanese marine, on Darroch Road, on November 9, last year. Yih Hai-sen, alias "Little Cantonese," reiterated that he shot the Japanese marine in order to create a disturbance in Hongkew; and Judge Chien Hung-yih announced that he, the police lawyer and counsel for defence would witness a reconstruction of the Darroch Road crime at 2 p.m. to-morrow. These were the developments in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon when the hearing was resumed of the case against Yang Ven-tao and Yih Hai-sen, both Cantonese, accused of H. Nakayama's murder.

At the outset of yesterday's hearing Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, prosecuting, told the Judge that during the period of remand, Chow Zeu-yoong, alias Chow Yao-yung, who had been implicated in Nakayama's murder by "Little Cantonese," was arrested in the "Continental" Dancing Hall, Ningpo Road, and he likewise was charged with murder. Mr. Ru added that a bullet, which was found by police near the scene of the crime, had been examined by experts but no trace of blood on it could be found. At the station, the newly-arrested man admitted he was a member of the Cantonese society known as Dong Nyi Yat Hui, but denied having taken part in the shooting.

Yih Hai-sen, who changed his statement each time he appeared before the court, made another sensational statement yesterday. In reply to the Judge, he stated that the motive of killing the Japanese marine was to create a disturbance in Hongkew. This, he told the Judge, would increase the number of members of the society of which he was a member and enhance the influence of his society. How the murder of a Japanese could increase his society's influence the prisoner did not disclose, despite the Judge's questioning on this point. The prisoner repeated that the plot to kill a Japanese was mapped out by the Koreans and he fired the shot that killed Nakayama.

Changed His Statement

Det.-Sub-Inspr. Crowther entered the witness' box again and told the Judge that information which led to the arrest of Yang Ven-tao was furnished by one Hariyama whose Chinese name was Tseng Wei-ming, a naturalized Japanese subject. Witness said that "Little Cantonese" was twice taken to the scene of the Darroch Road crime for a reconstruction of the murder and, on the first occasion, "Little Cantonese" told the police that after firing the shot he went back to North Szechuen Road, and, on the second occasion, he said that he went to the Fong Loh Li Alleyway after firing the shot that killed Nakayama. Witness also reported on his investigations concerning the bank accounts of "Little Cantonese" in December last year. Regarding the Korean named Jack, who was mentioned several times by "Little Cantonese," witness said that he understood the Japanese authorities had not completed their investigations and the Korean was not in court yesterday.

Two Japanese detectives of S.M. Police testified in regard to the information which led to the arrest of Yang Ven-tao, after which, Det.-Sub-Inspr. Dickson, of the finger-print department, gave evidence concerning the seized pistol and a book that was alleged to have been used to conceal the pistol. Other witnesses included Tsu Sheng-foo, landlord of the building in which was situated the society known as Dong Nyi Yat Hui, and Ah Keng, a servant of the society.

Will See Reconstruction

Before the conclusion of the hearing, "Little Cantonese" burst into cries in the accused's dock and his attorney-at-law suggested that he be held in the Court's civil detention house instead of at the station cell during the period of adjournment, but the application was not granted. The Judge told "Little Cantonese" that he might say anything he wished to say before him and questioned him why he cried. In reply, the prisoner said he was not falsely accused.

The Judge adjourned the hearing till next Wednesday afternoon, and ordered that the Korean named Jack should be brought to his court as a witness at next hearing. At 2 p.m. to-morrow, the Judge said, he would visit the scene of the Darroch Road crime to see a reconstruction of the crime.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年5月21日，星期四

达罗克路命案又一名嫌疑人

叶海森讲述枪击中山（Nakayama）的动机

法官将于明日视察谋杀现场

去年11月9日，一名日本海军陆战队员H. Nakayama在达罗克路（Darroch Road）被杀，第三名男子被控与此谋杀案有关。叶海森，绰号“小广东”，重申他枪击该日本海军陆战队员是为了在虹口制造骚乱；钱弘义法官宣布，他本人、警务处律师以及辩护律师将于明日下午2时见证达罗克路命案的现场重演。昨日下午，第一特区法院恢复审理针对两名广东籍被告杨文道和叶海森涉嫌谋杀H. Nakayama一案，上述即为庭审进展。

在昨日庭审开始时，助理市检察官鲁保罗先生（Mr. Paul Y. Ru）向法官陈述，在还押候审期间，被“小广东”指认卷入Nakayama谋杀案的周兆荣（Chow Zeu-yoong），又名周耀荣（Chow Yao-yung），在宁波路“大陆”舞厅被捕，并同样被控谋杀罪。鲁先生补充说，警方在犯罪现场附近发现的一颗子弹已经过专家检验，但未发现血迹。在警局，这名新被捕的男子承认他是名为“东义益会”（Dong Nyi Yat Hui）的广东帮会成员，但否认参与枪击。

叶海森每次出庭都改变供词，昨日他又作出惊人陈述。回答法官提问时，他表示杀害日本海军陆战队员的动机是为了在虹口制造骚乱。他告诉法官，这将增加其所属帮会的成员数量并提升该帮会的影响力。尽管法官就此点进行了讯问，但被告并未透露杀害一名日本人如何能增加其帮会的影响力。被告重申，杀害日本人的阴谋是由朝鲜人策划的，而他开枪射杀了Nakayama。

更改供词

副巡官克罗瑟（Det.-Sub-Inspr. Crowther）再次进入证人席，告诉法官，导致杨文道被捕的情报是由一名叫Hariyama的人提供的，其中文名为曾伟明（Tseng Wei-ming），是一名归化日本籍民。证人称，“小广东”曾两次被带到达罗克路命案现场进行谋杀重演，第一次时，“小广东”告诉警方，开枪后他回到了北四川路；第二次时，他说在开枪射杀Nakayama后，他去了丰乐里弄堂。证人还报告了他去年12月对“小广东”银行账户的调查情况。关于“小广东”多次提到的名叫杰克（Jack）的朝鲜人，证人表示他获悉日本当局尚未完成调查，且该朝鲜人昨日未出庭。

两名工部局警务处的日本侦探就导致杨文道被捕的情报作证，随后，指纹科的迪克森副巡官（Det.-Sub-Inspr. Dickson）就缴获的手枪以及据称用于藏匿手枪的一本书提供证词。其他证人包括“东义益会”所在楼宇的房东朱生福（Tsu Sheng-foo），以及该帮会的一名仆役阿庚（Ah Keng）。

将观看重演

庭审结束前，“小广东”在被告席上痛哭流涕，其辩护律师建议在休庭期间将其羁押于法院民事拘留所而非警局牢房，但该申请未获批准。法官告诉“小广东”，他可以在法官面前畅所欲言，并询问他为何哭泣。被告回答说，他并非被诬告。

法官宣布休庭至下周三下午，并命令在下次庭审时将名叫杰克的朝鲜人作为证人带到法庭。法官称，明日下午2时，他将亲自达罗克路命案现场观看案件重演。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MAY 21, 1936
14603
Yih Changes
Killing Story
Once Again
Fresh Motive Present-
ed For Murder Of
Nakayama
SAYS SOCIETY
WANTED SLAYING
"Hsiao Kwangtung" In
Court Once More Over
Hongkew Death Case

Although still admitting that it was he who fired the shot that killed Hideo Nakayama, member of the Japanese Naval Land Party, on the night of November 9, 1935, Yih Hai-sen, better known as "Hsiao Kwangtung," further revised his confession at the third opening hearing of the case held before Judge Chien Hung-nich, presiding, and a full tribunal in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon.

This revision presented a fresh motive for the killing. In one of his earlier confessions, Yih declared that he killed Nakayama, single-handed and without any prompting, because he had wanted to kill a Japanese since the Sino-Japanese trouble.

Yesterday, he stated that the motive for the murder was because the Tung Yih Association, a Cantonese organization, headed by Yang Wen-tao, second accused, had decided that it would be beneficial to the association to have a Japanese killed. Yih declared that Yang and others in the association, including Chow Yao-yung, assistant manager of the Continental Ball-room, and "Jack," the Korean, now in Japanese hands, were implicated in the plot.

Ru Outlines New Statement

At the opening of the session yesterday, Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, informed the court that Yih had revised his confession in a statement to the police and proceeded to outline that revision. He stated that Yih had declared the plotters believed that by killing a Japanese subject, considerable unrest could be stirred up in Hongkew and that after this unrest had subsided, the association could become more powerful and gather more members. Questioned later during the hearing, Yih admitted that this was the statement he had made to the police.

Yih's revision continued that considerable time had been spent in plotting the crime. On November 3, the plotters, made up of Yih, Yang, Chow and the Korean, had gone to Darroch Road to look over the scene of the contemplated shooting, the statement continued. It continued that on the night of the shooting, the group went to the Moon Palace Hotel and engaged Room No. 9 under the name of Hsiau Cheng-chi.

Mr. Ru stated that police had investigated this statement by going to the Moon Palace and making inquiries. The hotel management had informed them Room 9 had been let to a group of men under the name given by Yih on the specified night.

Both Yang and Chow flatly denied implication in the case. Yang was questioned for a considerable length of time by Judge Chien but the man continued his statements of "I know nothing" with dogged persistence. All statements made against him he branded as lies and charged a "frame-up." No amount of ques-
tioning could shake him from his story.

Asked why he told the police that the book which contained the death weapon was his, and why he later retracted this statement, Yang declared that he never told the police anything of the kind.

Home In Bed

Asked what he knew about the killing, Chow declared that he knew absolutely nothing. He stated that on the night of the shooting, he was home in bed. It was impossible for him to be any place else, he continued, because he had no clothes. He had sent all his wearing apparel to the pawnshop, he continued.

Although yesterday's hearing lasted from 2 to 4.30 p.m., aside from Yih's revision of his confession, and the continued questioning of Yang, other testimony given was largely an expansion of that already taken by the court. Police witnesses testified concerning the reconstruction of the crime which was carried out on May 2, and later Judge Chien announced that he would personally attend another reconstruction tomorrow. The prosecution further offered evidence to show that Yih had received money in various sums ranging as high as $600 in the form of remittances from Tsingtao. This money was received by Yih while he was in Shanghai in December, 1935, and February, of this year. The case was remanded until May 27 at 2 p.m. for further hearing.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》，1936年5月21日，星期四
14603
叶某再次
更改杀人供词
提出杀害
中山的新动机
称帮会希望
实施杀戮
“小广东”因虹口
命案再次受审

尽管仍承认是他在1935年11月9日晚开枪射杀了日本海军陆战队成员Hideo Nakayama，但绰号“小广东”的叶海森在昨日下午第一特区法院由钱弘义法官主持、全体推事出席的该案第三次开庭审理中，进一步修改了他的供词。

此次修改提出了一个新的杀人动机。在此前的一份供词中，叶声称他独自且无人唆使地杀害了Nakayama，因为自中日纠纷以来他一直想杀死一名日本人。

昨日，他陈述谋杀的动机是因为由第二被告杨文道领导的广东组织“同义会”（Tung Yih Association）决定，杀死一名日本人对该会有利。叶宣称，杨及该会其他成员，包括大陆舞厅副经理周耀荣和目前处于日本当局控制下的朝鲜人“杰克”，均卷入该阴谋。

鲁氏概述新供词

在昨日庭审开始时，助理市检察官鲁保罗先生告知法庭，叶在向警方所作的陈述中修改了供词，并随即概述了该修改内容。他指出，叶声称策划者认为，通过杀害一名日本臣民，可以在虹口引起相当大的动荡，而在动荡平息后，该帮会可以变得更加强大并吸纳更多成员。在随后的庭审讯问中，叶承认这是他曾向警方作出的陈述。

叶的修改供词继续称，策划该罪行花费了大量时间。陈述接着指出，11月3日，由叶、杨、周和该朝鲜人组成的策划团伙前往达罗克路勘察预谋枪击的现场。陈述还称，在枪击当晚，该团伙前往月宫饭店（Moon Palace Hotel），以萧成基（Hsiau Cheng-chi）的名义预订了9号房间。

鲁先生 stated 警方通过前往月宫饭店并进行查询来核实这一陈述。酒店管理层告知他们，在指定的夜晚，9号房间已租给了一群使用叶所提供名字的男子。

杨和周均断然否认卷入此案。钱法官对杨进行了长时间的讯问，但该男子顽固地坚持其“我一无所知”的说法。他将所有针对他的陈述斥为谎言，并指控这是“栽赃陷害”。无论怎样讯问，都无法动摇他的说法。

当被问及为何告诉警方装有致命武器的那本书是他的，以及为何后来撤回这一陈述时，杨宣称他从未向警方说过此类话。

在家卧床

当被问及他对杀人案了解多少时，周宣称他绝对一无所知。他陈述说，在枪击当晚，他在家卧床。他接着说，他不可能在其他任何地方，因为他没有衣服穿。他继续说，他已将所有衣物送进了当铺。

虽然昨日的庭审从下午2时持续到4时30分，但除了叶修改供词以及对杨的持续讯问外，其他证词 largely 是对法庭已采纳证词的扩展。警方证人就5月2日进行的犯罪重演作了证，随后钱法官宣布他将于次日亲自参加另一次重演。检方进一步提供证据，显示叶曾以汇款形式收到来自青岛的多笔款项，最高达600美元。这笔钱是叶在1935年12月和今年2月身在上海时收到的。案件被延期至5月27日下午2时继续审理。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, MAY 21, 1936

Nakayama Killing Said
Planned To Create New
Political Incident Here

Murder Plot
Details Told
By Accused

Slayer Selected By Lot
After Meeting Of Tung
Yi Organization

JUDGE PROTESTS ON
WITNESS' ABSENCE

"Jack The Korean" Still In
Japanese Police Hands;
Third Man Charged

Further astonishing confessions were made by Yih Hai-sen, alias "Shao Kwangtung," in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon, when the hearing was resumed of the murder charge brought against him in connection with the shooting in Darroch Road of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama, of the Japanese Landing Force, at 9 p.m. on November 9.

"Shao Kwangtung," who broke down and cried several times during the hearing, revealed that the killing was planned by the Tung Yi Association, an alleged philanthropic organisation, in order to create a political incident here, and thus bring more members into their Association. He added that the slayer had been selected by lottery, to which he had been summoned after a meeting of the Association.

Chou Tso-yun, the third suspect in the case, who was arrested in the Continental Ballroom, Ningpo Road, on the night of May 8, appeared in court yesterday, and was charged with complicity in the murder. He was implicated by "Shao Kwantung" as the man who called him to the Moon Palace Cabaret on the eventful night at the request of Yang Wen-tao, 42-year-old Cantonese former employee of the China Navigation Company. "Shao Kwangtung" also alleged that Chou as a member of the Tung Yi Association, had called him to participate in the drawing of lots in order to decide who was to kill a Japanese Naval officer. Chou denied this.

"Shao Kwangtung" stated in court yesterday that the suggestion for the killing was made by "Jack," the Korean, at present held by the Japanese Consular Police, and who, notwithstanding the repeated requests made by Judge Dzien, has so far not been brought before the tribunal to be questioned as a witness.

It was stated in court that "Jack" was not brought to court by the Japanese Consular Police as they had not completed their inquiries. Judge Dzien for the third time yesterday asked a representative of the Shanghai Municipal Police to make a strong representation to the Japanese authorities to allow the Korean to be questioned in open court.

Yang Denies Allegations
It will be remembered that at the hearing held on May 1, "Shao Kwangtung" implicated Yang as being the actual killer of Warrant Officer Nakayama, stating at the time that he was present at the scene of the crime together with the Korean, Jack. At the next hearing on May 6, "Shao Kwangtung" retracted his previous statements and said that he himself killed the Japanese Marine and that Yang had nothing to do with it. At the same hearing a sensation was caused at the trial when a defence attorney called a witness who stated that the allegations against "Shao Kwantung" and Yang constituted a frame-up, stories fabricated by police informers in order to collect rewards offered.

Yesterday "Shao Kwantung" again implicated Yang in complicity in the murder by stating that the pistol used in the crime was given to him by Yang and, further, that Yang together with "Jack" accompanied him to the scene of the crime.

Doing a great deal of confessing at the trial, "Shao Kwantung" stated that it was Chou, the third accused, who called him on November 5, four days before the murder, to discuss the plot with Yang and two Koreans. "Shao Kwantung" then related that at the meeting, after it was decided that a Japanese official had to be murdered, Yang wrote the character "Chui" meaning "go" on a slip of paper, then tore three similar pieces of paper and rolled all four into balls. Then each of the men present took one and the lot to kill the Japanese official fell to him, "Shao Kwantung."

When asked as to who was the actual intended victim and what was the motive behind the plot, "Shao Kwantung" said that they had no definite victim in mind and that they wanted to kill a Japanese in order to create a disturbance in Hongkew and to increase the power of the Tung Yi Association. More people would become members of the association and more money would be forthcoming. "Shao Kwantung" alleged that the suggestion was made by "Jack," who, he said at the last hearing, had become a member of his association.

Crime To Be Re-enacted
Prior to the court rising yesterday, and after evidence was given by Sub-Inspector Crowther, attached to Dixwell Road Police Station, Judge Dzien stated that he himself would visit the scene of the crime to-morrow and have "Shao Kwantung" re-enact the murder.

Yang denied everything alleged by "Shao Kwangtung" and did very little talking. When questioned as to his former confession at the police station, that the book hollowed out at the centre to fit in with the pistol used in the crime, was his, he repudiated his former statement. The judge questioned him at length, but he would not reveal anything. He repeated that he had not seen clearly the book which was found by the police in his home.

At the beginning of the hearing Mr. Paul Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, stated that Chou had confessed that he was a member of the Tung Yi Association and that he knew the two others accused. Chou, it was said, denied that he had any knowledge of the Nakayama murder plot. Chou was also said to have denied that he had been asked by Yang to call "Shao Kwangtung" to discuss the murder plot. Mr. Ru also repeated "Shao Kwangtung's" confession regarding the motive of the crime, but said that he could exonerate Chou who did not actually go to the scene of the crime, but had participated in criminal deliberations before and after the crime.

Hence Chou was also charged with complicity in the murder, he said.

Police Evidence
Detective Sub-Inspector Crowther of the Dixwell Road Police Station described the two demonstrations of the crime given by "Shao Kwangtung" during the postponement of the hearing. According to his descriptions "Shao Kwangtung" made conflicting reports as to the actual killer during both demonstrations. At the first demonstration held on May 2, it was stated, "Shao Kwangtung" said that at the corner of Darroch Road both "Jack" and Yang walked before him with the Japanese sailor walking ahead of the group. Yang shot the sailor. Yang did not pass him ("Shao Kwangtung") a pistol. After the shooting "Shao Kwangtung" fled.

During the second demonstration on May 4, "Shao. Kwangtung" repudiated his former statement giving positions of "Jack" and Yang while committing the crime. He was about 10 paces away from both "Jack" and Yang, "Shao Kwangtung" was quoted as saying. Yang passed him the pistol and he ("Shao Kwangtung") shot the Japanese sailor. After shooting down the victim "Shao Kwangtung" fled through the Feng Lo Alley in Darroch Road. Hu Hsiang-wu, a Chinese shoemaker who saw a man running into the alley after the shooting, testified during the demonstration that the man who was dressed in black was not as high as "Shao Kwangtung," but the fleeing man was stouter. The fleeing man wore leather shoes but "Shao Kwangtung" also wore leather shoes during the demonstration, it was said.

Informers' Statements
A Japanese detective handling the case told the court that he received his information from a Japanese named Harayama, in December of last year. The Japanese Consular police arrested Yang when he was in Tsingtao. Two Chinese, Wang Ching-sung and Li Yeo, were said to have also supplied him with information. Mr. Paul Ru said, however, that both informants refused to sign reports. Li Yeo was said to have told the police that he saw "Shao Kwangtung" lying in a bed in the Moon Palace Cabaret on November 9, about 8 p.m. About half an hour later "Jack" entered the room and gave "Shao Kwangtung" something black. The latter refused to accept it saying that he ("Jack") might just as well keep it for himself. Both later left the cabaret.

Chou Tso-yun, the third accused, told the court that he knew Yang Wen-tao for four years, but that he had only been a member of his (Yang's) association for one year. He slept on the premises of the association. He became a member at the end of 1934, but the association was dissolved at the end of the last Lunar year because of lack of funds. "Shao Kwangtung" seldom came to the association, he stated. Yang had never asked him (Chou) to go to a meeting to discuss a murder plot.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年5月21日，星期四

称中山（Nakayama）遇害案
系策划在此制造新的
政治事件

谋杀阴谋
被告供出
细节

凶手经同义会
会议后抽签选定

法官抗议
证人缺席

“朝鲜人杰克”仍由
日本警方羁押；
第三人被起诉

昨日下午，第一特区法院恢复审理关于11月9日晚9时在日本登陆部队准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）于达罗克路（Darroch Road）枪击案中对其提出的谋杀指控，化名“邵广东”的易海森（Yih Hai-sen，音译）在庭上作出了更多令人震惊的供认。

“邵广东”在审讯过程中数次崩溃大哭，他透露，这起杀人案是由所谓慈善组织“同义会”策划的，目的是在此制造一起政治事件，从而为该会吸纳更多成员。他补充说，凶手是在该会一次会议后，通过抽签方式选定的，而他本人正是在被召至会后参与了这一过程。

本案第三名嫌疑人周作云（Chou Tso-yun，音译）于5月8日晚在宁波路大陆舞厅被捕，昨日出庭，被控参与谋杀。据“邵广东”指证，周作云是受42岁的广东人、前英商中国轮船公司雇员杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao，音译）之托，在案发当晚将他叫至月宫舞厅的人。“邵广东”还指控称，周作云作为同义会成员，曾叫他参与抽签，以决定由谁去杀害一名日本海军军官。周作云对此予以否认。

“邵广东”昨日在庭上陈述，杀人建议是由目前被日本领事馆警察羁押的朝鲜人“杰克”提出的，尽管迪恩法官（Judge Dzien）多次要求，但至今仍未将该朝鲜人带至法庭接受讯问。

庭上指出，日本领事馆警察未将“杰克”带至法庭，理由是他们的调查尚未完成。昨日，迪恩法官第三次要求上海公共租界工部局警务处代表向日本当局提出强烈交涉，允许该朝鲜人在公开法庭上接受讯问。

杨文涛否认指控
记得在5月1日的审讯中，“邵广东”曾指证杨文涛是杀害中山准尉的实际凶手，并称当时他与朝鲜人杰克一同出现在犯罪现场。在随后5月6日的审讯中，“邵广东”推翻了之前的供述，称是他自己杀害了这名日本海军陆战队员，与杨文涛无关。在同次审讯中，辩护律师传唤了一名证人，该证人声称对“邵广东”和杨文涛的指控是一场构陷，是警方线人为获取悬赏而编造的故事，这在庭审中引起了轰动。

昨日，“邵广东”再次指证杨文涛参与谋杀共谋，称作案使用的手枪是杨文涛交给他的，此外，杨文涛还与“杰克”一同陪他前往犯罪现场。

“邵广东”在庭审中大量招供，称是第三名被告周作云在谋杀案发生前四天，即11月5日，将他叫去与杨文涛及两名朝鲜人商议阴谋。“邵广东”接着叙述，在会议上，当决定必须谋杀一名日本官员后，杨文涛在一张纸条上写了一个意为“去”的“吹”字（注：此处原文为Chui，意指“去”，但汉字“吹”通常无此意，可能为音译或特定暗语，依原文直译），然后撕了三张类似的纸条，将四张纸全部揉成团。随后，在场的每人取走一个纸团，结果抽中杀害日本官员这一签的是他，“邵广东”。

当被问及实际预谋受害者是谁以及阴谋背后的动机时，“邵广东”称他们并没有确定的目标，而是想杀害一名日本人，以便在虹口制造骚乱，并增强同义会的势力。这样会有更多人加入该会，也会有更多的资金流入。“邵广东”指控称，该建议是由“杰克”提出的，他在上次审讯中曾说，“杰克”已成为其协会的成员。

将重演犯罪过程
昨日休庭前，在隶属于狄思威路（Dixwell Road）警察局的副督察克劳瑟（Crowther）提供证词后，迪恩法官表示，他将于次日亲自前往犯罪现场，并由“邵广东”重演谋杀过程。

杨文涛否认了“邵广东”的所有指控，且极少发言。当被问及之前在警察局所作的供认，即那本中间挖空以适配作案手枪的书是他的时，他推翻了之前的陈述。法官对他进行了长时间讯问，但他不愿透露任何信息。他重申，警方在他家中发现的那本书，他并未看清。

审讯开始时，助理公诉人保罗·鲁（Paul Ru，音译）先生指出，周作云已承认他是同义会成员，并认识另外两名被告。据说，周作云否认他对中山谋杀阴谋有任何了解。据说周作云还否认曾受杨文涛之托叫来“邵广东”商议谋杀阴谋。鲁先生还复述了“邵广东”关于犯罪动机的供词，但表示他可以免除周作云的罪责，因为周并未实际前往犯罪现场，只是在犯罪前后参与了犯罪密谋。

因此，他说，周作云也被控参与谋杀共谋。

警方证据
狄思威路警察局的侦探副督察克劳瑟描述了“邵广东”在审讯延期期间进行的两次犯罪演示。据他描述，“邵广东”在这两次演示中关于实际凶手的说法相互矛盾。据称，在5月2日举行的第一次演示中，“邵广东”说，在达罗克路的拐角处，“杰克”和杨文涛走在他前面，那名日本水手走在队伍最前方。杨文涛开枪射击了该水手。杨文涛并未递给他（“邵广东”）手枪。枪击发生后，“邵广东”逃跑了。

在5月4日的第二次演示期间，“邵广东”推翻了之前关于“杰克”和杨文涛在作案时所处位置的陈述。据引述，“邵广东”称他当时距离“杰克”和杨文涛约10步远。杨文涛将手枪递给他，他（“邵广东”）开枪射击了那名日本水手。击倒受害者后，“邵广东”经由达罗克路的凤乐里（Feng Lo Alley，音译）逃跑。一名目睹枪击后有人跑进巷子的中国鞋匠胡祥武（Hu Hsiang-wu，音译）在演示期间作证称，那个身穿黑衣的人没有“邵广东”高，但逃跑者更壮实。据说，逃跑者穿着皮鞋，而在演示中“邵广东”也穿着皮鞋。

线人陈述
负责此案的一名日本侦探告诉法庭，他于去年12月从一名名叫原山（Harayama，音译）的日本人那里获得情报。日本领事馆警察在青岛逮捕了杨文涛。据说还有两名中国人，王景松（Wang Ching-sung，音译）和李耀（Li Yeo，音译），也向他提供了情报。然而，保罗·鲁先生说，这两名线人均拒绝签署报告。据说李耀告诉警方，他在11月9日晚8点左右，看见“邵广东”躺在月宫舞厅的一张床上。大约半小时后，“杰克”进入房间，给了“邵广东”一个黑色的东西。后者拒绝接受，说他（“杰克”）最好自己留着。随后两人离开了舞厅。

第三名被告周作云告诉法庭，他认识杨文涛已有四年，但加入其（杨的）协会仅一年。他住在协会的处所内。他于1934年底成为会员，但该协会因缺乏资金于上一个农历年年底解散。他说，“邵广东”很少来协会。杨文涛从未叫他（周）去开会讨论谋杀阴谋。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, May 20, 1936

Nakayama Case
Hearing Opened

Murder Charges Filed
Against Big Chow;
Frame-Up Alleged

Formal charges of murder are expected to be filed against Chow Sha-yung, cabaret inspector, this afternoon when he faces the First Special District Court with Yih Hai-sen. alias "Shao Kwangtung," and Yang Wen-tao for alleged complicity in the killing of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Force on Darroch Road on November 9. 1935

Chow, alias "Ta (Big) Chow," an ex-compositor formerly in the employ of a local English-language newspaper, was arrested some 10 days ago at the Continental Ball-room, Ningpo Road, where he was employed as an inspector. He was implicated by "Shao Kwangtung" as the messenger Yang sent to ask his attendance at a conference allegedly called to discuss the murder of the Japanese bluejacket. "Shao Kwangtung" and Yang are both charged with murder under Article 271 of the Chinese Criminal Code.

Spectators Limited

In view of the congestion in the courtroom during the previous sessions, the full court of the criminal division of the court has decided to limit the number of spectators to 40. Only that number of tickets will be issued this afternoon. The courtroom will be guarded by special police to prevent any disturbances. Judge Chien Hung-nieh is scheduled to preside over the hearing as usual.

Further allegations against the witnesses for prosecution have been promised by the defense lawyers for this afternoon's session. Attorney Wong Shih-chung, appearing for "Shao Kwangtung" who has confessed to the charges, this afternoon was to produce in court documents intended to show that Tseng Yuan, the star witness of the prosecution, had attempted to extort money from his client in Tsingtao shortly before his arrest.

Frame-Up Alleged

Charges of a "frame-up" will be pressed by Attorney G. R. Grove, appearing for Yang Wen-tao, who during the last hearing two weeks ago introduced evidence which he claims would prove that his client was a victim of a "frame-up." He would ask the court to investigate the alleged affair this afternoon.

Warrant Officer Nakayama was killed at 9 p.m. on November 9, last year. His murder caused a panic in Chapel and Hongkew, resulting in the exodus of residents from those areas in fear of a new Sino-Japanese "war." After months of investigation, police rounded up a total of seven suspects. While the three are being held on murder charges, a fourth one is held by the Japanese Consular police. He is a Korean by name of "Jack." A fifth suspect was released while two women, mother and sweetheart of "Shao Kwangtung," arrested by the Public Safety Bureau at the request of the Japanese authorities, also regained freedom after a prolonged detention.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年5月20日，星期三

中山案
审讯开始

对“大周”提出谋杀指控；
声称系栽赃陷害

预计今天下午，当舞厅稽查员周守庸（Chow Sha-yung）与叶海生（Yih Hai-sen，别名“小广东”）及杨文道（Yang Wen-tao）一同在第一特区法院出庭，被控涉嫌共谋于1935年11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）杀害日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）时，将正式对其提出谋杀指控。

周守庸，别名“大周”（Ta (Big) Chow），曾任一家本地英文报纸的排字工人，被捕前受雇于宁波路大陆舞厅（Continental Ball-room）担任稽查员，约十天前在该处被捕。“小广东”指证他是杨文道派去邀请其参加所谓讨论杀害日本水兵会议的信使。“小广东”和杨文道均依据《中华民国刑法》第271条被控谋杀罪。

限制旁听人数

鉴于前几次开庭期间法庭内拥挤不堪，法院刑事庭全体法官决定将旁听人数限制为40人。今天下午仅发放相应数量的入场券。法庭将由特别警察守卫，以防任何骚乱。钱鸿业法官将照常主持审讯。

辩护律师承诺在今天下午的庭审中进一步指控检方证人。代表已认罪的“小广东”出庭的黄世忠律师，今天下午将在法庭出示文件，旨在证明检方主要证人曾元在其被捕前不久曾在青岛试图向其当事人勒索钱财。

声称系栽赃陷害

代表杨文道出庭的G. R. Grove律师将坚持提出“栽赃陷害”的指控。在两周前的上一次听证会上，他引入了据称能证明其当事人是“栽赃陷害”受害者的证据。他将于今天下午请求法庭调查这一所谓事件。

去年11月9日晚9时，中山准尉遇害。他的死在闸北和虹口引起恐慌，导致居民因担心新的中日“战争”而逃离这些地区。经过数月的调查，警方共逮捕了七名嫌疑人。目前其中三人因谋杀罪被羁押，第四人由日本领事馆警察羁押，此人为一名名叫“杰克”（Jack）的朝鲜人。第五名嫌疑人已被释放，而另外两名女性——即“小广东”的母亲及其情妇——此前应日本当局要求由公安局逮捕，在长期拘留后也重获自由。

May 21, 1936. Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao, Shun Pao, Sin Wan Pao and other local newspapers:-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE

The case against the persons charged with the murder of a Japanese marine named Hideo Nakayama came up for a further hearing yesterday afternoon at the Shanghai First Special District Court. In addition to the special admission tickets issued to newspaper reporters, only 40 ordinary admission tickets were issued by the Court. Persons attending the hearing were subject to a search by the Judicial Police before being permitted to enter the Court room. This precaution was to prevent trouble.

The Shanghai City Government yesterday detailed Chang Ding Yung (張定庸), a Secretary, and Huang Hwa (黃華), a departmental chief of the Bureau of Public Safety, to attend the hearing. More than 10 members of the Japanese Landing Party were also present.

Chien Hung Nieh (錢鴻業), the Presiding Judge of the Criminal Division, Judges Feng (馮) and Siao (蕭) and Procurator Chang Chung Shih (張仲儒) took their seats at two o'clock.

The accused Yang Vung Tao (楊文道), Yih Hai Sung (葉海生) alias Siao Kwangtung (小廣東) and Tseu Shou Yong (周守庸) were then ordered to be brought before the Judges. Yih Hai Sung appeared to be more down-hearted.

Interrogated by the Presiding Judge Chien, (錢業) Tseu Shou Yong said that he was also known as Tseu Yao Yong and that he was employed as a private detective with the Ta Loh Dance Hall (大樂舞廳). He resided in House No. 13 Ta Tuh Lee (大德里) alleyway off North Szechuen Road.

Paul Ru (陸保華), Municipal Advocate, then said:- "Tseu is being charged with homicide together with Yih and Yang because he had also participated in the crime. A statement was made by Chang Tsun (張尊) in the course of which he described the circumstances under which he appeared as a witness at the last hearing. The blood-stained bullet has been examined by an expert, but the expert was unable to give any opinion because the blood stain had already disappeared when the bullet was sent to him. The connection of Yang Vung Tao with this case and the circumstances surrounding his arrest are set out in the reports made by Japanese Detective Tanaka and Japanese Detective Sub-Inspector Nakamura. Zung Wei Tsung (宗維宗) and the chief tenant of the house in which the Dong Nyi Association (東義協會) is located have been summoned to the Police Station for questioning. They are in Court to-day. The accused Yih Hai Sung has made another statement since the last hearing. In this statement, he said he decided to kill a Japanese in order to create a disturbance in the Hongkew district so that he could take advantage of the opportunity to expand his influence. He did not disclose what this influence was. The plan was discussed on several occasions in the Dong Nyi Association, and the person who was to do the killing was selected by drawing lots, the one who picked up a ball of paper on which the word 'go' had been written being assigned the task. Yih stated that he picked up that particular ball of paper, so he was detailed

1936年5月21日。晨间译稿。

《大公报》、《申报》、《新闻报》及其他本地报纸：

中山谋杀案

涉及被控谋杀一名名为中山秀雄的日本海军陆战队员的案件，昨日下午在上海第一特区法院继续审理。除向报社记者发放的特别入场券外，法院仅发放了40张普通入场券。出席听证的人员在进入法庭前须接受司法警察的搜查。此项预防措施旨在防止滋事。

上海市政府昨日指派秘书处秘书张定庸和公安局科长黄华出席听证会。另有十余名日本陆战队成员在场。

刑事庭审判长钱鸿业、冯法官、萧法官以及检察官张仲儒于两点钟入席。

随后，被告杨文道、叶海生（别名小广东）和周守庸被提审至法官面前。叶海生显得更为沮丧。

经审判长钱鸿业讯问，周守庸称他也叫周耀庸，受雇于大乐舞厅担任私人侦探。他居住在四川北路大德里弄堂13号。

公设辩护人陆保华随后表示：“周守庸因参与犯罪，与叶海生和杨文道一同被控杀人罪。张尊在陈述中描述了他在上次听证会上作为证人出庭的情况。带血子弹已由专家检验，但由于送交专家时血迹已消失，专家无法发表任何意见。杨文道与此案的关联及其被捕情形，详见日本侦探田中和日本侦探副巡官中村所作的报告。宗维宗及东义协会所在房屋的二房东已被传唤至警察局问话。他们今日到庭。被告叶海生自上次听证会后又作了一份陈述。在该陈述中，他说他决定杀害一名日本人，以便在虹口区制造事端，从而利用机会扩大其影响力。他未说明这种影响力具体指什么。该计划曾在东义协会多次讨论，执行杀人任务的人选通过抽签决定，抽中写有‘去’字纸团的人被指派执行任务。叶海生称他抽中了那个特定的纸团，因此被指派

pages.en:
May 21, 1936. Morning Translation.

to kill the Japanese. This statement is very clear and is corroborated by enquiries made by the Police. On being taken to the scene of crime, Yih gave a clear account of how he shot the Japanese."
Advocate Paul Ru then produced the various statements and exhibits.
A foreign Detective Sub-Inspector attached to Dixwell Police Station, giving evidence relating to the arrest of Yang Vung Tao, said that information was given by Zung Wei Ming (張偉民) (Zung has now become a Japanese subject under the name of Hirayama) and this information was transmitted to the witness by Japanese Detective Tanaka and Japanese Detective Sub-Inspector Nakamura. Yang Vung Tao was then arrested.
Referring to the investigation into the finances of Yih Hai Sung, the witness said: "On November 16 last year, a person named Tang (唐) in the employ of the Kiaochow-Tsinan Railway Administration sent $600 to Yih Hai Sung by post. When Tang came to Shanghai on February 15 this year he resided with Yih in the Yangtsze Hotel (揚子飯店). A sum of $400 was sent by post to Tang from Tsingtao. Formerly Yih operated a dancing hall at Tsingtao with a capital of $300, the money being supplied by his paramour Zung Wei Tsung".
Japanese Detective Sub-Inspector Nakamura then gave the following evidence :- "In December last year, Doctor Zung Wei Ming came to me and said that Yang Vung Tao was the principal spirit in the San Hai Huei Society (三合會) and was also the Chairman of the Dong Nyi Association. Doctor Zung added that Yang was connected with the Nakayama murder case. Information subsequently secured from other sources collaborated Doctor Zung's statement. The doctor's statement was then regarded as reliable".
Japanese detective Tanaka said :- "Zung Wei Ming once introduced to me a person named Li Yao (李耀). Li said: 'At 8 p.m. November 9 last year, I visited the Moon Palace Hotel (月宮飯店) and saw Siao Kwangtung alias Yih Hai Sung sleeping on a bed. Afterwards, I saw the Korean Jack (傑克) come into the room and give Yih a black thing having the shape of a pistol. Yih, however, refused to accept it and advised Jack to keep it himself. Yih then left the room together with Jack. I left also. When passing the Wang Pang Jao Bridge (萬邦橋), North Szechuen Road, I again saw Yih and Jack walking on the same road towards the northern direction'. The above statement was made to me by Li Yao".
The Court then questioned Yih Hai Sung.
The latter said: "What I have stated to the Police is all true. At the beginning of October last year, Yang Vung Tao detailed Tseu Shou Yong to find me at the Moon Palace Cabaret (月宮舞廳) and to ask me to proceed to the Dong Nyi Association at No. 71 Range Road. At that time 'Jack' and another Korean were already there. Knowing that there was some ill-feeling between 'Jack' and myself, Yang Vung Tao began to mediate. He then told me that the Koreans were planning to kill some Japanese and asked me to join in the discussion of a plan to carry out the plot. As no definite scheme was reached that day, Yang Vung Tao
pages.zh:
1936年5月21日。晨间译稿。

去杀害那名日本人。这份陈述非常清晰，并得到警方调查的佐证。在被带到犯罪现场时，叶海生清楚交代了他如何枪杀那名日本人的经过。”
随后，陆保华律师出示了各项供词和物证。
隶属于狄思威路捕房的一名外籍侦探副巡官就杨文道被捕一事作证称，情报由张伟民（Zung Wei Ming）提供（张现已归化日本籍，改名平山），该情报由日本侦探田中和日本侦探副巡官中村转告给证人。随后杨文道被捕。
谈及对叶海生财务状况的调查，该证人称：“去年11月16日，胶济铁路管理局一名姓唐的雇员通过邮局汇给叶海生600美元。今年2月15日唐某来沪时，与叶海生同住扬子饭店。有一笔400美元的款项从青岛通过邮局汇给唐某。此前，叶海生在青岛经营一家舞厅，资本为300美元，资金由其情妇宗维宗提供。”
日本侦探副巡官中村随后提供如下证词：“去年12月，张伟明博士来找我，说杨文道是三合会的骨干分子，也是东义协会的会长。张博士还补充说，杨文道与中山谋杀案有关。随后从其他渠道获得的信息证实了张博士的说法。因此，张博士的陈述被视为可靠。”
日本侦探田中说：“张伟明曾向我介绍过一个名叫李耀的人。李耀说：‘去年11月9日晚8点，我去了月宫饭店，看见小广东（即叶海生）睡在床上。后来，我看见朝鲜人杰克走进房间，递给叶海生一个形状像手枪的黑色物体。然而，叶海生拒绝接受，并建议杰克自己留着。随后，叶海生与杰克一同离开房间。我也离开了。在经过四川北路万邦桥时，我又看见叶海生和杰克沿同一条路向北走去’。上述陈述是李耀对我说的。”
法庭随后讯问叶海生。
后者称：“我向警方所作的一切陈述均属真实。去年10月初，杨文道指派周守庸到月宫舞厅找我，让我前往兰路71号的东义协会。当时‘杰克’和另一名朝鲜人已在那里。杨文道知道‘杰克’与我之间存在嫌隙，便开始调解。随后他告诉我，朝鲜人正计划杀害一些日本人，并邀请我参与讨论实施该阴谋的计划。由于当天未能达成确切方案，杨文道

pages.en:
4
May 21, 1936. Morning Translation.

again sent Tseu Shou Yong to ask me to go to the Association at the end of that month. 'Jack' and the other Korean were already there. On November 2 and 3, Yang Vung Tao, Tseu Shou Yong, 'Jack', one other person and myself went out to find a suitable locality in which to carry out the plan. On November 5 we drew lots at the Association. I drew the lot which contained the word 'go'. I, therefore, proceeded to carry out the plan on the night of November 9th. It was originally proposed to kill several Japanese superior naval officers, but as I met only a Japanese marine that night, I shot him. The object of the plot was to secure more members for the Association as well as extending its influence. On that night (November 9) we started from the Moon Palace Hotel, Room No. 9, with Yang Vung and 'Jack' following behind me. When I shot the marine, my companions had already disappeared. The weapon with which I committed the crime was brought to me by Yang Vung Tao in a book. After the shooting, I escaped through Feng Loh Lee (丰樂里) where I discarded the pistol. When I returned to the Moon Palace Hotel, I found Yang Vung Tao and 'Jack' were already there."

Interrogated by the Court, Tseu Shou Yong said: "I have known Yang Vung Tao for 4 years. I was a member of the Dong Nyi Association for one year and I lived in the premises of the Association after I joined. The Association was dissolved in January on account of financial difficulties. At ordinary times, Yih Hai Sung did not often attend the Association. There were no Koreans among the members. I became acquainted with 'Jack' at a cabaret. I do not know whether Yang Vung Tao has a pistol."

Yang Vung Tao here informed the Court that he had been maliciously implicated by Yang Chien Tsong(楊建中) who had planted the evidence against him.

Here a detective made a report on the investigations regarding Yang Chien Tsong and stated that the man's present whereabouts were unknown.

The chief tenant of the house in which the Dong Nyi Association was located gave the following evidence: "Yang Vung Tao rented the parlour on the ground floor of my house as an office for the Association and paid $20 as monthly rent. Tseu Shou Yong and a servant lived on the premises. I have not seen Yih Hai Sung. They always held their meetings at night. There were about 20 members but none of them was a Korean."

The manager of the Moon Palace Hotel was called. He testified that Room No. 9 was occupied by Au Tshung Kee(區春記).

At this stage, Yih Hai Sung's lawyer, on seeing tears rolling down Yih's cheeks, requested the Court to hold Yih in custody in another place and not to send Yih back to the Police Station. The lawyer said that judging by Yih's condition, the heavy sufferings he had undergone and the contradictions in his different statements ----- Yih appeared to be in possession of secrets which he found difficult to disclose. The lawyer further requested that after Yih's removal to another place of custody, he be given pen and paper in order to enable him to write out a true statement.
pages.zh:
4
1936年5月21日。晨间译文。

再次派周社荣来请我于该月底前往协会。“Jack”和另一名朝鲜人已经在那里。11月2日和3日，杨文道、周社荣、“Jack”、另一人以及我外出寻找实施计划的合适地点。11月5日，我们在协会抽签。我抽到了写有“去”字的签。因此，我于11月9日晚着手执行计划。原计划是杀害几名日本海军高级军官，但当晚我只遇到一名日本海军陆战队员，便开枪将其射杀。该阴谋的目的是为协会吸纳更多成员，并扩大其影响力。当晚（11月9日），我们从月宫饭店9号房出发，杨文和“Jack”跟在我身后。当我射击那名陆战队员时，我的同伴已经消失。作案用的武器是由杨文道夹在一本书里带给我的。枪击发生后，我经由丰乐里逃脱，并在那里丢弃了手枪。当我回到月宫饭店时，发现杨文道和“Jack”已经在那里。”

经法庭讯问，周社荣称：“我认识杨文道已有4年。我是东义协会的成员一年，加入后便住在协会会址内。该协会因财务困难于一月解散。平时，叶海生不常到协会来。成员中没有朝鲜人。我是在一家舞厅结识‘Jack’的。我不知道杨文道是否有手枪。”

杨文道此时向法庭表示，他遭到杨建中(楊建中)的恶意诬陷，后者栽赃陷害了他。

此时，一名侦探就针对杨建中的调查情况作了报告，并称该人目前下落不明。

东义协会所在房屋的总租户提供了以下证词：“杨文道租用了我家底层的客厅作为协会办公室，每月支付租金20元。周社荣和一名仆人住在屋内。我没见过叶海生。他们总是在夜间开会。成员约有20人，但没有一个是朝鲜人。”

传召了月宫饭店经理。他作证说，9号房由区春记(區春記)租用。

在此阶段，叶海生的律师看到叶海生脸颊流泪，请求法庭将叶海生羁押在其他地方，不要将其送回警察局。律师称，根据叶海生的状况、其所遭受的巨大痛苦以及其不同供词中的矛盾之处来看，叶海生似乎掌握着难以披露的秘密。律师进一步请求，在将叶海生转移至其他羁押地点后，应提供纸笔，以便其写出真实供词。

5
May 21, 1936. Morning Translation.

Presiding Judge Chien here ordered Yih Hai
Sung to relate to the Court any wrongs he had suffered.
In reply, Yih simply repeated his statement
that the crime was committed by him and that he had not
suffered any wrongs.
The Court then resumed the interrogation of
the accused Yang Vung Tao.
Steadfastly denying the charge, accused said:-
"Yang Chien Tsong, who has a grudge against me because I had
refused his request for a loan, secretly planted the book
(referring to the book on Physics in which a hole had been
made to conceal the pistol) in my home. As I have a book
of about the same shape, I did not make a careful examination
of the book when it was shown to me at a former hearing and
hastily admitted that the book was mine."
The Court adjourned the hearing till the
afternoon of next Wednesday, May 27. The Court will
inspect the scene of the crime on Friday, May 22.
pages.zh:
5
1936年5月21日。晨间译文。

主审法官钱此时命令叶海生向法庭陈述其所遭受的任何冤屈。
作为回应，叶海生只是重复了他的供词，称罪行是他所为，且未遭受任何冤屈。
法庭随后恢复对被告杨文道的讯问。
被告坚决否认指控，称：“杨建中因我拒绝其借款请求而对我怀恨在心，秘密将那本书（指那本挖空以藏匿手枪的物理书）放置在我家中。因为我有一本形状大致相同的书，所以在之前的庭审中向我出示该书时，我没有仔细检查，便匆忙承认那本书是我的。”
法庭宣布休庭，直至下周三（5月27日）下午继续审理。法庭将于5月22日（星期五）勘察犯罪现场。

pages.en:
May 19, 1936.
4. Afternoon Translation.
World Morning News (世界晨報) publishes the following articles:-

In connection with the murder of the Japanese marine Nakayama, the Police have arrested a Korean named "Jack" and two Cantonese named Yang Vung Tao (楊文道) and Yih Hai Sung (葉海生). Later a man named Chow Zeu Yung (周社榮), a private detective in the employ of the Da Loh (大陸) Cabaret, was also suspected. The Shanghai Municipal Police are charging the men with homicide.
Some say that Yang and Yih had been framed by Tseng Yuan (常元)(alias Tseng Yuan Chih 常元佳), who supplied the information to the Police. Tseng Yuan knew a wealthy Japanese resident. With the object of obtaining money from this Japanese, Tseng conspired with two of his friends and told the Japanese that they knew something about the murder of Nakayama but that they required money to enable them to get to the bottom of the murder. The Japanese supplied him with various amounts of money totalling about $1,000. Later, however, the Japanese became impatient for results and over Tseng's repeated demands for money, so he informed a certain Japanese policeman who detained Tseng Yuan and compelled him to name the murderers. In his dilemma, Tseng gave the names of Yang and Yih, his enemies. But the truth will one day come out.
It is learned that when Yang Vung Tao was arrested, a certain person intended to bail him out, but he did not do so as this case is an international one.
Tseng Yuan is now confined in the Rokusen Garden. Every day, the Japanese authorities give him five dollars for meals and opium. Whenever he goes out, two plain-clothes soldiers follow him under the pretext of according him protection, but in reality, the soldiers have been set to keep a watch on him to prevent him from making his escape.
pages.zh:
1936年5月19日。
4. 下午译文。
《世界晨报》刊登以下文章：

关于日本海军陆战队员中山被杀一案，警方逮捕了一名名为“Jack”的朝鲜人，以及两名广东人杨文道(楊文道)和叶海生(葉海生)。后来，受雇于大陆(Da Loh)舞厅的私家侦探周社榮(Chow Zeu Yung)也涉嫌其中。上海公共租界工部局警务处正以杀人罪起诉这些人。
有人说，杨和叶是被常元(常元)（别名常元佳(常元佳)）陷害的，常元向警方提供了情报。常元认识一位富有的日本侨民。为了从这位日本人那里获取钱财，常元与两名朋友合谋，告诉该日本人他们知道一些关于中山被杀案的内情，但需要资金才能彻底查清此案。该日本人向他提供了总计约1,000元的多笔款项。然而，后来该日本人对结果感到不耐烦，加之常元反复索要钱财，于是常元向某位日本警察告发，该警察拘留了常元并迫使他供出凶手。在困境中，常元供出了他的仇人杨和叶的名字。但真相总有一天会大白。
据悉，杨文道被捕时，曾有人打算保释他，但因本案涉及国际关系而未果。
常元现被拘禁在六仙花园(Rokusen Garden)。日本当局每天给他五美元用于膳食和鸦片。每当他外出时，便有两名便衣士兵以保护为名跟随他，但实际上，这些士兵是被派来监视他以防止其逃跑的。

pages.en:
May 19, 1936.
Afternoon Translation.
Lih Pao ( 立報 ):
THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE
A further hearing of the case against the persons arrested in connection with the murder of the Japanese marine named Hideo Nakayama will take place at 2 p.m. May 20 in Shanghai First Special District Court. As the case has taken on a new aspect after the appearance in the Court of one named Chang Tsun ( 張琛 ), it is believed that important developments may be expected after the hearing on May 20.
Lawyer Kuh Chao Chi ( 葛肇基 ) is appearing for the defence of the accused Yang Vung Tao ( 楊文道 ). Tseu Shou Yong ( 周社榮 ) who has also been arrested on suspicion of being connected with the case will be brought before the Court to-morrow when he will be confronted with the accused Yih Hai Sung ( 葉海生 ) and Yang Vung Tao.
It is understood that Miss Loh ( 陸 ), a cabaret girl, will testify to-morrow.
Kwangtung Pao ( 廣東報 ) :-
Kwangtung Middle School to Hold Meeting on May 20
Miss Zung Hoong Pih ( 陳鴻璧 ), Principal of the Kwangtung Middle School ( 廣東中學 ), has tendered her resignation to the Board of Directors of the school because of the false accusations made against her in connection with the murder of the Japanese marine Nakayama. In view of the fact that Miss Zung is a well-behaved person, the directors of the school are very angry at the false accusations and will hold a meeting at 3 p.m. May 20 at the Cantonese Guild, Ningpo Road, to discuss the affair.
Ling Feng An ( 林楓庵 ), Dean of the Kwangtung Middle School, has sent the following letter to this paper:-
"On May 14, your paper published a detailed report regarding the false accusations against Miss Zung Hoong Pih, the Principal of our school. Truly, many strange events have happened in our school between January 27 the date on which Li Zuh Gin ( 李曙琴 ) visited our school and asked a specimen of the handwriting of the Principal, and April 21 when foreign policemen conducted a search at the school. We know nothing about the case or the motive of Li Zuh Gin.
"When various Kwangtung public bodies formed a Yang Vung Tao Case Support Committee on May 15, I attended the meeting and made a report on the false accusations against the Principal of our school, as it has been ascertained that the affair was also connected with Yang Vung Tao's case. Unexpectedly, Li Zuh Gin, who was present, said that my report impaired his reputation. I do not know whether Li's endeavour to obtain a specimen of the handwriting of the Principal was well-intentioned."

1936年5月19日。
下午译文。
《立报》：
中山谋杀案
涉及日本海军陆战队员中山秀雄(Hideo Nakayama)被杀案的被捕人员案件将进一步审理，将于5月20日下午2时在上海第一特区地方法院开庭。由于一名叫张琛(張琛)的人出庭后，案件出现了新局面，人们认为5月20日的庭审后可能会有重要进展。
葛肇基(Kuh Chao Chi)律师出任被告杨文道(楊文道)的辩护律师。同样因涉嫌与此案有关而被捕的周社荣(Tseu Shou Yong)将于明天被带上法庭，与被告叶海生(葉海生)和杨文道当面对质。
据悉，舞女陆小姐(Miss Loh (陸))将于明天作证。
《广东报》：
广东中学将于5月20日召开会议
广东中学(廣東中學)校长陈鸿璧(Zung Hoong Pih (陳鴻璧))女士因在中山海军陆战队员被杀案中受到不实指控，已向学校董事会提出辞呈。鉴于陈女士品行端正，校董会对这些不实指控感到非常愤怒，将于5月20日下午3时在宁波路的广东公所举行会议讨论此事。
广东中学校长林楓庵(Ling Feng An)致函本报如下：
“5月14日，贵报详细报道了关于我校校长陈鸿璧女士受到不实指控的情况。的确，自1月27日李曙琴(Li Zuh Gin (李曙琴))访问我校并要求采集校长笔迹样本之日起，至4月21日外籍警察在校内进行搜索之日止，我校发生了许多奇怪的事件。我们对案情或李曙琴的动机一无所知。
“当各广东公团于5月15日成立‘杨文道案后援会’时，我出席了会议，并就我校校长受到不实指控一事作了报告，因为经查实，此事也与杨文道案有关。出乎意料的是，在场的李曙琴称我的报告损害了他的名誉。我不知道李曙琴试图获取校长笔迹样本是否出于善意。”

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MAY 16, 1936

Cantonese Meet
2nd Time To
Talk Yang Aid

Suspect In Murder Of
Nakayama Said Falsely
Accused

Some 50 prominent local Canton-
ese, whose identity was not reveal-
ed, held another meeting yesterday
afternoon to discuss plans to aid
Yang Wen-tao, now facing a mur-
der charge with Yih Hai-sen, or
"Hsiao Kwangtung," for the killing
of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama
on November 9, 1935, it was learned
yesterday.

Veiled behind a screen of secrecy,
the meeting, attended by representa-
tives of different Shanghai Canton-
ese clubs, is understood to have been
held at a place on North Szechuen
Road.

Chang Seng, chief defense wit-
ness at Yang's trial May 7, was pre-
sent yesterday to tell the gathering
about the alleged frame-up. He
retold the story which he related to
the Court accusing Tseng Yuan and
Dr. Chen Wei-ming as conspiring to
give false testimony against Yang.

Following closely on the meeting
of the Cantonese Residents' Associa-
tion Wednesday, which outlined
plans to help Yang in his legal fight,
the gathering yesterday endorsed the
aid program.

The Residents' Association at its
meeting Wednesday declared that
Yang was falsely accused by wit-
nesses who wanted to get the large
reward.

Yang, who heads several local
Cantonese clubs, including the Tung
Yi Association, is well-known in
the Cantonese community here.

《字林西报》，1936年5月16日，星期六

广东人第二次集会
商讨援助杨文道

中山谋杀案嫌疑人
据称遭诬陷

据悉，约50名身份未予透露的本地知名广东人士于昨日下午再次举行会议，讨论援助杨文道的计划。杨文道目前正与叶海森(Yih Hai-sen)，即“小广东”，面临1935年11月9日杀害准尉中山秀雄(Hideo Nakayama)的谋杀指控。

这次会议在四川北路某地举行，笼罩在保密的面纱之下，据悉有上海各广东同乡会的代表出席。

在5月7日杨文道庭审中担任主要辩方证人的张森(Chang Seng)昨日到场，向与会者讲述了所谓的构陷内幕。他重述了在法庭上讲述的故事，指控常元和陈维明博士(Chen Wei-ming)共谋提供针对杨文道的伪证。

紧随周三广东居民协会会议之后——该会议概述了在法律斗争中帮助杨文道的计划——昨日的集会认可了这项援助方案。

居民协会在周三的会议上声明，杨文道是被那些企图获取高额赏金的证人诬告的。

杨文道统领包括东义协会在内的数个本地广东同乡会，在此地的广东社区中颇有名气。

May 16, 1936.
Morning Translation.

Lih Pao (立報) and other local newspapers ; -
THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE : MEETING HELD IN SUPPORT OF YANG
VUNG TAO.

At 3 p.m. May 15, the Kwangtung Fellow
Provincials Association, the Chung San Fellow Countrymen's
Association, the Cantonese Guild, the Chaochow Fellow
Countrymen's Association, the Cantonese Merchants'
Association, the Dah Pu Fellow Countrymen's Association,
the Chaochow Guild, the Kwangtung Middle and Primary School,
the Sin Wei Fellow Countrymen's Association, the Tai San
Fellow Countrymen's Association, the Yu San Tong (禺山堂),
the Wu Hwa Fellow Countrymen's Association and the Pei San
Fellow Countrymen's Association held a meeting at a certain
place in Chapel to discuss ways and means for rendering
assistance to Yang Vung Tao (楊文道), who is under arrest
in connection with the Nakayama Murder Case. Kuo Chi Ming
(郭啟明) presided.
A Cantonese named Kuh Chao Chi (古肇基), who
is appearing for the defence of Yang Vung Tao, made the
following report:- "The present case is a frame-up arranged
by Zung Wei Ming (鄭偉民) and others. With the object of
securing the large reward, Zung first attempted to drag Zung
Hoong Pih into the case. When the attempt failed, he
involved Yang Vung Tao. All this can be proved by the fact
that the book was not thrown away after the murder and that
Yih Hai Sung had changed his statement several times. At
first Tseng Yuan (曾元) intended to let Chang Tsun
(張瑮) arrange the frame-up; he also tried to obtain the
service of a Miss Loh (羅), a cabaret girl, to act as
witness, but both these persons refused to be drawn in.
Finally, Tseng (曾), Zung (鄭) and Chang (張) conspired together
to bring the false charge."
Chang Tsun who was the next speaker made a
statement which was similar to that he made in the 1st Special
District Court on May 6. His speech included the following
points which are not contained in his statement made in Court:
(1) When Zung Ping San (鄭平山) went to the Military
Headquarters of a certain nation to pick out the pistol,
he was in great fear and was given protection by
detectives and policemen of a certain nation.
(2) A dancing girl named Loh (羅) who was detained for
money owing to an Indian was bailed out by Tseng Yuan and
told by him to go to the Japanese Military Headquarters
to act as a witness. She was told by Tseng what to say
at the Headquarters. As no money was forthcoming,
nothing was done.
(3) A Cantonese named Liu Zoong Zung (劉從順) who was
assaulted and wounded with a chopper on Peking Road was
visited by Tseng Yuan and told to go to the Japanese
Military Headquarters and tell them that it was he who
had been assaulted by Zung Hoong Pih (陳鴻璧) because
he (Liu) knew something of the affair.
(4) In an attempt to obtain money from a certain party, Tseng
Yuan once rubbed his chest with a cash until the skin
became red and then alleged that he had been assaulted.
A certain party promised to give him money for medical
expenses.
(5) At one time Tseng Yuan did not dare to come out for fear
that the plot might be exposed. Later detectives of a
certain nationality protected him.

1936年5月16日。
晨间译稿。

《立报》及其他本地报纸；——
中山谋杀案：举行会议支持杨文道。

5月15日下午3时，广东同乡会、中山同乡会、广东会馆、潮州同乡会、广东商人协会、大埔同乡会、潮州会馆、广东中小学、新会同乡会、台山同乡会、禺山堂、五华同乡会及北山同乡会在闸北某地举行会议，讨论援助因中山谋杀案被捕的杨文道（楊文道）的方法与途径。郭啟明（郭啟明）担任主席。
一位名为古肇基（古肇基）的广东人，作为杨文道的辩护代表，作了如下报告：“本案是由郑伟民（鄭偉民）等人策划的诬陷。为了获取巨额赏金，郑首先试图将郑鸿璧卷入此案。企图失败后，他又牵连了杨文道。所有这些都可以由以下事实证实：凶案发生后那本书并未被丢弃，以及叶海松多次更改供词。起初，曾元（曾元）打算让张璘（張瑮）安排这次诬陷；他还试图聘请一名姓罗（羅）的舞女作证人，但这两人均拒绝被卷入。最后，曾（曾）、郑（鄭）和张（張）共谋提出虚假指控。”
接下来发言的张璘所作的陈述，与他于5月6日在第一特区法院所作的陈述相似。他的发言包括以下几点，这些内容未包含他在法庭上的陈述中：
(1) 当郑平山（鄭平山）前往某国军事司令部挑选手枪时，他非常恐惧，并得到了某国侦探和警察的保护。
(2) 一名姓罗（羅）的舞女因欠一名印度人钱款而被拘留，曾元将其保释，并告诉她去日本军事司令部作证人。曾元告诉她在司令部该如何说。由于没有拿到钱，此事便无下文。
(3) 一名叫刘从顺（劉從順）的广东人在北京路遭到斧头袭击受伤，曾元探望了他，并让他去日本军事司令部，告诉他们他是被陈鸿璧（陳鴻璧）袭击的，因为他（刘）知道一些内情。
(4) 曾元为了从某方获取钱财，曾用铜板摩擦胸部直至皮肤发红，然后声称自己遭到袭击。某方答应给他医药费。
(5) 曾元一度因担心阴谋败露而不敢露面。后来，某国籍的侦探保护了他。

May 16, 1936. Morning Translation.

(6) When Tseng Yuan went to Tsingtao on April 12, he tried
to induce two persons named Lee (李) and Yang (楊)
to act as witnesses for him, but they refused.

Ling Foong An (林庵), the Dean of the
Kwangtung Middle School, acting as representative of Miss
Zung Hoong Pih, the Principal of the school, made a report
on the intimidation of Miss Zung Hoong Pih by certain
persons. As what he said was somewhat similar to what was
published in this paper on May 14, his address is not
reproduced.

The meeting then discussed measures to be
taken to assist Yang Vung Tao.
It was resolved to form a "Yang Vung Tao
Case Support Committee" with 15 Cantonese, who are well
known in Shanghai, as members.
It was also decided to assemble all the
evidence and to publish the true circumstances attending
the arrest of Yang Vung Tao.

An Important Witness Interviewed

Interviewed by a reporter of this paper,
Chang Tsun, one of the important witnesses in the Nakayama
murder case, made the following statement yesterday:-
"It was my conscience that urged me to
surrender to the Police and the Court and to volunteer a
statement. I had no other motive whatever. I am well
informed about the facts in the case. Furthermore, I did
not desire to see innocent persons suffer for something
with which they had absolutely no connection whatever. I,
therefore, made up my mind to surrender to the Police."
When questioned by the reporter about the
document in Tseng Yuan's handwriting, which was handed
in to the Court on May 6 by lawyer Kuh Chao Chi, as well
as the allegations made by Tseng Yuan to the effect that
he (Chang Tsun) had demanded a certain sum of money from
the Japanese detective, Chang Tsun replied: "The document
in question was handed to me by Tseng Yuan on April 11,
the day before he (Tseng Yuan) left Shanghai for Tsingtao.
He asked me to inform Zung Hoong Pih, as my cousin is
employed as a teacher in the Kwangtung Middle School. I
was somewhat unwilling to do this, but I asked my cousin
to give a hint to Miss Zung to prepare her. However, due
to the fact that my cousin is not on close terms with Zung
Hoong Pih, the Principal of the Kwangtung Middle School,
he did not give her the hint. As regards the statement
made in Court by Tseng Yuan at the last hearing of the
case to the effect that I had demanded $500 from the
Japanese detective, it is a false allegation."

1936年5月16日。晨间译稿。

(6) 4月12日曾元前往青岛时，试图诱使两名姓李（李）和姓杨（楊）的人为他作证人，但遭到拒绝。

广东中学校长林庵（林庵）作为该校校长郑鸿璧小姐的代表，就某些人对郑鸿璧小姐进行恐吓一事作了报告。由于他的讲话内容与本报5月14日刊登的内容大致相同，故不再复述其讲话全文。

随后，会议讨论了援助杨文道的措施。
决议成立“杨文道案后援会”，由15位在上海知名的广东人担任委员。
还决定收集所有证据，并公布杨文道被捕的真实情况。

采访重要证人

本报记者采访了中山谋杀案的重要证人之一张璘，他昨日作出如下声明：
“是良心促使我向警方和法院自首并自愿提供证词。我没有任何其他动机。我对案件事实非常了解。此外，我不愿看到无辜者因与他们毫无关系的事情而受苦。因此，我决定向警方自首。”
当记者问及律师古肇基于5月6日提交给法院的曾元手书文件，以及曾元指控他（张璘）向日本侦探索要一定数额金钱的说法时，张璘回答说：“该文件是曾元在4月11日，即他（曾元）离开上海前往青岛的前一天交给我的。他让我通知郑鸿璧，因为我的表亲在广东中学任教。我有些不愿意这样做，但我让我的表亲给郑小姐暗示，让她有所准备。然而，由于我的表亲与广东中学校长郑鸿璧关系不密切，他没有给她暗示。至于曾元在案件上次庭审时在法庭上所称我向日方侦探索要500美元的说法，纯属诬蔑。”

May 15, 1936.
7
Afternoon Translation.

The Crystal (晶報) publishes the following article contributed
by one named Mei Miao (曼妙) :-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE

The details of the case of the murder of
the Japanese marine Nakayama in Shanghai are very complicated
and are full of attempts at corruption. One man has
surrendered himself and disclosed a malicious accusation,
while another has retracted his statement, confessing his
previous activities. The public has been greatly puzzled
over the developments of this case which involves schools
and cabarets.

Some say that the reason why the case
has assumed such proportions is because of the desire to
obtain the huge reward, while it is also alleged that
besides receiving the reward, there is also the desire to
extort money from some person.

For instance, Miss Zung Hoong Pih (陳鴻璧),
the Principal of the Kwangtung Middle School (廣東中學),
was intimidated by some unscrupulous persons who intended
to extort from her a large sum of money in connection with
this case. However, the attempt met with no good result.
Later a search was conducted by the Japanese detectives
at the school, but nothing was unearthed. Had not Miss Zung
made a report previously to the North Station Branch Bureau
of Public Safety on the attempt of these unscrupulous
elements, she would have then been put under arrest and
been made to undergo undeserved imprisonment as the result
of this malicious accusation.

Miss Zung is very keen on education and
never aspires to fame. The Kwangtung Middle School where
there are in all more than 690 students, including those
in the kindergarten, is the outcome of her painstaking
efforts over the past twenty years. Her assigned salary
per month is $150, but she only draws $50 per month as
locomotion allowance, the rest being contributed to the
school funds. She is generally regarded by us as a law
abiding and respectable person, and yet there are persons
who have even counterfeited false letters and documents
as a means to implicate her in a crime of which she is
innocent. It is, therefore, probable that in future any
law abiding and respectable person may be accused of being
communist.

The Kwangtung Fellow Provincials Association
is now devising ways and means to counteract the false
accusation against Yang Vung Tao (楊文道) who was implicated
in this case by false evidence. I hope the authorities of
the Settlement as well as the senior officials of the Court
will make a careful study of the case so as to bring about
an impartial and just judgment of the case, while the entire
number of local residents should keep their eyes open so
as to avert the trickery and treachery of the unscrupulous
elements.

1936年5月15日。
7
午后译稿。

《晶报》刊登了一篇署名为曼妙（曼妙）的文章：——

中山谋杀案

上海日本海军陆战队员中山被杀案的细节非常复杂，充满了腐败企图。一人自首并揭露了恶意诬告，另一人则撤回供词，承认了其先前的活动。公众对这起涉及学校和舞厅的案件的发展感到十分困惑。

有人说，案件之所以发展到如此规模，是因为渴望获得巨额赏金，同时也有说法称，除了领取赏金外，还有向某人勒索钱财的欲望。

例如，广东中学（廣東中學）校长郑鸿璧小姐（陳鴻璧）受到一些不法分子的恐吓，这些人企图借此案向她勒索巨款。然而，这一企图未能得逞。后来，日本侦探在学校进行了搜查，但未发现任何线索。如果不是郑小姐此前向北站公安分局报案，揭露这些不法分子的企图，她当时就会因这项恶意诬告而被捕，并遭受不白之冤的监禁。

郑小姐热衷于教育事业，从不追求名利。广东中学包括幼儿园学生在内共有690多名学生，是她过去二十年辛勤努力的成果。她的月薪定为150元，但她每月只支取50元作为交通费，其余部分都捐献给学校基金。她通常被我们视为守法且受人尊敬的人，然而竟有人伪造信件和文件，企图将她卷入一项她完全无辜的罪行。因此，很可能将来任何守法且受人尊敬的人都可能被指控为共产党。

广东同乡会目前正在设法对策，以反击对杨文道（楊文道）的虚假指控，杨文道是因伪证而被卷入此案的。我希望租界当局以及法院的高级官员仔细研究此案，以便对案件作出公正公平的判决，同时全体本地居民应保持警惕，以防备不法分子的诡计和背叛。

May 14, 1936. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao :-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE : MEETING OF KWANG TUNG FELLOW
PROVINCIALS ASSOCIATION.

The Standing Committee of the Kwangtung Fellow
Provincials Association held its 15th meeting yesterday, at
which H.O. Tong 唐泌安 (Superintendent of Customs), Li Dah
Chao 李大超 (a Departmental Chief of the Shanghai City
Government), Kwok Zuong 郭顺 (Chinese Councillor of the
S.M.C.), Kwok Zoong iang(郭仲良), Chen Feng Yuan(陳風元),
Chen Gee Feng(陳其方) and Li Chih(李澤) were present.
H.O. Tong presided.
After opening the proceedings, the chairman
of the meeting declared :- "Following the arrest of Yang
Vung Tao(楊文道) and others by the S.M.P. on suspicion of
being concerned in the murder of the Japanese marine Hideo
Nakayama last year, the Association has requested the
Shanghai City Government, the First Special District Court
and the Police to ascertain the truth of the case so that
innocent persons may not be involved. The Court has
held two hearings of the case, during which many new items
of evidence have been brought to light which tend to prove
that Yang Vung Tao is really innocent and that he is a
victim of the false accusation framed by Zung Ping San
(鄭平山), Tseng Yuan(曾元) and Chang Zai Yuan(張財源)
with the object of securing the reward. In the cause of
humanity and for the purpose of upholding justice, the
Association should endeavour to render its assistance."
The following resolutions were then passed:-
(1) That in conjunction with other public
bodies, a Yang Vung Tao Case Support Committee be formed
for the purpose of effecting his release.
(2) That a manifesto be issued giving the
truth of the case for the benefit of the public.
(3) That the Shanghai City Government be
petitioned to decide on the truth of the case and to render
assistance.
(4) That a letter be sent to the S.M.C. and
the Chinese Ratepayers Association requesting them to pay
attention to the truth of the case and to render their
assistance.
(5) That a letter be sent to the Court
requesting it to decide on the truth of the case and to
render its legal assistance so as to prevent innocent
persons from being involved in the intrigue.

our principal was connected with the Communist Party and

《申报》：——

中山谋杀案：广东同乡会会议。

广东同乡会常务委员会昨日举行第15次会议，唐泌安（海关监督）、李大超（上海市政府处长）、郭顺（工部局华董）、郭仲良（郭仲良）、陈风元（陳風元）、陈其方（陳其方）和李泽（李澤）出席。唐泌安担任主席。
会议开始后，主席宣布：“继去年公共租界警务处因涉嫌参与杀害日本海军陆战队员中山秀雄而逮捕杨文道（楊文道）等人后，本会已请求上海市政府、第一特区法院和警方查明案件真相，以免无辜者受牵连。法院已对此案进行了两次审理，期间许多新证据浮出水面，倾向于证明杨文道确实是无辜的，他是郑平山（鄭平山）、曾元（曾元）和张财源（張財源）为了获取赏金而策划的诬陷的受害者。出于人道主义和维护正义的目的，本会应努力提供援助。”
随后通过以下决议：
(1) 与其他公共团体联合，成立杨文道案后援会，旨在促成其获释。
(2) 发表宣言，向公众公布案件真相。
(3) 请愿上海市政府查明案件真相并提供援助。
(4) 致函工部局和华人纳税会，请求他们关注案件真相并提供援助。
(5) 致函法院，请求其查明案件真相并提供法律援助，以防止无辜者卷入阴谋。

《立报》：

本报记者采访了广东中学（廣東中學）的一位负责人，该负责人作了如下声明：
“今年1月27日上午11点左右，两名名叫李琴（李琴）和吴子垣（吳子垣）的陌生人来到我校，要求会见我校校长谭鸿璧（譚鴻璧）。据这两人称，有人向虹口警察局秘密举报，称我校校长与共产党有关，并且

that she had used bogus debenture bonds. The callers added that there were letters written in her own handwriting which could be produced as proof against her, and that if that was true, they could render her some assistance as they knew a Japanese detective quite well, but if there was no such case, legal proceedings could be instituted. At the same time, the two persons asked the principal to sign her name and to give it to them for comparison. As it seemed very strange to her, Zung Hoong Pih emphatically refused to give them her signature and told them that as she was not a member of the Communist Party, there would be no necessity for her to give them her signature for comparison. Subsequently, Woo Ts Han asked Zung Hoong Pih which doctor she was used to send for whenever she was sick and whether she had signed any I.O.U. outside. Zung Hoong Pih replied that in case of sickness, she would call in her brother for consultation and there was no I.O.U. made by her outside. Woo Ts Han and Li Zuh Gin then left the premises.

"After their request for a written signature of Zung Hoong Pih had been rejected, Woo Ts Han and Li Zuh Gin then used their efforts ;;; the teachers of the Kwangtung Middle School named Ma Siao ( 麥嘯 ), Chong Ting ( 蒼丁 ) and Zung Soo Fong ( 陳素芳 female, whose father is known to Li Zuh Gin). On February 1, Li Zuh Gin called on Ma Siao and told her that someone had taken legal action against the principal and that the complainant was one named Zung Ping San (alias Zung Wei Ming 鄭偉民 , a Japanese subject of Chinese origin. He once had been shown over the school under the guidance of Liao Ting , an ex-teacher of the school). Li Zuh Gin also asked her to call at the Police Station to identify the writing in the Japanese detective's office and told her that certain sums of money would be given for her service. Ma Siao did not go there and informed Zung Hoong Pih and Ling Foong An ( 林鳳庵 ), Dean of the school, about the matter. Unexpectedly, on the following day Li Zuh Gin called again on Ma Siao and asked her to accompany him to see a Japanese at the Sun Ya ( 新雅 ) Restaurant and to identify the writing there. As his request met with refusal, he made three or four requests to Zung Soo Fong and Yan Li Zong ( 嚴禮宗 ) to do the work, but these requests were also rejected.

"Upon learning of this, Zung Hoong Pih, besides safeguarding herself, submitted on February 5 a detailed report on the treacherous acts of Li Zuh Gin to Liang Fu Chu ( 梁扶初 ), Chief of the North Railway Station Branch Bureau of Public Safety. She requested the Chief of the Branch Bureau to put the report on record and to render her protection.

"But stranger things had yet to happen. On April 18, when the teachers and staff of the school were having tiffin, a third year student of the junior middle school, named Voong Zau Tsoong ( 馮肇忠 ), age 15 years, came to Ling Foong An, Dean of the school, and told him: 'There is someone outside who wants to see you. He is wearing a long gown, he carries a stick, and has a mustache; he is of short build. He said he could not come in here and would not give his name. He further said that you must not speak to him when you go out, but just follow him.'

称她使用了伪造的债券。来访者还补充说，有她亲笔书写的信件可作为指控她的证据，如果属实，他们可以提供一些帮助，因为他们与一名日本侦探非常熟识；但如果并无此事，则可提起法律诉讼。同时，这两人要求校长签名并交给他们以作比对。钟宏璧（Zung Hoong Pih）觉得此举十分奇怪，坚决拒绝提供签名，并告诉他们，由于她并非共产党成员，没有必要向他们提供签名进行比对。随后，吴子汉（Woo Ts Han）询问钟宏璧，生病时通常请哪位医生诊治，以及是否在外签署过任何借据。钟宏璧回答说，若生病她会叫来兄弟商议诊治，且她从未在外签署过借据。吴子汉和李祖根（Li Zuh Gin）随即离开该处。

“在索取钟宏璧书面签名的要求被拒后，吴子汉和李祖根转而努力接触广东中学的教师麦啸（Ma Siao）、苍丁（Chong Ting）和陈素芳（Zung Soo Fong，女性，其父为李祖根所认识）。2月1日，李祖根拜访麦啸，告诉她有人对校长提起了诉讼，原告名为郑平三（Zung Ping San，别名郑伟民 Zung Wei Ming，系日籍华人。他曾在该校前教师廖丁（Liao Ting）的引导下参观过学校）。李祖根还要求她去警察局，在日本侦探办公室辨认笔迹，并告知为此服务将给予一定金额的报酬。麦啸未去，并将此事告知了钟宏璧及学校教务主任林凤庵（Ling Foong An）。不料次日李祖根再次拜访麦啸，要求她陪同他去新雅（Sun Ya）酒楼见一名日本人，并在那里辨认笔迹。由于他的要求遭到拒绝，他又向陈素芳和严礼宗（Yan Li Zong）提出了三四次请求，要求他们做这项工作，但这些请求也均被拒绝。

“得知此事后，钟宏璧除采取自我保护措施外，还于2月5日向公安局北站分局局长梁扶初（Liang Fu Chu）提交了一份关于李祖根奸诈行为的详细报告。她请求分局局长将该报告备案，并给予她保护。

“但更奇怪的事情还在后面。4月18日，当学校教职员工正在吃午饭时，一名15岁的初中三年级学生冯肇忠（Voong Zau Tsoong）来到学校教务主任林凤庵处，告诉他说：‘外面有人想见你。他身穿长衫，手持手杖，留着胡子，身材矮小。他说他不能进来，也不愿留下姓名。他还说，你出去时不要和他说话，只要跟着他走就行。’

"Ling Foong An thought it was very extraordinary
and on questioning the student, the latter went on: 'That man
said to me, "Your principal has been accused by someone.
Some former employee of the school who once obtained
contributions amounting to $10,000 for the school has committed
a serious crime. Your school is now surrounded by detectives
and policemen, so I cannot come in. I have come to rescue
your people. We must not carry on any conversation until we
are on the other side of the railway. Or else I will

"Suspecting that the caller had no good intention,
Ling Foong An told the student to tell the man that 'Mr. Ling
was not in'.
The reporter of this paper was told by Mr. Ling that
the strange caller might possibly be Zung Ping San, as Mr.
Ling visited Zung once and they knew each other.
"The next day after the call (April 19) the
school received a letter written in pencil. It reads:
'Comrade Hoong Pi',
'The case is very serious. I received
a letter from Zung Voong Yuan (陳鳳源) yesterday stating
that he(she) had seen Pao Kyu (鮑居) in Tientsin, but not
Yih Hoi Sung (葉海生). Since the Korean named "Zuh Ka
Pei" (直加彼) was arrested, our party has sent all those
who participated in the affair to other places for safety.
Make your escape as soon as you see this letter, otherwise
your life is in danger. Two comrades obtained contributions
amounting to more than $3,000 and $8,000 respectively in the

two comrades also have to hide themselves in other places we

'Be sure not to go to any court when you

Written by Ying (英), Head of

"The receipt of this letter has caused great
surprise to the school authorities, but as it was Sunday when
the letter was received, nothing was done to deal with the
matter. It was not until the arrival at the school of the

letter was forwarded in company with a written statement to

"Acting on this request, the Bureau of Public

Japanese detective officers disclosed that the search would

“林凤庵觉得此事非常离奇，经询问该学生，后者继续说道：‘那人对我说，“你们的校长被人控告了。学校的一名前雇员曾为学校募集到一万元捐款，此人犯有重罪。现在你们学校周围布满了侦探和警察，所以我不能进去。我是来救你们的人的。在到达铁路另一边之前，我们不得进行任何交谈。否则我将在下午1点打电话（他向我要了我们的电话号码）。”’
“怀疑来访者不怀好意，林凤庵让学生告诉那人‘林先生不在’。
本报记者从林先生处获悉，这名奇怪的来访者可能是郑平三，因为林先生曾拜访过郑，两人互相认识。
“在该次造访的第二天（4月19日），学校收到一封用铅笔写的信。内容如下：
‘宏璧同志’，
‘案情非常严重。我昨天收到陈凤源（Zung Voong Yuan）的来信，称他（她）在天津见到了鲍居（Pao Kyu），但未见到叶海生（Yih Hoi Sung）。自从名为“直加彼”（Zuh Ka Pei）的朝鲜人被捕后，我们党已将所有参与此事的人送往其他地方以确保安全。见此信后请立即逃离，否则你的生命会有危险。在一·二八事变后，有两名同志以你们学校的名义分别募集了三千多元和八千多元的捐款。由于这两名同志也必须躲藏到其他地方，我们希望你能将钱款汇给我们的社团，因为我们急需这笔钱。
‘收到传票时切勿前往任何法庭，否则你将丧命，因为某起案件已被发现，且我们早已将你的名字告知外人。只需躲藏在安全的地方即可。
杨久道（Yang Vung Tao）
由妇女部部长英（Ying）代笔。’
“收到这封信令校方大为惊讶，但由于收到信件时正值星期日，未对该事采取任何处理措施。直到4月20日校长钟宏璧小姐抵达学校后，这封奇怪的信件才连同一份书面陈述一并送交公安局北站第五分局备查。然而，就在当天信件送达公安局分局后，两名日本侦探督察（一名来自当地日本领事馆，另一名来自工部局警务处）来到南市公安局，请求协助在闸北逮捕某人。在被问及详情时，他们不愿透露相关人员的姓名。
“应此请求，公安局指令北站分局局长梁扶初陪同他们进行搜索。直到搜查令签发后，日本侦探官员才透露搜查将在

However, the two Japanese officers insisted upon making the

"Being well conversant with the circumstances,
the Chief of the Branch Bureau, therefore, exhibited the
written statement submitted Miss Zung for reference as well
as the threatening letter and explained to them (the Japanese

rang up the Japanese Consulate who instructed that no arrest

"The Japanese detectives then left the place
and took with them the documents, which were submitted to the

According to Ling Foong An, the Dean of
the school, Principal Zung has devoted her life to education
for approximately 30 years and the Kwangtung Middle School
is the outcome of her strenuous efforts during the past twenty

per month as locomotion allowance, the remaining sum being
contributed to the school funds.
This school was established in the first
year of the Chinese Republic. It was completely demolished

广东中学针对钟宏璧进行。对此，分局局长向他们通报了钟小姐提交的备查文件，并要求他们在前往该地之前等待并商讨此事。他还拿出了钟小姐的文件。然而，两名日本官员坚持要进行搜查。分局局长梁扶初遂带上四名侦探，乘坐两辆警车陪同他们前往该地进行搜查。一行人于5点30分抵达学校，对校长室进行了搜查，但直到约九点钟，并未获得任何定罪证据。然而，其中一名日本官员仍坚持拘留钟宏璧。
“鉴于对该情况十分了解，分局局长遂出示了钟小姐提交的备查书面陈述以及那封恐吓信，并用日语向他们（日本官员）进行解释，随后其中一名日本侦探致电日本领事馆，领事馆指示因无证据不得实施逮捕。接着，分局局长要求钟宏璧签署一份保释书，承诺随传随到。
“日本侦探随后离开现场，并带走了钟宏璧提交给分局备查的文件，以供审阅和检查。钟宏璧因此事深受刺激，身体严重不适。因此，她向董事会辞去学校校长职务，但学校教职员工和学生劝她留任。”
据学校教务主任林凤庵称，钟校长投身教育事业约三十年，广东中学是她过去二十年辛勤努力的成果。她的月薪为150元，但她每月仅领取50元作为交通津贴，其余款项均捐赠给学校基金。
该校成立于民国元年。在一·二八事变期间被完全摧毁，但现已恢复原状。该校共有学生693名，包括幼儿园学生。据悉，该校校长钟宏璧小姐已向广东同乡会报告了本案的过往经过。

Lih Pao (立報) :-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE - LOCAL CANTONESE PUBLIC BODIES
TO HOLD MEETING

At 6 p.m. May 11; the Kwangtung
Fellow Provincials Association held a meeting at its office
at No. 32 Rue Corneille, French Concession, to discuss
ways and means to effect the release of Yang Vung Tao
(楊久道) who was arrested in connection with the Nakayama
murder case. More than ten persons, including H.O. Tong
(Superintendent of Customs), Li Dah Chao (李大超) (A
Departmental Chief of the Shanghai City Government), Kwok
Zung (郭順) (Chinese Councillor on the S.M.C.), Li Chih
(李澤), Yang Mei Nan (楊梅南), Chen Feng Yuan (陳鳳元),
and Chen Chi Feng (陳其芳), were present. Mr. Tong
stated at the meeting that Yang Vung Tao was implicated
by some persons on false evidence.
It was latter decided at the meeting that
a general meeting of representatives of the various local
Cantonese public bodies be held in Shanghai (venue not
mentioned) on the afternoon of May 15 to discuss measures
to secure for his release.
It is learned that the Association will
issue a manifesto announcing the facts of Yang's arrest
on false accusation as well as the present condition of
Yih Hai Sung (葉海生) during his detention by the Police.
The Association will at the same time petition the Shanghai
City Government, the S.M.C., and the Chinese Ratepayers
Association of the International Settlement requesting
them to uphold justice.

Kwangtung Pao (廣報) :-

At a meeting held at 3.30 p.m. May 11 by
the Kwangtung Fellow Provincials Association, the following
decisions were reached:-
(1) That a meeting be held by various
public bodies on the afternoon of May 14 to devise ways
and means to support Yang Vung Tao.
(2) That a manifesto be issued relating
to the false allegations against Yang Vung Tao.
(3) That a letter be forwarded to the
Shanghai City Government and the S.M.C. requesting them
to investigate into the real facts of the case.
(4) That the Court be requested to investigate
into the matter with a view to saving the innocent person
from suffering.

The Hongkong Chung San Overseas Chinese
Commercial Association and the Pei San Fellow Provincials
Association are indignant over the involving of Yang Vung
Tao in a crime of which he is innocent. Yesterday the two
Associations sent a joint telegram to the Kwangtung Fellow
Provincials Association in Shanghai requesting it to effect
the release of Yang Vung Tao in order to protect their
fellow countrymen.

《立报》（Lih Pao）:-

中山谋杀案——本地粤籍公共团体将举行会议

5月11日下午6时，广东同乡会在法租界高乃依路（Rue Corneille）32号会所举行会议，讨论设法释放因中山谋杀案被捕的杨久道（Yang Vung Tao）的方法。出席者十余人，包括海关总监唐（H.O. Tong）、上海市政府部门主管李大超（Li Dah Chao）、工部局华董郭顺（Kwok Zung）、李泽（Li Chih）、杨梅南（Yang Mei Nan）、陈凤元（Chen Feng Yuan）和陈其芳（Chen Chi Feng）。唐先生在会上表示，杨久道是被一些人以伪证诬陷的。
会议后来决定，于5月15日下午在上海（地点未提及）举行各本地粤籍公共团体代表联席会议，讨论确保其获释的措施。
据悉，该会将发表宣言，公布杨久道被诬告逮捕的事实，以及叶海生（Yih Hai Sung）在被警方拘留期间的现状。该会同时将向上海市政府、工部局及国际租界华人纳税会请愿，请求他们主持公道。

《广报》（Kwangtung Pao）:-

在5月11日下午3时30分举行的广东同乡会会议上，达成以下决议：-
(1) 各公共团体于5月14日下午举行会议，策划支持杨久道的方法。
(2) 就针对杨久道的虚假指控发表宣言。
(3) 致函上海市政府和工部局，请求他们调查案件的真实事实。
(4) 请求法院调查此事，以使无辜者免受苦难。

香港中山华侨商业协会和北山同乡会对杨久道被卷入其无辜的罪行感到愤慨。昨日，这两个协会联合向上海广东同乡会发出电报，请求其促成杨久道获释，以保护他们的同胞。

May 11, 1936. Morning Translation.

"Le Jade"(理報) published the following editorial on May 9:-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE.

The truth of the events of the Nakayama murder case has at last begun to unfold itself before the public following the arrest of Yih Hai Sung(葉海生) alias Siao Kwangtung and Yang Vung Tao(楊文道).
However, now the case has assumed a new aspect through the unexpected retraction of his statement by Yih Hai Sung and the surrender of one Chang Tsun(張琛). According to the latter's statement, the whole affair is due to the connivance of Tseng Yuan(曾元), Zung Wei Ming (鍾偉明), Chang Zai Yuan(張才元) and others to accuse Yih Hai Sung, Yang Vung Tao and the Korean named "Jack", falsely, as the perpetrators of the crime, with the ultimate object of securing the reward. The statement made by Chang Tsun gives a vivid description of the plot and it seems to be a correct one, because if it were false, it could not have been fabricated to such a degree. However, what we cannot understand is that since the whole affair is the work of an organized plot on the part of Tseng Yuan et al, then why has Yih Hai Sung admitted during Court hearings and at the Police Station that he committed the crime?
At the last hearing of the case, Yih Hai Sung retracted his statement and whilst exonerating Yang Vung Tao of any connections with the case, he confessed to the crime to himself alone.
By virtue of its mysterious changes, this case is undoubtedly a very complicated one. Fortunately, the three judges handling the case are all noted for their ability and cleverness, and we are sure that the judgment to be rendered in the case will be fair.

"Holmes"(福尔摩斯) published the following comment on May 9:-

At the time when the developments of the Nakayama murder case were about to come to a head, suddenly a man named Chang Tsin surrendered himself to the Police stating that the informer Tseng Yuan had falsely accused Yang Vung Tao and Yih Hai Sung with the intent of securing the reward. However, Yih Hai Sung retracted his statement and stated that it was he who had murdered Nakayama. The case has thus become obscure and none of the statements of the persons concerned can be believed.
According to the statement made by Yih Hai Sung, he committed the murder, having been embittered by the January 28 Incident. This may be true. Since Yih was upset by the January 28 Incident, he should have given the pistol to the opposite side and asked that side to put an end to his grief. This is the proper attitude with which to treat a friendly nation.

1936年5月11日。晨间译件。

《理报》（Le Jade）于5月9日发表如下社论：

中山案。

随着叶海生（Yih Hai Sung，别名小广东）和杨文道（Yang Vung Tao）的被捕，中山谋杀案的真相终于开始在公众面前展现。
然而，由于叶海生意外翻供，以及一名叫张琛（Chang Tsun）的人自首，此案目前呈现出新的面貌。据后者陈述，整件事是由于曾元（Tseng Yuan）、钟伟明（Zung Wei Ming）、张才元（Chang Zai Yuan）等人串通一气，诬陷叶海生、杨文道和一名名叫“杰克”（Jack）的韩国人为凶手，其最终目的是获取赏金。张琛的供述对阴谋进行了生动的描述，且似乎属实，因为若是虚假，不可能编造得如此详尽。然而，令我们无法理解的是，既然整件事是曾元等人有组织的阴谋，那么叶海生为何在法庭审讯和警察局期间承认自己犯了罪？
在案件的最后一次聆讯中，叶海生翻供，在免除杨文道与案件的任何关联的同时，独自承认了罪行。
鉴于其神秘的变化，此案无疑非常复杂。幸运的是，审理此案的三位法官均以能干和聪慧著称，我们相信对此案作出的判决将是公正的。

《福尔摩斯》（Holmes）于5月9日发表如下评论：

正当中山谋杀案的发展即将达到高潮之际，突然有一名名叫张琛（Chang Tsin）的人向警方自首，称举报人曾元为了获取赏金而诬陷杨文道和叶海生。然而，叶海生翻供，并称是他杀害了中山。因此，案件变得扑朔迷离，相关人员的供词均不可信。
根据叶海生的供词，他因一·二八事变而心生怨恨，从而实施了谋杀。这可能是真的。既然叶海生因一·二八事变而感到不安，他本应将手枪交给对方，并请对方结束他的悲痛。这才是对待友好邦交的正确态度。

May 10, 1936.
Morning Translation.
（印：CRIME BRANCH）

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE : OVERSEER OF TA LOH DANCE HALL
ARRESTED

In connection with the Nakayama murder case,
the accused Yih Hai Sung (叶海生), on the afternoon of
May 8, stated to the Police that a Cantonese named Tseu
Shou Yong (周社荣) alias Yao Yong (姚勇) alias Ta Tseu
(大周) alias Ya Tseu (亚周), age 30, residing at No. 13
Ta Tuh Li (大德里), North Szechuen Road, was also present
when Yang Vung Tao (杨文道) and the others discussed
the plot at the Dong Nyi Association (东义协会) to kill
a Japanese, previous to the murder of Nakayama. Yih added
that Tseu was employed as an overseer in the Ta Loh Dance
Hall (大乐舞厅), No. 33 Ningpo Road. On the strength
of the statement, D.S.I. Crawford and D.S.I. Ross visited
the Ta Loh Dance Hall at 11 p.m. May 8 and arrested Tseu
Shou Yong.

At 11.05 a.m. yesterday, Tseu Shou Yong was
arraigned before Judge Feng Sz Tuh (冯司徒) of the First
Shanghai Special District Court, when Assistant Municipal
Advocate Y.D. Wong addressed the Court as follows :- "As
Yih Hai Sung, an accused in the Nakayama murder case, has
stated that Tseu Shou Yong was also present at the discussion
in the Dong Nyi Association, No. 71 Yung Chi Li (永吉里),
Range Road, in the plot to kill a Japanese, previous to the
murder of Nakayama, D.S.I. Crawford and D.S.I. Ross of the
Municipal Police on the evening of May 8 arrested Tseu in
the Ta Loh Dance Hall. Tseu was taken to the Police
Station and confronted with Yih Hai Sung before the two
foreign officers, Assistant Commissioner Uyehara and
D.I. Sih Tse Chien (薛志泉). The Police will conduct
a detailed investigation as to whether or not Tseu is really
connected with the murder, and request the Court's permission
to detain Tseu in accordance with Articles 76 and 101 of
the Code of Criminal Procedure. If Tseu is actually found
to have committed a crime, he will be charged on May 20
together with Yang Vung Tao and the other accused. Yih
Hai Sung is also in Court. With a view to preventing Yih
from retracting his statement, the Court is requested to
question him".

D.S.I. Crawford then gave particulars regarding
the arrest of Tseu Shou Yong and said, "Yih Hai Sung
previously stated that Tseu was present when discussion
took place in the plot to kill a Japanese. On May 8, Yih
repeated this statement, therefore, the Police visited the
Ta Loh Dance Hall and arrested Tseu".

The Judge then interrogated Tseu Shou Yong as
follows :-
Q:- Do you know Yang Vung Tao, Yih Hai Sung and Han Chi
Liang (韩奇良)?
A:- Yes.
Q:- Are you a member of the Dong Nyi Association?
A:- Yes.
Q:- Did you participate in the discussion of the murder of
the Japanese marine?
A:- I know nothing at all about it.

晨间译件。
