《大公报》及其他本地报纸：

中山谋杀案：大乐舞厅监工被捕

关于中山谋杀案，被告叶海生于5月8日下午向警方陈述，一名叫周社荣（Tseu Shou Yong，别名姚勇、大周、亚周）的广东人，现年30岁，住四川北路大德里13号，在中山被杀之前，杨文道等人在东义协会讨论杀害一名日本人的阴谋时，周也在场。叶海生补充说，周受雇于宁波路33号的大乐舞厅（Ta Loh Dance Hall）担任监工。基于该供词，副总督察克劳福德（Crawford）和副总督察罗斯（Ross）于5月8日晚11点前往大乐舞厅，逮捕了周社荣。

昨日上午11时05分，周社荣在上海第一特区地方法院冯司徒（Feng Sz Tuh）法官面前受审，此时副市检察官黄以德（Y.D. Wong）向法庭陈述如下：“鉴于中山谋杀案被告叶海生称，在中山被杀之前，周社荣也参与了在永吉里71号东义协会举行的杀害一名日本人的阴谋讨论，公共租界警务处的克劳福德副总督察和罗斯副总督察于5月8日晚在大乐舞厅逮捕了周。周被带到警察局，在外籍助理总监上原（Uyehara）和侦探长薛志泉（Sih Tse Chien）两位外籍警官面前与叶海生对质。警方将对周是否确实与谋杀案有关进行详细调查，并请求法庭依据《刑事诉讼法》第76条和第101条批准拘留周。如果确实发现周犯罪，他将于5月20日与杨文道及其他被告一起被起诉。叶海生也在庭上。为了防止叶海生翻供，请求法庭对其进行讯问”。

随后，克劳福德副总督察提供了关于逮捕周社荣的细节，并称：“叶海生此前称，在讨论杀害一名日本人的阴谋时，周在场。5月8日，叶海生重复了这一供词，因此，警方前往大乐舞厅逮捕了周”。

随后，法官对周社荣进行了如下讯问：
问：你认识杨文道、叶海生和韩奇良（Han Chi Liang）吗？
答：认识。
问：你是东义协会的会员吗？
答：是。
问：你参与了杀害日本海军陆战队士兵的讨论吗？
答：我对此一无所知。

Yih Hai Sung was then called into the witness
box made the following statement:-
"Tseu Shou Yong and I have long been known to
each other. Tseu was also present when the plot was
discussed at the Dong Nyi Association. Furthermore,
I was asked by Tseu to attend the discussions. The
first request was made by Tseu on or about October 3 (?)
when he came to the Moon Palace Dance Hall (月宮舞場) and
asked me to go to the Dong Nyi Association. I went
there and saw Yang Vung Tao and two Koreans. One of
the Koreans was 'Jack'. I felt very displeased because
I once had a fight with 'Jack'. As Yang knew of this,
he said, 'Now that you have been introduced by Tseu, you
should be on friendly terms with 'Jack'. Furthermore,
many Koreans will join the Association in future.'
At the end of October Tseu came to the Moon Palace and
again asked me to go to the Dong Nyi Association. I
went there and was told by Yang Vung Tao that preparations
were being made to kill a Japanese. Yang asked us
whether we agreed to his suggestion. We gave no answer
but Yang hinted that Tseu and I had agreed, whereupon
the two Koreans said that the pistol would be provided
by them. Subsequently, we went to Darroch Road in
order to make ourselves familiar with the locality. On
the 8th of November (?), Yang Vung Tao produced four
rolled-up papers, of which three were blank and the remaining
one bore the Chinese character 'Go'. Yang asked Tseu,
the two Koreans and myself to pick one. As I picked the
one which bore the character 'Go', I had to carry out
the murder. Yang was not required to draw lots as he
was the chairman of the Association. At 8 p.m.
November 9 we set out and fearing that too many of us
might spoil our mission, Yang Vung Tao told Tseu Shou
Yong not to come. When we reached the Japanese School,
Yang handed over a pistol to me. I then proceeded to
Darroch Road where I waited until I saw Yang Vung Tao
coming and walking behind a Japanese marine who was to
be killed. I then carefully followed the Japanese
marine and shot him dead in the vicinity of the Foong Loh
Li alleyway (丰樂里). After the shooting, I went
back to the Moon Palace Dance Hall where I met Tseu Shou
Yong. Tseu asked me about the matter and I told him
everything was alright. These are the full particulars
of the case."
Judge Feng then asked Tseu Shou Yong whether
the statement made by Yih Hai Sung was correct. Tseu
replied, "I know nothing at all about the matter nor did
I participate in any discussions of the plot, and as
regards the 'joint approval in the plot and the drawing
of the rolled-up papers' mentioned in Yih's statement,
I have not the slightest idea about them." The Court
then asked whether he had any enmity with Yih Yih Hai
Sung, Tseu Shou Yong replied in the negative.
Judge Feng then ordered that Tseu Shou Yong be
detained until the afternoon of May 20 when he would be
brought before the Court, and released if the Police
found that he was not connected with the case. The
accused Yih Hai Sung and Tseu Shou Yong were then taken
back to the Police Station under the escort of four
Japanese policemen, and Chinese and foreign detectives.

1936年5月10日。
2. 晨间译件。

随后，叶海生被传唤至证人席，作出如下陈述：
“我与周社荣相识已久。在东义协会讨论阴谋时，周也在场。此外，我是应周的邀请去参加讨论的。第一次邀请大约是在10月3日（?），当时他来到月宫舞场（Moon Palace Dance Hall），叫我去东义协会。我去了那里，见到了杨文道和两名韩国人。其中一名韩国人是‘杰克’。我感到非常不悦，因为我曾与‘杰克’打过架。由于杨知道此事，他说：‘既然你是由周介绍来的，你应该与‘杰克’和睦相处。此外，未来将有许多韩国人加入协会。’
10月底，周来到月宫舞场，再次叫我去东义协会。我去了那里，杨文道告诉我，正在准备杀害一名日本人。杨问我们是否同意他的建议。我们没有回答，但杨暗示周和我已经同意，于是两名韩国人说手枪将由他们提供。随后，我们去到达罗路（Darroch Road），以便熟悉当地环境。11月8日（?），杨文道拿出四卷纸，其中三卷是空白的，剩下的一卷写着汉字‘去’。杨让周、两名韩国人和我各抽一卷。因为我抽到了写有‘去’字的那一卷，所以我必须执行谋杀。杨不需要抽签，因为他是协会的会长。11月9日晚8点，我们出发，由于担心人多会坏事，杨文道告诉周社荣不要来。当我们到达日本学校时，杨递给我一把手枪。然后我前往达罗路，在那里等待，直到看见杨文道走来，走在那名将被杀害的日本海军陆战队士兵身后。随后我仔细跟踪那名日本海军陆战队士兵，并在丰乐里（Foong Loh Li）弄堂附近将其开枪打死。枪击发生后，我回到月宫舞场，在那里遇到了周社荣。周问我情况如何，我告诉他一切顺利。这就是案件的全部细节。”
随后，冯法官询问周社荣，叶海生的陈述是否正确。周回答说：“我对此事一无所知，也没有参与任何阴谋讨论，至于叶海生陈述中提到的‘共同批准阴谋和抽签’，我毫不知情。”法庭随后问他是否与叶海生有仇，周社荣予以否认。
冯法官随后命令拘留周社荣，直至5月20日下午将其带上法庭，如果警方发现他与案件无关，则予以释放。被告叶海生和周社荣随后在四名日本警察以及中外侦探的护送下被带回警察局。

THE CHINA PRESS, SUNDAY, MAY 10, 1936

More Revising
In Yih Story
Of Killing Seen

'Hsiao Kwangtung' Once
Again Changes Tale Of
Nakayama Murder

A further revision in the confession of Yih Hai-sen, perhaps better known as "Hsiao Kwangtung," and now being held in connection with the murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama, of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, on November 9 of last year, can be expected at the next hearing of the case as a result of a statement made by the man in the First Special District Court yesterday morning.

Yih was brought into court yesterday to appear as a witness against Chow Yao-yung, assistant manager of the Continental Ballroom, 33 Ningpo Road, who was arrested shortly before midnight Friday on charge of being implicated in the affair. The man was rushed to court about 11 a.m. and brought before Judge Feng Shih-teh on application for custody on a writ of detention. The application was granted and the man ordered held in custody until May 20 when the trial of Yih and Yang Wen-tao, another suspect, will be continued.

The statement made by Yih yesterday was brief but it seriously involved members of the Tung Yih Association, a Cantonese organization, which has figured prominently in the case since the first open hearings 10 days ago. Yih declared that Chow was the man whom Yang Wen-tao had sent to the Moon Palace Cabaret to summon him to the Association to discuss the murder plot.

Lots Declared Drawn

As a result of this statement, the case has become more involved than ever, for at the hearing on Wednesday, Yih confessed that he was the man who actually fired the shot and that he did so because he had wanted to kill a Japanese ever since the Sino-Japanese trouble in Shanghai in 1932.

It is understood that Yih has now prepared to make a statement that lots were drawn among the alleged members of the murder gang to see who would fire the fatal bullet.

Yih further implicated Yang in his statement to the court yesterday by branding him as the "master-mind" behind the shooting and declared that Chow was his assistant. He had been called to the club several times, he stated, and Chow was usually the messenger sent to summon him.

Asked what he had to say about Yih's statement, Chow declared that it was all false and that he had nothing to do with the crime. He maintained that he is an innocent man and has been falsely accused.

Motive Still Lacking

From the present outlook, it would appear that the police still lack a motive for the killing. Yih first confessed complicity and declared that Yang, said to be a respected employee of a local shipping firm, was the person who shot Nakayama on Darroch Road. In that confession, he declared he and "Jack," the Korean now in Japanese hands, had accompanied Yang to the scene of the crime.

At the last session of the trial Wednesday afternoon, Yih declared that it was he who fired the fatal plot hatched at the Tung Yih Association, which has its headquarters on Urga Road, of which Yang is president.

Summed up briefly, the case has become a matter of wondering just what Yih is going to say next.

《字林西报》，1936年5月10日，星期日

叶海生杀人供词
再次出现修改

“小广东”再次改变
关于中山谋杀案的说法

预计在下一次案件聆讯中，叶海生（Yih Hai-sen，或许更为人知的是“小广东”，目前因去年11月9日谋杀日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄而被羁押）的供词将出现进一步修改，这是基于该男子昨天上午在第一特区地方法院所作陈述的结果。

叶海生昨天被带上法庭，作为指控周耀荣（Chow Yao-yung，宁波路33号大陆舞厅副经理）的证人出庭，周于周五午夜前不久因涉嫌卷入此案而被捕。该男子于上午11点左右被紧急送往法庭，并在申请拘留令拘押方面前冯司徒（Feng Shih-teh）法官。申请获准，该男子被命令拘留至5月20日，届时将继续审理叶海生和另一名嫌疑人杨文道（Yang Wen-tao）的案件。

叶海生昨天的陈述简短，但严重牵涉到广东组织东义协会的成员，该组织自10天前首次公开聆讯以来一直在案件中占据突出地位。叶海生宣称，周是杨文道派往月宫歌舞厅召他去协会讨论谋杀阴谋的人。

宣称进行了抽签

由于这一陈述，案件变得比以往更加复杂，因为在周三的聆讯中，叶海生承认他是实际开枪的人，他这样做是因为自从1932年上海发生中日冲突以来，他一直想杀死一名日本人。

据悉，叶海生现在准备作出陈述，称所谓的谋杀团伙成员之间进行了抽签，以决定由谁发射致命子弹。

叶海生在昨天向法庭的陈述中进一步牵连杨文道，称其为枪击背后的“主谋”，并宣称周是他的助手。他说，他曾被多次叫到俱乐部，而周通常是奉命召他的信使。

当被问及他对叶海生的陈述有何说法时，周宣称这一切都是假的，他与犯罪无关。他坚持认为自己是无辜的，是被诬陷的。

动机仍然缺失

从目前的情况来看，警方似乎仍然缺乏杀人动机。叶海生最初承认共谋，并宣称杨（据称是当地一家航运公司的受人尊敬的雇员）是在达罗路枪击中山的人。在那份供词中，他宣称他和“杰克”（这名韩国人目前在日本人手中）陪同杨前往犯罪现场。

在周三下午的最后一次庭审中，叶海生宣称是他发射了致命子弹，并 stated that the reason he did so was because of a personal desire to kill a Japanese, and added that nobody else had anything to do with it. （原文此处英文混杂，意为：并称他这样做的原因是出于个人想要杀死一名日本人的愿望，并补充说没有其他人参与其中。）

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SUNDAY, MAY 10, 1936

FOURTH SUSPECT IN
NAKAYAMA CASE
Chow Seu-yoong Arrested in
Continental Cabaret
IMPLICATED BY "LITTLE
CANTONESE"

A fourth man suspected of being concerned in the murder of N. Nakayama, Japanese warrant officer, on Darroch Road, on November 9 last year, was brought before the First Special District Court yesterday and a writ of detention was issued against him by Judge Feng on police application, pending his trial with those already in custody on the afternoon of May 20.

The man is Chow Seu-yoong, alias Tseu Yao-yung. He was arrested shortly before midnight on Friday in the "Continental" Dancing Hall, 33 Ningpo Road, he having been implicated in the crime by Yih Haisen, alias "Little Cantonese", who was arrested about two weeks ago, together with two other Cantonese, Yang Ven-tao and Zung Yung-sen, by detectives headed by Det.-Sub-Inspr. Crowther. Zung was later released as there was insufficient evidence against him, but both Yih and Yang were charged with murder.

When Chow appeared before the court, Yih appeared as a witness and told the Judge that, on November 9 last year, he, Chow, Yang and two Koreans held a meeting in a room of the Moon Palace Hotel, North Szechuen Road, to discuss the proposed murder of a Japanese, but, at Yang's suggestion, only three of them went to commit the crime, Chow being left in the hotel.

Yih continued that, when they were near the Japanese school in North Szechuen Road, Yang gave him a pistol and told him to go to Darroch Road. Soon after, a Japanese marine appeared not far from the Foong Loh Lee Alleyway and he fired a shot at the marine after Yang had pointed out to him that this was the man they wanted to kill, Yih said.

Mr. Y. D. Wong, Assistant Municipal Advocate, prosecuting, stated that, prior to the murder of Darroch Road, Chow also attended a meeting in the Cantonese society known as Dong Nyi Yat Hui, Range Road, to discuss the murder of a Japanese, according to a statement made at the police station by the "Little Cantonese".

Like Yang Ven-tao, Chow denied knowing anything about the shooting of Nakayama and said he was absolutely innocent.
pages.zh:
14J12
《字林西报》，1936年5月10日，星期日

中山案中第四名嫌疑人
周修荣（Chow Seu-yoong）在大陆舞厅被捕
受“小广东”牵连

去年11月9日，日本军曹N. Nakayama（中山）在达罗克路（Darroch Road）遇害。昨日，一名涉嫌与此案有关的第四名男子被提审至第一特区法院。应警方申请，冯法官对其签发拘留令，待其于5月20日下午与已在押人员一同受审。

该男子名为周修荣（Chow Seu-yoong），别名周耀荣（Tseu Yao-yung）。他于周五午夜前不久在宁波路33号的“大陆”（Continental）舞厅被捕。约两周前，由副巡官克劳瑟（Crowther）率领的侦探逮捕了义海森（Yih Haisen，别名“小广东”）以及另外两名广东人杨文道（Yang Ven-tao）和钟荣森（Zung Yung-sen），义海森供出周修荣涉案。钟荣森后因证据不足获释，但义海森和杨文道均被控谋杀罪。

周修荣出庭时，义海森作为证人出庭，并向法官陈述：去年11月9日，他、周修荣、杨文道及两名朝鲜人在北四川路月宫饭店（Moon Palace Hotel）的一个房间内举行会议，商讨谋杀一名日本人的计划；但根据杨文道的建议，仅其中三人前去实施犯罪，周修荣则留在饭店内。

义海森继续称，当他们接近北四川路的日本学校时，杨文道递给他一把手枪，并让他前往达罗克路。不久后，一名日本海军陆战队员出现在丰乐里（Foong Loh Lee Alleyway）附近，杨文道向他指出此人即为欲杀之目标，随后他向该海军陆战队员开了一枪。

助理市检察官黄以德（Y. D. Wong）先生在起诉时指出，据“小广东”在警局的供述，在达罗克路谋杀案发生之前，周修荣还参加了位于兰路（Range Road）的广东社团“东义会”（Dong Nyi Yat Hui）的一次会议，商讨谋杀一名日本人的事宜。

与杨文道一样，周修荣否认知晓任何关于枪击中山的情况，并称自己完全无辜。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, MAY 10, 1936

“Ever Righteous” Society
Planned Nakayama Crime

Shao Kwangtung Changes Story For Third Time,
Now Names Co-Defendant As Master Mind;
Group Drew Papers To Determine Killer

Changing his “confession” for the third time, Shao Kwangtung, in the First Special District Court yesterday morning, made a detailed explanation of the plot which resulted in the fatal shooting of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama near the Japanese barracks in Darroch Road, on November 9. Exonerating a co-defendant, Yang Wen-tao, in the last hearing, Shao Kwangtung yesterday named Yang as the master mind of the “Ever Righteous” Society.

This society, witness said, was headed by Yang and included four other members who met on November 8 to discuss the murder of some Japanese. Yang did not participate in the drawing himself, but prepared four scraps of paper on one of which was written the word “go,” designating the killer. The papers were then rolled into balls and each of the other four men were instructed to draw. Shao Kwangtung said he drew the fateful paper.

Story Of Shooting

About 8 p.m. on November 9 witness, Yang and two Korean members of the gang started out. When they reached the Japanese School, Yang passed him a pistol and he went to Darroch Road. Soon he saw Yang following a Japanese sailor and, at a signal given by Yang, he walked behind him into Feng Lo alley and shot him from behind. Then witness went to the Moon Palace Cabaret, where he met the fifth member of the gang Chou Tso-yung. Chou asked him if he had carried out his duty, and witness replied that he had.

Fourth Suspect Taken

This fifth alleged member of the gang was arrested on Friday night by Central Police at the Continental Ballroom, Ningpo Road, where he has been employed as an inspector. In court yesterday he violently denied any knowledge of the crime. Asked by Judge Feng if he had ever angered Shao Kwangtung, he shook his head in negation.

Judge Feng ordered Chou to be kept in custody until the trial of Yang and Shao Kwangtung before a full court on May 20. A fourth suspect, a Korean named Jack, is being held by the Japanese authorities and only one more Korean member of the alleged group is now at liberty.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年5月10日

“正义社”策划中山案

邵广东第三次改变供词，现指认同案被告为主谋；团伙抽签决定杀手

邵广东（Shao Kwangtung）昨日早晨在第一特区法院第三次改变其“供词”，详细解释了导致11月9日海军军曹中山英夫（Hideo Nakayama）在达罗克路日本兵营附近被枪杀的阴谋。在上次听证会上，邵广东曾为同案被告杨文道开脱，但昨日他指认杨文道为“正义社”（Ever Righteous Society）的主谋。

证人称，该社团由杨文道领导，另有四名成员，他们于11月8日集会讨论谋杀某些日本人的事宜。杨文道本人未参与抽签，但他准备了四张纸条，其中一张写有“去”字，指定持此条者为杀手。随后将纸条揉成团，指示其余四人各抽一张。邵广东称他抽到了那张决定命运的纸条。

枪击经过

11月9日晚8时许，证人、杨文道及该团伙的两名朝鲜成员出发。当他们到达日本学校时，杨文道递给他一把手枪，他便前往达罗克路。不久，他看见杨文道跟踪一名日本水手，并在杨文道发出信号后，他尾随该水手进入丰乐里（Feng Lo alley），从背后向其开枪。随后证人前往月宫舞厅（Moon Palace Cabaret），在那里遇到了该团伙的第五名成员周佐荣（Chou Tso-yung）。周问他是否完成了任务，证人回答已完成。

第四名嫌疑人被捕

这名所谓的团伙第五名成员于周五晚被中央捕房在宁波路大陆舞厅（Continental Ballroom）逮捕，他受雇于该处担任稽查员。昨日在法庭上，他激烈否认对罪行有任何知情。当冯法官问他是否曾惹怒邵广东时，他摇头否认。

冯法官命令将周佐荣收押，直至5月20日杨文道和邵广东在全体法庭面前接受续审。第四名嫌疑人是一名名叫杰克（Jack）的朝鲜人，正由日本当局羁押，目前该所谓团伙中仅剩一名朝鲜成员在逃。

14J'2
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, May 9, 1936

'Big Chow'
Arrested In
Sailor Case

Third Suspect Appears
As Nakayama Death
Accomplice

POLICE SEIZE MAN
IN CABARET RAID

'Little Kwangtung' Says
Chow With Others
Involved

Implicated by Yih Hai-sen, alias
"Shao Kwangtung," whose confession as being the man who shot
and killed Warrant Officer Hideo
Nakayama of the Japanese Naval
Landing Party on Darroch Road on
November 9 caused a sensation this
week, Chow Cha-yung, alias Chow
Yao-yung, alias "Ta (Big) Chow"
alias "Ya (Second) Chow," was
arrested by Central Station police
last night and brought before the
First District Court this morning
as another suspect in the murder
case which last year threatened a
serious Sino-Japanese crisis in
Shanghai.

Chow was arrested at 11.30 last
night at the Continental Ballroom,
53 Ningpo Road, where he is employed as an inspector. On the
basis of the statement given in
court by "Shao Kwangtung," a
squad of officers headed by Detective Sub-Inspector Ross visited
the cabaret and placed him under
arrest.

Denies Complicity

Taken before Judge Feng Shih-teh in the First Special District
Court this morning, Chow denied
any connection with the Nakayama
murder. An application was made
by Assistant Municipal Advocate
Y. D. Wong for a writ of detention.
Judge Feng, who is one of the three
judges of the full court entrusted
with the trial of the important
case, granted the application and
ordered the suspect remanded until
May 20 when "Shao Kwangtung"
and Yang Wen-tao, alleged instigator of the crime, are to be
brought before the court for a
resumed hearing.

Taking the witness box this
morning, "Shao Kwangtung" insisted that Chow was the man
whom Yang sent to the Moon
Palace Cabaret to summon him
(Yih) to the offices of the Tung
Yih Hwei, a club of which Yang
is the chairman and which is
situated on Urga Road. Twice
Yang sent Chow for "Shao Kwangtung" for conferences to discuss the
murder plot, the confessed
murderer declared in court today.

Confession Modified

In his testimony before the court
this morning, Yih modified his confession made last Wednesday when
he said that he had shot and killed
Nakayama to satisfy a long cherished desire to kill a Japanese. This
morning, however, Yih again implicated Yang as the "mastermind" of the gang and accused
Chow of being Yang's assistant.

Following the brief court session,
during which Chow repeatedly and
emphatically denied any connection
with the murder, the third suspect
now held by police was taken to
S.M.P. headquarters to face further
questioning by the Political Branch
officers. He was to be put later into
the detention cell inside the police
compound on Foochow Road.

Meanwhile, Yang's defense counsel, Attorney G. R. Grove, is proceeding with his efforts to substantiate his contention that his
client is the victim of a frame-up.
He is understood to have deposited with the court a paper which
is said to be a written document
signed by the informants and witnesses for prosecution on percentages for the distribution of the
reward money.
pages.zh:
14J'2
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年5月9日，星期六

“大周”
在水手案中
被捕

第三名嫌疑人现身
成为中山死亡案
从犯

警方突袭舞厅
抓获一人

“小广东”称
周氏与其他人
涉案

义海森（Yih Hai-sen，别名“邵广东”）供认自己是11月9日在达罗克路枪杀日本海军陆战队军曹中山英夫（Hideo Nakayama）的凶手，其供词本周引起轰动。受其牵连，周查荣（Chow Cha-yung，别名周耀荣 Chow Yao-yung，别名“大周” Ta (Big) Chow，别名“二周” Ya (Second) Chow）于昨晚被中央捕房警察逮捕，并于今晨被提审至第一特区法院，作为另一起谋杀案的嫌疑人。该谋杀案去年曾在上海引发严重的中日危机。

周查荣于昨晚11时30分在宁波路53号的大陆舞厅（Continental Ballroom）被捕，他受雇于该处担任稽查员。基于“邵广东”在法庭上的供述，由副巡官罗斯（Ross）率领的一队警官前往该舞厅并将其逮捕。

否认共谋

今晨，周查荣在第一特区法院被提审至冯师德（Feng Shih-teh）法官面前，他否认与中山谋杀案有任何关联。助理市检察官黄以德（Y. D. Wong）申请签发拘留令。冯法官是负责审理此重要案件的全体法庭三名法官之一，他批准了该申请，并命令将该嫌疑人还押，直至5月20日“邵广东”和被指控为犯罪煽动者的杨文道被带上法庭进行续审。

“邵广东”今晨出庭作证时坚持称，周查荣是杨文道派往月宫舞厅传唤他（义海森）去同义会（Tung Yih Hwei）办事处的人。该俱乐部由杨文道担任主席，位于乌拉路（Urga Road）。这名已认罪的凶手今日在法庭上宣称，杨文道曾两次派遣周查荣去找“邵广东”开会，商讨谋杀阴谋。

修改供词

义海森在今晨的法庭证词中，修改了他上周三所作的供词。当时他说，为了满足长期以来杀害一名日本人的愿望，他开枪打死了中山。然而，今晨义海森再次指认杨文道为该团伙的“主谋”，并指控周查荣是杨文道的助手。

在简短的庭审结束后，周查荣反复且坚决地否认与谋杀案有任何关联。目前被警方羁押的这第三名嫌疑人随后被带往工部局警务处总部，面对政治部的进一步讯问。他随后将被关入福州路警局大院内的拘留所。

与此同时，杨文道的辩护律师G. R. Grove先生正致力于证实他的主张，即他的当事人是栽赃陷害的受害者。据悉，他已向法庭提交了一份文件，据称这是一份由线人和控方证人签署的书面文件，内容涉及分配赏金的分成比例。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, May 7, 1936
Nakayama Case
Puzzling Court
Confessions, Charges
Confusing; Alleged
Contract Filed

Who killed Nakayama?
And like the Sparrow, Yih Hai-sen alias "Little Kwangtung", Cantonese dancing-man and cabaret habitue, now declares that he did, with his own little pistol, he killed Nakayama. He made this astonishing confession in the First District Court yesterday afternoon at the continuation of his trial on the charge of murdering Warrant Officer Nakayama on Darroch Road last November 9.
But a week ago "Little Kwangtung" made his first confession, in which he asserted that the murder was committed by his fellow prisoner, Yang Wen-tao, chief of the Dong Nyi Yah Hui, Cantonese society in Hongkew. Yang vehemently denied the accusation.
Frame-Up Alleged
Then came forward yesterday one Chang Sen, an ex-jockey, who blandly announced that Tseng Yuan, star prosecution witness, and Tseng Ping-san, China-born Japanese, had approached him after the murder asking him to act as witness falsely implicating the accused —Yih, Yang and the Korean now held by Japanese Consular Police—in order to collect the cash reward of $12,000 offered by police for arrest of the killer. In short, he alleged a "frame up," and involved one Dr. Cheng Wei-ming in the plot.
All these developments had the court and spectators and police so confused yesterday that the judge granted the prosecution a remand of two weeks for investigation of the new complications.
Contract Filed
Last night, however, Mr. G. R. Grove, attorney for Yang, filed a document with the court which he wishes to be used as evidence at the next hearing. This document, if bona fide, promises to produce some fireworks, as it is allegedly a contract signed by Chang Sen, Tseng Yuan and Dr. Cheng wherein they settled the problem of how they would split the $12,000 reward after they had "framed" Yang and Yih. This document would thus corroborate Chang Sen's evidence yesterday.
"Little Kwangtung" had always wanted to kill him a Japanese, he told the court yesterday in explanation of his motive. He had wanted to draw Nipponese blood ever since the Shanghai War, and brooded on it. He wanted to get a high Japanese officer. The urge being with him on the night of November 9, he said, he suddenly got his gun and went out alone from the Moon Palace Cabaret, and on Darroch Road started looking for such a victim. No officer of any consequence came along, but Warrant Officer Nakayama did, so Yih shot the man in the head, threw his gun away and ran.
"Lied To Court"
"I did it all myself," he said. "Yang had nothing to do with it and I lied when I told the court at the last hearing that he was the man who fired the shot."
What the mysterious Korean known as "Jack" has to say about these conflicting revelations remains unknown, as he has not yet appeared in open court and is closely guarded by Japanese police. His real name is Han Jur-ling.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年5月7日，星期四

中山案
令法庭困惑
供词与指控
令人混淆； alleged 合同已提交

谁杀了中山？

就像麻雀一样，义海森（Yih Hai-sen，别名“小广东”），一名广东籍舞男和舞厅常客，现在宣称是他干的，他用他那把小手枪杀死了中山。昨日下午，在就去年11月9日在达罗克路谋杀中山军曹一案进行的续审中，他在第一特区法院作出了这一惊人的供认。

但在一周前，“小广东”作了第一次供认，声称谋杀是由他的同囚犯、虹口广东社团“东义会”（Dong Nyi Yah Hui）首领杨文道实施的。杨文道强烈否认了这一指控。

指控栽赃

随后，一名前骑师张森（Chang Sen）于昨日出面，平淡地宣布，在谋杀案发生后，主要控方证人曾元（Tseng Yuan）和日籍华人曾平三（Tseng Ping-san）曾接触他，要求他作伪证诬陷被告——义海森、杨文道以及目前被日本领事警察羁押的朝鲜人——以便获取警方为逮捕凶手提供的12,000美元现金悬赏。简而言之，他指控存在“栽赃”行为，并将程伟明博士（Dr. Cheng Wei-ming）卷入该阴谋。

所有这些进展使得昨日的法庭、观众和警方都感到十分困惑，法官因此批准控方延期两周，以调查这些新的复杂情况。

提交合同

然而，昨晚，杨文道的律师G. R. Grove先生向法庭提交了一份文件，他希望该文件能在下次听证会上作为证据使用。如果属实，这份文件预计会引起轩然大波，因为据称这是一份由张森、曾元和程博士签署的合同，其中规定了他们在“栽赃”杨文道和义海森后如何瓜分12,000美元赏金的问题。这份文件 thus 将佐证张森昨日的证词。

“小广东”昨日在法庭上解释其动机时称，他一直想杀死一名日本人。自上海战争以来，他就一直渴望沾染日本人的鲜血，并对此耿耿于怀。他想杀掉一名日本高级军官。他说，11月9日晚，这种冲动驱使着他，他突然拿起枪，独自离开月宫舞厅，在达罗克路开始寻找这样的受害者。虽然没有遇到什么重要军官，但遇到了中山军曹，于是义海森朝该男子头部开枪，扔掉手枪后逃跑。

“对法庭撒谎”

“这一切都是我自己做的，”他说。“杨文道与此无关，我在上次听证会上告诉法庭是他开的枪，那是我在撒谎。”

这位被称为“杰克”（Jack）的神秘朝鲜人对这些相互矛盾的披露有何说法，目前尚不得而知，因为他尚未在公开法庭露面，且受到日本警察的严密看守。他的真名是韩朱林（Han Jur-ling，音译）。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, MAY 7, 1936
“I Killed Nakayama”,
“Hsiao Kwangtung” Says
In Changing Confession
Cabaret Owner Now Denies Yang Wen-tao Had
Anything To Do With Murder Of Japanese
On Darroch Road, Says He Shot Marine In
Grip Of Old Urge To Kill A Nipponese

“I did it all myself. Yang had nothing to do with it
and I lied when I told the court at the last hearing that
he was the man who fired the shot.”

This was the sensational statement made by Yih Hai-
sen, known as “Hsiao Kwangtung.” Before presiding
Judge Chien Hung-nieh and a full tribunal at the First
Special District Court yesterday when he was further
questioned concerning the murder of Warrant Officer
Hideo Nakayama, Japanese, on Darroch Road, November
9, 1935.

At the first hearing of the case
in open court last Friday, Yih, who
is a Tsingtao cabaret owner, and a
former Shanghai cabaret employee,
confessed to complicity in the crime
but stated that his co-accused,
Yang Wen-tao, formerly employed
by a local shipping company, and
head of the Tong Yih Association,
was the man who actually fired the
shot that killed Nakayama.

Questioned as to why he had
changed his confession, Yih de-
clared that at first, he thought to
save himself by implicating Yang.

“I also wanted to escape police
punishment,” he said, “so last Fri-
day I thought that by becoming a
witness for the police, I might get
only a 10 or 15 year prison sen-
tence. If I served the full term, I
could still come out and only be 40
or 45 years old. That way, I
could start life again.

“I Killed Nakayama”

“I have since thought the matter
over and have now decided to tell
the truth. I killed Nakayama. No-
body helped me.”

Judge Chien wanted to know what
motive he had for killing Naka-
yama, and then Yih provided an-
other sensation. He stated that he
killed Nakayama because he was
the only Japanese naval man in
sight when he went to Darroch
Road on the night of November 9.

Yih declared that he had had a
burning desire to kill a Japanese
ever since the Sino-Japanese
trouble in Shanghai in 1932. Every
now and then, he continued, this
desire got possession of his better
judgment and he would sit down
and plan how to kill a Japanese in
uniform.

Continuing his strange story, he
declared that on the night of
November 9, this urge to kill grip-
ped him again and this time he
made up his mind to go out and
kill a high Japanese naval official.

Taking his pistol with him, he
said, he walked from the Moon
Palace Cabaret to Darroch Road
and looked up and down the street
for a “high official.” He saw no
such person, he continued, but he
did see a Japanese sailor. The urge
to kill a Japanese was so strong in
him, the man declared, that he
simply went ahead and committed
the crime.

Ran Away, Dropped Gun

After he had fired the shot, he
declared, he ran away and drop-
ped the gun several hundred feet
from the body. Questioned about
the spot in which the death wea-
pon had been kept, Yih declared
that the weapon was his. He cut it
out to fit the shape of the gun.
Asked how it happened to be found
in Yang’s home on Tongshan Road,
Yih declared that after the killing,
he took it to the Tong Yih Associa-
tion and there presented it to
Yang.

At the beginning of the proceed-
ings yesterday, it was brought out
by Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant
Municipal Advocate, who together
with Municipal Advocate Robert T.
Bryan, Jr., is prosecuting the case,
that Yih had changed his confes-
sion in a statement given to the
police. He gave an outline of the
confession and subsequently stated
that Yih had been acquainted with
Yang long before the killing of
Nakayama. In fact, it was point-
ed, out the pair had met two or
three years ago at the Yang Woo
Association, another Cantonese or-
ganisation, of which Mr. Yang was
then the president.

It was further brought out by the
prosecution that Yang, Yih and
“Jack,” the Korean, and a fourth
party named Chow had gone to the
Tong Yih Association on several
occasions. This statement, Yang
denied when questioned by Judge
Chien. He flatly stated that no
Korean was a member of the asso-
ciation.

Yih Ah-dao, a servant employed
by the club, was called as a witness
and told the court that he knew
Yang. He declared that Yang was
president and came every day while
Yih came once or twice monthly.
Asked if Yang was at the associa-
tion on November 9, the witness
stated that he thought he was;
that Yang came to the association
in the daytime and never went
away until late.

Defense Witness Called

The next big sensation of the
proceedings came when the de-
fense produced a witness in an
effort to allege a “frame-up”
against Yih and the Korean, whose
name, it was brought out, is Ran
Jur-ling, but better known as
“Jack.”

The witness was a mild-manner-
ed, well-dressed man wearing for-
eign clothes and a pair of spec-
tacles and named Chang Seng. He
stated that he was a native of
Kwangtung and was 38 years old.
He declared that he had been a
friend of Tseng Yuen, a witness at
the Friday hearing. On the latter
occasion, Tseng testified that Yih
had come to him to obtain a loan
on a pistol and that he had refus-
ed the loan. Mrs. Tseng Yuen con-
firmed her husband’s statement.

The witness Chang Seng declar-
ed that after the Nakayama kill-
ed he called at the home of the
Tseng Yuen’s and while there saw
a man named Dr. Cheng Wei-
ming. He said that the doctor and
Tseng were talking over some busi-
ness. He also saw, the witness
continued, a diagram of a gun on a
piece of paper lying on the table.
The drawing had the initials
“P.B.” on the butt, he said. The
death weapon also had the same
initials on the butt, it had pre-
viously been pointed out by the
prosecution.

Bribe Said Offered

Chang Seng continued that later
on, Dr. Cheng came to him and
offered him $4,000 to go to the
Japanese Consular Police and
make the statement that he had
the inside on the shooting of
Nakayama. He was to say, the
man continued, that Yih fired the
shot but that he was given the gun
by “Jack” the Korean. He added
that he refused to make such a
statement and that the doctor told
him he would find somebody else
who would do it.

In making this statement, the
man involved the doctor and Tseng
Yuen in a plot to collect the $12,000
reward which is being offered by
the Shanghai Municipal Police, the
Japanese Consulate-General and
the City Government of Greater
Shanghai for the arrest of the
slayer.

Tseng Yuen, who was in the court-
room, was called to the witness box.
Glaring at Chang Sheng, he flatly
denied any such plot to collect the
reward and in loud tones, declared
that the witness was a prevaricator.

He admitted that he, Chang, had once
been his friend but that their friend-
ship had come to an end sometime
ago. Tseng declared that the reason
for the breach was a plain and
simple matter of attempted wife-
stealing.

Tseng continued that while he
was in Tsingtao some months ago,
Chang Seng had called at his home
and had attempted to steal his wife
away from him. He discovered this
when he returned to the city, he
said, and something of an argu-
ment ensued. He declared that
Chang Seng had charged him with
being involved in a “frame-up” be-
cause he was no longer friendly with
the Tseng Yuen family.

Went To Police

Aside from Yih’s change in con-
fession and Chang Sheng’s state-
ment alleging a frame-up, nothing
of a very startling nature occurred
at yesterday’s proceedings. Chang
Sheng stated that an attorney
had made a draft of his allegation
of frame-up and that he had gone
to the police with it. He added that
the reason he had made the state-
ment is because he was troubled
over having the matter on his con-
science.

Two Chinese police constables
testified to finding the body of
Nakayama on the night of Novem-
ber 9, while a Chinese shoe-maker
named Hu Siang-wu, residing in the
Darroch Road district, gave evi-
dence to the effect that he had heard
the shooting and had seen the dead
Japanese.

Hu declared that at the time, he
was on his way to the shop of a
Japanese shoemaker on Darroch
Road. The first thing that he did
was to rush into the Japanese shop

（印：MUNICIPAL REC. D. 76）

《字林西报》，1936年5月7日，星期四
“我杀了中山”，
“小广东”在改变供词时称
舞厅老板现否认杨文涛与达罗克路日本人被杀案有任何牵连，称其枪击海军陆战队员是出于杀害日本人的旧有冲动

“全是我一个人干的。杨与此事无关，我在上次庭审告诉法庭是他开的枪，那是撒谎。”

这是被称为“小广东”的易海森（Yih Hai-sen）所作的惊人陈述。昨日，在第一特区法院，主审法官钱洪业（Chien Hung-nieh，音译）及全体推事就1935年11月9日发生在达罗克路（Darroch Road）的日本军曹中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）被杀案对他进行进一步讯问时，他作出了上述陈述。

在上周五该案的初次公开庭审中，身为青岛舞厅老板、前上海舞厅雇员的易某承认参与犯罪，但声称其同案被告、前受雇于本地轮船公司且为通义会头目的杨文涛，才是实际开枪杀死中山的人。

当被问及为何改变供词时，易某宣称，起初他想通过诬陷杨某来保全自己。

“我也想逃避警方的惩罚，”他说，“所以上周五我想，如果成为警方的证人，我可能只会被判处10或15年监禁。如果服满刑期，我出来时也才40或45岁。那样我就可以重新开始生活。

“我杀了中山”

“此后我反复思考此事，现在决定说出真相。是我杀了中山。没有人帮我。”

钱法官想知道他杀害中山的动机，随后易某又提供了一则轰动性消息。他声称，他之所以杀害中山，是因为11月9日晚他去达罗克路时，眼前只有这一名日本海军人员。

易某宣称，自1932年上海中日冲突以来，他就一直有着杀害日本人的强烈欲望。他继续说，这种欲望时不时会压倒他的理智，他会坐下来策划如何杀害一名身穿制服的日本人。

他继续讲述这段离奇的经历，宣称11月9日晚，这种杀人冲动再次控制了他，这次他下定决心出去杀害一名日本海军高级官员。

他说，他带上手枪，从月宫舞厅（Moon Palace Cabaret）走到达罗克路，在街上上下寻找“高官”。他继续说，他没看到这样的人，但他确实看到了一名日本水兵。此人宣称，他内心杀害日本人的冲动如此强烈，以至于他径直实施了犯罪。

逃跑并丢弃枪支

他宣称，开枪后他逃跑了，并在距离尸体几百英尺的地方丢掉了枪。当被问及凶器存放地点时，易某宣称该武器是他的。他切割了枪套以适配枪支形状。当被问及枪支为何会在同山路杨某家中被发现时，易某宣称，杀人后他将枪带到通义会，并在那里将其交给了杨某。

在昨日的诉讼程序开始时，助理市检察官鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru，音译）指出，易某在向警方的一份陈述中改变了供词。鲁先生与市检察官罗伯特·T·布莱恩二世（Robert T. Bryan, Jr.）共同负责起诉此案。他概述了供词内容，随后指出，易某在中山被杀很久之前就认识杨某。事实上，有人指出，两人两三年前在杨武协会（Yang Woo Association，音译）相遇，那是一个广东人组织，当时杨某担任会长。

控方进一步指出，杨某、易某、朝鲜人“杰克”以及另一名姓周的当事人曾多次前往通义会。钱法官讯问时，杨某否认了这一说法。他断然声明，该协会中没有朝鲜人成员。

俱乐部雇佣的仆人易阿道（Yih Ah-dao，音译）作为证人出庭，告诉法庭他认识杨某。他宣称，杨某是会长，每天都来，而易某每月来一两次。当被问及11月9日杨某是否在协会时，证人表示他认为他在；杨某白天来到协会，直到很晚才离开。

传唤辩方证人

诉讼程序的下一个重大轰动时刻出现在辩方提出一名证人，试图指控对易某和朝鲜人进行“栽赃陷害”。据披露，该朝鲜人名叫兰朱林（Ran Jur-ling，音译），但更广为人知的名字是“杰克”。

证人名叫张生（Chang Seng，音译），是一位举止温和、衣着考究、身穿西式服装并戴着眼镜的男子。他声称自己是广东人，今年38岁。他宣称自己曾是周五庭审证人曾元（Tseng Yuen，音译）的朋友。在那次庭审中，曾元作证说易某曾向他借钱买手枪，但他拒绝了贷款。曾元的妻子证实了她丈夫的陈述。

证人张生宣称，中山被杀后，他曾拜访曾元家，在那里见到了一位名叫郑伟明（Cheng Wei-ming，音译）的医生。他说医生和曾某正在谈论一些业务。证人继续说，他还看到桌上放着一张纸，上面画着手枪的示意图。他说，图纸上枪柄处标有“P.B.”字样。控方此前曾指出，凶器枪柄上也有同样的缩写。

称有人行贿

张生继续说，后来郑医生找到他，出价4000美元，让他去日本领事馆警察那里作伪证，声称他掌握中山枪击案的内幕。此人继续说，他要声称是易某开的枪，但枪是朝鲜人“杰克”给他的。他补充说，他拒绝作此类陈述，而医生告诉他，他会找其他人来做这件事。

通过这一陈述，此人将郑医生和曾元卷入了一场阴谋，旨在获取由上海公共租界工部局警务处、日本总领事馆和大上海市政府为逮捕凶手而提供的12000美元赏金。

当时在法庭内的曾元被传至证人席。他怒视张生，断然否认任何此类骗取赏金的阴谋，并大声宣称该证人是说谎者。

他承认张曾一度是他的朋友，但他们的友谊不久前已终结。曾某宣称，关系破裂的原因是一件简单明了的企图诱拐其妻子的事件。

曾某继续说，几个月前他在青岛时，张生曾到他家，企图诱拐他的妻子。他说，当他回到城里时发现了这一点，随后发生了一些争执。他宣称，张生指控他参与“栽赃陷害”，是因为他不再与曾元一家友好。

前往警局

除了易某改变供词和张生指控存在栽赃陷害外，昨日的庭审没有发生其他特别令人震惊的事情。张生表示，一名律师起草了他关于栽赃陷害的指控材料，他已带着材料去了警局。他补充说，他作出这一陈述的原因是因为良心不安。

两名中国巡捕作证说，他们在11月9日晚发现了中山的尸体，而居住在达罗克路地区的一名名叫胡祥武（Hu Siang-wu，音译）的中国鞋匠提供的证据表明，他听到了枪声并看到了死去的日本人。

胡某宣称，当时他正前往达罗克路上一名日本鞋匠的店铺。他做的第一件事就是冲进那家日本店铺

（印：MUNICIPAL REC. D. 76）

The Japanese shoemaker, who
answered to the name of Takahashi,
declared that he also heard the shot.
Asked how much time elapsed be-
tween the moment he heard the
shot before Hu rushed into his place,
the witness said he wasn't exactly
sure. He was playing a phonograph
at the time, he declared, and the
time that elapsed was about three
turns of the phonograph record. In
other words, it was about two sec-
onds.
Changes Statement
He continued that Hu had told
him that he saw a man running
away from the scene, and that the
man was dressed in dark clothes.
It was brought out that Hu was
questioned at the police station and
that he first stated that the man
he saw running away was dressed
in dark clothes resembling a uni-
form, but later changed this state-
ment. In his new statement, he said
the man had only worn dark
clothes.
Hu was asked if it was Yih whom
he had seen on the night of the
murder. The witness declared that
it was not, or at least he didn't
recognize him.
Yih spoke up and addressed the
witness: "You may not have seen
me, but I saw you," he declared.
Dr. Okawa, Japanese military
surgeon, testified to examining the
body. He was shown the bullet pick-
ed up by the police. Asked if the
wound in Nakayama's head was
made by that bullet, he declared
that he could not say, but believed
that the wound was made by a
similar bullet. Judge Chien ordered
the bullet handed over to the police
with the request that they look for
blood stains and compare such
stains with the blood of the dead
man.
Yesterday's hearing concluded at
about 4.45 p.m. and the case was re-
manded for two weeks. It was point-
ed out that the Korean could not
be called as a witness because the
Japanese Consular authorities were
still investigating the man. He will
be called, it was stated, when this
investigation is completed.
As at Friday's hearing, the
courtroom was crowded yesterday.
Japanese naval officers were present
but they took off their swords before
entering the courtroom.

那位名叫高桥（Takahashi）的日本鞋匠宣称，他也听到了枪声。当被问及从他听到枪声到胡某冲进他的店铺之间隔了多长时间时，证人说他不太确定。他宣称当时他正在放留声机，间隔的时间大约是留声机唱片转了三圈。换句话说，大约是两秒钟。
改变陈述
他继续说，胡某告诉他，他看到一个人从现场跑开，那人穿着深色衣服。据披露，胡某在警察局接受过讯问，他最初陈述说他看到逃跑的人穿着类似制服的深色衣服，但后来改变了这一陈述。在新的陈述中，他说那人只穿了深色衣服。
胡某被问及他在谋杀案当晚看到的是否是易某。证人宣称不是，或者至少他不认识他。
易某插话并对证人说：“你可能没看到我，但我看到了你，”他宣称。
日本军医大川博士（Dr. Okawa，音译）作证说他对尸体进行了检查。向他展示了警方捡到的子弹。当被问及中山头部的伤口是否由该子弹造成时，他宣称他不能确定，但认为伤口是由类似的子弹造成的。钱法官命令将子弹移交警方，并要求他们寻找血迹，并将这些血迹与死者的血液进行比较。
昨日的听证会于下午4点45分左右结束，案件延期两周审理。有人指出，由于日本领事当局仍在调查该朝鲜人，因此无法将其作为证人传唤。据称，待调查结束后将传唤他。
与周五的庭审一样，昨天法庭内挤满了人。日本海军军官在场，但他们在进入法庭前卸下了佩剑。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, MAY 7, 1936
“Shao Kwangtung” Says
He Murdered Nakayama;
Huge Frame-Up Alleged
Self-Confessed Murderer Completely Exonerates
Yang; New Witness Alleges Frame-Up In Order
To Collect Rewards; Two Weeks’ Remand
AUTHORITIES COMPLETELY AT A LOSS;
KOREAN NOT BROUGHT TO COURT
Two bombshells were thrown in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon during the trial of two Cantonese on charges of murder in connection with the killing of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama, of the Japanese Naval Landing force, on Darroch Road at 9 p.m. on November 9, last. The first sensation burst over the court room when Yih Hai-sen, alias “Shao Kwangtung” 28-year-old alleged Hongkew underworld figure, stated that he had killed Warrant Officer Nakayama. This statement was received with a mixed feeling of surprise and laughter in the crowded courtroom, as at the last hearing on Friday “Shao Kwangtung” had implicated the other accused, Yang Wen-tao, 42-year-old Cantonese former employee of the China Navigation Company, in the shooting, stating at the time that he was present at the scene together with the Korean, Jack, now being held by the Japanese Consular Police.
The second surprise came when a new witness, Chang Sen, a former automobile salesman, stepped into the witness stand, and after the presiding judge had overruled the police objection, stated that the allegations made by Tseng Yuan, star witness for the prosecution, against the two accused had no foundation at all and that Tseng Yuan, Chang Tsai-yuen and another man had allegedly “framed” the case against “Shao Kwangtung” and Yang in order to collect the rewards offered by the City Government of Greater Shanghai, the Shanghai Municipal Police and the Japanese authorities.
With “Shao Kwangtung” repudiating his statements made at the last hearing incriminating Yang and now completely exonerating him as well as confessing to committing the crime himself, followed by an allegation of a frame-up by an independent witness, the trial seemed to make to headway at all, but commenced becoming more and more complicated. At this stage, the prosecution asked for a remand of two weeks in order to enable the police to investigate the new sensational developments. Judge Dzien, who is presiding over the trial, assisted by two other judges and a procurator, granted the remand immediately.
Wanted To Kill
“I wanted to kill a high Japanese officer ever since the Sino-Japanese hostilities in 1932,” stated “Shao Kwangtung” in admitting the crime and repudiating all the statements made by him at the previous hearing. “Not being able to find a high officer and seeing a Japanese sailor walking along Darroch Road on the night of November 9, I killed him,” concluded the man.
Judge Dzien immediately commenced questioning “Shao Kwangtung” in detail as a hush fell over the courtroom following the bursting of the bombshell. Yih, alias “Shao Kwangtung,” then told the Judge that neither Yang nor Jack, the Korean, were with him when he shot and killed Warrant Officer Nakayama. He repudiated all the statements made by him to the police in the last few days that the murder plot was discussed by him with Yang, another Chinese named Chou and two Koreans. To convince the Court, Yih stated that he was suffering from a great mental strain when he made these statements to the police and further that he was afraid of the police methods.
A sense of irony was injected into the tense situation after Hu Hsian-ho, a Chinese shoemaker, who was one of the nearest to the scene of the crime, stated that he had never seen “Shao Kwangtung” before, and “Shao Kwangtung” spoke up quickly, saying that the witness might not have seen him, but that he saw the witness when he fired at the Japanese sailor.
Korean Not Brought
Despite the request made by Judge Dzien at the last hearing that the Korean, Jack, now being held by the Japanese Consular Police, in connection with the murder, be brought to the court yesterday, the Korean did not appear. Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Y. Ru, who is conducting the prosecution, informed the Court that the Japanese Consular Police had not yet completed their inquiries in connection with the Korean and, therefore, could not bring him down.
As at the previous hearing, many Japanese, Chinese and Shanghai Municipal Police officials were present at the hearing. Municipal Advocate Robert T. Bryan, Jr., sat beside Mr. Ru all through the hearing.
Yang’s Boy Released
A third prisoner, Yang’s boy, who was arrested by the police together with Yang and stood in the dock all through the last hearing, was not present in court yesterday, having been released since the last hearing.
At the opening of the hearing, the Assistant Municipal Advocate, Mr. Paul Ru, told the Judge that during the adjournment, the police had not yet completed the investigation of witnesses. He wished that the Court would question several other witnesses, namely, two Chinese constables (C. P. C. 2891 and 2864) who were on the scene of the crime soon after it was committed, Hu Hsian-ho, a Chinese shoe-maker, a Japanese shoe shop manager and the official doctor of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, who examined the dead sailor’s body.
Murder Planned
Mr. Ru alleged that at the police station, Yih said that in October of 1935, Yang Wen-tao and another Chinese named Chou went to the Moon Palace Cabaret to meet him. They later went together to the Tung Yi Association (of which Yang Wen-tao was chairman) and there they discussed the murder plot with two Koreans, who had secretly become members of the association, “Shao Kwangtung” was said to have told the police.
At the end of October, Chou went to see “Shao Kwangtung” at the request of Yang to discuss the plot, and this discussion was also participated in by two Koreans, one of whom was Jack. On November 2, the two accused and Jack went to the Hongkew Park to discuss the methods of committing the crime and of escaping. Yang made no confessions at the police station, it was said.
None of the witnesses yesterday made important statements that would tend to help solve the mystery. The two Chinese constables said that when they arrived at the scene of the crime, they saw the body of a Japanese officer lying in a pool of blood. They informed their station. One of them claimed that he had questioned two people, the Japanese and Chinese shoemakers, regarding the crime.
Hu Hsian-ho, the Chinese shoe-maker, said that on November 9 last, he was just about to enter a Japanese shoemaker’s shop on Darroch Road, when he heard a gunshot. He also saw a man running into Feng Lo Alley. That man was wearing a black coat and trousers, but he was not sure that his dress was similar to that worn by the dead officer. The Japanese shoemaker admitted that he knew Hu and that the latter entered his shop after he had heard the shooting.
The Japanese witness further said that at the time of the shooting, he was playing some records on a gramophone. When the machine had turned three rounds, Hu entered and told him of the shooting. At that time, Hu did not tell him about the man running away, but later he did. Hu said that he had not seen the hat worn by the fleeing man nor did he remember whether or not the man wore a hat at all.
Doctor’s Evidence
Dr. Okawa, of the Japanese Naval Landing Party Hospital, said that he had examined the body of the dead Japanese officer. He testified that the bullet had pierced through the officer’s head from the back. He did not examine the bullet on the day when he examined the body. The bullet was given him the next day and he thought that that bullet could have killed the officer in the way he described.
The Judge was not satisfied with this evidence. He immediately wrapped up the bullet produced by the police with a sheet of paper and returned it to the police for further examination. The Judge stated that he wanted to know whether or not the bullet had ever been blackened.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年5月7日，星期四
“邵广东”称
他杀害了中山；
指控存在巨大构陷
自首凶手完全为杨开脱；新证人指控为领取赏金而构陷；还押两周
当局完全不知所措；
朝鲜人未被带至法庭

昨日下午，在第一特区法院审理两名广东人涉嫌谋杀案的过程中，投下了两枚“炸弹”。该案涉及去年11月9日晚9时在大路（Darroch Road）杀害日本海军陆战队军曹中山英夫（Hideo Nakayama）。当28岁、据称为虹口黑社会人物的易海森（Yih Hai-sen），别名“邵广东”，声称是他杀害了中山军曹时，第一个轰动性消息在法庭上爆发。这一陈述在拥挤的法庭内引起了惊讶与笑声交织的反应，因为在上周五的上一次聆讯中，“邵广东”曾牵连另一名被告、42岁的广东人、前中国轮船公司雇员杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao）参与枪击，当时他声称自己与现在被日本领事警察拘留的朝鲜人杰克（Jack）一同在现场。

第二个意外出现在新证人、前汽车推销员张森（Chang Sen）走上证人席时。在主审法官驳回警方异议后，张森陈述称，控方主要证人曾元（Tseng Yuan）对两名被告的指控毫无根据，并指称曾元、张载元（Chang Tsai-yuen）及另一人为了获取上海特别市政府、上海公共租界工部局警务处及日本当局提供的赏金， allegedly “构陷”了“邵广东”和杨文涛。

随着“邵广东”推翻上次聆讯中牵连杨文涛的供词，不仅完全为其开脱，还承认罪行系自己所为，加之独立证人提出构陷指控，审判似乎毫无进展，反而变得愈发复杂。在此阶段，控方请求还押两周，以便警方调查这些新的轰动性进展。主持审判的丁恩（Dzien）法官，在另外两名法官和一名检察官的协助下，立即批准了还押。

意图杀人
“自从1932年中日敌对行动以来，我就想杀死一名日本高级军官，”“邵广东”在承认罪行并推翻上次聆讯中的所有陈述时说道。“由于找不到高级军官，而在11月9日晚看到一名日本水兵沿大路行走，我便杀了他，”该男子总结道。

随着这枚“炸弹”爆炸，法庭内一片寂静，丁恩法官随即开始详细讯问“邵广东”。易某，别名“邵广东”，随后告诉法官，当他开枪杀害中山军曹时，杨文涛和朝鲜人杰克都不在他身边。他推翻了前几天向警方所作的所有供词，即他曾与杨文涛、另一名中国人周某以及两名朝鲜人商讨谋杀计划。为了让法庭信服，易某称他在向警方作这些陈述时承受着巨大的精神压力，并且害怕警方的手段。

在紧张的气氛中注入了一丝讽刺意味的是，离犯罪现场最近的证人之一、中国鞋匠胡贤和（Hu Hsian-ho）表示他以前从未见过“邵广东”，而“邵广东”迅速插话称，证人可能没看见他，但他在向日本水兵开枪时看见了该证人。

朝鲜人未被带来
尽管丁恩法官在上次聆讯中要求将现在因谋杀案被日本领事警察拘留的朝鲜人杰克于昨日带上法庭，但该朝鲜人并未出现。负责提起公诉的助理市政检察官鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru）先生告知法庭，日本领事警察尚未完成对该朝鲜人的调查，因此无法将其带至法庭。

与上次聆讯一样，许多日本人、中国人和上海公共租界工部局警务处官员出席了聆讯。市政检察官小罗伯特·T·布莱恩（Robert T. Bryan, Jr.）在整个聆讯期间坐在鲁先生身旁。

杨的伙计获释
第三名囚犯，即杨的伙计，此前与杨一同被警方逮捕并在上次聆讯全程站在被告席上，昨日未出庭，自上次聆讯以来已获释。

聆讯开始时，助理市政检察官鲁保罗先生告诉法官，在休庭期间，警方尚未完成对证人的调查。他希望法庭讯问其他几名证人，即两名在案发后不久到达现场的中国巡捕（编号C. P. C. 2891和2864）、中国鞋匠胡贤和、一家日本鞋店经理以及检查死者遗体的日本海军陆战队官方医生。

谋杀预谋
鲁先生指控称，在警察局，易某说1935年10月，杨文涛和另一名中国人周某去月宫舞厅（Moon Palace Cabaret）见他。后来他们一起去了同义会（Tung Yi Association，杨文涛任会长），在那里他们与两名秘密成为该会成员的朝鲜人讨论了谋杀计划，据说“邵广东”曾这样告诉警方。

10月底，周某应杨的要求去见“邵广东”讨论该计划，两名朝鲜人也参与了此次讨论，其中一人是杰克。11月2日，两名被告和杰克去虹口公园讨论实施犯罪和逃跑的方法。据说杨在警察局没有作任何供述。

昨天的证人中没有谁作出有助于解开谜团的重要陈述。两名中国巡捕说，当他们到达犯罪现场时，看到一名日本军官的尸体躺在血泊中。他们通知了警局。其中一人声称他就此案讯问了两人，即日本和中国鞋匠。

中国鞋匠胡贤和说，去年11月9日，他正欲进入大路上一家日本鞋匠的店铺时，听到一声枪响。他还看到一个人跑进凤乐里（Feng Lo Alley）。那人穿着黑色外套和裤子，但他不确定那人的衣着是否与死去的军官相似。日本鞋匠承认认识胡，并称胡在听到枪声后进入了他的店铺。

这位日本证人进一步说，枪击发生时，他正在留声机上播放唱片。机器转了三圈后，胡进来告诉他发生了枪击。当时胡没有告诉他有人逃跑的事，但后来告诉了。胡说他没看到逃跑者戴的帽子，也不记得那人是否戴了帽子。

医生证词
日本海军陆战队医院的大川（Okawa）医生说，他检查了那名日本军官的尸体。他作证说，子弹从后方穿透了军官的头部。他在检查尸体当天没有检查子弹。第二天有人把子弹交给他，他认为那颗子弹可能以他所描述的方式杀死了军官。

法官对这一证据不满意。他立即用一张纸将警方出示的子弹包好，退回警方进行进一步检查。法官表示，他想知道子弹是否曾被熏黑过。

Mrs. Tseng Yuen, wife of the
informant and witness, told the
Judge that she knew "Shao
Kwangtung," as the latter had
visited her home, asking for a
loan of $25 and offering a pistol
as security. Her husband refus-
ed to lend him money, she said.
She further said that when "Shao
Kwangtung" asked for a loan, he
prepared a "petition" to that
effect, but that the petition had
been thrown away. Her husband's
friend, Chang Sen, asked that the
matter be brought to the atten-
tion of the police, but she opposed
it, she said.

Complete Confession

When questioned by the Judge
regarding his alleged confession
made at the police station, "Shao
Kwangtung" said that the murder
was committed by him single-
handed. Ever since the January
28 Incident, he had planned to
kill a high Japanese officer. It was
he who possessed the pistol which
was identified by the police to
have been used in the Nakayama
murder. It was his book hollowed
out at the centre in which he put
his pistol. The book was hollow-
ed out by him, he said.
Judge Dien pointed out that his
statement must be wrong because
at the last hearing, Yang Wen-
tao confessed that it was he
(Yang) himself who had hollowed
out the book at the centre. Yih
opposed the Judge's statement
and went on to say that when he
committed the crime, he was
dressed in black. He did not wish
to do harm to others because he
alone had committed the crime,
he emphasized.
Yang Wen-tao denied that his
association had any Korean mem-
bers. He said he knew Chou, who
was a member of his organization.
At the police station, when "Shao
Kwangtung" made his confession,
he (Yang) was not at the ("Shao
Kwangtung's") side.

Frame-Up Alleged

Despite oppositions from the
police, the Judge summoned
Chang Sen, a friend of Tseng
Yuen, and former motor car
salesman, for questioning at the
request of a lawyer for the de-
fence. Chang was the man who
went to the police station on
Tuesday afternoon, asserting that
the whole thing was a frame-up.
Chang told the Judge that he
had been Tseng's friend for many
years. He often visited Tseng's
home. On December 10 of last
year (according to the Lunar
Calendar), he said, he saw Tseng
and a friend, a Dr. Tsen Wei-min,
smoking opium. The doctor drew
a picture of a pistol on a sheet of
paper. He was allowed to see the
picture afterwards. On the handle
of that pistol he saw the letters
"F. B." marked.
Tseng wanted to get the reward
money, he said, and so obtained
correct information regarding the
make of the pistol used in the
murder from official Japanese
sources. Dr. Tsen Wei-min asked
him (Chang) several times to see
the Korean (Jack) in the Japanese
Consulate but he (Chang) refused
to do so. Chang said that he was
asked to name "Shao Kwangtung"
as the killer. When he refused to
take part in the frame-up, Dr.
Tsen invited Chang Tsai-yuen to
participate. Chang Tsai-yuen
was the man who, at the last
hearing, said that he saw "Shao
Kwangtung," Jack and another
man driving a car of North
[illegible] afterwards
on November [illegible].

告密者兼证人曾元的妻子曾夫人告诉法官，她认识“邵广东”，因为后者曾到她家拜访，请求借款25美元，并提出以一把手枪作为抵押。她说，她丈夫拒绝借钱给他。她还说，当“邵广东”请求借款时，他为此准备了一份“呈文”，但该呈文已被丢弃。她说，她丈夫的朋友张森曾要求将此事项提请警方注意，但她表示反对。

完全供认

当法官就其在警察局所谓的供认进行讯问时，“邵广东”说谋杀是他单独实施的。自一·二八事变以来，他就计划杀死一名日本高级军官。警方认定用于中山谋杀案的手枪归他所有。那本中间被挖空以放置手枪的书也是他的。他说，书是他自己挖空的。

丁恩法官指出，他的陈述肯定是错误的，因为在上次聆讯中，杨文涛供认是他（杨）自己挖空了书的中心部分。易某反对法官的说法，并继续说，他在作案时身穿黑衣。他强调，他不想伤害他人，因为罪行是他一人所为。

杨文涛否认其协会有任何朝鲜成员。他说他认识周某，周是其组织的一员。他说，在警察局“邵广东”作供时，他（杨）并不在（“邵广东”）身边。

指控构陷

尽管遭到警方反对，应辩护律师的请求，法官传唤曾元的朋友、前汽车推销员张森接受讯问。张森就是周二下午去警察局声称整件事是一起构陷的人。

张森告诉法官，他曾是曾元多年的朋友。他经常去曾元家。他说，去年农历十二月初十，他看见曾元和一位朋友、岑维民（Tsen Wei-min）医生在吸鸦片。医生在一张纸上画了一把手枪的图样。事后他被允许看了这幅图。在那把手枪的握把上，他看到了标记字母“F. B.”。

他说，曾元想要得到赏金，因此从日本官方渠道获得了关于谋杀所用枪支型号的正确信息。岑维民医生多次要求他（张森）去日本领事馆见那名朝鲜人（杰克），但他（张森）拒绝了。张森说，他被要求指认“邵广东”为凶手。当他拒绝参与构陷时，岑医生邀请了张载元参与。张载元就是在上次聆讯中说他在11月[原文不清]之后看到“邵广东”、杰克和另一人驾驶一辆北[原文不清]汽车的人。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, May 6, 1936
1448
Jockey Confesses
Alleged Frame-Up
In Nakayama Case

Sensational Hearing In
Murder Trial Slated
This Afternoon

CASE MADE UP TO
COLLECT REWARDS

Chinese Grilled During
Night By Detectives;
Conscience Hurts

Sensational developments in the trial of two Cantonese on charges of being involved in the murder of warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party in Darroch Road on November 9 last year, were expected in the First Special District Court this afternoon.

One Chang Sen, a former automobile salesman and jockey, late yesterday afternoon surrendered himself to the Central Station police and is said to have written a lengthy confession stating that he, with Tseng Yuan, one of the star witnesses of the prosecution, and a China-born Japanese by the name of Tseng-Ping-san, had allegedly "framed" the case against Yang Wen-tao and Yih-Hai-sen, alias "Shao Kwangtung," with the intent of collecting the $12,000 reward offered by the City Government of Greater Shanghai, the Shanghai Municipal Police and the Japanese authorities.

Questioned Till Midnight

Accompanied by a former Cantonese detective, Chang went to the Central Station at 2 o'clock yesterday afternoon and remained there until midnight, questioned at length by Assistant Commissioner T. Robertson of the Special Branch, Japanese Sub-Inspector Nakamura and Detective Tanaka, according to information gathered this morning. Chang and his written document will be sent to the court this afternoon, it is understood.

While official circles continued to maintain a wall of reticence, it is learned from reliable sources that Chang had told the officers in his confession that he and his accomplices had first attempted to "frame" a case against a high Chapel police officer to add "political color" to the Nakayama murder. When this failed, they are alleged to have attempted to victimise a Miss Chen Hung-pi, principal of a Cantonese school in Chapel, seeking to collect blackmail from her wealthy parents.

"To Clear Conscience"

The second alleged plot also failed and the gang turned their attention to Yang and Yih, Chang is reported to have told the officers. Chang also is said to have told the officers that he has surrendered and made the confession in order to clear his conscience when he saw two "innocent" men face the serious charges of murder.

Attorney G. R. Grove, popular Chinese practitioner who is appearing for Yang, is understood to have established contact with Chang as early as last Friday and had persuaded him to sign a document to be presented to the court this morning before the trial resumes. Chang, however, suddenly changed his mind and went to the police station yesterday.

Yih Confession Hit

Attorney Grove has also collected evidence to be present in court this afternoon substantiating the confessions made by Chang and to show that Yang could not have been on Darroch Road the night of the murder and that he was spending the evening at a club on Urga Road. He was also to challenge the testimony given by "Shao Kwangtung" that Yang had fired the shot, intimating, when approached by The Shanghai Evening Post and Mercury, that Yih may also have something to do with the alleged "frame up."

Until Chang's appearance in the Central Station yesterday with a new story, officers handling the investigations had apparently been working on the case according to the confession by Yih during the last session. On Monday night, the crime was re-enacted, at the spot where the Japanese officer was killed, by police and Japanese consular police officials. The results were not made known.

The two Cantonese were to be brought before the court at 2 o'clock this afternoon before a full court presided over by Judge Chien Hung-nieh. Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Y. Ru will appear for the prosecution.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年5月6日，星期三
1448
骑师供认
中山案中
涉嫌构陷

谋杀案审判预计
今日下午出现
轰动性听证

案件系为
领取赏金而捏造

华人夜间遭侦探
严加盘问；
良心不安

今天下午，第一特区地方法院预计将在两名广东人因涉嫌参与去年11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）谋杀日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）一案的审判中，出现轰动性的进展。

一名叫张森（Chang Sen）的前汽车推销员兼骑师，于昨日下午向中央巡捕房自首。据称，他写了一份长篇供词，陈述他与控方主要证人之一曾元（Tseng Yuan），以及一名生于中国的日本人曾平三（Tseng-Ping-san，音译），涉嫌“构陷”杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao）和易海森（Yih-Hai-sen，别名“邵广东”），意图获取由大上海市政府、上海公共租界工部局警务处及日本当局提供的12,000美元赏金。

审讯至午夜

据今晨获悉的消息，张森由一名前广东籍侦探陪同，于昨日下午2时前往中央巡捕房，并一直停留至午夜，期间接受了特务科助理总监T. Robertson（罗伯逊）、日本副巡官中村（Nakamura）以及侦探田中（Tanaka）的详细讯问。据悉，张森及其书面供词将于今天下午送交法院。

尽管官方人士继续守口如瓶，但从可靠消息来源得知，张森在供词中告诉警官，他和同伙最初试图“构陷”一名高级华捕，以便为中山谋杀案增添“政治色彩”。当这一企图失败后，据称他们又试图陷害闸北一所广东学校的女校长陈鸿璧（Chen Hung-pi，音译）小姐，企图向其富有的父母勒索钱财。

“为了良心安宁”

据称张森告诉警官，第二次阴谋也失败了，于是该团伙将目标转向了杨和易。据说张森还告诉警官，当他看到两名“无辜”的人面临严重的谋杀指控时，为了良心安宁，他选择自首并作出供认。

代表杨文涛出庭的知名华人律师G. R. Grove（格罗夫），据悉早在上周五就已与张森取得联系，并说服他签署一份文件，打算在今日上午庭审恢复前提交给法院。然而，张森突然改变主意，于昨日前往警察局。

易之供词受冲击

格罗夫律师还收集了证据，将于今天下午在法庭上出示，以证实张森的供词，并证明杨文涛在谋杀案发生当晚不可能出现在达罗克路，当时他正在乌拉路（Urga Road）的一家俱乐部度过夜晚。他还打算质疑“邵广东”关于杨文涛开枪射击的证词，并在接受《上海晚邮报与水星报》采访时暗示，易海森可能也与所谓的“构陷”有关。

直到昨天张森带着新的说法出现在中央巡捕房之前，负责调查的警官显然一直在根据易海森在上一次庭审期间的供词处理此案。周一晚上，警方和日本领事馆警察官员在日军军官被杀的地点重新演绎了犯罪过程。结果尚未公布。

这两名广东人将于今天下午2时在钱洪业（Chien Hung-nieh，音译）法官主持的全庭审理中被提审。市公署检察官Paul Y. Ru（鲁保罗，音译）将代表控方出庭。

THE CHINA PRESS, WEDNESDAY, MAY 6, 1936

Shooting Is
Re-enacted At
Hongkew Spot

Incidents Of Nakayama
Slaying Gone Over
On Death Site

Reconstruction of the crime in
the Nakayama Murder Case was
carried out by Shanghai Municipal
Police and Japanese Consular
Police officials at the scene of the
killing on Darroch Road, at 9 p.m.
Monday, a CHINA PRESS reporter
was informed yesterday.

Yih Hai-sen, better known as
"Hsiao Kwangtung," who has al-
ready confessed to complicity in
the slaying, Yang Wen-tao, promi-
nent Cantonese resident of Shang-
hai, and the mysterious "Jack,"
the Korean, all accused of being
involved, were led out of their de-
tention cells and taken to the
scene.

While no official report has been
issued on results of the crime re-
construction scene, it is believed
that it was carried out in an effort
to break the silence of Yang Wen-
tao, who was accused by "Hsiao
Kwangtung" in open court last
Friday of having been the man
who fired the death bullet.

Warrant Officer Hideo Nakaya-
ma, of the Japanese Naval Landing
Party, was shot at 9 p.m., Novem-
ber 9, 1935, as he was on his way
to barracks. Yih, in his confes-
sion, declares that he went with
Yang and the Korean from the
Moon Palace Cabaret on North
Szechuen Road an hour before the
shooting occurred and walked to
Darroch Road. After turning onto
the latter street, the man stated
in court, he saw Yang remove a
pistol from a book which the latter
was carrying under his arm.

Yih continued that he saw Yang
raise the gun and fire. He did not
see who was hit, he declared, be-
cause he took to his heels and ran.
He heard later that the murdered
man was a Japanese.

Yang flatly denied the accusation
and declared that he was being
made the victim of a "frame-up."

He had never gone to the Moon
Palace, he declared, and didn't
know Yih until he was brought
into court with him to answer to
a murder charge. Aside from this
brief statement, the man has
maintained a strict silence through-
out the court investigation and
has even refused to present an
alibi.

Both men are scheduled to be
brought into court at 2 p.m. today
and further sensational develop-
ments that may throw some light
on the new obscure motive for the
killing of Nakayama are expected.
It is understood that the Korean
will testify today.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年5月6日，星期三

枪击案在
虹口现场
重新演绎

中山谋杀案
情节在死亡
地点重现

据《字林西报》记者昨日获悉，上海公共租界工部局警务处和日本领事馆警察官员于周一晚上9点，在达罗克路的杀人现场进行了中山谋杀案的犯罪重建。

已承认参与杀人的易海森（更为人知的名字是“小广东”）、上海著名广东居民杨文涛，以及被指控涉案的神秘朝鲜人“杰克”，均被带出拘留牢房，押往现场。

虽然官方尚未发布关于犯罪重建结果的报告，但人们认为，此举旨在打破杨文涛的沉默。在上周五的公开法庭上，“小广东”指控杨文涛是发射致命子弹的人。

1935年11月9日晚上9点，日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄在前往兵营途中被枪杀。易海森在供词中声称，在枪击发生前一小时，他与杨文涛及那名朝鲜人一起从北四川路的月宫舞厅（Moon Palace Cabaret）出发，步行前往达罗克路。该男子在法庭上陈述，转入达罗克路后，他看见杨文涛从夹在腋下的书中取出一把手枪。

易海森继续说，他看见杨文涛举枪射击。他声称自己没有看到谁被击中，因为他拔腿就跑。后来他听说死者是一名日本人。

杨文涛断然否认了这一指控，并宣称自己正成为“构陷”的受害者。

他声称自己从未去过月宫舞厅，并且在因谋杀指控被带上法庭与易海森对质之前，根本不认识易海森。除了这简短的声明外，该男子在整个法庭调查过程中一直保持严格的沉默，甚至拒绝提供不在场证明。

两人定于今天下午2时被带上法庭，预计会有进一步的轰动性发展，这可能为中山被杀这一新的晦涩动机提供一些线索。据悉，那名朝鲜人将于今日作证。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, May 5, 1936
11406

Japanese Death
Creates Uproar
In Swatow City

Nipponese Constable's
Collapse Results In
Indemnity Demand

MAYOR OPPOSES
$60,000 DEMAND

Second 'Nakayama Case'
Causes Wild Rumors,
Increased Tension

A tense situation is again pre-
vailing in Swatow, northern
Kwangtung city, as result of a de-
mand by Japanese Consul Tsunoda
for the immediate payment of an
"indemnity" of $60,000 for the
alleged murder of Constable
Harada of the Japanese Consular
Police, according to Chinese press
reports today.

The presence of three Japanese
warships is causing additional ex-
citement to the populace while the
"ronins" in the city have redoubled
their activities, causing minor
trouble, the reports added.

Demand Rejected

It was revealed that Consul
Tsunoda sent the demand to the
Swatow Municipal Government on
May 1, asking that the "indemnity"
be paid the following day. Upon
receipt of the demand, the Swatow
mayor immediately telegraphed the
Kwangtung Provincial Government
for instructions. On May 2, the
mayor formally rejected the Japan-
ese demand.

Admiral Nishioka, commander of
the 10th Squadron of the Japanese
Navy, has offered his services to
mediate in the dispute. Negotia-
tions are still going on while
nervousness prevails among the
Chinese. Wild rumors of impending
conflict are circulating.

It is stated that the Municipal
Government of Swatow has declar-
ed martial law because of the
tension.

ANOTHER NAKAYAMA INCIDENT

YELLOW SEA
NANKING
SHANGHAI
EAST CHINA SEA
HANKOW
CHANGSHA
FOOCHOW
SCENE OF LATEST INCIDENT
AMOY
CANTON
SWATOW
FORMOSA
FRENCH INDO CHINA
HONGKONG
SIAM
BURMA

Japanese Collapsed

Constable Harada collapsed near
his home at 12.30 p.m. on January
21. He was sent to a Japanese
Hospital by a Chinese policeman
where he died. At 3 p.m. the same
day, the Japanese consul register-
ed a protest with the Swatow
mayor, declaring that Harada was
shot 12 times by unknown as-
sailants. Investigation by the Swa-
tow Municipal Government, how-
ever, revealed that no residents
near Harada's home had heard of
the shooting affair nor could any
blood be found at the spot where
he collapsed. The Chinese demand
for an autopsy was rejected. The
body was cremated on January 23.

The case has caused tension com-
parable to the murder of Warrant
Officer Hideo Nakayama of the
Japanese Naval Landing Force in
Shanghai last November. More
than 10 Japanese warships were
rushed to Swatow. The Chinese
refused responsibility for the death.

The trial of two Cantonese held
in connection with the Nakayama
murder case is to be resumed at
the First Special District Court
here at 2 o'clock tomorrow after-
noon. During the first public hear-
ing last Friday, "Shao Kwangtung,"
one of the accused, confessed his
part but implicated Yang Wen-tao,
the other accused, as the man who
had actually fired the shots killing
the Japanese bluejacket.

(印：...AL MUNICIP...)

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年5月5日，星期二
11406

日本人之死
在汕头市
引起骚动

日本警员倒地
导致赔偿要求

市长反对
六万美元要求

第二起“中山案”
引发疯狂谣言，
紧张局势加剧

据今日中文报纸报道，由于日本领事角田（Tsunoda，音译）要求立即支付60,000美元作为所谓日本领事馆警察原田（Harada）警员被谋杀的“赔偿金”，广东省北部城市汕头再次出现紧张局势。

报道补充说，三艘日本军舰的存在引起了民众的额外激动，而市内的“浪人”则加倍活动，制造了小麻烦。

要求被拒

据悉，角田领事于5月1日向汕头市政府发出要求，要求次日支付“赔偿金”。收到要求后，汕头市长立即致电广东省政府请示。5月2日，市长正式拒绝了日本方面的要求。

日本海军第十战队司令西冈（Nishioka，音译）海军少将已提出协助调解争端。谈判仍在进行中，而中国人中间弥漫着紧张情绪。关于即将发生冲突的疯狂谣言正在流传。

据悉，汕头市政府已因紧张局势宣布戒严。

另一起中山事件

黄海
南京
上海
东海
汉口
长沙
福州
最新事件发生地
厦门
广州
汕头
台湾
法属印度支那
香港
暹罗
缅甸

日本人倒地

1月21日中午12时30分，原田警员在其住所附近倒地。一名中国警察将他送往一家日本医院，他在那里死亡。同日下午3时，日本领事向汕头市长提出抗议，宣称原田被不明袭击者射击12次。然而，汕头市政府的调查显示，原田住所附近的居民均未听闻枪击事件，在他倒地的地方也未发现任何血迹。中方提出的尸检要求被拒绝。尸体于1月23日被火化。

此案造成的紧张局势可与去年11月上海日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄被谋杀案相媲美。十多艘日本军舰紧急驶往汕头。中方拒绝为死亡承担责任。

与中山谋杀案有关的两名广东人的审判，将于明天下午2时在此处的第一特区地方法院恢复审理。在上周五的首次公开听证会上，被告之一“邵广东”承认了自己的参与，但牵连另一名被告杨文涛，称其为实际开枪杀死这名日本水兵的凶手。

(印：...AL MUNICIP...)

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, May 2, 1936

Yih's Confession
Hides Intrigue

Underworld Connection
With Mysterious
'Jack' Unknown

The "inside story" of the Nakayama murder case, as related before the First Special District Court, was characterized here today by police observers and officials not directly connected with investigation of the case as a "surface confession" which leaves the ramifications of the murder still deeply by prevarication and intrigue in the Hongkew underworld. Just what connection, if any, Yang Wen-tao, 47-year-old Cantonese, had with the mysterious prisoner of the Japanese Consular Police known only as "Jack," is unknown —or at least carefully guarded by the Japanese. Yih Hai-sen's part in the murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama last November 9, as told by himself yesterday, is believed to be only to a small extent factual.

"Little Kwangtung" confessed to complicity in the murder in open court yesterday afternoon, naming Yang as the man who fired the fatal shot on Darroch Road that felled a Japanese officer and created a Chapel stampede. He also declared that the alleged Korean, "Jack" was the third member of the party. But Yang flatly denied police charges and all statements made by Yih, declaring that he had had absolutely no part in the affair. This was made in the face of damning circumstantial evidence offered by police officers of the S.M.P. after formal charges of murder had been filed.

"Jack" A Mystery

Attention swung back today to the part "Jack" is believed to have had in the crime. This man, arrested by Japanese officers in Tsingtao, was first described as a Korean. Yet "Jack"—which is not his real name—is declared to have been born in Russia and to have come to China only last year from Vladivostok. What his name is Japanese Consular Police don't know or won't tell. He does not know the Korean language and speaks haltingly in Japanese.

He is still be carefully guarded at Japanese Police Headquarters. Whether he has appeared before the Japanese Consular Court, whether he has made a confession or not, is a secret kept by headquarters. The Japanese lifted their press ban on Japanese newspapers last night and these papers published accounts of the District Court hearing this morning, but no mention was made of "Jack." The press ban, therefore, has been only partly lifted and papers may publish only the District Court proceedings. The third figure in the case remains shadowy in the backgrounds.

Motive A Puzzle

In addition, police are still puzzled about the motive for the crime, though today it was generally considered that the possibility of a political crime was very remote, and that Nakayama had been murdered as results of a personal quarrel between himself and "Jack," who may have later enlisted the support of notorious Hongkew underworld habitues to help him get his enemy. That "Little Kwangtung" is such a character there is little doubt; the part Yang played is still obscure. This man, on the surface at least, has been a faithful employee of the China Navigation Company for a number of years and chairman of a benevolent association in his own guild.

After Yih's confession yesterday, Yang, in denying the accusations, declared that he is the innocent victim of a police frame-up.

Yih had said that he met Yang and "Jack" at the Moon Palace Cabaret that night and had been asked to go with them "to kill a man." He had denied knowledge of what man was to be killed, or why. He went along, he said, and saw Yang take a pistol out of a book and fire at a man in Darroch Road, after which the three scattered.

Yang "Goat"

Yang maintains that he is being made the "goat" in the case. Police evidence against him, introduced yesterday, includes discovery of a book in Yang's house, the leaves hollowed out to hold a pistol, as well as evidence given by one Tseng Yuen who declared that the gun found at the scene of the crime was one belonging to Yang. Yang's alibi was more or less broken down by police in court, through testimony by ballistics experts.

It was also declared that before Nakayama was murdered Yih had been very poor, a hanger-on in the Hongkew cafes, but afterwards he suddenly had money, went to Tsingtao and bought a cabaret there. Yih said in defense that his mother and sweetheart, released a few days ago, had given him the money.

The third Cantonese, Chen Yung-sen, was to be released today, charges against him being dropped for lack of police evidence.

The hearing of the case will be continued next Wednesday before Judge Chien Hung-nieh, presiding, and Associate Judges Feng Shih-tsh and Shaw Shih-feng.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年5月2日，星期六

易的供词
掩盖阴谋

黑社会联系
与神秘的
“杰克”身份不明

今日，警方观察员及未直接参与该案调查的官员称，在第一特区法院陈述的中山（Nakayama）谋杀案“内幕”，不过是一份“表面供词”，通过闪烁其词和阴谋手段，使谋杀案的枝节仍深深隐藏在虹口黑社会的迷雾中。47岁的广东人杨文涛（Yang Wen-tao，音译）与日本领事警察手中那名仅被称为“杰克”的神秘囚犯之间究竟有何关联（如果有的话），目前尚不清楚——或者至少被日方严密 guarded。易海森（Yih Hai-sen，音译）在去年11月9日杀害日军准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）一案中所扮演的角色，据他昨日所述，被认为只有小部分属实。

“小广东”昨日下午在公开法庭上承认伙同谋杀，指认杨是在达罗克路（Darroch Road）开枪击倒一名日本军官并引发教堂人群恐慌的凶手。他还声称，那名所谓的朝鲜人“杰克”是团伙中的第三名成员。但杨断然否认警方的指控以及易的所有陈述，宣称自己与此事毫无瓜葛。这是在工部局警务处（S.M.P.）警官在正式提出谋杀指控后提供的不利间接证据面前做出的表态。

“杰克”是个谜

今日的注意力再次转向人们认为“杰克”在犯罪中所扮演的角色。此人由日本警官在青岛逮捕，最初被描述为朝鲜人。然而，“杰克”（并非其真名）据称出生于俄罗斯，去年才从符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostok）来到中国。日本领事警察不知道或不愿透露他的真实姓名。他不懂朝鲜语，日语也说得结结巴巴。

他仍在日本警察总部受到严密看守。他是否曾出庭日本领事法院，是否已做出供认，均为总部保守的秘密。日本人昨晚解除了对日本报纸的新闻禁令，这些报纸刊登了今早特区法院听证会的报道，但未提及“杰克”。因此，新闻禁令仅部分解除，报纸仅可刊登特区法院的诉讼程序。本案的第三个人物仍然隐没在背景阴影之中。

动机成谜

此外，警方对犯罪动机仍感到困惑，尽管今日普遍看法是政治犯罪的可能性微乎其微，中山被杀是他本人与“杰克”之间私人争吵的结果，后者随后可能招募了臭名昭著的虹口黑社会常客来帮助他对付敌人。“小广东”是这样的人物，这一点几乎毋庸置疑；杨所扮演的角色仍然模糊不清。这个人，至少在表面上，多年来一直是中国轮船公司（China Navigation Company）的忠实雇员，并且是其同乡公会中一个慈善协会的主席。

在易昨日供认后，杨在否认指控时宣称，自己是警方栽赃陷害的无辜受害者。

易称，当晚他在月宫舞厅（Moon Palace Cabaret）遇见杨和“杰克”，并被要求随他们去“杀一个人”。他否认知晓要杀的是谁，或为何要杀人。他说他随同前往，看见杨从一本书中取出手枪，向达罗克路上的一名男子开枪，随后三人四散而逃。

杨是“替罪羊”

杨坚持认为自己在本案中成了“替罪羊”。昨日提出的针对他的警方证据包括：在杨家中发现一本挖空以藏匿手枪的书；以及证人曾元（Tseng Yuen，音译）提供的证词，称在犯罪现场发现的手枪属于杨。通过弹道专家的证词，杨的不在场证明在法庭上或多或少被警方瓦解。

另有说法称，在中山被杀之前，易非常贫穷，只是虹口咖啡馆里的依附者，但事后他突然有了钱，去了青岛并在那里买下了一家舞厅。易辩解说，这笔钱是他母亲和未婚妻给的，她们于几天前获释。

第三名广东人陈永森（Chen Yung-sen，音译）将于今日获释，因缺乏警方证据，针对他的指控已被撤销。

案件听证会将于下周三继续举行，由法官钱洪业（Chien Hung-nieh，音译）主审，陪审法官冯世泽（Feng Shih-tsh，音译）和邵世凤（Shaw Shih-feng，音译）陪同。

144207
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, MAY 2, 1936

DARROCH RD. CRIME
OF NOVEMBER 9
Two Suspects Charged with
Murder of Japanese
ONE TELLS HIS PART IN
NAKAYAMA SHOOTING

Two of the three Chinese arrested as suspects in connection with the murder, on November 9 last year, of the Japanese Warrant Officer, H. Nakayama, in Darroch Road, were charged in the First Special District Court, yesterday. The accused were Yang Ven-tao and Yih Hai-sen, the latter being nicknamed "Little Cantonese." The third suspect, Zung Yoong-sen, is not to be charged, the police said. After a hearing which lasted three hours, it was adjourned till next Wednesday. The ban on reporting the case was lifted yesterday.

The prosecution was conducted by Mr. Robert T. Bryan, the Municipal Advocate, with Mr. Paul Y. Ru assisting. According to the prosecution, the shot which killed the Japanese marine was fired by Yang, while the second accused assisted in the commission of the crime. The police searched Yang's home and found a foreign book, the middle part of which had been removed in order to conceal the "P.B." pistol which was used to kill the Japanese. Yang, however, stated at the police station that, although he had a pistol, it was not a "P.B." weapon, but a "Demon" pistol, and that the book was used to conceal the "Demon" pistol. When the "Demon" pistol was put into the book, it did not fit.

Prisoner's Admission

Admission of his part in the crime was made by Yih Hai-sen, who told the Judge that, on November 7, Yang wrote him a letter, asking him to meet him at his home, but he did not go. On the evening of November 9, he met Yang outside the Moon Palace Cabaret, North Szechuen Road, near Jukong Road, where Yang told him that he wanted to kill a Japanese, but did not mention whom, or why he wished to commit the crime. This was about 7 p.m. and a Korean named "Jack" accompanied Yang at that time.

He, Yang, and the Korean went along North Szechuen Road, and when they reached Darroch Road he saw a Japanese marine. Yang opened a book he carried, produced a pistol, and fired a shot. They then escaped in different directions.

Shown the book which had been produced in Court by the police, Yih said it was the one Yang carried.

Yang made an emphatic denial to the charge, saying that he was falsely implicated by the other accused and he did not know anything about the shooting. The book the police found at his home was not his. He also denied having written a letter to the accused and said he had never been to the Moon Palace Cabaret, and he did not know the Korean mentioned. As a matter of fact, on November 9 he was in an Urga Road house from 3 p.m. to about 11 p.m. and he had two witnesses to prove it.

Pistol for Loan

Eight witnesses gave evidence for the prosecution, these being Det.-Sub-Inspr. Crowther, officers from the arms identification section and finger-print department, three Japanese officers of the S.M. Police, and two Chinese, named Tseng Yuen and Tsang Zai-yuan. Tseng Yuen said that Yih Hai-sen once wished to get a loan from him, with a pistol as security, and he refused. The pistol was similar to that produced in Court.

Tsang Zai-yuan said that, on the night of November 9, when he was walking along North Szechuen Road, he saw Yih Hai-sen, the Korean named "Jack," and another man, and, shortly after, a report was circulated that a Japanese marine had been murdered.

An officer from the arms identification section said the pistol found near the scene of the shooting was that used to kill the Japanese.
pages.zh:
144207
《字林西报》，1936年5月2日，星期六

11月9日达罗克路
犯罪案
两名嫌疑人被控
谋杀日本人
一人讲述其在
中山枪击案中的角色

去年11月9日，日本准尉H. 中山（H. Nakayama）在达罗克路被谋杀，与此案有关而被捕的三名中国人中的两人，昨日在第一特区法院被起诉。被告为杨文涛（Yang Ven-tao，音译）和易海森（Yih Hai-sen，音译），后者绰号“小广东”。警方表示，第三名嫌疑人钟永森（Zung Yoong-sen，音译）将不被起诉。经过三小时的听证会后，庭审延期至下周三。对该案报道的禁令于昨日解除。

公诉由市公廨律师罗伯特·T·布莱恩（Robert T. Bryan）先生进行，保罗·Y·鲁（Paul Y. Ru，音译）先生协助。根据公诉方说法，杀死日本海军陆战队员的一枪由杨射出，而第二被告协助实施了犯罪。警方搜查了杨的家，发现一本外文书，其中间部分被挖去，以藏匿用于杀害日本人的“P.B.”牌手枪。然而，杨在警察局称，虽然他有一把手枪，但不是“P.B.”牌武器，而是一把“恶魔”（Demon）牌手枪，那本书是用来藏匿“恶魔”牌手枪的。当把“恶魔”牌手枪放入书中时，并不合适。

囚犯的供述

易海森承认其在犯罪中的角色，他告诉法官，11月7日，杨给他写了一封信，约他在家见面，但他没有去。11月9日晚，他在北四川路靠近菊康路（Jukong Road，音译）的月宫舞厅外遇见杨，杨告诉他想杀一个日本人，但未提及是谁，也未说明为何要实施犯罪。当时大约是晚上7点，一名叫“杰克”的朝鲜人当时与杨在一起。

他、杨和那个朝鲜人沿着北四川路走去，到达达罗克路时，他看见一名日本海军陆战队员。杨打开随身携带的一本书，取出一把手枪，开了一枪。随后他们向不同方向逃跑。

看到警方在法庭上出示的那本书，易说那就是杨携带的那本。

杨坚决否认指控，称自己被其他被告诬陷，他对枪击一事一无所知。警方在他家中发现的书不是他的。他还否认曾给被告写过信，并称自己从未去过月宫舞厅，也不认识提到的那个朝鲜人。事实上，11月9日下午3点至晚上11点左右，他一直在乌尔加路（Urga Road，音译）的一所房子里，并有两名证人可以证明。

手枪借贷

八名证人为公诉方作证，他们是副督察克劳瑟（Crowther）侦探、武器识别科和指纹科的警官、三名工部局警务处的日本警官，以及两名中国人，名为曾元（Tseng Yuen，音译）和庄在源（Tsang Zai-yuan，音译）。曾元说，易海森曾希望向他借款，并以一把手枪作为抵押，但他拒绝了。那把手枪与法庭上出示的手枪相似。

庄在源说，11月9日晚，当他沿北四川路行走时，看见了易海森、名叫“杰克”的朝鲜人和另一名男子，不久后，便流传出日本海军陆战队员被谋杀的消息。

武器识别科的一名警官表示，在枪击现场附近发现的手枪就是用于杀害日本人的那把。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, MAY 2, 1936

"Shao Kwangtung" Puts
Blame For Shooting On
Yang In Admitting Crime

Tells Court That He Was Present At Scene Of
Murder Of Japanese Marine, Saw Yang Take
Out Pistol, Heard Shot, Then Ran Away

YANG DENIES EVERYTHING; KOREAN
SAID TO HAVE BEEN PRESENT

Admitting that he himself was present at the scene of
the crime, Yih Hai-sen alias "Shao Kwangtung," 28-year-old
alleged Hongkew underworld figure, implicated Yang Wen-
tao, 42-year-old Cantonese former employee of the China
Navigation Company, in the actual killing of Warrant Officer
Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Force on
Darroch Road at 9 p.m. on November 9, last in a confession
made in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon.
Formal charges of murder were framed against the two
men at the first public hearing of the trial, the veil of secrecy
surrounding all the inquiries of the Settlement, Chinese and
Japanese authorities being lifted for the first time since the
arrest of the men about two weeks ago. The filled court
room resembled a cross between an armed camp and a
diplomatic gathering with representatives of all interested
parties being present.

Yang in his turn upon being
brought before the presiding
judges for questioning, emphatic-
ally denied any connection with
the crime and stated that on the
particular evening he was not
anywhere near the scene of the
crime nor had he met "Shao
Kwangtung" on that day. With
the mystery being more or less
cleared with the statement made
in court yesterday by "Shao
Kwangtung" the authorities are
still at a loss as to the motive of
the crime.

Korean To Appear

The Korean named Jack, now
held by the Japanese authorities,
who "Shao Kwangtung" stated
was with him and Yang at the
time of the shooting will be
brought as a witness before the
Chinese tribunal on Wednesday
afternoon when the next hearing
of the case will be held. It has
been rumoured that this Korean
was the actual instigator of the
murder, as it is believed that he
and the murdered officer had a
quarrel over a woman or that Jack
nursed a grudge against the
Japanese Marine as the latter had
replaced him as the lover of some
woman.
