1936年4月28日。下午译件。

法官随后传唤证人张在源，其作如下陈述：
“去年11月9日半夜，我在北四川路的月宫饭店看见小广东（指着叶海生）。小广东、一名叫杰克（Chi Kuh，音译）的朝鲜人以及另一名我不认识的人离开了月宫饭店。小广东先走出来，朝鲜人和另一名中国人跟在后面。几分钟后，据报道一名日本海军陆战队员在达罗克路（Darroch Road）被杀。不久之后，小广东和另外两人一起回来，他们看起来非常慌张。因此，我认为他们与日本海军陆战队员被杀案有关。”
证人曾元作如下陈述：
“我是一名小规模放贷者。非常贫穷的小广东（指着叶海生）向我借款约30元。我以除非提供担保人否则不能放款为由，拒绝向他贷款。后来，小广东告诉我，他找不到人做他的担保人，但他有一把手枪可以抵押。我拒绝接受他的手枪作为抵押。”
经萧法官讯问，被告作如下陈述：
叶海生：“虽然我以前很穷，但我比曾元有钱。后来，因为我的情妇通过跳舞赚了很多钱，我变得更加富有。我从未向曾元借过钱，也没有给他任何手枪作为担保。我认识那个叫杰克的朝鲜人。我们曾打过一次架，因为我拒绝借给他50美元。他没有给我任何手枪。关于杀害日本海军陆战队员一事，我是完全无辜的。”
杨文道：“我是同仁协会（Doong Zung Association）的组织者。这是一个慈善组织。虹口区的大多数居民都知道我是个好人。民国二十二年（1933年），我向朋友借了一把手枪。那既不是‘P.B.’牌手枪，也不是警方发现的那一把。那把手枪在同年就还给了我的朋友。警方现在作为证物出示的那本中间挖空的中国书不属于我。以前我确实有一本中间挖空的书用来藏手枪，但那本书是英文的。我这样做是为了防止孩子乱动手枪；我没有非法意图。我对杀害日本海军陆战队员一事一无所知。”
陈荣生：“我在同仁协会受雇为仆人。我不知道杨先生（杨文道）是否有手枪。我对杀害日本海军陆战队员一事一无所知。”
此时，下午3时45分，鉴于警方尚未完成调查，萧法官认为需要再次还押。辩护律师顾肇基随即请求法庭尽可能缩短还押期限，因为被告已被拘留很长时间，而警方无法

After the order for the remand was given, lawyer
Kuh Chao Chi asked for permission to read the statements

Sin Wan Pao publishes the following letter dated April 27
from the Bureau of Social Affairs:-

"In connection with the killing of Japanese
marine Nakayama, to-day's newspapers publish reports to
the effect that Yang Vung Tao is the director of the Doong
Zoong Association and that a "registration certificate
issued by the Bureau of Social Affairs" or a "certificate
of permission for registration" in respect of the said
Doong Zung Association has been found by the Police.
"Our records show that Yang Vung Tao was the
organizer of a Hoong Zung Mutual Aid Society (洪顺互助会).
This society was ordered by this Bureau on March 19, 1935
to be disorganized and the registration certificate for
the society has been returned to the Bureau.
"As regards the Doong Zung Association, this
Bureau addressed a letter on March 12, 1935 to the local
Tangpu requesting them to give this organization their
attention. A letter (No.4167) dated March 27, 1935,
was received from the Tangpu in reply to this stating that
the Association had been notified to the effect that its

"As the reports in the papers vary from the
facts, this Bureau requests that you rectify them."

Eastern Times (Hsuchow telegram):

A "CERTAIN NATION" SMUGGLES GOODS INTO THE INTERIOR

Smuggled goods of a "certain nation" have been
transported as much as possible into the interior.
Recently, a large number of merchants of a "certain nation"
came to Hsuchow and other cities to dispose of these smuggled
goods.
At noon April 27, Takahashi and 5 others arrived
at Hsuchow from Tientsin, while Kim Myung Sub (金明洙)
and 2 other Koreans reached here in the evening of April 26
to make necessary arrangements with the various piece
goods hongs.
On the morning of April 26 Okamune (?) and 4
others arrived here from Tientsin on their way to Honan,
Shense, Kiangsu and Anhwei provinces where they will
dispose of the smuggled goods.

提供充分证据证明被告与犯罪有关。案件被还押至5月1日（星期五）下午2时。
下达还押令后，顾肇基律师请求允许阅读被告的供词。法庭书记员丁（Ting，音译）向律师宣读了供词，随后法官退庭。三名嫌疑人在中、日及外籍侦探和警察的押解下，连同作为证据查获的皮箱及其他物品，被带回中央捕房拘留。

《新闻报》刊登了社会局4月27日的如下信函：

“关于日本海军陆战队员中山被杀一事，今日各报刊登报道，称杨文道是同仁协会的主任，且警方发现了该同仁协会的‘社会局颁发的注册证书’或‘注册许可证’。
“我局记录显示，杨文道是洪顺互助会（Hoong Zung Mutual Aid Society）的组织者。该局于1935年3月19日命令解散该会，该会的注册证书已交回我局。
“至于同仁协会，我局于1935年3月12日致函当地党部，请其关注该组织。党部于1935年3月27日复函（第4167号），称已通知该会，当局不允许其存在。
“由于报纸报道与事实不符，我局请予更正。”

《字林西报》（徐州电）：

“某国”走私货物入内地

“某国”的走私货物已尽可能多地运往内地。最近，大量“某国”商人来到徐州和其他城市处理这些走私货物。
4月27日中午，高桥（Takahashi）等5人从天津抵达徐州，而金明洙（Kim Myung Sub）等2名朝鲜人于4月26日晚抵达此处，与各布匹行号进行必要的安排。
4月26日上午，Okamune（?，原文不清）等4人从天津抵达此处，途经河南、陕西、江苏和安徽各省，将在这些地方处理走私货物。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, TUESDAY, APRIL 26, 1938

Apparent Lack Of Motive For
Murder Puzzles Police

Three Accused In Nakayama Case Appear In Fresh
Hearing Behind Guard Doors; Adjournment
For Fortnight; No Charge Yet Laid

With armed police barring the entrance to the court-room, permitting only prisoners, police officers and counsel to pass, the three Chinese held in connection with the Nakayama murder case, appeared before District Court judges for further in camera proceedings yesterday.

It is now known, from an authoritative source, that no charge has yet been definitely laid against any of the men, who remain held upon a writ of detention.

Police are hampered, it is understood, by the apparent lack of motive for the crime, and it is believed that yesterday's hearing, taking the form of a preliminary investigation, terminated with a police request for an adjournment for a fortnight to enable them to pursue further lines of inquiry.

This, it is also believed, was granted.

Yih Hai-sen, one of the three held, is being represented by Mr. Wang Shih-chung, who told "The Shanghai Times" that nothing important transpired during the hearing yesterday.

Alleged Identification

One witness, however is reported to have identified Yih as one of a group of three men whom he saw walking along North Szechuen Road in a northerly direction on the night of November 9 last year and whom he saw returning hurriedly some little time later. He did not, however, hear any shot fired.

The precincts of the District Court were crowded during the period of the hearing, many relatives and friends of the arrested men being present. They were not allowed to approach when the accused were brought down to be returned to cells in the "Black Maria."

Yih Hai-sen was attired in a black tunic with yellow trousers and Chinese shoes. The other two wore black overcoats and foreign-style shoes.

《上海泰晤士报》，1938年4月26日，星期二

谋杀动机明显缺乏令警方困惑

中山案三名被告在警卫门后出席新一轮听证；休庭两周；尚未正式起诉

武装警察把守法庭入口，仅允许囚犯、警官和律师通行，与中山谋杀案有关的三名中国人在昨日出庭，在地方法院法官面前进行了进一步的闭门诉讼程序。

据权威消息来源获悉，目前尚未对任何人正式提出指控，这些人仍依据拘留令被羁押。

据悉，警方因犯罪动机明显缺乏而受阻，据信昨日的听证会以初步调查的形式进行，最终以警方请求休庭两周告终，以便他们 pursue further lines of inquiry（开展进一步的调查线索）。

据信，这一请求已获批准。

三名被拘者之一的叶海森（Yih Hai-sen，即叶海生）由王士宗先生代理，王告诉《上海泰晤士士报》，昨日听证期间未发生重要事项。

指认指控

然而，据报道有一名证人指认叶是去年11月9日晚他在北四川路向北行走的三人小组中的一员，并看到他们在稍后匆忙返回。但是，他没有听到任何枪声。

听证期间，地方法院周围挤满了人，被捕者的许多亲友在场。当被告被带下楼送回“黑玛丽亚”（警车）牢房时，他们不被允许靠近。

叶海森身穿黑色上衣、黄色裤子和中式鞋子。另外两人身穿黑色大衣和西式鞋子。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, April 25, 1936
D. 703

"Officialdom" Lifts Press Ban
On Udopia's Crown Mystery;
Pours Out Heart To Reporter

Authorities Break All Records By Issuing Two
Sentences In Two Days On Burning Question;
Newsman To Padded Cell After Interview

THE padded cell in the men's ward of the Municipal Mental Hospital is today occupied by a representative of the Chapel Afternoon Post-Press-Times-News. He was taken with a violent seizure in the editorial offices late yesterday and was rushed to hospital in an ambulance, guarded by a squad of officers. He is under observation and is reported to be a little quieter, but physicians have not yet ascertained the exact nature of or cause for his aberrations.

He had been typing rapidly at his machine just before the attack and several sheets of copy were left scattered on his desk. The uncompleted story follows:

Statement Issued

"I have nothing to say regarding the matter." General Percival Ricardo Heinrich Cholmondeley-Ealesky, X.O.B., C.O.D., A.D.C., A.A.A., P.H.D., S.M.C., commissioner of the Bureau of International Inquiry into Political Incidents in the International Settlement of the Greater Concession of Shanghai, declared to a representative (bought and paid for) of the Chapel Afternoon Post-Press-Times-News, then questioned this morning regarding the mystery of the missing crown of the Kingdom Of Udopia, reported to have been stolen from the local Udopian Embassy by a beautiful American girl named F. Ritz.

"Is it true, General P.R.H.C.-S. that the girl has been located in the Municipal Dog Kennels at Gordon Road Police Station?" he was asked.

"H'm," said the commissioner. Is the girl's name Ritz, or is it Ztir? If Ztir, is she in stir?"

"Never heard of tzir," the commissioner barked.

In The Soup

'Can you tell me if the missing crown of the Kingdom of Udopia, sought so frantically by King Konrad, is being used for a soup tureen in the officers' mess of the Russian Regiment, S.V.C.?"

"Hrummp," the commissioner gargled.

"Can you tell me, then, if the Udopian Embassy has lodged a charge of grand larceny against Miss Ritz, or Tzir?"

"Never heard of it."

"Is there a Udopian Embassy in Shanghai?"

"I don't know."

"Where is Udopia?"

"I have the records in the files of the office, but I certainly cannot allow the Press to see my private geography books."

"Can you tell me nothing about this case?"

"I didn't know there was any case. What case?"

"It's been in the newspapers for days."

"Never read the newspapers."

Brains Puzzled

"It's been in your private files for weeks."

"Never read my private files."

"I understand that officers have been puzzling their brains for weeks on this mystery, commissioner."

"Young man, officers of this department never puzzle their brains. I don't know anything. Besides, there is a clause in my contract which forbids me to give out any information whatsoever regarding anything that has any interest, directly or indirectly, to the public and the taxpayers of this city who employ me at a whacking fine salary to keep secrets from the newspapers. If you want to continue being a pest, go and obtain your information from the Press Information Office of the I.S.G.C.S."

"But the Press Information Officers of the I.S.G.C.S. also have similar contracts forbidding them to give out any information."

"Hrummph. Good day."

Cakes And Crowns

Mr. X. Y. Nip, of Nip & Tuck, private investigators, did not know anything either about the case, when interviewed.

"What the public doesn't know won't hurt it," Mr. Nip said. "Let them eat cake. You can't have your cake and eat it too."

"Was there a well-organized plot engineered by the Udopian Embassy to steal the crown back from Miss Ritz?" he was asked.

"The company submitted," Mr. Nip said, lighting a cigar, "that it had effected all possible economies in construction and operation, consistent with good service, but that the net returns were inadequate, and under the conditions then existing were likely to remain so. It was stated that the net return on the capital invested was in 1934 equivalent to 6.13 per cent and that in order to increase this figure to 10 per cent it was estimated that an overall increase in gross revenues amounting to 29.89 per cent was required. To achieve this it was...."

To The Point

"Is there any verification of the rumor that Miss Ritz has committed suicide, Mr. Nip?"

That's all I have to say on the subject. But don't quote me."

Mr. Eric John Pierre Fritz Pedro Dmitri Phillpot, chairman of the Municipal House of Deputies of the I.S.G.C.S., said, in answer to an inquiry regarding the inquiry: "I am in favor of giving the widest possible publicity to municipal activities, as I stated in my pre-election statement to voters. Good afternoon."

A ricsha coolie, Yang Yang-yang, P.M.A.A., suspected of having seen a foreign woman riding in a tramcar carrying golden crown on the night of November 9, 1935, was located by a fluke. "No can talkee Ingrish," the coolie said. "No quotee my."

Quotes Filed Off

A significant factor in this case is that on all office typewriters in municipal offices, the quotation mark keys have been filed off by an engineer of the Public Labors Bureau.

When questioned by a representative of the Chapel Afternoon Post-Press-Times-News this morning, a representative of the Chapel Afternoon Post-Press-Times-News said, "Pardon me for breathing municipal air, but I am a representative of the Chapel Afternoon Post - Press - Times - News. Please don't quote me, but spell my name right!"

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年4月25日，星期六
D. 703

“官场”解除对乌多皮亚王冠谜案的新闻禁令；
向记者吐露心声

当局在两天内就这一热点问题连发两句声明，打破纪录；
记者在采访后被送入软禁病房

市立精神病院男病房的软禁病房今天住进了一位《教堂午后邮报-出版社-时报-新闻》的代表。他在昨天傍晚于编辑部突发剧烈痉挛，随后在一队警员的看守下，由救护车紧急送往医院。他目前正接受观察，据称情绪稍显平静，但医生尚未查明其精神异常的确切性质或原因。

发病前，他正在打字机上快速打字，几页稿纸散落在他的办公桌上。这篇未完成的故事如下：

发布的声明

“对此事我无可奉告。”大上海公共租界国际政治事件调查局局长珀西瓦尔·里卡多·海因里希·乔蒙德利-伊尔斯基将军（Percival Ricardo Heinrich Cholmondeley-Ealesky），X.O.B.勋爵，C.O.D.勋爵，A.D.C.副官，A.A.A.会员，哲学博士，工部局委员，向《教堂午后邮报-出版社-时报-新闻》的一位代表（已收买并付酬）宣称，随后在今早被问及关于乌多皮亚王国（Kingdom Of Udopia）失踪王冠的谜案时发表了上述言论，该王冠据报被一名名叫F.里茨（F. Ritz）的美国美女从当地的乌多皮亚大使馆盗走。

“P.R.H.C.-S.将军，有说法称该女孩已在戈登路警察局的市立狗舍中被找到，这是真的吗？”有人问道。

“嗯，”局长说道。“这女孩的名字是里茨（Ritz），还是齐蒂尔（Ztir）？如果是齐蒂尔，她是不是在坐牢（in stir）？”

“从来没听说过‘tzir’这个词，”局长厉声说道。

陷入困境

“能否告诉我，康拉德国王（King Konrad）如此急切寻找的乌多皮亚王国失踪王冠，是否正被俄国志愿队（S.V.C.）军官食堂用作汤盆？”

“呼噜姆普，”局长发出咕噜声。

“那么，能否告诉我，乌多皮亚大使馆是否已以重大盗窃罪起诉里茨小姐，或者齐蒂尔小姐？”

“从未听说此事。”

“上海有乌多皮亚大使馆吗？”

“我不知道。”

“乌多皮亚在哪里？”

“我办公室的档案里有记录，但我当然不能让新闻界查看我的私人地理书籍。”

“关于这个案子，你就不能透露一点消息吗？”

“我都不知道有什么案子。什么案子？”

“报纸上已经刊登好几天了。”

“从不看报。”

脑筋困惑

“在你的私人档案里已经放了好几个星期了。”

“从不看我的私人档案。”

“据我所知，警官们为这个谜案已经绞尽脑汁好几个星期了，局长先生。”

“年轻人，本部门的警官从不绞尽脑汁。我一无所知。此外，我的合同中有一项条款，禁止我发布任何与本市公众和纳税人直接或间接感兴趣的任何事情有关的信息，他们支付我极高的薪水就是为了让我对报纸保守秘密。如果你还想继续当个讨厌鬼，就去大上海公共租界（I.S.G.C.S.）的新闻发布处获取信息吧。”

“但是大上海公共租界的新闻发布官也有类似的合同，禁止他们发布任何信息。”

“呼噜姆夫。再见。”

蛋糕与王冠

在接受采访时，“捏与扯”（Nip & Tuck）私人侦探社的X. Y.尼普（X. Y. Nip）先生也表示对该案一无所知。

“公众不知道的事情不会伤害他们，”尼普先生说。“让他们吃蛋糕吧。你不可能既拥有蛋糕又吃掉它。”

“是否有由乌多皮亚大使馆策划的、旨在从里茨小姐手中偷回王冠的周密阴谋？”有人问道。

“本公司提出，”尼普先生点燃一支雪茄说道，“它在建设和运营方面已实现了所有可能的节约，同时保持了良好的服务，但净回报不足，且在当时条件下可能仍将如此。据悉，1934年投入资本的净回报率为6.13%，为了将这一数字提高到10%，估计总收入需要整体增加29.89%。为了实现这一目标……”

切入正题

“尼普先生，有关于里茨小姐自杀的传闻得到证实了吗？”

这就是我对这个话题要说的全部。但不要引用我的话。”

大上海公共租界市议会主席埃里克·约翰·皮埃尔·弗里茨·佩德罗·德米特里·菲尔波特（Eric John Pierre Fritz Pedro Dmitri Phillpot）先生在回答关于该调查的询问时说：“正如我在选前对选民的声明中所说，我主张尽可能广泛地宣传市政活动。下午好。”

一位名叫杨洋洋（Yang Yang-yang）、P.M.A.A.的黄包车夫，因涉嫌在1935年11月9日晚看到一名外国女子乘坐电车并携带金色王冠而被偶然找到。“不会说英语，”该车夫说。“别引用我的话。”

引号键被锉掉

此案的一个重要因素是，市政机关办公室的所有打字机上的引号键均已被工务局的一名工程师锉掉。

今早，当《教堂午后邮报-出版社-时报-新闻》的一位代表接受《教堂午后邮报-出版社-时报-新闻》另一位代表的提问时，他说：“请原谅我呼吸市政空气，但我是《教堂午后邮报-出版社-时报-新闻》的代表。请不要引用我的话，但要把我的名字拼写正确！”

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, APRIL 26, 1936
MYSTERY! SECRECY! SILENCE!
High Officials In Daily
Conference Over Strange
Murder Of W.O. Nakayama
Three Chinese Closely Guarded As Suspects; Korean
Believed Involved; But British, Japanese, Chinese
Authorities Enforce Strict Ban On Developments
WHAT WAS BEHIND BRUTAL KILLING OF
JAPANESE OFFICER ON NOVEMBER 9?
The Press, public and even police, outside a select inner
circle, are to-day asking what was behind the brutal killing
of Hideo Nakayama, Japanese Warrant Officer attached to
the Japanese Naval Landing Party, on Darroch Road on
the night of November 9, last year.
It is freely asserted that a political motive was behind
the murder.
The police neither deny nor confirm this. But what-
ever the motive, whatever the circumstances surrounding
the crime, they are obviously of sufficient gravity to have
prompted an official silence and a press ban the like of which
has not been hitherto encountered locally.
Who killed Nakayama and why?
The victim was shot dead from
behind by an unknown assassin or
group of assassins on the night of
November 9, on Darroch Road, a
short distance from the Japanese
Barracks. A pistol from which
the fatal bullet was fired was
picked up a stone's throw from
the body. There were no eye-
witnesses to the killing of suffi-
cient reliability to assist the police
in their investigations, although a
Chinese "sweep" was detained, but
subsequently released when he
denied having witnessed anything
connected with the crime.
Far-Reaching Effects
But the effects of Nakayama's
death on the Japanese community
were such that a crisis in Sino-
Japanese relations of considerable
magnitude resulted. Rumours of
Japanese reprisals and the possi-
bility of another Chapei Incident
resulted in a general exodus of
Chinese from the area believed
imperilled. An anti-Japanese de-
monstration followed on Nanking
Road within a couple of days of
the shooting. Anti-Japanese hand-
bills were distributed in the city.
And the murder assumed the
proportions of a major incident.
The question was then asked,
and is still being asked, whether
the assassination of Nakayama
had been plotted for the purpose
of precipitating a crisis in Sino-
Japanese relations? Was there a
political motive in the shooting to
death of the Japanese sailor?
In the arrests of the three
Chinese a few days ago by Settle-
ment police and the detention of
a Korean in connection with the
November murder, there was no-
thing unusual. They came as the
outcome of careful investigations
by the police who have been seek-
ing the murderer for more than
six months.
But if the police believe they
hold the men directly or indirectly
responsible for the crime, and that
crime was committed as the result
of a quarrel, for the purpose of
robbery or, possibly, as the out-
come of jealousy, why is the case
shrouded with so much extra-
ordinary secrecy and mystery?
Why have the Japanese and
Chinese press been forbidden to
publish anything regarding the
case (with one exception) and why
have the police persistently refus-
ed to disclose anything regarding
the progress or lack of progress
in their investigations?
Japanese Press Ban
So strict is the Japanese press
ban that one Japanese correspond-
ent who dared to cable to Japan
a message relating to the case has
been sent back to Japan. Yet, at
the time of the murder, unusual
publicity was given the crime in
the Japanese press.
What has since been discovered
that has altered the complexion of
the case sufficiently to bring about
this press ban?
It has been freely hinted that
the men in the custody of the
S.M.P., although connected with
the crime, may not have actually
been at the scene of the shooting;
that there is an organization which
had connived the murder for
political purposes and that the
ramifications of that organization
extends beyond this city. That if
any of the men now in custody
actually committed the murder, he
was acting under instructions from
persons higher up.
And that the disclosures of
statements alleged to have been
made by the prisoners might have
repercussions the extent of which
it is difficult to define at this stage.
Such are the current rumours.
To those who have any know-
ledge of police procedure it is
well-known that any straight-
forward murder or major crime,
when once the police are sure of
their ground, does not warrant the
inordinate secrecy which has grown
round the Nakayama case. The
inference is drawn that there is
something much deeper behind the
killing than jealousy, robbery or
a grudge.
Behind Locked Doors
Representatives of the Japanese
and Chinese authorities do not
usually confer with the Shanghai
Municipal Police officers behind
closed and locked doors to keep
from the public details of a
murder. Not, of course, unless
there is something sinisterly
significant in that murder and its
motive. Yet these precautions
have been taken during the past
week and officials have declined to
offer any explanation nor give any
indication of the extent of their
investigations. Even the prelimin-
ary hearing of the charge against
the Chinese was held in secret in
the Shanghai District Court and
the precaution taken to see that
the records did not pass through
the judicial channels.
This procedure is only adopted
in the cases of highly important
political trials or trials in which
prisoners are involved whose
statements might affect inter-
national relations.
The question is being asked
whether statements or disclosures
of such a nature have not been
made by the prisoners.
Pistol Identified
One of the Chinese now in
custody is known in the Hongkew
District as Siau Kuantung ("Little
Kuantung) and his arrest was
effected in Tsingtao by Japanese
police representatives. It was
upon information supplied by
another Chinese named Tseng
Yuan that "Little Kuantung" was
taken into custody. The informant
at the time of giving the informa-
tion to the police identified the
pistol found at the scene of the
crime as one which had been in
the possession of "Little Kuan-
tung." It was a .32 calibre auto-
matic of Italian manufacture and
Tseng stated that he had once
loaned "Little Kuantung" money,
with the pistol as security. "Little
Kuantung" later redeemed the
weapon.
Two other Chinese were arrested
here and also a Korean. The part
they are alleged to have played
in the murder is not disclosed. Two
Chinese women who were taken
into custody for investigation have
been released.
It has been stated that one of
the hitches in the case is that of
jurisdiction and the legality of the
arrest made in Tsingtao, but the
police have had nothing to say on
that aspect of the case any more
than on any of the other unex-
plained reasons for their baffling
silence.

《上海星期泰晤士报》，1936年4月26日
谜团！保密！缄默！
高官每日开会研讨
中山（音译）中尉离奇被杀案
三名华人作为嫌疑人受到严密看守；据信有朝鲜人涉案；但英、日、中当局严格禁止披露案情进展
11月9日日本军官惨遭杀害的背后隐情是什么？
除了少数核心圈内人士外，新闻界、公众甚至警方今天都在问，去年11月9日晚，附属于日本海军陆战队的日本准尉中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）在达罗克路（Darroch Road）惨遭杀害的背后隐情是什么。
人们普遍声称，这起谋杀案背后有政治动机。
警方既未否认也未证实这一点。但无论动机如何，无论犯罪周围的情况如何，其性质显然足够严重，以至于引发了官方的沉默和新闻禁令，这种情形在当地此前从未遇到过。
谁杀了中山，为什么？
受害者于11月9日晚在达罗克路被一名或多名不明刺客从背后枪杀，该处距离日本兵营不远。发射致命子弹的手枪在距尸体一箭之遥的地方被发现。虽然一名中国“清道夫”曾被拘留，但他否认目睹任何与犯罪有关的事情后随即获释，因此没有足够可靠的目击者协助警方调查。
深远影响
但是，中山之死对日本社区的影响导致了相当规模的中日关系危机。关于日本报复以及另一次闸北事变可能性的谣言，导致中国人普遍认为该地区处于危险之中而纷纷逃离。枪击发生后两天内，南京路上发生了反日游行。市内散发了反日传单。这起谋杀案演变成了一起重大事件。
当时有人提出，现在仍在追问的问题是，刺杀中山是否是为了引发中日关系危机而策划的？枪杀这名日本水兵是否有政治动机？
几天前，租界警察逮捕了三名华人，并因涉及11月的谋杀案拘留了一名朝鲜人，这并无不寻常之处。这是警方六个多月来一直搜寻凶手并进行仔细调查的结果。
但是，如果警方相信他们掌握了直接或间接对犯罪负责的人，并且该犯罪是因争吵、抢劫目的或可能是出于嫉妒而实施的，那么为什么此案被笼罩在如此非同寻常的秘密和谜团之中？
为什么禁止日本和中国媒体发布任何关于此案的消息（除一个例外），为什么警方坚持拒绝披露其调查进展或缺乏进展的任何情况？
日本新闻禁令
日本的新闻禁令如此严格，以至于一名敢于向日本发送有关此案消息的日本记者已被遣返回日本。然而，在谋杀发生时，日本媒体对该罪行进行了不同寻常的大肆报道。
此后发现了什么，足以改变案件性质从而带来这一新闻禁令？
有人 freely 暗示，虽然被上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）羁押的人与犯罪有关，但他们可能实际上并未出现在枪击现场；有一个组织为了政治目的纵容了这起谋杀，且该组织的分支延伸到了本市之外。如果目前被羁押的人中有任何人实际实施了谋杀，他是按照上级人员的指示行事的。
而且，披露据称由囚犯作出的陈述可能会产生难以在此阶段界定的反响。
这些就是当前的谣言。
对于那些了解警察程序的人来说，众所周知，任何单纯的谋杀或重大犯罪，一旦警方确信其立场，就不需要围绕中山案产生的那种过度保密。由此推断，这起杀戮背后有着比嫉妒、抢劫或宿怨更深层的东西。
紧闭的门后
日本和中国当局的代表通常不会与上海公共租界工部局警务处的警官在关闭并锁上的门后开会，以向公众隐瞒谋杀案的细节。当然，除非该谋杀案及其动机具有某种险恶的重大意义。然而，在过去的一周里采取了这些预防措施，官员们拒绝提供任何解释，也不透露其调查范围的任何迹象。甚至针对华人的指控预审也在上海特区法院秘密举行，并采取了预防措施，确保记录不通过司法渠道流转。
这种程序仅在极其重要的政治审判或涉及囚犯陈述可能影响国际关系的审判中采用。
有人正在询问，囚犯是否没有作出此类性质的陈述或披露。
手枪已确认
目前在押的一名华人在虹口区被称为“小广东”（Siau Kuantung），他是由日本警察代表在青岛逮捕的。正是根据另一名名为曾元（Tseng Yuan，音译）的华人提供的信息，“小广东”才被拘留。线人在向警方提供信息时，指认在现场发现的手枪为“小广东”曾经拥有的一把。那是一把意大利制造的.32口径自动手枪，曾元表示他曾借钱给“小广东”，并以该手枪作为抵押。“小广东”后来赎回了该武器。
另外两名华人在此被捕，还有一名朝鲜人。据称他们在谋杀案中扮演的角色并未披露。两名被拘留调查的中国妇女已被释放。
据说，此案的一个症结在于管辖权以及在青岛逮捕的合法性问题，但警方对此方面以及对其令人困惑的沉默的其他未解释原因均未置评。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, APRIL 25, 1936

OWNER OF MURDER
PISTOL TRACED

Chinese Press Explains
Arrest of Three

WEAPON IDENTIFIED BY
PAWNBROKER

The official silence regarding the new developments in the Nakayama murder investigation continued yesterday, but the local Chinese press at the same time related certain alleged facts which would explain the arrests of the three Chinese now being held as suspects.

Hideo Nakayama, a Japanese marine, was shot dead in Darroch Road last November and within a few hours of the murder the pistol in the case was found in an alley-way leading off Darroch Road. Yesterday morning the "Sin Wan Pao," one of the largest Chinese dailies in Shanghai, published an article saying that the ownership of the weapon had been determined and that the owner is the Chinese who was arrested in Tsingtao and returned to Shanghai last week.

The pistol, a .32-calibre automatic of Italian manufacture, trapped its owner, according to the Chinese paper. Some time ago a Chinese informed the Settlement Police that he recalled a pistol similar to the one used, which he had seen in the possession of a Cantonese nicknamed "Siau Kuangtung" ("Little Kuangtung"). Siau Kuangtung once had pawned the weapon with another Cantonese, named Tseng Yuan, and the latter was consequently picked up by the Police for questioning.

Pistol Identified

At one of the police stations, the "Sin Wan Pao" further relates, Tseng Yuan was confronted with a number of different pistols and asked to pick out the one which had formerly been in his possession. Tseng Yuan without hesitation elected the weapon with which Nakayama had been murdered.

The next problem was to find Siau Kuangtung. After weeks of investigation it was learned that he had gone to Tsingtao, where he was subsequently arrested to be extradited to Shanghai.

Before Siau Kuangtung's return, the Police arrested two other suspects in Shanghai. Both are Chinese and in the room of one was found a foreign book the central part of which had been cut so as to allow a pistol to be concealed—a favourite device of arms runners. The pistol with which Nakayama was shot fitted perfectly into this book, according to the Chinese report. Therefore the occupant of the room was arrested, as was another man closely connected with him.

The case of the three suspects, which opened in the First Special District Court early this week, will continue on Monday morning.

The reasons for the deep secrecy with which all the officials concerned are surrounding the case have not been explained. When the Japanese marine was murdered, the Japanese news agencies started to issue columns of matter on the case, but now the Japanese press is silent. The Chinese authorities likewise have refused to comment.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年4月25日，星期六

谋杀用手枪所有者
已被追踪

中文报纸解释
三人被捕

典当商识别
武器

关于中山谋杀案调查新进展的官方沉默昨日仍在继续，但当地中文报纸同时叙述了一些所谓的事实，这些事实可以解释目前作为嫌疑人被拘留的三名华人的被捕。

日本海军陆战队员中山秀夫去年11月在达罗克路被枪杀，谋杀发生后几小时内，涉案手枪在达罗克路的一条小巷中被发现。昨天上午，上海最大的中文日报之一《新闻报》发表文章称，该武器的所有权已确定，所有者是上周在青岛被捕并送回上海的华人。

据该中文报纸称，这把意大利制造的.32口径自动手枪使其所有者落网。不久前，一名华人向租界警察报告说，他回忆起一把类似所用枪支的手枪，他曾看到它在一个绰号为“小广东”（Siau Kuangtung）的广东人手中。“小广东”曾将这把武器典当给另一名名为曾元（Tseng Yuan）的广东人，后者因此被警方带走问话。

手枪已确认

《新闻报》进一步报道，在一个警察局，曾元面对许多不同的手枪，并被要求挑出以前归他所有的那一把。曾元毫不犹豫地选出了用于谋杀中山的武器。

下一个问题是找到“小广东”。经过数周的调查，得知他已前往青岛，随后在那里被捕并被引渡回上海。

在“小广东”返回之前，警方在上海逮捕了另外两名嫌疑人。两人均为华人，在其中一人的房间里发现了一本外国书籍，其中间部分被挖空以便藏匿手枪——这是军火走私者常用的手段。据中文报道，射击中山的手枪完美地 fit 进这本书中。因此，该房间的居住者被捕，与他密切相关的另一人也一同被捕。

本周初在第一特区法院开庭审理的这三名嫌疑人的案件，将于周一上午继续审理。

所有相关官员对此案严加保密的原因尚未得到解释。当这名日本海军陆战队员被谋杀时，日本新闻机构开始发布大量关于此案的报道，但现在日本媒体保持沉默。中国当局也拒绝发表评论。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, APRIL 25, 1936

NAKAYAMA SUSPECTS
GRILLED AGAIN

Japanese Guard Kept As
Men Lie In Cells At
Central Station

Lights burned late in one of the offices opening into the compound of the Central Police Station last night as two male Chinese suspects in the mysterious killing of Hideo Nakayama, of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, in Darroch Road last November, underwent a long grilling. About 11 p.m. they were taken back to their cells, where Japanese constables of the S.M.P. are maintaining a day and night watch over them.

There were reports yesterday, unconfirmed of course, that the pistol found on that fateful night near the body of the murdered bluejacket had been identified as one pawned by a Cantonese in Hongkew. Wild stories of $50,000 paid to a gang for the assassination were also circulated.

Another hearing in the case will be held in the First Special District Court on Monday, it is reported, when the two male Chinese held at Central Station and two Chinese women held by the District Court will be questioned. A Korean is still in the custody of Japanese Consular Police.

* * *

Have a shrewd suspicion that there is less in this oyster mummery of the respective police departments in the Nakayama case developments than meets the eye. Heard it suggested in one quarter, who knows how reliable, that enthusiasm to make arrests may have caused some slight overlooking of the necessity for the production of convincing evidence. In short, it is hinted that the police have little "on" the suspects, other than suspicion. If that in any way represents even the partial truth, the lifting of the veil may find the police having difficulty in explaining why it was ever let down.

* * *

What is not generally known—but ought to be—in this business, is the rather unexpected belief in the power of the press indicated at headquarters. For instance, believe it or not, the particular special died-in-the-wool hush-hush department at Central—I must forbear revealing its exact location—has been pasted up with newspapers so that snooping reporters shall obtain no glimpse of the internal mysteries.

It is, of course, also a fact that newspapers are efficacious in keeping out moths.

* * *
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年4月25日，星期六

中山案嫌疑人
再次受审

日本人看守
中央捕房牢房中的
嫌疑人

昨晚，在通往中央捕房大院的一间办公室里，灯光亮到很晚，两名涉嫌去年11月在达罗克路神秘杀害日本海军陆战队队员中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）的男性华人嫌疑人接受了长时间的严厉审讯。晚上11点左右，他们被带回牢房，上海公共租界工部局警务处的日本巡捕正日夜看守着他们。

昨天有未经证实的报道说，在那位不幸遇害的水兵尸体附近发现的手枪已被确认为一名虹口广东人典当的物品。还流传着荒诞的故事，称支付给一个团伙5万美元用于实施刺杀。

据报道，周一将在第一特区法院举行另一次听证会，届时将讯问拘押在中央捕房的两名男性华人和由特区法院拘押的两名中国妇女。一名朝鲜人仍由日本领事警察羁押。

* * *

有一种敏锐的怀疑认为，在中山案的发展中，各警察部门这种故弄玄虚的做法背后，实际情况并不像表面看起来那样复杂。从一个不知可靠性如何的消息来源听到一种说法，即急于逮捕可能导致稍微忽视了提供确凿证据的必要性。简而言之，有人暗示警方除了怀疑之外，对嫌疑人几乎没有其他“实据”。如果这在某种程度上代表了部分真相，那么揭开面纱后，警方可能会发现很难解释当初为何要掩盖真相。

* * *

在这件事中，不为一般人所知——但应该为人所知——的是总部表现出的对媒体力量的出乎意料的重视。例如，信不信由你，中央捕房那个特别的、顽固的、专门负责保密的部门——我必须克制不透露其确切位置——已经贴满了报纸，以便窥探的记者无法瞥见内部的奥秘。

当然，报纸在防蛾方面也确实有效。

* * *

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, April 24, 1936

Nakayama Case
'Solved' Through
Gun Identifying

'Little Kwangtung' Said
To Have Pawned Pistol
Found Near Body

CABARET DANCERS
RELATED TO 'KING'

Mysterious Tseng Still
Sought As Witness;
Case Up Monday

Whether or not the pistol used in
the murder of Warrant Officer
Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese
Naval Landing Party on Darioch
Road on November 9 last year was
the same one which Yih Hi-sen,
better known in the Hongkew dis-
trict as "Shao (Little) Kwangtung,"
mortgaged for cash from Informant
Tseng Yuen earlier in 1935, is one
of the vital points being investigat-
ed by officers of the Shanghai
Municipal Police.

From the solid wall of official
secrecy, information has leaked out
that Informant Tseng Yuen, whose
presence in the First Special Dis-
trict Court at the next hearing of
the three suspects held in con-
nection with the murder has been
ordered by the judge, told the
police that the pistol found near
the body of the Japanese blue-
jacket was identical to the one
"Shao Kwangtung" pawned for a
loan. It was this statement that
led to the apprehension of the
Hongkew "cabaret-girl king" in
Tsingtao, it is reported.

Boek Concealed Gun

The two other Cantonese, both
named Chen, were arrested in
Shanghai by a separate group of
officers when comrades were putting
their handcuffs on "Shao Kwang-
tung" and Jack, believed to be a
Korean, held in connection with the
murder in the Japanese Consular
Police Headquarters in the Shau-
tung resort city. In the room of
one of the Chens was said to have
been found a volume which was
hollowed out in the center. The
hollow, it is reported, was found
to fit exactly the pistol used in the
murder of Nakayama. The other
Chen was arrested because they
are intimate friends, it is said.

At the time of the murder of
Nakayama, officers from the Japan-
ese Landing Party Headquarters
and the Dirwell Station of the
S.M.P. picked up a pistol bearing
the P.B. While ballistics experts
were busy studying the weapon, an
informant came to the police lured
by the substantial rewards issued
for the arrest of the murderer or
murderers. He reported that he
had seen a pistol of the same make
which "Shao Kwangtung" mortgag-
ed for cash from Tseng Yuen, also
a native of Kwangtung.

Picks Out Pistol

Tseng was immediately located
and brought to the station. A
number of pistols were placed in
front of him. Tseng was in-
structed to identify the pistol be-
longing to "Shao Kwangtung."
Tseng hesitated but finally picked
out a pistol and declared that it
was the property of the Hongkew
"king." The pistol was none other
than the one picked up at the scene
of the murder!

Tseng is said to have explained
to the officers that "Shao Kwang-
tung" had redeemed the loan and
taken back the pistol. The police
activities then were narrowed down
to the Hongkew man. After months
of detective work, information was
received that "Shao Kwangtung"
was in Tsingtao in connection with
a cabaret business. Officers were
sent to the Shantung resort and
the wanted man was taken into
custody together with Jack, the
latter being handed over to the
Japanese authorities.

Case Up Monday

While officers were laying their
hand on these two suspects, those
in Shanghai arrested two others
on Sunday after having found in
their possession the hollowed book
allegedly used in hiding the pistol.
The pair faced the court on Mon-
day and were brought again on
Tuesday together with "Shao
Kwangtung." It is understood that
the case will be resumed in the
First Special District next Monday
instead of May 1, as previously re-
ported.

Information from other sources
alleged that Tseng, the informant,
had not only identified the pistol
but also told the officers that
"Shao Kwangtung" and his gang
had been paid $50,000 for the "job"
of removing Hideo Nakayama. The
trio, however, emphatically denied
these charges in the First Special
District although "Shao Kwang-
tung's" alibi concerning the pistol
could not be learned.

Mother Of Prisoner

It now transpires that Mrs. Yih
Ling-sz, the 45-year-old Cantonese
woman arrested in Room 40 at the
Moon Palace Hotel and identified
as a shareholder in the cabaret of
the same name, is the alleged

mother of "Shao Kwangtung"
while Miss Chen Kwei-tseng, the
28-year-old Ningpo dancing girl,
was not his wife but a former
"sweetheart." They lived together
in Chapei four years ago but
separated shortly afterwards. She
later left for Tsingtao and joined
the Vienna Cabaret in the Shan-
tung city, where, ironically, "Shao
Kwangtung" was employed as
"manager of dancing girls." On
April 7, Mrs. Yih decided to re-
turn to Shanghai and Miss Chen
accompanied her to join the Moon
Palace Cabaret. On April 10, they
arrived here but on April 21, they
were arrested by the Public Safety
Bureau officers at the request of the
Japanese Consular Police.

The two women still are being
held at the Public Safety Bureau.
Their release on bail has been sug-
gested by the Judicial Department
of the Bureau but approval of re-
commended, release has not been
obtained from the superiors. It is
believed that the two will be kept
in custody, although given better
treatment than a prisoner is en-
titled to, pending the outcome of
the case. The Chinese authorit-
ies, while refusing to hand them
over to the Japanese, wish to play
safe by keeping them in custody
lest they disappear after the re-
lease, it is believed.

Girl's Manager

"Shao Kwangtung" is Mrs. Yih's
second son. He is 28 years old and
is a well-known figure in the Hong-
kew district and in the smaller
cabarets. His last job with Shang-
hai cabarets was as "dancing girl
manager" at the New Royal
Cabaret, Rue Chu Pao San. He
left for Tsingtao last year to take
over a similar job at the Vienna
Cabaret.

Official circles, including the
Japanese consular authorities, the
City Government and the Shang-
hai Municipal Council, today con-
tinued to shroud the investigations
with a veil of secrecy.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年4月24日，星期五

中山案
通过枪支辨认
“告破”

称“小广东”将
在尸体附近发现的手枪
典当

舞厅舞女
与“大王”有关联

神秘的曾某仍作为
证人被搜寻；
案件周一审理

去年11月9日，日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）在达罗路（Darioch Road）遇害，作案手枪是否与1935年初由虹口区人称“小广东”的叶希森（Yih Hi-sen，音译）向线人曾元（Tseng Yuen，音译）抵押换取现金的那把手枪相同，这是上海公共租界工部局警务处警官正在调查的关键点之一。

从官方保密的铜墙铁壁中泄露出的消息显示，法官已命令线人曾元在下一次审理与该谋杀案有关的三名嫌疑人时出席第一特区法院，他曾告诉警方，在日本水兵尸体附近发现的手枪与“小广东”为贷款而典当的那把完全相同。据报道，正是这一陈述导致这位虹口“舞女大王”在青岛被捕。

博克藏匿枪支

另外两名姓陈的广东人，在上海被另一组警官逮捕，当时他们的同伙正给“小广东”戴上手铐，还有一名被认为是朝鲜人的杰克（Jack），因与该谋杀案有关而被关押在山东度假城市青岛的日本领事警察总部。据说在其中一名陈某的房间裡发现了一本中心被挖空的书。据报道，这个空洞被发现与杀害中山的手枪完全吻合。另一名陈某被捕是因为据称他们是密友。

中山遇害时，日本海军陆战队总部和工部局警务处狄思威路（Dirwell Station）分局的警官捡到了一把刻有P.B.字样的手枪。当弹道专家忙于研究该武器时，一名线人被逮捕凶手的高额赏金所吸引，来到警局。他报告说，他曾看到一把相同品牌的手枪，是“小广东”向同为广东人的曾元抵押换取现金的。

挑出手枪

曾元立即被找到并带到警局。多把手枪摆在他面前。曾元受命识别属于“小广东”的手枪。曾元犹豫了一下，但最终挑出了一把手枪，并宣称那是这位虹口“大王”的财产。而这把手枪正是在谋杀现场捡到的那一把！

据说曾元向警官解释说，“小广东”已经赎回贷款并取回了手枪。随后警方的行动范围缩小到这名虹口男子身上。经过数月的侦探工作，收到情报称“小广东”因舞厅生意身在青岛。警官被派往山东度假胜地，将该通缉犯连同杰克一起拘留，后者被移交给日本当局。

案件周一审理

当警官抓获这两名嫌疑人时，在上海的警官于周日逮捕了另外两人，因为在他们身上发现了据称用于藏匿手枪的挖空书籍。这对男女周一出庭，周二又与“小广东”一起被提审。据悉，该案将于下周一在第一特区法院恢复审理，而非此前报道的5月1日。

来自其他渠道的消息称，线人曾元不仅识别了手枪，还告诉警官，“小广东”及其团伙因“除掉”中山秀雄这项“工作”获得了5万美元的报酬。然而，这三人在第一特区法院坚决否认这些指控，尽管无法得知“小广东”关于手枪的不在场证明。

囚犯之母

现在透露，45岁的广东女子叶林氏（Mrs. Yih Ling-sz，音译）在月宫酒店40号房间被捕，并被确认为同名舞厅的股东，她是“小广东”的母亲；而28岁的宁波舞女陈桂珍小姐（Miss Chen Kwei-tseng，音译）并非他的妻子，而是前“情人”。四年前他们曾住在闸北，但不久后分居。她后来前往青岛，加入了该山东城市的维也纳舞厅，具有讽刺意味的是，“小广东”在那里受雇为“舞女经理”。4月7日，叶氏决定返回上海，陈小姐陪同她加入月宫舞厅。4月10日，她们抵达此处，但4月21日，应日本领事警察的要求，她们被公安局警官逮捕。

这两名妇女仍被拘押在公安局。该局司法科已建议保释她们，但上级尚未批准推荐的释放。据信，在案件结果出来之前，两人将被继续羁押，尽管待遇优于囚犯应得的待遇。据信，中国当局虽然拒绝将她们移交给日本人，但希望稳妥起见将她们羁押，以防释放后失踪。

女孩经理

“小广东”是叶氏的次子。他28岁，是虹口区及小型舞厅中的知名人物。他在上海舞厅的最后一份工作是朱葆三路（Rue Chu Pao San）新皇家舞厅的“舞女经理”。去年他前往青岛，在维也纳舞厅担任类似职务。

包括日本领事当局、市政府和上海公共租界工部局在内的官方圈子，今天继续用保密的面纱笼罩着调查工作。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, APRIL 25, 1936
Arrest Circumstances
Said Behind Secrecy
In Nakayama Case

Pick-Up Procedure In
North Said To Have
Caused Complications

POLITICAL MOTIVE
STRONGLY DOUBTED

Police Continue Work
To Unfold Details Of
Hongkew Killing

While officials in charge of the investigation of the Nakayama case continued to guard their secrets with jealousy and considerable misgiving yesterday, a CHINA PRESS reporter obtained from authentic sources that the real reason for the present silent attitude on the part of the authorities is because of the circumstances surrounding the arrest of one of three Chinese suspects now being held.

The man referred to was taken into custody in Tientsin more than two weeks ago and subsequently brought back to Shanghai by Japanese Police. Although an extradition order had been issued in this city on the strength of a report that he actually had been arrested in the North, two Japanese police who went to Tientsin to get him discovered that he was not in custody, THE CHINA PRESS was informed.

Despite this fact, the man was arrested by Japanese and brought back to Shanghai, with the result that legal and political difficulties have arisen, causing hearings on the case to be held behind closed doors. In the meantime, however, the business of carrying on the investigation into affairs concerned with the actual slaying of Warrant Office Hideo Nakayama on Darroch Road last November is still continuing.

Just how much evidence the authorities have against the three Chinese being held at the Central Station has now become a matter of mere conjecture. Officials don't want to talk about the case, or rather they won't talk about it.

Man Not Arrested

The point remains that the extradition warrant which was obtained here in Shanghai was apparently granted on the strength of an application presented to the First Special District Court that a man had actually been taken into custody in North China on suspicion of having been directly connected with the Nakayama murder. When it was learned that the man had not been arrested, it is stated, a certain amount of fireworks were touched off that led to complications.

It was reported to THE CHINA PRESS that at the first hearing at the First Special District Court on Monday, the day after the first two suspects were lodged in the Central Station on the request of Japanese, nothing startling in the way of evidence against the accused was produced. It was known that the man who had been arrested in Tientsin had left Shanghai shortly after the slaying of Nakayama.

As far as the actual slaying of Nakayama is concerned, it is still stated that no political motive is involved but that the affair was the outgrowth of a private quarrel. This, however, is mere supposition and has not been confirmed.

Cheng Badly Wanted

The man Cheng Yuen, said to have been the man who gave out the information to Japanese authorities leading up to the arrest of the persons now in custody, is badly wanted for the purpose of identifying the accused held in custody.

The latter are being detained only on writ of detention for one week, it has been explained, and unless a prima facie case is established against them, the matter must be dropped and the prisoners given their release.

According to reports appearing in local Chinese papers yesterday, more light was thrown onto the activities of the missing Cheng Yuen. It is declared that he informed the authorities investigating the case that the pistol found near the body of the murdered Japanese sailor was identical with one a man named "Shao Kwangtung" had pawned previously for loan. It was this statement, it is declared, that led to the arrest of the third suspect who was brought back from Tsingtao Monday night.

It must be explained that the pistol referred to was picked up and taken to the Dixwell Road Station and later turned over to ballistics experts for examination. At that time, it is stated that an informant came to the station and declared that he had seen a pistol of the same make which the so-called "Shao Kwangtung," otherwise known as the "king" of the cabaret district on North Szeuhuen Road, had pawned to Cheng Yuen, the present missing man.

Cheng is reported to have later called at the station and to have identified the pistol, and more recently, according to the Chinese press, is declared to have implicated the man arrested in Tsingtao.

In view of the circumstances surrounding the arrest of the man brought in from Tientsin, which were reported yesterday, and the close secrecy which is being maintained in the case, there is really nothing definite that can be stated until the case actual comes before open court.

Known In Cabaret Circles

The man "Shao Kwangtung" is a Cantonese who is quite well-known in local cabaret circles. The woman, Mrs. Yih Ling-sze, 45 years old, who was arrested in Room 40 at the Moon Palace Hotel, and identified as a shareholder in the cabaret of the same name, is said to be the mother of the prisoner.

Miss Chen Kwai-tseng, 28-year-old Ningpo dancing girl, is said to have been his mistress. She once worked in the Vienna Cabaret where it is said that "Shao Kwangtung" was employed as manager of the dancing girls. The pair were arrested it is understood because of their connection with "Shao Kwangtung." The two women were still in the hands of the Public Safety Bureau last night, and although their release on bail has been suggested by the Judicial Department of the Bureau, approval of the recommendation has not yet been made.

The next hearing of the case is scheduled to come before the First Special District Court on Monday. It is understood that it will be held behind closed doors.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年4月25日，星期六
称逮捕情况
导致中山案
保密

称北方的
逮捕程序引起
并发症

强烈怀疑
政治动机

警方继续工作
以揭开虹口
杀人案细节

昨天，负责中山案调查的官员继续嫉妒且相当疑虑地守护着他们的秘密，与此同时，《字林西报》记者从可靠来源获悉，当局目前保持沉默态度的真正原因，是与目前被拘留的三名中国嫌疑人中一人的逮捕情况有关。

所指之人于两周多前在天津被拘留，随后由日本警察带回上海。尽管本市基于一份报告签发了引渡令，称该人实际上已在北方被捕，但《字林西报》获悉，两名前往天津抓他的日本警察发现他并未被拘留。

尽管事实如此，该人仍被日本人逮捕并带回上海，结果引发了法律和政治困难，导致该案的听证会在闭门状态下进行。然而，与此同时，对去年11月在达罗路实际杀害准尉中山秀雄相关事务的调查工作仍在继续。

当局对中央捕房拘留的三名中国人掌握多少证据，现在已成为纯粹的猜测。官员们不想谈论此案，或者更确切地说，他们不愿谈论此案。

此人未被逮捕

关键在于，在上海获得的引渡令显然是基于向第一特区法院提交的申请而颁发的，该申请称一名男子因涉嫌直接参与中山谋杀案而在华北被拘留。据悉，当得知该人并未被捕时，引发了一些导致复杂局面的风波。

据向《字林西报》报道，周一在第一特区法院的首次听证会上，即在应日本人要求将前两名嫌疑人关进中央捕房的第二天，并没有提出任何针对被告的惊人证据。众所周知，在天津被捕的那名男子在中山遇害后不久就离开了上海。

就中山的实际遇害而言，目前仍称不涉及政治动机，而是私人争吵的结果。然而，这仅仅是推测，尚未得到证实。

急需程某

据说向日本当局提供信息从而导致目前被拘留者被捕的程元（Cheng Yuen，音译）男子，急需其来指认被拘留的被告。

据解释，后者仅凭为期一周的拘留令被拘押，除非能确立针对他们的初步案件，否则必须撤销此事并释放囚犯。

根据昨天当地中文报纸出现的报道，失踪的程元的活动得到了更多披露。据称，他向调查此案的当局通报，在遇害日本水兵尸体附近发现的手枪，与一名叫“小广东”的男子此前为贷款而典当的一把手枪相同。据称，正是这一陈述导致了第三名嫌疑人的逮捕，该嫌疑人于周一晚从青岛被带回。

必须说明的是，所指的手枪被捡起并带到狄思威路分局，后来移交给弹道专家进行检查。据称，当时一名线人来到分局，声称他曾看到一把相同品牌的手枪，即所谓“小广东”（又名北四川路舞厅区“大王”）典当给目前失踪的程元的那把。

据报道，程元后来曾到分局并识别了该手枪，而据中文报刊最近称，他还牵连了在天津被捕的男子。

鉴于昨天报道的从天津带回之人的逮捕情况，以及本案保持的严密保密，在案件真正进入公开法庭之前，确实没有什么可以确定的陈述。

在舞厅圈中知名

“小广东”是一名广东人，在当地舞厅圈中颇有名气。45岁的女子叶林氏（Mrs. Yih Ling-sze，音译）在月宫酒店40号房间被捕，并被确认为同名舞厅的股东，据说是该囚犯的母亲。

28岁的宁波舞女陈桂珍小姐（Miss Chen Kwai-tseng，音译）据说是他的情妇。她曾在维也纳舞厅工作，据说“小广东”在那里受雇为舞女经理。据悉，这两人因与“小广东”的关系而被捕。昨晚，这两名妇女仍掌握在公安局手中，尽管该局司法科已建议保释她们，但对该建议的批准尚未作出。

该案的下次听证会定于周一在第一特区法院进行。据悉，听证会将闭门举行。

pages.en:
4.
April 27, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

The "Kwangtung Pao"(廣東板) published the following article
on April 25, 1936 :-

H.O. Tang, Chairman of the Kwangtung Fellow
Provincials Association in Shanghai, has sent the following
letter to Mayor Wu Teh Cheng of the Shanghai City Government
and to the Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police :-
"The following letter has been received from
the Poh San Fellow Provincials Association in Shanghai
(北山旅沪同鄉會) :-
"At about 10 a.m. April 19, Mr. Yang
Vung Tao(楊文道), an Honorary Advisor and Super-
visor of this Association, left his home at Dong An
Lee(同安里), Tongshan Road, to attend his business
accompanied by an attendant. On the way both of them
were arrested by the Police, the cause being unknown.
"According to reliable information,
Mr. Yang is now detained in the Special Branch of the
S.M.P. Headquarters on Foochow Road. The matter is
very serious and no interview with him is allowed.
"The circumstances are as follows :
About a month ago, a certain member of this Association
named Yang(楊) reported to this Association that a
friend of his named Cheng(鄭), who is working as
an interpreter with the Japanese Naval Landing Party,
gave out information to the effect that Yang Vung Tao
had also played a part in the murder of a Japanese
marine on Darroch Road. He requested this Association
to notify Yang Vung Tao to go away. This Association
rejected this report as sheer nonsense, because Yang
Vung Tao's upright character is known to the public
and he would not commit such an atrocious crime. Even
Yang Vung Tao at that time paid no heed to this talk.
"Unexpectedly a month later, the man
named Yang, again acting on information received
from the man named Cheng, came to this Association
requesting it to notify Yang Vung Tao immediately
to go into hiding. Yang further requested the
Association to advise Yang Vung Tao to call at his
home for a consultation.
"This Association is suspicious of
the action of the man named Yang. Yang and Yang
Vung Tao are uncle and nephew and why did not Yang
give this secret information direct to Yang Vung Tao?
Later Yang Vung Tao came to this Association and told
the Association not to believe the rumours. Yang
went into hiding when enquiries were made into the
source of this matter. This shows clearly that
there is a certain motive behind Yang's action.
"It has been ascertained that Yang
Vung Tao, who lives in Hongkew, is quite honourable
and has often rendered assistance by mediating in
trouble. The public appreciate his services.
This is not the one-side talk of this Association.
He used to attend to his office daily in the Dong
Jen Association regardless to the inclement weather.
pages.zh:
4.
1936年4月27日。下午译文。

《广东报》于1936年4月25日刊登了以下文章：

上海广东同乡会主席唐豪致函上海市政府市长吴铁城及上海公共租界工部局警务处处长，信函内容如下：“本会收到上海北山旅沪同乡会来函，内容如下：
‘4月19日上午10时许，本会名誉顾问兼监理杨文道先生由一名随从陪同，离开其位于同山路同安里的寓所外出办事。途中二人均被警方逮捕，原因不明。
据可靠消息，杨先生现被拘押于福州路工部局警务处总部特别支部。事态严重，且不允许与其会面。
具体情况如下：约一个月前，本会一名姓杨的会员向本会报告称，其友人郑某在日本海军陆战队担任翻译，郑某透露消息称杨文道也参与了达罗克路（Darroch Road）一名日本水兵被杀一案。该会员请求本会通知杨文道离开上海。本会认为此报告纯属无稽之谈而予以拒绝，因为杨文道品行端正，众所周知，绝不会犯下如此残暴的罪行。当时杨文道本人对此流言也未予理会。
不料一个月后，该名杨姓男子再次依据从郑姓男子处获得的消息，来到本会，请求本会立即通知杨文道躲藏起来。杨某还请求本会建议杨文道前往其家中商议。
本会对该杨姓男子的行为表示怀疑。杨某与杨文道系叔侄关系，为何杨某不直接将此秘密信息告知杨文道？后来杨文道来到本会，告知本会不要相信谣言。当对本事件的消息来源进行调查时，杨某却躲藏了起来。这清楚地表明，杨某的行为背后必有某种动机。
经查证，居住在虹口的杨文道为人正派，常通过调解纠纷提供帮助。公众对其服务表示赞赏。这并非本会的片面之词。无论天气如何恶劣，他每天都去同仁协会处理事务。

pages.en:
April 27, 1936.
Afternoon Translation.

If he is connected with the Darroch Road murder
case, the Japanese Landing Force might co-operate
with the police in affecting his arrest at any
time. The necessity of affecting his arrest
through Cheng and Yang seems very suspicious.
Despite the warnings he received on two occasions
within a period of one month, Yang Vung Tao did
not attempt to make his escape. This proves that
he has not the slightest connection with the case.
He gave an explanation of the affair and asks the
public not to believe this rumour. He was
arrested three days after giving this explanation.
Is not this strange? In short, this affair must
have been caused by the two bad characters named
Yang and Cheng, who, having failed in their attempt
at extortion, must have made a false report to
the Japanese Naval Landing Party Headquarters with
the intent to bring an accusation against Yang Vung
Tao. Their cruel action against such a good person
is indeed terrifying. As this Association is
a small organization, it is powerless to do anything
in this matter, although it has good intentions.
However, realizing his innocence, we would regret
remaining indifferent, without giving him a hand.
Our only hope is to submit you all the details
herewith, with a request that your Association
will devise ways and means to help Yang Vung Tao
so as to enable him to secure an early release.'
"In compliance with the above request,
we, therefore, forward you this letter with a request
that you will ask the Central Police Station to investigate
into this matter and enable him to avoid undergoing
punishment as a result of a malicious accusation."
pages.zh:
1936年4月27日。
下午译文。

如果他涉及达罗克路谋杀案，日本海军陆战队随时可能与警方合作将其逮捕。通过郑某和杨某来实施逮捕的必要性显得非常可疑。尽管在一个月内两次收到警告，杨文道并未试图逃跑。这证明他与该案毫无关联。他对此事作了解释，并要求公众不要相信这一谣言。他在作出解释三天后即被捕。这难道不奇怪吗？总之，此事必定是由杨、郑两名劣迹斑斑的人物所致，他们敲诈未遂，便向日本海军陆战队总部虚假举报，意图诬告杨文道。他们对这样一位好人采取如此狠毒的手段，确实令人恐惧。鉴于本会是一个小型组织，虽有心相助，却无力在此事上采取任何行动。然而，念及其无辜，我们若袖手旁观，不予援手，实感不安。我们唯一的希望是将详细情况呈报给各位，恳请贵会设法帮助杨文道，使其能早日获释。’
“应上述请求，特此转呈此信，恳请贵方要求中央捕房调查此事，使其免于因恶意诬告而受罚。”

pages.en:
April 27, 1936.
Afternoon Translation.

Ta Kung Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE MURDER OF JAPANESE MARINE NAKAYAMA

In connection with the murder of the Japanese marine Hideo Nakayama, our reporter has obtained the following reliable particulars which originate from a senior Police officer who is in charge of the case :-
In the middle of the night on November 9, 1935, Japanese marine Nakayama was murdered on Darroch Road, North Szechuen Road corner, near the Foong Lo Li (丰樂里) alleyway. The officers of the S.M.P. and the Japanese military officers later found a "P.B." Brand pistol at a spot some 90 yards away from the place where the Japanese marine was murdered, and they came to the opinion that this pistol was the weapon which killed Nakayama.
Following the occurrence of the murder, Japanese Detective Sub-Inspector Nakamura attached to the S.M.P. Headquarters and Japanese detectives and policemen attached to the various Police Stations began to do their utmost to identify the murderer or murderers. Sometime later, a Japanese detective named Haramosa (?) made the following report to D.S.I. Nakamura :- "Investigations show that the culprits in the Nakayama murder case are a Korean named Chi Kuh (傑克) and two Chinese, one of whom is nicknamed Siao Kwangtung (小廣東), the name of the other being unknown. The pistol was owned by Chi Kuh. In the middle of the night on November 9, 1935, Chi Kuh, Siao Kwangtung and the other Chinese walked in the same direction as Nakayama on Darroch Road following behind him. When they had come near the Foong Lo Li alleyway, Chi Kuh gave the pistol to Siao Kwangtung who shot Nakayama. The movements of Chi Kuh and the others, however, are not clear".
Considering that this gave some light on the case, Nakamura instructed Haramosa to make further investigations into the case.
Later, Haramosa made another report to Nakamura as follows :- "It has now been ascertained that Siao Kwangtung, the culprit in the Nakayama murder case, is a member of the San Hai Huei Society (三合會). A member of this society named Tseng Yuan (曾元), a Cantonese, is acquainted with Siao Kwangtung. In October last year, Siao Kwangtung wished to raise a loan, trying to mortgage a pistol shaped like a "P.B." Brand one. Tseng Yuan gave back the pistol to Siao Kwangtung as he had no money. It has been ascertained that at the end of November last year, Siao Kwangtung left Shanghai for Tsingtao and returned here later. In December, he went again to Tsingtao, this time bringing some dancing girls with him, and, together with another person, established the Vienna Dance Hall (維也納跳舞場) on Chong Kew Road (沖口路). In February this year, Siao Kwangtung came to Shanghai again. He attended the Dance Hall in the Yangtsze Hotel (揚子飯店), Hankow Road, several times and later returned to Tsingtao again".
Upon receipt of the above report, Nakamura instructed Haramosa to send for Tseng Yuan and question him. The "P.B." Brand pistol obtained at the place near the spot where the murder took place was put among three other pistols and Tseng Yuan identified the "P.B." Brand pistol as the pistol which Siao Kwangtung had tried to mortgage with him.
pages.zh:
1936年4月27日。
下午译文。

《大公报》、《新闻报》、《申报》及其他本地报纸：

日本水兵中山遇害案

关于日本水兵中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）被杀一案，本报记者从负责此案的一名高级警官处获得了以下可靠详情：
1935年11月9日半夜，日本水兵中山在北四川路与达罗克路（Darroch Road）拐角处、靠近丰乐里弄堂附近被杀。工部局警务处官员和日本军方军官后来在距日本水兵遇害地点约90码处发现了一把“P.B.”牌手枪，他们认为这支手枪就是杀害中山的凶器。
谋杀案发生后，隶属于工部局警务处总部的日本巡官中村以及隶属于各捕房的日本侦探和警察开始竭尽全力查明凶手。不久后，一名名叫Haramosa（音译）的日本侦探向中村巡官提交了如下报告：“调查显示，中山谋杀案的罪犯是一名名叫Chi Kuh（杰克）的朝鲜人和两名中国人，其中一人绰号‘小广东’，另一人姓名不详。手枪归Chi Kuh所有。1935年11月9日半夜，Chi Kuh、‘小广东’和另一名中国人在达罗克路上沿着与中山相同的方向行走，尾随其后。当他们接近丰乐里弄堂时，Chi Kuh将手枪交给‘小广东’，后者开枪射杀了中山。然而，Chi Kuh等人的行踪尚不清楚。”
鉴于这为案件提供了一些线索，中村指示Haramosa对此案进行进一步调查。
随后，Haramosa又向中村提交了另一份报告，内容如下：“现已查明，中山谋杀案的罪犯‘小广东’是三合会成员。该会一名名叫曾元的广东籍会员认识‘小广东’。去年十月，‘小广东’希望借款，试图抵押一把形状类似‘P.B.’牌的手枪。曾元因无钱借出，将手枪退还给了‘小广东’。经查证，去年十一月底，‘小广东’离开上海前往青岛，后又返回上海。十二月，他再次前往青岛，这次带了几名舞女，并与另一人在冲口路开设了维也纳跳舞场。今年二月，‘小广东’再次来到上海。他曾数次光顾汉口路扬子饭店的舞厅，随后又返回青岛。”
收到上述报告后，中村指示Haramosa传唤曾元并进行讯问。将在案发地点附近缴获的“P.B.”牌手枪与其他三支手枪混在一起，曾元指认出该“P.B.”牌手枪即为“小广东”曾试图向他抵押的那支手枪。

pages.en:
2.
April 27, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

D.S.I. Nakamura regarded the information as reliable, and on April 12 he, accompanied by a party of Japanese detectives and the informant Tseng Yuan(曾元), left for Tsingtao to conduct enquiries. There they visited the Vienna Dance Hall where the informant pointed out Siao Kwangtung although he only knew Siao Kwangtung's surname as Yih(葉). After his return from Tsingtao, D.S.I. Nakamura made an application on April 14 to the Legal Department for the issue of an official dispatch from the Shanghai First Special District Court for the extradition of the prisoner, in which he stated that a murderer named Yih, alias Siao Kwangtung, had been arrested in Tsingtao. Acting on the request of the Legal Department, the First Special District Court issued the official dispatch for the extradition of the prisoner. Armed with this dispatch, D.S.I. Nakamura left for Tsingtao by aeroplane on April 15 in company with several other Japanese detectives. He applied to the Public Safety Bureau for assistance. The Commissioner of the Bureau was greatly surprised at reading the official dispatch presented by D.S.I. Nakamura, because the Bureau had not arrested any person by the name of Yih. D.S.I. Nakamura then informed the Bureau that the accused Yih had not yet been arrested but he wished for assistance to arrest him. The Commissioner of the Bureau regarded the procedure as improper because an official dispatch for the extradition of a prisoner could not be used as a warrant for arrest. Subsequently, D.S.I. Nakamura employed other steps which finally brought about the arrest and extradition of Siao Kwangtung to Shanghai. These are the circumstances surrounding the arrest of Siao Kwangtung.

Siao Kwangtung alias Yih Hai Sung is about 28 or 29 years of age.

On April 19, Dixwell Road Police Station applied to the First Special District Court for the issue of two search warrants in respect of House No.36 in a certain alleyway on Urga Road and a certain house in an alleyway on Tongshan Road, where it was alleged important criminals were in hiding. Armed with the warrants issued by the Court, Dixwell Road Police Station, on the same day, detailed a number of Japanese detectives to execute them. House No. 36 on Urga Road was first visited, but nothing incriminating was found. The Police next searched a house in Tongshan Road where a book on physics written in English was seized. This book bound in a stiff cover had a cavity scooped out inside in the shape of a "PB" Brand pistol. Furthermore, on the inside of the book, there was the imprint of the two characters of P and B. Yang Vung Tao(楊文道), age about 40, native of Kwangtung, the tenant of the house in question, who is the Chairman of the Shanghai Municipality Dong Jen Association(上海市同人物会) which holds a certificate issued by the authorities granting its registration, was put under arrest, whilst another Cantonese named Zung Yoong Sung(陳榮生), age about 30, a member of the Dong Jen Association, was also taken into custody as he is on intimate terms with Yang Vung Tao.
pages.zh:
2.
1936年4月27日。下午译文。

中村巡官认为该情报可靠，遂于4月12日带领一队日本侦探及线人曾元前往青岛进行调查。在那里，他们走访了维也纳跳舞场，线人指认出了“小广东”，尽管他只知“小广东”姓叶。从青岛返回后，中村巡官于4月14日向法律处提出申请，请求上海第一特区地方法院签发引渡囚犯的公函，他在申请中称一名名叫叶某、别名“小广东”的谋杀犯已在青岛被捕。应法律处的请求，第一特区地方法院签发了引渡囚犯的公函。持有该公函，中村巡官于4月15日乘飞机与其他几名日本侦探一同前往青岛。他向公安局请求协助。公安局长在阅读中村巡官出示的公函后大为惊讶，因为该局并未逮捕任何姓叶的人。中村巡官随即告知该局，被告叶某尚未被捕，但他希望得到协助以将其逮捕。公安局长认为此程序不当，因为引渡囚犯的公函不能用作逮捕令。随后，中村巡官采取了其他措施，最终导致“小广东”被捕并被引渡至上海。以上即为“小广东”被捕的相关情况。

“小广东”又名叶海松（Yih Hai Sung，音译），年龄约28或29岁。

4月19日，狄思威路捕房向第一特区地方法院申请签发两张搜查令，分别针对乌尔嘎路（Urga Road）某弄堂36号房屋以及同山路某弄堂的一处房屋，据称重要罪犯藏匿于此。凭借法院签发的搜查令，狄思威路捕房于同日派遣多名日本侦探执行搜查。首先搜查了乌尔嘎路36号房屋，但未发现任何罪证。警方接着搜查了同山路的一处房屋，查获了一本英文物理学书籍。这本硬皮书内部被挖空，形状恰如一支“PB”牌手枪。此外，书的内侧印有“P”和“B”两个字符。该房屋的租户、约40岁的广东人杨文道被捕，他是持有当局颁发注册证书的上海市同仁协会主席；另一名约30岁的广东人陈荣生（Zung Yoong Sung，音译），系同仁协会会员，因与杨文道关系密切，也被拘留。

pages.en:
3
April 27, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

The two suspects named Yang Vung Tao
and Zung Yoong Sung were arraigned before the Shanghai
First Special District Court on April 20 when they were
ordered to be detained, while an application for the
detention of Siao Kwangtung alias Yih Hai Sung was made
on April 21. They are at present all being detained at
the Central Police Station.
During the course of investigations,
Yang Vung Tao confessed that the "P.B." brand pistol had
once been in his possession but alleged that the same
was lost over a year ago. He also acknowledged that the
book in English belonged to him; but denied all knowledge
about the murder of the Japanese marine Nakayama. The
other suspect Zung Yoong Sung also denied having had any
connections with the case, while Siao Kwang Tung alias
Yih Hai Sung made the following statement:-
"I was poor before. The reason that
I have got money now is because of my reunion with my
wife Zung Kwei Tsung (陳桂珍), a dancing partner at
present detained at the Bureau of Public Safety, from whom
I separated several years before. After our separation,
my wife became a dancing partner and so became acquainted
with a rich merchant named Wang. Last year Wang died and
his estate was all inherited by Kwei Tsung. We became
reunited last year. That is why I have money to establish
dance halls at present."
In his statement, Siao Kwangtung denied
having committed this murder.
The Police Department at present regards
Siao Kwangtung as the culprit in connection with the
Nakayama case, while Yang Vung Tao is regarded as an
instigator. Zung Yoong Sung's connections with this case
are regarded as less serious, while the Korean Chi Kuh is
the originator of the plot. The Police Department also
holds the view that this case bears no political significance.
It is learned that Yih Hai Sung alias
Siao Kwangtung has confessed that he knows the Korean
Chi Kuh, but he quarreled with him (the Korean) before over
the dispute of a lorn. The three accused all denied having
known Tseng Yuan.
According to the information obtained
from some person who is closely associated with the Legal
Department of the S.M.C., it is stated that the Municipal
Advocate's Office of the S.M.C. considers from a legal
point of view that the evidence against the three suspects
is in sufficient.
Realizing the significance of the case,
the Court has decided to open a joint hearing of the case
before Chien Hung Nieh (錢鴻業), the Chief of the
Criminal Division, and Judges Feng (馮 ) and Siao (蕭 )
at about 2 p.m. on April 27. The presentation of the case
will be postponed till the afternoon, while the hearing
of the case will probably take place at the first Criminal
Division. Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Ru will
represent the S.M.C.
According to information released from
the office of lawyer Vai Kong (范剛), the Court has
appointed Lawyer Vai to act for the defence of the three
accused. It is reported that the hearing of the case
may not be held in camera.
pages.zh:
3
1936年4月27日。下午译件。

两名嫌疑人杨文涛（Yang Vung Tao，音译）和曾永松（Zung Yoong Sung，音译）于4月20日被提解至上海第一特区地方法院，当时法院下令予以羁押；而关于拘押萧广东（Siao Kwangtung），又名叶海生（Yih Hai Sung）的申请则于4月21日提出。目前他们均被羁押于中央捕房。

在调查过程中，杨文涛供认“P.B.”牌手枪曾为其所有，但声称该枪已于一年多前遗失。他还承认那本英文书属于他；但否认对日本海军陆战队士兵中山（Nakayama）被杀案有任何了解。另一名嫌疑人曾永松也否认与本案有任何牵连，而萧广东（又名叶海生）则作了如下陈述：

“我以前很穷。我现在有钱的原因是因为我与妻子陈桂珍（Zung Kwei Tsung）团聚，她目前是公共安全局羁押的一名舞女，我们在几年前分居。分居后，我的妻子成为了一名舞女，因此结识了一位名叫王的富商。去年王某去世，其遗产全部由桂珍继承。我们于去年复婚。这就是为什么我现在有钱开设舞厅的原因。”

在陈述中，萧广东否认犯下此谋杀罪。

警务处目前视萧广东为中山案的主犯，而杨文涛被视为教唆者。曾永松与本案的关联被认为较轻，而朝鲜人池赫（Chi Kuh，音译）则是该阴谋的策划者。警务处还认为本案不具有政治意义。

据悉，叶海生（又名萧广东）已供认认识朝鲜人池赫，但他此前曾因争夺一名妓女（lorn，原文疑为girl之误或特定俚语，此处依语境译为妓女/女子）与该朝鲜人发生过争吵。三名被告均否认认识曾元（Tseng Yuan，音译）。

据从与工部局法律处关系密切的人士处获得的消息称，工部局市政检察官办公室从法律角度认为，针对这三名嫌疑人的证据不足。

鉴于案件的重要性，法院决定于4月27日下午2时许，由刑事庭庭长钱鸿业以及冯法官（Feng，音译）和萧法官（Siao，音译）共同开庭审理此案。案情陈述将推迟至下午进行，而案件审理可能在第一刑事庭进行。助理市政检察官保罗·鲁（Paul Ru，音译）将代表工部局出庭。

据范刚（Vai Kong）律师办公室发布的消息，法院已指定范律师担任三名被告的辩护律师。据报道，本案审理可能不会闭门进行。

April 26, 1936.    Morning Translation
（印：7 / 1936 (CRIME BRANCH)）

Lih Pao Evening Edition :-

THE MURDER OF JAPANESE MARINE NAKAYAMA

The suspects connected with the murder of
the Japanese marine Nakayama will be tried again on Monday
next in the First Special District Court. The case is
being kept secret.
According to observations by various circles,
it is simply a case of a dispute in a dance hall and
there is no political motive behind the case. The reason
why the case is being kept so secret is, it is said, as
follows :-
At the beginning of this month, a certain
Japanese political detective of the S.M.P. told the Legal
Department that a suspect connected with the murder of
Nakayama had already been arrested at Tientsin and
requested the Legal Department to apply to the First
Special District Court for a dispatch warrant in order to
remove the suspect from Tientsin to Shanghai for trial.
The Legal Department accordingly requested the Court to
issue a dispatch warrant. When the Japanese detective
arrived at Tientsin, however, the suspect had not yet
been arrested. The suspect was arrested several days
later in the Japanese Concession at Tientsin by the
Japanese Police and was sent to Shanghai under escort.
Furthermore, on his arrival in Shanghai the suspect was
detained some days at the Police Station and was not
immediately arraigned before the Court. The Court regards
this procedure as irregular and has asked the S.M.C. for
an explanation. On April 24, General Han Fu Chu, Chairman
of the Shantung Provincial Government, considering that
the procedure of the S.M.P. in arresting an accused at
Tsingtao was not in order, made enquiries from the First
Special District Court about the matter. For this reason,
neither the Court nor the S.M.C. wish to publish the
particulars of the case. The case may be heard publicly
when all the minor questions have been settled.

Lih Pao Evening Edition published the following comment on
April 25 :-

HOW TO GET RID OF ROBBERS IN THE INTERNATIONAL SETTLEMENT

Cases of robbery are daily occurrences in the
local foreign Settlements. It is a serious question
affecting the public peace and order.
The International Settlement Chinese Ratepayers
Association has submitted certain proposals to the S.M.C.
requesting it to study and draw up fundamental measures to
clear up these robbers.
No mercy should be shown to robbers. The
Settlement authorities should, (1) study the cause why
robbers are so plentiful, (2) draw up measures to punish
robbers and (3) devise measures to wipe out the evil of
robbers.
The S.M.C. spends several tens of millions
in dollars every year on the maintenance of peace by the
Police, yet cases of robbery are daily occurrences as is
mentioned in the letter from the Chinese Ratepayers
Association. The Council should study measures to
eliminate the evil of robbers and then bring these measures
into effect.

《立报》晚刊：

日本海军陆战队士兵中山被杀案

与日本海军陆战队士兵中山被杀案有关的嫌疑人将于下周一在第一特区地方法院再次受审。该案目前处于保密状态。

据各界观察，这仅仅是一起舞厅纠纷案件，背后没有政治动机。据说，该案之所以如此保密，原因如下：

本月初，工部局警务处的一名日本政治侦探告知法律处，一名与中山被杀案有关的嫌疑人已在天津被捕，并请求法律处向第一特区地方法院申请遣送令，以便将该嫌疑人从天津移解至上海受审。法律处遂请求法院签发遣送令。然而，当这名日本侦探抵达天津时，嫌疑人尚未被捕。几天后，该嫌疑人在天津日租界被日本警察逮捕，并在押解下送往上海。此外，该嫌疑人抵达上海后，在捕房被拘留数日，并未立即被提解至法院。法院认为此程序不合常规，并要求工部局作出解释。4月24日，山东省政府主席韩复榘将军认为工部局警务处在青岛逮捕被告的程序不当，就此事项向第一特区地方法院查询。因此，法院和工部局均不愿公布案件详情。待所有次要问题解决后，本案可能会公开审理。

《立报》晚刊于4月25日发表如下评论：

如何清除国际公共租界的强盗

抢劫案在本市外国租界每日发生。这是一个影响公共治安秩序的严重问题。

公共租界华人纳税会已向工部局提交若干提案，要求其研究并制定根本措施以清除这些强盗。

对强盗不应手软。租界当局应当：(1) 研究强盗如此众多的原因，(2) 制定惩罚强盗的措施，以及 (3)  devise（制定）措施以根除强盗之害。

工部局每年花费数千万美元用于维持警务治安，然而正如华人纳税会来信所述，抢劫案仍每日发生。董事会应研究消除强盗之害的措施，并将这些措施付诸实施。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, APRIL 24, 1936

Cabaret Girls Reported Set
Free In Nakayama Case

Said To Have Been Allowed Out On Bail Owing To
Lack Of Evidence; Police Continue Hush-
Hush Policy On Activities

Usually reliable sources report-
ed late last night that the two
Chinese cabaret girls arrested in
Hongkew in connection with
Nakayama murder developments
have been released, on shop secur-
ity for their subsequent appear-
ance, owing to the meagre nature
of evidence associating them with
the crime.
No confirmation was, of course,
available.
Apart from reiterating their
decision not to communicate any-
thing to the public until their
investigations had been completed,
officials of the Shanghai Municipal
Police yesterday had nothing to
say regarding the progress made
in the solution of the murder of
Hideo Nakayama, Japanese Naval
Warrant Officer, who was shot to
death in the Dixwell Road District
on November 9 last year.
Senior officials of the S.M.P.,
Japanese Consular Police and
Bureau of Public Safety were in
conference on two occasions yes-
terday, and further interrogation
of the persons now in custody
continued. But nothing regarding
the conferences nor any indication
of the extent of the complicity
of the prisoners in the murder
was revealed.
It was intimated yesterday that
a tripartite agreement had been
reached early in the investigations
by which all three police bodies
were not to divulge anything to
the press in connection with the
investigation. It was freely hinted
again yesterday that political
considerations of the utmost
importance were involved; and
that until the allegations of the
prisoners had been confirmed or
disproved, disclosures at this stage
might result in serious complica-
tions.
In the meantime, three Chinese
and a Korean are held, and the
two Chinese women are subject
to supervision, in connection with
the crime.
The only suspicion that led
Japanese police to request the ar-
rest of the women, it is now re-
ported, was their relationship with
one of the men accused. His name
is given, unofficially, as Yih Hai-
sen, and one of the women is said
to be his wife.
It is further understood that
the case will come into court for
resumed hearing to-day week.

《字林西报》，1936年4月24日，星期五

报道称中山案中的舞女获释

据悉因证据不足准予保释；警方继续对行动采取保密政策

通常可靠的消息源昨晚报道，因虹口地区与中山谋杀案进展有关而被捕的两名中国舞女，由于将她们与犯罪联系起来的证据微薄，已通过店铺担保获释，以保证其随后出庭。

当然，此事无法得到证实。

上海公共租界警务处官员昨日除了重申在调查完成之前不向公众透露任何信息的决定外，对于去年11月9日在狄思威路（Dixwell Road）地区被枪杀的日本海军准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）谋杀案的侦破进展，无可奉告。

工部局警务处高级官员、日本领事馆警察和公共安全局官员昨日两次举行会议，并继续对目前在押人员进行审讯。但会议内容以及囚犯在谋杀案中的共谋程度均未透露。

昨日有人暗示，在调查初期已达成了三方协议，即所有三个警察机构不得向新闻界泄露任何与调查有关的信息。昨日再次有明确暗示称，涉及极其重要的政治考量；且在囚犯的指控得到证实或反驳之前，此阶段的披露可能会导致严重的复杂局面。

与此同时，三名中国人和一名朝鲜人因与该犯罪有关而被拘留，两名中国妇女则受到监视。

据报道，导致日本警察要求逮捕这些妇女的唯一怀疑，是她们与其中一名被指控男子的关系。非官方消息称该男子名为叶海森（Yih Hai-sen，音译），据说其中一名妇女是他的妻子。

另据悉，本案将于下周同日恢复法庭审理。

April 25, 1936.
Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pac :-

THE MURDER OF A JAPANESE MARINE : COMPLAINT AS TO POLICE
PROCEDURE

In connection with the murder of the Japanese
marine Nakayama, Mr. Tsiang Pac Lier, Assistant Municipal
Advocate, will conduct the prosecution. When the case
against the accused is again heard on Monday next, the
Municipal Police will charge the three suspects with
homicide. As it will take some time for the Police
to complete their investigations into the case, it is
possible that the date of the next hearing may be postponed.
Siao Kwangtung (小廣東) alias Yih Hai Sung
(叶海生), one of the three accused in the case, was
escorted to Shanghai from Tsingtao. As the procedure
of the Shanghai Municipal Police in sending officers to
Tsingtao to arrest this accused and take him to Shanghai
was not in order, General Han Fu Chu, Chairman of the
Shantung Provincial Government, is investigating the
matter. When the officers of the S.M.P. arrived at
Tsingtao, the documents they produced stated that the
accused Siao Kwangtung had been arrested and that his
extradition was requested. As a matter of fact, the
accused had not yet been arrested and the officers of the
S.M.P. requested the Tsingtao Public Safety Bureau for
assistance in effecting the arrest of the accused.
General Han regards the procedure as irregular and has
sent a telegram to the Special District Court in Shanghai
enquiring into the matter.
Mr. Paul Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate,
at the last hearing of the case, stated that a Japanese
Sub-Inspector, acting on instructions from his senior
officer, had requested the Legal Department to apply to
the Court for a dispatch warrant. He added that neither
the Court nor the Legal Department was responsible for
the mistake.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

Accused to be Charged with Homicide

According to reliable information, the three
Chinese suspects now in the custody of the S.M.P., two of
whom are named Zung (曾) and the third is known as Yih
Hai Sung alias Siao Kwangtung, will be arraigned before
the First Shanghai Special District Court on the morning
of April 27.
The Police will be represented by Assistant
Municipal Advocate Paul Ru who will probably conduct the
prosecution. A charge of homicide will be filed against
the accused.
It is reported that the hearing on next
Monday will be held in camera.

上午译件。

《大美晚报》：

日本海军陆战队士兵被杀案：对警方程序的投诉

就日本海军陆战队士兵中山被杀案而言，助理市政检察官蒋帕利尔（Tsiang Pac Lier，音译）将负责公诉。当下周一再次审理针对被告的案件时，市政警察将以杀人罪起诉这三名嫌疑人。由于警方需要一些时间来完成对案件的调查，下次审理的日期可能会推迟。

本案三名被告之一的小广东（Siao Kwangtung），又名叶海生（Yih Hai Sung），是从青岛被押解至上海的。由于上海公共租界警务处派遣警员前往青岛逮捕该被告并将其带至上海的程序不当，山东省政府主席韩复榘将军正在调查此事。当工部局警务处警员抵达青岛时，他们出示的文件称被告小广东已被逮捕，并请求引渡。事实上，该被告当时尚未被捕，工部局警务处警员请求青岛公共安全局协助逮捕该被告。韩将军认为此程序不合常规，并已致电上海特区地方法院查询此事。

助理市政检察官保罗·鲁（Paul Ru）先生在最后一次庭审中表示，一名日本巡佐奉上级指示，请求法律处向法院申请遣送令。他补充说，法院和法律处均不对这一错误负责。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

被告将被控杀人罪

据可靠消息，目前由工部局警务处羁押的三名中国嫌疑人，其中两人姓曾（Zung），第三人名为叶海生，又名小广东，将于4月27日上午在上海第一特区地方法院受审。

警方将由助理市政检察官保罗·鲁代表出庭，他可能会负责公诉。将对被告提出杀人罪指控。

据报道，下周一的审理将闭门进行。

April 24, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE CIRCUMSTANCES SURROUNDING THE DISCOVERY OF THE CULPRITS
IN CONNECTION WITH THE MURDER OF A JAPANESE MARINE

After the death of the Japanese marine
named Nakayama, both the Japanese Landing Party Headquarters
and the International Settlement Police detailed detectives
to the scene of the incident for enquiries. A "B.P." brand
pistol was found at the place, which was later certified
as the weapon that was used to murder the Japanese marine.
Sometime afterwards, a certain person reported to the
Settlement Police that he had once seen a similar brand of
pistol which had been given as security by one named Siao
Kwang Tung (小廣東) to a Cantonese named Tseng Yuan
(曾元) for the loan of a certain sum of money.
On receipt of this information, the
Settlement Police summoned the Cantonese and asked him to
pick out from among several pistols, including the one that
was found at the place of the incident, the pistol that had
been given to him by Siao Kwang Tung as security. After
examining the weapons, the Cantonese picked out a pistol
stating that it was the pistol handed to him by Siao Kwang
Tung. He also stated that the pistol had been returned to
Siao Kwang Tung after he had refunded the money.
Acting on this information, the Settlement
Police immediately started to locate Siao Kwang Tung. The
first several months of the investigations met with no result.
Recently, however, information was received that Siao Kwang
Tung was staying at Tsingtao, whereupon competent officers
were sent to Tsingtao where they arrested him, but up till
Sunday last, Siao Kwang Tung had not been brought to Shanghai.
In the meantime, the Settlement Police had arrested two
other Chinese. At the place of abode of one of these two
latter arrested persons, a book in a foreign language was
discovered, in which was found a hole cut out exactly in
the shape of a pistol. It was later found that the shape
of the hole corresponded exactly with the pistol that was
discovered at the scene of the incident. One of the two
persons was, therefore, suspected as having had connections
with this murder, while the other one was involved on account
of his close association with the former.
The two persons appeared in the Shanghai
First Special District Court on Monday, April 20, when they
were ordered to be detained. The following morning Siao Kwang
Tung was brought to Shanghai and was immediately escorted to
the Court. After the hearing, he was likewise ordered to
be detained. It is learned that the three persons arrested
will appear at the Court for interrogation again next Monday.

China Evening News (23/4) :-

The Relationship between the two Chinese Females and One of
the Three Male Suspects named Yih Hai Sung.

On the night of April 21, the local
Japanese Consular Police, in conjunction with the Shanghai
Bureau of Public Safety, visited the Moon Palace Cabaret on
North Szechuen Road and arrested two Chinese females named
Yih Ling Sz(葉林氏), Cantonese, a shareholder of the

1936年4月24日。晨间译稿。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

关于日本海军陆战队员被杀案凶手发现经过之情形

在日本海军陆战队员中山（Nakayama）死后，日本登陆部队总部与国际租界警方均派遣侦探前往事发地点进行调查。现场发现一支“B.P.”牌手枪，后经鉴定确认为杀害该日本海军陆战队员的凶器。此后不久，有人向租界警方报告称，他曾见过一支类似品牌的手枪，该枪系一名叫小广东（Siao Kwang Tung）的人作为抵押品交给一名叫曾元（Tseng Yuan）的广东人，以借贷一定数额的款项。

接到此情报后，租界警方传讯了该名广东人，并要求他从包括在现场发现的那支在内的几支手枪中，辨认出由小广东交给他作为抵押的那一支。经查验武器后，该广东人挑出一支手枪，称这就是小广东交给他的那支。他还表示，在他退还借款后，该手枪已归还给小广东。

根据这一线索，租界警方立即着手查找小广东。调查的前几个月毫无结果。然而，最近收到情报称小广东正逗留于青岛，遂派遣主管官员前往青岛将其逮捕，但截至上周日，小广东尚未被押解至上海。

与此同时，租界警方还逮捕了另外两名中国人。在这两名后来被捕者之一的住所内，发现一本外文书籍，书中有一个恰好呈手枪形状的镂空孔洞。后经查明，该孔洞的形状与在案发现场发现的手枪完全吻合。因此，这两人中的一人被怀疑与此谋杀案有关联，另一人则因与前者的密切关系而被卷入。

这两人于4月20日（星期一）出庭受审于上海第一特区地方法院，并被裁定羁押。次日上午，小广东被押解至上海，并立即被护送至法院。聆讯后，他同样被裁定羁押。据悉，这三名被捕者将于下周一再次出庭接受审讯。

《China Evening News》（4月23日）：

两名中国女性与三名男性嫌疑人之一叶海生（Yih Hai Sung）之关系

4月21日晚，日本驻沪领事馆警察会同上海市公安局，前往北四川路月宫舞厅（Moon Palace Cabaret），逮捕了两名中国女性，分别是叶林氏（Yih Ling Sz），广东人，该舞厅股东，以及

pages.en:
2.
April 24, 1936. Morning Translation.

cabaret, and Zung Kwei Tsung(陳桂珍), a modern girl, native of Ningpo, who had recently arrived here from Tsingtao to work as a dancing partner in the cabaret. The two females were taken to the Bureau of Public Safety for investigation. In view of the serious nature of the case, the authorities have been reticent over the matter.
According to information gathered by a reporter of this paper this morning, the Police of the International Settlement have now in custody three Chinese suspected of being concerned in the murder of the Japanese marine named Nakayama, on Darroch Road in November last. Two of the three suspects were brought here from Tientsin and Tsingtao, while the third was arrested in Shanghai. The man brought here from Tsingtao is reported to be named Yih Hai Sung(葉海生), age 28, native of Kwangtung. He was formerly a supervisor of dancing partners in various cabarets in Tsingtao and Shanghai, and he is the second son of the Cantonese woman named Yih Ling Sz now in the custody of the Shanghai Bureau of Public Safety. Four years ago, he met a girl named Zung Kwei Tsung, native of Ningpo, and the two lived together in the downstairs portion of the San Ming(三明) School in Chapei. They parted sometime later owing to a disagreement. The girl immediately left for Tsingtao where she made her living as a dancing partner, while Yih Hai Sung took up a position supervising dancing partners in a cabaret in Tsingtao. It is learned that his mother Yih Ling Sz is not aware of his arrest and subsequent extradition to Shanghai, since Yih Ling Sz came to Shanghai from Tsingtao by steamer on April 7 in company with Zung Kwei Tsung, since when they had stayed at Room No. 40, Moon Palace Hotel, North Szechuen Road. Yih Ling Sz came to Shanghai for the purpose of attending to her ancestral grave, while Zung Kwei Tsung was to join the Moon Palace Cabaret as a dancing partner. The report that Yih Ling Sz is a shareholder of the Moon Palace Cabaret is untrue.
Acting on the information that the two females are related to the suspect Yih Hai Sung, the Japanese Consulate detailed its officials, with the assistance of Mr. Robertson, Assistant Commissioner of the Shanghai Municipal Police, to apply to the Bureau of Public Safety for assistance to search Room No. 40, Moon Palace Hotel, for evidence that might have some connection with the case. As nothing incriminating against the two females were found, the Bureau of Public Safety refused to hand them over.
According to reliable information received, the two females were found as a result of thorough investigations conducted by the Detective Branch and the Third Department of the Bureau of Public Safety not to be connected with the case, and on this account General Tsai Chin Chun, Commissioner of the Bureau, has decided to submit a report on the case to the Shanghai City Government and will allow the two females to be released on security after instructions have been received from the City Government.

2.
1936年4月24日。晨间译稿。

陈桂珍（Zung Kwei Tsung），摩登女郎，宁波人，近期从青岛来沪，在该舞厅担任舞女。两名女子被带往公安局接受调查。鉴于案情严重，当局对此事保持缄默。

据本报记者今晨搜集到的消息，国际租界警方目前羁押着三名涉嫌参与去年11月在达罗克路（Darroch Road）杀害日本海军陆战队员中山（Nakayama）的中国嫌疑人。三名嫌疑人中的两人分别从天津和青岛押解至此，第三人则在上海被捕。据悉，从青岛押解至此的男子名叫叶海生（Yih Hai Sung），28岁，广东人。他曾任青岛和上海各舞厅的舞女领班，他是目前被上海市公安局羁押的广东女子叶林氏的次子。四年前，他结识了一名名叫陈桂珍（Zung Kwei Tsung）的宁波籍女子，两人同居于闸北三明（San Ming）学校楼下部分。后因不和分手。该女子随即前往青岛，以做舞女为生，而叶海生则在青岛一家舞厅担任舞女领班。据悉，其母叶林氏并不知晓其被捕及随后被引渡至上海之事，因为叶林氏于4月7日与陈桂珍一同乘轮船从青岛来到上海，此后一直住在北四川路月宫饭店40号房间。叶林氏来沪是为了祭扫祖坟，而陈桂珍则是为了加入月宫舞厅担任舞女。有关叶林氏是月宫舞厅股东的报道不实。

鉴于两名女性与嫌疑人叶海生有关联的情报，日本领事馆派遣官员，并在工部局警务处副总巡捕罗伯逊（Robertson）先生的协助下，向公安局申请协助搜查北四川路月宫饭店40号房间，以寻找可能与案件有关的证据。由于未发现对两名女性不利的证据，公安局拒绝将她们移交。

据收到的可靠消息，经公安局侦缉队和三科彻底调查，发现两名女性与本案无关，为此，公安局局长蔡劲军将军决定就此案向上海市政府提交报告，并在接到市政府指示后，允许两名女性具保释放。
