根据初审法庭的记录。由于易海松的供词在5月6日之前已记录在案，他声称供词是通过刑讯获得的，显然是捏造。
本次上诉基于五点。除第(3)点关于杀人动机、第(4)点关于被告提出的反证以及第(5)点关于各种事实等外，其余均为推测，缺乏具体证据支持其主张。
第(1)点批评警方提出的物证。它声称，由于子弹从中山（Nakayama，音译）的后脑射入并从额头穿出，子弹应掉落在该海军陆战队员的前方，而不是实际上发现的在该海军陆战队员后方约8英尺处。经查阅初审法庭在重建犯罪现场时绘制的图表，我们发现中山被射击的地点（标红）与他倒下的地点相距三步，而子弹掉落在两点之间（标绿）。子弹掉落地点位于中山被射击地点的前方。根据日本医务官小川（Ogawa）的报告，当中山被送往日本海军陆战队总部时，他的体温为36.5度，脉搏90，呼吸22。他的状况如同正常人，即使在中枪后也有可能走了几步。鉴于中山体格强壮，合理推测他在中枪后短时间内向前走了三步然后倒下。不能固执地坚持子弹掉落在受害者倒地地点之后这一观点，而无视犯罪现场重建时绘制的图表。
此外，穿透活体的子弹可能不会沾染血迹。工部局法医实验室和枪械鉴定科的各位专家已证实这一点。上诉人仅凭空言无法驳斥此类证据。
上诉状进一步称：“证人张尊（Chang Tsun）在陈述中说，当曾元（Tseng Yuan）和郑惠民（Zung Wei Ming）在床上吸鸦片时，他用铅笔画了一把手枪的草图。后来曾元将他介绍给郑惠民，郑说如果他（张尊）去日本海军陆战队总部报案，称海军陆战队员中山被易海松、杨文道和一名叫杰克的韩国人谋杀，他就可以领取4,000美元赏金。在初审法庭听证会上就此事进行质询时，曾元回答：‘没错，没错。’在初审法庭听证会上，杨建中（Yang Chien Chung）也承认他认识郑惠民，并且因郑惠民向他借款而将杨文道的地址提供给了郑惠民。那本挖有手枪形状空洞的书由杨建中作为郑惠民和曾元阴谋的一部分而栽赃，这并非完全不可能。”

Chang Tsun was formerly on friendly terms with
Tseng Yuan, Zung 'ei Ming and others and was one of the party
to claim the reward. Later, there was a rupture over
conflicting interests and he called at the office of lawyer
Kuh Chao Chi, the lawyer of Yang Wen Dao, to give his evidence.
His petition which is in favour of Yang Wen Dao was drawn up
by a man named Yih(叶) and submitted to the Court. It is
doubtful whether his words are reliable. Assuming, as
contended by appellants, that Zung Wei Ming and others had
actually conspired to give information in order to secure the
reward, this is a totally different matter from the planting
of evidence and the making of a malicious accusation. The
evidence given by Chang Tsun merely proves that Zung Wei Ming
and others are suspected of having conspired to give the
information. No proof was produced to show how Zung 'ei
Ming had planted the false evidence. The ruling of the
Court of First Instance in rejecting the evidence given by
Chang Tsun, Zung Wei Ming and Tseng Yuan cannot, therefore,
be said to be without reason. It is alleged that according
to the report of the Medico-Legal Laboratory, none of the
finger-prints and blood stains found in the book were similar
to the finger-prints or palm-prints of Yang Wen Dao; that the
paper had been broken at two places at a spot directly
opposite the safety catch of the pistol; that the edges of
the breaks had curled and bore rust marks and grease stains;
that the rust had been caused by grease; that the deep
impressions and breaks in the pages of the book could not
have been made without strong pressure from the outside,
showing that the impressions and breaks had been deliberately
and extemporarily made by applying exterior pressure on the
book; that the marks of excavating the hole in the book were
very fresh, especially at the two bends on the lower left
side and at the short left-hand edge on the upper left side
of the book, showing that the book had been manufactured
extemporarily and planted in the house of Yang Wen Dao. The
accused had failed to note that the finger-prints left in the
book were few and mostly incomplete, as pointed out in Report
No. 100, Character "Chien"(检), made by the Medico-Legal
Laboratory, and it was for this reason that the Laboratory
had been unable to find any of Yang Wen Dao's finger-prints
in the book. At the most, we can only say that the
result of the examination failed to prove that the book
bore the finger-prints of Yang Wen Dao, but it cannot be
taken as evidence in favour of the accused. Rust is caused
by the oxidation of iron in the air. The speed of the process
of rusting is according to the humidity of the air at the
place where the pistol is kept and by the presence of grease
on the surface of the pistol; therefore it is impossible to
determine from the rust marks the period of time in which
the pistol had been kept. As to the deep impressions
and breaks in the pages, they could not have been made if
there had been no external pressure or if the pistol had not
moved to and fro inside the book because the weight of the
pistol was only 600 grams. Any heavy book or other article
placed on the book containing the pistol would have provided
the pressure required to make the impressions and breaks.
The marks of excavation were inside the book and did not come
into contact with light or dust; the period of their existence
cannot therefore be determined according to freshness. All
this has been explained in Report No. 99 of the Medico-Legal
Laboratory. If a pistol is put in dry place and coated

1936年12月11日。下午译本

张尊此前与曾元、郑惠民等人关系友好，是索取赏金团伙的一员。后来因利益冲突发生破裂，他便前往杨文道的律师顾兆麒（Kuh Chao Chi，音译）律师事务所提供证词。有利于杨文道的诉状是由一名姓叶（Yih）的人起草并提交法庭的。其言辞是否可靠值得怀疑。即便如上诉人所主张，郑惠民等人确实合谋提供情报以获取赏金，这与栽赃证据和恶意诬告完全是两回事。张尊提供的证据仅证明郑惠民等人涉嫌合谋提供情报。并无证据证明郑惠民是如何栽赃假证据的。因此，不能说初审法庭驳回张尊、郑惠民和曾元证词的裁决没有理由。据称，根据法医实验室的报告，在书中发现的指纹和血迹均与杨文道的指纹或掌纹不符；纸张在手枪保险扣正对面的位置有两处断裂；断裂边缘卷曲并带有锈迹和油渍；锈迹是由油脂引起的；书页上的深痕和断裂若无外部强力压迫是不可能形成的，表明这些痕迹和断裂是通过对书本施加外部压力而故意且临时制造的；书中挖洞的痕迹非常新鲜，特别是在书的左下角两个弯曲处和左上角短左边缘处，表明该书是临时制造并栽赃在杨文道家中的。被告未能注意到，正如法医实验室在第100号“检”字报告中所指出的，留在书中的指纹很少且大多不完整，正因如此，实验室未能在书中找到杨文道的任何指纹。我们最多只能说，检查结果未能证明书上有杨文道的指纹，但这不能作为有利于被告的证据。锈迹是由空气中的铁氧化造成的。生锈过程的速度取决于存放手枪地点的空气湿度以及手枪表面的油脂情况；因此，不可能根据锈迹确定手枪存放的时间长短。至于书页上的深痕和断裂，如果没有外部压力或手枪未在书内来回移动，是不可能形成的，因为手枪的重量仅为600克。任何放在藏有手枪的书本上的重物或其他物品都会提供造成痕迹和断裂所需的压力。挖凿痕迹位于书内，未接触光线或灰尘；因此，不能根据其新鲜程度确定其存在的时间。所有这些已在法医实验室第99号报告中作出解释。如果将手枪放置在干燥处并涂上

pages.en:
7
December 12, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

with grease, oxidation will take place more slowly. Now the pistol in this case was greased on the surface and this grease should have had an anti-rust effect upon the pistol. Yet the appellant alleges that the grease had accelerated the rusting. This is not in accordance with the statement made in the report of the Medico-Legal Laboratory. Furthermore, the breaks in the pages can also be caused by the pistol moving to and fro inside the book, external pressure is not the only cause. Therefore, the appellants cannot attack the original judgment on this point.

The second point stressed that the statements and reconstructions made by Yih Hai Sung had not been made voluntarily. This Court has examined the record of the Court of First Instance and found that although the various confessions of Yih Hai Sung did not totally correspond with one another, they had not been made under torture; they corresponded with the facts. The Court record regarding the reconstruction made at the scene of the crime by Yih Hai Sung and and the witness Hu Ziang Wu in the presence of the Judge of the Court of First Instance contains nothing to show that Yih Hai Sung had been prevented from making his reconstruction freely by threats or inducements or by some forcible or fraudulent or other unlawful means. The lawyers of the appellants were present at the reconstruction and had accepted the record as correct and signed it. They had not said anything about Yih Hai Sung not having been allowed to reconstruct the crime freely. How can the appellants now say this after they have filed the appeal? Yih Hai Sung had both of his hands handcuffed to two Japanese policemen only as a measure of safeguard; he cannot be said to have lost his freedom because of being thus handcuffed.

According to a reconstruction given by accused Yih Hai Sung, the distance between the spot where he fired the pistol and the spot where Nakayama stood was about five or six ordinary paces. The distance was found incorrect because an examination by the Medico-Legal Laboratory of the powder marks on the wound of entry showed that the distance must have been about 5 centimetres. When a person commits a murder, he is usually over-excited. It is true that he will not lose valuable time in considering the distance of the shooting and to keep the fact carefully in mind. We cannot overlook the facts entirely because of the slight differences about the distance of the shooting during the reconstruction.

According to a statement made by witness Pan Chiao Yin, she saw a marine and another person walking in the same direction one behind the other. The statement made by accused Yih Hai Sung to the effect that he followed the marine is therefore not absolutely unsupported.

During the reconstruction given by witness Hu Ziang Wu, the latter pointed out that accused Yih Hai Sung escaped by the side of an electric pole and that the clothing worn by the escaping man was similar to that worn by a marine. This point has been explained by this Court as well as by the Court of First Instance in its judgment as being due to a mistake of judgment.

Besides, witnesses Chu Sun Fu (朱森甫) and Chi Ah Keng (纪阿根) stated during the hearings at the Court of First Instance that Yang Wen Dao seldom went to the Dong Nyi

1936年12月12日。下午译件。

涂有油脂，氧化过程会较慢。本案中的手枪表面涂有油脂，这种油脂本应对手枪起到防锈作用。然而，上诉人声称油脂加速了生锈。这与法医实验室报告中的陈述不符。此外，书页的破损也可能是由手枪在书内来回移动造成的，外部压力并非唯一原因。因此，上诉人不能以此点攻击原判。

第二点强调，叶海生（Yih Hai Sung）所作的供述和现场重建并非自愿。本院审查了一审法院的记录，发现虽然叶海生的各项供词并不完全一致，但并非在刑讯逼供下作出；且与事实相符。关于叶海生和证人胡祥武（Hu Ziang Wu）在一审法官面前进行的犯罪现场重建的法庭记录中，没有任何内容显示叶海生受到威胁、引诱、暴力、欺诈或其他非法手段的阻碍，从而无法自由地进行重建。上诉人的律师在场见证了重建过程，并认可记录无误且签了字。他们当时并未提及叶海生未被允许自由重建犯罪现场一事。上诉人在提起上诉后，如今怎能提出此说法？叶海生双手被铐在两名日本警察身上，这仅是一种安全措施；不能说他因此被铐而失去了自由。

根据被告叶海生所作的重建，他开枪地点与中山（Nakayama）站立地点之间的距离约为五六步普通步幅。经法医实验室对伤口入口处的火药痕迹进行检查，发现该距离有误，实际距离必须约为5厘米。人在实施谋杀时，通常处于极度兴奋状态。确实，他不会浪费宝贵时间去考虑射击距离并仔细记住这一事实。我们不能仅仅因为重建过程中关于射击距离的细微差异而完全忽视事实。

根据证人潘巧英（Pan Chiao Yin）的陈述，她看到一名海军陆战队员和另一人朝同一方向一前一后行走。因此，被告叶海生所称他跟随该海军陆战队员的说法并非完全没有依据。

在证人胡祥武（Hu Ziang Wu）进行的重建过程中，后者指出被告叶海生是从一根电线杆旁逃跑的，且逃跑者所穿衣物与海军陆战队员的服装相似。本院以及一审法院在判决中已解释这一点是由于判断失误所致。

此外，证人朱森甫和纪阿根在一审法院听证期间陈述，杨文道很少去东亚

Federation as he had been there only one or two times in all

that he attended to his duties at the Federation everyday

According to a statement made by witness Hung Wen Wei, between
7 and 11 p.m. November 9 last year, he was in the Federation
with Yang Wen Dao. After he (Hung) reached home, he was
informed by some boys that a Japanese marine had been murdered.
Next day, he told Yang Wen Dao of the matter.
Witness Hung Wen Wei and accused Yang Wen Dao
also stated that they learned of the murder three or four days
later from the newspapers. As there are likewise some
contradictory points in these statements, the evidence presented
by the witness Hung Wei Wei cannot be accepted.
In conclusion, with the exception of the case
against Chow Shou Yong (周守庸), which has been concluded
and requires no further discussion, the Court of First Instance
has regarded the murder of the Japanese marine Hideo Nakayama
by the appellants as a matter of great importance because the
murder was liable to give rise to trouble between China
and foreign nations. There is no possibility of granting
a pardon to the accused. Yih Hai Sung is the principal
culprit, while Yang Wen Dao was responsible for having planned
the murder. It is only reasonable that under Article 28,
Article 271, Section 1, Article 37, Section 1, Article 38,
Section 1, Paragraph 1 and 2, of the Criminal Code, the
accused are sentenced to death and deprived of civil rights
for life, while the pistol, the six rounds of ammunition,
the empty cartridge, the bullet and the book on Practical
Physics which was used to conceal a pistol were ordered to be
confiscated. As the reasons given in the appeal can hardly
be considered as logical, the case should therefore be dealt
with as above in accordance with Article 360 of the Code
of the Criminal Procedure. Procurator Ling Ngoo Min of
this Court has attended Court to deliver his views in this
case.

同盟会，因为他总共只去过一两次，而且他们从未见过被告叶海生或那名朝鲜人。将这些陈述与被告杨文道所称他每天在同盟会履行职责，或与洪文蔚在本院听证过程中作为证人出庭时所称杨文道一直在同盟会的陈述进行比较时，发现存在一些差异。根据证人洪文蔚的陈述，去年11月9日晚7点至11点间，他与杨文道一同在同盟会。他（洪）回家后，从一些男孩处得知一名日本海军陆战队员被杀。次日，他将此事告知杨文道。
证人洪文蔚和被告杨文道还陈述，他们是三四天后从报纸上得知谋杀案的。由于这些陈述中也存在一些矛盾之处，证人洪文蔚提供的证据不能被采信。
综上所述，除周守庸一案已结案且无需进一步讨论外，一审法院将上诉人谋杀日本海军陆战队员中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）一案视为重大事项，因为该谋杀案可能引发中外之间的纠纷。不可能对被告予以赦免。叶海生是主犯，而杨文道负责策划谋杀。根据《刑法》第28条、第271条第1款、第37条第1款、第38条第1款第1项和第2项，判处被告死刑并终身剥夺公民权利是合理的，同时下令没收用于藏匿手枪的手枪、六发子弹、空弹壳、子弹以及《实用物理学》一书。鉴于上诉理由很难被认为是合乎逻辑的，因此应根据《刑事诉讼法》第360条按上述方式处理本案。本院检察官凌牛民（Ling Ngoo Min，音译）出庭就本案发表意见。

October 1, 1936. Morning Translation /
Min Pao and other local newspapers :-
THE NAKAYAMA CASE.
Yang Vung Tao, Yih Hai Sung alias Siao Kwang-tung and Tseu Shou Yong are being charged by the International Settlement Police with the murder of a Japanese marine named Nakayama. The case has had several hearings at the Shanghai First Special District Court before Judges Chien Hung Nieh, Siao Sih Feng and Feng Shih Tuh.
At first it was announced that judgment would be delivered on June 17, but as it was necessary to ascertain whether the rust marks on the pistol corresponded with those in the hole excavated inside a book on physics for the purpose of concealing the pistol and whether the finger prints of Yang Vung Tao were identical with the finger prints found in the hole of the book, the case was remanded and all the exhibits were sent to the Medico-Legal Laboratory for further examination.
In the meantime, Yang Chien Chung(楊建中), an important witness in the case, appeared. The Court ordered that his finger prints be taken and submitted to the Medico-Legal Laboratory for examination with a view to ascertaining whether they corresponded with the marks found in the book. Later Chang Vung Hwa(張文華) and various other prisoners who were arrested in connection with the attempted assassination of Wang Ching Wei, the former President of the Executive Yuan, were brought before the Court for interrogation and confrontation with Yang Vung Tao. etc.
In short, the Judges trying the case have been very careful to make themselves acquainted with all the points, however trivial they may be. As the investigation has now been completed, the case will again come up for hearing at 2 p.m. to-day before Judge Chien (presiding) and Judges Siao and Feng.
The report of the Medico-Legal Laboratory has been already forwarded to the Court. A study of the report reveals that the Laboratory is not in a position to say definitely whether the rust marks on the pistol and those inside the hole of the book were identical, nor can it say that the finger prints of Yang Vung Tao and Yang Chien Chung were identical with those inside the hole of the book, because the marks of the finger prints inside the hole are wholly incomplete. If no question is raised by the Police or the accused regarding the report of the Medico-Legal Laboratory, it is probable that the lawyers will sum up their respective cases to-day.
The accused were arrested in the middle of April this year. According to Article 108 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the period of detention of an accused is not to exceed three months, but in case it is found necessary to extend the period of detention the Court is entitled to prolong it before its expiry. As the first extension of the detention period of these accused is about to expire, a further extension of two months was ordered by the Court yesterday. Yesterday both the accused and their lawyers were notified of this extension by the Court.
（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER 1 OCT 1936 CRIME BRANCH）

中山案。
杨文道（Yang Vung Tao）、叶海生（别名小广东）和周守庸被公共租界警方指控谋杀一名名为中山的日本海军陆战队员。该案在上海第一特区地方法院经过多次听证，主审法官为钱洪业（Chien Hung Nieh，音译）、萧世凤（Siao Sih Feng，音译）和冯士笃（Feng Shih Tuh，音译）。
起初宣布将于6月17日宣判，但由于需要确认手枪上的锈迹是否与为了藏匿手枪而在物理教科书内挖出的洞孔中的锈迹相符，以及杨文道的指纹是否与在该书洞孔中发现的指纹一致，案件被延期审理，所有证物被送往法医实验室进行进一步检查。
在此期间，该案的重要证人杨建中（Yang Chien Chung）出庭。法院命令提取其指纹并提交给法医实验室进行检查，以确定它们是否与书中发现的痕迹相符。随后，张文华（Chang Vung Hwa）及其他几名因企图刺杀前行政院院长汪精卫而被捕的囚犯被带上法庭接受讯问，并与杨文道等人当面对质。
简而言之，审理此案的法官非常谨慎，力求熟悉所有细节，无论其多么琐碎。由于调查现已完成，案件将于今天下午2点再次开庭审理，由钱法官（主审）以及萧法官和冯法官共同审理。
法医实验室的报告已送交法院。对该报告的研究显示，实验室无法明确说明手枪上的锈迹与书内洞孔中的锈迹是否相同，也无法断定杨文道和杨建中的指纹与书内洞孔中的指纹相同，因为洞孔内的指纹痕迹完全不完整。如果警方或被告对法医实验室的报告没有提出异议，律师们很可能今天将进行总结陈词。
被告于今年四月中旬被捕。根据《刑事诉讼法》第108条，被告的拘留期限不得超过三个月，但如果发现有必要延长拘留期，法院有权在期满前予以延长。由于这些被告的第一次拘留延长期即将届满，法院昨天命令再延长两个月。昨天，法院已将此延期通知被告及其律师。
（印章：副总监 1936年10月1日 刑事科）

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Saturday, October 3, 1936

Japanese May
Ask Indemnity

Judge Releases Text
Of Judgment Given
In Nakayama Case

Apparently satisfied by the death penalties pronounced on the alleged murderers of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party, Japanese authorities, through Consul-General K. Wakasugi, have informed Mayor Wu Te-chen at the City Government of Greater Shanghai that they reserve their rights to discuss the case diplomatically.

It is generally believed that the Japanese action was taken in order to reserve rights to demand indemnity or other assurances in connection with the murder, now that it has been ascertained that Nakayama was murdered by Chinese as implied in the court decision.

Text Released

Presiding Judge Dzien last night released the full text of the judgment which he pronounced on Yang Wen-tao and Yih Hai-sen (Chao Kwangtung) yesterday. He also explained the court findings and reasons for sentencing Yang and Yih to death and for acquitting Chow Sha-yung, the third accused.

Under the Chinese law of criminal procedure, Yang and Yih must file their appeal within 10 days upon receipt of the full text of the judgment while the prosecution is granted the same period to file its appeal against the acquittal of Chow.

Confessions True

Judge Dsien and his associates are convinced that Yih's earlier confessions were true and the Cantonese's claims that the statements were extracted through torture, being not confirmed by judicial physicians, were not exactly true. The court was also satisfied that Yang had instigated the murder. In connection with Chow's case, the evidence produced by the prosecution was not strong enough to warrant a conviction, the court ruled.

According to findings of the court, Yang was chairman of the Hung Zeng Mutual Aid Society while Yih was a member. The society was notorious as an "axe gang."

Sought Power

During November, 1934, Yang left Shanghai and the society was dissolved. When he returned a month later, Yang again organized a "Dong Yi" society and a "Dong Yi" Society with Yih. Yang served as chairman of both societies. Yih was a member. Owing to the limited number of members, the influence of the new organizations was far less than that of the Hung Zeng Mutual Aid Association.

By the end of October, 1935, Yang and Yih conspired to kill a Japanese officer or a marine in order to cause a panic during which they might gain a bigger influence in the Hongkew area. At 5 p.m. on November 3, they went to Darroch Road to view the area and in the evening on the 5th, they met at 71 Yungchill alley, Range Road, in the office of the "Dong Yi" Society to determine by lots who should carry out the mission. Yih drew one on which was the character "go."

Got A Pistol

At 8 p.m. on the 8th, Yang handed Yih a pistol, with which he went to Darroch Road. At 9 p.m., he saw a Japanese marine, Nayskama, walking there. Yih followed. When they reached near the mouth of Funglohli alley, Yih fired from the side towards the head of the Japanese, who fell at the report of the gun. Yih immediately ran into the alley, throwing the pistol (No. 24246) under an empty wooden shelter. He ran back to the Moon Palace.

He was arrested by police in April of this year in Tsingtao. On the 19th of the same month; Yang was arrested at 18 Tunganli, Tangshan Road. In his room, a green colored book on practical physics, hollowed in the center to conceal a gun, was found.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年10月3日，星期六

日本方面可能
要求赔偿

法官公布中山案
判决书全文

鉴于日本特别海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama） alleged 凶犯已被判处死刑，日本当局似乎对此表示满意。日本总领事若杉要（K. Wakasugi）已通知大上海市政府市长吴铁城，日方保留通过外交途径讨论此案的权利。

普遍看法认为，既然法院判决已确认中山系被中国人所杀，日本采取此举旨在保留就谋杀案要求赔偿或其他保证的权利。

公布文本

主审法官钱（Dzien）昨晚公布了其昨日对杨文涛和易海森（又名赵广东）宣判的判决书全文。他还解释了法庭的调查结果，以及判处杨、易二人死刑并宣告第三名被告周少庸无罪的理由。

根据中国刑事诉讼法，杨、易二人须在收到判决书全文后10天内提出上诉；检方亦获同等期限，可就周的无罪判决提出上诉。

供词属实

钱法官及其同僚确信易早前的供词属实，而该名广东人声称供词系刑讯逼供所得、且未获法医证实的说法并不完全属实。法庭亦确信杨煽动了此次谋杀。关于周的案件，法庭裁定检方提供的证据不足以支持定罪。

根据法庭调查结果，杨是“洪增互助社”的主席，易是该社成员。该社团以“斧头帮”恶名昭著。

谋求势力

1934年11月期间，杨离开上海，该社团随之解散。一个月后杨返回上海，再次与易组织了一个“东义”社和一个“东义”会（原文如此）。杨担任这两个社团的主席，易为成员。由于成员人数有限，新组织的影响力远不及洪增互助协会。

至1935年10月底，杨与易密谋杀害一名日本军官或水兵，以便制造恐慌，从而在虹口地区获得更大的影响力。11月3日下午5时，他们前往达罗克路（Darroch Road）察看地形；5日晚，他们在兰路（Range Road）永吉里71号的“东义”社办公室通过抽签决定由谁执行任务。易抽中了写有“去”字的签。

获得手枪

8日晚8时，杨交给易一把手枪，易携枪前往达罗克路。晚9时，他看见一名日本水兵中山（Nayskama，原文拼写有误，应为Nakayama）在那里行走。易尾随其后。当行至凤乐里（Funglohli alley，音译）巷口附近时，易从侧面朝该日本人的头部开枪，枪响后日本人倒地。易随即跑入巷内，将手枪（编号24246）扔在一个空木棚下。他跑回月宫舞厅（Moon Palace）。

今年4月，他在青岛被警方逮捕。同月19日，杨在唐山路同安里18号被捕。在其房间内，发现一本绿色封面的实用物理学书籍，中间被挖空以藏匿枪支。

APPEALS

Wen-tao and Yih Hai-sen, alias
"Shao Kwangtung," who were sen-
tenced to death in the Nakayama
Case, are preparing to file appeals

《上海星期时报》，1936年10月4日

中山案
上诉

据可靠消息获悉，在中山案中被判处死刑的杨文涛和易海森（别名“邵广东”）正准备对判决提出上诉。
目前尚不知警方是否会对第三名被告周作云（Chou Tso-yun，音译，前文作周少庸/周泽荣等）的无罪判决提出上诉，但据报道，其案件极有可能不会上诉。

CHINA DAILY HERALD, SUNDAY, OCTOBER 4, 1936.

Judge Releases Text
Of Judgment Given
In Nakayama Case

Japanese authorities through
Consul-General K. Wakasugi,
have informed Mayor Wu Te-
chen at the City Government
of Greater Shanghai that they
reserve their rights to discuss
the case diplomatically.
Presiding Judge Dzien releas-
ed the full text of the judg-
ment which he pronounced on
Yang Wen-tao and Yih Hai sen
(Shau Kwangtung) on Friday. He
also explained the court find-
ings and reasons for sentencing
Yang and Yin to death and for
acquitting Chow Sha-yung, the
third accused.
Judge Dzien and his asso-
ciates are convinced that Yih's
earlier confessions were true
and the Cantonese's claims
that the statements were ex-
tracted through torture, being
not confirmed by judicial physi-
cians were not exactly true.
The court was also satisfied
that Yang had instigated the
murder. In connection with
Chow's case the evidence pro-
duced by the prosecution was
not strong enough to warrant
a conviction, the court ruled.

《字林西报周刊》（China Daily Herald），1936年10月4日，星期日

法官公布中山案
判决书全文

日本当局通过总领事若杉要（K. Wakasugi）通知大上海市政府市长吴铁城，日方保留通过外交途径讨论此案的权利。
主审法官钱（Dzien）公布了其周五对杨文涛和易海森（Shau Kwangtung，音译）宣判的判决书全文。他还解释了法庭的调查结果，以及判处杨和尹（Yin，原文误植，应为易）死刑并宣告第三名被告周少庸无罪的理由。
钱法官及其同僚确信易早前的供词属实，而该名广东人声称供词系刑讯逼供所得、且未获法医证实的说法并不完全属实。
法庭亦确信杨煽动了此次谋杀。关于周的案件，法庭裁定检方提供的证据不足以支持定罪。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3, 1936

Nakayama Case
Concludes with
Death Sentence

Two Cantonese Will Pay the
Supreme Penalty

ACQUITTAL OF THIRD
PRISONER

Two of the three Cantonese accused of being concerned in the murder of H. Nakayama, a Japanese sailor, in Darroch Road, on November 9 last year, were sentenced to pay the death penalty by the First Special District Court, with Judges Tsien, Feng, and Hsiao sitting, yesterday. They were Yang Ven-tao, a former Shanghai shipping mgr. and Yih Hai-sen, known in Chinese circles as "Little Cantonese," who formerly was a cabaret manager in the Hongkew District.

The third Cantonese accused in the case, Chow Zeu-yoong, was acquitted. Chow was, until his arrest, employed at the Continental Ballroom in Ningpo Road.

After pronouncing judgment Judge Tsien told Yang and Yih that they may appeal against the decision within ten days after receipt of a written judgment. The detention of Chow was ordered, pending a possible appeal by the police.

《字林西报》，1936年10月3日，星期六

中山案
以死刑判决
结案

两名广东人将付出
最高代价

第三名囚犯
获释

去年11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）涉嫌参与谋杀日本水兵H.中山（H. Nakayama）的三名广东籍被告中，有两人昨日被第一特区地方法院判处死刑。审理此案的法官为钱、冯和萧。他们是杨文涛（Yang Ven-tao，原文拼写有误），前上海航运经理；以及易海森，在华界圈子中被称为“小广东”，前虹口区舞厅经理。

本案第三名广东籍被告周泽荣（Chow Zeu-yoong，音译）被宣告无罪。周在被捕前受雇于宁波路的大陆舞厅（Continental Ballroom）。

宣判后，钱法官告知杨和易，他们可在收到书面判决书后十天内对判决提出上诉。鉴于警方可能提出上诉，命令继续羁押周。

RECEIVES DEATH PENALTY
847
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3. 1936
Yih Hai-sen alias "Shao Kwangtung" is shown being led out of the First Special District Court under a heavy escort of Japanese constables of the S. M. P., after being sentenced to death by Judge Ixien yesterday afternoon upon being found guilty of being concerned in the murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party on Darroch Road on November 9, last.
[Domei.
Officials Satisfied With
Nakayama Case Verdict
Commander Of Naval Landing Party, Consul And
Naval Attache Praise Efforts Of S.M.P.;
Need For Protection Stressed
Voicing satisfaction at the death sentences imposed on two of the three defendants charged with the murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama, Japanese naval and diplomatic officials yesterday united in paying tribute to the untiring efforts of officials of the Shanghai Municipal Council in securing the convictions.
"From the very outset, I was convinced that Yang Wen-tao and Yeh Hai-sen, who were condemned to death, were guilty," Rear-Admiral Eijiro Kondo, Commander of the Japanese Special Naval Landing Party, said yesterday afternoon.
"As Commander of the Landing Party, I cannot but feel deeply touched at the thought that at last the soul of Warrant Officer Nakayama can now rest in peace.
"I regret, however, that this landing party finds itself compelled to take measures for self-protection in view of the recurrent incidents.
"I wish to express my highest appreciation of the efforts exerted by the officials of the Shanghai Municipal Council during the last several months," he stated.
Consul's Opinion
Pointing out that "a readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations cannot be hoped for so long as the lives and property of Japanese residents are in constant danger," Mr. Kaname Wakasugi, Japanese Consul-General, last night urged Chinese officials to "stamp out anti-Japanese terrorism and those who profit from these activities."
"Both the Japanese people and the Government were highly indignant at the murder of Warrant Officer Nakayama because it was different from an ordinary crime in that it was a carefully prepared plot aiming at the killing of a member of the Japanese navy in uniform.
S.M.C. Praised
"Though we were convinced from the very outset that Chinese were responsible for the outrage, we patiently watched the steps taken by the Chinese authorities for almost a year. During that period, various delays occurred, but at last the material proof and witnesses provided by the Shanghai Municipal Council have secured the conviction of Yang Wen-tao and of Yeh Haisheng.
"It has also been established that the principal in the Kayau murder was a Chinese with secret society affiliations.
"Moreover, there is no doubt that Chinese were also responsible for the recent murder of another sailor on Haining Road.
"A readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations cannot be hoped for so long as the lives and property of Japanese residents are in constant danger because of the continued existence and the activities of terrorist organizations aimed at Japanese nationals.
"That is why I believe that the Chinese authorities, not only should punish those responsible for these various affairs, but should determinedly stamp out anti-Japanese terrorism and those who profit by these activities so that all roots of evil hampering amicable Sino-Japanese relations may be eradicated," Mr. Wakasugi declared.
Reserve Demands
The Consul-General yesterday afternoon also notified both the Shanghai Municipal Council and the Municipality of Greater Shanghai that he "reserved all rights" regarding possible demands to be made in connection with the Haining Road and Kayau cases in view of their "obvious relation to the Nakayama affair."
"The conviction of Yang and Yeh is significant not only because it reveals the existence of strong and sinister secret societies, which so far have been immune from prosecution by the Chinese authorities," Lieut.-Commander Matao Okino, assistant Japanese naval attache, who represented the Imperial Navy in the investigations, said last night.
"I am convinced that to-day's result was solely due to the untiring activities of the members of the Special Political Branch of the S.M.P.
"Special credit should be given to the efforts of the Japanese S.M.P. officers who made the arrests," he added.

被判死刑
847
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年10月3日，星期六

易海森，别名“邵广东”，昨日下午因被认定参与去年11月9日在达罗克路谋杀日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄一案罪名成立，被钱（Ixien，原文拼写有误，应为Tsien/Dzien）法官判处死刑。图中显示他在大量上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）日本巡捕的严密押解下，走出第一特区地方法院。
[同盟社]

官员对中山案判决
表示满意

海军陆战队指挥官、领事及海军武官赞扬工部局警务处的努力；强调保护的必要性

日本海军和外交官员昨日一致赞扬上海公共租界工部局官员在确保定罪方面不懈的努力，并对三名被控谋杀日本海军准尉中山秀雄的被告中有两人被判处死刑表示满意。
日本特别海军陆战队司令近藤英次郎（Eijiro Kondo）海军少将昨日下午表示：“从一开始，我就确信被判处死刑的杨文涛和叶海森（Yeh Hai-sen，即易海森）是有罪的。”
“作为陆战队司令，想到中山准尉的在天之灵终于得以安息，我不禁深受感动。
“然而，鉴于事件频发，本陆战队不得不采取自我保护措施，对此我深感遗憾。
“我对上海公共租界工部局官员在过去几个月中的努力表示最高赞赏。”他说。

领事的观点

日本总领事若杉要（Kaname Wakasugi）昨晚指出，“只要日本居民的生命财产处于持续危险之中，就难以指望中日关系得到调整”，并敦促中国官员“铲除反日恐怖主义及从中牟利者”。
“日本人民和政府对于中山准尉被谋杀一事感到极为愤慨，因为这不同于普通犯罪，而是一个精心策划的阴谋，旨在杀害一名身穿制服的日本海军人员。

赞扬工部局

“虽然我们从一开始就确信中国人应对这一暴行负责，但我们耐心地观察中国当局采取的行动近一年。在此期间，出现了各种延误，但最终，上海公共租界工部局提供的物证和证人确保了杨文涛和叶海生（Yeh Haisheng，即易海森）的定罪。
“此外，已确定加藤（Kayau，音译，可能指另一案件受害者）谋杀案的主犯是一名具有秘密社会背景的中国人。
“而且，毫无疑问，最近在海宁路发生的另一名水兵被谋杀案也是中国人所为。
“只要针对日本国民的恐怖组织持续存在并进行活动，导致日本居民的生命财产处于持续危险之中，就难以指望中日关系得到调整。
“因此，我认为中国当局不仅应惩罚对这些各类事件负责的人，还应坚决铲除反日恐怖主义及从中牟利者，以便根除阻碍中日友好关系的一切祸根。”若杉先生宣称。

保留索赔权利

昨日下午，总领事还通知上海公共租界工部局和大上海市政府，鉴于海宁路案和加藤（Kayau）案与中山案有“明显关联”，他就这些案件可能提出的要求“保留一切权利”。
代表帝国海军参与调查的日本助理海军武官奥野又雄（Matao Okino，音译）中校昨晚表示：“杨和叶的定罪意义重大，不仅因为它揭示了那些迄今免受中国当局起诉的强大而邪恶的秘密社会的存在。”
“我确信，今天的成果完全归功于上海公共租界工部局警务处特别政治部的不懈努力。
“应当特别表彰实施逮捕的日本籍工部局警务处官员的努力。”他补充道。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3, 1936
16869
Death Penalty Imposed
On Shao Kwangtung And
Yang In Nakayama Case

Chou Tso-yun Is Found Not Guilty; Judge Takes
One Minute To Read Out Judgment; Accused
Have 10 Days In Which To Appeal

GENERAL TENSION EASES AS VERDICT
PRONOUNCED ON NOV. 9 MURDER

Bringing to a close a trial and a re-trial lasting five months, and easing the general tension existing on account of the indefiniteness of the whole affair, Judge Dzien yesterday imposed the death sentence on both Yih Hai-sen, alias "Shao Kwangtung," 28-year-old alleged underworld figure, and Yang Wen-tao, 42-year-old Cantonese, former employee of the China Navigation Company, upon finding them guilty of being concerned in the murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party, on Darroch Road, on the night of November 9, last. At the same time Judge Dzien pronounced Chou Tso-yun, the third suspect and an employee of a cabaret, not guilty before a crowded courtroom in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon.

The conviction of both "Shao Kwangtung" and Yang did not come as a surprise to officials who filled the courtroom yesterday and Chou's acquittal was also expected. "Shao Kwangtung's" and Yang's lawyers indicated yesterday that an appeal against the death penalties would be filed within the prescribed time limit.

The courtroom was filled to overflowing long before the hour set by Judge Dzien for the pronouncement of the judgment. A general calm, however, prevailed both in the courtroom and in the compound, where, as on previous occasions, officers of the Reserve Unit, S.M.P., were on duty. Walking into Courtroom No. 1 at four minutes past two, accompanied by two other judges and a prosecutor, Judge Dzien sat down, unwrapped his file and then stood up and pronounced the sentence, the whole proceedings being over by six minutes past two.

A general hum sounded through the courtroom as the judges prepared to leave and handcuffs were placed back on the hands of the accused by their guards, Japanese constables of the S.M.P., who led them through the crowded courtyard.

Crime 11 Months Old

The conviction of the two men in connection with the crime, which occurred almost 11 months ago, partly cleared up one mystery surrounding the first of a series of murders of Japanese citizens in China by an alleged secret Chinese political society.

The announcement on Thursday afternoon, at the conclusion of the last hearing of the re-trial of the three men, that sentence would be handed down yesterday afternoon came as a surprise to all present, as it is the usual procedure of the court to adjourn cases for at least one week for judgment, or in the case of petty crimes to sentence the criminals immediately. On Thursday great precaution was taken by the Japanese Naval Landing Party to prevent any further terroristic outrages, as the killing of Kosaku Kayau, Japanese sea-food broker, took place on Dixwell Road, on the night of July 10, a few hours after the prosecutor closed his summing up of the original case. Instead of delivering judgment as expected on July 17, Judge Dzien ordered the trial to be re-opened.

Since then very little or almost no new evidence was introduced and the close of the case yesterday with the pronouncement of the death sentences came as an end to the first part of the legal battle.

The second stage of the legal battle will open in the High Court when the appeal of "Shao Kwangtung" and Yang against their death sentences will be heard. Whether or not the police will appeal against the decision of the court in acquitting Chou has not been decided as yet.

With the "Nakayama Murder Trial" concluded, attention will now be centred on the trial of three suspects held by officers of the Bureau of Public Safety in connection with the murder of Kosaku Kayau. The Chinese authorities have stated that they have in their custody the actual murderer.

Arrested Five Months Ago

The murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama remained a complete mystery for several months after the killing and it was not until April that the police arrested "Shao Kwangtung" and Yang and other suspects. The Japanese Consular Police also took into custody at the time a Korean named, "Jack," who was alleged to have been connected with the crime. Complete secrecy was maintained by the authorities regarding the arrest of the men and they were all at first questioned in camera hearings.

The first public hearing was held on May 1, when "Shao Kwangtung" told the court that he was present at the shooting and saw Yang Wen-tao actually shoot the Japanese marine. He also implicated the Korean as being at the scene of the crime. Various statements made by "Shao Kwangtung" were checked by police with witnesses of the killing and it was ascertained that a man wearing a short jacket had shot at the marine, while "Shao Kwangtung" had stated that Yang had been wearing a long gown at the time.

Admits Killing

At the next hearing on May 6, "Shao Kwangtung" completely denied his previous statements, exonerated Yang and confessed that he murdered Nakayama himself. A witness brought to the court by the defence alleged a frame-up on the part of the police informers in order to collect a reward. At the time, and at the previous hearing, Judge Dzien requested that the Japanese Consular Police bring the Korean, Jack, to court to testify, this however, was not done until a couple of months later.

A further bombshell was thrown into the courtroom at the hearing on May 20, when "Shao Kwangtung" alleged that the Nakayama killing had been planned in order to create a new political incident. He outlined how the plot was hatched by the members of the Tung Yin Association, an alleged philanthropic organization and that in the drawing of lots it fell to him to do the actual killing. This time "Shao Kwangtung" again implicated Yang as having supplied the pistol to him. Yang continued to maintain his innocence.

Torture Alleged

The following week "Shao Kwangtung" denied all his previous confessions and allegations and stated that he had been forced to make them after being tortured by police. He exhibited his alleged wounds to the court and stated that he tried to end his life in his cell. He was ordered to be examined by court physicians, who found that he had not been hurt to any extent.

The trial was gradually drawing towards the close, but on July 10, after a speech by the prosecutor stating that he did not think the men guilty, Kosaku Kayau was murdered. Feeling ran high among the Japanese and tension reached a high pitch on the morning of July 17, when judgment was to be handed down. Judge Dzien however, announced then that he was not satisfied with certain portions of the evidence and ordered the trial to be re-opened. Tension eased slightly, but again rose to a high pitch following the Chengtu outrage, the Pakhoi incident, as well as the shooting of the Japanese constable in Hankow.

The local situation reached fever pitch with the fatal shooting of one marine and the wounding of two others on Haining Road near Woosung Road, on the night of September 23. Three suspects are being held in connection with the shooting and will be brought before the First Special District Court this morning. In authoritative circles of the police it is believed that the men had nothing whatsoever to do with the killing.

Investigations of the police in the Nakayama killing led them to Tsingtao, where "Shao Kwangtung" was arrested. His mother and sister were also taken into custody, but later released. Several other Chinese were held for questioning, but released shortly after. The crime was reconstructed on Darroch Road several occasions with and without the presence of the accused. Once "Shao Kwangtung" himself demonstrated how he did the shooting. Yesterday after sentence was passed "Shao Kwangtung" seemed to be more cool and collected than at any previous hearings. After hearing his fate he said that he was quite satisfied and did not care what happened to him.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年10月3日，星期六
16869
邵广东与杨文涛在中山案中
被判处死刑

周作云被判无罪；法官宣读判决书耗时一分钟；被告有十天时间提出上诉

随着11月9日谋杀案宣判，普遍紧张局势得以缓解

昨日，季恩（Dzien）法官结束了历时五个月的初审及重审，并缓解了因整个事件悬而未决而存在的普遍紧张局势。季恩法官裁定28岁的 alleged 黑社会人物伊海森（又名“邵广东”）以及42岁的广东人、前英商中国航业公司（China Navigation Company）雇员杨文涛犯有参与谋杀日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）罪，该谋杀案发生于去年11月9日晚的达罗克路（Darroch Road）。季恩法官对二人均判处死刑。与此同时，昨日下午在第一特区地方法院座无虚席的法庭上，季恩法官宣布第三名嫌疑人、某歌舞厅雇员周作云无罪。

昨日挤满法庭的官员们对“邵广东”和杨文涛的定罪并不感到意外，周作云的获释也在意料之中。“邵广东”和杨文涛的律师昨日表示，将在规定期限内针对死刑判决提出上诉。

早在季恩法官预定宣判的时间之前，法庭内就已人满为患。然而，法庭内及大院里都保持着一片平静，公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）后备队警官像以往一样在此执勤。下午两点零四分，季恩法官在另外两名法官和一名检察官的陪同下走进第一法庭，坐下后打开卷宗，随即起立宣读判决，整个程序于两点零六分结束。

当法官们准备离庭时，法庭内响起一阵嗡嗡声，法警——即公共租界工部局的日本巡捕——给被告重新戴上手铐，并带领他们穿过拥挤的庭院。

案发已11个月

这两名男子与近11个月前发生的罪行有关，对他们的定罪部分澄清了围绕一系列据称由中国秘密政治社团实施的在华日本人谋杀案中的首起案件的神秘谜团之一。

周四下午，在三人的重审最后一次听证会结束时，法庭宣布将于昨日下午宣判，这一消息令在场所有人感到意外，因为法院的通常做法是将案件休庭至少一周以待判决，或者在轻微犯罪案件中立即对罪犯量刑。周四，日本海军陆战队采取了严密的预防措施，以防发生进一步的恐怖暴行，因为在检察官结束对原案的总结陈词几小时后，日本海鲜经纪人加屋小作（Kosaku Kayau）于7月10日晚在狄思威路（Dixwell Road）被杀。季恩法官并未如预期在7月17日宣判，而是下令重审此案。

此后，几乎没有或完全没有引入新证据，昨日以宣读死刑判决告终的案件标志着这场法律斗争第一部分的结束。

法律斗争的第二阶段将在高等法院展开，届时将审理“邵广东”和杨文涛针对其死刑判决提出的上诉。警方是否会对法院宣告周作云无罪的决定提出上诉，目前尚未决定。

随着“中山谋杀案审判”的结束，注意力现在将集中在公共安全局警官拘留的三名嫌疑人的审判上，他们与加屋小作谋杀案有关。中国当局已声明，实际凶手已在他们的羁押之下。

五个月前被捕

中山秀雄准尉被杀后，该谋杀案在数月内一直是个完全的谜团，直到四月警方才逮捕了“邵广东”、杨文涛及其他嫌疑人。日本领事警察当时还拘留了一名名叫“杰克”（Jack）的朝鲜人，据称他与该罪行有关。当局对逮捕这些人严守秘密，起初所有审讯均在不公开听证中进行。

第一次公开听证会于5月1日举行，当时“邵广东”告诉法庭，他在枪击现场，并亲眼看到杨文涛开枪射杀那名日本海军陆战队员。他还牵连那名朝鲜人在犯罪现场。“邵广东”所作的各项陈述经警方与谋杀案证人核对，查明是一名身穿短夹克的男子向海军陆战队员开枪，而“邵广东”曾声称杨文涛当时身穿长袍。

承认杀人

在5月6日的下一次听证会上，“邵广东”完全否认了他先前的陈述，为杨文涛开脱，并供认是他自己杀害了中山。辩方传唤到庭的一名证人指控警方线人为获取赏金而设局陷害。当时以及在前一次听证会上，季恩法官要求日本领事警察将朝鲜人杰克带到庭上作证，但这直到两个月后才得以实现。

5月20日的听证会上，法庭再次受到震撼，“邵广东”声称杀害中山是为了制造新的政治事件而被策划的。他概述了该阴谋是如何由同寅会（Tung Yin Association，一个据称的慈善组织）成员策划的，以及在抽签中轮到他实施实际杀戮。这一次，“邵广东”再次牵连杨文涛，称是其向他提供了手枪。杨文涛继续坚持自己无罪。

指控遭受酷刑

接下来的一周，“邵广东”否认了他之前所有的供词和指控，并称他是在遭受警察酷刑后被迫作出的。他向法庭展示了他所谓的伤口，并称他曾在牢房中试图自杀。法庭命令法医对他进行检查，医生发现他并未受到任何程度的伤害。

审判逐渐走向尾声，但在7月10日，在检察官发表讲话称他认为这些人无罪之后，加屋小作被杀。日本人情绪高涨，7月17日上午原定宣判时，紧张局势达到高潮。然而，季恩法官当时宣布他对某些证据部分不满意，并下令重审此案。紧张局势略有缓解，但在成都惨案、北海事件以及汉口日本巡捕被枪击事件发生后，紧张局势再次升至高点。

9月23日晚，在靠近吴淞路的海宁路上，一名海军陆战队员被枪杀，另两名受伤，当地局势达到白热化。三名嫌疑人因该枪击案被拘留，将于今天上午被提审至第一特区地方法院。警方权威人士认为，这些人与该杀人案毫无关系。

警方对中山谋杀案的调查将他们引至青岛，在那里逮捕了“邵广东”。他的母亲和妹妹也被拘留，但随后获释。另有几名中国人被拘留问话，但不久后释放。警方在达罗克路多次重建犯罪现场，有时被告在场，有时不在。有一次，“邵广东”亲自演示了他如何开枪。昨日宣判后，“邵广东”似乎比以往任何一次听证会都更加冷静和镇定。听完自己的命运后，他表示相当满意，并不在乎自己会发生什么。

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, OCTOBER 3, 1936
Support Of Entire
Nation Urged
In Crisis
NO PLACE HELD
FOR LIGHT TALK
Attitude Of Defeatism
Deplored; Sacrifice
May Be Necessary

NANKING, Oct. 2.—(Central):—A frank and outspoken public statement setting forth the extremely explosive clouds which hover above the political horizon of China and Japan and appealing to both Chinese and Japanese people to do their utmost to avert the present crisis was issued today by the leading vernaculars of Nanking and Shanghai.

The declaration outlines in detail the gravity of the present Sino-Japanese deadlock and its disastrous consequences on both nations if the current extremely unhappy state of affairs were allowed to take its own course.

Stating that as China is now confronted with an unprecedented crisis all Chinese citizens should unwaveringly share the responsibilities of the country, the manifesto warns the public against any rash action which may further aggravate the situation. “We should,” the message says, “stand together and adhere to the concrete national policy and assist the government in suppressing all short-sighted anti-foreign acts.”

Calm Urged

The manifesto further exhorts the public not to get unduly excited over the present uncertainty.

“As we should take the future existence into consideration,” it proceeds, “we should not talk lightly of breaking off our relations with Japan just to appease our momentary impulse. On the other hand, we should not adopt a defeatist attitude and leave the destiny of the nation in the hands of fate.”

“For China’s present foreign relations are in no way similar to those of several years ago. Once she breaks off with another country it would be tantamount to gambling the existence of the nation to the last straw, and there is no way of retracting.

“Should a rupture occur between China and Japan, the situation would be as serious as just pictured. Once the hostilities were started and should China be forced to surrender it would mean endorsing a pledge of giving up her own independence. In that event our posterity would be left to suffer and chances of national revival would be nil.

“It is therefore imperative that we should consider the rupture of diplomatic relations as the last resort. Meanwhile we should still entertain the hope that some satisfactory solution to the deadlock may be reached. But should the last resort fail, the whole populace should not hesitate to lay down their lives for their fatherland.”

Chinese Not Anti-Japanese

Turning its appeal to the Japanese authorities and Japanese people the statement asserts that it is grossly unjust to accuse the Chinese people of being anti-Japanese just because of the outbreak of the recent Chengtu, Pakhoi, Hankow and Shanghai incidents.

Although the relations between the two countries have become more strained now, the statement explains, the Japanese nationals residing in China have been doing their business as usual during the last four or five days, and no unfortunate incidents occurred.

Oct. 2.—(Reuters).—The Government’s “intentions” to China will be conveyed to Mr. S. Kawagoe, Ambassador to China, by Ijima, Director of the Bureau, according to an announcement today by the spokesman of the Foreign Office.

A mission to dispatch Mr. Ijima to China was reached after a conference between high officials, who discussed developments in the Sino-Japanese situation based on reports received.

Those who participated in the conference which was held prior to a meeting of the Cabinet were Mr. Koki Hirota, the Premier, Admiral Nagano, the Navy Minister, Mr. H. Arita, the Foreign Minister and Mr. Umetsu, the Vice-Minister of War.

Ijima Here On 6th

G. Oct. 2.—(Central).—Mr. Kuwashima is expected to arrive in Nanking on October 6, via Kobe for Shanghai tomorrow.

Responsibility Shifted

Oct. 2.—(Reuters).—Whether the Sino-Japanese negotiations had recently been successful, the spokesman of the Foreign Office, in an interview with correspondents today, said he did not know; everything depended on the attitude of Japan.

He had no definite information as to when General Chiang Kai-shek, President of the Executive Yuan, would return to Nanking, but he understood that the Chinese capital was preparing to celebrate the unification of China, and he envisaged the Generalissimo making a triumphal entry into Nanking in the manner of Signor Mussolini’s entry into Rome.

During the interview, the spokesman was called away for a conference with other senior officials of the Foreign Office. He was absent for ten minutes, and, when he returned, read the following statement:—

“As Mr. Arita (the Foreign Minister) said to pressmen on September 28, the present Sino-Japanese negotiations are grave. China is at the cross-roads. The Japanese Government is conducting the negotiations with a careful attitude. At the same time, the situation is grave. Therefore we recognize that it is necessary to convey Japan’s real intentions to General Chiang Kai-shek and General Chang Chun (the Chinese Foreign Minister).

“We exchange telegrams with Mr. Kawagoe (the Japanese Ambassador to China), but sometimes these do not convey our full meaning. Therefore the Minister for Foreign Affairs has decided to send Mr. Kuwajima (Director of the East Asia Bureau of the Foreign Office) to convey the Japanese Government’s intentions to Mr. Kawagoe.”

2 Defendants Franco Named
In Nakayama Head Of New
Case Get Death Rebel State

Yang, Yih Draw Extreme Induction Ceremony Seen
Penalty In Shang- As Omen Of Fascist
hai Court Victory

Before a courtroom crowded with police, Japanese plainclothes men, newspaper reporters and Chinese relatives of the accused, Judge Daien, presiding over a tribunal in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon, sentenced Yang Wen-tao, former shipping clerk, and Yih Hai-seng (Hsiao Kwangtung), one-time cabaret manager and dancing instructor, to the death penalty for the murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama, Japanese blue-jacket, on November 9, 1935.

Chow Sha-yung, cabaret manager, also accused of implication in the slaying, was found not guilty but will be detained in custody pending the period of appeal. It was understood last night, however, that the police will not appeal against the judgment in his case and it will probably be only a matter of a week or two before he is once again a free man.

Yang Unmoved

Yang received the sentence with the same stoicism that has featured his every appearance in court. The same smirk he has worn at every one of the 21 sessions held since he was arrested last April played over his face. Asked if he was satisfied with the sentence, he mumbled a few words that were audible only to the strong Japanese police guard standing near him.

Yih, however, broke down at this and wept for about 10 minutes.

BURGOS, Oct. 2.—(Havas).—At solemn ceremony held here yesterday morning, General Cabanellas, President of the National Defense Junta, invested General Francisco Franco with the powers of “Head of the Spanish State” on behalf of the Burgos Government, and yesterday afternoon General Franco, presiding over a meeting of Government officials, decided that the Despatch Junta would nevertheless retain its full powers.

Observers pointed out that General Franco now possesses dictatorial powers as least as important as those of any existing dictator, but declared that the outstanding leader of the insurgent movement asked that his title be “Head of the State” as he allegedly dislikes hearing the title of “dictator.” The observers also stressed that the new decision implies the fact that nationalists are now assured of victory, since it was generally anticipated that General Franco would be invested with his new rank only after the conquest of Madrid.

Fall Of Capital Predicted

Military experts here declare that nationalist troops will be the masters of Madrid within three or four weeks. They state that 150,000 men in rebel ranks are increasing their pressure on all fronts with the view to completely encircling the Capital. 《字林西报》，1936年10月3日，星期六
呼吁举国支持
以渡危机
轻率言论无立足之地
痛斥失败主义态度；
牺牲或属必要

南京，10月2日电（中央社）：——南京和上海的主要中文报纸今日发表了一份坦率而直言不讳的公开声明，阐述了笼罩在中日政治地平线上的极具爆炸性的阴云，并呼吁中日两国人民竭尽全力避免当前的危机。

该宣言详细概述了当前中日僵局的严重性，以及如果听任目前这种极其不幸的事态自行发展，将对两国造成的灾难性后果。

声明指出，鉴于中国正面临前所未有的危机，所有中国公民应坚定不移地分担国家责任，同时警告公众不要采取任何可能进一步加剧局势的鲁莽行动。“我们应当，”文告称，“团结一致，坚持具体的国家政策，协助政府镇压一切短视的反外行为。”

呼吁冷静

宣言进一步劝诫公众不要因当前的不确定性而过度激动。

“考虑到未来的生存，”文告继续说道，“我们不应为了平息一时的冲动而轻言与日本断绝关系。另一方面，我们也不应采取失败主义的态度，将国家的命运交给天命。”

“因为中国目前的外交关系与几年前截然不同。一旦与另一国断交，就等于将国家的存亡孤注一掷，且无法收回成命。

“如果中日之间发生破裂，局势将如前所述般严峻。一旦战端开启，若中国被迫投降，则意味着签署放弃自身独立的承诺。在那种情况下，我们的后代将遭受苦难，民族复兴的机会将为零。

“因此，我们必须将断绝外交关系视为最后手段。同时，我们仍应抱有希望，认为僵局可能会得到某种令人满意的解决。但如果最后手段失效，全体民众应毫不犹豫地为祖国献出生命。”

中国人并非反日

该声明在向日本当局和日本人民发出呼吁时断言，仅因最近成都、北海、汉口和上海事件的发生就指责中国人民反日，是极不公正的。

声明解释说，尽管两国关系目前变得更加紧张，但在过去四五天里，居住在中国的日本国民一直照常经商，未发生任何不幸事件。

10月2日电（路透社）：——据外交部发言人今日宣布，局局长饭岛（Ijima）将向驻华大使川越茂（S. Kawagoe）先生传达政府对中国之“意图”。

在高级官员会议之后，作出了派遣饭岛先生前往中国的任务安排，这些官员根据收到的报告讨论了中日局势的发展。

参加在内阁会议之前举行的此次会议的有：首相广田弘毅（Koki Hirota）、海军大臣永野（Nagano）上将、外相有田八郎（H. Arita）和陆军次官梅津（Umetsu）。

饭岛将于6日抵达

广州，10月2日电（中央社）：——预计桑岛（Kuwashima）先生将于10月6日经神户抵沪后到达南京。

责任转移

10月2日电（路透社）：——外交部发言人在今日接受记者采访时说，他不知道近期中日谈判是否成功；一切取决于日本的态度。

他没有关于行政院院长蒋介石将军何时返回南京的确切消息，但他获悉中国首都正准备庆祝中国统一，并设想委员长将以墨索里尼先生进入罗马的方式凯旋进入南京。

在采访过程中，发言人被叫去与其他外交部高级官员开会。他离开了十分钟，回来后宣读了以下声明：——

“正如外相有田先生在9月28日对记者所说，当前的中日谈判十分严峻。中国处于十字路口。日本政府正以谨慎的态度进行谈判。同时，局势严峻。因此，我们认为有必要向蒋介石将军和张群将军（中国外交部长）传达日本的真实意图。

“我们与川越先生（日本驻华大使）交换电报，但有时这些电报未能充分传达我们的意思。因此，外务大臣决定派遣久慈间（Kuwajima，外务省东亚局局长）先生向川越先生传达日本政府的意图。”

两名被告被判死刑
中山案中杨、易获极刑
新叛军首领佛朗哥就职
被视为法西斯胜利之兆

上海法庭判处杨文涛、易海生（即萧广东）死刑

昨天下午，在第一特区法院的一个挤满了警察、日本便衣侦探、报社记者以及被告中国亲属的法庭上，主审法官戴恩（Daien）判处前航运职员杨文涛和前舞厅经理兼舞蹈教师易海生（萧广东）死刑，罪名是于1935年11月9日谋杀日本水兵中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）准尉。

同样被指控参与该谋杀案的舞厅经理周少庸（Chow Sha-yung）被判无罪，但在上诉期间将被拘留。然而，昨晚据悉，警方不会对其案件判决提出上诉，他可能只需再过一两周即可重获自由。

杨无动于衷

杨以一贯出现在法庭上的那种坚忍态度接受了判决。自去年四月被捕以来，他在21次庭审中脸上始终挂着的那丝冷笑再次浮现。当被问及是否对判决满意时，他咕哝了几句，只有站在他身边的强壮日本警 guard 才能听见。

然而，易在此刻崩溃，哭了大约10分钟。

布尔戈斯，10月2日电（哈瓦斯社）：——昨天上午在这里举行的庄严仪式上，国防委员会主席卡瓦内拉斯（Cabanellas）将军代表布尔戈斯政府授予弗朗西斯科·佛朗哥（Francisco Franco）将军“西班牙国家元首”的权力；昨天下午，佛朗哥将军主持政府官员会议，决定政务委员会仍将保留其全部权力。

观察家们指出，佛朗哥将军现在拥有的独裁权力至少与任何现存独裁者一样重要，但宣称这位叛乱运动的杰出领导人要求他的头衔为“国家元首”，因为他据称不喜欢听到“独裁者”的头衔。观察家们还强调，这一新决定意味着民族主义者现在确信胜利，因为人们普遍预期佛朗哥将军只有在征服马德里后才会被授予新职。

预测首都陷落

这里的军事专家宣称，民族主义军队将在三到四周内成为马德里的主人。他们表示，叛军队伍中的15万人正在各条战线增加压力，旨在完全包围首都。目前在巴利亚多利德叛军总司令部的埃米利奥·莫拉（Emilio Mola）将军将重新——

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, October 2, 1936

Shao Kwangtung,
Yang Get Death

Chow Found Not Guilty
In Nakayama Murder;
Court Packed

(Concluded from Page 1)
fingerprints supposed to have been
on the book in which the death
weapon is alleged to have been
concealed. The report stated
that fingerprints were found on
the book, but that they could
not be identified since they were
incomplete. Mr. Paul Y. Ru, As-
sistant Municipal Advocate in
charge of the prosecution, then
asked for the extreme penalty for
all three accused on evidence pro-
duced during the prolonged trial,
after which attorneys for the de-
fense countered by asking for
acquittal on grounds of in-
sufficient evidence.

The procurator summarised his
opinions briefly, saying that
numerous sessions had been held
in the case and the judge may
now pronounce the judgment ac-
cording to law. He avoided divulg-
ing his opinion in connection with
the case without saying whether
the accused are, from his stand-
point, guilty or not.

Arrested 5 Months Ago
Yang Wen-tao, Yih Hai-sen
(better known as Shao Kwang-
tung) and Chow Sha-yung were
arrested about five months ago.
Yang, Yih and another were first
taken into custody in Shanghai
and in Tsingtao, to which city the
police officers have extended their
search and investigations. Chow,
"inspector" in a Ningpo Road
cabaret, was arrested about three
weeks later.

Sensations followed sensations
when the trial opened. Yih made
a lengthy confession, declaring
that he shot and killed Nakayama
in his desire to kill a Japanese.
Then he revised his confession,
implicating Yang as the instigator.
All of a sudden, however, he re-
tracted the statements and hurled
charges of third degree treatment
at the hands of police officers.

Denies Part
Yang completely denied com-
plicity in the murder which last
November caused a big exodus of
Chinese from Chapei and Hong-
kew areas. He claimed that he
was "framed" by one Yang Chien-
chung, allegedly an ally of Japan-
ese "ronin." In his home, a book
hollowed in the center was seized.
It is said that the pistol used
in the crime was once concealed
in the book.

Chow also denied the charges.
According to police testimony,
however, he is alleged to be a
member of the gang and was
actually sent by Yang Wen-tao
to invite Yih Hai-sen to attend
a conference in the Moon Palace
where the murder plot was
allegedly hatched.

Women Questioned
Several others, including
females, had been rounded up in
connection with the now-famous
"Nakayama Murder Case." They
have been released. Those who
were once in custody included
Yih's mother and wife who were
arrested at the Moon Palace hotel.
The murder took place at 9 p.m.
on November 9, 1935. Warrant
Officer Hideo Nakayama was
walking on Darroch Road when
he was shot at close range. The
assailant escaped before arrival
of police and Japanese armed
forces. The crime caused such a
strain in Sino-Japanese relations
in Shanghai that rumors of a
Japanese invasion immediately
went into circulation. Populace
evacuated the "danger zones."

Rewards were offered by the
authorities for the arrest of the
culprits. After months of tire-
less investigations, Yih was ar-
rested in Tsingtao in a cabaret
and taken to Shanghai. The
action of arresting and removing
a prisoner from Tsingtao without
permission of the Chinese auth-
orities caused much consternation
in Shantung. At the same time,
Yang and another were taken
into custody in Shanghai. The
third man was later acquitted.
Chow was arrested later.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年10月2日，星期五

萧广东、
杨文涛获死刑

周少庸在中山谋杀案中被判无罪；
法庭座无虚席

（接第1版）
据称藏匿凶器的书上应该有指纹。报告称在书上发现了指纹，但由于指纹不完整，无法识别。负责起诉的助理市检察官陆伯鸿（Paul Y. Ru）先生随后根据长期审判中提出的证据，要求对所有三名被告处以极刑，此后辩护律师则以证据不足为由要求宣告无罪。

检察官简要总结了他的意见，称本案已举行多次庭审，法官现在可以依法宣判。他避免透露他对本案的看法，也没有说明从他的角度来看被告是否有罪。

五个月前被捕

杨文涛、易海生（更广为人知的名字是萧广东）和周少庸大约在五个月前被捕。杨、易和另一人最初在上海和青岛被拘留，警察将搜索和调查范围扩展到了青岛。周是宁波路一家舞厅的“稽查”，约三周后被捕。

审判开始后，轰动事件接连不断。易作了长篇供认，声称他出于杀死一名日本人的愿望开枪杀死了中山。随后他修改了供词，牵连杨文涛为幕后指使。然而，他突然撤回了陈述，并指控警察对他施以严刑逼供。

否认参与

杨完全否认参与了去年十一月导致闸北和虹口地区大量中国人逃离的谋杀案。他声称自己被杨建中（Yang Chien-chung，音译）“陷害”，后者据称是日本“浪人”的同伙。在他家中，搜获了一本中心被挖空的书。据说作案使用的手枪曾藏在这本书里。

周也否认了指控。然而，根据警方证词，他据称是该团伙成员，实际上是受杨文涛派遣，邀请易海生参加在月宫饭店（Moon Palace）举行的会议，谋杀阴谋据称就是在那里策划的。

询问妇女

另有数人，包括几名女性，因这起如今著名的“中山谋杀案”而被捕。她们已被释放。曾被拘留的人包括易的母亲和妻子，她们是在月宫饭店被捕的。谋杀发生在1935年11月9日晚上9点。准尉中山秀夫在达罗克路（Darroch Road）行走时遭到近距离枪击。刺客在警察和日军武装部队到达之前逃脱。这起犯罪导致上海中日关系如此紧张，以至于日本入侵的谣言立即流传开来。民众撤离了“危险区域”。

当局为逮捕罪犯提供了悬赏。经过数月不懈的调查，易在青岛的一家舞厅被捕并被带往上海。未经中国当局许可在青岛逮捕并转移囚犯的行动在山东引起了极大恐慌。与此同时，杨和另一人在上海被拘留。第三人后来被宣告无罪。周随后被捕。

October 5, 1936.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
Morning Translation S. R. REGISTRY.
No. D 7073
Date 5 / 10 / 36

Ta Kung Pao :-

THE NAKAYAMA CASE.

Yang Vung Tao and Yih Hai Sung were sentenced to death by the Shanghai First Special District Court on October 2 for the murder of a Japanese marine named Nakayama. The third accused named Tseu Shou Yong was found not guilty.
It was widely reported yesterday that the two prisoners had committed suicide in their cells. When approached by a reporter of this paper, the authorities as well as the family of Yang Vung Tao and the lawyer of Yih Hai Sung all denied the report.
It is said that on October 3 lawyer Chang Ts Niang (張子讓), who was appointed by the Court to defend Yih Hai Sung, filed on Yih's behalf an appeal with the Second Branch of Kiangsu High Court.
According to a statement made by lawyer Tang Wei Chuin (唐懷群), the family of Yang Vung Tao on October 3 had instructed him to file an appeal which will be presented to the Court to-day.

Ta Kung Pao :-

NORMAL CONDITIONS IN HONGKEW.

The additional marine posts detailed by the Japanese Naval Landing Party along North Szechuen Road were withdrawn on the morning of October 3. However, four or five Japanese marines are still on guard in the vicinity of Jukong Road and Sz Dah Road.
A reporter of this paper made an inspection yesterday morning and found definite signs of improvement in the district. The number of Japanese marines on duty on Jukong Road, Tien Tung An Railway Station and other places have been reduced to two. The situation has now returned to normalcy. The situation in Chapel is also quiet.

Ta Kung Pao :-

IMPORTANT FOREIGN OFFENDER REMOVED TO SHANGHAI FROM TIENTSIN BY AIR.

Yesterday morning Mr. A. Kosenboger, an employee of a certain local foreign organization, left Tientsin by air with an important political offender named "Le Granclaude". The aeroplane landed at the Lunghwa Aerodrome at 6.50 p.m. yesterday and the prisoner was immediately removed to a certain organization in the charge of armed detectives.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER 5 OCT 1936 CRIME BRANCH）

1936年10月5日。

上海公共租界工部局警务处
晨间译件 S. R. 登记处。
编号 D 7073
日期 36年10月5日

《大公报》：

中山案。

杨文道（Yang Vung Tao）与叶爱生（Yih Hai Sung）因谋杀一名名为中山（Nakayama）的日本海军陆战队员，于10月2日被上海第一特区地方法院判处死刑。第三名被告周守庸（Tseu Shou Yong）被判无罪。
昨日有广泛报道称，这两名囚犯已在牢房中自杀。当本报记者向当局以及杨文道的家属和叶爱生的律师求证时，各方均否认了这一报道。
据悉，10月3日，法院指派为叶爱生辩护的律师张子让（Chang Ts Niang，音译：张子让）代表叶爱生向江苏高等法院第二分院提交了上诉状。
据唐怀群（Tang Wei Chuin，音译：唐怀群）律师声明，杨文道家属于10月3日委托其提起上诉，该上诉状将于今日呈交法院。

《大公报》：

虹口局势恢复正常。

日本海军陆战队沿北四川路增派的额外哨位已于10月3日上午撤除。然而，在掘港路（Jukong Road，音译）和四达路（Sz Dah Road，音译）附近仍有四五名日本海军陆战队员站岗。
本报记者昨日上午巡视发现，该地区情况有明显好转。在掘港路、天通庵火车站（Tien Tung An Railway Station，音译）等地执勤的日本海军陆战队员人数已减至两人。目前局势已恢复正常。闸北（Chapel，此处应为Chapei之误，按当时通行译名译为闸北）的局势也很平静。

《大公报》：

重要外籍罪犯由天津空运至上海。

昨日上午，某本地外籍机构雇员A. Kosenboger先生（音译）与一名名为“Le Granclaude”（音译）的重要政治犯乘飞机离开天津。飞机于昨日下午6时50分降落在龙华机场，该囚犯随即由武装侦探押送至某机构。

（印：副警务处长 1936年10月5日 刑事科）

October 4, 1936. Morning translation

Lih Pao and other local newspapers;-

YANG YUNG TAO UNDER DEATH SENTENCE: ACCUSED TO FILE APPEAL

Yang Yung Tao (楊文道) and Yeh Ai Sheng (葉愛生), who had been charged with the murder of a Japanese marine named Nakayama, were sentenced to death by the 1st Shanghai Special District Court.

It is learned that the family of Yang Yung Tao and the lawyer for his defence have decided to file an appeal in the 2nd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court. Chang Tse Hsiang (張子驤) and other defence lawyers for Yeh Hai Sheng will also file an appeal for Yeh. It is has been decided that an appeal will be submitted at the beginning of next week. The S.M.P. has not yet decided whether they will file an appeal against the Court decision which finds Tseu Shou Yong (周守庸) "not guilty", and it is possible that the S.M.P. will drop the appeal.

Li Pao:-
Accused Attempt to Commit Suicide

Yesterday it was reported that Yeh Hai Sheng and Yang Wen Tao, who had been sentenced to death in connection with the Nakayama murder case, attempted to commit suicide in the gaol. According to a statement made by Captain Wahl, Governor of Gaols of the Shanghai Municipal Police yesterday evening, the report is entirely groundless.

1936年10月4日。晨间译件

《立报》及本地其他报纸：

杨文道被判死刑：被告将提起上诉

杨文道（楊文道）和叶爱生（葉愛生）被控谋杀一名名为中山（Nakayama）的日本海军陆战队员，被上海第一特区地方法院判处死刑。

据悉，杨文道的家属及其辩护律师决定向江苏高等法院第二分院提起上诉。叶海生（Yeh Hai Sheng，即前文叶爱生）的辩护律师张子驤（Chang Tse Hsiang，音译）等人也将为叶提起上诉。已决定于下周初提交上诉状。上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）尚未决定是否就法院判决周守庸（Tseu Shou Yong，音译：周守庸）“无罪”一事提起上诉，警务处有可能放弃上诉。

《立报》：
被告企图自杀

昨日有报道称，因中山谋杀案被判处死刑的叶海生和杨文道在狱中企图自杀。据上海公共租界工部局警务处监狱长瓦尔上尉（Captain Wahl）昨晚发表的声明，该报道完全毫无根据。

S. M. C. POLICE
Morning Translation D 73
Date ... / ... / ...

October 3, 1936.

NIPPO

CONSUL-GENERAL KASUGI ISSUES STATEMENT REGARDING
SUPPRESSION OF ANTI-JAPANESE TERRORISTS

At 4 p.m. yesterday Mr. Kasugi,
Japanese Consul-General in Shanghai, issued the following
statement:-

"Our government and people
have been exceedingly indignant over the Nakayama case.
It could not be regarded as a simple police case; it was
a well planned murder of a Japanese bluejacket in uniform.
We, Japanese officials and civilians, had from the very
beginning strongly believed that it was the work of
Chinese. For nearly one year, we have watched with
great patience the handling of the case by the Chinese
authorities. There were a few difficulties during the
hearings of the case but the strong evidence produced by
the S.M.P. has now resulted in the capital sentence being
imposed on the accused Yang Ven Tao and Yih Hai Sung on
October 2. This verdict makes it clear to the public
that the persons responsible for the crime were Chinese.
"As regards the Kayau murder
case, it has also been established that culprits are
Chinese and that certain secret terrorist societies are
connected with the crime. As regards the murder of a
Japanese sailor on Haining Road the culprit or culprits are
undoubtedly Chinese. The existence of such a terrorist
corps which attacks Japanese is a serious menace to the
safety of Japanese residents and obstructs improvement
of Sino-Japanese relations. For this reason, the
Chinese authorities should be requested to eradicate all
acts of anti-Japanese terrorism and deal with the persons
or organizations behind the scenes and to deal drastically
with persons directly responsible for the crime and to
adopt every possible measure to wipe out all causes
which are obstructing Sino-Japanese relations."

SECRETARY PHILLIPS REPLIES TO JAPANESE PETITION
FOR MORE JAPANESE PLAIN CLOTHES CONSTABLES AND
APPOINTMENT OF JAPANESE IN CHARGE OF POLICE STATIONS

The other day the Japanese
Amalgamated Association of Street Unions sent a petition
to Mr. Fessenden, Secretary-General of the S.M.C. asking
for more Japanese plain clothes constables and the
appointment of Japanese officers to take charge of
Hongkew Station and Dixwell Road Station.
On October 1, Mr. Fessenden
sent a reply to Mr. Kondo, Chairman of the Standing
Committee of the Association, stating that he would
consider the matter.
At 11 a.m. October 2, Mr.
Hayashi, honorary Chairman of the Association, and Mr.
Kondo, Chairman of the Standing Committee of the Association,
called on Mr. Phillips, Secretary of the S.M.C. and gave
an explanation of the petition with the help of Mr. Ibusuki,
Assistant Secretary, who interpreted.

（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (CRIME BRANCH)）

1936年10月3日。

《日日新闻》

总领事春日发表关于镇压反日恐怖分子的声明

昨日下午4时，
日本驻上海总领事春日先生，
发表了如下声明：

“我国政府及人民
对中山案感到极其愤慨。
此案不能被视为简单的治安案件；这是一起
经过周密策划的、针对身穿制服的日本水兵的谋杀案。
我们日本官员和平民从一开始就坚信这是
中国人所为。近一年来，我们以
极大的耐心观察了中国当局对此案的处理。在案件
审理过程中遇到了一些困难，但上海公共租界工部局警务处提供的有力证据
现已导致被告杨文道（Yang Ven Tao，音译）和叶海生（Yih Hai Sung，音译）于
10月2日被判处死刑。这一判决向公众
清楚地表明，犯罪责任人是中国人。
“至于加藤（Kayau，音译）谋杀
案，也已确定罪犯是
中国人，且某些秘密恐怖社团与
该罪行有关。至于在海宁路谋杀
一名日本水兵的案件，凶手无疑
是中国人。存在这样一个袭击日本人的恐怖
团体，严重威胁到日本居民的安全，并阻碍
中日关系的改善。因此，应要求
中国当局铲除一切反日恐怖主义
行为，处理幕后人员或组织，严厉
处置直接负责犯罪的人员，并采取一切可能措施消除
所有阻碍中日关系的因素。”

菲利普斯秘书回复日本方面关于增加日本便衣巡捕及任命日本人负责警察局的请愿

日前，日本各街道工会联合会向工部局总秘书费森登（Fessenden）先生递交请愿书，要求增加日本便衣巡捕，并任命日本警官负责虹口警察局和狄思威路（Dixwell Road，今溧阳路）警察局。
10月1日，费森登先生复函该协会常务委员会主席近藤（Kondo）先生，表示将考虑此事。
10月2日上午11时，该协会名誉主席林（Hayashi，音译）先生和协会常务委员会主席近藤先生拜访了工部局秘书菲利普斯（Phillips）先生，并在助理秘书伊吹（Ibusuki，音译）先生的翻译协助下，对请愿书作了说明。

（印：副警务处长（刑事科））

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, OCTOBER 2, 1936.
16820
7.2

JUDGMENT TO-DAY IN
NAKAYAMA CASE

Decision Of Court To
Give Verdict Comes
As Big Surprise

ACCUSED MAINTAIN
INNOCENCE

Judgment upon three suspects held for almost five months in connection with the killing of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama, of the Japanese Naval Landing Party on Darroch Road, on the night of November 9 last, will be pronounced at 2 p.m. to-day by Judge Dzien in the First Special District Court.

The announcement that he would deliver judgment this afternoon came as a great surprise to the court room, filled with Shanghai Municipal Police, Naval Landing Party men, Japanese Consular Police and Chinese officials. The men have already been in custody for five months—two months over the specified period under the Chinese law—and a remand for another long period was generally expected following yesterday's hearing.

Judge Dzien's announcement, therefore, came as a great surprise in view of the general tension prevailing in the Hongkew district.

A Japanese Naval spokesman stated yesterday morning, according to Domei, that defensive positions were taken up by Japanese in Hongkew against possible new anti-Japanese terroristic activities. He mentioned that a few hours after the prosecutor had summed up the case against the same three accused on July 10, Kosaku Kayau, Japanese seafood broker, was slain.

Court Quiet

No excitement was seen at all around the First Special District Court yesterday. The three accused, "Shao Kwantung," alias Yih Hai-sen, Yang Wen-tao and Chou Tso-yun, were taken to court without special escorts. However, officers of the Reserve Unit, S.M.P., were stationed all round the court compound. No Japanese marines were present as at previous hearings.

The hearing was occupied with the final summing-up of the prosecution by Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Y. Ru, the defence counsel's addresses and statements by the three accused. The findings of the Institute of Legal Medicine were read out prior to that.

A conviction was asked for by the prosecution; while the accused and their counsel maintained that if the men in the dock were guilty, they would not have remained in Shanghai after the shooting and that in the case of Yang Wen-tao, Cantonese seaman, he would not have supplied a great deal of information to the police prior to his arrest.

The report from the Chenji Institute stated that none other than Yang Wen-tao's fingerprints could be clearly distinguished on the hollowed-out book found in his home. He alleged, however, that it was planted there by a relative of his.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年10月2日，星期五。
16820
7.2

中山案今日宣判

法院决定
作出判决
令人深感意外

被告坚持
无罪

去年11月9日晚，日本海军陆战队准尉中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）在达罗克路（Darroch Road，今多伦路）被杀，三名嫌疑犯因此被羁押近五个月，丁赞（Dzien）法官将于今日下午2时在第一特区地方法院对此案作出判决。

宣布将于今天下午宣判的消息令挤满了上海公共租界工部局警务人员、海军陆战队队员、日本领事馆警察和中国官员的法庭大为惊讶。这些人已被羁押五个月——超过中国法律规定期限两个月——且在昨天的听证会后，人们普遍预期会将案件延期审理很长一段时间。

因此，鉴于虹口地区普遍存在的紧张局势，丁赞法官的宣布令人深感意外。

据同盟社报道，日本海军发言人昨日上午称，日本人在虹口采取了防御阵地，以应对可能发生的新反日恐怖活动。他提到，在检察官于7月10日对上述三名被告的案件进行总结陈词几小时后，日本海鲜经纪人加藤功作（Kosaku Kayau，音译）被杀害。

法庭平静

昨天第一特区地方法院周围完全没有出现骚动。三名被告，“肖广东”（Shao Kwantung，别名叶海森 Yih Hai-sen）、杨文道（Yang Wen-tao）和周佐云（Chou Tso-yun，音译），在没有特别护卫的情况下被带往法庭。然而，上海公共租界工部局警务处后备队军官部署在法庭大院四周。与之前的听证会不同，现场没有日本海军陆战队员。

听证会主要进行了市助理检察官保罗·胡（Paul Y. Ru，音译）的最终总结陈词、辩护律师的陈述以及三名被告的发言。在此之前，宣读了法医研究所的报告。

检方要求定罪；而被告及其律师则坚持认为，如果被告席上的人有罪，他们在枪击案后就不会留在上海，并且就广东籍海员杨文道而言，他在被捕前不会向警方提供大量信息。

陈记研究所（Chenji Institute，音译）的报告指出，在杨文道家中发现的挖空书籍上，只能清晰辨别出杨文道一人的指纹。然而，他声称这是他的亲戚栽赃陷害。

pages.en:
168 : 21
THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, OCTOBER 2, 1936

Nakayama Case
Verdict To Be
Given Today

Municipal Advocate
Requests Extreme
Penalty

The Nakayama Murder Case will come to a close at 2 o'clock this afternoon when judgment is handed down by Judge Dzien and full tribunal in the First Special District Court. This was the announcement made by the judge at the conclusion of lawyers' pleadings in the case conducted yesterday afternoon.

The announcement came as a complete surprise since it had been previously understood that at least a week would elapse before judgment. The news, however, was most welcome in all quarters interested and concerned in the case.

Yang Wen-tao, erstwhile Shanghai shipping man; Yih Hai-ser. (Hsiao Kwangtung), and Chow Sha-ying, the latter both former cabaret managers, smiled as the judge announced that decision was finally to be handed down. In fact, they looked considerably relieved to hear that after more than five months of periodic facing the court, they are at last to learn their fate.

Hearing Opens Late

The proceedings yesterday lasted approximately two hours. The van with Yih Hai-sen in it arrived about 20 minutes after the other two prisoners had taken their place in court with the result that the case didn't get underway until 2.30 p.m., about 30 minutes late.

At the beginning of the session, the court clerk read the findings of the judicial laboratory at Chenju on the findings connected with the fingerprints supposed to have been on the book in which the death weapon is alleged to have been concealed.

At a previous hearing of the case, Yang, who is charged with having plotted the crime, declared that the book, which was found in his house, had been planted there by a distant relative, Yang Chen-tsoong.

The latter appeared at a recent hearing and testified against the accused, stating that he had never been near the house and that he certainly had never left a book containing a gun there. The court ordered that the book be sent to the laboratory to be examined for fingerprints.

Fingerprints Incomplete

The report read by the court yesterday stated that fingerprints were found on the book but that it was impossible to tell just whose they were since they were incomplete.

After the reading of the report had been finished, Mr. Paul Y. Hu, Assistant Municipal Advocate in charge of the prosecution, delivered his closing arguments and asked for conviction of all three and the extreme penalty as punishment. He maintained that the evidence produced during the long trial was sufficient to convict and that the accused are guilty beyond all reasonable doubt.

Attorneys for the defense occupied about one hour with their speeches, all of which were of about the same tone. They based their acquittal on grounds of insufficient evidence.

168 : 21
《大美晚报》，1936年10月2日，星期五

中山案
判决将于
今日下达

市检察官
请求判处
极刑

中山谋杀案将于今天下午2时结束，届时丁赞法官及第一特区地方法院全体法官将作出判决。这是法官在昨天下午进行的该案律师辩论结束时宣布的。

这一宣布完全出人意料，因为此前人们认为至少需要一周时间才会作出判决。然而，这一消息受到各方关注者的热烈欢迎。

杨文道，前上海航运业人士；叶海瑟（Yih Hai-ser，即肖广东 Hsiao Kwangtung）；以及周少英（Chow Sha-ying，音译），后两人均为前舞厅经理，在法官宣布最终将作出判决时面露微笑。事实上，听到经过五个多月断续出庭受审后终于要知晓自己的命运，他们看起来如释重负。

听证会迟到开始

昨天的诉讼持续了约两个小时。载有叶海森的警车比其他两名囚犯到达法庭晚了约20分钟，导致案件直到下午2时30分才开始审理，迟到了约30分钟。

庭审开始时，法庭书记员宣读了陈菊（Chenju，音译）司法实验室关于据称藏有致死武器的书籍上指纹鉴定结果的报告。

在此前的一次听证会上，被控策划犯罪的杨氏声称，在他家中发现的那本书是其远房亲戚杨宗佐（Yang Chen-tsoong，音译）栽赃的。

后者在最近一次听证会上出庭作证反对被告，声称他从未靠近过那所房子，也肯定没有在那里留下过一本藏有枪支的书。法院命令将该书送往实验室进行指纹检查。

指纹不完整

法庭昨天宣读的报告指出，书上发现了指纹，但由于指纹不完整，无法确定究竟是谁的。

读完报告后，负责公诉的市助理检察官保罗·胡（Paul Y. Hu）发表了结案陈词，要求判定三人有罪并处以极刑作为惩罚。他坚持认为，在漫长的审判过程中提出的证据足以定罪，被告的罪行确凿无疑，不容合理怀疑。

辩护律师花了大约一个小时进行演讲，基调大致相同。他们以证据不足为由要求宣告无罪。

律师在中山案中作结案陈词
判决将于今日在特区法院宣布

第一特区法院法官钱鸿业将于今日下午2时就中山案作出判决。在该案中，广东人叶海森（别名“小广东”）、杨文道和周守勇被控于去年11月9日在达罗路（Darro Road）谋杀一名日本水兵。该案的辩论已于昨日下午重新开启并结束。负责公诉的助理市检察官鲁平先生要求对所有被告判处死刑。鲁先生表示，他不再重复此前为公诉方作结案陈词时已陈述的内容，但必须指出，杨建中的证词将证明杨文道所言不实；杨文道曾声称杨建中在其家中放置了那本被搜获的挖空书籍，以陷害其卷入刑事诉讼。

六名律师代表被告发言，以证据不足为由请求宣告各自当事人无罪。“小广东”的辩护律师指出，警方证人潘巧英的陈述对被告非常有利，因为该证人称，在11月9日枪击发生前，她看到一名身穿深色衣服的男子与遇害的日本水兵几乎并肩行走；而在犯罪现场重建过程中，“小广东”却称自己在枪击发生前行走在水兵身后。

在昨日庭审开始时，法庭宣读了真如司法实验室关于被搜获的挖空书籍的鉴定报告。该报告指出，由于书中留下的指纹不完整，无法断定这些指纹是否属于被告杨文道或证人杨建中。报告还涉及了书中发现的锈迹。

Central China Daily News and other local newspapers :-

THE NAKAYAMA CASE

The case against Yang Vung Tao (楊文道), Yih
Hai Jung (叶海榮) alias Siao Kwangtung (小廣東) and Tseu
Shou Yong (周守勇), all natives of Kwangtung Province,
charged with the murder of a Japanese marine named Hideo
Nakayama, was resumed at the First Shanghai Special District
Court at 2 p.m. yesterday before Judges Chien Hung Nieh
(錢鴻業), Siao Sih Feng (蕭世鳳) and Feng Shih Tuh (馮士德).
Representatives of the Shanghai City Government, the Bureau
of Public Safety and the Japanese Consulate-General were
present.
The Police was represented by the Municipal
Advocate, Mr. Paul Y Ru; the prisoners were defended by
Chang Tae Niang (張太娘), Van Kong (范剛), Wang Shih
Chong (王士崇) and Tong Wai Chung (唐衛中).
After an interrogation of the accused,
Presiding Judge Chien announced that the investigation into
this case had already been completed and moreover the report
from the Medico-Legal Laboratory had now been received.
Court Clerk Ting then read out the report
of the Laboratory:-
(1) An experiment was made to prove whether
a pistol of the size and brand as the one which was seized
by the Police, when placed inside another book, would
produce similar marks of pressure and the same rust marks
as those found in the hole excavated in the book which was
seized at the home of Yang Vung Tao for the purpose of
concealing the pistol. It was found that although one or
two points may be proved to correspond, yet it was impossible
to produce traces that were absolutely identical with those
found inside the book.
(2) It was impossible to identify the finger
prints of Yang Vung Tao with the finger prints found inside
the book because it was impossible to make a more definite
examination of the finger prints in the book for they
had already existed inside the book for quite a length of
time.
(3) It was likewise impossible to identify
the finger prints of Yang Chien Chung (楊建中) with the
finger prints inside the book.
At the close of the reading of the report,
Presiding Judge Chien put the following question to Yang
Vung Tao: "You have stated that you have been implicated
in this case by the evidence planted by Yang Chien Chung.
Then how is it that none of his finger prints have been
found in the book? Furthermore, the book was seized at
your home. It is, therefore, quite clear that the book
in question belongs to you."
Yang Vung Tao still flatly denied the ownership
of the book.

Police Request Capital Punishment

As no further questions were forthcoming,
Presiding Judge Chien announced the lawyers could sum/their
respective cases.

《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：

中山案

指控广东省籍人士杨文道（楊文道）、叶海荣（叶海榮，别名小廣東）及周守勇（周守勇）谋杀名为中山秀雄的日本海军陆战队士兵一案，于昨日下午2时在上海第一特区法院恢复审理。主审法官为钱鸿业（錢鴻業）、萧世凤（蕭世鳳）和冯士德（馮士德）。上海市政府、公安局及日本总领事馆的代表出席了庭审。

警方由市政检察官鲁平（Paul Y Ru）先生代表；囚犯由张太娘（張太娘）、范刚（范剛）、王士崇（王士崇）和唐卫中（唐衛中）辩护。

在对被告进行讯问后，主审法官钱宣布，本案调查已经完成，且已收到法医实验室的报告。

随后，法庭书记员丁宣读了实验室报告：
(1) 进行了一项实验，以验证若将一支与警方缴获的手枪尺寸和品牌相同的手枪放入另一本书中，是否会产生与在杨文道家中搜获的用于藏匿手枪的挖空书籍孔洞内发现的压痕和锈迹相似的痕迹。结果发现，虽然有一两点可能证明相符，但不可能产生与书内发现的痕迹完全一致的痕迹。
(2) 无法将杨文道的指纹与书内发现的指纹进行比对认定，因为书内的指纹存在时间已相当长，无法进行更明确的检验。
(3) 同样无法将杨建中（楊建中）的指纹与书内的指纹进行比对认定。

读完报告后，主审法官钱向杨文道提出以下问题：“你曾声称是杨建中放置证据陷害你卷入此案。那么，为何书中未发现他的任何指纹？此外，该书是在你家搜获的。因此，很明显该书属于你的。”
杨文道仍断然否认对该书的所有权。

警方要求判处死刑

由于没有进一步的问题，主审法官钱宣布律师可以进行各自的结案陈词。

October 2, 1936. Morning Translation

Paul Y. Ru, the Municipal Advocate, then
addressed the Court as follows:-
"I will not repeat the arguments which
I have outlined on a previous occasion. However, I have
the following two points to explain at present:
(1) The evidence given in Court by the
witness Pu Chiao Ying (浦巧英) is quite clear. It does
not conflict with the evidence submitted by the Police;
on the contrary it substantiates the various points which
were formerly obscure. After this clarification, they
have become strong evidence in this case.
(2) In his pleadings, Yang Vung Tao has
stated that he was implicated in this case by the false
evidence (referring to the book for concealing the pistol)
planted by Yang Chien Chung. Now Yang Chien Chung has
surrendered himself to the authorities and has made a
detailed statement which contained an explanation showing
that there was no reason for him to implicate the accused.
Furthermore, according to the facts, he had no personal grudge
at all against Yang Vung Tao. In an endeavour to save
innocent people from being punished, your Honour some time
ago ordered that the finger prints of Yang Chien Chung
be taken and forwarded for examination by the Medico-
Legal Laboratory. Now the report from the Medico-Legal
Laboratory shows that none of the finger prints inside
the book are identical with the finger prints of Yang
Chien Chung. Thus the statement of Yang Vung Tao is
unacceptable. Consequently the accused should be held
fully responsible for the book which was used to conceal
the pistol; this book was unearthed at his home.
"As regards the accused Yih Hai Sung, no
new developments have taken place after the Court
had ordered a resumption of arguments. Fortunately he
has already made several statements, and furthermore as
the evidence of Chu Kwei Sung (朱贵生), King Tao Chuen
(金道权) and various other important criminals who
were arrested in connection with another case fully
corroborate the facts contained in the statements of Yih
Hai Sung regarding the murder of the Japanese marine
Nakayama, the Court is, therefore, requested to accept
His (Yih Hai Sung's) statements. As regards the accused
Tseu Shou Yong, the Court should decide whether or not
he is guilty. In short, as the prosecution instituted
by the Police has been supported by reliable evidence,
the Court is requested to impose capital punishment on
the three accused according to law."
Lawyer Tong Wei Chung requested the Court
to find all the accused not guilty.
Lawyer Chang Tse Ning, for the defence
of all three accused, then made the following statement :-
"The following points are favourable to the accused :-
At the very beginning, witness Pu Chiao Ying stated that
she saw on the road two Japanese marines walking shoulder
to shoulder in a northerly direction. I am of the opinion
that this statement is consistent with the facts as also
with the report of the Medico-Legal Laboratory that the
shot was fired about 5 centimeters away from the deceased
marine. Pu's statement as regards the distance was
found to be entirely different when Yih Hai Sung gave a
reconstruction of the shooting. Pu made a hesitating

1936年10月2日。晨间译文

市政检察官鲁平（Paul Y. Ru）随后向法庭陈述如下：
“我不再重复我此前概述的论点。然而，目前我有以下两点需要说明：
(1) 证人浦巧英（浦巧英）在法庭上提供的证词非常清晰。它与警方提交的证据并不冲突；相反，它证实了此前模糊不清的各个要点。经过这一澄清，它们已成为本案的有力证据。
(2) 杨文道在辩护中称，他是被杨建中放置的虚假证据（指藏匿手枪的书）所陷害。现在杨建中已向当局自首，并作了详细陈述，其中解释表明他没有理由陷害被告。此外，根据事实，他对杨文道根本没有任何个人恩怨。为了挽救无辜者免受惩罚，阁下此前下令提取杨建中的指纹并送交法医实验室检验。现在法医实验室的报告显示，书内的任何指纹均与杨建中的指纹不符。因此，杨文道的说法不可接受。 Consequently，被告应对用于藏匿手枪的书籍负全部责任；该书是在其家中挖出的。
“至于被告叶海松（注：此处原文为Yih Hai Sung，前文为Yih Hai-sen/Hai Jung，依上下文应指同一人），在法庭命令恢复辩论后，没有出现新的进展。幸运的是，他已经作了几次陈述，而且，由于朱贵生（朱贵生）、金道权（金道权）以及其他几名因另一案件被捕的重要罪犯的证词充分佐证了叶海松关于谋杀日本海军陆战队士兵中山的陈述中所包含的事实，因此请求法庭接受他（叶海松）的陈述。至于被告周守勇，法庭应裁定其是否有罪。总之，由于警方提起的公诉有可靠证据支持，请求法庭依法对三名被告判处死刑。”

律师唐卫中请求法庭宣告所有被告无罪。
代表三名被告辩护的律师张子宁（注：音译，对应Chang Tse Ning，前文为Chang Tae Niang/张太娘，疑为同一人或笔误，此处依音译保留或参照前文，鉴于前文已有张太娘，此处可能是不同律师或拼写差异，按指令不确定保留原文加注音译，但考虑到上下文连贯性，若指代同一辩护团队，可能为张太娘之误或另一位律师。根据指令“不确定的保留原文并加括号注明「(音译)」”，此处处理为：律师张子宁（音译））随后作了如下陈述：
“以下各点对被告有利：起初，证人浦巧英称她在路上看到两名日本海军陆战队士兵肩并肩向北行走。我认为这一陈述与事实相符，也与法医实验室关于枪击发生在距遇害海军陆战队士兵约5厘米处的报告相符。当叶海松重建射击过程时，发现浦关于距离的陈述完全不同。浦在法庭上的陈述犹豫不决，
