August 20, 1936. Morning Translation.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE

Three men named Yang Vung Tao (楊文道), Yih Hai Sung (叶海生) and Tseu Shou Yong (周守荣) are being charged in connection with the murder of the Japanese marine Nakayama.

In the course of their investigations, the Police found in the home of Yang Vung Tao a book with an excavated hole in the centre for the keeping of a pistol. Yang Vung Tao acknowledged that the book belonged to him, but later he alleged that one Yang Chien Chung (楊建中), a man of the same clan, had planted the book in his home in order to implicate him.

Thus, Yang Chien Chung became a very important witness in the case. The Court therefore instructed the Municipal Police to locate Yang Chien Chung. As Yang had already left Shanghai, there was no means to show whether the allegation made by Yang Vung Tao was true or otherwise.

On August 18, Yang Chien Chung surrendered himself to the Police declaring that he was willing to confront Yang Vung Tao in Court.

At 2 p.m. yesterday, Judge Siao Sih Feng of the 1st Shanghai Special District Court held a further hearing of the case. Officers of the Japanese Landing Force were present. Tang Van Jin (唐振) and Kuo Chi Ming (郭啟明), the lawyers defending Yang Vung Tao, were in attendance. Only Yang Vung Tao was brought into Court because the Court desired to investigate the question of the book only.

Opening the proceedings, Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Ru said :- "During the first two hearings of the case, the accused Yang Vung Tao acknowledged that the book which had an excavated hole in the centre for keeping the pistol used in killing the Japanese marine and which was seized in his home, was his property. The hole in the book was actually used for the keeping of the pistol. When the Municipal Police gave evidence, after an investigation, that the pistol concealed in the book was the one used in the murder of the Japanese marine, Yang changed his statement at the third hearing of the case and stated that the book which was seized by the Police at his home had been placed there by one Yang Chien Chung who did it to implicate him in the case. This statement remained unchecked until recently. Fortunately, on August 18 Yang Chien Chung surrendered himself to the Police. He stated that although his surname was the same as that of Yang Vung Tao, they were not of the same clan.(?) He added that as he did not know Yang Vung Tao's address, he could not have gone to his home to plant the evidence in order to implicate him. After the arrest of Yang Vung Tao, Yang Chien Chung was threatened several times, and in order to avoid danger, he left Shanghai. He says that he has surrendered himself so that the truth might be known. Yang Chien Chung is now in Court and the Court is requested to interrogate him".
pages.zh:
2
1936年8月20日。晨间译件。

《申报》及其他本地报纸：

中山谋杀案

三名男子杨文道（楊文道）、叶海生（叶海生）和周守荣（周守荣）因涉嫌谋杀日本海军陆战队员中山而受到指控。

在调查过程中，警方在杨文道家中发现了一本书，书中心被挖空，用于藏放手枪。杨文道承认该书属于他，但后来他声称，同宗族的杨建中（楊建中）为了陷害他，将这本书放置在他家中。

因此，杨建中成为该案中非常重要的证人。法庭因此指令工部局警务处寻找杨建中。由于杨建中已离开上海，无法证实杨文道的指控是否属实。

8月18日，杨建中向警方自首，声明愿意在法庭上与杨文道对质。

昨日下午2时，上海第一特区地方法院法官萧世丰（Siao Sih Feng，音译）对该案进行了进一步审理。日本登陆部队军官出席。为杨文道辩护的律师唐振（唐振）和郭啟明（郭啟明）到庭。只有杨文道被带上法庭，因为法庭希望仅就书籍问题进行调查。

开庭时，助理市检察官保罗·鲁（Paul Ru，音译）说道：“在该案的前两次审讯中，被告杨文道承认，在其家中搜获的、中心被挖空用于存放杀害日本海军陆战队员所用枪支的那本书，是他的财产。书中的空洞确实用于藏放手枪。当工部局警务处在调查后作证称，书中藏匿的手枪即为谋杀日本海军陆战队员所用的凶器时，杨文道在第三次审讯中改变了供词，声称警方在他家中搜获的那本书是由杨建中放置在那里的，目的是使他卷入此案。这一说法直到最近都未经核实。幸运的是，8月18日杨建中向警方自首。他陈述说，虽然他与杨文道同姓，但他们并非同宗族。（？）他补充说，由于他不知道杨文道的住址，他不可能去杨文道家栽赃证据以陷害他。在杨文道被捕后，杨建中多次受到威胁，为了躲避危险，他离开了上海。他说，他自首是为了让真相大白。杨建中现在庭上，请求法庭对他进行讯问”。

pages.en:
3.
August 20, 1936. Morning Translation.

Witness Yang Chien Chung was then interrogated. In reply to the Court, he said: "I am 53 years of age and am at present living at House No.377 Hung An Li alleyway off Range Road. I was related to the family of Yang Vung Tao and I belong to the Yang clan in Peishan (北山). As we are members of the Peishan Fellow Provincials Association we are therefore known to each other. I call him uncle. We have not met since our last interview in August last year at the Dong Zung Association which was formed by Yang Vung Tao. If I have actually been to his home, the members of his family would surely recognize me. They can be summoned here to identify me."
The Court here showed him the book used for concealing the pistol which was discovered at the home of Yang Vung Tao.
After making an examination of the book, the witness said: "I have never seen this book before, nor have I ever told Yang Vung Tao how to excavate a hole in the book for the purpose of concealing a pistol. As I have a fortune of several tens of thousands of dollars, there is no need for me to seek loans from Yang Vung Tao."
Questioned by the Court, the accused, Yang Vung Tao said: "In October of the 22nd Year of the Chinese Republic (1933) when I was in a godown of Butterfield & Swire, Yang Chien Chung called on me. As I had no safe place in which to conceal my pistol, he told me how to excavate a hole in a book, saying that it was the safest way to conceal anything inside a book. At that time, he wore a Chinese dress and a felt hat and not in foreign clothing as he is dressed to-day. As he and I are related as uncle and nephew, how could I be so unfeeling as to bring a false accusation against him?"
In reply to further questions put by the Court, the witness, Yang Chien Chung, said: "I am acquainted with doctor Zung Wei Ming (鄭惠民). On April 28 (? year), Zung came to the Peishan Fellow Provincials Association. Noticing the name of Yang Vung Tao in a list of the names of members, he asked me whether I knew Yang Vung Tao's address, and added that the Police were seeking for him. In the midst of our conversation, another member of the Association named Yang Kwei Mei (楊桂明) wrote down the address of Yang Vung Tao on a cigarette picture and handed it to Zung. Later, doctor Zung called on me and told me that he had located the address but was informed that Yang Vung Tao did not reside at that place. I, therefore, took Zung to the home of Yang Kwei Mei so that they might make further enquiries to locate the whereabouts of Yang Vung Tao. The doctor did not promise to give me some reward should Yang Vung Tao be located, nor did he give me the reason why the Police were seeking for him. Later, Yang Vung Tao was arrested, but I only learnt of it through newspaper reports. By this time, I found myself in a more delicate position. For this reason, I left for Kwangtung to seek shelter there for the time being. Later, I returned to Shanghai and made trips to Nanking, Hangchow and various other places. It then occurred to me that unless the allegations against are satisfactorily cleared up, they would not only affect my reputation but would seriously interfere with my search for employment. That is why I surrendered myself."
pages.zh:
3.
1936年8月20日。晨间译件。

随后对证人杨建中进行了讯问。他在回答法庭提问时说：“我今年53岁，目前住在兰路（Range Road）洪安里377号。我与杨文道家有亲戚关系，我属于北山（Peishan）杨氏家族。由于我们都是北山同乡会的成员，因此彼此认识。我称他为叔叔。自从去年8月在杨文道成立的东宗协会（Dong Zung Association，音译）最后一次会面以来，我们就再未见过面。如果我真的去过他家，他的家人肯定会认出我。可以传唤他们来此辨认我。”

法庭随即向他展示了在杨文道家中发现的用于藏匿手枪的那本书。

在检查了该书后，证人说：“我以前从未见过这本书，也从未告诉过杨文道如何在书中挖洞以藏匿手枪。我有数万美元的家产，没有必要向杨文道借款。”

经法庭讯问，被告杨文道说：“中华民国二十二年（1933年）10月，当我在太古洋行（Butterfield & Swire）的仓库时，杨建中来拜访我。由于我没有安全的地方藏放手枪，他告诉我如何在书中挖洞，说这是将物品藏在书中最安全的方法。当时，他身穿中式服装，头戴毡帽，不像今天这样穿着西式服装。既然我和他是叔侄亲属关系，我怎么会如此无情地诬告他呢？”

在回答法庭提出的进一步问题时，证人杨建中说：“我认识郑惠民（Zung Wei Ming，音译）医生。4月28日（年份不详），郑医生来到北山同乡会。他在会员名单中看到杨文道的名字，便问我是否知道杨文道的住址，并补充说警方正在寻找他。在我们谈话期间，另一位名为杨桂明（楊桂明）的同乡会成员将杨文道的地址写在一张香烟画片上，交给了郑医生。后来，郑医生来拜访我，告诉我他已经找到了地址，但被告知杨文道并不住在那里。因此，我带郑医生去了杨桂明家，以便他们进一步查询以确定杨文道的下落。郑医生并没有承诺如果找到杨文道会给我报酬，也没有告诉我警方寻找他的原因。后来，杨文道被捕，但我只是通过报纸报道得知的。这时，我发现自己的处境更加微妙。出于这个原因，我前往广东暂时避难。后来，我回到上海，并前往南京、杭州等地。随后我想到，除非对我的指控得到令人满意的澄清，否则这不仅会影响我的声誉，还会严重妨碍我找工作。这就是我自首的原因。”

pages.en:
4.
August 20, 1936. Morning Translation.

In reply to the Court, The accused Yang Vung Tao
said: "Yang Chien Chung once told Yang Kwei Mei that the
Police were anxious to locate me and asked Yang Kwei Mei
to give me a tip so that I could make an early escape."
The witness Yang Chien Chung, however, flatly
denied this allegation made by Yang Vung Tao.
At this stage, the Court rose.
Accused Yang Vung Tao was returned to the Police
Station for detention.
The Finger Print Office of the Police was ordered
to take the finger prints of Yang Chien Chung.
pages.zh:
4.
1936年8月20日。晨间译件。

被告杨文道在回答法庭提问时说：“杨建中曾告诉杨桂明，警方急于找到我，并请杨桂明给我通风报信，以便我能尽早逃脱。”

然而，证人杨建中断然否认了杨文道的这一指控。

此时，法庭休庭。

被告杨文道被送回警察局羁押。

警方指纹室奉命采集杨建中的指纹。

pages.en:
August 20, 1936. Morning Translation.

MAI ICHI

THE NAKAYAMA CASE

At 2.30 p.m. yesterday the
12th hearing of the Nakayama case was held at the First
Special District Court. A heavy guard was in attendance.
Judge Hsiao presided in the absence of Chief Judge Chien
and Procurator Chang. Amongst those present were Navy
Resident Officer Okino, Municipal Police Advocate Paul
Ru, Assistant Police Commissioner Uyehara with the entire
staff of the Special Political Office of the S.M.P.,
Secretary Tanaka of the local Japanese Consulate-General,
and Mr. Okamoto, Japanese lawyer, and the Chinese lawyers
for the defence. Only Yang Ven Tao, one of the three
accused, was brought into Court.
Mr. Paul Ru, Municipal Advocate,
asked the Court to examine a new witness named Yang
Chien Chung. Yang Ven Tao, one of the three accused, had
alleged that Yang Chien Chung had planted in his house
the book used to conceal a pistol in order to implicate
him in the Nakayama murder case. Yang Chien Chung had
now voluntarily surrendered himself to the S.M.P. to
clear up an allegation printed by the newspapers that he
(Yang Chien Chung) was involved in the Nakayama case.
In May, Yang Chien Chung went to Canton to find work.
At one time a Chinese doctor named Chen asked Yang Chien
Chung for the address of Yang Ven Tao but the address that
Yang Chien Chung gave the doctor was wrong. This proved
that Yang Chien Chung did not know Yang Ven Tao's address.
The Judge here asked Yang Chien
Chung whether he knew Yang Ven Tao.
Yang Chien Chung replied that
he had not seen Yang Ven Tao for the past 7 or 8 years
and that he did not know Yang Ven Tao was living in Shanghai.
The Judge ( showing a book to the witness): Do you
recognize this book?
Witness: Absolutely no.
Q. Have you ever borrowed money from Yang Ven Tao?
A. I am the owner of property valued at about $100,000,
therefore, there is no need for me to borrow money from
others.
Q. Have you ever visited Yang Ven Tao's home?
A. No.
Q. How did you come to know Dr. Chen?
A. Because Dr. Chen once examined my wife when she
was sick.
Q. What did Dr. Chen say to you when he asked you
about Yang Ven Tao's address?
A. Dr. Chen made no mention of Yang Ven Tao being
implicated in the Nakayama case.
Q. Yang Ven Tao has stated that it was you who showed
him how to conceal a pistol in a book.
A. It is untrue.
Asked by the Judge why he went
to Canton, the witness replied that he went there to
seek a job from one Liu Ki Voong and produced a letter of
introduction in that connection. He further stated that
he had visited Hangchow, Nanking, Hankow and Tientsin
because he had heard that some one would attempt to kill him.
pages.zh:
1936年8月20日。晨间译件。

每日新闻

中山案

昨日下午二时三十分，中山案第十二次审讯在第一特区地方法院举行。现场戒备森严。在首席法官钱（音译）和检察官张（音译）缺席的情况下，由萧法官主持庭审。出席者包括海军驻在武官奥野（Okino，音译）、工部局警务处公诉人保罗·鲁（Paul Ru，音译）、警务处副总监上原（Uyehara，音译）及其特别政治科全体职员、日本驻上海总领事馆秘书田中（Tanaka，音译）、日本律师冈本（Okamoto，音译）先生以及被告方的中国律师。三名被告中，仅有杨文涛一人被提庭受审。

工部局公诉人保罗·鲁先生请求法庭传讯一名名为杨建忠的新证人。三名被告之一的杨文涛曾指控称，杨建忠将一本用于藏匿手枪的书放入其家中，以诬陷其卷入中山谋杀案。杨建忠现已主动向工部局警务处自首，以澄清报纸刊登的关于他（杨建忠）卷入中山案的指控。今年五月，杨建忠前往广州找工作。期间，一位姓陈的中国医生向杨建忠询问杨文涛的地址，但杨建忠提供给医生的地址是错误的。这证明杨建忠并不知道杨文涛的地址。

法官随即询问杨建忠是否认识杨文涛。
杨建忠回答说，他在过去七、八年间未曾见过杨文涛，且不知道杨文涛居住在上海。

法官（向证人展示一本书）：你认识这本书吗？
证人：完全不认识。
问：你是否曾向杨文涛借过钱？
答：我拥有价值约十万元的财产，因此无需向他人借钱。
问：你是否曾去过杨文涛的家？
答：没有。
问：你是如何认识陈医生的？
答：因为陈医生曾在我妻子生病时为她诊病。
问：当陈医生向你询问杨文涛的地址时，他说了什么？
答：陈医生并未提及杨文涛卷入中山案一事。
问：杨文涛声称，是你向他展示了如何将手枪藏在书中。
答：这不属实。

当法官询问证人为何去广州时，证人回答他是去向一位刘启荣（Liu Ki Voong，音译）求职，并出示了相关的推荐信。他还进一步陈述，由于听说有人企图杀害他，他曾前往杭州、南京、汉口和天津。

pages.en:
August 20, 1936.    Morning Translation
-2-
The Judge then asked the witness
why he had come back to Shanghai.
The witness replied that he
had come to clear up his position because he had read
newspaper reports to the effect that he was involved in
the Nakayama case.
(Yang Chien Chung's statement
has thus disproved Yang Ven Tao's statement and his
alibi. Neither Yang Ven Tao nor the lawyers for the
defence had anything to say about the statement made by
the witness)
The Judge here questioned the
accused Yang Ven Tao.
Q. You have stated that Yang Chien Chung had visited
your home. Was he seen by anybody when he visited your
home?    have
A. My children must/probably seen him.
Q. Is this true?
To this question the accused
Yang Ven Tao could not give a definite reply and he
simply repeated the statement made at the last hearing.
Yang Ven Tao said that on April 17 when on his way home
he found that some one was following him. He thought
that the man was either Yang Chien Chung or his agent
and he feared that he might be killed by him.
At this juncture, the Municipal
Advocate stated that it was true that some was shadowing
Yang Ven Tao but it was not Yang Chien Chung; it was a
Municipal detective.
The lawyer for the defence then
demanded that Yang Chien Chung prove his statements,
but the Judge ordered the lawyer to remain seated.
Yang Ven Tao went on to say
that it was strange that Yang Chien Chung should have made
his escape while he (Yang Ven Tao) did not attempt to
escape.
The Judge closed the hearing
at 3.30 p.m. after asking the S.M.P. to take the finger
prints of Yang Chien Chung.

Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory works very
slowly

At the last hearing the Court
adjourned sine die on the ground that the finger prints
and the Chinese newspaper of March 31 containing a report
of the hearing of the Wang Ching Wei case must be
examined by the Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory, while
the photographs of the three accused have to be submitted
for identification by the accused in the Wang Ching Wei
case at Nanking.
At yesterday's hearing, the Court
again adjourned the hearing and asked the Police to take
the finger prints of Yang Chien Chung.
The attitude of the Court is very
suspicious because it is attempting to identify Yang Chien
Chung's finger prints with those in the book although
the book has been handled by a large number of officers
concerned in the case and other persons. The Chenju Medico
Legal Laboratory works very slowly.
pages.zh:
1936年8月20日。晨间译件
-2-

法官随后询问证人为何返回上海。
证人回答说，因为他看到报纸报道说他卷入中山案，所以回来澄清自己的处境。
（杨建忠的证词 thus 驳斥了杨文涛的陈述及其不在场证明。杨文涛及辩护律师均未对证人的陈述发表任何意见）

法官随即讯问被告杨文涛。
问：你曾陈述杨建忠去过你家。他去你家时，有没有人看见他？
答：我的孩子应该/可能看见了他。
问：这是真的吗？
对于这个问题，被告杨文涛无法给出明确答复，只是重复了上次庭审时的陈述。杨文涛称，4月17日他在回家途中发现有人跟踪他。他认为那人要么是杨建忠，要么是其代理人，他担心自己会被此人杀害。

此时，工部局公诉人指出，确实有人在跟踪杨文涛，但那人并非杨建忠，而是一名工部局侦探。

辩护律师随后要求杨建忠证明其陈述，但法官命令该律师坐下。
杨文涛继续说道，奇怪的是杨建忠逃走了，而他（杨文涛）却并未试图逃跑。

下午三时三十分，法官在要求工部局警务处采集杨建忠的指纹后，宣布休庭。

真如法医实验室工作进展非常缓慢

在上次庭审中，法庭宣布无限期休庭，理由是必须由真如法医实验室检验指纹以及包含汪精卫案庭审报道的3月31日中文报纸，同时必须将三名被告的照片提交给在南京的汪精卫案被告进行辨认。

在昨天的庭审中，法庭再次宣布休庭，并要求警方采集杨建忠的指纹。

法庭的态度非常可疑，因为它试图将杨建忠的指纹与书上的指纹进行比对，尽管该书已被大量涉案警官及其他人员经手。真如法医实验室的工作进展非常缓慢。

pages.en:
August 21, 1936. Afternoon Translation.

NIPPO

THE NAKAYAMA CASE

The Nippo publishes the following
comment:-
Already 12 hearings have been
held of the Nakayama case since May 1, 1936. The
Court is simply attempting to prolong the case. The
Court is not sincerely dealing with the case because
despite the indisputable evidence brought against the
accused it is still trying to find pretexts to prolong
the case.
The 12th hearing was attended
by only two of the lawyers for the defence. It
is interesting to note that lawyer Kuh, who is defending
Yang Ven Tao, did not put in an appearance at the 11th
hearing. This lawyer was a member of the Peisan
Fellow Countrymen's Association at the time when Yang
Ven Tao was arrested and he was actively engaged in
the movement to support Yang Ven Tao and during the
hearings he made many statements in favour of Yang Ven
Tao. Lawyer Kuh went to Canton as soon as Customs
Superintendent Tang Hai En went to Canton as Salt
Commissioner at Canton. At one of the hearings one of
the lawyers for the defence left Court after making a
statement to the effect that a Chinese Court should not
deal with a case against the interests of Chinese citizens.
The unscientific method adopted
by the Special District Court in dealing with the
Nakayama case has been made clear during the hearings.
At the 12th hearing the Court asked the S.M.P. to take
the finger prints of Yang Chien Chung, who is a witness
and not an accused. Questioned as to the purpose
of the prints being taken, the Court stated that they
could be compared with the prints found in the book
which had concealed the pistol used in the crime. The
book in question was seized on April 19. Since then
it has been handled by the Municipal identification
department, the Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory and the
Court. Even the identification of Yang Ven Tao's
finger prints was already found to be difficult. If
the Court continue to act in this childish manner we
cannot tell when the case will be settled. If the
Chinese people desire to be treated on a basis of equality
with civilized nations and wish to abolish extraterritoriality
they should behave like people of a civilized nation.
The witness Yang Chien Chung,
whose presence in Court had been strongly demanded by
the lawyers for the defence, gave his evidence, but the
lawyers for the defence stated that his statement was
unreliable although they had believed that Yang Chien
Chung would prove Yang Ven Tao's innocence.
The hearing should have ended
a long time ago, but the defence demanded the attendance
of an amah and of Yang Chien Chung. Now both these
witnesses have been produced by the S.M.P. The Court
will be simply irritating the feelings of Japanese
should it continue this attitude.
pages.zh:
1936年8月21日。午后译件。

日日新闻

中山案

《日日新闻》发表如下评论：
自1936年5月1日以来，中山案已进行了12次庭审。法庭简直是在试图拖延案件。法庭并非真诚地处理此案，因为尽管针对被告的证据确凿无疑，它仍在寻找借口以延长案件审理时间。

只有两名辩护律师出席了第12次庭审。值得注意的是，为杨文涛辩护的顾律师在第11次庭审中并未露面。在杨文涛被捕时，这位律师是北山同乡会（Peisan Fellow Countrymen's Association，音译）的成员，他积极参与支持杨文涛的运动，并在庭审期间发表了许多有利于杨文涛的言论。海关监督唐海恩（Tang Hai En，音译）赴广州担任广东盐务专员后，顾律师随即也去了广州。在一次庭审中，一名辩护律师在发表声明称中国法院不应审理损害中国公民利益的案件后离开了法庭。

特区地方法院在处理中山案时所采用的不科学方法，在庭审过程中已暴露无遗。在第12次庭审中，法庭要求工部局警务处采集证人杨建忠（而非被告）的指纹。当被问及采集指纹的目的时，法庭称这些指纹可与在藏匿作案用手枪的书上发现的指纹进行比对。涉案书籍于4月19日被扣押。此后，该书已由工部局识别科、真如法医实验室以及法庭经手。即便是要识别杨文涛的指纹已被发现十分困难。如果法庭继续以这种幼稚的方式行事，我们无法预料案件何时才能结案。如果中国人民希望在与文明国家平等的基础上受到对待，并希望废除治外法权，他们就应当表现得像文明国家的人民一样。

辩护律师强烈要求出庭的证人杨建忠提供了证词，但辩护律师称其陈述不可靠，尽管他们原本相信杨建忠能证明杨文涛的清白。

审讯本应早已结束，但辩方要求传唤一名阿妈（女佣）和杨建忠出庭。现在这两名证人均已由工部局警务处带到。如果法庭继续保持这种态度，只会激怒日本人的感情。

MAINICHI

Yesterday the S.M.P. sent
the finger prints of Yang Chien Chung to the Special
District Court and requested the Court to hold the
next hearing of the Nakayama case as soon as possible.
It is expected that the next hearing will take place
some time next week.

GENERAL MEETING OF "HUNG MEN" (FEDERATION OF SECRET
SOCIETIES)

While the hearing of the
Nakayama case is taking place, the Aayau case occurred
and this was followed by the arrival of a number of
professional assassins in Shanghai.
A general meeting of the "Hung
Men", Federation of Secret Societies, was held at a

the united association. Important resolutions are
reported to have been passed.

1936年8月21日。午后译件。
-2-

每日新闻

昨日，工部局警务处将杨建忠的指纹送至特区地方法院，并请求法庭尽快举行中山案的下一次庭审。预计下一次庭审将于下周某时举行。

“洪门”（秘密会社联合会）大会

在中山案审理期间，发生了亚耀（Aayau，音译）案，随后有一批职业刺客抵达上海。

“洪门”秘密会社联合会在租界内某地召开了一次大会，会上选举了干部，并实现了所有属于“洪门”的社团的统一。洪松协会（Hung Sung Association，音译）被指定管理联合协会的事务。据报道，会议通过了重要决议。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, August 19, 1936

Surprise Murder
Hearing Today

New Evidence Causes
Police To Resume
Killing Charge

Yang Wen-tao, local Cantonese merchant accused of complicity along with Yih Hai-sen (Shao Kwangtung) and Chao Hsia-yung in the murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama on Darroch Road November 9 last year, was being brought up before the First Special District Court at 2:30 o'clock this afternoon in a surprise hearing before Judge Dzlen.

The Shanghai Evening Post learned this morning that the police have new evidence to show that Yang knew that the book in which the murder gun is supposed to have been hid was in his house.

Denies Knowledge

Yang has during the course of the trial stoutly disclaimed any knowledge of the Nakayama murder and has stated that the book found in his house was planted there without his knowledge.

A new witness was being brought into court this afternoon to testify that Yang positively knew of the book's presence in his house, Mr. Paul Y. Ru, assistant municipal advocate, will present the evidence for the police.

Important Link

The hollowed-out book which was so constructed as to conceal a gun has all along been an important link in the chain of evidence against Yang and also against Shao Kwangtung to whom, it is claimed, Yang gave the gun that eventually fired the shot that killed Nakayama. Tests carried out by police experts revealed the fact that in one corner of the book rust marks were found. These marks are alleged to have come from the gun which was concealed for some time in the book.

In the meantime, officials of the Public Safety Bureau in Shanghai have in their custody a man named Chang Yu-hwa, one of the defendants charged with plotting the abortive assassination of Mr. Wang Ching-wei last November. The man was brought here at the request of the Shanghai Municipal Police and will be brought before the First Special District Court in the near future to face the three accused in the Nakayama case.

At a recent hearing hearing in the case, testimony was given in court that Shao Kwangtung once confessed in the police station that he and his accomplices had planned to kill Wang Ching-wei or General Chiang Kai-shek. Failing these, he is reported to have said that his group would murder some Japanese officials. These statements, however, were later repudiated by Shao Kwangtung. It is believed that there might be some connection between the man brought from Nanking and Yih's group and this is the reason he will be brought before the court soon.

（批：D. 7073 / 24 8 36）
（批：S.2 / 16 8/19）
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年8月19日，星期三

今日突发谋杀案听证

新证据促使警方
恢复杀人指控

当地粤商杨文涛被控与叶海森（即邵广东）和赵夏勇（Chao Hsia-yung，音译）共谋，于去年11月9日在达罗克路谋杀军曹中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）。今天下午二时三十分，他在甄法官（Judge Dzlen，音译）主持的一次突发听证会上，被提至第一特区地方法院受审。

《上海晚邮报》今晨获悉，警方掌握新证据，表明杨文涛知道那本据称藏有凶器的书就在他的家中。

否认知情

在审判过程中，杨文涛坚决否认对中山谋杀案有任何了解，并声称在他家中发现的那本书是在他不知情的情况下被人栽赃的。

今天下午将有一名新证人出庭作证，证明杨文涛确实知道该书在其家中。助理市公诉人保罗·Y·鲁（Paul Y. Ru，音译）先生将代表警方出示证据。

重要关联

那本经过挖空以藏匿枪支的书，一直以来都是针对杨文涛以及邵广东的证据链中的重要一环。据称，杨文涛将最终射杀中山的那把枪交给了邵广东。警方专家进行的测试显示，在该书的一个角落里发现了锈迹。据称，这些锈迹来自曾在书中藏匿一段时间的手枪。

与此同时，上海公共安全局官员拘留了一名名为张玉华（Chang Yu-hwa，音译）的男子，他是去年11月策划刺杀汪精卫先生未遂案的被告之一。此人是应工部局警务处的要求被带至此地的，不久将被提至第一特区地方法院，与中山案的三名被告对质。

在该案最近的一次庭审中，法庭上有证词称，邵广东曾在警察局供认，他和同伙曾计划杀害汪精卫或蒋介石将军。据称他还表示，如果未能得手，其团伙将谋杀一些日本官员。然而，邵广东后来否认了这些陈述。人们认为，从南京带来的这名男子可能与叶氏团伙存在某种联系，这也是他即将被提堂的原因。

（批注：D. 7073 / 24 8 36）
（批注：S.2 / 16 8/19）

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, AUGUST 20, 1936

New Witness
In Nakayama
Trial Appears

Yang Chien-ching, Sought
In Hongkew Slaying,
Turns Up Voluntarily

ASKS PROTECTION
AGAINST GANG

Yang Wen-tao Accuses
Witness Of False
Statements

Wanted since last April to testify in connection with the Nakayama murder case. Mr. Yang Chien-chung, former clerk in the employ of the law offices of Mr. L. K. Kentwell, British attorney, made his appearance in the First Special District Court yesterday and gave evidence for the prosecution. The occasion was a surprise hearing of the case.

Only one of the three accused men, Yang Wen-tao, former local shipping man who is alleged to have plotted the killing of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama, Japanese subject, murdered on November 9, 1935, was brought before the tribunal. This was because the evidence to be taken concerned only him and had nothing to do with the cases against Yih Hai-sen (Hsiao Kwangtung), and Chow Shan-yung, the other two accused.

At the time of Yang's arrest last April, he contended that the ex-law office clerk had framed him. He charged that the man had placed the book containing the death weapon in his house on Tongshan Road where the police would find it. He further contended the missing man was a relative of his and had held a grudge against him because he refused to loan the fellow money.

Appears Unexpectedly

In view of the fact that the accused man offered no other explanation as to why he had been arrested, and because of his repeated statements that he was innocent of any implication in the Nakayama affair, the court asked the police to do everything possible to bring the man into the tribunal to testify. Detectives in charge of the case searched the city but failed to locate Yang Chien-chung. Quite unexpectedly, the fellow appeared quite voluntarily and announced that he was willing to take the witness

New Witness
In Nakayama
Trial Appears

(Continued from Page 1, Col. 6.)

stand. He told detectives he had nothing to hide and that Yang Wan-tao's charges of frame-up against him were completely false. All he wanted to be sure of, he said, was protection against the Tung Yih Association, Yang Wentao's club, which, he added had threatened his life.

When the witness appeared in the courtroom yesterday afternoon, he was flanked by Japanese detectives. Nor was he left alone for a single instant after he had entered the room. Before the session started, he took a seat on a long bench near the witness box. On each side sat two detectives, all of them armed. An elderly man of 53 years, he was attired in a light gray suit of foreign cut and at first glance, would ordinarily be taken for a prosperous business man.

Ru Makes Statement

Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, opened the proceedings by informing the court of the identity of the witness. He also stated that the man would deny the accusations made against him by the first accused, thereby strengthening the case for the prosecution.

Taking the witness box, Mr. Yang declared that he was not a relative of the accused man as the latter implied. He said that the two families were related once upon a time but as he could trace it back, that was 700 years ago. Since that early date, he added that the family connection had been lost and that he considered himself in no way related to the man who was standing trial.

He continued that he had formerly been in the employ of the Kentwell office but had left that concern in April after the arrest of the three accused. The first accused had made charges of frame-up against him, he said, and he had received threats against his life from members of the Tung Yih Association. He declared that he had no desire to remain in Shanghai and get killed, even if the charges made against him were false.

After leaving the city, he declared that he had gone to Nanking in search of a job. He later went to Hangchow and then to Chekiang, also looking for work. He declared, however, that he possessed independent financial means and that it wasn't necessary for him to work if he chose to remain idle. However, he said, he liked to keep busy and for that reason continued to seek work.

Returned To Shanghai

Asked when he first knew about the case against the three accused, he stated he had heard nothing about it until he read the newspaper reports. He declared that as soon as he learned that the police wanted him to testify, he came back to

Shanghai and reported to detectives in charge of the case.

He was shown the book which had hidden the death pistol. Asked if he recognized it, he replied in the negative, stating that he had never seen it before. Asked if he knew Yang Wen tao, he declared that he did but that he had never visited the man's home nor had he ever had anything to do with him. Continuing, he flatly denied all of the prisoner's allegations.

For the first time since the trial started months ago, Yang Wen-tao became talkative yesterday afternoon. He accused the witness of prevarication and stated that the fellow had called at his house. He said that he came to his place three years ago in October and suggested that Yang use a book to hide a gun in. Yang, it will be remembered, stated that he originally possessed a gun and that he had used a book in which to hide it. Police investigation revealed that it was not the same gun used to shoot Nakayama.

Yang further declared that the witness held a grudge against him because he had refused to loan the man money. The court asked the witness if this was true.

"I is not," came the quick reply. "I never tried to borrow any money from him and why should I? I am well-to-do and have several tens of thousands of dollars of my own."

Denies Charge Flatly

The accused alleged that the witness had planted the book and the gun in his house so that he would be arrested and the witness and others mixed up with him could collect the rewards offered by the authorities. This, the witness also flatly denied.

Questioning of the witness and Yang occupied most of the afternoon. At its conclusion, the court stated that if the prisoner's allegations were correct and the witness had planted the book and gun in Yang Wen-tao's house, then his fingerprints must be on the book. The police were ordered to take Yang's fingerprints and then send them, together with the book and the gun, to the judicial laboratory for comparison. The case was then remanded to an indefinite date.

Because of the fact that the hearing had not been publicly announced, there were no spectators in the courtroom yesterday afternoon. The hearing was attended only by police and a handful of newspapermen.

Reports that Mr. Yang Chien-chung, appearance before the police and in court yesterday afternoon had a connection between the recent arrest of Chang Yu-hwa, member of the bomb terrorist gang now standing trial and also wanted for participation in the attempted assassination of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, former president of the Executive Yuan, were categorically denied.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年8月20日，星期四

新证人
出现在中山
案审判中

杨建清（音译），虹口
杀人案通缉犯，
主动现身

请求保护
免受帮会迫害

杨文涛指控
证人作伪证

自今年四月以来一直因与中山谋杀案有关而被要求出庭作证的前英国律师L. K. Kentwell先生律师事务所职员杨建忠（音译）先生，昨日在第一特区法院出庭，为控方提供证词。此次庭审是该案件的一次突发性聆讯。

三名被告中，只有被指策划杀害1935年11月9日遇害的日本籍警长中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）的前本地航运商人杨文涛一人被带上法庭。这是因为所采集的证词仅涉及他本人，而与另外两名被告易海森（即萧广东）和周善庸的案件无关。

在去年四月杨文涛被捕时，他声称这位前律所职员陷害了他。他指控此人将藏有凶器的书籍放置在他位于同山路（Tongshan Road）的住所内，以便警察发现。他还辩称，这名失踪者是他的亲戚，因他拒绝借钱给此人而对他怀恨在心。

意外现身

鉴于被告男子对于为何被捕未提供其他解释，且因其反复声明自己与中山案毫无牵连，法庭要求警方尽一切可能将该男子带至法庭作证。负责此案的侦探在全市搜寻，但未能找到杨建忠（音译）。出乎意料的是，此人自愿出现，并宣布愿意作为证人

新证人
出现在中山
案审判中

（续第1版第6栏。）

出庭。他告诉侦探们他没有什么可隐瞒的，杨文涛对他提出的陷害指控完全是虚假的。他说，他唯一希望得到保证的是，免受杨文涛所属社团“统益会”（Tung Yih Association）的伤害，他补充说该组织曾威胁他的生命。

当这位证人昨日下午出现在法庭时，两侧均有日本侦探陪同。在他进入房间后，片刻也未让他独处。开庭前，他在靠近证人席的一张长凳上坐下。两边各坐着两名侦探，均携带武器。这位53岁的长者身着西式浅灰色西装，乍看之下通常会被认为是一位富裕的商人。

茹氏发表声明

助理市检察官茹志良（Paul Y. Ru，音译）先生开场时向法庭说明了证人的身份。他还表示，该男子将否认第一被告对他提出的指控，从而加强控方的案情。

杨先生走上证人席，声明他并非如被告所暗示的那样是被告的亲戚。他说，两家人曾经有过亲戚关系，但据他追溯，那已是700年前的事了。他补充说，自那个早期年代以来，家族联系已经中断，他认为自己与正在受审的男子没有任何亲属关系。

他继续说道，他以前曾在Kentwell律师事务所工作，但在三名被告被捕后的四月离开了该机构。他说，第一被告对他提出了陷害指控，并且他收到了来自“统益会”成员的生命威胁。他宣称，即使针对他的指控是虚假的，他也不愿留在上海送命。

他宣称，离开上海后，他去了南京寻找工作。后来他又去了杭州，随后去了浙江，同样是在找工作。然而，他宣称自己拥有独立的经济来源，如果选择无所事事，并不一定需要工作。不过，他说自己喜欢忙碌，因此继续寻求工作。

返回上海

当被问及何时首次得知针对这三名被告的案件时，他表示直到看到报纸报道后才有所耳闻。他宣称，一旦得知警方希望他作证，他便回到

上海，并向负责此案的侦探报到。

有人向他展示了那本藏有致命手枪的书。当被问及是否认得此书时，他予以否认，称以前从未见过。当被问及是否认识杨文涛时，他承认认识，但声称从未去过此人家中，也从未与他有任何往来。接着，他断然否认了囚犯的所有指控。

自数月前提审开始以来，杨文涛在昨日下午首次变得多话。他指责证人闪烁其词，并称此人曾到过他家。他说，此人三年前的十月来到他的住处，建议杨文涛用一本书来藏枪。记得杨文涛曾声称他原本拥有一把枪，并用一本书将其藏匿。警方调查显示，那并非用于射击中山的那把枪。

杨文涛还宣称，证人因他拒绝借钱给此人而对他怀恨在心。法庭询问证人这是否属实。

“不是，”他迅速回答。“我从未试图向他借过钱，何必呢？我很富有，自有数万美元资产。”

断然否认指控

被告 alleges 称，证人将书和枪植入了他的家中，以便使他被捕，从而使证人及其他与他勾结的人能够领取当局提供的赏金。对此，证人也予以断然否认。

对证人和杨文涛的讯问占据了下午的大部分时间。结束时，法庭表示，如果被告的指控属实，即证人将书和枪植入了杨文涛家中，那么书上必定留有他的指纹。警方奉命提取杨文涛的指纹，并将其连同书籍和枪支一起送往司法实验室进行比对。案件随后被延期至不定日期。

由于此次聆讯未公开宣布，昨日下午法庭内没有旁听者。出席聆讯的仅有警察和少数几名新闻记者。

有关杨建忠（音译）先生昨日下午在警方及法庭的出现与近期逮捕炸弹恐怖团伙成员张裕华（Chang Yu-hwa，音译）之间存在关联的报道——该团伙成员目前正在受审，并因参与企图暗杀前行政院院长汪精卫先生而被通缉——遭到断然否认。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES. THURSDAY. AUGUST 20. 1936

NEW WITNESS FOUND
IN NAKAYAMA CASE
Missing Nephew Of Yang
Wen-tao Makes Surprise
Appearance In Court

Missing ever since the opening
of the Nakayama trial, Yang
Gien-chun, a nephew of Yang
Wen-tao, one of the three accused
men, made a surprise appearance
in the First Special District Court
yesterday, following his surrender
on Tuesday to the Shanghai
police.
Yang Gien-chun, who had been
accused by his uncle of "trap-
ping" him by planting the fatal
pistol in a book hollowed out for
the purpose and found by the
police in Yang Wen-tao's library,
made a heated denial of the alle-
gations.
He had fled from Shanghai,
Yang told the court, as soon as
he heard that his uncle was at-
tempting to implicate him in the
case. After visiting Hangchow,
Hankow, Hongkong and Canton,
he had decided to return to
Shanghai and clear his name.
Aged 52, Yang Gien-chun is
much older than his uncle. He
told the judge that he last saw
his uncle in August. He did not
know his uncle's address and could
not therefore have left the book
in his library. He was not a
member of the Tung Yi Associa-
tion, of which his uncle was chair-
man.
Yang Wen-tao declared that a
few days before his arrest, his
nephew came to his home. Three
years ago, when he was working
with Messrs. Butterfield and
Swire, his nephew had told him
how to hide his licensed pistol
by hollowing out a book in the
centre.

16.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年8月20日，星期四

中山案中发现
新证人
杨文涛失踪的侄子
在法庭上意外现身

自中山案审判开始以来一直失踪的杨建春（Yang Gien-chun，音译），系三名被告之一杨文涛的侄子，于周二向上海警方自首后，昨日在第一特区法院意外现身。

杨建春曾被其叔叔指控通过在一本特意挖空的书里放置致命手枪来“设局”陷害他，该书后被警方在杨文涛的书房中发现，对此指控，他进行了激烈的否认。

杨建春告诉法庭，他一听说叔叔试图将他卷入此案，便逃离了上海。在走访了杭州、汉口、香港和广州之后，他决定返回上海以洗清自己的名声。

现年52岁的杨建春比他的叔叔年长许多。他告诉法官，他最后一次见到叔叔是在八月。他不知道叔叔的地址，因此不可能将书留在他书房里。他不是其叔叔担任主席的“统益会”（Tung Yi Association）的成员。

杨文涛宣称，在他被捕前几天，他的侄子曾来到他家。三年前，当他在太古洋行（Butterfield and Swire）工作时，他的侄子曾告诉他如何通过将书中心挖空来藏匿其持照手枪。

16.

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, August 20, 1936

Witness Denies
Part In Slaying

Clerk Voluntarily Goes
To Court To Testify
In Nakayama Case

In a surprise hearing of the
Nakayama murder case held in
the First Special District Court
yesterday afternoon, Mr. Yang
Chien-chung, former clerk in the
employ of Mr. L. K. Kentwell,
British attorney, took the witness
stand to deny the allegations of
Yang Wen-tao, former local ship-
ping man and at present charged
with complicity in the murder
of the Japanese Marine last
November claiming that he had
never before seen the hollowed-
out book which had hidden the
death pistol and which had been
found in Yang Wen-tao's home.
The former clerk, who claims to
have independent means, came
into court yesterday of his own
volition as he wished to deny the
allegations made by the accused
that he had planted the book in
his house. The witness claimed
that he had received threatening
letters from members of the
Tung Yih Association and for
this reason he had left town last
April. Now, all he asked was pro-
tection, which he received yester-
day afternoon on his entrance
into court, being heavily flanked
by Japanese detectives.
At the conclusions of the hear-
ings, which were mostly occupied
with the questioning of the wit-
ness and Yang Wen-tao, the court
ordered that the clerk's finger-
prints be taken in an effort to
find if such prints were on the
book which the accused alleges
Yang Chien-chung placed in his
house.
Neither Yih Hai-sen (Shao
Kwangtung) nor Chow Hsia-yung,
the other accused in the
Nakayama case, appeared in court
yesterday as the evidence con-
cerned only Yang Wen-tao. The
case has been remanded to an in-
definite date.

"Red" Base Again

While minimizing the usefulness
of Shanghai as a base for Comin-
tern activities, reported to have
been revived here lately, The
Shanghai Nippo today editorially
noted the need for caution.
"At present, when various coun-
tries are nervous about Soviet spy
activities, how can the Comin-
tern hope to carry on effective
underground activities here?" the
paper asked. "But the Soviet
Union being skilled in such mat-
ters, she may resort to the use
of 'White' Russians. Japanese
should pay special attention to
this point at this time when the
Nakayama and Kayau cases are
still unsolved."
The daily cited a report that
having been driven out of "Man-
chukuo," Comintern headquarters
for the Far East had been set up
in Shanghai.

Typical Tactics

This, the Nippo said, was typi-
cal of Soviet tactics, as it had
skillfully utilized a time when the
eyes of the world were focused on
western Europe and Spain to take
this step.
"The Soviets first selected Tien-
tsin as a base for agitators. Balk-
ed, however, by the formation of
an anti-Communist bloc in North
China, Russia is now transferring
the influential Reds she sent to
the northern city south to Shang-
hai."
Shanghai, the paper noted, was
"second choice" for the Soviets.
While on the one hand, the
tangled international relations
here made it easy for spies and
agitators to operate, Shanghai
was, on the other hand, subject
to close surveillance by various
Powers.

World Watches

"Every country is paying close
attention to Soviet maneuverings
here. That is why the Soviets
first chose Tientsin and later
moved to Shanghai," the Nippo
said.
The journal declared that at
the time of the formation of the
Front Populaire cabinet in
France, rumors were current that
the French Consulate-General and
the Concession authorities were
closing their eyes to the activities
of Red agitators.
"Mr. Seiichi Uyeda, then chief
of the police affairs section of
the Japanese Consulate-General,
however, issued a statement at the
time noting that a close co-
operation existed between his
office and the French authorities
for the curbing of Communist
activities," the daily added.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年8月20日，星期四

证人否认
参与谋杀

书记员自愿出庭
在中山案中作证

昨天下午在第一特区法院举行的中山谋杀案听证会上出现意外情况，英国律师L. K. Kentwell先生（肯特韦尔）的前雇员杨建忠先生出庭作证，否认前本地船务人员、目前被控参与去年十一月杀害日本海军陆战队士兵一案的杨文涛的指控。杨建忠声称，他以前从未见过那本挖空用来藏匿致死手枪的书，而该书是在杨文涛家中发现的。这位自称有独立经济来源的前书记员昨天自愿来到法庭，因为他希望否认被告关于是他将书栽赃在其家中的指控。该证人声称，他曾收到同义会成员的恐吓信，因此于今年四月离开上海。现在，他所要求的只是保护；昨天下午他进入法庭时得到了这种保护，当时有大量日本侦探在两侧护卫。

听证会结束时，大部分时间用于询问证人和杨文涛，法院下令提取该书记员的指纹，以查明被告所称由杨建忠放置在他家中的书上是否有此类指纹。

中山案的其他两名被告叶海森（邵广东）和周夏勇昨天未出庭，因为证据仅涉及杨文涛。案件已被延期至不定日期。

“红色”基地再起

《上海日报》今日在社论中指出需要保持谨慎，尽管它淡化了上海作为共产国际活动基地的作用，据报道该活动最近在此复活。“目前，当各国对苏联间谍活动感到紧张时，共产国际怎能希望在此进行有效的地下活动？”该报问道。“但苏联擅长此类事务，她可能会诉诸使用‘白’俄人。在中山案和加屋案尚未侦破之际，日本人应特别注意这一点。”

该日报引用一份报告称，共产国际远东总部在被赶出“满洲国”后，已在上海设立。

典型战术

《上海日报》称，这是苏联的典型战术，因为它巧妙地利用了世界目光聚焦于西欧和西班牙的时机采取这一步骤。“苏联人首先选择天津作为煽动者的基地。然而，由于华北反共集团的形成受阻，俄罗斯现在正将其派往北方城市的那些有影响力的‘红色’分子南调至上海。”该报指出，上海是苏联人的“第二选择”。一方面，这里错综复杂的国际关系使间谍和煽动者易于活动；另一方面，上海受到各列强的严密监视。

世界关注

《上海日报》称：“各国都在密切关注苏联在此的举动。这就是为什么苏联人首先选择天津，后来才转移到上海的原因。”该刊物宣称，在法国人民阵线内阁组建之时，有谣言流传称法国总领事馆和租界当局对红色煽动者的活动视而不见。该日报补充道：“然而，当时日本总领事馆警务课课长上田清一先生发表声明，指出其办公室与法国当局在遏制共产主义活动方面存在密切合作。”

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, AUGUST 20, 1936

NAKAYAMA CASE
REOPENED

Witness Denies Planting Book
in Accused's House

ALLEGATION OF THREAT
TO HIS LIFE

Yang Kyung-chun, said to have planted a book used to conceal a pistol in the house of Yang Ven-tao and thus to have implicated the latter in Mr. Nakayama's murder, appeared in the First Special District Court yesterday, as a witness, and strongly denied the allegation. The witness who had been sought by the prosecution for many months, suddenly communicated with the Settlement Police on Tuesday. According to Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Municipal Advocate, he escaped from Shanghai after he had heard that his life was threatened by members of the Tung Yih Club, of which one of the accused, Yang Ven-tao, was a member. He returned to Shanghai to clear up the matter, so that he might continue his work here.

After an hour's questioning, the Court ordered that prints of the witness's fingers and palms be taken and compared with those found in the book. No date was fixed for the next hearing.

Witness' Statement

The witness told the Court that he was aged 53 years, and a native of Chungshan, in Kwangtung. The accused and he were of one family 700 years ago but were not related at present. He had never visited the accused's house and had never borrowed money from him, as he was quite well-to-do himself.

When shown a book in which the police said the pistol had been concealed, the witness said he had never seen it before.

The accused thereupon said the witness was not telling the truth. The witness visited his house in October three years ago, dressed in a long black gown, not in a foreign suit, as he appeared in Court. At that time, the accused obtained a pistol and did not know how to conceal it, whereupon the witness suggested the use of a book.

The witness, however, insisted that he had never been to the accused's house. When asked by Dr. Chen Wei-ming regarding Yang Ven-tao's address, witness referred him to Yang Kia-mei, who wrote down Yang Ven-tao's address. Dr. Chen could not find the accused's house, however.

Asked if he had obtained any money from Dr. Chen, the witness said he had not. On one occasion he asked Dr. Chen to approach the Kwangtung Hospital, to allow him to delay the payment of medical expenses for his nephew. When Dr. Chen asked him about the address of the accused, he did not know why the accused was wanted by the police. Dr. Chen did not mention any reward offered in the murder case.

Left in May

The witness said he left Shanghai for Canton in May, to call on a high official for a job. He had also heard that his life was threatened by Tung Yih Club members. After he learned from the papers that he was wanted to give evidence in the case, he returned here. He also desired to clear up the matter.

The witness said he never had any ill-feeling against the accused. The latter, however, said the witness did have a grudge against him, because he had refused to give support to the witness on a certain mission in the south.

S.2

pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年8月20日，星期四

中山案
重开审理

证人否认在被告家中栽赃书籍

声称其生命受到威胁

据称杨庆春（音译）将一本用于藏匿手枪的书栽赃在杨文涛家中，从而牵连后者卷入中山先生谋杀案，他昨天作为证人出现在第一特区法院，并强烈否认这一指控。检方数月来一直在寻找这位证人，他于周二突然与工部局警务处取得联系。据助理市检察官Paul Y. Ru（鲁保罗）先生称，他在听说自己的生命受到同义俱乐部成员（被告之一杨文涛是该俱乐部成员）的威胁后逃离了上海。他返回上海以澄清此事，以便能继续在此工作。

经过一小时的讯问，法院下令提取该证人的手指和手掌指纹，并与书中发现的指纹进行比对。下次听证会的日期尚未确定。

证人陈述

证人告诉法院，他现年53岁，籍贯广东中山。被告与他700年前同属一家族，但目前并无亲属关系。他从未去过被告家，也从未向他借过钱，因为他自己相当富裕。

当向他展示警方称藏有手枪的那本书时，证人说他以前从未见过。

被告随即表示证人没有说实话。证人三年前的十月曾拜访过他的家，当时身穿黑色长袍，而非像他在法庭上那样穿着西装。当时，被告弄到了一把手枪，不知如何藏匿，于是证人建议使用一本书。

然而，证人坚持说他从未去过被告家。当陈伟明博士问及杨文涛的地址时，证人让他去找杨家梅（音译），后者写下了杨文涛的地址。然而，陈博士找不到被告的住所。

当被问及是否从陈博士那里得到任何钱财时，证人说他没得。有一次，他请陈博士向广东医院交涉，允许他延缓支付侄子的医疗费用。当陈博士问他被告的地址时，他不知道警方为何通缉被告。陈博士并未提及谋杀案中提供的任何赏金。

五月离开

证人说，他五月离开上海前往广州，去拜访一位高官谋求职位。他也听说自己的生命受到同义俱乐部成员的威胁。当他从报纸上得知他被要求在此案中作证后，便回到了这里。他也希望澄清此事。

证人说他对被告从未有过任何恶感。然而，被告称证人确实对他怀恨在心，因为他拒绝支持证人在南方执行的某项任务。

S.2

THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 11, 1936

Four Nakayama
Case Suspects
In Court Again

Police Recommend Trial
At Hearing Held
In Camera

The four men arrested recently on suspicion of having been involved in the killing of Kosaku Kayau and Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama, were brought before the First Special District Court yesterday morning, and after a short hearing were remanded in custody until September 18 for trial. The hearing yesterday was held in camera.

The hearing was brief. The four accused men were brought before the court, questioned briefly and recommended by the police for trial. The court consented and the group was ordered held for another week.

The four men, Tseu Kwei-soong, age 39; Ching Dao-jin, age 19; Zung Eng-ming, age 32; and Tsang Tse-ming, age 27, are alleged to have been involved in the shooting last July of Kosaku Kayau, Japanese sea-food broker. While all hearings in connection with their case have been held in camera, and no information has been given out to the public, it is stated that the men belonged to a Cantonese club engaged in the business of assassination.

The hearing yesterday was conducted early in the morning. Only the four accused, the judge and the few detectives connected with the case were allowed to enter the courtroom. The prosecution outlined the case against the quartet and insisted that they be brought before the court for trial. The court agreed and the request was granted.

Kosaku Kayau was shot down on the night of July 9 while he was walking along Chimei Road, off Cixwell Road, with two children. When found, one of the children was clinging to his neck while the other was standing at his side.

After a long search, two of the men alleged to have been connected with the shooting were taken into custody while the two others were not nabbed until three or four days later.

Just why the four are being held has not been made clear and possibly won't be until they appear for open trial next week.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》，1936年9月11日，星期五

四名中山案
嫌疑犯再次
出庭

警方在闭门听证会上
建议起诉

最近因涉嫌参与杀害加屋小作（Kosaku Kayau）和中士中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）而被捕的四名男子，昨天上午被带至第一特区法院，经过简短听证后，被还押候审至9月18日以备审判。昨天的听证会是闭门进行的。

听证会很简短。四名被告被带上法庭，接受了简短讯问，警方建议对他们提起诉讼。法院予以同意，并命令将该团伙再羁押一周。

这四名男子分别是：谢桂松（音译），39岁；程道金（音译），19岁；钟英明（音译），32岁；曾子明（音译），27岁。据称他们参与了去年七月枪杀日本海鲜经纪人加屋小作的行动。虽然与他们案件有关的所有听证会都是闭门进行的，且未向公众发布任何信息，但据悉这些人属于一个从事暗杀业务的广东帮会。

昨天的听证会在清晨进行。只有四名被告、法官以及与该案有关的几名侦探被允许进入法庭。公诉方概述了对这四人的指控，并坚持要求将他们提交法庭审判。法院表示同意，批准了这一请求。

加屋小作于7月9日晚在与两个孩子沿着奇美路（Chi Mei Road，近Cixwell路）行走时被枪杀。被发现时，一个孩子紧紧抱住他的脖子，另一个站在他身边。

经过长时间搜寻，两名据称与枪击案有关的男子被拘留，另外两人直到三四天后才被抓获。

究竟为何拘留这四人尚不清楚，可能要等到下周公开审判时才会明朗。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, FRIDAY, SEPTEMBER 11, 1936

MURDER SUSPECTS TO BE
HELD ANOTHER WEEK
Tseu Kwei-sung, Ching Dao-joen,
Zung Eng-ming and Tsang Tse-ming,
arrested recently on suspicion of
being concerned in the murder of H.
Nakayama, a Japanese marine, on
Daffoch Road, and K. Kayau, a
Japanese clerk, on Chi Mei Road,
whose detention was ordered by the
First Special District Court last week
to enable the police to make investi-
gations, were remanded for another
week by the court yesterday, the
police mentioning that more time
would be required to complete
inquiries in the case.

《字林西报》，1936年9月11日，星期五

谋杀嫌疑人
将被再羁押一周

谢桂松（Tseu Kwei-sung）、程道仁（Ching Dao-joen）、钟英明（Zung Eng-ming）和曾子明（Tsang Tse-ming），最近因涉嫌参与在达罗克路（Daffoch Road）谋杀日本海军陆战队员H. 中山（Nakayama）以及在奇美路（Chi Mei Road）谋杀日本职员K. 加屋（Kayau）而被捕，上周第一特区法院下令拘留他们以便警方进行调查，昨天法院将他们再延期羁押一周，警方表示需要更多时间来完成此案的调查。

The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Wednesday, August 5, 1936

Nakayama Case
Defies Agitation

Prospects For Speedy
Verdict Dim Despite
Japanese Demands

Efforts to keep the Nakayama
case "hot" seemed to be producing
little effect this morning just a
few hours before the scheduled
hearing in the First District
Court this afternoon, and police,
defense and prosecution were in-
clined to be non-committal and
just a bit indifferent concerning
the day by day statements of local
Japanese newspapers to the effect
that the trial has dragged on long
enough and that a verdict of
guilt should be rendered im-
mediately.

While local Japanese papers are
alleging that three accused, Yih
Hai-sen (Shao Kwangtung), Yang
Wen-tao and Chow Hsia-yung,
are backed by strong political
support and that the three
accused are "political assassins,"
the concerted action of the
journals for a speedy verdict is
not likely to have the desired
effect, it was pointed out here
this morning.

The pleadings in the Nakayama
case were reopened in order that
the presiding judges might hear
the testimony of an amah who
was walking down Darroch Road
the night Nakayama was shot and
that they might try to find the
motive for the shooting—a motive
that appears just as obscure at
the present time as it did eight
and one half months ago when
the Japanese sailor was fatally
wounded.

As the three accused will in all
probability be questioned this
afternoon and as there is a pos-
sibility of witnesses being called,
it is almost certain that the case
will not be concluded. If time
allows, summing up by attorneys
for the defense and the prosecu-
tion may take place, but even
this appears doubtful, and it is ex-
pected that the pleadings of the
lawyers will not take place until a
further as yet unset hearing.

Asked To Get Killer

Speedy apprehension of the
murderer of Mr. Kosaku Kayau,
shot and killed on Chi Mei Road
on July 10, was asked yesterday
by Mr. Hideaki Kitamura, chief
of the Police Affairs Section of
the Japanese Consulate-General,
during a call on Gen. Tsai Chin-
chun, director of the Public
Safety Bureau.

A similar call was paid a day
earlier by Mr. Kaname Wakasugi,
consul-general, on Gen. Wu Teh-
chen, mayor of Greater Shanghai.

《上海晚邮报与水星报》，1936年8月5日，星期三

中山案
无视煽动

尽管日本方面提出要求
迅速判决的前景黯淡

就在今天下午第一区法院预定举行听证会前的几个小时，今早看来，试图让中山案保持“热度”的努力几乎未产生什么效果，警方、辩方和检方都倾向于不置可否，对当地日本报纸日复一日发表的所谓审判拖延已久、应立即作出有罪判决的声明显得有点漠不关心。

虽然当地日本报纸指控三名被告叶海森（邵广东）、杨文涛和周夏勇背后有强大的政治支持，并称这三名被告是“政治刺客”，但今天上午有人指出，各家报纸联合行动要求迅速判决，不太可能产生预期的效果。

中山案的辩论重新开启，以便主审法官能够听取一名在中山遇害当晚走在达罗克路上的阿妈的证词，并试图找出枪击的动机——这一动机在目前看来，与八个半月前那名日本水手受致命伤时一样模糊不清。

由于今天下午很可能会讯问这三名被告，并且有可能传唤证人，几乎可以肯定本案不会结案。如果时间允许，辩方和检方律师可能会进行总结陈词，但即使这也显得可疑，预计律师们的辩论将推迟到另一次尚未确定的听证会上进行。

要求缉拿凶手

日本总领事馆警务课课长北村英明（Hideaki Kitamura）先生昨天拜访公共安全局局长蔡劲军将军时，要求迅速逮捕7月10日在奇美路被枪杀的加屋小作先生的凶手。

前一天，总领事若杉要（Kaname Wakasugi）先生也类似地拜访了大上海市长吴铁城将军。

（印：上海工部局 / S. 登记处 / S & D. / 日期 ...）

（批：归档 / 2/2）
（批：8/5）

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, AUGUST 6, 1936

Nakayama Affair Accused
Suspected Of Concern In
Attack On Wang Ching-wei

Sensational Investigation Is Opened By Court On
Another Confession Made By “Shao Kwangtung”;
Accused Now Alleged To Be Terrorists

GANG ALLEGEDLY HAD PLANNED TO
MURDER CHIANG OR WANG FIRST

The Nakayama case took an altogether unexpected turn in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon when at the first investigation hearing Judge Shao commenced delving into an allegation that the three Chinese, accused of having murdered Warrant Officer Iiideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party on Darroch Road on November 9, last, belonged to the group of terrorists, who had made an attempt on the life of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, former President of the Executive Yuan, at Nanking on November 1, last.

The judge also commenced inquiring into a statement made by “Shao Kwangtung,” the chief suspect, that Yang Wen-tao, another accused had visited Canton not long ago, bound on a mission to assassinate General Chen Chi-tang, then the “strong man” of Canton.

Although the investigation opened by the court of inquiry was mainly based on statements made by “Shao Kwangtung,” in court he again denied that he had said anything of the kind and again alleged that he had been beaten by police officers. Judge Shao, however, in order to go thoroughly into the case and to leave open no loophole, remanded the hearing again sine die and ordered the pictures of the three accused to be sent to the Kiangsu High Court for identification by men held in connection with the attempted assassination of Mr. Wang Ching-wei. As none of Yang Wen-tao’s finger-prints were found on the book hollowed out to hold a pistol, allegedly used to kill Nakayama, the court ordered Yang’s palm prints to be taken and sent for examination to the Chenju Legal Institute of Medicine.

The new investigations were started on the since repudiated confession made by “Shao Kwangtung,” who is alleged to have stated that he, the other two accused and several other members of the Tung Yi Association of which Yang was the Chairman, met in October of last year and decided on a threefold plan. It was resolved first to murder General Chiang Kai-shek, failing that they had to turn their attention to Mr. Wang Ching-wei. If they did not succeed to murder Mr. Wang, it was decided that they would create a disturbance in Shanghai by killing some Japanese officers.

Alleges Beating

“Shao Kwangtung” again alleged having been beaten by police and said that he could not but say whatever the police wanted him to. He stated that he had only wanted to die as quickly as possible and therefore said anything. He denied that he and the other accused had met to discuss plans for organizing an “Iron And Blood National Salvation Corps,” in order to embark on an assassination programme.

Yang Wen-tao denied any knowledge of any assassination plot, saying that he did not know Wang Ya-chiao, a man linked up with the attempt on Mr. Wang’s life, nor did he know Li Fu-tze, another suspect in the Wang case. He never organized any “bloody” group and knew no instigator of any murders. The judge expressed a doubt that soon after the attempt on Mr. Wang’s life, Nakayama was murdered in Shanghai which fact indicated that the story of Yang’s alleged co-operation with the Nanking terrorists might be true. Yang completely denied the allegation.

Yang said he organized the Tung Jen and Tung Yi Associations for a philanthropic cause. Differences among members of the Tung Jen Association forced him to organize the latter association for which only a preparatory office was established. No murder plot was discussed in the preparatory office. The latter organization was closed soon. Questioned as to why he moved the office three times, he said that it proved necessary for financial reasons. After being Chairman of the Association for two or three months he resigned.

Accused Cries

Chou Tso-yung, the third accused, also denied his connection with the Nanking terrorists or any plotters planning to murder any Japanese. He cried loudly when asked whether or not he had received $20 for his part in the Nakayama murder, as was once alleged by “Shao Kwangtung” in his repudiated confession. While weeping he said that he would not be so foolish as to murder a man for $20. He would rather be a robber, he said. Before he was arrested a detective came and asked him his name and his connection with “Shao Kwangtung.” He told everything frankly to police. He did not try to escape although he was arrested half an hour after the detective’s visit.

Soon after the opening of the hearing three elder members of the Peh Shan Residents’ Guild, a Cantonese organization, and relatives of Yang Wen-tao, answered many questions asked by the judge in regard to two letters Yang Wentao once carried to Canton. It was revealed after interrogation that it was purely a family affair, Yang being asked to secure the help of seven persons belonging to the same clan in Canton to help him bring pressure upon an elder native in Canton who was alleged to have abused his power among his natives, selling many properties belonging to the clan.

Yang Wen-tao went to Canton to see his sick uncle and was therefore asked by the elder members of his guild to settle a trouble in the clan. The Shanghai guild was asked by natives of Peh Shan in Canton to settle the clan trouble. Yang Wen-tao completely denied the allegation that he went to Canton on a secret mission of organizing an attempt on General Chen Chi-tang’s life. He never entered into politics although he was once employed as a counsellor of the 55th Army stationed in Paotao. He served in that capacity for only two months while staying in Shanghai. He did not seek the job, he said. It was given him by the army commander through an introduction of his friend.

Before the hearing opened Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Ru told the court that police had been able to find Yang Gien-chun, a relative of Yang Wen-tao, who is alleged to have changed the hollowed book in order to trap the latter. The court record of the demonstration recently staged by an amah who claimed to have heard the shot on the night when Nakayama was murdered was read in court.

《字林西报》，1936年8月6日，星期四

中山案被告被控
涉嫌参与刺杀汪精卫

法院就“邵广东”的另一份供词展开轰动性调查；
被告现被指称为恐怖分子

帮派据称曾计划先谋杀蒋介石或汪精卫

昨日下午，在第一特区法院，中山案出现了完全出乎意料的转折。在首次预审听证会上，邵法官开始深入调查一项指控，即三名被控于去年11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）谋杀日本海军陆战队准尉饭田秀雄（Iiideo Nakayama）的中国人，属于去年11月1日在南京企图刺杀前行政院院长汪精卫先生的恐怖分子团伙。

法官还开始讯问主要嫌疑人“邵广东”所作的一份陈述，该陈述称另一名被告杨文涛不久前前往广州，执行一项刺杀当时广州“实权人物”陈济棠将军的任务。

虽然法院开展的调查主要基于“邵广东”的供词，但他在法庭上再次否认曾说过此类话，并再次声称自己遭到警员殴打。然而，邵法官为了彻底查清案情且不留任何漏洞，再次宣布无限期延期审理，并命令将三名被告的照片送往江苏高等法院，由与刺杀汪精卫未遂案有关的人员进行辨认。由于在据称用于杀害中山的挖空藏枪书籍上未发现杨文涛的任何指纹，法院命令提取杨文涛的掌纹，并送交陈居法医研究所（Chenju Legal Institute of Medicine）进行检验。

新的调查始于“邵广东”此后予以否认的供词。据称他曾表示，他本人、另外两名被告以及同益会（Tung Yi Association）的其他几名成员（杨为该会主席）于去年十月会面，并决定了一项三重计划。决议首先谋杀蒋介石将军，若不成，则转而针对汪精卫先生。如果未能成功刺杀汪先生，则决定通过杀害几名日本军官在上海制造骚乱。

声称遭殴打

“邵广东”再次声称遭到警察殴打，并称他不得不按警察的要求随意招供。他表示，自己只想尽快求死，因此胡言乱语。他否认自己与其他被告曾会面讨论组织“铁血救国团”以实施刺杀计划的事宜。

杨文涛否认知晓任何刺杀阴谋，称他不认识与刺杀汪先生一案有关的王亚樵，也不认识汪案中的另一名嫌疑人李福兹（Li Fu-tze，音译）。他从未组织过任何“血腥”团体，也不认识任何谋杀案的指使者。法官表示怀疑，即在汪先生遇刺后不久，中山便在上海被杀，这一事实表明杨文涛可能与南京恐怖分子勾结的说法或许属实。杨文涛完全否认了这一指控。

杨文涛称，他组织同仁会和同益会是出于慈善目的。同仁会成员之间的分歧迫使他组织了后者，而后者仅设立了一个筹备处。筹备处内并未讨论任何谋杀计划。该组织随后很快关闭。当被问及为何三次搬迁办公地点时，他表示这是出于财政原因的必要之举。在担任该会主席两三个月后，他便辞职了。

被告哭泣

第三名被告周作庸（Chou Tso-yung，音译）也否认自己与南京恐怖分子或任何策划谋杀日本人的阴谋家有关联。当被问及是否如“邵广东”在其已否认的供词中曾指控的那样，因参与中山谋杀案而收取了20美元时，他大声哭泣。他边哭边说，自己不会愚蠢到为20美元去杀人。他说，他宁愿去做强盗。在被捕前，一名侦探前来询问他的姓名以及与“邵广东”的关系。他向警方坦承了一切。尽管在侦探来访半小时后他就被捕了，但他并未试图逃跑。

听证会开始后不久，北山居民公会（Peh Shan Residents’ Guild，一个广东人组织）的三位资深成员以及杨文涛的亲属，回答了法官就杨文涛曾携带至广州的两封信件提出的许多问题。经讯问揭示，这纯属家族事务，杨文涛受嘱寻求在广州的同宗七人帮助，向一位在广州的同乡长者施压，该长者被指在同乡中滥用职权，变卖了许多属于宗族的财产。

杨文涛前往广州探望生病的叔叔，因此受其公会资深成员之托，去解决宗族纠纷。上海的公会受广州北山同乡之托，调解宗族矛盾。杨文涛完全否认了他前往广州是执行组织刺杀陈济棠将军的秘密任务的指控。他从未涉足政治，尽管他曾任驻包头第五十五军的顾问。他说，他在上海期间担任该职仅两个月。他并未谋求此职，而是由军长通过其朋友介绍给予他的。

在听证会开始前，助理市检察官保罗·鲁（Paul Ru，音译）告诉法院，警方已找到杨文涛的亲戚杨健春（Yang Gien-chun，音译），据称此人曾调换那本挖空的书籍以陷害后者。法庭宣读了最近由一名声称在中山被杀当晚听到枪声的女佣所进行的演示的法庭记录。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, THURSDAY, AUGUST 6, 1936

Ex-Bouncer
Breaks Down
In Nakayama
Death Trial

New Hearing Brings Out
Police Link With Big
Nanking Murder Plot

GANG SAID OUT
FOR OFFICIALS

Hsiao Kwangtung Denies
Confession To This Ef-
fect, Alleges Torture

The attempted murder of Mr. Wang
Ching-wei, former President of the
Executive Yuan, in Nanking last
November came up in the Naka-
yama trial at the First Special
District Court yesterday afternoon
when the three accused were ques-
tioned for their alleged complicity
in the Nanking case.

This new turn in the hearing came
as a result of the evidence pre-
sented by the police in an effort to
show that Yih Hai-sen ("Hsiao
Kwangtung"), one of the three
accused, had planned to assassinate
either General Chiang Kai-shek or
Mr. Wang.

The new police evidence was in
the form of a special booklet, which
contained several previous confes-
sions of "Hsiao Kwangtung" as well
as materials collected by indepen-
dent investigation by the police.

In one of these statements, Yih
was said to have told the officers
that Wang Ya-chiao, who is want-
ed by authorities as the alleged
leader of the gang which
plotted the killing of the
former Yuan president was
present at one of the meetings pre-
ceding the shooting of Japanese
Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama
on Nov. 9, 1935.

The evidence presented by the
police prosecutor also alleged that
"Hsiao Kwangtung," in his confes-
sion about two months ago, stated
that some eight persons, including
himself and Yang Wen-tao were
present at a meeting called to or-
ganize a "Blood and Iron Salva-
tion Group."

Chiang Chief Object

The chief object of this group, ac-
cording to alleged confession pre-
sented to the court by the police,
was to assassinate General Chiang.
If this should fail, the confession
was stated to have said, the next
person to be murdered was Mr.
Wang. In the event that the at-
tempt on the former Executive Yuan
president should again fall through,
the group, according to the police
evidence, planned to kill two Japan-
ese officers.

Questioned by the court on the
alleged confession yesterday, "Hsiao
Kwangtung" stuck to his story
that he was tortured by the police
and denied that the extensive plan
for murder was true. He stated
that the police suggested to him
that a large group of people must
have been present when the con-
ference was held to discuss the kill-
ing of the Japanese. He was asked
who these people were.

"I was being beaten at that time,"
he told the Court, "so in order
to stop the punishment I wrote
down the names I could think of.
Some of these people were my ac-
quaintances, others were merely fic-
titious to make up the seven or
eight insisted on by the police."

One of these eight names which
Yih Hai-sen wrote down was Wang
Ya-chiao.

Earlier in the trial, the name of
General Chen Chi-tang, deposed
Pacification Commissioner of the
Kwangtung Province, also came up
in the Court's questioning in regard
to a letter written to Yang
Wen-tao when he was in Canton
in 1934. Some of the relevant sen-
tences in the letter intimated that
Yang was to "get rid of a certain
man" and that "seven men would
help him in carrying out the work."
The concluding sentences in the
letter stated that if "it would cost
$3,000 or $4,000, the sum would be
comparatively a small amount," and
the writers of the letter would send
the fund.

3 Men In Court

The three writers of this myster-
ious letter were in Court yesterday
to answer questions regarding the
real meaning of the sentences
cited. They were asked whether the
man to "get rid of" was General
Chen Chi-fang. This was flatly
denied by the witnesses.

The three men are, Yang Tsung-
chien, Yang Hai-sen, a former
employee of the Sincere Company,
and Yang Wen-jih, Chinese pas-
senger agent of the Dollar Steam-
ship Company.

They told the Court that the
"certain man" was the magistrate
in their home county, Pei Hai in
Kwangtung Province, who had
been misappropriating funds in his
official capacity. As Yang was in
the South at that time, they asked
him to do whatever he could to
get the magistrate in question out
of office.

They mentioned the "seven men"
to help Yang, because the latter
was not familiar with local condi-
tions.

The three witnesses were ques-
tioned separately and later their
testimony was corroborated by Yang
Wen-tao, who was excused from
the courtroom when the questioning
of the three was in progress.

Ex-Bouncer Cries In Court

During the trial, Chow Sha-yung,
one-time cabaret "bouncer", who
was implicated as one of the plot-
ters of the Nakayama killing by
Yih Hai-sen, broke down and cried
when he was questioned by the
judge.

He was asked whether he received
a "pay-off" of $25 after killing the
Japanese is charged in one of the
repudiated confessions of "Hsiao
Kwangtung." Breaking into tears,
Chow turned to the interpreter and
implored:

"Please tell the Court . . . Why
should I go out and kill a man
against whom I have no grudge for
$25. If I wanted the money, I
could have gone out and robbed
someone."

Later, he again sobbed and said:
"The day I was arrested, some
detective came to the Continental
Ballroom and asked if my name was
Chow Sha-yung. I told him it was.
The man asked me to write my name
down and wait him. In about half
an hour he came back and arrested
me. If I was involved in the case,
I could have escaped easily during
the 30 minutes. I don't know any-
thing about this killing, I tell you.
I don't know anything about this."

Great Nervousness Displayed

Chow was by far the most nervous
man among the three standing in
the prisoners' dock yesterday. He
eyed the defense lawyers, drummed
his thin fingers on the railing and
appeared generally ill at ease.

"Hsiao Kwangtung" who was in
tears and cried several times during
previous hearings, was comparative-
ly calm yesterday. But when Chow
began to sob, tears also started to
stream down Yih's face.

Yang Wen-tao, who was charged
as the "brain" of the crime, re-
mained calm and immobile, his
facial expression revealing no
apparent emotion.

"Hsiao Kwangtung" was still
dressed in his dark serge trousers
and patent leather shoes in which he
was arrested more than three months
ago. Owing to the hot weather he
had taken off his coat, and came
into the Court in a slightly torn
and soiled shirt. Chow was also
clothed in the heavy brown
woolen trousers and brown shirt,
in which he was taken into custody.

Most of the hearing yesterday
was occupied by checking up the
statements made previously by the
three accused.

To clear up the angle on the
complication of the three accused
in the attempted murder of Mr.
Wang, pictures of the trio will be
sent to Nanking for identification by
the accused held in the Capital.

The book, in which the murder
gun was alleged to have been hid-
den, will be re-examined by the
Judicial Laboratory.

The trial was adjourned sine die.

《字林西报》，1936年8月6日，星期四

前保镖
在中山案
审讯中崩溃

新听证会揭露
警方与南京重大
谋杀阴谋之关联

据称团伙
针对政府官员

萧广东否认
曾作此类供认，
指控遭受酷刑

去年十一月在南京发生的刺杀前行政院院长汪精卫先生未遂案，于昨日下午在第一特区法院审理中山案时再次被提及，当时三名被告就其涉嫌参与南京一案接受了讯问。

听证会出现这一新转折，是由于警方提交了证据，试图证明三名被告之一的易海森（即“萧广东”）曾策划刺杀蒋介石将军或汪精卫先生。

警方的新证据以一本特别小册子的形式呈现，其中包含了“萧广东”此前的几份供词，以及警方通过独立调查收集的材料。

在这些陈述之一中，据说易某向警官透露，王亚樵（当局通缉的涉嫌策划刺杀前行政院院长的团伙头目）出席了1935年11月9日日本军曹中山秀雄遇刺前的一次会议。

警方检察官提交的证据还指控，“萧广东”在约两个月前的供词中称，包括他本人和杨文道在内的约八人出席了一次旨在组织“铁血救国会”的会议。

蒋介石是主要目标

根据警方提交法庭的所谓供词，该团体的主要目标是刺杀蒋介石将军。供词称，如果此计划失败，下一个谋杀对象将是汪精卫先生。据警方证据显示，若对前行政院院长的刺杀行动再次失败，该团体计划杀害两名日本军官。

昨日在法庭上就被指供词接受讯问时，“萧广东”坚持称其遭受警方酷刑，并否认存在大规模的谋杀计划。他表示，警方暗示他在讨论刺杀日本人的会议期间，现场一定有很多人。警方问他这些人是谁。

“我当时正遭到殴打，”他告诉法庭，“为了停止惩罚，我写下了我能想到的名字。这些人中有些是我的熟人，其他则是虚构的，以凑足警方坚持要求的七八个人。”

易海森写下的八个名字之一就是王亚樵。

在庭审早期，法庭在询问一封于1934年杨文道在广州时写给他的信时，也提到了前广东省绥靖主任陈济棠将军的名字。信中的一些相关句子暗示杨文道要“除掉某个人”，并且“有七个人会协助他完成这项工作”。信的结尾部分 stated 称，如果“花费3000或4000美元，这笔钱相对来说数目不大”，写信人将提供这笔资金。

三人在庭

这封神秘信函的三位作者昨日出庭，就上述句子的真实含义回答问题。他们被问及要“除掉”的人是否是陈济芳将军。证人对此予以断然否认。

这三人分别是：杨宗健、先施公司前雇员杨海森，以及美商轮船公司（Dollar Steamship Company）华籍客运代理杨文日。

他们告诉法庭，“某个人”是指他们在广东省北海县家乡的县长，该县长利用职权挪用公款。由于杨文道当时在南方，他们请求他尽其所能让该县长下台。

他们提到“七个人”协助杨文道，是因为后者不熟悉当地情况。

这三名证人分别接受了讯问，随后他们的证词得到了杨文道的证实；在对这三人进行讯问期间，杨文道被请出法庭。

前保镖在庭上哭泣

在审判过程中，周少庸（音译），一位曾是舞厅“保镖”的男子，因被易海森指控为中山刺杀案的策划者之一，在接受法官讯问时情绪崩溃并痛哭流涕。

他被问及是否在“萧广东”一份已被推翻的供词中所指控的那样，在杀死日本人后收到了25美元的“酬金”。周少庸泪流满面，转向翻译员恳求道：

“请告诉法庭……我怎么会为了25美元出去杀害一个与我无怨无仇的人。如果我想要钱，我大可以出去抢劫别人。”

随后，他再次抽泣着说：“我被捕那天，有个侦探来到大陆饭店（Continental Ballroom），问我的名字是不是周少庸。我说是。那人让我写下名字并等他。大约半小时后他回来逮捕了我。如果我与此案有关，我本可以在这30分钟内轻易逃脱。我告诉你们，我对这起杀人案一无所知。我对此一无所知。”

表现出极度紧张

周少庸是昨日站在被告席上的三人中最为紧张的一个。他注视着辩护律师，用手指在栏杆上敲击，显得普遍不自在。

“萧广东”在前几次听证会上曾流泪数次，昨日则相对平静。但当周少庸开始抽泣时，眼泪也开始顺着易某的脸颊流下。

被指控为犯罪“主脑”的杨文道保持冷静和不动声色，面部表情没有流露出明显的情绪。

“萧广东”仍穿着三个多月前被捕时所穿的深色哔叽长裤和漆皮鞋。由于天气炎热，他脱掉了外套，穿着一件略有破损和污渍的衬衫进入法庭。周少庸也穿着他被拘留时所穿的厚重棕色羊毛长裤和棕色衬衫。

昨日的听证会大部分时间用于核对三名被告此前所作的陈述。

为了厘清三名被告在刺杀汪精卫先生未遂案中的牵连角度，三人的照片将被送往南京，由扣押在首都的被告进行辨认。

据称藏匿凶枪的那本书，将由司法实验室重新检查。

审判无限期休庭。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, -Tuesday,-August 4, 1936

Nakayama Trial
To Take Weeks

Early Verdict Unlikely
Despite Agitations
By Japanese

The trial of the three Cantonese, Yih Hai-sen, alias Hsiao Kwangtung, Yang Wen-tao and Clow Sha-yung, on charges of murder of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama of the Japanese Naval Landing Party on Darroch Road on November 9, 1935, is to last for at least two more sessions despite the Japanese clamor for a speedy conclusion, it is learned at the First Special District Court this morning.

Despite earlier reports, it has now been ascertained that the session scheduled at 2 o'clock tomorrow afternoon will be devoted to further questioning of the accused and possibly several witnesses. If time allows, the prosecution and the defense will sum up their case and the trial will be again adjourned for judgment. It is generally believed, however, that the questioning will take up the whole session and that the next session will be for summing up, thus necessitating yet another session for the judgment.

Japanese Agitate

The Japanese community in Shanghai continued their agitation for a speedy conclusion of the trial today. Allegations that the three accused, particularly Hsiao Kwangtung and Yang Wen-tao, have political support and background and that the City Kuomintang is seeking to effect their release were contained in press reports.

Indicative of the Japanese press reports on the Nakayama case is the Shanghai Mainichi report this morning which predicts that tomorrow's session would be preceded by a secret conference of officials of the local Kuomintang, presidents of the Kiangsu High Court, the First and Second Special District Courts.

Similar Session

A similar meeting, the journal asserted, was held in the early morning hours of July 27, just prior to the ninth hearing.

The new deliberations are necessitated, according to the Mainichi, by the disclosure of powerful political support behind the two chief accused, Yang Wentao and "Hsiao Kwangtung".

The journal predicted that one of the consequences of the conference would be "a change of front" in the local Chinese press, the dailies presumably arguing that the two accused have no political affiliations or connections whatsoever.

To Rescue Yang

In addition to a number of Chinese notables and Kuomintang officials, who had come to the rescue of Yang, Mr. Mao Yun, an attorney and a member of the local Special Tangpu, has also played, according to the Japanese paper, a prominent part in seeking Yang's release.

Mr. Mao, the journal said, has long been active on behalf of Yang and the latter's Hung Shun Mutual Aid Society, a powerful organization of local Cantonese residents.

Both Yang and "Hsiao Kwangtung", were described yesterday by the Shanghai Nippo as "professional assassins", who had "their finger in almost every notorious political murder of recent years".

"It must also be noted", the paper declared, "that the two men have been actively engaged in anti-Japanese work since the Manchurian Incident of 1931".

"Both of the accused men", the daily continued, "are members of the Hung Pang, the notorious Cantonese underworld organization, controlled by the Hung Hsin Society".
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年8月4日，星期二

中山案审判
将持续数周

尽管日本人
鼓噪，早期
判决不太可能

据悉，第一特区法院今晨表示，尽管日本人呼吁迅速结案，但对三名广东人——易海森（别名萧广东）、杨文道和周少庸（Clow Sha-yung，原文如此）——因涉嫌于1935年11月9日在达罗克路（Darroch Road）谋杀日本海军陆战队军曹中山秀雄一案的审判，至少还将进行两次庭审。

尽管早先有报道，但现在已确定，定于明天下午两点进行的庭审将致力于进一步讯问被告，可能还包括几名证人。如果时间允许，控辩双方将进行总结陈词，然后审判将再次休庭以待判决。然而，人们普遍认为，讯问将占据整个庭审时段，下一次庭审将用于总结陈词，因此还需要再一次庭审来进行判决。

日本人鼓噪

上海日本侨民今日继续鼓动迅速结束审判。新闻报道中包含了指控，称三名被告，特别是萧广东和杨文道，拥有政治支持和背景，且市国民党正寻求释放他们。

上海《每日新闻》（Shanghai Mainichi）今晨的报道预示了日本媒体对中山案的报道倾向，该报预测明天的庭审之前，当地国民党官员、江苏高等法院院长以及第一和第二特区法院院长将举行秘密会议。

该刊声称，类似的会议曾在7月27日凌晨举行，就在第九次听证会之前。

据《每日新闻》称，新的审议是必要的，因为披露了两名主要被告杨文道和“萧广东”背后有强大的政治支持。

该报预测，会议的后果之一是当地中文报纸的“立场转变”，这些日报可能会辩称这两名被告没有任何政治隶属关系或联系。

营救杨文道

据该日文报纸称，除了许多前来营救杨文道的中国名人和国民党官员外，律师、当地特种唐浦（Special Tangpu，原文不清，可能指特定机构或团体）成员毛云先生也在寻求释放杨文道方面发挥了重要作用。

该报称，毛先生长期以来一直代表杨文道及其洪顺互助社（Hung Shun Mutual Aid Society，一个由当地广东居民组成的强大组织）积极活动。

《上海日报》（Shanghai Nippo）昨日将杨文道和“萧广东”描述为“职业刺客”，称他们“几乎插手了近年来每一起臭名昭著的政治谋杀案”。

该报宣称：“还必须注意到，自1931年满洲事变以来，这两人一直积极参与反日活动。”

该日报继续写道：“两名被告均为‘洪帮’成员，这是一个由洪兴社控制的臭名昭著的广东地下组织。”
