15699
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, August 3, 1936

Hsiao Kwangtung
"Hired Assassin"

Suspects Of Nakayama
Murder Said Belong
To "Ou Pang"

"Hsiao Kwangtung" and Yang Wen-tao, leading figures in the sensational "Nakayama trial", which is to be resumed on Wednesday afternoon were described yesterday by the Shanghai Nippo as "professional assassins", who had had "their fingers in almost every notorious political murder of recent years".

"It must also be noted," the paper declared, "that the two men have been actively engaged in anti-Japanese work since the Manchurian incident of 1931.

Belong To Ou Pang

"Both of the accused men", the daily continued, "are members of the Ou Pang, the notorious Cantonese underworld organization, controlled by the Hung Hsin Society".

The Nippo assailed the local office of the Kuomintang for continuing its alleged efforts to secure the release of "Hsiao Kwangtung" and Yang.

"Although it is certain that the Tangpu did not instruct the Ou Pang to murder Japanese, it should be held responsible for permitting the secret organization to exist.

Deplore Police Failure

"We cannot give up our doubts as to the true attitude of the Kuomintang, as long as several of its influential members, as well as officials of the Chinese Municipality, continue their efforts to regain freedom for Yang."

Expressing regret at the failure of the Public Safety Bureau to arrest the assassin of Mr. Kosaku Kayau, a Japanese sea-food broker, shot and killed on July 10, the daily saw little hope for the Chinese Government's efforts to secure the return of foreign settlements and concessions in China at an early date.

Pair Claimed Guilty

The daily expressed its scepticism over the attitude of the First Special District Court, and predicted that an acquittal of the accused would result in a revival of political assassinations.

"That Yang and Hsiao Kwangtung had committed the crime is beyond any doubt," the daily asserted.

"It is useless, however, to indulge in talk now. We must await the sincere and just verdict of the Court."

The Nippo concluded by urging the Nanking Government to suppress all anti-Nipponese and professional assassins' organizations, to prevent the recurrence of "lamentable cases."

Kayau Case

Mr. Kaname Wakasugi, Japanese Consul-General here, this morning called on General Wu Teh-chen, Mayor of Greater Shanghai, to ask for the speedy apprehension of the murderers of Mr. Kosaku Kayau.

The Japanese official pointed out that more than three weeks have already elapsed, since Mr. Kayau, a Japanese sea-food broker, was shot and killed in Chi Mei Road on the night of July 10, without the discovery of a single clue by the Chinese police.
pages.zh:
15699
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年8月3日，星期一

萧广东
“受雇刺客”

中山谋杀案嫌疑人
据称属于“欧帮”

《上海日报》昨日称，在将于周三下午复庭的轰动一时的“中山案审判”中的关键人物“萧广东”和杨文涛是“职业刺客”，近年来几乎每一起臭名昭著的政治谋杀案都有他们的份。

该报宣称：“还必须指出，这两人自1931年满洲事变以来一直积极参与反日活动。”

属于欧帮

该日报继续写道：“两名被告均为‘欧帮’成员，这是一个由洪兴社控制的臭名昭著的广东地下组织。”

《上海日报》抨击国民党当地办事处继续其所谓的为争取释放“萧广东”和杨文涛而进行的努力。

“虽然可以肯定，党部并未指示欧帮谋杀日本人，但应对其允许该秘密组织存在承担责任。”

痛惜警方无能

该报表示：“只要国民党的几位有影响力成员以及华界市政府官员继续为杨文涛重获自由而努力，我们就无法消除对国民党真实态度的怀疑。”

该报对公共安全局未能逮捕7月10日被枪杀的日本海鲜经纪人加屋（Kosaku Kayau）先生的凶手表示遗憾，并认为中国政府在短期内收回外国租界和租借地的努力希望渺茫。

二人被指有罪

该日报对第一特区地方法院的态度表示怀疑，并预测如果被告被判无罪，将导致政治暗杀活动死灰复燃。

该日报断言：“杨文涛和萧广东犯下了罪行，这是毫无疑问的。”

“然而，现在空谈无益。我们必须等待法院真诚公正的判决。”

《上海日报》最后敦促南京政府镇压所有反日组织和职业刺客组织，以防止再次发生“令人痛心的案件”。

加屋案

日本驻沪总领事若杉要（Kaname Wakasugi）今晨拜会大上海市长吴铁城将军，要求迅速缉拿杀害加屋（Kosaku Kayau）先生的凶手。

这位日本官员指出，自7月10日晚日本海鲜经纪人加屋先生在集美路被枪杀以来，已过去三周多，中国警方未发现任何线索。

pages.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, AUGUST 6, 1936

MORE WITNESSES IN
NAKAYAMA CASE

Yang Questioned About Plot
to Kill Gen. Chiang Kai-shek

YIH SAYS CONFESSION
OBTAINED BY TORTURE

Allegations that eight men, in-
cluding two of three Cantonese, Yih
Hai-sen, alias "Little Cantonese,"
and Yang Ven-tao, accused of the
murder of H. Nakayama, a Japanese
marine, on November 9 last, were
members of an assassination gang
which had plotted to murder Gen.
Chiang Kai-shek, Mr. Wang Ching-
wei, and two Japanese officers in
order to create disturbances were
made in the First Special District
Court yesterday afternoon when the
Nakayama case came up before Judge
Hsiao Shih-feng for another hearing.
Yang Ven-tao was questioned
about two letters which he received
from a Cantonese residents associa-
tion of Shanghai during his trip to
Kwangtung in 1934. These two let-
ters, it was said, contained a veiled
threat to kill a certain person. In
answer to the Judge, Yang stated
these letters referred to their attempt
to overthrow a depraved gentry in
his native district in Kwangtung,
Chungshan, who was alleged to have
unlawfully appropriated to his own
use property belonging to the public.
The Judge asked Yang whether the
threat to kill a person referred to in
the letters meant a plot to kill Gen.
Chen Chi-tang, until recently the
"Strong Man" of Kwangtung, and
Yang replied "No."
Four Cantonese witnesses, all from
the Yang family in Chungshan,
Kwangtung, testified about the two
letters and their evidence was to the
effect that the veiled threat contain-
ed in the letters meant an attempt
to remove a gentry in their native
district, but did not mean any plot
to kill Gen. Chen Chi-tang. These
letters were sent to Yang Ven-tao
during his visit to Kwangtung, wit-
nesses told the court.

Another Plot Alleged

The Judge then started to question
Yang Ven-tao about his past his-
tory. In answer to the Judge, Yang
denied he was once an officer of the
19th Route Army in Shanghai nor
was he the Public Safety Bureau
Commissioner or the Mayor of Amoy
when the "People's Revolutionary
Government" was established in
Foochow. The accused admitted he
was once a high officer of the 55th
Army for about two months.
Producing a copy of a written
statement made by Yih Hai-sen at
the police station, the Judge told
Yang that Yih had implicated him
and six others as members of a
well-organized murder gang with a
plot to kill Gen. Chiang Kai-shek.
If this plot failed, they would map
out plans to kill Mr. Wang Ching-
wei, and if this again failed, they
would kill two Japanese officers in
Shanghai in order to stir up troub-
les, according to Yih's statement. The
Judge said, according to Yih, the
gang was known as the "Iron and
Blood National Salvation Corps." The
Judge pointed out it was significant
that the attempt on Mr. Wang Ching-
wei's life was made on November 1
and the murder of the Japanese
marine on Darroch Road was com-
mitted on November 9, which were
close to each other. In reply to the
Judge, Yang said he knew nothing
of all these.

Both "Little Cantonese" and the
third accused, Chow Zeu-yoong, were
also questioned about the alleged plot
and they all denied any knowledge,
"Little Cantonese" saying he had
made this statement at the station by
torture.
Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant Muni-
cipal Advocate, prosecuting, told the
Judge that the police, during the
period of remand, could not find the
man named Yang Tsien-tsoong who
was alleged to have planted a book
used to conceal a pistol in the house
of Yang Ven-tao in order to implicate
the latter in Nakayama's murder.
At the conclusion of the hearing,
the Judge mentioned that a further
adjournment was necessary to enable
the Chenju Judicial Laboratory to
conduct another examination of the
book found in Yang Ven-tao's house
and make inquiries regarding the
three accused's past activities at the
Kiangsu High Court. No date was
fixed for the next hearing.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年8月6日，星期四

中山案更多证人出庭

杨文涛就刺杀蒋介石将军阴谋接受质询

易海森称供系刑讯逼供

昨日下午，中山案在法官萧世凤面前再次开庭审理。有人指控包括两名广东人在内的八名男子——其中两人是易海森（别名“小广东”）和杨文涛，他们被控于去年11月9日谋杀日本海军陆战队员H. 中山（H. Nakayama）——是一个刺杀团伙的成员，该团伙曾策划谋杀蒋介石将军、汪精卫先生和两名日本军官，以制造动乱。

杨文涛就他在1934年赴广东途中收到的两封来自上海广东居民协会的信件接受了质询。据说这两封信包含了对杀害某人的隐晦威胁。杨文涛回答法官时说，这些信件指的是他们试图推翻其家乡广东中山县的一名腐败士绅，该士绅被指控非法侵吞公共财产据为己有。法官问杨文涛，信中提到的杀人威胁是否意指策划杀害陈济棠将军（直至最近仍是广东的“强人”），杨文涛回答“不是”。

四名来自广东中山杨家的广东籍证人就这两封信作证，他们的证词大意是，信中包含的隐晦威胁是指试图除掉他们家乡的一名士绅，但并不意味任何刺杀陈济棠将军的阴谋。证人告诉法庭，这些信件是在杨文涛访问广东期间寄给他的。

另一起阴谋指控

随后，法官开始就杨文涛的过往经历对其进行质询。杨文涛回答法官时否认他曾是驻上海的第十九路军军官，也否认在福州成立“人民革命政府”时担任过公共安全局局长或厦门市市长。被告承认他曾在第五十五军担任高级军官约两个月。

法官出示了一份易海森在警察局所作的书面陈述副本，并告诉杨文涛，易海森牵连他和另外六人是一个组织严密的谋杀团伙成员，该团伙策划刺杀蒋介石将军。根据易海森的陈述，如果这一阴谋失败，他们将制定计划刺杀汪精卫先生；如果再次失败，他们将刺杀上海的两名日本军官以挑起事端。法官说，据易海森称，该团伙被称为“铁血救国团”。法官指出，值得注意的是，针对汪精卫先生的刺杀企图发生在11月1日，而达罗克路日本海军陆战队员被杀案发生在11月9日，两者时间相近。杨文涛回答法官说，他对所有这些情况一无所知。

“小广东”和第三名被告周祖荣也就所谓的阴谋接受了质询，他们都否认知情，“小广东”称他在警局的供述是遭受酷刑所致。

助理市政检察官鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru）先生告诉法官，在还押候审期间，警方未能找到名为杨建宗（音译，Yang Tsien-tsoong）的男子，据称此人为了陷害杨文涛参与中山谋杀案，将一本用于藏匿手枪的书放进了杨文涛的家中。

听证会结束时，法官提到有必要进一步休庭，以便震旦大学法医实验室对在杨文涛家中发现的那本书进行再次检验，并向江苏高等法院查询三名被告的过往活动。下次听证会的日期尚未确定。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JULY 30, 1926

Amah Gives Demonstration
Of Nakayama's Killing

Witness To Shooting Taken To Scene Of Crime
And Explains What She Saw To Chinese Judge;
Japanese Angry Over Delayed Decision

While charges of insincerity were being made by the Japanese press against those conducting the trial of the alleged slayers of Hideo Nakayama, and protests were made over the surprise re-opening of the trial on Tuesday for the purpose of taking testimony from a Chinese amah. opening of the trial on Tuesday night witnessed a demonstration by the amah at the scene of the crime.

According to the vernacular press Pan Chiao-ying, the Chinese amah who claimed to have been a witness to the shooting, was taken by officials of the First Special District Court to Darroch Road where Nakayama was killed by an unknown assassin in November of last year. In the presence of Judge Shiao and court officials the amah demonstrated how she saw the dead Japanese officer and his possible assassin about 30 paces apart when the shot was fired which ended Nakayama's life.

The woman showed how she was returning to the home of her mistress in Yung An Alley, after visiting a friend's home in Min Deh Fang. Walking along the footpath she demonstrated how she reached the junction of North Szechuen Road and Kiangwan Road. She walked and turned into Darroch Road and when opposite house No. 91 declared that she saw the Japanese coming towards her. He passed on the western side of the road and she saw a man in a black gown walking on the eastern side of the road some 30 feet behind the Japanese. They both passed her and a short time later she heard a shot and turning saw the Japanese lying on the ground. As she was carrying a Japanese child she did not return to see what had happened.

Continuing her demonstration the amah showed how she walked to a hot water shop and entering the front door went out into the alley at the back of the shop and thence to the house of her mistress.

The judge ordered one of the court officials to put on the coat of "Little Kwangtung," the alleged slayer of Nakayama, and stand where the man in the black coat had been seen. Asked if she could identify the coat, the amah said that the coat was similar to the one worn by the mysterious person who had passed her on Darroch Road, just prior to the shot.

This concluded the demonstration.

Insincerity Charged

Charges of insincerity were levelled yesterday by local Nipponese papers and officials against the Chinese judicial officials who are trying the alleged assassins of Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama.

The outburst of indignation was apparently caused by the Court session of the previous day, when a Chinese amah, Pu Chaoying, brought here for the purpose from Kompo, was examined by the court.

Lieut.-Commander Matao Okino, assistant naval attache to the Japanese Embassy here, told the Shanghai "Mainichi" that it was "unreasonable" of the Court to announce a postponement to enable it to pronounce the judgment, and then hold a surprise hearing for the amah.

"Such an attitude cannot but make all Japanese residents here extremely indignant. If the Court fails to announce definitely the date on which the verdict is to be handed down at the scheduled hearing on July 31, we shall regard it as a serious matter."

The three local Nipponese dailies also bitterly assailed the Court for its reported intention to postpone indefinitely the next scheduled session.

The Shanghai "Nichi-Nichi" asserted that the Court notified the Shanghai Municipal Council that last Tuesday's session would be closed to the public.

This intention, however, did not materialize, the "Nichi-Nichi" charged, as a reporter and a counsel for the defence were allowed to enter the Court Chamber, and were later responsible for making the hearing public.

In an editorial devoted to the "Nakayama" case, the "Mainichi" urged the Court to hold the scheduled hearing on July 31, announcing on that day the date when the final judgment would be given.

The "Nippo" demanded the "eradication" of the assassins of Nakayama, to maintain peace and order and to aid in the promotion of amicable relations between Japan and China.

The Kayau Case

Officers of the Bureau of Public Safety have so far made no arrest in connection with the murder of K. Kayau who was found dead with a bullet wound in his head, on July 10. Several officials of the bureau, including head of the detective department, Colonel Liang Fu-tsu of the North Railway Substation, have petitioned the bureau commissioner asking to be punished for their failure to arrest the murderer. Monday was the second deadline announced for making arrests in connection with the case. The reward for the arrest of the murderer offered by the Bureau has been increased to $1-000.
pages.zh:
《上海时报》，1926年7月30日，星期四

女佣演示中山遇害经过

目击枪击的女佣被带至犯罪现场，向中国法官解释其所见；日方因判决推迟而愤怒

就在日本报纸指责审理中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama） alleged slayers（涉嫌凶手）的人员缺乏诚意，并对周二突然重启庭审以听取一名中国女佣证词提出抗议之际，周二晚上的庭审见证了该女佣在犯罪现场的演示。

据中文报刊报道，声称目睹枪击过程的中国女佣潘巧英（Pan Chiao-ying）被第一特区地方法院的官员带到达罗克路，中山于去年11月在此地被一名不明刺客杀害。在萧法官和法院官员面前，女佣演示了当那颗结束中山生命的子弹射出时，她看到死者日本军官与其可能的刺客相距约30步的情景。

该女子展示她如何在拜访明德坊的一位朋友家后，返回永安里的女主人家中。沿着人行道行走时，她演示了自己如何到达四川北路与江湾路的交汇处。她走着转入达罗克路，当走到91号对面时，她声称看到一名日本人朝她走来。该日本人从道路西侧经过，她看到一名身穿黑袍的男子在道路东侧行走，落后那名日本人约30英尺。两人都从她身边经过，不久后她听到一声枪响，转身看到那名日本人倒在地上。由于她抱着一名日本儿童，她没有回去查看发生了什么事。

女佣继续演示，展示她如何走到一家热水店，从前门进入，再从店铺后面的弄堂出来，然后回到女主人的家。

法官命令一名法院官员穿上中山涉嫌凶手“小广东”的外套，站在那名穿黑外套男子被发现的位置。当被问及能否辨认出这件外套时，女佣说这件外套与枪响前刚刚在达罗克路上从她身边经过的那个神秘人所穿的外套相似。

演示至此结束。

被指缺乏诚意

昨日，当地日本报纸和官员指控审理海军士官中山秀雄涉嫌凶手的中国司法官员缺乏诚意。

这种愤怒的爆发显然是由前一天的庭审引起的，当时法院审讯了专门从虹口（Kompo）带来的一名中国女佣卜超英（Pu Chaoying，音译）。

日本驻沪大使馆海军副武官奥野又雄（Matao Okino）中校告诉上海《每日新闻》（Mainichi），法院宣布延期以便宣判，随后又突然举行听证会审讯女佣，这是“不合理的”。

“这种态度不得不令所有在沪日本居民极为愤怒。如果法院不能在定于7月31日举行的预定听证会上明确宣布宣判日期，我们将视其为严重事件。”

当地三家日本日报也严厉抨击法院据报道有意无限期推迟下一次预定庭审。

上海《日日新闻》（Nichi-Nichi）断言，法院通知上海工部局，上周二的庭审将对公众关闭。

然而，《日日新闻》指控称，这一意图并未实现，因为一名记者和一名辩护律师被允许进入法庭，并随后导致听证会对公众开放。

在一篇关于“中山”案的社论中，《每日新闻》敦促法院举行定于7月31日的听证会，并在当天宣布最终判决的日期。

《上海日报》（Nippo）要求“铲除”中山的刺客，以维持和平与秩序，并促进中日友好关系的发展。

加屋案

截至目前，公共安全局官员在加屋（K. Kayau）谋杀案中尚未逮捕任何人。加屋于7月10日被发现头部中弹身亡。该局包括北站侦探股股长梁福祖（Liang Fu-tsu，音译）上校在内的几名官员已向警务处长请愿，要求因未能逮捕凶手而受到处罚。星期一是该案逮捕嫌疑人的第二个最后期限。公共安全局提供的缉拿凶手赏金已增加至1,000美元。

pages.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, WEDNESDAY, JULY 29, 1936

AMAH QUESTIONED IN
NAKAYAMA CASE

Testimony of Witness from
North Kiangsu

Pu Chiao-ying, an 18-year old
maid-servant, said to be an import-
ant witness of the murder of H.
Nakayama, a Japanese marine, on
November 9 last, testified in the
First Special District Court yester-
day when the hearing was resumed
of the case against three Cantonese,
Yih Hai-sen, alias "Little Cantonese,"
Yang Ven-tao, and Chow Zeu-yung,
accused of the murder of the Japanese
marine. The maid-servant left for
her native district in north Kiangsu
some time ago and was brought
back here on Monday to tell what
she knew about the case.

Questioned by the Judge, the
witness said she was employed last
year at a Japanese house in the
Yung En Terrace, North Szechuen
Road. On November 9, at about 8
p.m., witness continued, she took a
child for a stroll and when they
passed Darroch Road, they saw a
Japanese marine and a man in black
foreign-style clothing were walking
from south to north along Darroch
Road, but the marine was on the
west side of the road and the other
one, along the east side. Witness,
however, said she could not identify
any of the three accused as the man
in black clothing whom she met on
the night in question.

Asked what happened after that,
witness said, when she was near a
hot water shop, she heard a shot
and then returned home by another
route.

The hearing was then further
adjourned.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年7月29日，星期三

中山案中受讯问的女佣

来自江苏北部的证人证词

蒲娇英（Pu Chiao-ying），一名18岁的女佣，据称是去年11月9日日本海军陆战队员H. Nakayama（中山）谋杀案的重要证人，昨日在第一特区法院出庭作证。当时法院恢复审理针对三名广东人——易海森（Yih Hai-sen，绰号“小广东”）、杨文道（Yang Ven-tao）和周祖荣（Chow Zeu-yung）——被控谋杀该日本海军陆战队员的案件。这名女佣前一段时间返回其江苏北部老家，周一被带回此处，以陈述其所知的案件情况。

经法官讯问，证人表示她去年受雇于北四川路永恩里（Yung En Terrace）的一户日本人家庭。证人继续说道，11月9日晚上8点左右，她带着一个孩子外出散步，当他们经过达罗克路（Darroch Road）时，看见一名日本海军陆战队员和一名身穿黑色西式服装的男子正沿着达罗克路从南向北行走，但海军陆战队员在路的西侧，而另一人在东侧。然而，证人表示她无法指认三名被告中的任何一人为她在案发当晚遇到的那名穿黑衣的男子。

当被问及随后发生了什么事时，证人表示，当她靠近一家热水店时，听到一声枪响，随后便经由另一条路线回家。

听证会随后再次休庭。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Tuesday, July 28, 1936

Nakayama Case
Hearing Held

Amah Kompo Returns
To Give Testimony
About Murder

Coming as a distinct surprise, the Nakayama case was again up for hearing in the First District Court this morning as an 18-year-old amah testified that on the night of November 9 last year on Darroch Road she had heard a shot and had turned to see Nakayama lying on the ground.

The amah, Pu Yao-yin, whom police brought down from Kompo yesterday, has been placed in the position of being the ostensible reason why the case was reopened on July 17 at a time when a verdict was scheduled to be given.

Hearing A Surprise

The hearing this morning came as a surprise to everyone except those in "the know," as the next hearing had not been scheduled until Friday. The amah's testimony was given before a court room empty of practically everyone but court officials, police and Japanese officials who stood in solemn array in the dock behind the three accused, Yih Hai-sen (Shao Kwangtung), Yang Wentao and Chow Hsia-yung. The usual full court did no attend and the hearings were conducted by Judge Siao Shih-feng. The case was adjorned sine die.

The amah testified that she was walking in a southerly direction on the night of the murder and that she passed between a civilian and a sailor who were walking on the east and west sides of the street, respectively. At the time, she noticed that the civilian was wearing a dark suit of clothes.

Heard Shot

Shortly after she passed the two men, she said she heard a shot and, turning, saw the sailor lying on the ground. This morning she failed to identify any of the three accused as the civilian she had seen on the night of November 9. In a previous hearing, however, Yih Hai-sen admitted that he was wearing a dark suit on that night.

This is the first time that the important evidence of the amah was given in court, but not the time that it had been heard, for after the shooting she made a statement to police which was taken down and later told to the court. At that time, the amah went away to Kompo, but police kept her whereabouts in mind.

It was pointed out this morning that Judge Dalen, presiding over the full court in the case, wanted to hear the testimony of the woman and that was the reason why he reopened the case on July 17.

Reopened July 17

The Nakayama case, after dragging on for weeks before Judge Dalen in the First District Court, was suddenly reopened on the morning of July 17, the next hearing scheduled for Friday, July 31. The reopening created a tremendous sensation in the Japanese community and lawyers, observers and police were astounded, though it had been rumored for several days that such action would be taken.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年7月28日，星期二

中山案
举行听证

女佣孔波（Kompo）归来
就谋杀案提供证词

令人颇感意外的是，中山案今天上午在第一特区法院再次开庭审理，一名18岁的女佣作证称，去年11月9日晚在达罗克路（Darroch Road），她听到一声枪响，转身看见中山倒在地上。

这名女佣名叫蒲耀英（Pu Yao-yin），警方昨天将其从孔波（Kompo，音译）带至上海。她成为了本案于7月17日重新审理的表面原因，而当时原定即将宣判。

听证会出人意料

除了“知情者”外，今天上午的听证会让所有人都感到意外，因为下一次听证会原定于周五举行。女佣的证词是在几乎空无一人的法庭上提供的，除了法庭官员、警察以及站在三名被告——易海森（即小广东）、杨文道和周夏荣（Chow Hsia-yung）身后被告席上肃立成排的日本官员外，别无他人。通常满座的法庭并未出席，听证由萧世丰（Siao Shih-feng）法官主持。案件无限期休庭。

女佣作证称，在谋杀案发生当晚，她正向南行走，经过分别走在街道东西两侧的一名平民和一名水手之间。当时，她注意到那名平民穿着深色西装。

听到枪声

她说，在经过那两名男子后不久，她听到一声枪响，转身看见那名水手倒在地上。今天上午，她未能指认三名被告中的任何一人为她在11月9日晚所见的那名平民。然而，在此前的听证中，易海森承认他在那天晚上穿着深色西装。

这是该女佣的重要证据首次在法庭上提供，但这并非该证据首次被听取，因为在枪击发生后，她曾向警方做过陈述，该陈述被记录下来并后来告知法庭。当时，这名女佣前往孔波（Kompo，音译），但警方一直掌握着她的行踪。

今天上午有人指出，主持本案全庭审理的大伦（Dalen）法官希望听取该女子的证词，这就是他于7月17日重新审理此案的原因。

7月17日重审

中山案在第一特区法院大伦法官面前拖延数周后，于7月17日上午突然重新开庭，下次听证会定于7月31日（星期五）举行。重审在日本社群中引起了巨大轰动，尽管此前几天已有谣言称将采取此类行动，但律师、观察员和警方仍感到震惊。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, July31, 1936

Nakayama Case
Set August 5

Hearing Is Postponed;
Japanese Clamor
For Verdict

Despite the increasing clamor in the local Japanese community for a verdict in the Nakayama case, no court session was held today and the next hearing was set for August 5 at 2 p.m. At that time the municipal advocate and defense attorneys for the three Chinese will sum up their arguments for and against Yih Hai-sen (Shao Kwangtung), Yang Wen-tao and Chow Shan-yung, charged with the murder of Japanese Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama last November.

Two officials of the Japanese Consulate-General called on Mr. Paul Y. Ru, assistant municipal advocate, this morning in regard to the case. It is understood they intimated that a speedy conviction of the three men is desirable. Agitation for an immediate verdict in the case has been gathering force in the Japanese community and dissatisfaction with the delay has been freely voiced. It was rumored that a monster rally of Nipponese residents would be held today if the session were postponed, but it failed to take place and the community was quiet this morning.

The Japanese have also rumored that the Chinese Public Safety Bureau would oppose by force Japanese independent action.

No session was held today because the unexpected hearing in the First District Court on Tuesday disposed of the testimony of a Chinese amah, who had originally been scheduled to appear today. The judge is apparently chiefly concerned with the motive for the alleged killing by Yih, as this motive has thus far in the trial been obscure.

The detention period of the three accused has been extended for another two months, this action being necessary because Chinese law specifies that a defendant in a criminal case can be held without bail only for three months unless a court order is made extending the original period.

Kao Sees Kawagoe
(Reuter's Agency)

NANKING, July 30.—Mr. Kao Tsung-wu, Chief of the Asiatic Affairs Department of the Foreign Office, is reliably learnt to be interviewing Mr. S. Kawagoe, the Japanese Ambassador, in Shanghai concerning the Kayau murder case and to be exchanging views on minor Sino-Japanese questions.

He is expected to return to Nanking tomorrow evening by train.

A readjustment of major Sino-Japanese issues is understood to be awaiting Mr. Kawagoe's coming to Nanking and further discussions between the Japanese Ambassador and General Chang Chun, the Foreign Minister.
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年7月31日，星期五

中山案
定于8月5日审理

听证会推迟；
日本人强烈要求
宣判

尽管当地日本社群对中山案宣判的要求日益强烈，但今天未举行法庭庭审，下次听证会定于下午2点，即8月5日举行。届时，市公诉人和三名中国人的辩护律师将总结支持或反对易海森（即小广东）、杨文道和周善荣（Chow Shan-yung）的论点，他们被控于去年11月谋杀日本准尉中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayama）。

今天上午，日本总领事馆的两名官员就本案拜访了助理市公诉人鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru）先生。据悉，他们暗示希望能迅速定罪这三名男子。日本社群中要求立即宣判本案的 agitation（煽动/鼓噪）正在积聚力量，人们对延误的不满情绪 freely voiced（ freely voiced，原文如此，意为公开表达）。有谣言称，如果庭审推迟，日本居民今天将举行大型集会，但该集会并未举行，今早社群保持平静。

日本人还谣传，中国公安局将以武力反对日本的独立行动。

今天未举行庭审，是因为周二在第一特区法院举行的意外听证会处理了一名中国女佣的证词，她原定于今天出庭。法官显然主要关注易某涉嫌杀人的动机，因为该动机在目前的审判中一直模糊不清。

三名被告的拘留期又延长了两个月，采取这一行动是必要的，因为中国法律规定，刑事案件的被告在无保释情况下只能被拘留三个月，除非法院下令延长原定期限。

高宗武会见川越
（路透社）

南京，7月30日电。据悉，外交部亚洲司司长高宗武先生正在上海会见日本大使川越茂（S. Kawagoe）先生，商讨加藤（Kayau，音译）谋杀案，并就中日间的次要问题交换意见。

预计他将于明天晚上乘火车返回南京。

据悉，中日重大问题的调整正等待川越先生前往南京，以及日本大使与外交部长张群将军之间的进一步讨论。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, AUGUST 1, 1936

Nippon Mass
Meeting Fails
To Materialize

Agitation On Nakayama
Case Continues To
Brew In Hongkew

Although the local Japanese com-
munity continued its concerted
agitation for a speedy conclusion
and an immediate verdict in the
Nakayama trial, no hearing of the
murder case was held at the First
Special District Court yesterday as
originally scheduled.

The Court, in an order, announced
that the next hearing will be held
at 2 o'clock Wednesday afternoon.

In view of new evidence given by
the police witness, Pan Chow-yin,
the amah employed by a Japanese
family, who is an eye-witness to the
shooting, another argument on the
case by the defense and prosecuting
attorneys is expected to be given
Wednesday.

Meantime, clamor by local Japan-
ese continues. Although nothing
could be learned regarding the
much - publicised monster rally
to protest against the alleged de-
lay of the Court, local Nipponese
dailies gave detailed accounts on
the various phases pointing to the
guilt of the three accused, Yih Hai-
sen (Hsiao Kwangtung), Yang Wen-
tao and Chow Shan-yung.

Meet Discouraged

The mass meeting of Shanghai
Nipponese residents has been dis-
cussed among local Japanese
leaders ever since July 10 when
Kosaku Kayau, an independent
Japanese broker was mysteriously
killed in almost the same manner as
Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama.
At that time, officials of the local
Japanese Consulate were said to
have advised against such a meet-
ing, fearing that the feeling of the
masses here would be fanned up
an uncontrollable state.

Since the re-opened hearing has
been in progress, sentiments for the
rally are said to have gained in-
creased support. Two days ago,
Japanese sources indicated that un-
less an immediate verdict is given,
the Nipponese residents here would
give vent to their dissatisfaction by
calling the mass meeting.

Yesterday two representatives
of the Japanese Consulate call-
ed on Mr. Paul Y. Ru, Assistant
Municipal Advocate, regarding the
case. It is understood that they
told Mr. Ru that a speedy con-
clusion of the trial is advisable.

The postponement of yesterday's
trial is understood to have made
necessary the hearing to be held
on Tuesday. At that session, when
Pan Chow yin was brought up for
testimony the evidence which would
have been presented to the Court
yesterday, was heard.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》，1936年8月1日，星期六

日本大型集会
未能举行

虹口地区关于
中山案的鼓噪
仍在酝酿

尽管当地日本社群继续协同鼓噪，要求迅速结案并立即对中山案进行宣判，但昨天第一特区法院未按原计划举行该谋杀案的听证会。

法院发布命令，宣布下次听证会将于周三下午2点举行。

鉴于警方证人、受雇于日本家庭的女佣潘娇英（Pan Chow-yin，音译）提供了新证据，她是枪击事件的目击者，预计辩方和控方律师将在周三就该案进行进一步辩论。

与此同时，当地日本人的鼓噪仍在继续。虽然关于那场广为宣传的、抗议法院所谓延误的大型集会的情况无从得知，但当地的日本日报详细报道了指向三名被告——易海森（即小广东）、杨文道和周善荣——有罪的各个方面。

集会受挫

自7月10日以来，上海日本居民的大型集会一直在当地日本领导人中讨论，当时日本独立经纪人加藤（Kosaku Kayau，音译）以与准尉中山秀夫几乎相同的方式被神秘杀害。据说，当时当地日本领事馆官员建议不要举行此类集会，担心这里民众的情绪会被煽动到不可控制的状态。

据说，自从重审听证会开始以来，支持集会的情绪获得了越来越多的支持。两天前，日本方面消息人士指出，除非立即宣判，否则这里的日本居民将通过召开大型集会来发泄他们的不满。

昨天，日本领事馆的两名代表就本案拜访了助理市公诉人鲁保罗（Paul Y. Ru）先生。据悉，他们告诉鲁先生，迅速结束审判是可取的。

据悉，昨天审判的推迟使得周二举行的听证会成为必要。在那次庭审中，当潘娇英（Pan Chow yin）被带上庭作证时，听取了本应于昨天向法庭提交的证据。

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, AUGUST 1, 1936

NAKAYAMA TRIAL SET
FOR AUGUST 5
Japanese Protesting
Further Delay In
Giving Verdict
The re-opening of the trial of
the three Chinese in connection
with the murder of the Japanese
sailor Hideo Nakayoma, which was
to have taken place yesterday,
failed to materialize. There was
no hearing yesterday. Officials of
the Court announced that the re-
trial would take place on August
5 at 2 p.m.
It had been previously indicated
in Japanese quarters that a mass
meeting would be held by the local
Nipponese community if the case
was not re-opened yesterday. The
purpose of the meeting, it was
stated in the Japanese press, was
to protest against the continued
delay in announcing a verdict. The
meeting did not materialize.
It is understood that at the next
hearing further arguments by the
prosecution and defence will be
offered and a decision given later.
The three Chinese held for the
killing of Nakayama on November
9, last year, are Yih Hai-sen, Yang
Wen-tao and Chow Shan-yung, all
Cantonese. A Korean is also being
held by the Japanese for com-
plicity in the murder.

《上海泰晤士报》，1936年8月1日，星期六

中山案审判
定于8月5日
日本人抗议
进一步延迟
宣判

与日本水手中山秀夫（Hideo Nakayoma，原文拼写有误，应为Nakayama）谋杀案有关的三名中国人的审判重审，原定于昨天举行，但未能实现。昨天没有举行听证会。法院官员宣布，重审将于8月5日下午2点举行。

此前日本方面曾表示，如果昨天不重新开庭，当地日本社群将举行大型集会。据日本媒体报道，集会的目的是抗议持续延迟宣判。该集会并未举行。

据悉，在下一次听证会上，控方和辩方将提出进一步的辩论，随后将作出裁决。

因去年11月9日杀害中山而被拘留的三名中国人是易海森、杨文道和周善荣，均为广东人。一名韩国人也因共谋谋杀罪被日本方面拘留。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, FRIDAY, JULY 31, 1936

Nakayama Retrial Rumours
Arouse The Japanese

Mass Meeting Of Protest Threatened If Court
Contemplates Postponement; Chang Chun's
Emissary Has Talk With Mr. Kawagoe

It was reliably learned yesterday that the retrial of the alleged assassins of Hideo Nakayama, which was set for to-day in the First Special District Court, will not take place. The retrial has been indefinitely postponed.
In view of this report the following statement issued through Domei News Agency is of interest:
Convocation of a monster rally of Nipponese residents, should the First Special District Court postpone to-day's session devoted to the Nakayama case, is steadily gaining favour in the ranks of the local Japanese community, the Shanghai "Nippo" reported yesterday.
The journal also reported the circulation of alarming rumours, dealing with the alleged intention of the Chinese Public Safety Bureau to oppose by force Japanese "independent action."
Lieut.-Commander Matao Okino, assistant naval attache to the Japanese Embassy, on Wednesday told Japanese reporters that the failure of the Court to announce definitely at to-day's session the date on which the verdict is to be delivered would be regarded by the Japanese as "a serious matter."

Mr. Kao Tsung-wu's Interest
Mr. Kao Tsung-wu, Director of the Asiatic Affairs Bureau of the Waichiaopu, called on Mr. Shigeru Kawagoe, Ambassador to China, on Wednesday to confer on the "Nakayama" and "Kayau" cases, on instructions from Gen. Chang Chun, Foreign Minister.
The Chinese official, the local Japanese papers reported, conveyed to Mr. Kawagoe the Nanking Government's sincere desire to see a satisfactory solution of the two cases.
The two officials, the papers said, also discussed the general readjustment of Sino-Japanese relations and economic collaboration between the two countries.

New Assault Allegation
Japanese newspaper also carried yesterday a report alleging that Miss Suwa Tamiura, of Dixwell Road, was struck by a rock while riding in a ricksha on Tuesday in Woosung Road. It was also alleged that Miss Tamura was confined to bed for two days as a result and reported the matter to the Consular Police only yesterday.
No confirmation of the report was obtainable from other sources.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年7月31日，星期五

中山（Nakayama）重审谣言
激起日人愤慨

若法院考虑延期，威胁举行大规模抗议集会；张群特使与川越茂会谈

据可靠消息，原定于今日在第一特区地方法院进行的涉嫌刺杀中山秀雄（Hideo Nakayama）凶手的重审将不会进行。重审已无限期推迟。
鉴于此报道，以下通过同盟通讯社发布的声明值得关注：
据上海《日本日报》昨日报道，如果第一特区地方法院推迟今日关于中山案的庭审，在当地日侨群体中，号召举行日籍居民大型集会的提议正日益获得支持。
该报还报道了令人不安的谣言流传，称中国公安局意图以武力反对日本的“独立行动”。
日本大使馆海军副武官奥野又太郎（Matao Okino）少校周三告诉记者，如果法院未在今日庭审中明确宣布宣判日期，日本人将视此为“严重事态”。

高宗武先生的关注
外交部亚洲司司长高宗武先生周三奉外交部长张群将军之命，拜访了中国驻日大使川越茂先生，就“中山案”和“加藤（Kayau）案”进行磋商。
据当地日文报纸报道，这位中国官员向川越先生传达了南京政府真诚希望圆满解决这两起案件的愿望。
据这些报纸称，两位官员还讨论了中日关系的全面调整以及两国间的经济合作。

新的袭击指控
日本报纸昨日还刊登了一篇报道，称周二住在狄思威路（Dixwell Road）的诹访民浦（Suwa Tamiura）小姐在吴淞路乘坐人力车时被石块击中。报道还称，田村（Tamura）小姐因此卧床两天，并于昨日才向领事警察报案。
其他来源无法证实该报道。

pages.en:
THE CHINA PRESS, FRIDAY, JULY 31, 1936

Verdict In
Sailor Case
Is Postponed

Further Investigations
In Nakayama Affair
Found Necessary

AMAH'S TESTIMONY
FORCES DELAY

Japanese Community
Restive, May Call
Big Mass Meet

A notice extending the detention period of the three accused in the Nakayama case for another two months was yesterday received by the defense lawyers from the First Special District Court. THE CHINA PRESS learned last night.

This action is made necessary because the Chinese law specifies that a defendant in a criminal case can be held without bail only for three months unless a Court order is made extending the original period.

Yesterday's Court order also informed the defense attorneys of Yih Hai-sen (Hsiao Kwangtung), Yang Wen-tao and Chow Shan-yung, the three accused, that there will be no hearing today as originally scheduled.

An unexpected session took place Tuesday in order that the Court might question Pan Chao-ying, an amah employed by a Japanese family, who was an eye-witness of the Darroch Road affair on November 9 last year.

It was explained yesterday that the Tuesday hearing was necessary because the amah, who was newly married, was eager to return to her home in Northern Kiangsu. Immediately upon her arrival, a special morning session was called and later the same day, the amah was taken to the scene of the crime to re-enact to the judge what she saw immediately before and after she heard the fatal shot that killed Japanese Warrant Officer Hideo Nakayama.

The notice to the lawyers yesterday stated that a further investigation of the case is necessary and mentioned no date for the resumption of the trial.

Japanese Claim For Verdict

Meantime, the agitation for an immediate verdict in the case continued to gather force in the local Japanese community yesterday. Leading Nipponese dailies gave prominent displays to articles voicing dissatisfaction with the alleged delay.

One report gaining wide currency among local Japanese residents stated that more Nipponese are favoring the idea of a mammoth rally if the First Special District Court postpones today's session.

Meanwhile, Bureau of Public Safety and the Settlement police are continuing their attempt to unravel the mystery of the murder of Kosuku Kayau, independent Japanese broker who was killed on Chimei Road on July 10.

The original reward of $2,000 for the apprehension of the murderer has been increased to $3,000. Officers of the Bureau directly in charge of the case have submitted themselves to the Municipality of Greater Shanghai officials for appropriate punishments for their failure to arrest the killer within the time prescribed.

Kao Interviewing Kawagoe

NANKING, July 30.—(Reuters).—Mr. Kao Tsung-wu, Chief of the Asiatic Affairs Department of the Foreign Office, is reliably learnt to be interviewing Mr. S. Kawagoe, the Japanese Ambassador, in Shanghai concerning the Kayau murder case and to be exchanging views on minor Sino-Japanese questions.

He is expected to return to Nanking tomorrow evening by train.

A readjustment of major Sino-Japanese issues is understood to be awaiting Mr. Kawagoe's coming to Nanking and further discussions between the Japanese Ambassador and General Chang Chun, the Foreign Minister.
pages.zh:
《大美晚报》，1936年7月31日，星期五

水兵案
判决
延期

发现有必要
对中山事件
作进一步调查

女佣证词
迫使延期

日侨社群
情绪躁动，可能召开
大型群众集会

《大美晚报》昨晚获悉，辩护律师昨日收到第一特区地方法院的通知，将中山案中三名被告的拘留期再延长两个月。

采取这一行动是必要的，因为中国法律规定，刑事案件的被告若无保释，仅可被羁押三个月，除非法院下令延长原定期限。

昨日的法院命令还通知了三名被告——叶海森（又名萧广东）、杨文涛和周山勇的辩护律师，原定于今日的庭审将不进行。

周二进行了一次临时庭审，以便法院讯问潘兆英（Pan Chao-ying），她是一名受雇于日本家庭的女佣，也是去年11月9日达罗路（Darroch Road）事件的目击者。

昨日解释称，周二之所以需要开庭，是因为这名刚结婚的女佣急于返回其在江苏北部的家中。她一抵达，法院便召开了特别晨间庭审，随后在同一天，女佣被带至犯罪现场，向法官重现她在听到杀害日本军曹中山秀雄的致命枪声前后所见的情景。

昨日发给律师的通知指出，有必要对该案进行进一步调查，并未提及恢复审理的日期。

日方要求宣判

与此同时，昨日当地日侨社群中要求立即对该案作出判决的 agitation（煽动/活动）继续加剧。主要日文日报显著刊登文章，表达对所谓延期的不满。

在当地日侨中广泛流传的一份报告称，如果第一特区地方法院推迟今日的庭审，越来越多的日本人倾向于举行大型集会。

与此同时，公安局和租界警方继续试图解开7月10日在集美路（Chimei Road）被杀的日本独立经纪人加藤（Kosuku Kayau）谋杀案之谜。

缉拿凶手的原始赏金2,000美元已增加至3,000美元。直接负责此案的局官员已向大上海市政府官员自首，请求因未能在规定期限内逮捕凶手而给予适当处罚。

高氏采访川越

南京，7月30日。（路透社）。——据可靠消息，外交部亚洲司司长高宗武先生正在上海采访日本大使川越茂（S. Kawagoe）先生，商讨加藤谋杀案，并就中日间的小问题进行意见交换。

预计他将于明晚乘火车返回南京。

据悉，中日重大问题的调整正等待川越先生前往南京，以及日本大使与外交部长张群将军之间的进一步讨论。

高氏采访
川越先生

讨论加藤谋杀案
及其他事件

南京，7月30日。——据可靠消息，外交部亚洲司司长高宗武先生正在上海采访日本大使川越茂（S. Kawagoe）先生，商讨加藤谋杀案，并就谣传的中日问题交换意见。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Thursday, July 30, 1936    NJ95

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL
S. I. RE.
S. B. D.

Japanese Rally
Due If Nakayama
Case Postponed

Nipponese Community
Aroused Over Hearing
Slated Tomorrow

CHINESE ACTIVITY
RUMORED IN CITY

Nanking Envoy Visits
Kawagoe Regarding
Two Cases

Convocation of a monster rally
of Nipponese residents, should the
First Special District Court post-
pone tomorrow's session devoted
to the "Nakayama case," is
steadily gaining favor in the ranks
of the local Japanese community,
Japanese sources report today.
These sources also report the
circulation of alarming rumors,
dealing with the alleged inten-
tion of the Chinese Public Safety
Bureau to oppose by force Japan-
ese "independent action."
Lieut.-Commander Matao Okino,
assistant naval attache to the
Japanese Embassy, yesterday told
reporters that the failure of the
court to announce definitely the
date on which the verdict is to be
delivered at today's session would
be regarded by the Japanese as
"a serious matter."

Reward Increased
Bringing the reward for the
apprehension of the murderer of
Mr. Kayau to $3000, the Public
Safety Bureau yesterday appro-
priated additional $1000.
Persons supplying clues leading
to the arrest of the culprit will
be awarded $2000.
Mr. Hideaki Kitamura, chief of
the Police Section of the Japanese
Consulate-General, will soon call
on General Tsai Chi-chung,
director of the Public Safety
Bureau, to discuss the "Kayau"
incident, and also to seek in-
formation on the reported arrival
here of a band of professional
assassins from the South.

Envoy Sees Kawagoe
Believed to be armed with in-
structions from General Chang
Chun, minister of foreign affairs,
Mr. Kao Chung-wu, chief of the
department of Asiatic Affairs of
the Waichiaopu, arrived from
Nanking yesterday morning and
called on Mr. S. Kawagoe, Japan-
ese ambassador to China, at the
latter's official residence at Route
Pichon at 2 o'clock yesterday
afternoon. Among the subjects
discussed in the conference, it is
learned, were those concerning
the "Nakayama Case" and the
"Kayau Case."

While details of the conference
could not be learned, much signi-
ficance is attached to the meeting
in view of the growing Japanese
sentiment towards the two "mur-
der mysteries" and the hurried
visit to Kuling by Mr. Kao before
he came to Shanghai for the con-
ference. Mr. Kao was sent to
Kuling to call on General Chiang
Kai-shek, president of the
Executive Yuan, and Mr. Hsu Mo,
political vice-minister of foreign
affairs. He returned to Nanking
to report on his mission to General
Chang on Tuesday and left the
capital city for Shanghai the same
night.

Session Necessary
The unexpected session held in
the First Special District Court in
connection with the Nakayama
case on Tuesday morning was to-
day explained as absolutely
necessary as the witness, Pan
Chao-yin, an amah formerly
employed in a Japanese family,
was brought from Northern
Kiangsu to Shanghai a few days
after her wedding. She left for
her native place again yesterday
after having given her testimony
and re-enacted what she saw on
the night of murder on Tuesday
night.
At the conclusion of the hear-
ing Tuesday afternoon, the court
ruled that the previous ruling ad-
journing the hearing until to-
morrow be cancelled and that a
date be set in Chambers for the
next session.

《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年7月30日，星期四 NJ95

上海公共租界
工部局警务处
特别分部

若中山案
延期，日人
将举行集会

日侨社群
对定于明日举行的
听证会感到激愤

谣传市内
有中方活动

南京特使就
两案拜访
川越

据日方消息源今日报道，如果第一特区地方法院推迟明日关于“中山案”的庭审，在当地日侨群体中，号召举行日籍居民大型集会的提议正日益获得支持。
这些消息源还报道了令人不安的谣言流传，称中国公安局意图以武力反对日本的“独立行动”。
日本大使馆海军副武官奥野又太郎（Matao Okino）少校昨日告诉记者，如果法院未在今日庭审中明确宣布宣判日期，日本人将视此为“严重事态”。

赏金增加

公安局昨日追加拨款1,000美元，将缉拿加藤先生凶手的赏金提高至3,000美元。
提供线索导致罪犯被捕的人将获得2,000美元。
日本总领事馆警务科科长北村秀明（Hideaki Kitamura）先生不久将拜访公安局局长蔡劲军将军，讨论“加藤”事件，并寻求有关据报道有一帮职业刺客从南方抵达此地的信息。

特使会见川越

据信持有外交部长张群将军的指示，外交部亚洲司司长高宗武先生昨日上午从南京抵达，并于昨日下午2时在毕勋路（Route Pichon）的官邸拜访了中国驻日大使川越茂（S. Kawagoe）先生。据悉，会议讨论的主题包括“中山案”和“加藤案”。

虽然无法得知会议的细节，但鉴于日本人对这两起“谋杀谜案”的情绪日益高涨，以及高先生在来上海开会前匆忙访问牯岭，此次会晤具有重要意义。高先生被派往牯岭拜访行政院院长蒋介石将军和外交部政务次长徐谟先生。他于周二返回南京向张群将军汇报任务，并于当晚离开首都前往上海。

庭审必要

今日解释称，周二上午第一特区地方法院就中山案举行的临时庭审是绝对必要的，因为证人潘兆英（Pan Chao-yin），一名曾受雇于日本家庭的女佣，在婚后几天内从江苏北部被带到上海。她在周二作证并重现了谋杀当晚所见情景后，于昨日再次返回家乡。
在周二下午的听证会结束时，法院裁定取消此前将听证会延期至明日的裁决，并在法官办公室确定下次庭审的日期。

pages.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, THURSDAY, JULY 30, 1936

At 9 p.m. on Tuesday, another
reconstruction of the Darroch Road
crime was made in the presence of
police and court officials, including
Judge Siau Shih-feng. Tuesday
night's reconstruction, however, was
made without the presence of the
three Cantonese, Yih Hai-sen, Yang
Ven-tao and Chow Zeu-yoong, who
were accused of being concerned in
the murder of H. Nakayama, the
principal actor being Pu Chiao-ying,
the 18-year old maid-servant, who was
brought to Shanghai from her native
district in north Kiangsu on Monday
as an important witness of the mur-
der. During the reconstruction, the
witness told the police and court
officials the spot where she first saw
the Japanese marine and the civilian
walking in a similar direction on dif-
ferent sides of the road and said
when she reached No. 191 Darroch
Road, she heard a shot. A man in
black foreign-style clothing enacted
the role of the assailant and witness
was asked whether the civilian whom
she saw on the night of murder wore
the same kind of clothing. Witness
replied they were of similar colour.
After the reconstruction, the party
broke up.
pages.zh:
《字林西报》，1936年7月30日，星期四

周二晚上9点，在包括萧世丰（Siau Shih-feng）法官在内的警察和法院官员在场的情况下，再次对达罗路犯罪现场进行了重建。然而，周二晚上的重建是在三名被控参与谋杀H. 中山（H. Nakayama）的广东人——叶海森、杨文涛和周祖荣（Chow Zeu-yoong）不在场的情况下进行的，主要参与者是18岁的女仆潘兆英（Pu Chiao-ying），她作为谋杀案的重要证人，于周一从其江苏北部的家乡被带到上海。在重建过程中，证人告诉警察和法院官员，她最初看到日本水兵和平民在道路两侧朝相同方向行走的地点，并说当她到达达罗路191号时，听到了一声枪响。一名身穿黑色西式服装的男子扮演了袭击者的角色，证人被问及她在谋杀当晚看到的平民是否穿着同样的服装。证人回答说颜色相似。重建结束后，众人散去。

pages.en:
THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, SATURDAY, AUGUST 1 1936

It was learned at the First Special
District Court yesterday that the
next hearing of the Nakayama case
in which three Cantonese are being
accused of having murdered a
Japanese marine on November 9 last,
will take place at 2 p.m. next
Wednesday, August 5. The hearing,
originally set for yesterday after-
noon, was postponed.

《字林西报》，1936年8月1日，星期六

昨日从第一特区地方法院获悉，中山案的下次听证会将于下周三（8月5日）下午2时举行，该案中三名广东人被控于去年11月9日谋杀了一名日本水兵。原定于昨日下午举行的听证会已被推迟。

pages.en:
July 22, 1936. Morning Translation,

NIPPO

THE NAKAYAMA CASE

It is reported that the hearing
of the Nakayama case, which was remanded sine die on July
17 by the Special District Court, will be resumed at 2 p.m.
on July 31.

It is expected that the S.M.C.
will strongly maintain the guilt of Yang Ven Tau and
Yih Hai Sung by exposing the relations between these two
prisoners and their past histories.

The Japanese authorities are
demanding a fair judgement so as to crush the evil Chinese
elements. Yang Ven Tao and Yih Hai Sung attacked
Nakayama with the object of creating bad feeling between
Japan and China; furthermore, they are elements harmful
to Sino-Japanese rapprochement. The Japanese authorities
will adopt resolute steps should an unsatisfactory
judgement be delivered.

GENERAL FENG YU HSIANG INSTIGATES ANTI-JAPANESE
MOVEMENT AMONG STUDENTS

A Taido telegram from Tientsin
reports that on July 20 the students of various universities
at Peiping and Tientsin, who had been on a visit to Nanking
to submit reports on the situation in the North to the
2nd Plenary Session, called on General Feng Yu Hsiang and
Mr. Sun Fo after making reports on their mission to the
officers of the Students Federation.

General Feng Yu Hsiang in
expressing his appreciation of their movement, informed
the students that the Central Government was engaged in
preparing for war against Japan and asked them to co-
operate with the Government in an anti-Japanese movement
as soon as the preparations have been completed. The
General requested the students to keep a watch on the
movements of the Government and to start anti-Japanese
activities at every opportunity.

The General afterwards exhibited
a number of Soviet military films to show that China
need not fear Japan.

KOREAN REVOLUTIONIST ARRESTED

A Korean named Lee , who was
arrested by the Japanese authorities in Shanghai for
revolutionary activities, is now undergoing an examination
at the hands of the 2nd Section of the Japanese Consular
Police. The prisoner is reported to be a graduate of the
Nanking Military Academy.

NEW CHIEF OF 1ST SECTION OF JAPANESE CONSULAR POLICE

Mr. Fukuyama, the officer in
charge of the 1st Section of the Japanese Consular Police,
left Shanghai on July 21. Mr. S. Tajima, officer in
charge of the Japanese Consular Police at Amoy, has been
appointed to succeed Mr. Fukuyama. Mr. Tajima will
arrive here on July 29.
pages.zh:
1936年7月22日。晨间译稿，

日报

中山案

据报，特别区法院于7月17日无限期延期审理的中山案，将于7月31日下午2时恢复审理。

预计上海公共租界工部局（S.M.C.）将通过揭露这两名囚犯之间的关系及其过往经历，强力主张杨文涛（Yang Ven Tau，音译）和易海松（Yih Hai Sung，音译）有罪。

日本当局要求作出公正判决，以打击邪恶的中国分子。杨文涛和易海松袭击中山的目的是制造中日之间的不良情绪；此外，他们是阻碍中日亲善的有害分子。如果判决不能令人满意，日本当局将采取坚决步骤。

冯玉祥将军煽动学生反日运动

天津《大公报》电称，7月20日，北平和天津各大学的学生在向学生联合会官员汇报其赴南京向二中全会提交北方局势报告的任务后，拜访了冯玉祥将军和孙科先生。

冯玉祥将军在表示赞赏他们的运动时告知学生，中央政府正在准备对日作战，并要求他们在准备工作完成后尽快与政府合作开展反日运动。冯将军要求学生监视政府的动向，并抓住一切机会发起反日活动。

随后，将军放映了几部苏联军事电影，以表明中国无需畏惧日本。

朝鲜革命者被捕

一名姓李（Lee）的朝鲜人因从事革命活动被上海日本当局逮捕，目前正接受日本领事警察第二课的审讯。据报，该囚犯是南京陆军军官学校毕业生。

日本领事警察第一课新任课长

负责日本领事警察第一课的福山（Fukuyama）先生于7月21日离开上海。负责厦门日本领事警察的田岛 S.（S. Tajima）先生已被任命接替福山先生。田岛先生将于7月29日抵达此地。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Monday, September 14, 1936

Curious And Curiouser
SURELY there can have been no stranger cases in court annals than Shanghai's now famous Nakayama-Kayau entanglement. What started out as a tragic shooting on November 10, 1935, moved into an uproarious bedlam of voices prophesying war a few days later, has now turned into one of the maddest of the mad trials that has ever puzzled an already bewildered public.
At various times in the trial of Yih Hai-sen and others, evidence has been heard that Nakayama was killed (1) because of Yih's patriotism; (2) because of a cabaret girl; (3) because of a vast plot against Japan (4) as a part of the plot against Wang Ching-wei; and now comes the statement that the South-west Political Council was behind the shooting of Kayau, an insignificant Japanese clerk.
We are told that the reasons for the latter shooting lay in the fact that Chen Chi-tang and his cohorts wished to stir Japan to such a fever pitch that open hostilities would break out between China and that country.
And in the same breath we are told that the police of the Settlement are not interested in the four men, but are going to hand them back to the Chinese authorities. Yet, the men are to be held for a few days for questioning! If the men are not connected with the Nakayama case, why are they to be held for interrogation?
And on the same morning, just two floors above the courtroom where the four men spilled their startling information about the Kayau case, six bombers of Chinese shops selling Japanese goods, are given prison sentences. And from the Japanese, we learn that these bombers have some mysterious connection with the attack on Wang Ching-wei and the Nakayama and Kayau cases.
From all this, we are unable to make head nor tale and we should not be in the least surprised if, in the next hearing of the already too long trial of the alleged Nakayama murderers, evidence were produced connecting up the "suitcase murder case," the Chaoufoong Road murder case and others with the slaying of the two Japanese subjects.
If we were to believe all the testimony coming from the courtroom, we should be forced to the conclusion that all China from North to South from East to West had somehow a hand in the murders of Hideo Nakayama and Kosaku Kayau.
There is an old saying in the East to the effect that there are "wheels within wheels," and no doubt there are, but our only reaction at the present time is that of Lewis Carroll.
It gets curious and curiouser.

（批：707.3 / y-36.）
（签名：Jules Chen）
pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年9月14日，星期一

怪事连连
当然，在上海法院的档案中，恐怕没有比现在著名的中山-加藤纠葛更离奇的案件了。这起始于1935年11月10日的悲剧性枪击事件，几天后演变成一片预言战争的喧嚣混乱，如今已变成令本就困惑的公众更加迷惑的最荒谬的审判之一。
在对易海森（Yih Hai-sen，音译）及其他人的审判过程中，不时有证据显示，中山被杀是因为：(1) 易的爱国心；(2) 因为一名舞女；(3) 因为一个庞大的反日阴谋；(4) 作为针对汪精卫阴谋的一部分；而现在又有说法称，西南政务委员会是幕后指使枪击加藤（Kayau，音译，注：即下文之加劳/Kayru或加藤）这名微不足道的日本职员的主谋。
我们被告知，后一起枪击案的原因在于，陈济棠及其同伙希望将日本激怒到如此狂热的地步，以致中国与该国之间爆发公开敌对行动。
与此同时，我们又被告知，租界警方对这四人并不感兴趣，打算将他们移交给中国当局。然而，这些人还要被拘留几天以备讯问！如果这些人与中山案无关，为何要将他们扣留审问？
就在同一天上午，就在四名男子吐出关于加藤案的惊人供词的那个法庭楼上两层，六名轰炸出售日货的中国商店的罪犯被判处监禁。而从日本人那里，我们得知这些轰炸者与袭击汪精卫以及中山和加藤案有着某种神秘的联系。
从这一切中，我们无法理清头绪，如果在已经拖得太久的所谓中山凶手案的下次听证会上，出现将“手提箱谋杀案”、兆丰路谋杀案等与两名日本臣民被杀联系起来的证据，我们也丝毫不会感到惊讶。
如果我们相信法庭上出现的所有证词，我们将被迫得出这样的结论：全中国从南到北、从东到西，都以某种方式参与了秀雄中山（Hideo Nakayama）和加作加藤（Kosaku Kayau，音译，注：此处原文为Kayau，前文亦作Kayau，后文作Kayru，均指同一受害者，通常译为加藤或类似发音）的谋杀案。
东方有句老话，意思是“环中有环”（意指错综复杂），无疑确实如此，但我们目前的唯一反应就像刘易斯·卡罗尔（Lewis Carroll）所说的那样。
事情变得越来越奇怪了。

（批注：707.3 / y-36.）
（签名：Jules Chen）

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI SUNDAY TIMES, SEPTEMBER 13. 1936

Police Withdraw Against
New Nakayama Suspects

Hearings For Interrogation Continue Despite
Alleged Lack Of Evidence; Fourth Suspect
Says War Was Object Of Leader

With Settlement Police having waived their rights of prosecution in the Nakayama murder case against the four Chinese who were originally held in Nanking for alleged participation in the attempted assassination of Mr. Wang Ching-wei, former President of the Executive Yuan, hearing for purposes of interrogation continued yesterday before Judge Siao in the First Special District Court. At a further hearing on Wednesday these four will be further questioned in company with three other accused previously arrested by Settlement police.

The four suspects who were brought here from Nanking are Chang Shih-min, alleged to be the leader of the quartette, Chu Kwei-sen, Chen En-min and Ching Tao-chuan. The first three testified on Friday, and denied any knowledge of the murder while the last named gave his story yesterday.

Ching told the court that he had nothing to do with the murder. He met Chang two years ago but became acquainted with the other two accused only a few months ago.

He said he was employed by a man named Hwa Ka-tze, who is still at large, in July of this year as a messenger. On July 10, the day before the murder of the Japanese seafood broker, Kayau, he went to see a subordinate of his master named Liu Lao-shih.

**Hwa Had Pistol**

Hwa came into the room with a leather box in his hand and took out a pistol, handing it to Liu. Witness said he heard a murmur to the effect that there were six shots in the weapon.

The next day the newspapers published the story of the Kayau murder. Witness went to Liu and asked him if he was the killer. Liu smiled and gave no answer.

According to the witness, the gang planned to murder a Japanese on August 8 and the day before he was sent to the Chien Deh Apartments to see if the others were ready. The plan did not materialize because of a dispute over the venue of the proposed crime.

The leader Hwa once told witness that he wanted to kill a Japanese to start a Sino-Japanese war.

The story of this fourth accused differs considerably from the stories related by the other three. The first accused told the court that he and his men were interested only in the assassination of Mr. Wang Ching-wei.
pages.zh:
《上海星期时报》，1936年9月13日

警方放弃起诉
新的中山案嫌疑人

尽管声称缺乏证据，讯问听证仍继续进行；第四名嫌疑人称首领的目标是战争

鉴于租界警方已放弃对四名中国人的起诉权——这四名中国人最初在南京因涉嫌参与刺杀前行政院院长汪精卫先生未遂案而被拘留——昨天，在第一特别区法院萧法官面前继续进行了旨在讯问的听证会。在周三的进一步听证会上，这四名嫌疑人将与之前被租界警方逮捕的另外三名被告一起接受进一步讯问。

从南京带到此地的四名嫌疑人是：张世民（Chang Shih-min，音译），据称是这四人的首领；朱桂森（Chu Kwei-sen，音译）；陈恩民（Chen En-min，音译）；以及荆道全（Ching Tao-chuan，音译）。前三人在周五作证，否认知晓任何谋杀事宜，而最后一名则在昨天陈述了他的故事。

荆告诉法庭，他与谋杀案无关。他两年前结识了张，但直到几个月前才熟悉另外两名被告。

他说，今年七月，他被一个叫华卡兹（Hwa Ka-tze，音译）的人雇用为信差，此人目前在逃。7月10日，即日本海鲜经纪人加藤（Kayau）被杀的前一天，他去见了他主人的一个名叫刘老师（Liu Lao-shih，音译）的下属。

**华持有手枪**

华手里拿着一个皮箱走进房间，取出一把手枪，递给刘。证人说他听到一阵低语，大意是武器里有六发子弹。

第二天，报纸刊登了加藤谋杀案的消息。证人去问刘，他是不是凶手。刘笑了笑，没有回答。

据证人称，该团伙计划于8月8日谋杀一名日本人，前一天他被派往建德公寓（Chien Deh Apartments，音译）查看其他人是否准备就绪。由于对预定犯罪地点发生争执，计划未能实施。

首领华曾告诉证人，他想杀死一名日本人以引发中日战争。

这第四名被告的故事与其他三人讲述的故事大相径庭。第一名被告告诉法庭，他和他的人只关心刺杀汪精卫先生。

pages.en:
THE SHANGHAI TIMES, SATURDAY, SEPTEMBER 12, 1936
Police Waive Right To
Prosecute Four Latest
Japan Murder Suspects
Judge Siao Insists On Having Further Hearing
This Morning; Three Of Four Men Recently
Handed Over Deny All Confessions Made
FIRST PUBLIC HEARING OF SUSPECTS
CALLED AT A MOMENT'S NOTICE
A sensation was caused in the First Special District
Court yesterday afternoon when, at the conclusion of the
first special public session held to hear the statements of
three of the four latest suspects now in custody in connection
with the murder of Warrant Officer Nakayama and Kosaku
Kayau, Japanese sea-food broker, assistant Municipal
Advocate Paul Y. Ru informed the Court that the police
did not wish to continue with the prosecution. Judge Siao,
however, ordered another hearing to be held this morning,
when he will once again question the suspects.
For some unknown reason, only
three of the four latest suspects
were brought before the tribunal
yesterday afternoon. The special
hearing was also arranged at the
last moment, as on Thursday
morning, when the four men were
brought before the tribunal, the
police asked for another remand
to complete their investigations,
and same was granted until Sept-
ember 16.
The four suspects were handed
over last week to the Settlement
Police by the Bureau of Public
Safety after the men had
been extradited from Nanking,
where they were held as suspects
in the attempted assassination of
Mr. Wang Ching-wei, then Pres-
ident of the Executive Yuan, on
November 1, last, in Nanking.
Deny Confessions
Mr. Ru informed the Court
that the police wished to waive
the right to prosecute the men,
after the three suspects had cate-
gorically denied that they had
been in any way associated in the
murders of the two Japanese in
Shanghai, one on November 9,
last, and the second on July 10.
These denials were made by the
men notwithstanding the state-
ments by the prosecution that the
men had confessed to complicity
in the crimes to both the Bureau
of Public Safety officials and the
International Settlement Police.
At the opening of the hearing,
Assistant Municipal Advocate Ru
informed the Court that the
suspects had associated them-
selves with the murders of the two
Japanese in Shanghai and that
they had actually hinted in their
confessions that their leader had
planned to kill a third Japanese.
The first accused told Judge Siao
yesterday that he had come to
Shanghai about three years ago
upon the request of Sun Wen-deh.
He was not given any work to do,
but paid $30 a month, the money
coming, he understood, from Hwa
Ka-tze, one of the men wanted in
connection with the Wang attempt-
ed assassination. This man also
alleged that he was beaten by the
Bureau of Public Safety officers,
and, therefore, implicated another
accused in the Nakayama killing,
by saying that on the night of
November 9, he met him outside
the head Post Office and was told
by him that the third accused had
undertaken to kill a Japanese and
that, after doing so, he had thrown
his pistol away and fled.
The second accused also denied
the statements implicating several
men made by him to the police,
as did the third accused. One of
the accused stated that he was
arrested as a suspect in the Wang
attempted assassination, as he
once lived in the house occupied
by a news agency in Nanking, a
reporter of which was involved in
the crime. All the men categoric-
ally denied any knowledge of the
killings or the three other suspects
held in the Nakayama killing since
the beginning of this year.
pages.zh:
《上海泰晤士报》，1936年9月12日，星期六
警方放弃起诉
四名最新的日本谋杀案嫌疑人
萧法官坚持今天上午再次开庭；最近移交的四名男子中的三人否认所有供词
嫌疑人的首次公开听证会
在瞬间通知下召开
昨天下午，在第一特别区法院，当旨在听取与海军陆战队中士中山和日本海鲜经纪人加作加藤（Kosaku Kayau）谋杀案有关的四名最新嫌疑人中三人的陈述的首次特别公开庭审结束时，助理市检察官保罗·Y·鲁（Paul Y. Ru）通知法庭，警方不希望继续起诉，此举引起了轰动。然而，萧法官命令今天上午再次开庭，届时他将再次讯问嫌疑人。
出于某种未知原因，昨天下午只有四名最新嫌疑人中的三人被带到法庭。这次特别听证会也是在最后一刻安排的，因为在周四上午，当这四名男子被带到法庭时，警方要求再次延期以完成调查，并获得批准直至9月16日。
这四名嫌疑人上周由公安局移交给租界警方，此前他们从南京被引渡至此，在那里他们因涉嫌参与去年11月1日在南京刺杀时任行政院院长汪精卫先生未遂案而被拘留。
否认供词
鲁先生通知法庭，在三名嫌疑人明确否认他们以任何方式参与去年11月9日和7月10日在上海发生的两起日本人谋杀案后，警方希望放弃对这些人的起诉权。尽管控方称这些人已向公安局官员和国际租界警方承认参与犯罪，但这些人都予以否认。
在听证会开始时，助理市检察官鲁通知法庭，嫌疑人与上海两起日本人谋杀案有关，并且他们在供词中实际上暗示他们的首领计划杀害第三名日本人。
第一名被告昨天告诉萧法官，他是大约三年前应孙文德（Sun Wen-deh，音译）的请求来到上海的。他没有被分配任何工作，但每月获得30美元，他理解这笔钱来自华卡兹（Hwa Ka-tze，音译），此人是与汪精卫刺杀案有关的通缉犯之一。此人还声称他遭到公安局人员的殴打，因此牵连了另一名被告参与中山谋杀案，他说11月9日晚上，他在邮政总局外遇见了那人，并听那人说第三名被告已承担杀害一名日本人的任务，并在事后扔掉了手枪逃走了。
第二名被告也否认了他向警方作出的牵连数人的陈述，第三名被告也是如此。其中一名被告表示，他因涉嫌参与汪精卫刺杀案而被捕，因为他曾住在南京一家通讯社所占用的房子里，该社的一名记者卷入了此案。所有人都明确否认自今年年初以来对谋杀案或中山谋杀案中拘留的另外三名嫌疑人有任何了解。

pages.en:
The Shanghai Evening Post & Mercury, Friday, September 11, 1936

* * *
Four Nakayama Suspects Go
On Trial Next Wednesday

Held on suspicion of having
been involved in the killing of
Kosaku Kayru and Warrant
Officer Hideo Nakayama, Japan-
ese Special Naval Landing Party,
the four men arrested recently
will come up for trial before the
First Special District Court next
Wednesday, September 16, it was
announced yesterday at a hear-
ing held in camera with only
the judge and a few detectives
present. The suspects have been
alleged to belong to a Cantonese
club engaged in the business of
assassination.

pages.zh:
《上海晚邮报与信使报》，1936年9月11日，星期五

* * *
四名中山案嫌疑人将于下周三受审

据昨日宣布，因涉嫌参与杀害日本特别海军陆战队中士秀雄中山（Hideo Nakayama）和加劳（Kosaku Kayru，音译，注：即前文之加藤/Kayau）而被捕的四名男子，将于下周三（9月16日）在第一特别区法院受审。该宣布是在一次仅有法官和几名侦探出席的秘密听证会上作出的。据称，这些嫌疑人属于一个从事暗杀业务的广东帮会。
* * *

pages.en:
SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE
S. B. REGISTRY.
No. D/
Date

July 8, 1936. Morning Translation.

Ta Kung Pao, Sin Wan Pao, Shun Pao and other local newspapers :-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE

At 2 p.m. to-day the First Special District Court will hold a further hearing of the case against Yang Vung Tao (楊文道), Yih Hai Sung (叶海生) and Tseu Shou Yong (周社勇) who are charged with the murder of the Japanese marine Nakayama. Assistant Municipal Advocate Paul Ru, who was absent at the last hearing owing to illness, has now recovered and may appear to-day.
The Court some time ago ordered the Police to summon for interrogation the Korean named Jack and Zung Wei Ming (鄭惠民), a Japanese subject of Chinese origin. The S.M.C. is negotiating with the Japanese Consulate for their attendance.
The lawyers for the defence of the accused have read the report of the Medico-Legal Laboratory at Chenju and arguments on this report may be heard to-day if time permits.
All the local Chinese newspapers to-day reproduce the report (which consists of four books) submitted by the Medico-Legal Laboratory.

Ta Kung Pao and other local newspapers :-

SHANGHAI STUDENTS LEAVE FOR VILLAGES ALONG SHANGHAI-HANGCHOW RAILWAY TO STAGE PATRIOTIC PLAYS

The Shanghai Students Dramatic Group was formed in January this year. In June, the group staged certain plays at Dazang and this was well received by the people.
During the past month, the group has been arranging many plays to promote the use of native goods. Taking advantage of the summer holidays, the members intend to proceed to rural regions along the Shanghai-Hangchow Railway to stage similar plays.
On July 7, some 40 members of the group left Shanghai for the rural regions along the Shanghai-Hangchow Railway. They were accompanied by 20 members of the Smuggled Goods Boycott Group formed by the students of Futan University, whose purpose is to induce the people to boycott smuggled goods.
It is reported that these two groups are registered with the local Tangpu and other political organizations.

Ta Kung Pao (Sungkiang telegram) :-

At 2 p.m. July 7, some 60 students from Shanghai arrived at Sungkiang and staged patriotic plays. Some disorder occurred at the stage owing to the large number of spectators present.
Fearing that undesirable elements may take advantage of the opportunity to create trouble, the Sungkiang Hsien Government and the Public Safety Bureau advised the students to stop the performance.
The students returned to Shanghai by the 9 p.m. train on the same day.

《大公报》、《新闻报》、《申报》及其他本地报纸：-

中山（Nakayama）谋杀案

今日下午二时，第一特区地方法院将继续审理杨文道、叶海生和周社勇被控谋杀日本海军陆战队士兵中山一案。上次庭审因病缺席的助理市检察官保罗·鲁（Paul Ru）现已康复，可能于今日出庭。
法院前已命令警方传唤一名名为杰克（Jack）的朝鲜人以及日籍华人郑惠民（Zung Wei Ming）到庭受讯。工部局正与日本领事馆协商，以安排他们出庭。
被告辩护律师已阅读陈竺（Chenju）法医实验室的报告，若时间允许，今日将听取关于该报告的辩论。
今日所有本地中文报纸均刊登了法医实验室提交的报告（共四册）。

《大公报》及其他本地报纸：-

上海学生赴沪杭铁路沿线乡村演出爱国话剧

上海学生剧团于今年一月成立。六月，该剧团在大场演出了一些剧目，受到民众欢迎。
在过去的一个月里，该剧团一直在编排许多提倡使用国货的话剧。利用暑假之机，成员们打算前往沪杭铁路沿线的农村地区演出类似剧目。
7月7日，该剧团约40名成员离开上海，前往沪杭铁路沿线农村地区。陪同他们的有复旦大学学生组成的“抵制私货团”的20名成员，其目的是劝导民众抵制私货。
据悉，这两个团体已向当地汤浦及其他政治组织注册。

《大公报》（松江电）：-

7月7日下午二时，约60名上海学生抵达松江，演出爱国话剧。由于观众众多，舞台现场发生了一些混乱。
担心不良分子趁机捣乱，松江县政府和公安局建议学生停止演出。
学生们于当晚九时乘火车返回上海。

Lih Pao (立報) :-
THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE : IMPORTANT DEVELOPMENTS EXPECTED AT TO-MORROW'S HEARING.

The Nakayama murder case will again come up for hearing before the First Special District Court at 2 p.m. July 8.

In view of the fact that the Korean named Jack will be brought up for confrontation with the accused and the report of the Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory is ready, important developments may be expected. The lawyers for both sides will submit their arguments at the hearing.

The Court is paying close attention to the statements and character of Cheng Wei Ming鄭偉民 (G. Hirayama) and Tseng Yuan(曾元), the informers in the present case.

At the last hearing, Tseng Yuan admitted having written a document threatening Miss Chen Hung Pih (陳鴻璧), Principal of the Kwangtung Public School (廣東公學), in an attempt to implicate her in other affairs. This document is now in the possession of this paper. It was written by Tseng Yuan who, after writing it, handed it over to Chang Tsun(張深), an important witness in the case, saying : "The murder of the Japanese marine is the work of Chen Hung Pih. Chen had a male secretary named Lieu Ching Hai(劉勁海) who had full knowledge of the affair. (In reality, Chen has no secretary by the name of Lieu). Fearing that Lieu might disclose the secret, Chen asked Yih Hai Sung(葉海生) to kill Lieu. A certain party would naturally believe this information and Miss Chen will find it difficult to extricate herself."

Tseng Yuan directed Chang Tsun to entrust Ying Kuh Tseu(邢克周), one of Chang's relations, to give information to Chen Hung Pih. As Chen Hung Pih was cautious, nothing took place. Shortly afterwards the whole case became public.

The original text of the said document is published hereunder :-
"Information has been received from certain people giving the following details :-
(1) Miss Loo (盧 ) of the Kwangtung Public School (a girl teacher) recommends a male teacher named Lieu Ching Hai to Miss Chen Hung Pih as her private secretary.
(2) Miss Chen Hung Pih is an educationalist. She is an important member of the committee of the Dong Nyi XX Society (同義xx社).
(3) She has appointed Lieu as secretary. (All letters relating to the murder of the Japanese marine were written by Lieu alone, so Lieu is fully acquainted with the affair and he now discloses it. Upon learning of the disclosure, Chen asked Yih Hai Sung (this man is a staff member of the Dong Nyi XX Society) to find a non-member to kill Lieu in order to avert the danger.)
(4) Whether or not Yih Hai Sung did find a non-member to kill Lieu cannot be said, but as Lieu died on Nanking Road, this certain party is inclined to believe the information.
(5) Now this certain party has made an investigation into the antecedents of Miss Chen and is trying to bring about her arrest. Should evidence be found, Miss Chen will not be able to escape."

《立报》：-
中山谋杀案：预计明日庭审将有重要进展。

中山谋杀案将于7月8日下午二时再次在第一特区地方法院开庭审理。

鉴于名为杰克的朝鲜人将被带上法庭与被告对质，且陈竺法医实验室的报告已准备就绪，预计会有重要进展。双方律师将在庭审中提交辩词。

法院正密切关注本案告发人郑伟民（G. Hirayama）和曾元的陈述及品行。

在上次庭审中，曾元承认曾撰写一份恐吓广东公学校长陈鸿璧女士的文件，企图将她卷入其他事件。该文件现由本报持有。该文件由曾元撰写，写好后交给本案重要证人张深，并称：“杀害日本水兵是陈鸿璧所为。陈有一名男秘书名叫刘劲海，完全知晓内情。（实际上，陈并没有名叫刘的秘书。）因担心刘泄露秘密，陈指使叶海生杀死刘。某些人自然会相信这一信息，陈小姐将难以脱身。”

曾元指示张深委托张的亲戚邢克周向陈鸿璧提供信息。由于陈鸿璧谨慎行事，未发生任何事。不久后，整个案件公之于众。

该文件原文刊登如下：
“从某些人处收到消息，详情如下：-
(1) 广东公学的卢小姐（女教师）向陈鸿璧女士推荐一名名叫刘劲海的男教师担任其私人秘书。
(2) 陈鸿璧女士是一位教育家。她是同义xx社委员会的重要成员。
(3) 她已任命刘为秘书。（所有关于杀害日本水兵的信件均由刘单独撰写，因此刘完全知晓内情并予以披露。得知披露后，陈指使叶海生（此人是同义xx社职员）寻找一名非社员杀死刘，以消除危险。）
(4) 叶海生是否真的找到非社员杀死刘尚不可知，但由于刘死于南京路，某些人倾向于相信这一消息。
(5) 现在某些人已调查陈小姐的背景，并试图促成其被捕。一旦发现证据，陈小姐将无法逃脱。”

China Evening News of July 5 :-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE : TWO NEW DISCOVERIES MADE AS A
RESULT OF THE EXAMINATION BY THE MEDICO-LEGAL LABORATORY.

The Medico-Legal Laboratory at Chenju has
completed the examination of the various exhibits in the
case against Yang Vung Tao, Yih Hai Sung (alias Siao Kwangtung)
and Tseu Shou Yong who are being charged with the murder of
the Japanese marine Nakayama. The case will be resumed in
the First Special District Court at 2 p.m. July 8.
According to information secured by a
reporter of this paper, Sung Kuei Faung (孫桂方), Director
of the Medico-Legal Laboratory, and other experts of the
Laboratory have made a careful examination, by means of
scientific processes, of the bullet and the hole excavated
in a book to hold the pistol. As a result, the following
two new discoveries were made :-
(1) During his reconstruction of the crime
on Darroch Road, the scene of the murder of Nakayama, Yih
Hai Sung admitted that he fired the shot behind the Japanese
marine from a distance of five feet. However, an examination
of the wound to which the Japanese marine succumbed discloses
that the shot could not have been fired from a distance of
five feet for the condition of the wound clearly showed that
the murderer and the deceased were close to each other and
the barrel of the pistol was only several centimetres from
the wound when the shot was fired. If the shot had been
fired from a distance of five feet, then the murderer must
have lain on the ground and fired the shot upwards. This
might have caused a wound similar to that sustained by
Nakayama.
(2) None of the fingerprints around the
hole excavated in the book on physics seized in the home of
Yang Vung Tao have been found to correspond with those of
Yang Vung Tao.

Shun Pao and other local newspapers (Nanking telegram) :-

THE TELEPHONE RIGHTS IN THE EXTRA SETTLEMENT ROADS AREA

Repeated negotiations have been conducted by
the Ministry of Communications for the recovery of the Telephone
Rights in the extra-Settlement roads area of Shanghai. The
Shanghai Telephone Company is willing to pay a certain percen-
tage of its monthly net profits to our Government as a kind of
"special tax", but the Ministry of Communications is insisting
upon the recovery of these rights and has detailed Wang (王),
a departmental chief of the Ministry, to Shanghai to resume
the negotiations with the Shanghai Telephone Company.
Mr. Wang arrived here on the night of July 5.

7月5日《字林西报晚刊》：-

中山谋杀案：法医实验室检验取得两项新发现。

陈竺法医实验室已完成对杨文道、叶海生（别名小广东）和周社勇被控谋杀日本水兵中山一案中各项物证的检验。该案将于7月8日下午二时在第一特区地方法院恢复审理。
据本报记者获得的消息，法医实验室主任孙桂方及其他专家通过科学手段，对子弹以及在书中挖出用于藏匿手枪的孔洞进行了仔细检查。结果有了以下两项新发现：-
(1) 在中山遇害现场达罗克路重建犯罪过程时，叶海生承认他在距离日本水兵五英尺的地方从其身后开枪。然而，对导致日本水兵死亡的伤口进行检查后发现，射击距离不可能为五英尺，因为伤口状况清楚表明凶手与死者距离很近，开枪时枪管距离伤口仅几厘米。如果是从五英尺外开枪，那么凶手必须躺在地上向上射击。这可能会造成与中山所受的类似的伤口。
(2) 在杨文道家中查获的物理书中挖出的孔洞周围，未发现任何指纹与杨文道的指纹相符。

《申报》及其他本地报纸（南京电）：-

越界筑路地区的电话权

交通部为收回上海越界筑路地区的电话权进行了多次谈判。上海电话公司愿意将其每月净利润的一定百分比作为“特别税”支付给我国政府，但交通部坚持收回这些权利，并已派遣部里的一位王姓科长前往上海，恢复与上海电话公司的谈判。
王先生于7月5日晚抵达此地。

July 5, 1936.    Morning Translation.

Lih Pao (立报) :-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE TO BE HEARD ON JULY 8.

With reference to the case in which Yang Vung Tao(楊文道), Yih Hai Sung(葉海生) alias Siao Kwangtung and Tseu Shou Yong(周社荣) are charged with having murdered the Japanese marine Nakayama, the First Special District Court recently ordered that the bullet, the pistol, the rust and the finger print marks on the hole of the book entitled "Practical Physics" where the pistol was put be examined by the Medico-Legal Laboratory at Chenju. Sung Kwei Faung (孫達方), Chief of the Laboratory, in conjunction with experts and doctors, has examined all these points for several weeks by means of modern scientific operations. The examination has now been completed and a report to that effect has been sent to the Court.

During the summer time, the Court does not work on the afternoon. In view of the importance and the complication of the case, the Court has now decided to hold a special joint hearing of the case at 2 p.m. July 8. The Japanese Consulate has agreed to hand over Jack to the Municipal Police to bring him to the Court at the next hearing to be confronted with Yih Hai Sung and the other accused.

According to information secured by our reporter from a certain reliable source, the Medico-Legal Laboratory, as a result of examinations, has come to the view that none of the prints of the ten fingers of Yang Vung Tao correspond to the finger print marks on the hole excavated in the book entitled "Practical Physics" for the holding of the pistol.

Ta Kung Pao :-

ZUH NYI DRAMA GROUP TO STAGE PLAYS AT THE KIU SING THEATRE.

The Zuh Nyi Small Drama Group(實驗小劇團) was originally scheduled to stage certain plays on July 2 at the Kiu Sing Theatre(九星大戲院) in the French Concession. As the necessary preparations had not yet been completed, it is said that the Group will stage at the same place on July 5 (Sunday) three plays entitled "The Mother"(母親), "Autumn Sun"(秋陽) and "A corner of the metropolis"(都會的一角).

THIRTY TRADE ASSOCIATIONS TO MEET TO-DAY.

《立报》：-

中山谋杀案将于7月8日审理。

关于杨文道、叶海生（别名小广东）和周社荣被控谋杀日本水兵中山一案，第一特区地方法院最近命令由陈竺法医实验室对子弹、手枪、锈迹以及放置手枪的题为《实用物理学》一书孔洞上的指纹印记进行检验。实验室主任孙达方会同专家和医生，通过现代科学手段对这些要点进行了数周的检验。检验现已完成，并已向法院提交了相关报告。

夏季期间，法院下午不办公。鉴于该案的重要性和复杂性，法院现决定于7月8日下午二时举行特别联合庭审。日本领事馆已同意将杰克移交给工部局警务处，以便在下次庭审时将其带至法庭与叶海生及其他被告对质。

据本报记者从可靠消息源获得的信息，法医实验室经检验后认为，杨文道的十指指纹均与题为《实用物理学》一书中用于藏匿手枪的挖孔处的指纹印记不符。

左翼戏剧小组将在九星大戏院演出剧目。

June 16, 1936.
Morning Translation,
（印：DEPUTY COMMISSIONER (CRIME BRANCH)）
Ta Kung Pao, Central China Daily News and other local newspapers:-

THE NAKAYAMA MURDER CASE: YESTERDAY'S COURT PROCEEDINGS

The 6th hearing of the Nakayama murder case was held in the First Special District Court yesterday afternoon. Owing to the fact that a report on the examination of a bullet and of the book seized at the house of Yang Vung Tao (楊文道), one of the accused, had not yet been sent by the Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory, only an Investigation Court sat with Judge Siao Sih Fun (蕭錫芬) on the Bench. Procurator Chang Chung Shih (張宗儒) and Court Clerk Ting Chung Nan (丁重南) were in attendance.

The three accused, Yang Vung Tao, Yih Hai Sung (葉海生) (alias Siao Kwangtung 小廣東) and Tseu Shou Yong (周社榮) were brought into the Court under an escort of several Japanese policemen. Precautionary measures were adopted. Representatives of various bodies were present. Municipal Advocate Paul Ru (汝保華) was unable to attend owing to sickness. His place was taken by Municipal Advocate Li Tse San (厲志山) who with Municipal Advocate Bryan represented the Police. Besides foreign Detective Sub-Inspector Crowther, the evidence of several other witnesses was heard, including that of Zung Yung Sung (陳榮生) who was arrested at the same time as Yang Vung Tao but was later released.

Addressing the Court, Municipal Advocate Li said:- "A written report has been made on the result of the investigations conducted by the Police during the period of remand. The report contains the following eight points:
(1) The Police have notified Zung Wei Ming (鄭偉民) to appear in Court. He will be present at the next hearing.
(2) It was found that the relations between Zung Wei Ming and Yang Chien Chung (楊建忠) were very simple. On April 18 Zung obtained a clue from Yang Chien Chung. He received a cigarette picture from Yang on which was written: 'Address of Yang (meaning Yang Vung Tao): No. 5 Doong Zung Li (同仁里), Tongshan Road.' Zung hired a car from the Koong Zung Garage (公順汽車行) but could not find the address. Later it was discovered that the correct address was No. 19 Doong An Li (同安里). Zung has made a written statement regarding this point.
(3) A full set of fingerprints of Yang Vung Tao as required by the Court has been prepared.
(4) Tseu Shou Yong stated that in November last year he was very poor, but according to his chief tenant Ts Sung Foo (朱申甫), Tseu wore foreign dress and frequently attended cabarets at the time, therefore he was not poor.
(5) The statement of Li Yao (李耀) has been found. It was not signed. He has changed his address and cannot be summoned.
(6) A file showing the connection of Zung Hoong Pih (陳鴻璧), a female teacher of the Kwangtung Primary School (廣東小學), with this case has been obtained from the Public Safety Bureau. The Court is requested to examine this file."

《大公报》、《华中日报》及其他本地报纸：-

中山案：昨日庭审情况

昨日下午，第一特区法院开庭审理中山谋杀案第六次听证。由于陈诸法医实验室尚未送交对被告之一杨文道家中搜获的子弹及书籍的检验报告，故仅由萧錫芬法官主持预审法庭。检察官张宗儒及书记员丁重南出庭。

三名被告杨文道、叶海生（别名小广东）及周社荣在数名日本警察的押解下被带入法庭。现场采取了预防措施。各团体代表出席。市政律师汝保华因病未能出庭，由市政律师厉志山代为出席，其与市政律师布莱恩（Bryan）共同代表警务处。除外籍巡官克劳瑟（Crowther）外，法庭还听取了其他几名证人的证词，其中包括与杨文道同时被捕但随后获释的陈荣生。

市政律师厉志山向法庭陈述如下：“警方在还押调查期间进行了调查，并已就调查结果提交书面报告。报告包含以下八点：
(1) 警方已通知郑伟民出庭。他将在下次听证时到庭。
(2) 经查，郑伟民与杨建忠之间的关系非常简单。4月18日，郑从杨建忠处获得线索。他从杨处收到一张香烟画片，上面写着：‘杨（指杨文道）地址：同山路同仁里5号。’郑从公顺汽车行租了一辆车，但未能找到该地址。后查明正确地址为同安里19号。郑已就此点作出书面陈述。
(3) 已按法庭要求制备了杨文道的全套指纹。
(4) 周社荣称去年十一月他非常贫困，但据其主租客朱申甫称，周当时身穿西装，并频繁出入舞厅，因此并不贫困。
(5) 已找到李耀的陈述书。该陈述书未签名。李已变更住址，无法传唤。
(6) 已从公安局获取一份档案，显示广东小学女教师陈鸿璧与本案的关联。请法庭查阅此档案。”

pages.en:
June 17, 1936.
2
Morning Translation.

(7) A written report has been made by the Japanese policeman Kaneyasu who found the pistol at the scene of crime.
(8) Li Hung Ping (李鴻賓), police watchman on duty at the entrance of Foong Lo Li (丰樂里) Alleyway has made a written statement. He is also present to-day and may be questioned."

Foreign Detective Sub-Inspector Crowther attached to Dixwell Road Police Station gave the following evidence:
I went to Tsingtao in company with Japanese detectives to conduct investigations. With the assistance of the Public Safety Bureau of Tsingtao, I found a suit of foreign dress in the cabaret established by Yih Hai Sung. Yih had stated that he wore this suit on the day he killed the Japanese marine. A photograph of Yih Hai Sung was also found. In this photograph he can be seen wearing the same pair of trousers that was seized. A number of witnesses were also questioned in Tsingtao. Their written statements have already been produced to the Court. It is a fact that after the murder of the Japanese marine, Yih Hai Sung had come into the possession of some money and opened a dance hall at Tsingtao with a man named Tang (唐). At first, Yih promised to produce a share of $1,000, but finally he contributed $500 and opened the hall with Tang. The agreement has been brought here and is now submitted for record. A letter was secured from Yang Tsho Zung (楊佐臣), brother-in-law of Yih Hai Sung, to prove certain connections really existing between Yih and Jack. This letter was written to Yih by a Korean named "Costa" (考司脫) and a man named Li (李), and was taken by Jack to Tsingtao to call on Yih to request him to give Jack favourable treatment. Thus, from this letter, it will be seen that the statement made by Yih that he had no connection with Jack is not true.

Municipal Advocate Li Tse San resumed his address: "Yih Hai Sung went to Tsingtao last Winter because a person named Tao Ts Zung (陶之順) who was operating dance halls at Tsingtao, desired to secure dancing girls. Yang Tsho Zung, Yih's brother-in-law, wrote a letter introducing Tao to Yih. On November 29, Yih took several dancing girls to Tsingtao, where, through the introduction of others, he became acquainted with a man named Tang (唐) of the Kiaochow-Tsinan Railway and opened a dance hall together with him. This hall was later closed owing to bad business. Afterwards Yih opened another dance hall jointly with other persons. When the foreign Detective Sub-Inspector was at Tsingtao conducting an investigation, the witnesses concerned were summoned and made statements. Yih Hai Sung has made a statement to the Court that several days before November 9 last year, he wrote out invitation cards at the Moon Palace Hotel, but according to investigations made by the Police into a statement made by the witness Hsu Lin Sung (徐林生), Yih's invitation cards were already issued on November 6. An invitation card was seized at the home of Yih's brother-in-law at Tsingtao, and on this card the date of the birthday celebration of Yih's mother was given as November 10. This corroborates the witness Chang Zai Yuan (張財源). Yih's statement to the effect that on November 9, the date on which the Japanese marine was murdered, he was holding a ceremony to celebrate the birthday of his mother at the

1936年6月17日。
2
晨间译件。

(7) 在现场发现手枪的日本警察金安（Kaneyasu，音译）已提交书面报告。
(8) 在丰乐里弄堂口执勤的警员李鸿宾已提交书面陈述。他今日也在场，可接受询问。”

隶属狄思威路捕房的外籍巡官克劳瑟提供如下证词：
我与日本侦探一同前往青岛进行调查。在青岛公安局的协助下，我在叶海生开设的舞厅内找到一套西装。叶曾声称，他在杀害日本海军陆战队员当天穿着这套西装。还发现了叶海生的一张照片。照片中，他穿着与被扣押的那条相同的裤子。在青岛还讯问了许多证人。他们的书面证词已呈交法庭。事实是，在日本海军陆战队员被杀后，叶海生获得了一些钱，并与一名姓唐的人在青岛开设了一家舞厅。起初，叶承诺出资1,000元入股，但最终他出资500元，与唐共同开设了该舞厅。协议已带至此地，现提交备案。从叶海生的姐夫杨佐臣处获取了一封信，以证明叶与杰克（Jack）之间确实存在某些联系。这封信是由一名叫“考司脫”（Costa，音译）的朝鲜人和一名姓李的人写给叶的，并由杰克带往青岛，以此拜访叶并要求叶给予杰克优待。因此，从这封信可以看出，叶声称他与杰克没有联系的说法是不实的。

市政律师厉志山继续陈述：“叶海生去年冬天去青岛，是因为在青岛经营舞厅的一个叫陶之顺的人想要招募舞女。叶的姐夫杨佐臣写信将陶介绍给叶。11月29日，叶带着几名舞女前往青岛，在那里经他人介绍，结识了胶济铁路的一名姓唐的人，并与他共同开设了一家舞厅。该舞厅后因生意不佳而关闭。之后，叶又与其他人合伙开设了另一家舞厅。当外籍巡官在青岛进行调查时，相关证人被传唤并作证。叶海生向法庭陈述称，在去年11月9日前几天，他在月宫饭店填写请柬，但根据警方对证人徐林生所作陈述的调查，叶的请柬早在11月6日就已发出。在叶位于青岛的姐夫家中搜获了一张请柬，上面写明叶母亲生日庆祝日期为11月10日。这与证人张财源的证词相符。叶声称在11月9日（即日本海军陆战队员被杀之日）他在

pages.en:
3
June 17, 1936. Morning Translation.

Great China Restaurant (大中華) is not reliable. The letter of introduction sent by Costa to Yih states that Jack is their special friend. This shows how close are the relations between Yih and Jack. Upon arriving at Tsingtao last Winter, Yih wore nice clothing and paid frequent visits to dance halls. This shows that Yih had money after the murder of the Japanese marine. As regards the conduct of Yih on ordinary days, Me Pao Sung (宓保生), Manager of the Moon Dance Hall, will testify that Yih is a bad man who is connected with gangs".
The Municipal Advocate then submitted for reference two photos showing the injuries sustained by Nakayama and also two reports made by foreign staff members named "Yeu Yin" (尤因) and "Dickson" (狄克生) who were detailed by the Municipal Police to the Chenju Medico-Legal Laboratory to conduct an examination together with other officers.
Replying to Judge Siao, Yih Hai Sung said:-
The foreign dress and the photo are my property. I cannot remember whether I was wearing the pair of trousers shown in the photo. The letter seized at the home of my brother-in-law was written to me in June last year by Costa and a man named Li introducing Jack to me. Later, Jack called on me at a dance hall at Tsingtao. As I did not entertain him, therefore he had a grudge against me. Fearing that Jack may attempt to harm me in future, I place the letter in my brother-in-law's home for safe custody. Thus, Jack has produced this letter as evidence. If I had murdered the Japanese marine with Jack, would not my brother-in-law have destroyed this letter? The letter says that Jack is our special good friend. This was said by Costa and Jack. I do not know why Jack went to Tsingtao.
The Judge then asked Yih whether the seized invitation card and the agreement belonged to him.
Yih replied in the affirmative and continued:-
"As regards the opening of a dance hall, at first I promised to take a share of $1,000 because I was going to ask people to take up shares. Finally, I paid only $250. The money was paid out by my wife Zung Kwei Tsung (莊桂宗) from the Shanghai Bank of Communications and was sent to Tsingtao".
The Judge asked the Police whether they had made inquiries at the Bank of Communications.
D.S.I. Crowther: Acting on instructions from the Court, I visited the Bank of Communications on May 8 to make inquiries about the depositor Zung Kwei Tsung. There are two Zung Kwei Tsung's; one lives on Tongshan Road. On March 17 this year, this person made a fixed deposit of $300 and on April 23, this person obtained a loan of $250 from this bank against the fixed deposit. The other depositor resides at No. 18 Zang An Li (藏安里), Woosung Road, and is an old client who has had dealings with the bank for several years. At present this depositor has a deposit of $258.20, but during the past eight months, no large amounts of money have either been paid in or withdrawn.
Questioned by Judge Siao, Yih Hai Sung said:-
"My wifes lives in Zang An Li and is probably this person".
